chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman. He said: Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ahwas al-Qummi narrated to me.
He (Muhammad ibn Ahmad) said: I said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), “How many rak‘ahs (units) are there in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Fifty-one rak‘ahs (units).”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْيَقْطِينِيِّ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَحْوَصُ اَلْقُمِّيُّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَ كَمِ اَلصَّلاَةُ مِنْ رَكْعَةٍ قَالَ« إِحْدَى وَ خَمْسُونَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: It was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman. He said: Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ahwas al-Qummi narrated to me.
thaqalaynMatn: He (Muhammad ibn Ahmad) said: I said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), “How many rak‘ahs (units) are there in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Fifty-one rak‘ahs (units).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
Imam (a.s) said: “The obligatory and recommended prayers are fifty-one rak‘ahs, among them two rak‘ahs after the ‘Atamah (night prayer) while sitting, which are counted as one rak‘ah when performed standing. The obligatory among them are seventeen rak‘ahs, and the recommended are thirty-four rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ فُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْفَرِيضَةُ وَ اَلنَّافِلَةُ إِحْدَى وَ خَمْسُونَ رَكْعَةً مِنْهَا رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ جَالِساً تُعَدَّانِ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ اَلْفَرِيضَةُ مِنْهَا سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً وَ اَلنَّافِلَةُ أَرْبَعٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The obligatory and recommended prayers are fifty-one rak‘ahs, among them two rak‘ahs after the ‘Atamah (night prayer) while sitting, which are counted as one rak‘ah when performed standing. The obligatory among them are seventeen rak‘ahs, and the recommended are thirty-four rak‘ahs.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And through this same chain of transmission, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, and al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, and Bukayr, they said:
We heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to perform supererogatory prayers equal to twice the number of the obligatory prayers, and He (saws) used to fast supererogatory fasts equal to twice the number of the obligatory fasts.”
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ وَ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ وَ بُكَيْرٍ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ مِثْلَيِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ يَصُومُ مِنَ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ مِثْلَيِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And through this same chain of transmission, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, and al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, and Bukayr, they said:
thaqalaynMatn: We heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to perform supererogatory prayers equal to twice the number of the obligatory prayers, and He (saws) used to fast supererogatory fasts equal to twice the number of the obligatory fasts.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 4

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Buzay‘ from Hanan. He said:
‘Amr ibn Hurayth asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), while I was sitting (there), and he said to Imam (a.s): “Inform me, may I be your ransom, about the prayers of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” So Imam (a.s) said to him: “The Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray eight rak‘ahs at the time of zawal, four (rak‘ahs) for the noon prayer (al-Dhuhr), and eight after it, and four (rak‘ahs) for the afternoon prayer (al-’Asr), and three (rak‘ahs) for the sunset prayer (al-Maghrib), and four after Maghrib, and the final night prayer (Isha al-akhirah) four (rak‘ahs), and eight for the night prayer (salat al-layl), and three for witr, and two rak‘ahs for the dawn prayer (al-fajr), and the morning prayer (salat al-ghadah) two rak‘ahs.” I said: “May I be your ransom, so if I have the strength for more than this, would Allah (swt) punish me for praying excessively?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, but He (swt) punishes for abandoning the Sunnah.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ عَنْ حَنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ عَمْرُو بْنُ حُرَيْثٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا جَالِسٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخْبِرْنِي جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ« كَانَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتِ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ أَرْبَعاً اَلْأُولَى وَ ثَمَانِيَ بَعْدَهَا وَ أَرْبَعاً اَلْعَصْرَ وَ ثَلاَثاً اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ أَرْبَعاً بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ أَرْبَعاً وَ ثَمَانِيَ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ ثَلاَثاً اَلْوَتْرَ وَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ صَلاَةَ اَلْغَدَاةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ» قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَإِنْ كُنْتُ أَقْوَى عَلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ هَذَا أَ يُعَذِّبُنِي اَللَّهُ عَلَى كَثْرَةِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ يُعَذِّبُ عَلَى تَرْكِ اَلسُّنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Buzay‘ from Hanan. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: ‘Amr ibn Hurayth asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), while I was sitting (there), and he said to Imam (a.s): “Inform me, may I be your ransom, about the prayers of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” So Imam (a.s) said to him: “The Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray eight rak‘ahs at the time of zawal, four (rak‘ahs) for the noon prayer (al-Dhuhr), and eight after it, and four (rak‘ahs) for the afternoon prayer (al-’Asr), and three (rak‘ahs) for the sunset prayer (al-Maghrib), and four after Maghrib, and the final night prayer (Isha al-akhirah) four (rak‘ahs), and eight for the night prayer (salat al-layl), and three for witr, and two rak‘ahs for the dawn prayer (al-fajr), and the morning prayer (salat al-ghadah) two rak‘ahs.” I said: “May I be your ransom, so if I have the strength for more than this, would Allah (swt) punish me for praying excessively?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, but He (swt) punishes for abandoning the Sunnah.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri. He said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The day prayers are sixteen rak‘ahs: eight when the sun passes the meridian (zawal), and eight after Dhuhr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib. O’ Harith, do not abandon them in travel or in residence. And two rak‘ahs after the final Isha prayer, my father (a.s) used to pray them while sitting, and I pray them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs in the night.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ اَلنَّصْرِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً ثَمَانٍ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَثَمَانٍ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَأَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ يَا حَارِثُ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي سَفَرٍ وَلاَ حَضَرٍ وَرَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ كَانَ أَبِي يُصَلِّيهِمَا وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ وَ أَنَا أُصَلِّيهِمَا وَ أَنَا قَائِمٌ وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The day prayers are sixteen rak‘ahs: eight when the sun passes the meridian (zawal), and eight after Dhuhr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib. O’ Harith, do not abandon them in travel or in residence. And two rak‘ahs after the final Isha prayer, my father (a.s) used to pray them while sitting, and I pray them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs in the night.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Maskan from Ibn Abi Umayr. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best that has been established by the Sunnah in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “The complete fifty (units).”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ مَا جَرَتْ بِهِ اَلسُّنَّةُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« تَمَامُ اَلْخَمْسِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Maskan from Ibn Abi Umayr. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best that has been established by the Sunnah in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “The complete fifty (units).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, during the day. Imam (a.s) said: “And who can endure that?” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Shall I not inform you how I myself do?” I said: “Yes.” So Imam (a.s) said: “Eight rak‘ahs before Dhuhr and eight after it.” I asked: “(What about) Maghrib?” Imam (a.s) said: “Four after it.” I asked: “(What about) the ‘atamah (night prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray ‘atamah and then sleep.” And Imam (a.s) moved his hand like this. Ibn Abi Umayr said: Then Imam (a.s) described it as our companions have mentioned.
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِالنَّهَارِ فَقَالَ« وَ مَنْ يُطِيقُ ذَلِكَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« وَ لَكِنْ أَ لاَ أُخْبِرُكَ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ أَنَا» فَقُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ« ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَبْلَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ ثَمَانٍ بَعْدَهَا» قُلْتُ فَالْمَغْرِبُ قَالَ« أَرْبَعٌ بَعْدَهَا» قُلْتُ فَالْعَتَمَةُ قَالَ« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَتَمَةَ ثُمَّ يَنَامُ» وَ قَالَ بِيَدِهِ هَكَذَا فَحَرَّكَهَا: قَالَ اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ ثُمَّ وَصَفَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَمَا ذَكَرَ أَصْحَابُنَا
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, during the day. Imam (a.s) said: “And who can endure that?” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Shall I not inform you how I myself do?” I said: “Yes.” So Imam (a.s) said: “Eight rak‘ahs before Dhuhr and eight after it.” I asked: “(What about) Maghrib?” Imam (a.s) said: “Four after it.” I asked: “(What about) the ‘atamah (night prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray ‘atamah and then sleep.” And Imam (a.s) moved his hand like this. Ibn Abi Umayr said: Then Imam (a.s) described it as our companions have mentioned.

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Ibn Maskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer of the nafilah (supererogatory prayer) is eight rak‘ahs when the sun passes the meridian (before Dhuhr), and six rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and two rak‘ahs after the final Isha prayer, you recite in them one hundred verses, whether standing or sitting, and standing is better, but do not count them among the fifty (rak‘ahs). And eight rak‘ahs at the end of the night, in the night prayer (salat al-layl), you recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al Kafirun) in the first two rak‘ahs, and in the rest you may recite whatever you wish from the Qur’an. Then comes the witr prayer, three rak‘ahs, in which you recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) in all of them, and you separate between them with a taslim. Then the two rak‘ahs before the dawn prayer, in the first of them you recite ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al Kafirun), and in the second (unit) ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas).”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَلنَّافِلَةِ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ حِينَ تَزُولُ اَلشَّمْسُ قَبْلَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَانِ قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَأَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَرَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ تَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا مِائَةَ آيَةٍ قَائِماً أَوْ قَاعِداً وَاَلْقِيَامُ أَفْضَلُ وَ لاَ تَعُدُّهُمَا مِنَ اَلْخَمْسِينَ وَ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ مِنْ آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ تَقْرَأُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ وَ تَقْرَأُ فِي سَائِرِهَا مَا أَحْبَبْتَ مِنَ اَلْقُرْآنِ ثُمَّ اَلْوَتْرُ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ تَقْرَأُ فِيهَا جَمِيعاً «قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ تَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُنَّ بِتَسْلِيمٍ ثُمَّ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَللَّتَانِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ تَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأُولَى مِنْهُمَا« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Ibn Maskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer of the nafilah (supererogatory prayer) is eight rak‘ahs when the sun passes the meridian (before Dhuhr), and six rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and two rak‘ahs after the final Isha prayer, you recite in them one hundred verses, whether standing or sitting, and standing is better, but do not count them among the fifty (rak‘ahs). And eight rak‘ahs at the end of the night, in the night prayer (salat al-layl), you recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al Kafirun) in the first two rak‘ahs, and in the rest you may recite whatever you wish from the Qur’an. Then comes the witr prayer, three rak‘ahs, in which you recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) in all of them, and you separate between them with a taslim. Then the two rak‘ahs before the dawn prayer, in the first of them you recite ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al Kafirun), and in the second (unit) ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for the narrations that have been reported regarding a lesser number than what we have mentioned concerning prayer, such as what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Do not pray less than forty-four rak‘ahs.” He (narrator) said: “And I saw him (Imam (a.s)) praying four rak‘ahs after the ‘atamah (final night prayer).
arabicText: فَأَمَّا اَلْأَحَادِيثُ اَلَّتِي رُوِيَتْ فِي نُقْصَانِ مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ مِثْلُ مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِنْتِ إِلْيَاسَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ أَقَلَّ مِنْ أَرْبَعٍ وَ أَرْبَعِينَ رَكْعَةً» قَالَ وَ رَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي بَعْدَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ
thaqalaynSanad: As for the narrations that have been reported regarding a lesser number than what we have mentioned concerning prayer, such as what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Yahya ibn Habib, he said:
I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s) about the best form of prayer through which the servants may draw near to Allah (swt), the Exalted. Imam (a.s) said: “Forty-six rak‘ahs, its obligatory and supererogatory prayers.” I said: “This is the narration of Zurarah.” Imam (a.s) said: “And do you see anyone who proclaimed the truth more clearly than he (Zurarah) did?”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ مَا يَتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ اَلْعِبَادُ إِلَى اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« سِتٌّ وَ أَرْبَعُونَ رَكْعَةً فَرَائِضُهُ وَ نَوَافِلُهُ» قُلْتُ هَذِهِ رِوَايَةُ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ« أَ وَ تَرَى أَحَداً كَانَ أَصْدَعَ بِالْحَقِّ مِنْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Yahya ibn Habib, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s) about the best form of prayer through which the servants may draw near to Allah (swt), the Exalted. Imam (a.s) said: “Forty-six rak‘ahs, its obligatory and supererogatory prayers.” I said: “This is the narration of Zurarah.” Imam (a.s) said: “And do you see anyone who proclaimed the truth more clearly than he (Zurarah) did?”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu‘ayb from Abu Basir. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about voluntary prayers during the night and day. Imam (a.s) said: “The amount that is recommended not to be left is: eight rak‘ahs at the time when the sun passes the meridian, and after Dhuhr two rak‘ahs, and before ‘Asr two rak‘ahs, and after Maghrib two rak‘ahs, and before ‘atamah two rak‘ahs, and at the time of sahar (pre-dawn) eight rak‘ahs, then he performs witr, and witr is three rak‘ahs, separated. Then two rak‘ahs before the salah of fajr. And the most beloved of the night prayer to them is at the end of the night.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ فَقَالَ« اَلَّذِي يُسْتَحَبُّ أَنْ لاَ يُقْصَرَ عَنْهُ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ عِنْدَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ رَكْعَتَانِ وَ قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ رَكْعَتَانِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ رَكْعَتَانِ وَ قَبْلَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ رَكْعَتَانِ وَ مِنَ اَلسَّحَرِ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ يُوتِرُ وَ اَلْوَتْرُ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ مَفْصُولَةً ثُمَّ رَكْعَتَانِ قَبْلَ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ أَحَبُّ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ إِلَيْهِمْ آخِرُ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu‘ayb from Abu Basir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about voluntary prayers during the night and day. Imam (a.s) said: “The amount that is recommended not to be left is: eight rak‘ahs at the time when the sun passes the meridian, and after Dhuhr two rak‘ahs, and before ‘Asr two rak‘ahs, and after Maghrib two rak‘ahs, and before ‘atamah two rak‘ahs, and at the time of sahar (pre-dawn) eight rak‘ahs, then he performs witr, and witr is three rak‘ahs, separated. Then two rak‘ahs before the salah of fajr. And the most beloved of the night prayer to them is at the end of the night.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the established Sunnah regarding prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Eight rak‘ahs at the time of zawal, and two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, and two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and thirteen rak‘ahs at the end of the night, including the witr, and the two rak‘ahs of fajr.” I (narrator) asked: “So is this all that the Sunnah has established?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Abu al-Khattab asked: “What if one is strong and adds more?” He (Imam (a.s)) sat up, He (a.s) had been reclining, and said: “If you are strong, then pray them as they were prayed before, and as long as they are not in a forbidden hour of the day, there is no forbidden hour of the night. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says: “And during parts of the night, glorify Him.” (Surah Taha 20:130)
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا جَرَتْ بِهِ اَلسُّنَّةُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتِ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَانِ قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنْ آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ مِنْهَا اَلْوَتْرُ وَ رَكْعَتَا اَلْفَجْرِ» قُلْتُ فَهَذَا جَمِيعُ مَا جَرَتْ بِهِ اَلسُّنَّةُ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ أَبُو اَلْخَطَّابِ أَ فَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ قَوِيَ فَزَادَ قَالَ فَجَلَسَ وَ كَانَ مُتَّكِئاً فَقَالَ« إِنْ قَوِيتَ فَصَلِّهَا كَمَا كَانَتْ تُصَلَّى وَ كَمَا لَيْسَتْ فِي سَاعَةٍ مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ فَلَيْسَتْ فِي سَاعَةٍ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ« وَ مِنْ آنٰاءِ اَللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the established Sunnah regarding prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Eight rak‘ahs at the time of zawal, and two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, and two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and thirteen rak‘ahs at the end of the night, including the witr, and the two rak‘ahs of fajr.” I (narrator) asked: “So is this all that the Sunnah has established?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Abu al-Khattab asked: “What if one is strong and adds more?” He (Imam (a.s)) sat up, He (a.s) had been reclining, and said: “If you are strong, then pray them as they were prayed before, and as long as they are not in a forbidden hour of the day, there is no forbidden hour of the night. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says: “And during parts of the night, glorify Him.” (Surah Taha 20:130)

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah. He said:
I (Zurarah) said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s): “I am a merchant, I travel and engage in trade. So how can I manage the time of zawal and maintain the prayer of zawal, and how many rak‘ahs should be prayed?” Imam (a.s) said: “You pray eight rak‘ahs when the sun passes the meridian, and two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, these are twelve rak‘ahs. And you pray two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and after the middle of the night, thirteen rak‘ahs, among which is the witr, and among which are the two rak‘ahs of fajr. That makes twenty-seven rak‘ahs besides the obligatory prayer. And indeed, all of this is supererogatory and not obligatory. Verily, the one who abandons the obligatory prayer is a disbeliever, and the one who abandons this (supererogatory) is not a disbeliever, but it is a sin, because it is recommended that when a man does a good deed, he remains consistent in it.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ تَاجِرٌ أَخْتَلِفُ وَ أَتَّجِرُ فَكَيْفَ لِي بِالزَّوَالِ وَ اَلْمُحَافَظَةِ عَلَى صَلاَةِ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ كَمْ تُصَلَّى قَالَ« تُصَلِّي ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتٍ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَرَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَرَكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ فَهَذِهِ اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً وَتُصَلِّي بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَبَعْدَ مَا يَنْتَصِفُ اَللَّيْلُ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنْهَا اَلْوَتْرُ وَمِنْهَا رَكْعَتَا اَلْفَجْرِ فَتِلْكَ سَبْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ رَكْعَةً سِوَى اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ إِنَّمَا هَذَا كُلُّهُ تَطَوُّعٌ وَ لَيْسَ بِمَفْرُوضٍ إِنَّ تَارِكَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ كَافِرٌ وَ إِنَّ تَارِكَ هَذَا لَيْسَ بِكَافِرٍ وَ لَكِنَّهَا مَعْصِيَةٌ لِأَنَّهُ يُسْتَحَبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ اَلرَّجُلُ عَمَلاً مِنَ اَلْخَيْرِ أَنْ يَدُومَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Zurarah) said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s): “I am a merchant, I travel and engage in trade. So how can I manage the time of zawal and maintain the prayer of zawal, and how many rak‘ahs should be prayed?” Imam (a.s) said: “You pray eight rak‘ahs when the sun passes the meridian, and two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, and two rak‘ahs before ‘Asr, these are twelve rak‘ahs. And you pray two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, and after the middle of the night, thirteen rak‘ahs, among which is the witr, and among which are the two rak‘ahs of fajr. That makes twenty-seven rak‘ahs besides the obligatory prayer. And indeed, all of this is supererogatory and not obligatory. Verily, the one who abandons the obligatory prayer is a disbeliever, and the one who abandons this (supererogatory) is not a disbeliever, but it is a sin, because it is recommended that when a man does a good deed, he remains consistent in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s): “Our companions differ regarding supererogatory prayers. Some of them pray forty-four, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me of that which you yourself practice, so that I may do the same.” Imam (a.s) said: “I pray fifty-one rak‘ahs.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Count with me,” and Imam (a.s) counted with his hand: “Eight at zawal, four after Dhuhr, four before ‘Asr, two after Maghrib, two before the final Isha, and two after Isha while sitting, they are counted as one rak‘ah when standing, and eight rak‘ahs of the night prayer, and witr three rak‘ahs, and two rak‘ahs of fajr, and the obligatory prayers are seventeen, that makes fifty-one rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بَعْضُهُمْ يُصَلِّي أَرْبَعاً وَ أَرْبَعِينَ وَ بَعْضُهُمْ يُصَلِّي خَمْسِينَ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِالَّذِي تَعْمَلُ بِهِ أَنْتَ كَيْفَ هُوَ حَتَّى أَعْمَلَ بِمِثْلِهِ فَقَالَ« أُصَلِّي وَاحِدَةً وَخَمْسِينَ رَكْعَةً» ثُمَّ قَالَ« أَمْسِكْ» وَ عَقَدَ بِيَدِهِ« اَلزَّوَالَ ثَمَانِيَةً وَ أَرْبَعاً بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ أَرْبَعاً قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ عِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ مِنْ قُعُودٍ تُعَدَّانِ بِرَكْعَةٍ مِنْ قِيَامٍ وَ ثَمَانِيَ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرَ ثَلاَثاً وَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ اَلْفَرَائِضَ سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ فَذَلِكَ إِحْدَى وَ خَمْسُونَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s): “Our companions differ regarding supererogatory prayers. Some of them pray forty-four, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me of that which you yourself practice, so that I may do the same.” Imam (a.s) said: “I pray fifty-one rak‘ahs.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Count with me,” and Imam (a.s) counted with his hand: “Eight at zawal, four after Dhuhr, four before ‘Asr, two after Maghrib, two before the final Isha, and two after Isha while sitting, they are counted as one rak‘ah when standing, and eight rak‘ahs of the night prayer, and witr three rak‘ahs, and two rak‘ahs of fajr, and the obligatory prayers are seventeen, that makes fifty-one rak‘ahs.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from one of our companions. He said:
Imam (a.s) said to me: “The day prayer is sixteen rak‘ahs, pray it at any time of the day you wish: if you wish, at its beginning; if you wish, in the middle of it; and if you wish, at its end.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ قَالَ لِي:« صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً صَلِّهَا فِي أَيِّ اَلنَّهَارِ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي وَسَطِهِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي آخِرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from one of our companions. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me: “The day prayer is sixteen rak‘ahs, pray it at any time of the day you wish: if you wish, at its beginning; if you wish, in the middle of it; and if you wish, at its end.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 9

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Harith al-Nasri from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “The day prayer is sixteen rak‘ahs, eight when the sun passes the meridian, and eight after Dhuhr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib. O’ Harith, do not abandon them whether in travel or at home. And two rak‘ahs after Isha, my father (a.s) used to pray them while sitting, and I pray them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs at night.”
arabicText: وروى أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى عن علي بن النعمان عن الحارث النصري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول صلاة النهار ست عشرة ركعة ثمان إذا زالت الشمس وثمان بعد الظهر واربع ركعات بعد المغرب يا حارث لا تدعها في سفر ولا حضر وركعتان بعد العشاء كان أبي يصليهما وهو قاعد وأنا اصليهما وأنا قائم وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله يصلي ثلاث عشرة ركعة من الليل
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Harith al-Nasri from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “The day prayer is sixteen rak‘ahs, eight when the sun passes the meridian, and eight after Dhuhr, and four rak‘ahs after Maghrib. O’ Harith, do not abandon them whether in travel or at home. And two rak‘ahs after Isha, my father (a.s) used to pray them while sitting, and I pray them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs at night.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from ‘Ammar ibn al-Mubarak from Ẓarif ibn Nasih from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Ghifari:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, how many rak‘ahs are the nawafil (supererogatory prayers) of the day?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are sixteen rak‘ahs. You may pray them at whichever hours of the day you wish, but if you pray them at their specified times, it is better.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ ظَرِيفِ بْنِ نَاصِحٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ اَلْغِفَارِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ اَلنَّوَافِلُ كَمْ هِيَ قَالَ« هِيَ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً أَيَّ سَاعَاتِ اَلنَّهَارِ شِئْتَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَهَا صَلَّيْتَهَا إِلاَّ أَنَّكَ إِنْ صَلَّيْتَهَا فِي مَوَاقِيتِهَا أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from ‘Ammar ibn al-Mubarak from Ẓarif ibn Nasih from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Ghifari:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, how many rak‘ahs are the nawafil (supererogatory prayers) of the day?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are sixteen rak‘ahs. You may pray them at whichever hours of the day you wish, but if you pray them at their specified times, it is better.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman. He said:
I asked him about the supererogatory prayer during the day, and he mentioned: “That eight rak‘ahs are to be prayed before Dhuhr, and eight after it.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِالنَّهَارِ فَذَكَرَ« أَنَّهُ يُصَلَّى ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ قَبْلَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ ثَمَانٌ بَعْدَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about the supererogatory prayer during the day, and he mentioned: “That eight rak‘ahs are to be prayed before Dhuhr, and eight after it.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is there anything before the final Isha and after it?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except that I pray two rak‘ahs after it, and I do not consider them part of the night prayer (salat al-layl).”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ قَبْلَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ بَعْدَهَا شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ غَيْرَ أَنِّي أُصَلِّي بَعْدَهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ لَسْتُ أَحْسُبُهُمَا مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is there anything before the final Isha and after it?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except that I pray two rak‘ahs after it, and I do not consider them part of the night prayer (salat al-layl).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Harun ibn Muslim from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Hannat. He said:
We went out, I (Musa al-Hannat), Jamil ibn Darraj, and ‘A’idh al-Ahmasi, for Hajj. And ‘A’idh would often say to us on the way, “I have a need I wish to ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), about.” And I (Musa al-Hannat) would say to him (‘A’idh), “Wait until we meet Him (a.s).” So when we entered upon Him (a.s), we greeted Him (a.s) and sat down. He (a.s) turned his face toward us and began by saying: “Whoever comes to Allah (swt) with what He (swt) has made obligatory upon him, Allah (swt) will not ask him about anything beyond that.” Then ‘A’idh gestured to us. When we stood up, we said to him, “What was your need?” He (‘A’idh) said: “What you just heard.” We said: “How was that your need?” He (‘A’idh) said: “I am a man who cannot endure standing at night in prayer, so I feared that I would be held accountable for it and destroyed.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْحَنَّاطِ قَالَ: خَرَجْنَا أَنَا وَ جَمِيلُ بْنُ دَرَّاجٍ وَ عَائِذٌ اَلْأَحْمَسِيُّ حُجَّاجاً فَكَانَ عَائِذٌ كَثِيراً مَا يَقُولُ لَنَا فِي اَلطَّرِيقِ إِنَّ لِي إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ حَاجَةً أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ عَنْهَا فَأَقُولُ لَهُ حَتَّى نَلْقَاهُ فَلَمَّا دَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ سَلَّمْنَا وَ جَلَسْنَا فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْنَا بِوَجْهِهِ مُبْتَدِئاً فَقَالَ« مَنْ أَتَى اَللَّهَ بِمَا اِفْتَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ لَمْ يَسْأَلْهُ عَمَّا سِوَى ذَلِكَ» فَغَمَزَنَا عَائِذٌ فَلَمَّا قُمْنَا قُلْنَا مَا كَانَتْ حَاجَتَكَ قَالَ اَلَّذِي سَمِعْتُمْ قُلْنَا كَيْفَ كَانَتْ هَذِهِ حَاجَتَكَ فَقَالَ أَنَا رَجُلٌ لاَ أُطِيقُ اَلْقِيَامَ بِاللَّيْلِ فَخِفْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مَأْخُوذاً بِهِ فَأَهْلِكَ
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Harun ibn Muslim from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Hannat. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: We went out, I (Musa al-Hannat), Jamil ibn Darraj, and ‘A’idh al-Ahmasi, for Hajj. And ‘A’idh would often say to us on the way, “I have a need I wish to ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), about.” And I (Musa al-Hannat) would say to him (‘A’idh), “Wait until we meet Him (a.s).” So when we entered upon Him (a.s), we greeted Him (a.s) and sat down. He (a.s) turned his face toward us and began by saying: “Whoever comes to Allah (swt) with what He (swt) has made obligatory upon him, Allah (swt) will not ask him about anything beyond that.” Then ‘A’idh gestured to us. When we stood up, we said to him, “What was your need?” He (‘A’idh) said: “What you just heard.” We said: “How was that your need?” He (‘A’idh) said: “I am a man who cannot endure standing at night in prayer, so I feared that I would be held accountable for it and destroyed.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from one of our companions from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abdillah ibn Muskan. He said:
Someone who asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), narrated to me about a man upon whom many prayers had accumulated. So He (Imam (a.s)) said: “Let them go and start afresh.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي مَنْ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَجْتَمِعُ عَلَيْهِ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ فَقَالَ «أَلْقِهَا وَ اِسْتَأْنِفْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from one of our companions from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abdillah ibn Muskan. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Someone who asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), narrated to me about a man upon whom many prayers had accumulated. So He (Imam (a.s)) said: “Let them go and start afresh.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 11

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d narrated from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from al-Halabi. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “With regard to witr, indeed, Allah (swt) has only made the five (obligatory prayers) obligatory, and witr is not obligatory. If you wish, you may pray it. And leaving it is unbecoming.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« فِي اَلْوَتْرِ إِنَّمَا كَتَبَ اَللَّهُ اَلْخَمْسَ وَ لَيْسَتِ اَلْوَتْرُ مَكْتُوبَةً إِنْ شِئْتَ صَلَّيْتَهَا وَ تَرْكُهَا قَبِيحٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d narrated from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from al-Halabi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “With regard to witr, indeed, Allah (swt) has only made the five (obligatory prayers) obligatory, and witr is not obligatory. If you wish, you may pray it. And leaving it is unbecoming.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 11

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from Mu‘ammar ibn Khallad from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s):
(Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said): “Indeed, Abu al-Hasan (a.s) (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)), whenever He (a.s) was distressed, would leave off the fifty (rak‘ahs).”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ إِذَا اِغْتَمَّ تَرَكَ اَلْخَمْسِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from Mu‘ammar ibn Khallad from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said): “Indeed, Abu al-Hasan (a.s) (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)), whenever He (a.s) was distressed, would leave off the fifty (rak‘ahs).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ali ibn Isma‘il from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri from Ali ibn Asbat from a group of our companions:
Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, whenever He (a.s) was burdened with worry, would leave off the nawafil (supererogatory prayers).
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْبَصْرِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا: أَنَّ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ إِذَا اِهْتَمَّ تَرَكَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ali ibn Isma‘il from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri from Ali ibn Asbat from a group of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, whenever He (a.s) was burdened with worry, would leave off the nawafil (supererogatory prayers).

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Amru ibn Uthman from Ali ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Sinan. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man has upon him missed supererogatory prayers (nawafil) in such number that he does not know how many they are because of their abundance, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Let him pray until he no longer knows how many rak‘ahs he has prayed because of their abundance, then he will have fulfilled what he knows he owes.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he is unable to make them up because of the burden of his preoccupations?” Imam (a.s) said: “If his preoccupations are due to seeking a livelihood which he cannot do without, or due to the need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his preoccupations are worldly matters that have distracted him from prayer, then he must make them up, otherwise he will meet Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, as one who has treated lightly, negligently, and wastefully the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” I (narrator) asked: “If he is unable to make them up, can he give charity (sadaqah) instead?” He (a.s) remained silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.” I (narrator) asked: “How much should he give in charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “According to his means. The minimum is one mudd for each needy person in place of every prayer.” I (narrator) asked: “How many prayers does one mudd become obligatory for?” Imam (a.s) said: “For every two rak‘ahs of night prayer and every two rak‘ahs of day prayer.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he cannot manage that?” Imam (a.s) said: “One mudd for every four rak‘ahs.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he still cannot?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then one mudd for the entire night prayer and one mudd for the day prayer. And prayer is better, and prayer is better.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّوَافِلِ مَالاَ يَدْرِي مَا هُوَ مِنْ كَثْرَتِهِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« فَلْيُصَلِّ حَتَّى لاَ يَدْرِيَ كَمْ صَلَّى مِنْ كَثْرَتِهِ فَيَكُونَ قَدْ قَضَى بِقَدْرِ عِلْمِهِ» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلْقَضَاءِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ شُغُلِهِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ شُغُلُهُ مِنْ طَلَبِ مَعِيشَةٍ لاَ بُدَّ مِنْهَا أَوْ حَاجَةِ أَخٍ مُؤْمِنٍ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ شُغُلُهُ لِدُنْيَا تَشَاغَلَ بِهَا عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْقَضَاءُ وَ إِلاَّ لَقِيَ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مُسْتَخِفّاً مُتَهَاوِناً مُضَيِّعاً لِسُنَّةِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلْقَضَاءِ فَهَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَتَصَدَّقَ فَسَكَتَ مَلِيّاً ثُمَّ قَالَ «نَعَمْ فَلْيَتَصَدَّقْ بِصَدَقَةٍ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا يَتَصَدَّقُ فَقَالَ« بِقَدْرِ طَوْلِهِ وَ أَدْنَى ذَلِكَ مُدٌّ لِكُلِّ مِسْكِينٍ مَكَانَ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ» فَقُلْتُ فَكَمِ اَلصَّلاَةُ اَلَّتِي يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ فِيهَا مُدٌّ لِكُلِّ مِسْكِينٍ فَقَالَ« لِكُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ» فَقُلْتُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ فَقَالَ« مُدٌّ لِكُلِّ أَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ» فَقُلْتُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ فَقَالَ« مُدٌّ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ مُدٌّ لِصَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةُ أَفْضَلُ وَ اَلصَّلاَةُ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Amru ibn Uthman from Ali ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Sinan. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man has upon him missed supererogatory prayers (nawafil) in such number that he does not know how many they are because of their abundance, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Let him pray until he no longer knows how many rak‘ahs he has prayed because of their abundance, then he will have fulfilled what he knows he owes.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he is unable to make them up because of the burden of his preoccupations?” Imam (a.s) said: “If his preoccupations are due to seeking a livelihood which he cannot do without, or due to the need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his preoccupations are worldly matters that have distracted him from prayer, then he must make them up, otherwise he will meet Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, as one who has treated lightly, negligently, and wastefully the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” I (narrator) asked: “If he is unable to make them up, can he give charity (sadaqah) instead?” He (a.s) remained silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.” I (narrator) asked: “How much should he give in charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “According to his means. The minimum is one mudd for each needy person in place of every prayer.” I (narrator) asked: “How many prayers does one mudd become obligatory for?” Imam (a.s) said: “For every two rak‘ahs of night prayer and every two rak‘ahs of day prayer.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he cannot manage that?” Imam (a.s) said: “One mudd for every four rak‘ahs.” I (narrator) asked: “What if he still cannot?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then one mudd for the entire night prayer and one mudd for the day prayer. And prayer is better, and prayer is better.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Non-Obligatory) Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Murazim. He said:
Isma’il ibn Jabir asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), and said: “May Allah (swt) set you right, there are many nawafil (supererogatory prayers) upon me, so what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Make them up.” He (Isma’il) said to him (a.s): “They are more than that.” Imam (a.s) said: “Make them up.” I said: “I cannot count them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Make an estimate.” Murazim then said: I was sick for four months and did not perform nawafil in that time. So I said to Imam (a.s): “May Allah (swt) set you right, or may I be your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not pray nawafil during that period.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no make-up upon you. The sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever overwhelms a person, Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse him in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُرَازِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَابِرٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ أَصْلَحَكَ اَللَّهُ إِنَّ عَلَيَّ نَوَافِلَ كَثِيرَةً فَكَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ فَقَالَ« اِقْضِهَا» فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّهَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ «اِقْضِهَا» قُلْتُ لاَ أُحْصِيهَا قَالَ« تَوَخَّ» قَالَ مُرَازِمٌ وَ كُنْتُ مَرِضْتُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ لَمْ أَتَنَفَّلْ فِيهَا فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَصْلَحَكَ اَللَّهُ أَوْ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي مَرِضْتُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ لَمْ أُصَلِّ نَافِلَةً فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءٌ إِنَّ اَلْمَرِيضَ لَيْسَ كَالصَّحِيحِ كُلُّ مَا غَلَبَ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Murazim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Isma’il ibn Jabir asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), and said: “May Allah (swt) set you right, there are many nawafil (supererogatory prayers) upon me, so what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Make them up.” He (Isma’il) said to him (a.s): “They are more than that.” Imam (a.s) said: “Make them up.” I said: “I cannot count them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Make an estimate.” Murazim then said: I was sick for four months and did not perform nawafil in that time. So I said to Imam (a.s): “May Allah (swt) set you right, or may I be your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not pray nawafil during that period.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no make-up upon you. The sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever overwhelms a person, Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse him in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man intends to travel, when should he shorten (his prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he disappears from the houses.” I asked: “A man intends to travel and departs when the sun has passed its zenith (zawal).” Imam (a.s) said: “When you depart, then pray two rak’ahs.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ مَتَى يُقَصِّرُ فَقَالَ« إِذَا تَوَارَى مِنَ اَلْبُيُوتِ» قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فَيَخْرُجُ حِينَ تَزُولُ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ« إِذَا خَرَجْتَ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man intends to travel, when should he shorten (his prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he disappears from the houses.” I asked: “A man intends to travel and departs when the sun has passed its zenith (zawal).” Imam (a.s) said: “When you depart, then pray two rak’ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 13

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who enters Makkah from his journey and the time of prayer has already entered. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak‘ahs. And if he departs for his journey and the time of prayer has already entered, then he should pray four rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَدْخُلُ مَكَّةَ مِنْ سَفَرِهِ وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَ إِلَى سَفَرِهِ وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَلْيُصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who enters Makkah from his journey and the time of prayer has already entered. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak‘ahs. And if he departs for his journey and the time of prayer has already entered, then he should pray four rak‘ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 13

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he also narrated from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma‘il ibn Jabir. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The time of prayer enters upon me while I am on a journey, so I do not pray until I reach my family.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray and complete the prayer.” I asked: “And if the time of prayer enters upon me while I am with my family, and I intend to travel, so I do not pray until I depart?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then pray and shorten the prayer, and if you do not, then by Allah (swt), you have opposed the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَيْضاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيَّ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَأَنَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَلاَ أُصَلِّي حَتَّى أَدْخُلَ أَهْلِي قَالَ« صَلِّ وَأَتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ» قُلْتُ فَدَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ أَنَا فِي أَهْلِي أُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فَلاَ أُصَلِّي حَتَّى أَخْرُجَ قَالَ« فَصَلِّ وَ قَصِّرْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَقَدْ وَ اَللَّهِ خَالَفْتَ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And he also narrated from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma‘il ibn Jabir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The time of prayer enters upon me while I am on a journey, so I do not pray until I reach my family.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray and complete the prayer.” I asked: “And if the time of prayer enters upon me while I am with my family, and I intend to travel, so I do not pray until I depart?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then pray and shorten the prayer, and if you do not, then by Allah (swt), you have opposed the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 14

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
Imam (a.s) was asked about a man upon whom the time of prayer had entered while he was on a journey, but he delayed the prayer until he arrived (home), intending to pray it after returning to his family, but then he forgot to pray it upon arrival until its time had passed. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray it as two rak’ahs, the prayer of a traveler, because the time entered upon him while he was traveling. It would have been proper for him to pray it at that time.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَيْضاً عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَأَخَّرَ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى قَدِمَ فَهُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَهَا إِذَا قَدِمَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فَنَسِيَ حِينَ قَدِمَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَهَا حَتَّى ذَهَبَ وَقْتُهَا قَالَ« يُصَلِّيهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلاَةَ اَلْمُسَافِرِ لِأَنَّ اَلْوَقْتَ دَخَلَ وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And he also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about a man upon whom the time of prayer had entered while he was on a journey, but he delayed the prayer until he arrived (home), intending to pray it after returning to his family, but then he forgot to pray it upon arrival until its time had passed. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray it as two rak’ahs, the prayer of a traveler, because the time entered upon him while he was traveling. It would have been proper for him to pray it at that time.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 14

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except for Maghrib, which is three.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَيْضاً عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثَلاَثٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And he also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except for Maghrib, which is three.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 14

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he also narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them. He said:
I asked Him (a.s) about supererogatory prayer during travel. Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray anything before the two rak’ahs (of an obligatory prayer), nor after them, during the day.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَيْضاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ تَطَوُّعاً فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ قَبْلَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْئاً نَهَاراً»
thaqalaynSanad: And he also narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about supererogatory prayer during travel. Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray anything before the two rak’ahs (of an obligatory prayer), nor after them, during the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 14

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he narrated from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Halabi. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I prayed Dhuhr as four rak’ahs while I was on a journey.” Imam (a.s) said: “Repeat it (the prayer).”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ أَنَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَالَ« أَعِدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And he narrated from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Halabi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I prayed Dhuhr as four rak’ahs while I was on a journey.” Imam (a.s) said: “Repeat it (the prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 14

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Prayer During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And he narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both:
The Imams (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ: «اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And he narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: The Imams (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 15

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Four rak’ahs after Maghrib, do not abandon them whether at home or while traveling.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ:« أَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لاَ سَفَرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Four rak’ahs after Maghrib, do not abandon them whether at home or while traveling.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 15

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Maskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak’ahs, do not abandon them whether at home or while traveling. And you are not obligated to make up the prayers of the day. But pray the night prayer and make it up (if missed).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّ بَعْدَهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لاَ سَفَرٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اِقْضِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Maskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s).
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak’ahs, do not abandon them whether at home or while traveling. And you are not obligated to make up the prayers of the day. But pray the night prayer and make it up (if missed).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 15

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn Sulayman from Sa’d ibn Sa’d from Muqatil ibn Muqatil from Abu al-Harith. He said:
I (narrator) asked Him (a.s), meaning (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), about the four rak’ahs after Maghrib during travel. The camel driver urges me onward, and I am not able to pray them on the ground, may I pray them in the howdah (riding seat)? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, pray them in the howdah.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ مُقَاتِلٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَارِثِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ يَعْنِي اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْأَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ يُعْجِلُنِي اَلْجَمَّالُ فَلاَ يُمْكِنُنِي اَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ هَلْ أُصَلِّيهَا فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ صَلِّهَا فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn Sulayman from Sa’d ibn Sa’d from Muqatil ibn Muqatil from Abu al-Harith. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Him (a.s), meaning (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), about the four rak’ahs after Maghrib during travel. The camel driver urges me onward, and I am not able to pray them on the ground, may I pray them in the howdah (riding seat)? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, pray them in the howdah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 15

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from Abu al-Hasan (a.s). He said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “Pray the two rak’ahs of the fajr (supererogatory prayer) in the howdah (riding seat).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from Abu al-Hasan (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “Pray the two rak’ahs of the fajr (supererogatory prayer) in the howdah (riding seat).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Maskan from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to me (narrator): “Do not abandon the four rak’ahs after Maghrib whether in travel or at home. And my father (a.s) never used to abandon thirteen rak’ahs at night, whether in travel or at home.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ تَدَعْ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَلاَ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ وَكَانَ أَبِي لاَ يَدَعُ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً بِاللَّيْلِ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ فِي حَضَرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Maskan from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to me (narrator): “Do not abandon the four rak’ahs after Maghrib whether in travel or at home. And my father (a.s) never used to abandon thirteen rak’ahs at night, whether in travel or at home.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
(Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s) used to say: “Indeed, I love to persist in a deed even if it is little.” He (narrator) said: We asked, “Do you make up the night prayer during the day while traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ أَنْ أَدُومَ عَلَى اَلْعَمَلِ وَ إِنْ قَلَّ»» قَالَ قُلْنَا تَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ بِالنَّهَارِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s) used to say: “Indeed, I love to persist in a deed even if it is little.” He (narrator) said: We asked, “Do you make up the night prayer during the day while traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Safwan the camel driver. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) used to pray the night prayer during the day on his mount, in whatever direction it faced.

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), said to me: “Pray the night prayer, the witr, and the two (rak’ahs of fajr) in the howdah (riding seat).”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرَ وَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), said to me: “Pray the night prayer, the witr, and the two (rak’ahs of fajr) in the howdah (riding seat).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Sayf al-Tammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
One of our companions said to me, “We used to make up the day prayers when we stopped between Maghrib and the final ‘ishaʾ.” So Imam (a.s) said: “No. Allah (swt) knows best about His (swt) servants when He (swt) granted them a concession. Allah (swt) has only obligated upon the traveler two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except the night prayer on your camel, in whatever direction it takes you.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ اَلتَّمَّارِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا نَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بَيْنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَاَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ اَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِعِبَادِهِ حِينَ رَخَّصَ لَهُمْ إِنَّمَا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَلَى اَلْمُسَافِرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ لاَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ عَلَى بَعِيرِكَ حَيْثُ تَوَجَّهَ بِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Sayf al-Tammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: One of our companions said to me, “We used to make up the day prayers when we stopped between Maghrib and the final ‘ishaʾ.” So Imam (a.s) said: “No. Allah (swt) knows best about His (swt) servants when He (swt) granted them a concession. Allah (swt) has only obligated upon the traveler two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them and nothing after them, except the night prayer on your camel, in whatever direction it takes you.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Ali ibn al-Hakam, both from Abu Yahya al-Hannat. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about praying the supererogatory prayers during the day while on a journey. Imam (a.s) said: “O my son, if the nawafil (supererogatory prayers) during travel were valid, then the obligatory prayer would have remained complete (four rak’ahs).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ أَبِي يَحْيَى اَلْحَنَّاطِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّافِلَةِ بِالنَّهَارِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« يَا بُنَيَّ لَوْ صَلَحَتِ اَلنَّافِلَةُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ تَمَّتِ اَلْفَرِيضَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Ali ibn al-Hakam, both from Abu Yahya al-Hannat. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about praying the supererogatory prayers during the day while on a journey. Imam (a.s) said: “O my son, if the nawafil (supererogatory prayers) during travel were valid, then the obligatory prayer would have remained complete (four rak’ahs).”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Safwan ibn Yahya. He said:
I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), about performing supererogatory prayers during the day while I am traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “No, but you may make up the night prayer during the day while you are traveling.” I asked: “May I be your ransom, the daytime prayers that I perform while at home, should I make them up during the day while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for me, I do not make them up.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشْيَمَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَأَنَا فِي سَفَرٍ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ تَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَأَنْتَ فِي سَفَرٍ» فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ اَلَّتِي أُصَلِّيهَا فِي اَلْحَضَرِ أَقْضِيهَا بِالنَّهَارِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا أَنَا فَلاَ أَقْضِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Safwan ibn Yahya. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), about performing supererogatory prayers during the day while I am traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “No, but you may make up the night prayer during the day while you are traveling.” I asked: “May I be your ransom, the daytime prayers that I perform while at home, should I make them up during the day while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for me, I do not make them up.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for the report narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I make up the day prayers at night while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Isma’il ibn Jabir said to Him (a.s): “May I make up the day prayers at night while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” So he (Isma’il) said: “But you just said ‘Yes’!” Imam (a.s) replied: “That one is capable, and you are not capable.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا اَلْخَبَرُ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ لَهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَابِرٍ أَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« لاَ» فَقَالَ إِنَّكَ قُلْتَ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ ذَاكَ يُطِيقُ وَ أَنْتَ لاَ تُطِيقُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for the report narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I make up the day prayers at night while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Isma’il ibn Jabir said to Him (a.s): “May I make up the day prayers at night while on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” So he (Isma’il) said: “But you just said ‘Yes’!” Imam (a.s) replied: “That one is capable, and you are not capable.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Maskan from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I asked you about making up the day prayers at night while on a journey, and you said, ‘Do not make them up.’ But your companions asked you, and you said, ‘Make them up.’” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Should I say to them, ‘Do not pray’? And I dislike saying to them, ‘Do not pray.’ By Allah (swt), that is not required of them.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ قَضَاءِ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقُلْتَ« لاَ تَقْضِيهَا» وَسَأَلَكَ أَصْحَابُنَا فَقُلْتَ« اِقْضُوا» فَقَالَ لِي« أَ فَأَقُولُ لَهُمْ لاَ تُصَلُّوا وَ إِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَقُولَ لَهُمْ لاَ تُصَلُّوا وَ اَللَّهِ مَا ذَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Maskan from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I asked you about making up the day prayers at night while on a journey, and you said, ‘Do not make them up.’ But your companions asked you, and you said, ‘Make them up.’” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Should I say to them, ‘Do not pray’? And I dislike saying to them, ‘Do not pray.’ By Allah (swt), that is not required of them.”

chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for the report narrated by al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hanan ibn Sadir from Sadir, he said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s) used to make up the daytime nawafil (supererogatory prayers) at night while on a journey, and He (a.s) would never complete (four rak’ahs of) an obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا اَلْخَبَرُ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ عَنْ سَدِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «كَانَ أَبِي يَقْضِي فِي اَلسَّفَرِ نَوَافِلَ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ لاَ يُتِمُّ صَلاَةً فَرِيضَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for the report narrated by al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hanan ibn Sadir from Sadir, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s) used to make up the daytime nawafil (supererogatory prayers) at night while on a journey, and He (a.s) would never complete (four rak’ahs of) an obligatory prayer.”
