chapter: Chapter on Recommended (Nafl) Prayers During Travel
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Amru ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
He (a.s) was asked about a man upon whom the sun has passed the meridian (zawal) while he is still in his home, then he sets out for travel. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin with the zawal nafilah, so he prays it. Then he prays the Dhuhr prayer shortened, two rak’ahs, because he departed from his home before the time of Dhuhr had fully arrived.” Then He (a.s) was asked: “And what if he left after the time of Dhuhr had already arrived?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he prays Dhuhr as four rak’ahs, and afterward he prays the nawafil, eight rak’ahs, because he left his home after the time of Dhuhr had entered. Then when the time of ‘asr enters, he prays ‘asr shortened, two rak’ahs, because he had departed on his journey before the time of ‘asr had entered.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ هُوَ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ فِي سَفَرٍ قَالَ« يَبْدَأُ بِالزَّوَالِ فَيُصَلِّيهَا ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى بِتَقْصِيرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ لِأَنَّهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ اَلْأُولَى» وَ سُئِلَ فَإِنْ خَرَجَ بَعْدَ مَا حَضَرَتِ اَلْأُولَى قَالَ« يُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي بَعْدُ اَلنَّوَافِلَ ثَمَانَ رَكَعَاتٍ لِأَنَّهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ بَعْدَمَا حَضَرَتِ اَلْأُولَى فَإِذَا حَضَرَتِ اَلْعَصْرُ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ بِتَقْصِيرٍ وَ هِيَ رَكْعَتَانِ لِأَنَّهُ خَرَجَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ اَلْعَصْرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Amru ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: He (a.s) was asked about a man upon whom the sun has passed the meridian (zawal) while he is still in his home, then he sets out for travel. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin with the zawal nafilah, so he prays it. Then he prays the Dhuhr prayer shortened, two rak’ahs, because he departed from his home before the time of Dhuhr had fully arrived.” Then He (a.s) was asked: “And what if he left after the time of Dhuhr had already arrived?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he prays Dhuhr as four rak’ahs, and afterward he prays the nawafil, eight rak’ahs, because he left his home after the time of Dhuhr had entered. Then when the time of ‘asr enters, he prays ‘asr shortened, two rak’ahs, because he had departed on his journey before the time of ‘asr had entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 18

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Umar ibn Aban from Sa’id ibn al-Hasan. He said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The beginning of the time (for Dhuhr) is the sun’s passing the meridian (zawal), and that is the first time of Allah (swt), and it is the best of the two times.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبَانٍ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتِ زَوَالُ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ هُوَ وَقْتُ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَوَّلُ وَ هُوَ أَفْضَلُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Umar ibn Aban from Sa’id ibn al-Hasan. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The beginning of the time (for Dhuhr) is the sun’s passing the meridian (zawal), and that is the first time of Allah (swt), and it is the best of the two times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 19

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, all from Al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "When the sun passes the meridian, the time for both Dhuhr and ‘Asr has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you remain in the time for both of them together until the sun sets."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ وَ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ وَاَلْعَصْرِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ دَخَلَ اَلظُّهْرُ وَ اَلْعَصْرُ جَمِيعاً إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ ثُمَّ أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتٍ مِنْهُمَا جَمِيعاً حَتَّى تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, all from Al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "When the sun passes the meridian, the time for both Dhuhr and ‘Asr has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you remain in the time for both of them together until the sun sets."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 19

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
I asked him about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. He said: “The time of Dhuhr is from when the sun declines (from the meridian) until the shadow reaches the length of one forearm, and the time of ‘Asr is from one and a half forearms to two forearms.”
arabicText: وعنه عن يعقوب بن يزيد عن الحسن بن علي الوشا عن أحمد بن عمر عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال سألته عن وقت الظهر والعصر فقال وقت الظهر إذا زاغت الشمس الى أن يذهب الظل قامة ووقت العصر قامة ونصف الى قامتين
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. He said: “The time of Dhuhr is from when the sun declines (from the meridian) until the shadow reaches the length of one forearm, and the time of ‘Asr is from one and a half forearms to two forearms.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed with the people Dhuhr and ‘Asr when the sun had passed the meridian, in congregation, without any excuse.
arabicText: وعنه عن أبي جعفر أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن عبد الله بن بكير عن زرارة عن أبي عبد الله ع قال صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله بالناس الظهر والعصر حين زالت الشمس في جماعة من غير علة
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja‘far Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed with the people Dhuhr and ‘Asr when the sun had passed the meridian, in congregation, without any excuse.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
(Imam (a.s) said): “When the sun passes the meridian, the time of both prayers, Dhuhr and ‘Asr, enters, and when the sun sets, the time of both prayers, Maghrib and ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah, enters. As for that which indicates the other type (of timing), it is the time for one who performs the supererogatory (nawafil) prayers.”
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن الحسين عن الحكم بن مسكين عن النضر ابن سويد عن عبد الله بن بكير عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إذا زالت الشمس دخل الوقتان الظهر والعصر وإذا غابت الشمس دخل الوقتان المغرب والعشاء الآخرة وأما الذي يدل على الضرب الآخر وهو وقت من يصلي النوافل
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said): “When the sun passes the meridian, the time of both prayers, Dhuhr and ‘Asr, enters, and when the sun sets, the time of both prayers, Maghrib and ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah, enters. As for that which indicates the other type (of timing), it is the time for one who performs the supererogatory (nawafil) prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and Imam (a.s) said: “One forearm's length (of shadow) from the sun's zenith; and the time of ‘Asr is one forearm's length from the time of Dhuhr, so that makes four forearms from the sun’s zenith. And Zurarah said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), said to me when I asked Him (a.s) about that: “The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was a man's height, and when the shadow from it extended one forearm, he would pray Dhuhr, and when the shadow extended two forearms, he would pray ‘Asr.” Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know why one forearm and two forearms were appointed?" I said: “Why was that set?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because of the supererogatory prayers. For you are allowed to perform supererogatory prayers from the sun’s zenith until the shadow reaches one forearm in length; and when your shadow reaches one forearm from the zenith, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.” Ibn Miskan said: “And Sulayman ibn Khalid and Abu Basir al-Muradi and Husayn, the one with the caps, and Ibn Abi Ya’fur, and others whom I cannot enumerate, also narrated to me regarding the one forearm and the two forearms.” And in this narration, there is a clear indication of what we have based this chapter upon, that these times were designated for the purpose of offering the supererogatory prayers.
arabicText: ما رواه الحسين بن سعيد عن محمد بن سنان عن ابن مسكان عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن وقت الظهر فقال ذراع من زوال الشمس ووقت العصر ذراع من وقت الظهر فذلك أربعة أقدام من زوال الشمس وقال زرارة قال لي أبو جعفر ع حين سألته عن ذلك إن حايط مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله كان قامة فكان إذا مضى من فيئه ذراع صلى الظهر وإذا مضى من فيئه ذراعان صلى العصر ثم قال أتدري لم جعل الذراع والذراعان؟ قلت لم جعل ذلك؟ قال لمكان النافلة فان لك ان تنتفل من زوال الشمس الى أن يمضي الفئ ذراعا فإذا بلغ فيئك ذراعا من الزوال بدأت بالفريضة وتركت النافلة قال ابن مسكان وحدثني بالذراع والذراعين سليمان بن خالد وأبو بصير المرادي وحسين صاحب القلانس وابن أبي يعفور ومن لا أحصيه منهم وفي هذا الخبر تصريح بما عقدنا عليه الباب ان هذه الاوقات إنما جعلت لمكان النافلة
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and Imam (a.s) said: “One forearm's length (of shadow) from the sun's zenith; and the time of ‘Asr is one forearm's length from the time of Dhuhr, so that makes four forearms from the sun’s zenith. And Zurarah said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), said to me when I asked Him (a.s) about that: “The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was a man's height, and when the shadow from it extended one forearm, he would pray Dhuhr, and when the shadow extended two forearms, he would pray ‘Asr.” Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know why one forearm and two forearms were appointed?" I said: “Why was that set?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because of the supererogatory prayers. For you are allowed to perform supererogatory prayers from the sun’s zenith until the shadow reaches one forearm in length; and when your shadow reaches one forearm from the zenith, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.” Ibn Miskan said: “And Sulayman ibn Khalid and Abu Basir al-Muradi and Husayn, the one with the caps, and Ibn Abi Ya’fur, and others whom I cannot enumerate, also narrated to me regarding the one forearm and the two forearms.” And in this narration, there is a clear indication of what we have based this chapter upon, that these times were designated for the purpose of offering the supererogatory prayers.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Indeed, ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us with a timing from you.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Then he does not lie upon us.” I (narrator) said: “He (ibn Hanzalah) mentioned that you said: ‘Verily, the first prayer that Allah (swt), the Exalted, made obligatory upon His Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was Dhuhr, and it is the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Establish the prayer at the declining of the sun’ (Surah Isra 17:78). So when the sun passes the meridian, nothing prevents you (from praying) except your tasbih (supererogatory prayer), and you remain in the time of Dhuhr until the shadow becomes one forearm’s length, and that is the end of the time. Then when the shadow becomes one forearm, the time of ‘Asr enters, and you remain in the time of ‘Asr until the shadow becomes two forearms, and that is the evening.” Imam (a.s) said: “He (ibn Hanzalah) has spoken the truth.”
arabicText: وروى محمد بن يعقوب عن علي بن إبراهيم عن محمد بن عيسى عن يونس عن يزيد بن خليفة قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام ان عمر بن حنظلة أتانا عنك بوقت فقال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إذن لا يكذب علينا قلت ذكر انك قلت ان أول صلاة افترضها الله تعالى على نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله الظهر وهو قول الله عزوجل أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس فإذا زالت الشمس لم يمنعك الا سبحتك ثم لا تزال في وقت الظهر الى أن يصير الظل قامة وهو آخر الوقت فإذا صار الظل قامة دخل وقت العصر فلم تزل في وقت العصر حتى يصير الظل قامتين وذلك المساء قال صدق
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Indeed, ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us with a timing from you.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Then he does not lie upon us.” I (narrator) said: “He (ibn Hanzalah) mentioned that you said: ‘Verily, the first prayer that Allah (swt), the Exalted, made obligatory upon His Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was Dhuhr, and it is the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Establish the prayer at the declining of the sun’ (Surah Isra 17:78). So when the sun passes the meridian, nothing prevents you (from praying) except your tasbih (supererogatory prayer), and you remain in the time of Dhuhr until the shadow becomes one forearm’s length, and that is the end of the time. Then when the shadow becomes one forearm, the time of ‘Asr enters, and you remain in the time of ‘Asr until the shadow becomes two forearms, and that is the evening.” Imam (a.s) said: “He (ibn Hanzalah) has spoken the truth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from his father, from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr has entered, except that there is a supererogatory prayer before it, and that is up to you, if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it.”
arabicText: وعنه عن محمد بن يحيى عن سلمة بن الخطاب عن علي بن سيف ابن عميرة عن أبيه عن عمر بن حنظلة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: إذا زالت الشمس فقد دخل وقت الظهر إلا أن بين يديها سبحة وذلك إليك إن شئت طولت وإن شئت قصرت
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from his father, from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr has entered, except that there is a supererogatory prayer before it, and that is up to you, if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 22

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash’ari narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from Isma’il al-Ju’fi, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the shadow of the wall reached one forearm, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr, and when it reached two forearms, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr.” I asked: “The walls differ, some are short and some are tall.” Imam (a.s) said: “The wall of the Prophet’s mosque, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at that time was one man's height.”
arabicText: وروى محمد بن أحمد بن يحيى الاشعري عن العباس بن معروف عن صفوان بن يحيى عن اسحاق بن عمار عن إسماعيل الجعفي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله إذا كان فئ الجدار ذراعا صلى الظهر وإذا كان ذراعين صلى العصر قال قلت: ان الجدار يختلف بعضها قصير وبعضها طويل فقال: كان جدار مسجد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله يومئذ قامة
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash’ari narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from Isma’il al-Ju’fi, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the shadow of the wall reached one forearm, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr, and when it reached two forearms, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr.” I asked: “The walls differ, some are short and some are tall.” Imam (a.s) said: “The wall of the Prophet’s mosque, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at that time was one man's height.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 22

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Isma’il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “After the sun passes the meridian by one foot or something close to that, except on the day of Jumu’ah or during travel, for its time is at the moment of decline.”
arabicText: وروى الحسين بن سعيد عن فضالة عن حسين بن عثمان عن عبد الله بن مسكان عن إسماعيل بن عبد الخالق قال: سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن وقت الظهر فقال: بعد الزوال بقدم أو نحو ذلك إلا في يوم الجمعة أو في السفر فان وقتها حين نزول
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Isma’il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “After the sun passes the meridian by one foot or something close to that, except on the day of Jumu’ah or during travel, for its time is at the moment of decline.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 22

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from ‘Isa ibn Abi Mansur, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to me: “When the sun passes the meridian, and you have prayed your supererogatory prayer, then the time for Dhuhr has entered.”
arabicText: وعنه عن فضالة عن حماد بن عثمان عن عيسى بن أبي منصور قال قال لي أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إذا زالت الشمس فصليت سبحتك فقد دخل وقت الظهر
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from ‘Isa ibn Abi Mansur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to me: “When the sun passes the meridian, and you have prayed your supererogatory prayer, then the time for Dhuhr has entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 23

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of the Dhuhr and ‘Asr prayers, so He (a.s) wrote: “One forearm’s length (of shadow) for Dhuhr, and one forearm’s length for ‘Asr.”
arabicText: وعنه عن أحمد بن محمد قال سألته عن وقت صلاة الظهر والعصر فكتب قامة للظهر وقامة للعصر
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of the Dhuhr and ‘Asr prayers, so He (a.s) wrote: “One forearm’s length (of shadow) for Dhuhr, and one forearm’s length for ‘Asr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 23

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during intense heat, but He (a.s) did not answer me. Then, sometime afterward, Imam (a.s) said to ‘Amr ibn Sa’id ibn Hilal: “Zurarah asked me about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during intense heat, and I did not inform him, and I felt uneasy about that. So convey my greetings to him and say to him: ‘When your shadow becomes equal to your height, then pray Dhuhr; and when your shadow becomes twice your height, then pray ‘Asr.’”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فِي اَلْقَيْظِ فَلَمْ يُجِبْنِي فَلَمَّا أَنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لِعَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ« إِنَّ زُرَارَةَ سَأَلَنِي عَنْ وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فِي اَلْقَيْظِ فَلَمْ أُخْبِرْهُ فَحَرِجْتُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَقْرِئْهُ مِنِّي اَلسَّلاَمَ وَ قُلْ لَهُ إِذَا كَانَ ظِلُّكَ مِثْلَكَ فَصَلِّ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ إِذَا كَانَ ظِلُّكَ مِثْلَيْكَ فَصَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during intense heat, but He (a.s) did not answer me. Then, sometime afterward, Imam (a.s) said to ‘Amr ibn Sa’id ibn Hilal: “Zurarah asked me about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during intense heat, and I did not inform him, and I felt uneasy about that. So convey my greetings to him and say to him: ‘When your shadow becomes equal to your height, then pray Dhuhr; and when your shadow becomes twice your height, then pray ‘Asr.’”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu’lu’i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri and ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
(Narrator said) ‘We used to measure the sun in Medina by the forearm. So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to us: “Shall I not inform you of something clearer than this?”’ They said: “Yes, may we be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, then the time for Dhuhr has entered, except that there is a supererogatory prayer before it, and that is up to you. So if you shorten your supererogatory prayer, then (the time for Dhuhr begins) when you finish your supererogatory prayer, and if you lengthen it, then (it begins) when you finish your supererogatory prayer.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَللُّؤْلُؤِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ اَلنَّصْرِيِّ وَ عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالُوا: كُنَّا نَعْتَبِرُ اَلشَّمْسَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ بِالذِّرَاعِ فَقَالَ لَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَ لاَ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِأَبْيَنَ مِنْ هَذَا» قَالُوا بَلَى جَعَلَنَا اَللَّهُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا سُبْحَةً وَ ذَلِكَ إِلَيْكَ فَإِنْ أَنْتَ خَفَّفْتَ سُبْحَتَكَ فَحِينَ تَفْرُغُ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ وَ إِنْ أَنْتَ طَوَّلْتَ فَحِينَ تَفْرُغُ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu’lu’i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri and ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Narrator said) ‘We used to measure the sun in Medina by the forearm. So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to us: “Shall I not inform you of something clearer than this?”’ They said: “Yes, may we be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, then the time for Dhuhr has entered, except that there is a supererogatory prayer before it, and that is up to you. So if you shorten your supererogatory prayer, then (the time for Dhuhr begins) when you finish your supererogatory prayer, and if you lengthen it, then (it begins) when you finish your supererogatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 23

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “The ‘qamah’ and the two ‘qamahs’, the ‘dhira’ and the two ‘dhiras’, are (equivalent) in the Book of Ali (a.s), peace be upon him.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْقَامَةُ وَ اَلْقَامَتَانِ اَلذِّرَاعُ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَانِ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “The ‘qamah’ and the two ‘qamahs’, the ‘dhira’ and the two ‘dhiras’, are (equivalent) in the Book of Ali (a.s), peace be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 24

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The ‘qamah’ is the ‘dhira’.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« اَلْقَامَةُ هِيَ اَلذِّرَاعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The ‘qamah’ is the ‘dhira’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 24

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Abu Basir said to Him (a.s): “How much is a ‘qamah’?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘dhira’ (forearm). Indeed, the ‘qamah’ of the saddle of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was a ‘dhira’.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: قَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ كَمِ اَلْقَامَةُ قَالَ فَقَالَ« ذِرَاعٌ إِنَّ قَامَةَ رَحْلِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَتْ ذِرَاعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Basir said to Him (a.s): “How much is a ‘qamah’?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘dhira’ (forearm). Indeed, the ‘qamah’ of the saddle of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was a ‘dhira’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 24

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Sa’id, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s), peace be upon him, about what came in the hadith: ‘Pray ‘Asr when the sun is at one qamah (height), two qamahs, one dhira (forearm), two dhiras, one qadam (foot), two qadams, from this and from that’, so when is this, and how is this, while at some times the shadow is only half a qadam?” Imam (a.s) said: ‘Indeed, he said ‘the shadow of the qamah’ and did not say ‘the qamah of the shadow’, because the shadow of the qamah varies, sometimes it increases, sometimes it decreases, while the qamah (the standing height) remains a qamah forever, it does not change.’ Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘One dhira and two dhiras, one qadam and two qadams, so the one dhira and two dhiras are the explanation of the qamah and the two qamahs during the time when the shadow of the qamah is one dhira, and the shadow of the two qamahs is two dhiras. Thus, the shadow of the qamah and the two qamahs, and the dhira and the two dhiras, are consistent in every time, known, and explained, one interpreted by the other, supported by it. So when the time is such that the shadow of the qamah is a dhira, then the time is a dhira of the shadow of the qamah, and the qamah is a dhira of the shadow. And if the shadow of the qamah is less or more, then the time is confined to the dhira and the two dhiras. This is the explanation of the qamah and the two qamahs, and the dhira and the two dhiras.”’
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ صَالِحِ اِبْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّا جَاءَ فِي اَلْحَدِيثِ« أَنْ صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ إِذَا كَانَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ قَامَةً وَ قَامَتَيْنِ وَ ذِرَاعاً وَ ذِرَاعَيْنِ وَ قَدَماً وَ قَدَمَيْنِ مِنْ هَذَا وَ مِنْ هَذَا» فَمَتَى هَذَا وَ كَيْفَ هَذَا وَ قَدْ يَكُونُ اَلظِّلُّ فِي بَعْضِ اَلْأَوْقَاتِ نِصْفَ قَدَمٍ قَالَ« إِنَّمَا قَالَ ظِلُّ اَلْقَامَةِ وَ لَمْ يَقُلْ قَامَةُ اَلظِّلِّ وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ ظِلَّ اَلْقَامَةِ يَخْتَلِفُ مَرَّةً وَ يَكْثُرُ مَرَّةً وَ يَقِلُّ وَ اَلْقَامَةُ قَامَةٌ أَبَداً لاَ تَخْتَلِفُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« ذِرَاعٌ وَ ذِرَاعَانِ وَ قَدَمٌ وَ قَدَمَانِ فَصَارَ ذِرَاعٌ وَ ذِرَاعَانِ تَفْسِيرَ اَلْقَامَةِ وَاَلْقَامَتَيْنِ فِي اَلزَّمَانِ اَلَّذِي يَكُونُ فِيهِ ظِلُّ اَلْقَامَةِ ذِرَاعاً وَظِلُّ اَلْقَامَتَيْنِ ذِرَاعَيْنِ فَيَكُونُ ظِلُّ اَلْقَامَةِ وَاَلْقَامَتَيْنِ وَاَلذِّرَاعِ وَاَلذِّرَاعَيْنِ مُتَّفِقَيْنِ فِي كُلِّ زَمَانٍ مَعْرُوفَيْنِ مُفَسَّراً أَحَدُهُمَا بِالْآخَرِ مُسَدَّداً بِهِ فَإِذَا كَانَ اَلزَّمَانُ يَكُونُ فِيهِ ظِلُّ اَلْقَامَةِ ذِرَاعاً كَانَ اَلْوَقْتُ ذِرَاعاً مِنْ ظِلِّ اَلْقَامَةِ وَكَانَتِ اَلْقَامَةُ ذِرَاعاً مِنَ اَلظِّلِّ وَإِذَا كَانَ ظِلُّ اَلْقَامَةِ أَقَلَّ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ كَانَ اَلْوَقْتُ مَحْصُوراً بِالذِّرَاعِ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَيْنِ فَهَذَا تَفْسِيرُ اَلْقَامَةِ وَ اَلْقَامَتَيْنِ وَ اَلذِّرَاعِ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Sa’id, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s), peace be upon him, about what came in the hadith: ‘Pray ‘Asr when the sun is at one qamah (height), two qamahs, one dhira (forearm), two dhiras, one qadam (foot), two qadams, from this and from that’, so when is this, and how is this, while at some times the shadow is only half a qadam?” Imam (a.s) said: ‘Indeed, he said ‘the shadow of the qamah’ and did not say ‘the qamah of the shadow’, because the shadow of the qamah varies, sometimes it increases, sometimes it decreases, while the qamah (the standing height) remains a qamah forever, it does not change.’ Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘One dhira and two dhiras, one qadam and two qadams, so the one dhira and two dhiras are the explanation of the qamah and the two qamahs during the time when the shadow of the qamah is one dhira, and the shadow of the two qamahs is two dhiras. Thus, the shadow of the qamah and the two qamahs, and the dhira and the two dhiras, are consistent in every time, known, and explained, one interpreted by the other, supported by it. So when the time is such that the shadow of the qamah is a dhira, then the time is a dhira of the shadow of the qamah, and the qamah is a dhira of the shadow. And if the shadow of the qamah is less or more, then the time is confined to the dhira and the two dhiras. This is the explanation of the qamah and the two qamahs, and the dhira and the two dhiras.”’

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 25

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, all from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for both Dhuhr and ‘Asr enters, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you remain within the time of both of them together until the sun sets.”
arabicText: ما رواه سعد بن عبد الله عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى عن الحسين بن سعيد ومحمد بن خالد البرقي والعباس بن معروف جميعا عن القاسم بن عروة عن عبيد بن زرارة قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن وقت الظهر والعصر فقال إذا زالت الشمس دخل وقت الظهر والعصر جميعا إلا أن هذه قبل هذه ثم أنت في وقت منهما جميعا حتى تغيب الشمس
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, all from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for both Dhuhr and ‘Asr enters, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you remain within the time of both of them together until the sun sets.”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The most beloved time to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, is its beginning, when the time of prayer enters. So perform the obligatory prayer. But if you do not do so, then you are still within the time of both of them until the sun sets.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «أَحَبُّ اَلْوَقْتِ إِلَى اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ أَوَّلُهُ حِينَ يَدْخُلُ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَصَلِّ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَإِنَّكَ فِي وَقْتٍ مِنْهُمَا حَتَّى تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The most beloved time to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, is its beginning, when the time of prayer enters. So perform the obligatory prayer. But if you do not do so, then you are still within the time of both of them until the sun sets.”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, and he is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time of Dhuhr has entered until the amount of time passes in which a person can pray four rak’ahs. When that has passed, then the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr both have entered, and that continues until there remains from the sun’s presence the amount of time needed to pray four rak’ahs. When that amount of time remains, then the time of Dhuhr has ended and the time of ‘Asr remains until the sun sets.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي يَزِيدَ وَ هُوَ دَاوُدُ بْنُ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ مِقْدَارُ مَا صَلَّى اَلْمُصَلِّي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا مَضَى ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ حَتَّى يَبْقَى مِنَ اَلشَّمْسِ مِقْدَارُ مَا يُصَلِّي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا بَقِيَ مِقْدَارُ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ خَرَجَ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ بَقِيَ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ حَتَّى تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, and he is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time of Dhuhr has entered until the amount of time passes in which a person can pray four rak’ahs. When that has passed, then the time of Dhuhr and ‘Asr both have entered, and that continues until there remains from the sun’s presence the amount of time needed to pray four rak’ahs. When that amount of time remains, then the time of Dhuhr has ended and the time of ‘Asr remains until the sun sets.”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Tha’labah ibn Maymun, from Ma’mar ibn Yahya, who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: “The time of ‘Asr is until the setting of the sun.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ إِلَى غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Tha’labah ibn Maymun, from Ma’mar ibn Yahya, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: “The time of ‘Asr is until the setting of the sun.”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Zayd, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said regarding the saying of the Most High: ‘Establish the prayer at the declining of the sun until the darkness of the night”’ (Surah Isra 17:78). Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, made four prayers obligatory, the beginning of whose time is from the sun’s decline until midnight. Among them are two prayers whose beginning time is from the sun’s decline until sunset, except that this one is before that one. And among them are two prayers whose beginning time is from sunset until midnight, except that this one is before that one.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلضَّحَّاكِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى« أَقِمِ اَلصَّلاٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلىٰ غَسَقِ اَللَّيْلِ» قَالَ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى اِفْتَرَضَ أَرْبَعَ صَلَوَاتٍُ أَوَّلُ وَقْتِهَا مِنْ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى اِنْتِصَافِ اَللَّيْلِ مِنْهَا صَلاَتَانِ أَوَّلُ وَقْتِهِمَا مِنْ عِنْدِ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ وَ مِنْهَا صَلاَتَانِ أَوَّلُ وَقْتِهِمَا مِنْ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى اِنْتِصَافِ اَللَّيْلِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Zayd, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said regarding the saying of the Most High: ‘Establish the prayer at the declining of the sun until the darkness of the night”’ (Surah Isra 17:78). Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, made four prayers obligatory, the beginning of whose time is from the sun’s decline until midnight. Among them are two prayers whose beginning time is from the sun’s decline until sunset, except that this one is before that one. And among them are two prayers whose beginning time is from sunset until midnight, except that this one is before that one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 27

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for the two prayers, Dhuhr and ‘Asr, has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you are within the time for both of them until the sun sets.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ اَلظُّهْرِ وَاَلْعَصْرِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ ثُمَّ أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتٍ مِنْهُمَا حَتَّى تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian, the time for the two prayers, Dhuhr and ‘Asr, has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr). Then you are within the time for both of them until the sun sets.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 27

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s): “When does the time of Dhuhr begin?” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian.” I asked: “When does its time end?” Imam (a.s) said: “After four forearms (aqdam) have passed from its zenith. Verily, the time of Dhuhr is narrow, not like other times.” I asked: “When does the time of ‘Asr begin?” Imam (a.s) said: “The end of the time of Dhuhr is the beginning of the time of ‘Asr.” I asked: “When does the time of ‘Asr end?” Imam (a.s) said: “The time of ‘Asr is until the sun sets, and that is in case of an excuse, and it is a form of negligence.” I said to him: “If a man were to pray Dhuhr after four forearms had passed from the sun's zenith, would he be considered, in your view, as not having fulfilled it?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he did that deliberately to oppose the Sunnah and the prescribed time, it would not be accepted from him, just as if a man were to delay ‘Asr until it is near sunset, deliberately, without excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Verily, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, assigned times for the obligatory prayers and set boundaries for them in his Sunnah for the people. So whoever turns away from one of his obligatory Sunnahs is like one who turns away from the obligations of Allah (swt), the Exalted.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْكَرْخِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَ مَتَى يَدْخُلُ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ قَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ» فَقُلْتُ مَتَى يَخْرُجُ وَقْتُهَا فَقَالَ« مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا يَمْضِي مِنْ زَوَالِهَا أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ إِنَّ وَقْتَ اَلظُّهْرِ ضَيِّقٌ لَيْسَ كَغَيْرِهِ» قُلْتُ فَمَتَى يَدْخُلُ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ آخِرَ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ هُوَ أَوَّلُ وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ» فَقُلْتُ فَمَتَى يَخْرُجُ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ فَقَالَ« وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ إِلَى أَنْ تَغْرُبَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلَّةٍ وَ هُوَ تَضْيِيعٌ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ بَعْدَ مَا يَمْضِي مِنْ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ أَ كَانَ عِنْدَكَ غَيْرَ مُؤَدٍّ لَهَا فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ تَعَمَّدَ ذَلِكَ لِيُخَالِفَ اَلسُّنَّةَ وَ اَلْوَقْتَ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ مِنْهُ كَمَا لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً أَخَّرَ اَلْعَصْرَ إِلَى قُرْبِ أَنْ تَغْرُبَ اَلشَّمْسُ مُتَعَمِّداً مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ مِنْهُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ ص قَدْ وَقَّتَ لِلصَّلَوَاتِ اَلْمَفْرُوضَاتِ أَوْقَاتاً وَ حَدَّ لَهَا حُدُوداً فِي سُنَّتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ فَمَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ سُنَّةٍ مِنْ سُنَنِهِ اَلْمُوجَبَاتِ كَانَ مِثْلَ مَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ فَرَائِضِ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s): “When does the time of Dhuhr begin?” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes the meridian.” I asked: “When does its time end?” Imam (a.s) said: “After four forearms (aqdam) have passed from its zenith. Verily, the time of Dhuhr is narrow, not like other times.” I asked: “When does the time of ‘Asr begin?” Imam (a.s) said: “The end of the time of Dhuhr is the beginning of the time of ‘Asr.” I asked: “When does the time of ‘Asr end?” Imam (a.s) said: “The time of ‘Asr is until the sun sets, and that is in case of an excuse, and it is a form of negligence.” I said to him: “If a man were to pray Dhuhr after four forearms had passed from the sun's zenith, would he be considered, in your view, as not having fulfilled it?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he did that deliberately to oppose the Sunnah and the prescribed time, it would not be accepted from him, just as if a man were to delay ‘Asr until it is near sunset, deliberately, without excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Verily, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, assigned times for the obligatory prayers and set boundaries for them in his Sunnah for the people. So whoever turns away from one of his obligatory Sunnahs is like one who turns away from the obligations of Allah (swt), the Exalted.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 27

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated it with a raised chain from Sama’ah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, when is the time of prayer?” He (a.s) began turning to the right and left, as if he were looking for something. When I saw that, I picked up a stick and said: “Is this what you are looking for?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then He (a.s) took the stick and set it upright facing the sun, and said: “When the sun rises, the shadow is long, and it continues to decrease until the sun passes the meridian. When it passes the meridian, it begins to increase again. When you clearly see the increase, then pray Dhuhr. Then wait the time it takes for one forearm, and pray ‘Asr.”
arabicText: فَقَدْ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى رَفَعَهُ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَتَى وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَأَقْبَلَ يَلْتَفِتُ يَمِيناً وَ شِمَالاً كَأَنَّهُ يَطْلُبُ شَيْئاً فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُ ذَلِكَ تَنَاوَلْتُ عُوداً فَقُلْتُ هَذَا تَطْلُبُ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» فَأَخَذَ اَلْعُودَ فَنَصَبَ بِحِيَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّ اَلشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَتْ كَانَ اَلْفَيْءُ طَوِيلاً ثُمَّ لاَ يَزَالُ يَنْقُصُ حَتَّى تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا زَالَتْ زَادَتْ فَإِذَا اِسْتَبَنْتَ اَلزِّيَادَةَ فَصَلِّ اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ تَمَهَّلْ قَدْرَ ذِرَاعٍ وَ صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated it with a raised chain from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, when is the time of prayer?” He (a.s) began turning to the right and left, as if he were looking for something. When I saw that, I picked up a stick and said: “Is this what you are looking for?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then He (a.s) took the stick and set it upright facing the sun, and said: “When the sun rises, the shadow is long, and it continues to decrease until the sun passes the meridian. When it passes the meridian, it begins to increase again. When you clearly see the increase, then pray Dhuhr. Then wait the time it takes for one forearm, and pray ‘Asr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 28

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama’ah narrated from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
The ‘zawal’ (sun’s meridian) was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (a.s), so Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “You take a stick whose length is three spans (‘shibr’), and if it is longer, that is clearer. It should be erected upright. As long as you see the shadow decreasing, the sun has not yet passed the meridian. But when the shadow begins to increase after its decrease, then the sun has passed the meridian (‘zalat’).”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ زَوَالُ اَلشَّمْسِ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« تَأْخُذُونَ عُوداً طُولُهُ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْبَارٍ وَ إِنْ زَادَ فَهُوَ أَبْيَنُ فَيُقَامُ فَمَا دَامَ تَرَى اَلظِّلَّ يَنْقُصُ فَلَمْ تَزُلْ فَإِذَا زَادَ اَلظِّلُّ بَعْدَ اَلنُّقْصَانِ فَقَدْ زَالَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama’ah narrated from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The ‘zawal’ (sun’s meridian) was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (a.s), so Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “You take a stick whose length is three spans (‘shibr’), and if it is longer, that is clearer. It should be erected upright. As long as you see the shadow decreasing, the sun has not yet passed the meridian. But when the shadow begins to increase after its decrease, then the sun has passed the meridian (‘zalat’).”

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Musa ibn Ja’far al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say regarding Maghrib: “When the disk (of the sun) disappears, the time for prayer has entered, and break your fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْبَغْدَادِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ يَقُولُ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ: «إِذَا تَوَارَى اَلْقُرْصُ كَانَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ أَفْطِرْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Musa ibn Ja’far al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say regarding Maghrib: “When the disk (of the sun) disappears, the time for prayer has entered, and break your fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It was narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Qasim, the freed slave of Abu Ayyub, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun sets, the time for the two prayers has entered until midnight, except that this one (Maghrib) is before that one (‘Isha’). And when the sun passes the meridian, the time for the two prayers has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr).”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ مَوْلَى أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ إِلَى نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ وَ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: It was narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Qasim, the freed slave of Abu Ayyub, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun sets, the time for the two prayers has entered until midnight, except that this one (Maghrib) is before that one (‘Isha’). And when the sun passes the meridian, the time for the two prayers has entered, except that this one (Dhuhr) is before that one (‘Asr).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It was narrated from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from someone who narrated it from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:
He (a.s) was asked about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “When its ‘kursi’ disappears.” I asked: “What is its ‘kursi’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Its disk (the sun’s disk).” I asked: “When does its disk disappear?” Imam (a.s) said: “When you look at it and you no longer see it.”
arabicText: وَرُوِيَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا غَابَ كُرْسِيُّهَا» قُلْتُ وَ مَا كُرْسِيُّهَا قَالَ« قُرْصُهَا» فَقُلْتُ مَتَى يَغِيبُ قُرْصُهَا قَالَ« إِذَا نَظَرْتَ إِلَيْهِ فَلَمْ تَرَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: It was narrated from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from someone who narrated it from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: He (a.s) was asked about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “When its ‘kursi’ disappears.” I asked: “What is its ‘kursi’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Its disk (the sun’s disk).” I asked: “When does its disk disappear?” Imam (a.s) said: “When you look at it and you no longer see it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usamah al-Shahham, who said:
A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I delay Maghrib until the stars become visible.” Imam (a.s) said: “That is the practice of the Khattabiyyah! Verily, Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, brought it down upon Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the time when the disk (of the sun) had set.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصُّهْبَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُؤَخِّرُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ حَتَّى تَسْتَبِينَ اَلنُّجُومُ قَالَ« فَقَالَ خَطَّابِيَّةٌ إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ نَزَلَ بِهَا عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حِينَ سَقَطَ اَلْقُرْصُ»
thaqalaynSanad: It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usamah al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I delay Maghrib until the stars become visible.” Imam (a.s) said: “That is the practice of the Khattabiyyah! Verily, Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, brought it down upon Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the time when the disk (of the sun) had set.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The time of Maghrib is when the sun sets and its disk disappears.” And I (narrator) heard him (a.s) say: “One night, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delayed the Isha prayer as long as Allah (swt) willed. So ‘Umar came and knocked on the door and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), the women have fallen asleep, the children have fallen asleep.’ The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, then came out and said: ‘You do not have the right to annoy me or to command me. It is upon you only to listen and obey.’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَغَابَ قُرْصُهَا» قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ« أَخَّرَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَيْلَةً مِنَ اَللَّيَالِي اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ مَا شَاءَ اَللَّهُ فَجَاءَ عُمَرُ فَدَقَّ اَلْبَابَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ نَامَ اَلنِّسَاءُ نَامَ اَلصِّبْيَانُ فَخَرَجَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُونِي وَ لاَ تَأْمُرُونِي إِنَّمَا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَسْمَعُوا وَ تُطِيعُوا»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The time of Maghrib is when the sun sets and its disk disappears.” And I (narrator) heard him (a.s) say: “One night, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delayed the Isha prayer as long as Allah (swt) willed. So ‘Umar came and knocked on the door and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), the women have fallen asleep, the children have fallen asleep.’ The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, then came out and said: ‘You do not have the right to annoy me or to command me. It is upon you only to listen and obey.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 30

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Musa ibn Ja’far, from Abu Ja’far, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, and he is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun sets, the time of Maghrib has entered, until the amount of time in which a person may pray three rak’ahs passes. When that has passed, the time of Maghrib and ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah has entered, until there remains from midnight the amount of time needed for a person to pray four rak’ahs. When that amount remains, then the time of Maghrib has ended, and the time of ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah remains until midnight.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي يَزِيدَ وَ هُوَ دَاوُدُ بْنُ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« إِذَا غَابَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ مِقْدَارُ مَا يُصَلِّي اَلْمُصَلِّي ثَلاَثَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا مَضَى ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ حَتَّى يَبْقَى مِنِ اِنْتِصَافِ اَللَّيْلِ مِقْدَارُ مَا يُصَلِّي اَلْمُصَلِّي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا بَقِيَ مِقْدَارُ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ خَرَجَ وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ بَقِيَ وَقْتُ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِلَى اِنْتِصَافِ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Musa ibn Ja’far, from Abu Ja’far, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, and he is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun sets, the time of Maghrib has entered, until the amount of time in which a person may pray three rak’ahs passes. When that has passed, the time of Maghrib and ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah has entered, until there remains from midnight the amount of time needed for a person to pray four rak’ahs. When that amount remains, then the time of Maghrib has ended, and the time of ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah remains until midnight.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 30

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “Time of Maghrib is when the redness disappears from the east.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Do you know how that is?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Because the east overlooks the west like this”, and He (a.s) raised his right hand above his left, “so when it disappears here (in the west), the redness disappears from there (in the east).”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشْيَمَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا ذَهَبَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ مِنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ وَ تَدْرِي كَيْفَ ذَاكَ» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« لِأَنَّ اَلْمَشْرِقَ مُطِلٌّ عَلَى اَلْمَغْرِبِ هَكَذَا وَ رَفَعَ يَمِينَهُ فَوْقَ يَسَارِهِ فَإِذَا غَابَتْ هَاهُنَا ذَهَبَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ مِنْ هَاهُنَا»
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “Time of Maghrib is when the redness disappears from the east.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Do you know how that is?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Because the east overlooks the west like this”, and He (a.s) raised his right hand above his left, “so when it disappears here (in the west), the redness disappears from there (in the east).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 30

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “When the redness disappears from this side, meaning from the direction of the east, then the sun has set from the east of the earth and from its west.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ وَاَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا غَابَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ مِنْ هَذَا اَلْجَانِبِ يَعْنِي مِنْ نَاحِيَةِ اَلْمَشْرِقِ فَقَدْ غَابَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ مِنْ شَرْقِ اَلْأَرْضِ وَ مِنْ غَرْبِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “When the redness disappears from this side, meaning from the direction of the east, then the sun has set from the east of the earth and from its west.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 31

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah al-’Ijli, who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: “When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, then the sun has set in the east of the earth.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ اَلْعِجْلِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا غَابَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ مِنْ هَذَا اَلْجَانِبِ يَعْنِي نَاحِيَةَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ فَقَدْ غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فِي شَرْقِ اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah al-’Ijli, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: “When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, then the sun has set in the east of the earth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 31

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said:
I (narrator) accompanied (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), during travel, and I saw Him (a.s) pray Maghrib when the darkness appeared from the east, meaning the blackness (of night).
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: صَحِبْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَرَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي اَلْمَغْرِبَ إِذَا أَقْبَلَتِ اَلْفَحْمَةُ مِنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ يَعْنِي اَلسَّوَادَ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) accompanied (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), during travel, and I saw Him (a.s) pray Maghrib when the darkness appeared from the east, meaning the blackness (of night).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 31

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Ja’far ibn Uthman, from Sama’ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s) regarding Maghrib: “Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun may still be behind the mountain, or the mountain may be concealing it from us.” Imam (a.s) said: “You are not required to climb the mountain.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ وَ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِنَّارُ بَّمَا صَلَّيْنَا وَ نَحْنُ نَخَافُ أَنْ تَكُونَ اَلشَّمْسُ خَلْفَ اَلْجَبَلِ أَوْ قَدْ سَتَرَنَا مِنْهَا اَلْجَبَلُ قَالَ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ صُعُودُ اَلْجَبَلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Ja’far ibn Uthman, from Sama’ah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s) regarding Maghrib: “Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun may still be behind the mountain, or the mountain may be concealing it from us.” Imam (a.s) said: “You are not required to climb the mountain.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 31

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
A man asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, says in His Book regarding Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘So when the night enveloped him, he saw a star…’ (Surah An'am 6:76), this is the beginning of the time. And the end of that is the disappearance of the twilight. The beginning of the time of ‘Isha’ is the fading of the redness, and its end is until the darkness of the night, meaning midnight.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ قَالَ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ فِي كِتَابِهِ لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« فَلَمّٰا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اَللَّيْلُ رَأىٰ كَوْكَباً» فَهَذَا أَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتِ وَآخِرُ ذَلِكَ غَيْبُوبَةُ اَلشَّفَقِ وَأَوَّلُ وَقْتِ اَلْعِشَاءِ ذَهَابُ اَلْحُمْرَةِ وَآخِرُ وَقْتِهَا إِلَى غَسَقِ اَللَّيْلِ يَعْنِي نِصْفَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, says in His Book regarding Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘So when the night enveloped him, he saw a star…’ (Surah An'am 6:76), this is the beginning of the time. And the end of that is the disappearance of the twilight. The beginning of the time of ‘Isha’ is the fading of the redness, and its end is until the darkness of the night, meaning midnight.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 32

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And that which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam Isma’il ibn Hammam, who said:
I saw (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), and we were with Him (a.s), and He (a.s) did not pray Maghrib until the stars had appeared. Then He (a.s) stood and led us in prayer at the door of the house of Ibn Abi Mahmud.
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي هَمَّامٍ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ هَمَّامٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ كُنَّا عِنْدَهُ لَمْ يُصَلِّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ حَتَّى ظَهَرَتِ اَلنُّجُومُ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَصَلَّى بِنَا عَلَى بَابِ دَارِ اِبْنِ أَبِي مَحْمُودٍ
thaqalaynSanad: And that which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam Isma’il ibn Hammam, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), and we were with Him (a.s), and He (a.s) did not pray Maghrib until the stars had appeared. Then He (a.s) stood and led us in prayer at the door of the house of Ibn Abi Mahmud.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 32

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdillah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, one day, and He (a.s) sat speaking until the sun had set. Then He (a.s) called for a candle while He (a.s) continued sitting and speaking. When I left the house, I looked and saw that the twilight had disappeared before He (a.s) had prayed Maghrib. Then He (a.s) called for water, performed wudu’, and prayed.
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِبْنَيْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْماً فَجَلَسَ يُحَدِّثُ حَتَّى غَابَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِشَمْعٍ وَهُوَ جَالِسٌ يَتَحَدَّثُ فَلَمَّا خَرَجْتُ عَنِ اَلْبَيْتِ نَظَرْتُ وَ قَدْ غَابَ اَلشَّفَقُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِالْمَاءِ فَتَوَضَّأَ وَ صَلَّى
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdillah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, one day, and He (a.s) sat speaking until the sun had set. Then He (a.s) called for a candle while He (a.s) continued sitting and speaking. When I left the house, I looked and saw that the twilight had disappeared before He (a.s) had prayed Maghrib. Then He (a.s) called for water, performed wudu’, and prayed.
