chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I am with these people and leave them at the time of Maghrib. As I pass by the mosques, the prayer has been established. If I were to stop and pray with them, I would not be able to perform the adhan and iqamah and begin the prayer properly.” So Imam (a.s) said: “Go to your home, take off your clothes, and if you wish to perform wudu’, then perform wudu’, and pray, for you are still within the time until one-fourth of the night has passed.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَكُونُ مَعَ هَؤُلاَءِ وَ أَنْصَرِفُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ عِنْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَأَمُرُّ بِالْمَسَاجِدِ فَأُقِيمَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَإِنْ أَنَا نَزَلْتُ أُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ لَمْ أَتَمَكَّنْ مِنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ وَ اِفْتِتَاحِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« اِئْتِ مَنْزِلَكَ وَ اِنْزِعْ ثِيَابَكَ وَ إِنْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَتَوَضَّأَ فَتَوَضَّأْ وَ صَلِّ فَإِنَّكَ فِي وَقْتٍ إِلَى رُبُعِ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I am with these people and leave them at the time of Maghrib. As I pass by the mosques, the prayer has been established. If I were to stop and pray with them, I would not be able to perform the adhan and iqamah and begin the prayer properly.” So Imam (a.s) said: “Go to your home, take off your clothes, and if you wish to perform wudu’, then perform wudu’, and pray, for you are still within the time until one-fourth of the night has passed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 32

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yunus and Ali al-Sayrafi, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I am on the outskirts of the city, and the time of Maghrib comes while I am intending to go home. If I delay the prayer until I reach home, it is more convenient for me, but evening overtakes me, so should I pray in one of the mosques?” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray in your home.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُونُسَ وَ عَلِيٍّ اَلصَّيْرَفِيِّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَكُونُ فِي جَانِبِ اَلْمِصْرِ فَتَحْضُرُ اَلْمَغْرِبُ وَ أَنَا أُرِيدُ اَلْمَنْزِلَ فَإِنْ أَخَّرْتُ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى أُصَلِّيَ فِي اَلْمَنْزِلِ كَانَ أَمْكَنَ لِي وَأَدْرَكَنِي اَلْمَسَاءُ أَفَأُصَلِّي فِي بَعْضِ اَلْمَسَاجِدِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ فِي مَنْزِلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yunus and Ali al-Sayrafi, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I am on the outskirts of the city, and the time of Maghrib comes while I am intending to go home. If I delay the prayer until I reach home, it is more convenient for me, but evening overtakes me, so should I pray in one of the mosques?” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray in your home.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 32

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the Maghrib prayer, when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay it for a while? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, if he is fasting, he may break his fast, and if he has a need, he may take care of it, then pray.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا حَضَرَتْ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ تُؤَخَّرَ سَاعَةً قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِنْ كَانَ صَائِماً أَفْطَرَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ لَهُ حَاجَةٌ قَضَاهَا ثُمَّ صَلَّى»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the Maghrib prayer, when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay it for a while? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, if he is fasting, he may break his fast, and if he has a need, he may take care of it, then pray.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 33

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And it was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is more convenient for you and easier for you in your prayer, and you are occupied with your needs, then you may delay it until one-fourth of the night.” Imam (a.s) said to me: “This is while he is present in his own town.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ أَرْفَقَ بِكَ وَ أَمْكَنَ لَكَ فِي صَلاَتِكَ وَ كُنْتَ فِي حَوَائِجِكَ فَلَكَ أَنْ تُؤَخِّرَهَا إِلَى رُبُعِ اَللَّيْلِ» قَالَ قَالَ لِي« هَذَا وَ هُوَ شَاهِدٌ فِي بَلَدِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And it was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is more convenient for you and easier for you in your prayer, and you are occupied with your needs, then you may delay it until one-fourth of the night.” Imam (a.s) said to me: “This is while he is present in his own town.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 33

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And it was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “‘Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us with a timing from you.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Then he does not lie upon us.” I said: “He (Umar ibn Hanzalah) said: ‘The time of Maghrib is when the disk (of the sun) disappears, except that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when travel became intense upon him, would delay Maghrib and combine it with ‘Isha’.” Imam (a.s) said: “He (Umar ibn Hanzalah) has spoken the truth.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The time of ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah is from when the twilight disappears until one-third of the night, and the time of Fajr is from when it first appears until it brightens.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ خَلِيفَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ حَنْظَلَةَ أَتَانَا عَنْكَ بِوَقْتٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« إِذَنْ لاَ يَكْذِبُ عَلَيْنَا» قُلْتُ قَالَ« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا غَابَ اَلْقُرْصُ إِلاَّ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ كَانَ إِذَا جَدَّ بِهِ اَلسَّيْرُ أَخَّرَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَهَا وَ بَيْنَ اَلْعِشَاءِ» فَقَالَ« صَدَقَ» وَ قَالَ« وَقْتُ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ حِينَ يَغِيبُ اَلشَّفَقُ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ وَقْتُ اَلْفَجْرِ حِينَ يَبْدُو حَتَّى يُضِيءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And it was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “‘Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us with a timing from you.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Then he does not lie upon us.” I said: “He (Umar ibn Hanzalah) said: ‘The time of Maghrib is when the disk (of the sun) disappears, except that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when travel became intense upon him, would delay Maghrib and combine it with ‘Isha’.” Imam (a.s) said: “He (Umar ibn Hanzalah) has spoken the truth.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The time of ‘Isha’ al-Akhirah is from when the twilight disappears until one-third of the night, and the time of Fajr is from when it first appears until it brightens.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 33

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja’far, from his father, peace be upon them both:
(Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said) “That the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, on a rainy night would delay Maghrib and hasten ‘Isha’, and He (saws) would pray them together, and He (saws) would say: “Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ فِي اَللَّيْلَةِ اَلْمَطِيرَةِ يُؤَخِّرُ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ يُعَجِّلُ مِنَ اَلْعِشَاءِ فَيُصَلِّيهِمَا جَمِيعاً وَ يَقُولُ« مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمْ لاَ يُرْحَمْ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja’far, from his father, peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said) “That the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, on a rainy night would delay Maghrib and hasten ‘Isha’, and He (saws) would pray them together, and He (saws) would say: “Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 33

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is overtaken by the time of Maghrib while on the road, may he delay it until the twilight disappears? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that during travel. As for when in residence (not traveling), then something less than that (delay is appropriate).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ تُدْرِكُهُ صَلاَةُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلطَّرِيقِ أَ يُؤَخِّرُهَا إِلَى أَنْ يَغِيبَ اَلشَّفَقُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَأَمَّا فِي اَلْحَضَرِ فَدُونَ ذَلِكَ شَيْئاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is overtaken by the time of Maghrib while on the road, may he delay it until the twilight disappears? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that during travel. As for when in residence (not traveling), then something less than that (delay is appropriate).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 34

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I delay Maghrib until the stars become visible?” Imam (a.s) said: “Khattabiyyah? Verily, Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, descended upon Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the time when the disk (of the sun) had set.”
arabicText: ما رواه محمد بن علي بن محبوب عن محمد بن أبي الصهبان عن عبد الرحمن بن حماد عن إبراهيم بن عبد الحميد عن أبي اسامة زيد الشحام قال قال رجل لابي عبد الله عليه السلام أؤخر المغرب حتى تستبين النجوم؟ قال فقال خطابية؟ ان جبرئيل عليه السلام نزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وآله حين سقط القرص
thaqalaynSanad: That which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I delay Maghrib until the stars become visible?” Imam (a.s) said: “Khattabiyyah? Verily, Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, descended upon Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the time when the disk (of the sun) had set.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 34

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Sa’id ibn Janah, from some of our companions:
(Imam) al-Ridha (a.s) said: “Indeed, Abu al-Khattab had corrupted most of the people of Kufah, and they would not pray Maghrib until the twilight had disappeared. But that (delay) is only for the traveler, the one in fear, and the person with a need.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جَنَاحٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ أَبَا اَلْخَطَّابِ قَدْ كَانَ أَفْسَدَ عَامَّةَ أَهْلِ اَلْكُوفَةِ وَ كَانُوا لاَ يُصَلُّونَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ حَتَّى يَغِيبَ اَلشَّفَقُ وَ إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ لِلْمُسَافِرِ وَ اَلْخَائِفِ وَ لِصَاحِبِ اَلْحَاجَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Sa’id ibn Janah, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s) said: “Indeed, Abu al-Khattab had corrupted most of the people of Kufah, and they would not pray Maghrib until the twilight had disappeared. But that (delay) is only for the traveler, the one in fear, and the person with a need.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 34

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from someone who mentioned it:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Cursed is the one who delays Maghrib seeking its (imagined) merit.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« مَلْعُونٌ مَنْ أَخَّرَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ طَلَبَ فَضْلِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from someone who mentioned it:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Cursed is the one who delays Maghrib seeking its (imagined) merit.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 34

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Jamil ibn Darraj. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "What do you say about a man who performs the Maghrib prayer after the redness (of the horizon) has disappeared?" Imam (a.s) said: "Due to a valid excuse, there is no problem." I asked: "And a man who performs the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the redness disappears?" Imam (a.s) said: "Due to a valid excuse, there is no problem."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلرَّجُلِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي اَلْمَغْرِبَ بَعْدَمَا يَسْقُطُ اَلشَّفَقُ فَقَالَ« لِعِلَّةٍ لاَ بَأْسَ» قُلْتُ فَالرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَسْقُطَ اَلشَّفَقُ فَقَالَ« لِعِلَّةٍ لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Jamil ibn Darraj. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "What do you say about a man who performs the Maghrib prayer after the redness (of the horizon) has disappeared?" Imam (a.s) said: "Due to a valid excuse, there is no problem." I asked: "And a man who performs the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the redness disappears?" Imam (a.s) said: "Due to a valid excuse, there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 35

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Dhurayh. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Indeed, some people from among the companions of Abu al-Khattab delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars become interwoven." Imam (a.s) said: "I detach myself before Allah (swt) from whoever does that deliberately."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ أُنَاساً مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ يُمَسُّونَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ حَتَّى تَشْتَبِكَ اَلنُّجُومُ قَالَ« أَبْرَأُ إِلَى اَللَّهِ مِمَّنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مُتَعَمِّداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Dhurayh. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Indeed, some people from among the companions of Abu al-Khattab delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars become interwoven." Imam (a.s) said: "I detach myself before Allah (swt) from whoever does that deliberately."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 35

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Imran ibn Ali al-Halabi. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): "When does the ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ prayer) become obligatory?" Imam (a.s) said: "When the shafaq disappears, and shafaq is the redness (in the sky)." ‘Ubaydullah asked: "May Allah (swt) set you right, indeed after the redness disappears, there remains a strong light spread across (the horizon)." Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, the shafaq is only the redness, and the light is not from the shafaq."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَتَى تَجِبُ اَلْعَتَمَةُ قَالَ« إِذَا غَابَ اَلشَّفَقُ وَ اَلشَّفَقُ اَلْحُمْرَةُ» فَقَالَ عُبَيْدُ اَللَّهِ أَصْلَحَكَ اَللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَبْقَى بَعْدَ ذَهَابِ اَلْحُمْرَةِ ضَوْءٌ شَدِيدٌ مُعْتَرِضٌ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« إِنَّ اَلشَّفَقَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ اَلْحُمْرَةُ وَ لَيْسَ اَلضَّوْءُ مِنَ اَلشَّفَقِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Imran ibn Ali al-Halabi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): "When does the ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ prayer) become obligatory?" Imam (a.s) said: "When the shafaq disappears, and shafaq is the redness (in the sky)." ‘Ubaydullah asked: "May Allah (swt) set you right, indeed after the redness disappears, there remains a strong light spread across (the horizon)." Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, the shafaq is only the redness, and the light is not from the shafaq."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 35

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn ‘Atiyyah from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Aba Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who performs the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the disappearance of the shafaq (redness), and they both said, "There is no problem with it."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ وَأَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ فَقَالاَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn ‘Atiyyah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who performs the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the disappearance of the shafaq (redness), and they both said, "There is no problem with it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated with this chain from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Ubaydullah and ‘Imran, the two sons of Ali al-Halabi, who said:
We used to argue on the road about the prayer, the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah, before the disappearance of the shafaq, and some among us would feel uneasy about that. So we entered upon Abu Abdillah (a.s) and asked him about performing the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah before the disappearance of the Shafaq. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that." We asked: "And what is the shafaq?" Imam (a.s) said: "The redness."
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِاَللَّهِ وَ عِمْرَانَ اِبْنَيْ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيَّيْنِ قَالاَ: كُنَّا نَخْتَصِمُ فِي اَلطَّرِيقِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ وَ كَانَ مِنَّا مَنْ يَضِيقُ بِذَلِكَ صَدْرُهُ فَدَخَلْنَا عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَسَأَلْنَاهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ» قُلْنَا وَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ اَلشَّفَقُ فَقَالَ« اَلْحُمْرَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated with this chain from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Ubaydullah and ‘Imran, the two sons of Ali al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We used to argue on the road about the prayer, the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah, before the disappearance of the shafaq, and some among us would feel uneasy about that. So we entered upon Abu Abdillah (a.s) and asked him about performing the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah before the disappearance of the Shafaq. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that." We asked: "And what is the shafaq?" Imam (a.s) said: "The redness."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And with this chain from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ishaq al-Batihi, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) perform the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the disappearance of the shafaq (redness), then He (a.s) departed.
arabicText: وَبِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْبَطِيحِيِّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّى اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ ثُمَّ اِرْتَحَلَ
thaqalaynSanad: And with this chain from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ishaq al-Batihi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) perform the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) before the disappearance of the shafaq (redness), then He (a.s) departed.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no problem in hastening the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) during travel before the disappearance of the shafaq."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُعَجِّلَ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَغِيبَ اَلشَّفَقُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no problem in hastening the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer) during travel before the disappearance of the shafaq."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from ‘Ubaydullah al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no problem in delaying the Maghrib prayer during travel until the shafaq disappears, and there is no problem in hastening the ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ prayer) during travel before the shafaq disappears."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عُبَيْدِاَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُؤَخِّرَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ حَتَّى يَغِيبَ اَلشَّفَقُ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُعَجِّلَ اَلْعَتَمَةَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَغِيبَ اَلشَّفَقُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from ‘Ubaydullah al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no problem in delaying the Maghrib prayer during travel until the shafaq disappears, and there is no problem in hastening the ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ prayer) during travel before the shafaq disappears."

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Abu ‘Ubaydah, who said:
I heard Aba Ja’far (a.s) say: "When there was a dark night with wind and rain, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) would perform the Maghrib prayer, then wait for the amount of time it would take for the people to pray their recommended prayers, then His (saws) muʾadhdhin would give the iqamah, and He (saws) would then perform the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer), and then they would disperse."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذَا كَانَتْ لَيْلَةٌ مُظْلِمَةٌ وَ رِيحٌ وَ مَطَرٌ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ مَكَثَ قَدْرَ مَا يَتَنَفَّلُ اَلنَّاسُ ثُمَّ أَقَامَ مُؤَذِّنُهُ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفُوا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Abu ‘Ubaydah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Ja’far (a.s) say: "When there was a dark night with wind and rain, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) would perform the Maghrib prayer, then wait for the amount of time it would take for the people to pray their recommended prayers, then His (saws) muʾadhdhin would give the iqamah, and He (saws) would then perform the ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah (the last evening prayer), and then they would disperse."

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Isma’il ibn Rabah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you pray while thinking that you are within the time (of the prayer), and the time has not yet actually begun, and then the time enters while you are in the prayer, then it suffices for you."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ[ رَبَاحٍ خ ل] عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنْتَ تَرَى أَنَّكَ فِي وَقْتٍ وَ لَمْ يَدْخُلِ اَلْوَقْتُ فَدَخَلَ اَلْوَقْتُ وَ أَنْتَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَدْ أَجْزَأَتْ عَنْكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Isma’il ibn Rabah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you pray while thinking that you are within the time (of the prayer), and the time has not yet actually begun, and then the time enters while you are in the prayer, then it suffices for you."

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to perform the two rak’ahs of the morning, which is the Fajr, when the dawn appeared and spread horizontally and gave a beautiful illumination."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلصُّبْحِ وَ هِيَ اَلْفَجْرُ إِذَا اِعْتَرَضَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ أَضَاءَ حُسْناً»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to perform the two rak’ahs of the morning, which is the Fajr, when the dawn appeared and spread horizontally and gave a beautiful illumination."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 37

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ali from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Yazid ibn Khalifah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Fajr time is from when it first appears until it becomes bright."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ خَلِيفَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ اَلْفَجْرِ حِينَ يَبْدُو حَتَّى يُضِيءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ali from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Yazid ibn Khalifah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Fajr time is from when it first appears until it becomes bright."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 37

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man prayed Fajr when the dawn appeared." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ صَلَّى اَلْفَجْرَ حِينَ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man prayed Fajr when the dawn appeared." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The time of the morning prayer is between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ اَلْغَدَاةِ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The time of the morning prayer is between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 38

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Husayn, who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja’far (a.s); “May I be your ransom, your followers have differed regarding the time of the Fajr prayer. Some of them pray when the first, vertical dawn appears in the sky, and some of them pray when it spreads horizontally at the lower part of the horizon and becomes clear. I do not know which of the two times is better, so I may pray at that time. If you would, O my master, may Allah (swt) make me your ransom, teach me which of the two times is better, and set for me a standard regarding what I should do when the moon is present and the Fajr is not clearly visible until it reddens and brightens. And how should I act concerning the moon? And what is the limit of that in both travel and residence? May you do so, if Allah (swt) wills.” So He (a.s) wrote back in his own handwriting (peace be upon him): "The Fajr, may Allah (swt) have mercy on you, is the white thread, and it is not the whiteness that rises upward. Do not pray, in travel or in residence, until it becomes clearly distinguishable. May Allah (swt) have mercy on you. Indeed, Allah (swt) has not placed His (swt) creation in confusion regarding this matter. He (swt), the Exalted, said: ‘'Eat and drink until the white thread becomes clear to you from the black thread of the dawn'‘ (Surah Baqarah 2:187), the white thread is the Fajr which makes eating and drinking prohibited in fasting, and likewise it is the one that makes prayer obligatory."
arabicText: وَرَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ اِخْتَلَفَ مَوَالِيكَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُصَلِّي إِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ اَلْأَوَّلُ اَلْمُسْتَطِيلُ فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُصَلِّي إِذَا اِعْتَرَضَ فِي أَسْفَلِ اَلْأَرْضِ وَاِسْتَبَانَ وَ لَسْتُ أَعْرِفُ أَفْضَلَ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ فَأُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ يَا مَوْلاَيَ جَعَلَنِي اَللَّهُ فِدَاكَ أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِي أَفْضَلَ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ وَ تَحُدَّ لِي كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ مَعَ اَلْقَمَرِ وَ اَلْفَجْرُ لاَ يَتَبَيَّنُ حَتَّى يَحْمَرَّ وَ يُصْبِحَ وَ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ مَعَ اَلْقَمَرِ وَ مَا حَدُّ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ اَلْحَضَرِ فَعَلْتُ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ فَكَتَبَ بِخَطِّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اَلْفَجْرُ يَرْحَمُكَ اَللَّهُ اَلْخَيْطُ اَلْأَبْيَضُ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ اَلْأَبْيَضَ صُعُداً وَ لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ فِي حَضَرٍ حَتَّى تَتَبَيَّنَهُ رَحِمَكَ اَللَّهُ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ خَلْقَهُ فِي شُبْهَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا فَقَالَ تَعَالَى« كُلُوا وَ اِشْرَبُوا حَتّٰى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ اَلْخَيْطُ اَلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ اَلْخَيْطِ اَلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ اَلْفَجْرِ» فَالْخَيْطُ اَلْأَبْيَضُ هُوَ اَلْفَجْرُ اَلَّذِي يَحْرُمُ بِهِ اَلْأَكْلُ وَ اَلشُّرْبُ فِي اَلصِّيَامِ وَ كَذَلِكَ هُوَ اَلَّذِي يُوجِبُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Husayn, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Ja’far (a.s); “May I be your ransom, your followers have differed regarding the time of the Fajr prayer. Some of them pray when the first, vertical dawn appears in the sky, and some of them pray when it spreads horizontally at the lower part of the horizon and becomes clear. I do not know which of the two times is better, so I may pray at that time. If you would, O my master, may Allah (swt) make me your ransom, teach me which of the two times is better, and set for me a standard regarding what I should do when the moon is present and the Fajr is not clearly visible until it reddens and brightens. And how should I act concerning the moon? And what is the limit of that in both travel and residence? May you do so, if Allah (swt) wills.” So He (a.s) wrote back in his own handwriting (peace be upon him): "The Fajr, may Allah (swt) have mercy on you, is the white thread, and it is not the whiteness that rises upward. Do not pray, in travel or in residence, until it becomes clearly distinguishable. May Allah (swt) have mercy on you. Indeed, Allah (swt) has not placed His (swt) creation in confusion regarding this matter. He (swt), the Exalted, said: ‘'Eat and drink until the white thread becomes clear to you from the black thread of the dawn'‘ (Surah Baqarah 2:187), the white thread is the Fajr which makes eating and drinking prohibited in fasting, and likewise it is the one that makes prayer obligatory."

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Inform me about the best time for the Fajr prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "At the time of the rising of the dawn. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘'Indeed, the recitation of Fajr is witnessed'‘ (Surah Isra 17:78), meaning the Fajr prayer is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. So when the servant performs the morning prayer at the time of the rising of the dawn, it is recorded for him twice, the angels of the night record it and the angels of the day record it."
arabicText: وَرَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَفْضَلِ اَلْمَوَاقِيتِ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ قَالَ« مَعَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ« إِنَّ قُرْآنَ اَلْفَجْرِ كٰانَ مَشْهُوداً» يَعْنِي صَلاَةَ اَلْفَجْرِ يَشْهَدُهُ مَلاَئِكَةُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ مَلاَئِكَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ فَإِذَا صَلَّى اَلْعَبْدُ صَلاَةَ اَلصُّبْحِ مَعَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ أُثْبِتَ لَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ تُثْبِتُهُ مَلاَئِكَةُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ مَلاَئِكَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Inform me about the best time for the Fajr prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "At the time of the rising of the dawn. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘'Indeed, the recitation of Fajr is witnessed'‘ (Surah Isra 17:78), meaning the Fajr prayer is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. So when the servant performs the morning prayer at the time of the rising of the dawn, it is recorded for him twice, the angels of the night record it and the angels of the day record it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 39

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hisham ibn al-Hudhayl from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of the Fajr prayer, and Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn spreads horizontally, and you see it like a stream of light across the horizon."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْهُذَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« حِينَ يَعْتَرِضُ اَلْفَجْرُ فَتَرَاهُ مِثْلَ نَهَرِ سُورَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hisham ibn al-Hudhayl from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of the Fajr prayer, and Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn spreads horizontally, and you see it like a stream of light across the horizon."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 39

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Atiyyah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The Subh (morning) is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as if it were the whiteness of a stream."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصُّبْحُ هُوَ اَلَّذِي إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُ مُعْتَرِضاً كَأَنَّهُ بَيَاضُ سُورَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Atiyyah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The Subh (morning) is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as if it were the whiteness of a stream."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 39

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Amr ibn Uthman from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Sa’d ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s)) said: "Whoever catches a rak’ah of the morning prayer before the rising of the sun has caught the full morning prayer."
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ اَلْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ عَنِ اَلْأَصْبَغِ بْنِ نُبَاتَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ اَلْغَدَاةِ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ اَلْغَدَاةَ تَامَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Amr ibn Uthman from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Sa’d ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s)) said: "Whoever catches a rak’ah of the morning prayer before the rising of the sun has caught the full morning prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 39

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who is overcome by sleep or hindered by something from performing the obligatory Fajr prayer, (he may pray it) between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun, and that is specific to the obligatory prayer. So if he performs one rak’ah of the morning prayer and then the sun rises, he should complete (the prayer), and his prayer is valid."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« فِي اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا غَلَبَتْهُ عَيْنُهُ أَوْ عَاقَهُ أَمْرٌ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ مِنَ اَلْفَجْرِ مَا بَيْنَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ خَاصَّةً فَإِنْ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً مِنَ اَلْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَلْيُتِمَّ وَ قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who is overcome by sleep or hindered by something from performing the obligatory Fajr prayer, (he may pray it) between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun, and that is specific to the obligatory prayer. So if he performs one rak’ah of the morning prayer and then the sun rises, he should complete (the prayer), and his prayer is valid."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The time of Fajr is from when the dawn splits until the morning light covers the sky. It is not appropriate to delay it deliberately, but it is a valid time for one who is preoccupied, forgets, or sleeps."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ اَلْفَجْرِ حِينَ يَنْشَقُّ اَلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَجَلَّلَ اَلصُّبْحُ اَلسَّمَاءَ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي تَأْخِيرُ ذَلِكَ عَمْداً لَكِنَّهُ وَقْتٌ لِمَنْ شُغِلَ أَوْ نَسِيَ أَوْ نَامَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The time of Fajr is from when the dawn splits until the morning light covers the sky. It is not appropriate to delay it deliberately, but it is a valid time for one who is preoccupied, forgets, or sleeps."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir al-Makfuf, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the fasting person; when does food become forbidden for him? Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn is like the white Coptic garment." I asked: "Then when does the prayer become permissible?" Imam (a.s) said: "When it is like that." I asked: "Am I not within the time (of prayer) from that moment until the sun rises?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, we only count that as the prayer of children." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, it was not commendable for a man to pray in the mosque and then return to wake up his family and children"
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ اَلْمَكْفُوفِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ مَتَى يَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ اَلطَّعَامُ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفَجْرُ كَالْقُبْطِيَّةِ اَلْبَيْضَاءِ» قُلْتُ فَمَتَى تَحِلُّ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ كَذَلِكَ» فَقُلْتُ أَ لَسْتُ فِي وَقْتٍ مِنْ تِلْكَ اَلسَّاعَةِ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ« لاَ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّهَا صَلاَةَ اَلصِّبْيَانِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يُحْمَدُ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ يَرْجِعَ فَيُنَبِّهَ أَهْلَهُ وَ صِبْيَانَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir al-Makfuf, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the fasting person; when does food become forbidden for him? Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn is like the white Coptic garment." I asked: "Then when does the prayer become permissible?" Imam (a.s) said: "When it is like that." I asked: "Am I not within the time (of prayer) from that moment until the sun rises?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, we only count that as the prayer of children." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, it was not commendable for a man to pray in the mosque and then return to wake up his family and children"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr and Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the first of the two is the better. The time of the Fajr prayer is from the moment the dawn splits until the morning light covers the sky, and it is not appropriate to delay that deliberately, but it is the time for one who is preoccupied, forgets, is heedless, or sleeps. And the time of Maghrib is from the setting of the sun until the stars become interwoven. And no one should make the latter of the two times their time (of prayer), except due to an excuse or a valid reason."
arabicText: وَرَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ وَفَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَقْتَانِ وَ أَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ أَفْضَلُهُمَا وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ حِينَ يَنْشَقُّ اَلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَجَلَّلَ اَلصُّبْحُ اَلسَّمَاءَ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي تَأْخِيرُ ذَلِكَ عَمْداً لَكِنَّهُ وَقْتُ مَنْ شُغِلَ أَوْ نَسِيَ أَوْ سَهَا أَوْ نَامَ وَ وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ حِينَ تَجِبُ اَلشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَشْتَبِكَ اَلنُّجُومُ وَ لَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ آخِرَ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتاً إِلاَّ مِنْ عُذْرٍ أَوْ عِلَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr and Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the first of the two is the better. The time of the Fajr prayer is from the moment the dawn splits until the morning light covers the sky, and it is not appropriate to delay that deliberately, but it is the time for one who is preoccupied, forgets, is heedless, or sleeps. And the time of Maghrib is from the setting of the sun until the stars become interwoven. And no one should make the latter of the two times their time (of prayer), except due to an excuse or a valid reason."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 41

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning of the time is the best of it. And it is not for anyone to make the latter of the two times his (designated) time except in a case of excuse without (blameworthy) reason."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَقْتَانِ وَ أَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُهُ وَ لَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ آخِرَ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتاً إِلاَّ فِي عُذْرٍ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning of the time is the best of it. And it is not for anyone to make the latter of the two times his (designated) time except in a case of excuse without (blameworthy) reason."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 41

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning of the time is the better of the two."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ أَوِ اِبْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَقْتَانِ وَأَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning of the time is the better of the two."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Bakr ibn Muhammad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last is better for the believer than his children and his wealth."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لَفَضْلُ اَلْوَقْتِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَى اَلْأَخِيرِ خَيْرٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ مِنْ وَلَدِهِ وَ مَالِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Bakr ibn Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last is better for the believer than his children and his wealth."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "May Allah (swt) set you right, is the beginning of the time for each prayer better, or the middle, or the end?" Imam (a.s) said: "The beginning." He (a.s) then said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, Allah (swt) loves from goodness that which is done promptly.’"
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَصْلَحَكَ اَللَّهُ وَقْتُ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ أَوَّلُ اَلْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُ أَوْ وَسَطُهُ أَوْ آخِرُهُ فَقَالَ« أَوَّلُهُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مِنَ اَلْخَيْرِ مَا يُعَجَّلُ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "May Allah (swt) set you right, is the beginning of the time for each prayer better, or the middle, or the end?" Imam (a.s) said: "The beginning." He (a.s) then said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, Allah (swt) loves from goodness that which is done promptly.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sa’d ibn Abi Khalaf:
(Imam) Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The obligatory prayers, when performed at their initial time while fulfilling their proper conditions, are more fragrant than the myrtle branch when it is freshly taken from its tree in its fragrance, scent, and freshness. So adhere to the first time (of prayer)."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلْمَفْرُوضَاتُ فِي أَوَّلِ وَقْتِهَا إِذَا أُقِيمَ حُدُودُهَا أَطْيَبُ رِيحاً مِنْ قَضِيبِ اَلْآسِ حِينَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنْ شَجَرِهِ فِي طِيبِهِ وَ رِيحِهِ وَ طَرَاوَتِهِ فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالْوَقْتِ اَلْأَوَّلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sa’d ibn Abi Khalaf:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The obligatory prayers, when performed at their initial time while fulfilling their proper conditions, are more fragrant than the myrtle branch when it is freshly taken from its tree in its fragrance, scent, and freshness. So adhere to the first time (of prayer)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from his father from Qutaybah al-A’sha:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, the superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last is like the superiority of the Hereafter over this world."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ قُتَيْبَةَ اَلْأَعْشَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ فَضْلَ اَلْوَقْتِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَى اَلْأَخِيرِ كَفَضْلِ اَلْآخِرَةِ عَلَى اَلدُّنْيَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from his father from Qutaybah al-A’sha:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, the superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last is like the superiority of the Hereafter over this world."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "Know that the beginning of the time is always better, so hasten toward good as much as you are able. And the most beloved of deeds to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, is that which the servant remains consistent upon, even if it is little."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اِعْلَمْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَ اَلْوَقْتِ أَبَداً أَفْضَلُ فَتَعَجَّلِ اَلْخَيْرَ مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ وَ أَحَبَّ اَلْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَادَامَ اَلْعَبْدُ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ قَلَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "Know that the beginning of the time is always better, so hasten toward good as much as you are able. And the most beloved of deeds to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, is that which the servant remains consistent upon, even if it is little."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "When the time of a prayer enters, the gates of the heavens are opened for the ascent of deeds. So I do not wish that any deed ascends before mine, nor that anyone's name is recorded in the scroll (of deeds) before mine."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةٍ فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُ اَلسَّمَاءِ لِصُعُودِ اَلْأَعْمَالِ فَمَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَصْعَدَ عَمَلٌ أَوَّلُ مِنْ عَمَلِي وَ لاَ يُكْتَبَ فِي اَلصَّحِيفَةِ أَحَدٌ أَوَّلُ مِنِّي»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "When the time of a prayer enters, the gates of the heavens are opened for the ascent of deeds. So I do not wish that any deed ascends before mine, nor that anyone's name is recorded in the scroll (of deeds) before mine."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Times of Prayer and Sign of Each of Its Times
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Isma‘il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Rib‘i:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, we advance and delay (the prayer), and it is not as people say: ‘Whoever misses the time of prayer has perished.’ Rather, there is a concession for the one who forgets, the sick person, the severely ill, the traveller, and the one asleep, in delaying it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« إِنَّا لَنُقَدِّمُ وَ نُؤَخِّرُ وَ لَيْسَ كَمَا يُقَالُ مَنْ أَخْطَأَ وَقْتَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَدْ هَلَكَ وَ إِنَّمَا اَلرُّخْصَةُ لِلنَّاسِي وَ اَلْمَرِيضِ وَ اَلْمُدْنِفِ وَ اَلْمُسَافِرِ وَ اَلنَّائِمِ فِي تَأْخِيرِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Isma‘il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Rib‘i:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, we advance and delay (the prayer), and it is not as people say: ‘Whoever misses the time of prayer has perished.’ Rather, there is a concession for the one who forgets, the sick person, the severely ill, the traveller, and the one asleep, in delaying it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 43

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘"So set your face toward the religion, upright (hanifan)."‘ (Surah Rum 30:30) Imam (a.s) said: "He (swt) commanded him to direct his face toward the qiblah, with nothing of idol worship in it, purely and sincerely (for Allah (swt))."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً» قَالَ« أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُقِيمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلْقِبْلَةِ لَيْسَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ عِبَادَةِ اَلْأَوْثَانِ خَالِصاً مُخْلِصاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘"So set your face toward the religion, upright (hanifan)."‘ (Surah Rum 30:30) Imam (a.s) said: "He (swt) commanded him to direct his face toward the qiblah, with nothing of idol worship in it, purely and sincerely (for Allah (swt))."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 45

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘"And direct your faces at every place of worship."‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29) Imam (a.s) said: "This also refers to the qiblah."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« وَ أَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ» قَالَ« هَذِهِ اَلْقِبْلَةُ أَيْضاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘"And direct your faces at every place of worship."‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29) Imam (a.s) said: "This also refers to the qiblah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 45

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "When was the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, turned toward the Ka’bah?" Imam (a.s) said: "After his return from Badr."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَتَى صُرِفَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِلَى اَلْكَعْبَةِ فَقَالَ« بَعْدَ رُجُوعِهِ مِنْ بَدْرٍ
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "When was the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, turned toward the Ka’bah?" Imam (a.s) said: "After his return from Badr."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 45

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu Jamilah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And direct your faces at every place of worship,"‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29) Imam (a.s) said: "Newly built mosques, so they were commanded to direct their faces ‘toward al-Masjid al-Haram’."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى« وَأَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ» قَالَ« مَسَاجِدُ مُحْدَثَةٌ فَأُمِرُوا أَنْ يُقِيمُوا وُجُوهَهُمْ« شَطْرَ اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرٰامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu Jamilah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And direct your faces at every place of worship,"‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29) Imam (a.s) said: "Newly built mosques, so they were commanded to direct their faces ‘toward al-Masjid al-Haram’."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And We did not make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from those who turn back on their heels"’ (Surah Baqarah 2:143). Was He (saws) commanded with it?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to turn His (saws) face toward the sky, and Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, knew what was in His (saws) soul, so He (swt) said: ‘'Indeed, We see the turning of your face toward the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you.'’" (Surah Baqarah 2:144)
arabicText: اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى« وَ مٰا جَعَلْنَا اَلْقِبْلَةَ اَلَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهٰا إِلاّٰ لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ اَلرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ» أَمَرَهُ بِهِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ يُقَلِّبُ وَجْهَهُ فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ فَعَلِمَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ فَقَالَ« قَدْ نَرىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي اَلسَّمٰاءِ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضٰاهٰا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And We did not make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from those who turn back on their heels"’ (Surah Baqarah 2:143). Was He (saws) commanded with it?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to turn His (saws) face toward the sky, and Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, knew what was in His (saws) soul, so He (swt) said: ‘'Indeed, We see the turning of your face toward the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you.'’" (Surah Baqarah 2:144)

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Wuhayb from Abu Basir from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they were upon? Say: To Allah (swt) belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path."’ (Surah Baqarah 2:142) I (Abu Basir) said to Him (a.s): "Did Allah (swt) command Him (saws) to pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Do you not see that Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘'And We did not make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from those who turn back on their heels. And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah (swt) has guided. And Allah (swt) would never let your faith go to waste. Indeed, Allah (swt) is Kind and Merciful to the people.'‘" (Surah Baqarah 2:143) Imam (a.s) said: "The tribe of Banu Abd al-Ashhal came to them while they were in prayer and had already prayed two rak’ahs facing Bayt al-Maqdis. It was said to them, 'Indeed, your Prophet has now been directed toward the Ka’bah.' So the women switched places with the men, and the men switched places with the women, and they made the remaining two rak’ahs facing the Ka’bah. Thus, they prayed one prayer toward two qiblahs. For that reason, their mosque was named 'Masjid al-Qiblatayn' (the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs)."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ وُهَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى« سَيَقُولُ اَلسُّفَهٰاءُ مِنَ اَلنّٰاسِ مٰا وَلاّٰهُمْ عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ اَلَّتِي كٰانُوا عَلَيْهٰا قُلْ لِلّٰهِ اَلْمَشْرِقُ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشٰاءُ إِلىٰ صِرٰاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ اَللَّهُ أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ إِلَى اَلْبَيْتِ اَلْمُقَدَّسِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ أَ لاَ تَرَى أَنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ« وَ مٰا جَعَلْنَا اَلْقِبْلَةَ اَلَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهٰا إِلاّٰ لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ اَلرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ وَإِنْ كٰانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلاّٰ عَلَى اَلَّذِينَ هَدَى اَللّٰهُ وَمٰا كٰانَ اَللّٰهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمٰانَكُمْ إِنَّ اَللّٰهَ بِالنّٰاسِ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ»» قَالَ« إِنَّ بَنِي عَبْدِ اَلْأَشْهَلِ أَتَوْهُمْ وَ هُمْ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ قَدْ صَلَّوْا رَكْعَتَيْنِ إِلَى بَيْتِ اَلْمَقْدِسِ فَقِيلَ لَهُمْ إِنَّ نَبِيَّكُمْ قَدْ صُرِفَ إِلَى اَلْكَعْبَةِ فَتَحَوَّلَ اَلنِّسَاءُ مَكَانَ اَلرِّجَالِ وَ اَلرِّجَالُ مَكَانَ اَلنِّسَاءِ وَ جَعَلُوا اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْبَاقِيَتَيْنِ إِلَى اَلْكَعْبَةِ فَصَلَّوْا صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً إِلَى قِبْلَتَيْنِ فَلِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَ مَسْجِدُهُمْ مَسْجِدَ اَلْقِبْلَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Wuhayb from Abu Basir from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they were upon? Say: To Allah (swt) belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path."’ (Surah Baqarah 2:142) I (Abu Basir) said to Him (a.s): "Did Allah (swt) command Him (saws) to pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Do you not see that Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘'And We did not make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from those who turn back on their heels. And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah (swt) has guided. And Allah (swt) would never let your faith go to waste. Indeed, Allah (swt) is Kind and Merciful to the people.'‘" (Surah Baqarah 2:143) Imam (a.s) said: "The tribe of Banu Abd al-Ashhal came to them while they were in prayer and had already prayed two rak’ahs facing Bayt al-Maqdis. It was said to them, 'Indeed, your Prophet has now been directed toward the Ka’bah.' So the women switched places with the men, and the men switched places with the women, and they made the remaining two rak’ahs facing the Ka’bah. Thus, they prayed one prayer toward two qiblahs. For that reason, their mosque was named 'Masjid al-Qiblatayn' (the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs)."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from some of his men:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, made the Ka’bah the qiblah for the people of the Masjid, and made the Masjid the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and made the Haram the qiblah for the people of the world."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى جَعَلَ اَلْكَعْبَةَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَجَعَلَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ اَلْحَرَمِ وَجَعَلَ اَلْحَرَمَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ اَلدُّنْيَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from some of his men:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, made the Ka’bah the qiblah for the people of the Masjid, and made the Masjid the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and made the Haram the qiblah for the people of the world."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Abu al-Abbas Ibn ‘Uqdah from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hazim, who said: Taghlib ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Ja’far al-Ju’fi Abu al-Walid narrated to us, who said:
I (Bishr ibn Ja’far) heard (Imam) Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "The House (Ka’bah) is the qiblah for the people of the Mosque, and the Mosque is the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and the Haram is the qiblah for all people."
arabicText: أَبُو اَلْعَبَّاسِ اِبْنُ عُقْدَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا تَغْلِبُ بْنُ اَلضَّحَّاكِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْجُعْفِيُّ أَبُو اَلْوَلِيدِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« اَلْبَيْتُ قِبْلَةٌ لِأَهْلِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَ اَلْمَسْجِدُ قِبْلَةٌ لِأَهْلِ اَلْحَرَمِ وَ اَلْحَرَمُ قِبْلَةٌ لِلنَّاسِ جَمِيعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Abu al-Abbas Ibn ‘Uqdah from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hazim, who said: Taghlib ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Ja’far al-Ju’fi Abu al-Walid narrated to us, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Bishr ibn Ja’far) heard (Imam) Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "The House (Ka’bah) is the qiblah for the people of the Mosque, and the Mosque is the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and the Haram is the qiblah for all people."
