chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Muhammad, who raised it, said:
It was said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Why does a person turn slightly to the left during prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because the Ka’bah has six sides, four of them are on your left and two of them are on your right. Therefore, the slight turning is toward the left."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ: قِيلَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لِمَ صَارَ اَلرَّجُلُ يَنْحَرِفُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ إِلَى اَلْيَسَارِ فَقَالَ« لِأَنَّ لِلْكَعْبَةِ سِتَّةَ حُدُودٍ أَرْبَعَةٌ مِنْهَا عَلَى يَسَارِكَ وَ اِثْنَانِ مِنْهَا عَلَى يَمِينِكَ فَمِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ وَقَعَ اَلتَّحْرِيفُ عَلَى اَلْيَسَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Muhammad, who raised it, said:
thaqalaynMatn: It was said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Why does a person turn slightly to the left during prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because the Ka’bah has six sides, four of them are on your left and two of them are on your right. Therefore, the slight turning is toward the left."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the slight turning to the left from the qiblah by our companions and about the reason for it. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, when the Black Stone was brought down from Paradise and placed in its position, the boundaries (ansab) of the Haram were set according to the extent reached by the light, the light of the Stone. So the boundary on the right side of the Ka’bah is four miles, and on its left side is eight miles, altogether twelve miles. Therefore, if a person turns to the right, he exits the boundary of the qiblah due to the shorter extent of the Haram markers on that side. But if he turns to the left, he is not outside the boundary of the qiblah."
arabicText: وَ سَأَلَ اَلْمُفَضَّلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ: عَنِ اَلتَّحْرِيفِ لِأَصْحَابِنَا ذَاتَ اَلْيَسَارِ عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ عَنِ اَلسَّبَبِ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «إِنَّ اَلْحَجَرَ اَلْأَسْوَدَ لَمَّا أُنْزِلَ بِهِ مِنَ اَلْجَنَّةِ وَ وُضِعَ فِي مَوْضِعِهِ جُعِلَ أَنْصَابُ اَلْحَرَمِ مِنْ حَيْثُ يَلْحَقُهُ اَلنُّورُ نُورُ اَلْحَجَرِ فَهِيَ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلْكَعْبَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَمْيَالٍ وَ عَنْ يَسَارِهَا ثَمَانِيَةُ أَمْيَالٍ كُلُّهُ اِثْنَا عَشَرَ مِيلاً فَإِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ اَلْإِنْسَانُ ذَاتَ اَلْيَمِينِ خَرَجَ عَنْ حَدِّ اَلْقِبْلَةِ لِقِلَّةِ أَنْصَابِ اَلْحَرَمِ وَ إِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ ذَاتَ اَلْيَسَارِ لَمْ يَكُنْ خَارِجاً عَنْ حَدِّ اَلْقِبْلَةِ»
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the slight turning to the left from the qiblah by our companions and about the reason for it. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, when the Black Stone was brought down from Paradise and placed in its position, the boundaries (ansab) of the Haram were set according to the extent reached by the light, the light of the Stone. So the boundary on the right side of the Ka’bah is four miles, and on its left side is eight miles, altogether twelve miles. Therefore, if a person turns to the right, he exits the boundary of the qiblah due to the shorter extent of the Haram markers on that side. But if he turns to the left, he is not outside the boundary of the qiblah."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Ja’far ibn Sama’ah from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: "Place al-Jady (the Pole Star) behind you and pray."

thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Tatari from Ja’far ibn Sama’ah from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Isma’il ibn Abbad from Khirash from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, these opponents of ours say that when the sky is covered or darkened so we cannot recognize the direction of the sky, we and you are the same in exercising ijtihad (independent judgment)." Imam (a.s) said: "It is not as they say. When that happens, then one must pray in four directions."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ عَنْ خِرَاشٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ اَلْمُخَالِفِينَ عَلَيْنَا يَقُولُونَ إِذَا أُطْبِقَتْ عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَظْلَمَتْ فَلَمْ نَعْرِفِ اَلسَّمَاءَ كُنَّا وَ أَنْتُمْ سَوَاءً فِي اَلاِجْتِهَادِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُصَلَّ لِأَرْبَعِ وُجُوهٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Isma’il ibn Abbad from Khirash from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, these opponents of ours say that when the sky is covered or darkened so we cannot recognize the direction of the sky, we and you are the same in exercising ijtihad (independent judgment)." Imam (a.s) said: "It is not as they say. When that happens, then one must pray in four directions."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "Estimation (taharri) is always sufficient when the direction of the qiblah is not known."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يُجْزِي اَلتَّحَرِّي أَبَداً إِذَا لَمْ يُعْلَمْ أَيْنَ وَجْهُ اَلْقِبْلَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "Estimation (taharri) is always sufficient when the direction of the qiblah is not known."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, said:
I asked Him (a.s) about praying during the night and the day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars can be seen. Imam (a.s) said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ إِذَا لَمْ تُرَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ لاَ اَلْقَمَرُ وَ لاَ اَلنُّجُومُ قَالَ« اِجْتَهِدْ رَأْيَكَ وَ تَعَمَّدِ اَلْقِبْلَةَ جُهْدَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about praying during the night and the day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars can be seen. Imam (a.s) said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about prayer during the night and day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars are visible. Imam (a.s) said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن الحسن عن زرعة عن سماعة قال سألته عن الصلاة بالليل والنهار إذا لم تر الشمس ولا القمر ولا النجوم قال تجتهد رأيك وتعمد القبلة جهدك
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about prayer during the night and day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars are visible. Imam (a.s) said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from ‘Amr ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after he had entered the time of another prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat that prayer before performing the one whose time has now entered."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ تَبَيَّنَتْ لَهُ اَلْقِبْلَةُ وَقَدْ دَخَلَ فِي وَقْتِ صَلاَةٍ أُخْرَى قَالَ« يُعِيدُهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ هَذِهِ اَلَّتِي قَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from ‘Amr ibn Yahya, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after he had entered the time of another prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat that prayer before performing the one whose time has now entered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 50

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ma’mar ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after the time of another prayer had entered. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat the former prayer before performing the one whose time has entered, unless he fears missing the one whose time has now entered."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ اَلْقِبْلَةُ وَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةٍ أُخْرَى قَالَ« يُصَلِّيهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ هَذِهِ اَلَّتِي دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَخَافَ فَوْتَ اَلَّتِي دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا» فلو لم يكن المراد بتلك الاحاديث حال الاضطرار لم يكن لايجاب الاعادة بعد خروج الوقت معنى حسب ما تضمنه هذان الخبران لان ظاهرهما يقضي انه متى تحرى القبلة وصلى ثم خرج الوقت فانه اجزأت صلاته
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ma’mar ibn Yahya, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after the time of another prayer had entered. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat the former prayer before performing the one whose time has entered, unless he fears missing the one whose time has now entered."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Ali ibn Mahzyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you pray while not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed not facing the qiblah while still within the time (of that prayer), then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ اِسْتَبَانَ لَكَ أَنَّكَ صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَأَعِدْ وَ إِنْ فَاتَكَ اَلْوَقْتُ فَلاَ تُعِدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Ali ibn Mahzyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you pray while not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed not facing the qiblah while still within the time (of that prayer), then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man is in a remote land on a cloudy day and prays not facing the qiblah, then the sky clears and he realizes that he prayed in the wrong direction, what should he do?" Imam (a.s) said: "If he is still within the time (of that prayer), then he should repeat his prayer. But if the time has passed, then his effort (ijtihad) suffices him."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ فِي قَفْرٍ مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ فِي يَوْمِ غَيْمٍ فَيُصَلِّي لِغَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ يُصْحِي فَيَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى لِغَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِدْ صَلاَتَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَضَى اَلْوَقْتُ فَحَسْبُهُ اِجْتِهَادُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man is in a remote land on a cloudy day and prays not facing the qiblah, then the sky clears and he realizes that he prayed in the wrong direction, what should he do?" Imam (a.s) said: "If he is still within the time (of that prayer), then he should repeat his prayer. But if the time has passed, then his effort (ijtihad) suffices him."

englishText: Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s): the same (report).

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you pray while not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you were not facing the qiblah while you are still within the time (of that prayer), then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
arabicText: وعنه عن محمد بن زياد عن أبان بن عثمان عن عبد الرحمن ابن أبي عبد الله عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إذا صليت وأنت على غير القبلة واستبان لك انك على غير القبلة وأنت في وقت فأعد وان فاتك فلا تعد

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih (a.s)) about a man who prayed on a cloudy day not facing the qiblah, and then the sun rose while he was still within the prayer time. Should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the qiblah, even if he had made his best effort to determine its direction? Does his prayer suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat what was within the time. But once the time has passed, there is no repetition upon him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَبْداً صَالِحاً عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى فِي يَوْمِ سَحَابٍ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ هُوَ فِي وَقْتٍ أَ يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ تَحَرَّى اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِهِ أَ تُجْزِيهِ صَلاَتُهُ فَقَالَ« يُعِيدُ مَا كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ اَلْوَقْتُ فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih (a.s)) about a man who prayed on a cloudy day not facing the qiblah, and then the sun rose while he was still within the prayer time. Should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the qiblah, even if he had made his best effort to determine its direction? Does his prayer suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat what was within the time. But once the time has passed, there is no repetition upon him."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ahmad from al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "If you prayed not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you before morning that you had prayed not facing the qiblah, then repeat your prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَاسْتَبَانَ لَكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصْبِحَ أَنَّكَ صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَأَعِدْ صَلاَتَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ahmad from al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "If you prayed not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you before morning that you had prayed not facing the qiblah, then repeat your prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said (to Imam (a.s)): "A man stands in prayer, and then after finishing he notices that he had deviated from the qiblah to the right or to the left." Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is valid. What lies between the East and the West is qiblah."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ ثُمَّ يَنْظُرُ بَعْدَ مَا فَرَغَ فَيَرَى أَنَّهُ قَدِ اِنْحَرَفَ عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ يَمِيناً وَ شِمَالاً قَالَ« قَدْ مَضَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ مَا بَيْنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ قِبْلَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said (to Imam (a.s)): "A man stands in prayer, and then after finishing he notices that he had deviated from the qiblah to the right or to the left." Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is valid. What lies between the East and the West is qiblah."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ahmad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, who said:
I asked him about a man who realizes during his prayer that he is not facing the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should turn toward it if that is confirmed. But if he has already finished the prayer, then he does not need to repeat it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ أَنَّهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُهَا إِذَا أُثْبِتَ ذَلِكَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ فَرَغَ مِنْهَا فَلاَ يُعِيدُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ahmad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about a man who realizes during his prayer that he is not facing the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should turn toward it if that is confirmed. But if he has already finished the prayer, then he does not need to repeat it."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and he realizes this while still in his prayer, before completing it. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is facing a direction between the East and the West, then he should turn his face toward the qiblah when he becomes aware. But if he is facing the opposite of the qiblah (his back toward it), then he should stop the prayer, then turn his face toward the qiblah, and then begin the prayer anew."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَيَعْلَمُ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ مُتَوَجِّهاً فِيمَا بَيْنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَلْيُحَوِّلْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ حِينَ يَعْلَمُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مُتَوَجِّهاً إِلَى دُبُرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَلْيَقْطَعْ ثُمَّ يُحَوِّلُ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynMatn: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and he realizes this while still in his prayer, before completing it. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is facing a direction between the East and the West, then he should turn his face toward the qiblah when he becomes aware. But if he is facing the opposite of the qiblah (his back toward it), then he should stop the prayer, then turn his face toward the qiblah, and then begin the prayer anew."

chapter: Chapter on the Qiblah (Direction of Prayer)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said:
I (Muhammad ibn al-Husayn) wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking; “A man prays on a cloudy day in an open desert and does not know the direction of the qiblah, so he prays, and then after finishing his prayer, the sun appears and he realizes that he had prayed in the wrong direction. Should he count his prayer as valid, or must he repeat it?” He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "He should repeat it, as long as the time has not passed. Do you not know that Allah (swt) says, and His (swt) word is the truth, ‘So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah (swt)’?" (Surah Baqarah 2:115)
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى عَبْدٍ صَالِحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي فِي يَوْمِ غَيْمٍ فِي فَلاَةٍ مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ وَ لاَ يَعْرِفُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ فَيُصَلِّي حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ بَدَتْ لَهُ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ صَلَّى لِغَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ أَ يَعْتَدُّ بِصَلاَتِهِ أَمْ يُعِيدُهَا فَكَتَبَ« يُعِيدُهَا مَا لَمْ يَفُتْهُ اَلْوَقْتُ أَوَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اَللَّهَ يَقُولُ وَقَوْلُهُ اَلْحَقُّ« فَأَيْنَمٰا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اَللّٰهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Muhammad ibn al-Husayn) wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking; “A man prays on a cloudy day in an open desert and does not know the direction of the qiblah, so he prays, and then after finishing his prayer, the sun appears and he realizes that he had prayed in the wrong direction. Should he count his prayer as valid, or must he repeat it?” He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "He should repeat it, as long as the time has not passed. Do you not know that Allah (swt) says, and His (swt) word is the truth, ‘So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah (swt)’?" (Surah Baqarah 2:115)

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahb or Ibn ‘Ammar from al-Sabbah ibn Sayyabah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me (al-Sabbah): "Do not abandon the adhan in any of the prayers. But if you do leave it, then do not leave it for Maghrib and Fajr, for there is no shortening in them."
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ أَوِ اِبْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ:« لاَ تَدَعِ اَلْأَذَانَ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا فَإِنْ تَرَكْتَهُ فَلاَ تَتْرُكْهُ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا تَقْصِيرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahb or Ibn ‘Ammar from al-Sabbah ibn Sayyabah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me (al-Sabbah): "Do not abandon the adhan in any of the prayers. But if you do leave it, then do not leave it for Maghrib and Fajr, for there is no shortening in them."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When you stand for an obligatory prayer, then give the adhan and the iqamah, and separate between the adhan and the iqamah by sitting, or by speaking, or by glorifying (tasbih)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ فَأَذِّنْ وَ أَقِمْ وَ اِفْصِلْ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ بِقُعُودٍ أَوْ بِكَلاَمٍ أَوْ بِتَسْبِيحٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When you stand for an obligatory prayer, then give the adhan and the iqamah, and separate between the adhan and the iqamah by sitting, or by speaking, or by glorifying (tasbih)."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s): "Is one adhan sufficient?" Imam (a.s) said: "If you are praying in congregation, then one adhan and one iqamah are required. But if you are alone and hastening due to a matter you fear may pass you by, then the iqamah suffices, except for Fajr and Maghrib, for it is proper that you give the adhan and the iqamah for them, because they are not shortened like the other prayers."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ أَ يُجْزِي أَذَانٌ وَاحِدٌ قَالَ« إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ جَمَاعَةً لَمْ يُجْزِ إِلاَّ أَذَانٌ وَ إِقَامَةٌ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ تُبَادِرُ أَمْراً تَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْوتَكَ يُجْزِيكَ إِقَامَةٌ إِلاَّ اَلْفَجْرَ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُؤَذِّنَ فِيهِمَا وَ تُقِيمَ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّهُ لاَ تَقْصُرُ فِيهِمَا كَمَا تَقْصُرُ فِي سَائِرِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s): "Is one adhan sufficient?" Imam (a.s) said: "If you are praying in congregation, then one adhan and one iqamah are required. But if you are alone and hastening due to a matter you fear may pass you by, then the iqamah suffices, except for Fajr and Maghrib, for it is proper that you give the adhan and the iqamah for them, because they are not shortened like the other prayers."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If the people are not waiting for anyone, then one iqamah alone suffices."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْقَوْمُ لاَ يَنْتَظِرُونَ أَحَداً اِكْتَفَوْا بِإِقَامَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If the people are not waiting for anyone, then one iqamah alone suffices."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (narrates) from his father (a.s): "That He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)), when He (a.s) prayed alone in the house, would give the iqamah and would not give the adhan."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ:« أَنَّهُ كَانَ إِذَا صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ أَقَامَ إِقَامَةً وَ لَمْ يُؤَذِّنْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (narrates) from his father (a.s): "That He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)), when He (a.s) prayed alone in the house, would give the iqamah and would not give the adhan."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "It suffices you, when you are alone in your house, to give one iqamah without an adhan."
arabicText: وَرَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ إِذَا خَلَوْتَ فِي بَيْتِكَ إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "It suffices you, when you are alone in your house, to give one iqamah without an adhan."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Do not pray the morning (ghadah) and Maghrib prayers except with adhan and iqamah, and it is permitted in the rest of the prayers to suffice with the iqamah, but the adhan is better."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ أَخِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ اَلْغَدَاةَ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ إِلاَّ بِأَذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَةٍ وَ رُخِّصَ فِي سَائِرِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ بِالْإِقَامَةِ وَ اَلْأَذَانُ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Do not pray the morning (ghadah) and Maghrib prayers except with adhan and iqamah, and it is permitted in the rest of the prayers to suffice with the iqamah, but the adhan is better."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "One iqamah suffices you for the prayer, except for the morning (ghadah) and Maghrib."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ إِلاَّ اَلْغَدَاةَ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "One iqamah suffices you for the prayer, except for the morning (ghadah) and Maghrib."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about giving the iqamah without the adhan for Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm in it, but I do not like that it becomes a habit."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْإِقَامَةِ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يُعْتَادَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about giving the iqamah without the adhan for Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm in it, but I do not like that it becomes a habit."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: "The adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is shortened. One iqamah suffices."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« يُقْصَرُ اَلْأَذَانُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ كَمَا تُقْصَرُ اَلصَّلاَةُ تُجْزِي إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: "The adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is shortened. One iqamah suffices."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man, does it suffice him in travel and at home to give only the iqamah without the adhan? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, there is no harm in it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يُجْزِيهِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ اَلْحَضَرِ إِقَامَةٌ لَيْسَ مَعَهَا أَذَانٌ قَالَ« نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man, does it suffice him in travel and at home to give only the iqamah without the adhan? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, there is no harm in it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
(Imam (a.s)), peace be upon them, said: "One iqamah suffices you in travel."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تُجْزِيكَ إِقَامَةٌ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ» فدلت هذه الاخبار على أن الاولى في الحضر فعل الاذان لانها تضمنت الرخصة في حال السفر ولو لم يكن الامر على ما ذكرناه لم يكن لاختصاصه بحال السفر فائدة
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon them, said: "One iqamah suffices you in travel."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Yahya al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you give the adhan and the iqamah in an open, deserted land, two rows of angels will pray behind you. But if you give only the iqamah without the adhan, then one row of angels will pray behind you."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ فِي أَرْضِ فَلاَةٍ وَ أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفَّانِ مِنَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ وَ إِنْ أَقَمْتَ وَ لَمْ تُؤَذِّنْ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفٌّ وَاحِدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Yahya al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you give the adhan and the iqamah in an open, deserted land, two rows of angels will pray behind you. But if you give only the iqamah without the adhan, then one row of angels will pray behind you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me (Muhammad ibn Muslim): "Indeed, if you give the adhan and the iqamah, two rows of angels will pray behind you. But if you give only the iqamah without the adhan, then one row of angels will pray behind you."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :«إِنَّكَ إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ وَ أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفَّانِ مِنَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ وَ إِنْ أَقَمْتَ إِقَامَةً بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفٌّ وَاحِدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me (Muhammad ibn Muslim): "Indeed, if you give the adhan and the iqamah, two rows of angels will pray behind you. But if you give only the iqamah without the adhan, then one row of angels will pray behind you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Halabi from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "The mu’adhdhin (caller to prayer) is forgiven for the extent of his voice, and everything that hears him bears witness for him."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ مَدَّ صَوْتِهِ وَ يَشْهَدُ لَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ سَمِعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Halabi from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "The mu’adhdhin (caller to prayer) is forgiven for the extent of his voice, and everything that hears him bears witness for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from Yahya al-Halabi from ‘Imran ibn Ali, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about giving the adhan before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is in congregation, then no [it is not permissible]; but if he is alone, then there is no harm."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ يَحْيَى اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْأَذَانِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَلاَ وَ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from Yahya al-Halabi from ‘Imran ibn Ali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about giving the adhan before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is in congregation, then no [it is not permissible]; but if he is alone, then there is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "We have a mu’adhdhin who gives the adhan during the night." Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, that benefits the neighbors by prompting them to rise for prayer. But as for the sunnah, it is that the call (adhan) is made at the rising of the dawn (tulu’ al-fajr), and there should be nothing between the adhan and the iqamah except the two [Sunnah] rak’ahs."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ لَنَا مُؤَذِّناً يُؤَذِّنُ بِلَيْلٍ فَقَالَ« أَمَا إِنَّ ذَلِكَ يَنْفَعُ اَلْجِيرَانَ لِقِيَامِهِمْ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ أَمَّا اَلسُّنَّةُ فَإِنَّهُ يُنَادَى مَعَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ لاَ يَكُونُ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ إِلاَّ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "We have a mu’adhdhin who gives the adhan during the night." Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, that benefits the neighbors by prompting them to rise for prayer. But as for the sunnah, it is that the call (adhan) is made at the rising of the dawn (tulu’ al-fajr), and there should be nothing between the adhan and the iqamah except the two [Sunnah] rak’ahs."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about calling (the adhan) before the rising of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm, but the sunnah is to call at the time of Fajr. And indeed, that (calling before Fajr) benefits the neighbors", meaning, before the Fajr.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلنِّدَاءِ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ وَ أَمَّا اَلسُّنَّةُ مَعَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيَنْفَعُ اَلْجِيرَانَ يَعْنِي قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about calling (the adhan) before the rising of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm, but the sunnah is to call at the time of Fajr. And indeed, that (calling before Fajr) benefits the neighbors", meaning, before the Fajr.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm in giving the adhan while you are not in a state of purity (wuduʾ), but do not give the iqamah except while you are in a state of wuduʾ."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُؤَذِّنَ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ طَهُورٍ وَ لاَ تُقِيمُ إِلاَّ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm in giving the adhan while you are not in a state of purity (wuduʾ), but do not give the iqamah except while you are in a state of wuduʾ."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm if a man gives the adhan while not in a state of wuduʾ, but he should not give the iqamah unless he is in a state of wuduʾ."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَ لاَ يُقِيمُ إِلاَّ وَ هُوَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm if a man gives the adhan while not in a state of wuduʾ, but he should not give the iqamah unless he is in a state of wuduʾ."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub ibn Fayhas from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (narrates) from his father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)), that (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: "There is no harm if a boy gives the adhan before reaching puberty, and there is no harm if the mu’adhdhin gives the adhan while in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), but he should not give the iqamah until he has performed ghusl."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بِي مُوسَى اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ كَلُّوبِ بْنِ فَيْهَسٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ اَلْغُلاَمُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَحْتَلِمَ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ وَ هُوَ جُنُبٌ وَ لاَ يُقِيمُ حَتَّى يَغْتَسِلَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub ibn Fayhas from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (narrates) from his father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)), that (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: "There is no harm if a boy gives the adhan before reaching puberty, and there is no harm if the mu’adhdhin gives the adhan while in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), but he should not give the iqamah until he has performed ghusl."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man speak during the adhan?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm." I asked: "What about during the iqamah?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يَتَكَلَّمُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي اَلْأَذَانِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» قُلْتُ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man speak during the adhan?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm." I asked: "What about during the iqamah?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the mu’adhdhin, may he speak while giving the adhan? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm after he finishes his adhan."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُؤَذِّنِ أَ يَتَكَلَّمُ وَ هُوَ يُؤَذِّنُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ حِينَ يَفْرُغُ مِنْ أَذَانِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the mu’adhdhin, may he speak while giving the adhan? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm after he finishes his adhan."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man speak during the adhan?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: وعنه عن أحمد عن الحسين بن سعيد عن فضالة بن أيوب عن الحسين بن عثمان عن عمرو بن أبي نصر قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام أيتكلم الرجل في الاذان؟ قال لا بأس
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from ‘Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man speak during the adhan?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "O Abu Harun, the iqamah is part of the prayer, so when you have given the iqamah, do not speak and do not gesture with your hand."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ أَبِي هَارُونَ اَلْمَكْفُوفِ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ:« يَا أَبَا هَارُونَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَإِذَا أَقَمْتَ فَلاَ تَتَكَلَّمْ وَلاَ تُومِ بِيَدِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "O Abu Harun, the iqamah is part of the prayer, so when you have given the iqamah, do not speak and do not gesture with your hand."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who speaks during his adhan or during his iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي أَذَانِهِ أَوْ فِي إِقَامَتِهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who speaks during his adhan or during his iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man, may he speak after he has given the iqamah for prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ أَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بَعْدَ مَا يُقِيمُ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man, may he speak after he has given the iqamah for prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ja’far ibn Bashir from al-Hasan ibn Shihab, who said:
I (al-Hasan ibn Shihab) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "There is no harm if a man speaks while he is giving the iqamah, or after he has given the iqamah, if he wishes."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ يُقِيمُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ بَعْدَ مَا يُقِيمُ إِنْ شَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ja’far ibn Bashir from al-Hasan ibn Shihab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (al-Hasan ibn Shihab) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "There is no harm if a man speaks while he is giving the iqamah, or after he has given the iqamah, if he wishes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who speaks during the iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but when the mu’adhdhin says ‘Qad qamat al-salah’ (the prayer has been established), then speech becomes forbidden for the people in the mosque, except if they have gathered from different places and have no imam; then there is no harm if some of them say to one another, ‘Go ahead, so-and-so (and lead the prayer).’"
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ فَإِذَا قَالَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ قَدْ قَامَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَقَدْ حَرُمَ اَلْكَلاَمُ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونُوا قَدِ اِجْتَمَعُوا مِنْ شَتَّى وَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ إِمَامٌ فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يَقُولَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ تَقَدَّمْ يَا فُلاَنُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who speaks during the iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but when the mu’adhdhin says ‘Qad qamat al-salah’ (the prayer has been established), then speech becomes forbidden for the people in the mosque, except if they have gathered from different places and have no imam; then there is no harm if some of them say to one another, ‘Go ahead, so-and-so (and lead the prayer).’"

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When the mu’adhdhin gives the iqamah for the prayer, then speaking becomes prohibited, except if the people do not have a known imam."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا أَقَامَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقَدْ حَرُمَ اَلْكَلاَمُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ اَلْقَوْمُ لَيْسَ يُعْرَفُ لَهُمْ إِمَامٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When the mu’adhdhin gives the iqamah for the prayer, then speaking becomes prohibited, except if the people do not have a known imam."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Do not speak once you have given the iqamah for the prayer, for if you speak, you must repeat the iqamah."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ تَتَكَلَّمْ إِذَا أَقَمْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتَ أَعَدْتَ اَلْإِقَامَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Do not speak once you have given the iqamah for the prayer, for if you speak, you must repeat the iqamah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 60

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm in giving the adhan while riding, walking, or without wuduʾ. But do not give the iqamah while riding or sitting, except due to an ailment or if you are in a slippery land."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُؤَذِّنَ رَاكِباً أَوْ مَاشِياً أَوْ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَ لاَ تُقِيمُ وَ أَنْتَ رَاكِبٌ أَوْ جَالِسٌ إِلاَّ مِنْ عِلَّةٍ أَوْ تَكُونَ فِي أَرْضٍ مَلَصَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm in giving the adhan while riding, walking, or without wuduʾ. But do not give the iqamah while riding or sitting, except due to an ailment or if you are in a slippery land."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 60

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm for a traveller to give the adhan while riding, and to give the iqamah while standing on the ground."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ لِلْمُسَافِرِ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ وَ هُوَ رَاكِبٌ وَ يُقِيمُ وَ هُوَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَائِمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "There is no harm for a traveller to give the adhan while riding, and to give the iqamah while standing on the ground."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 60

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Hammad from Rib’i from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man give the adhan while sitting?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but he should not give the iqamah except while standing."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُؤَذِّنُ اَلرَّجُلُ وَهُوَ قَاعِدٌ قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ لاَ يُقِيمُ إِلاَّ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Hammad from Rib’i from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "May a man give the adhan while sitting?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but he should not give the iqamah except while standing."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 60

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated from him from Ahmad ibn Muhammad:
The Righteous servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, said: "A man may give the adhan while sitting, but he should not give the iqamah except while standing." And Imam (a.s) said: "You may give the adhan while riding, but do not give the iqamah except while on the ground."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدٍ صَالِحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُؤَذِّنُ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ لاَ يُقِيمُ إِلاَّ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ» وَ قَالَ« تُؤَذِّنُ وَ أَنْتَ رَاكِبٌ وَ لاَ تُقِيمُ إِلاَّ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated from him from Ahmad ibn Muhammad:
thaqalaynMatn: The Righteous servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, said: "A man may give the adhan while sitting, but he should not give the iqamah except while standing." And Imam (a.s) said: "You may give the adhan while riding, but do not give the iqamah except while on the ground."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 61

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Narrated from him from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who gives the adhan while walking, or on the back of his animal, or without being in a state of ritual purity. Imam (a.s) said: "If the tashahhud (the part of the adhan with ‘Ashhadu...’) is said while facing the qiblah, then there is no harm."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ هُوَ يَمْشِي أَوْ عَلَى ظَهْرِ دَابَّتِهِ وَ عَلَى غَيْرِ طَهُورٍ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلتَّشَهُّدُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynMatn: Narrated from him from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who gives the adhan while walking, or on the back of his animal, or without being in a state of ritual purity. Imam (a.s) said: "If the tashahhud (the part of the adhan with ‘Ashhadu...’) is said while facing the qiblah, then there is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Sulayman ibn Salih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "None of you should give the iqamah for prayer while walking, or riding, or lying down, unless he is ill. And let him be firmly settled during the iqamah just as he is firmly settled during the prayer, for when he begins the iqamah, he is already in a state of prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يُقِيمُ أَحَدُكُمُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَهُوَ مَاشٍ وَلاَ رَاكِبٌ وَلاَ مُضْطَجِعٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَرِيضاً وَ لْيَتَمَكَّنْ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ كَمَا يَتَمَكَّنُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا أَخَذَ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ فَهُوَ فِي صَلاَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Sulayman ibn Salih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "None of you should give the iqamah for prayer while walking, or riding, or lying down, unless he is ill. And let him be firmly settled during the iqamah just as he is firmly settled during the prayer, for when he begins the iqamah, he is already in a state of prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 61

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Buzay’ from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Yunus al-Nisbani from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "May I give the adhan while I am riding?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: "Then may I give the iqamah while I am riding?" Imam (a.s) said: "No." I asked: "May I give the iqamah while I am walking?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, walking toward the prayer." Then Imam (a.s) said to me: "When you give the iqamah, give it calmly (with composure), for indeed you are in the prayer." I said to Him (a.s): "But I asked you whether I may give the iqamah while walking, and you said yes. So is it permissible for me to walk while in prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if you enter from the door of the mosque and you have said the takbir while following a just imam, and then you walk toward the prayer, that suffices for you."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ يُونُسَ النسباني عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أُؤَذِّنُ وَ أَنَا رَاكِبٌ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقُلْتُ فَأُقِيمُ وَ أَنَا رَاكِبٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ» قُلْتُ فَأُقِيمُ وَ أَنَا مَاشٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ مَاشٍ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ» قَالَ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي« إِذَا أَقَمْتَ فَأَقِمْ مُتَرَسِّلاً فَإِنَّكَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَقَدْ سَأَلْتُكَ أُقِيمُ وَ أَنَا مَاشٍ فَقُلْتَ لِي نَعَمْ أَ فَيَجُوزُ أَنْ أَمْشِيَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ مِنْ بَابِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَكَبَّرْتَ وَ أَنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ ثُمَّ مَشَيْتَ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ أَجْزَأَكَ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Buzay’ from Salih ibn ‘Uqba from Yunus al-Nisbani from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "May I give the adhan while I am riding?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: "Then may I give the iqamah while I am riding?" Imam (a.s) said: "No." I asked: "May I give the iqamah while I am walking?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, walking toward the prayer." Then Imam (a.s) said to me: "When you give the iqamah, give it calmly (with composure), for indeed you are in the prayer." I said to Him (a.s): "But I asked you whether I may give the iqamah while walking, and you said yes. So is it permissible for me to walk while in prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if you enter from the door of the mosque and you have said the takbir while following a just imam, and then you walk toward the prayer, that suffices for you."
