chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu Khalid from Humran, who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about giving the adhan while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "No one gives the adhan while sitting except one who is riding or ill."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي خَالِدٍ عَنْ حُمْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْأَذَانِ جَالِساً قَالَ« لاَ يُؤَذِّنُ جَالِساً إِلاَّ رَاكِبٌ أَوْ مَرِيضٌ» فهذا الخبر محمول على الاستحباب لانا قد بينا جواز الاذان جالسا من غير علة وهذا محمول على الفضل والندب
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu Khalid from Humran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about giving the adhan while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "No one gives the adhan while sitting except one who is riding or ill."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 61

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated to us from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a woman, is adhan and iqamah obligatory upon her? Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ أَ عَلَيْهَا أَذَانٌ وَ إِقَامَةٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: al-Husayn ibn Sa’id narrated to us from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a woman, is adhan and iqamah obligatory upon her? Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 62

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘eed from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Are women required to perform the Adhan?” Imam (a.s) said: “If she proclaims the two testimonies, that is sufficient for her.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلنِّسَاءُ عَلَيْهِنَّ أَذَانٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا شَهِدَتِ اَلشَّهَادَتَيْنِ فَحَسْبُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘eed from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Are women required to perform the Adhan?” Imam (a.s) said: “If she proclaims the two testimonies, that is sufficient for her.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 62

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr and Fadhala, from Abdullah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a woman giving the Adhan for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is good if she does so, and if she does not do it, it suffices for her to say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and to bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) and that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) send blessings upon him and his family.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ وَفَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُؤَذِّنُ لِلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« حَسَنٌ إِنْ فَعَلَتْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ أَجْزَأَهَا أَنْ تُكَبِّرَ وَ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِِه» قال الشيخ رحمه الله
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr and Fadhala, from Abdullah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a woman giving the Adhan for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is good if she does so, and if she does not do it, it suffices for her to say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and to bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) and that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) send blessings upon him and his family.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 62

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Adhan is to be pronounced clearly, with articulation of the Alif’ and the ‘ha’, and the Iqamah is to be recited quickly in a flowing manner.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «اَلْأَذَانُ جَزْمٌ بِإِفْصَاحِ اَلْأَلِفِ وَ اَلْهَاءِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ حَدْرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Adhan is to be pronounced clearly, with articulation of the Alif’ and the ‘ha’, and the Iqamah is to be recited quickly in a flowing manner.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Khalid ibn Najeeh:
(Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Takbir is to be pronounced firmly in the Adhan with clear articulation of the ‘ha’ and the Alif’.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ نَجِيحٍ عَنِ اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ جَزْمٌ فِي اَلْأَذَانِ مَعَ اَلْإِفْصَاحِ بِالْهَاءِ وَ اَلْأَلِفِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Khalid ibn Najeeh:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Takbir is to be pronounced firmly in the Adhan with clear articulation of the ‘ha’ and the Alif’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you perform the Adhan, do not lower your voice, for Allah (swt) rewards you for extending your voice in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ فَلاَ تُخْفِيَنَّ صَوْتَكَ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ يَأْجُرُكَ مَدَّ صَوْتِكَ فِيهِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you perform the Adhan, do not lower your voice, for Allah (swt) rewards you for extending your voice in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The height of the wall of Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was the height of a man, so He (saws), peace be upon him, used to say to Bilal; ‘When the time (for prayer) enters, O Bilal, climb up on top of the wall and raise your voice with the Adhan, for indeed Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has assigned a wind for the Adhan that carries it up to the heavens. And indeed, when the angels hear the Adhan from the people of the earth, they say: ‘These are the voices of the nation of Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, proclaiming the oneness of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and they seek forgiveness for the nation of Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, until they complete that prayer.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلٍ عَنِ اِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ طُولُ حَائِطِ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَامَةً فَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ لِبِلاَلٍ« إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلْوَقْتُ يَا بِلاَلُ اُعْلُ فَوْقَ اَلْجِدَارِ وَ اِرْفَعْ صَوْتَكَ بِالْأَذَانِ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَدْ وَكَّلَ بِالْأَذَانِ رِيحاً تَرْفَعُهُ إِلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ إِنَّ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةَ إِذَا سَمِعُوا اَلْأَذَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْأَرْضِ قَالُوا هَذِهِ أَصْوَاتُ أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِتَوْحِيدِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِأُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حَتَّى يَفْرُغُوا مِنْ تِلْكَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The height of the wall of Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was the height of a man, so He (saws), peace be upon him, used to say to Bilal; ‘When the time (for prayer) enters, O Bilal, climb up on top of the wall and raise your voice with the Adhan, for indeed Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has assigned a wind for the Adhan that carries it up to the heavens. And indeed, when the angels hear the Adhan from the people of the earth, they say: ‘These are the voices of the nation of Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, proclaiming the oneness of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and they seek forgiveness for the nation of Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, until they complete that prayer.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and the Iqamah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Rashid who said: Hisham ibn Ibrahim narrated to me:
He (Hisham ibn Ibrahim) complained to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about his illness and that he had no children. So He (a.s) instructed him to raise his voice with the Adhan in his house. He (Hisham ibn Ibrahim) said: ‘I did so, and Allah (swt) removed my illness and increased my children.’
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: أَنَّهُ شَكَا إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ سُقْمَهُ وَأَنَّهُ لاَ يُولَدُ لَهُ فَأَمَرَهُ بِأَنْ يَرْفَعَ صَوْتَهُ بِالْأَذَانِ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَأَذْهَبَ اَللَّهُ عَنِّي سُقْمِي وَكَثُرَ وُلْدِي.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Rashid who said: Hisham ibn Ibrahim narrated to me:
thaqalaynMatn: He (Hisham ibn Ibrahim) complained to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about his illness and that he had no children. So He (a.s) instructed him to raise his voice with the Adhan in his house. He (Hisham ibn Ibrahim) said: ‘I did so, and Allah (swt) removed my illness and increased my children.’

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi who said:
I heard (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “The Adhan and the Iqamah are thirty-five phrases.” Then He (a.s) counted them with His (a.s) hand, one by one: “The Adhan is eighteen phrases, and the Iqamah is seventeen phrases.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« اَلْأَذَانُ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ خَمْسَةٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ حَرْفاً فَعَدَّ ذَلِكَ بِيَدِهِ وَاحِداً وَاحِداً اَلْأَذَانَ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفاً وَ اَلْإِقَامَةَ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “The Adhan and the Iqamah are thirty-five phrases.” Then He (a.s) counted them with His (a.s) hand, one by one: “The Adhan is eighteen phrases, and the Iqamah is seventeen phrases.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the Adhan. Imam (a.s) said: “You say, ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadur Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadur Rasulullah, Hayya alas-salah, Hayya alas-salah, Hayya alal-falah, Hayya alal-falah, Hayya ala khayril-amal, Hayya ala khayril-amal, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah La ilaha illallah.’” (Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt). I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt). Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah (swt), there is no god but Allah (swt).)
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْأَذَانِ فَقَالَ« تَقُولُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the Adhan. Imam (a.s) said: “You say, ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadur Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadur Rasulullah, Hayya alas-salah, Hayya alas-salah, Hayya alal-falah, Hayya alal-falah, Hayya ala khayril-amal, Hayya ala khayril-amal, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah La ilaha illallah.’” (Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt). I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt). Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah (swt), there is no god but Allah (swt).)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar:
(Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was taken on the night journey and reached the Bayt al-Ma‘mur, the time of prayer came, so Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, gave the Adhan and the Iqamah. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, stepped forward, and the angels and the prophets lined up behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” He (ibn Yasar) said: “So we (Zurarah and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar) said to Him (a.s), “How did He (saws) give the Adhan?” Imam (a.s) said: “‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah; Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal; Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah.’ And the Iqamah is like it, except that in it is: ‘Qad qamatis-salah, qad qamatis-salah’ placed between ‘Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal’ and ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.’ So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, instructed Bilal with it, and he (Bilal) continued to call it until Allah (swt) took the soul of His Messenger, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَمَّا أُسْرِيَ بِرَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَبَلَغَ اَلْبَيْتَ اَلْمَعْمُورَ حَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَأَذَّنَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَأَقَامَ فَتَقَدَّمَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ صَفَّ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَاَلنَّبِيُّونَ خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ» قَالَ فَقُلْنَا لَهُ كَيْفَ أَذَّنَ فَقَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ» «وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ مِثْلُهَا إِلاَّ أَنَّ فِيهَا قَدْ قَامَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ قَدْ قَامَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ بَيْنَ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ وَ بَيْنَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَأَمَرَ بِهَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِلاَلاً فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُؤَذِّنُ بِهَا حَتَّى قَبَضَ اَللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was taken on the night journey and reached the Bayt al-Ma‘mur, the time of prayer came, so Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, gave the Adhan and the Iqamah. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, stepped forward, and the angels and the prophets lined up behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” He (ibn Yasar) said: “So we (Zurarah and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar) said to Him (a.s), “How did He (saws) give the Adhan?” Imam (a.s) said: “‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah; Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal; Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah.’ And the Iqamah is like it, except that in it is: ‘Qad qamatis-salah, qad qamatis-salah’ placed between ‘Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal’ and ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.’ So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, instructed Bilal with it, and he (Bilal) continued to call it until Allah (swt) took the soul of His Messenger, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Fadhala from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from Abu Abdillah (a.s), and from Kulayb al-Asadi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) recited the Adhan to both of them (Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Kulayb al-Asadi), and Imam (a.s) said: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah; Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal; Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah. And the Iqamah is likewise.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ كُلَيْبٍ اَلْأَسَدِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ حَكَى لَهُمَا اَلْأَذَانَ فَقَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ اَلْعَمَلِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ كَذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Fadhala from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from Abu Abdillah (a.s), and from Kulayb al-Asadi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) recited the Adhan to both of them (Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Kulayb al-Asadi), and Imam (a.s) said: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah; Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal, Hayya ‘ala khayr al-‘amal; Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah. And the Iqamah is likewise.”

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from al-Mu‘alla ibn Khunays who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) performing the Adhan, and Imam (a.s) said: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah”, until He (a.s) completed the Adhan. Imam (a.s) said at the end of it: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلْمُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُؤَذِّنُ فَقَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ» حَتَّى فَرَغَ مِنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ قَالَ فِي آخِرِهِ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from al-Mu‘alla ibn Khunays who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) performing the Adhan, and Imam (a.s) said: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah; Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah; Hayya ‘ala al-salah, Hayya ‘ala al-salah; Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah”, until He (a.s) completed the Adhan. Imam (a.s) said at the end of it: “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar; La ilaha illallah, La ilaha illallah.”

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Zurarah:
(Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “O Zurarah, you begin the Adhan with four Takbirs and you end it with two Takbirs and two declarations of ‘La ilaha illallah’.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَا زُرَارَةُ تَفْتَتِحُ اَلْأَذَانَ بِأَرْبَعِ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَ تَخْتِمُهُ بِتَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ وَ تَهْلِيلَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “O Zurarah, you begin the Adhan with four Takbirs and you end it with two Takbirs and two declarations of ‘La ilaha illallah’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Adhan is in pairs, two by two, and the Iqamah is single, one by one.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْأَذَانُ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ وَاحِدَةً وَاحِدَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Adhan is in pairs, two by two, and the Iqamah is single, one by one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Iqamah is once, once, except for the statement ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar’, for it is said twice.”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْإِقَامَةُ مَرَّةً مَرَّةً إِلاَّ قَوْلَهُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَإِنَّهُ مَرَّتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Iqamah is once, once, except for the statement ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar’, for it is said twice.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who said:
I (al-Hadhdha’) saw (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying the Takbir one by one in the Adhan, so I said to Him (a.s): “Why are you saying the Takbir one by one?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it if you are in a hurry.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ اَلْحَذَّاءِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُكَبِّرُ وَاحِدَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي اَلْأَذَانِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لِمَ تُكَبِّرُ وَاحِدَةً وَاحِدَةً فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِذَا كُنْتَ مُسْتَعْجِلاً»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (al-Hadhdha’) saw (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying the Takbir one by one in the Adhan, so I said to Him (a.s): “Why are you saying the Takbir one by one?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it if you are in a hurry.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Adhan is in pairs, two by two, and the Iqamah is in pairs, two by two.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «اَلْأَذَانُ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Adhan is in pairs, two by two, and the Iqamah is in pairs, two by two.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadhala from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Yazid, the client of al-Hakam, from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), he said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “For me to perform the Iqamah in pairs, two by two, is more beloved to me than to perform the Adhan and the Iqamah each as single statements, one by one.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ مَوْلَى اَلْحَكَمِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« لَأَنْ أُقِيمَ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُؤَذِّنَ وَ أُقِيمَ وَاحِداً وَاحِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadhala from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Yazid, the client of al-Hakam, from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “For me to perform the Iqamah in pairs, two by two, is more beloved to me than to perform the Adhan and the Iqamah each as single statements, one by one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah:
(Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is shortened, the Adhan is single, one by one, and the Iqamah is single, one by one.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْأَذَانُ يُقْصَرُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ كَمَا تُقْصَرُ اَلصَّلاَةُ اَلْأَذَانُ وَاحِداً وَاحِداً وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ وَاحِدَةً وَاحِدَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is shortened, the Adhan is single, one by one, and the Iqamah is single, one by one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Nu‘man al-Razi who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “It suffices you in place of the Iqamah during travel to say each phrase once, once.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ نُعْمَانَ اَلرَّازِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «يُجْزِيكَ عَنِ اَلْإِقَامَةِ طَاقٌ طَاقٌ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Nu‘man al-Razi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “It suffices you in place of the Iqamah during travel to say each phrase once, once.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu‘ayb ibn Ya‘qub from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The call (Adhan) and the repetition (Tathwib) in the Iqamah are from the Sunnah.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلنِّدَاءُ وَ اَلتَّثْوِيبُ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu‘ayb ibn Ya‘qub from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The call (Adhan) and the repetition (Tathwib) in the Iqamah are from the Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was also narrated by him from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from Fadhala from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
(Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “My father (a.s) used to call out in His (a.s) house; ‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’ (Prayer is better than sleep), and if you repeat that, there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ هُوَ أَيْضاً عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَبِي يُنَادِي فِي بَيْتِهِ« بِاَلصَّلاَةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اَلنَّوْمِ» وَ لَوْ رَدَّدْتَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهِ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was also narrated by him from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from Fadhala from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “My father (a.s) used to call out in His (a.s) house; ‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’ (Prayer is better than sleep), and if you repeat that, there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the ‘tathwib’ (‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’) that occurs between the Adhan and the Iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: “We do not recognize it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّثْوِيبِ اَلَّذِي يَكُونُ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ فَقَالَ« مَا نَعْرِفُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the ‘tathwib’ (‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’) that occurs between the Adhan and the Iqamah. Imam (a.s) said: “We do not recognize it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
(Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “O Zurarah, you begin the Adhan with four Takbirs and you end it with two Takbirs and two declarations of ‘La ilaha illallah ‘. And if you wish, you may add in place of ‘tathwib’, after ‘Hayya ‘ala al-falah’, the phrase ‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا زُرَارَةُ تَفْتَتِحُ اَلْأَذَانَ بِأَرْبَعِ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَتَخْتِمُهُ بِتَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ وَ تَهْلِيلَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ زِدْتَ عَلَى اَلتَّثْوِيبِ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ مَكَانَ اَلصَّلاَةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اَلنَّوْمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “O Zurarah, you begin the Adhan with four Takbirs and you end it with two Takbirs and two declarations of ‘La ilaha illallah ‘. And if you wish, you may add in place of ‘tathwib’, after ‘Hayya ‘ala al-falah’, the phrase ‘Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 67

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If a mu’adhdhin were to repeat the testimony or ‘Hayya ‘ala al-salah’ or ‘Hayya ‘ala al-falah’ two times, three times, or more than that, if he is an imam who wishes to gather the people together for congregational prayer, then there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَوْ أَنَّ مُؤَذِّناً أَعَادَ فِي اَلشَّهَادَةِ وَ فِي حَيَّ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ أَوْ حَيَّ عَلَى اَلْفَلاَحِ اَلْمَرَّتَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثَ وَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَ إِمَاماً يُرِيدُ جَمَاعَةَ اَلْقَوْمِ لِيَجْمَعَهُمْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهِ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If a mu’adhdhin were to repeat the testimony or ‘Hayya ‘ala al-salah’ or ‘Hayya ‘ala al-falah’ two times, three times, or more than that, if he is an imam who wishes to gather the people together for congregational prayer, then there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 68

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from al-Hasan ibn Shihab:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There must be a sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لاَ بُدَّ مِنْ قُعُودٍ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from al-Hasan ibn Shihab:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There must be a sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 68

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “Separate between the Adhan and the Iqamah with a sitting or with two units of prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْجَعْفَرِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« اُفْرُقْ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ بِجُلُوسٍ أَوْ بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “Separate between the Adhan and the Iqamah with a sitting or with two units of prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 68

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad:
He (Imam al-Ridha (a.s)) said: “The sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah is for all the prayers, if there is no prayer being performed before the Iqamah.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ:« اَلْقُعُودُ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ كُلِّهَا إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ قَبْلَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ صَلاَةٌ يُصَلِّيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad:
thaqalaynMatn: He (Imam al-Ridha (a.s)) said: “The sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah is for all the prayers, if there is no prayer being performed before the Iqamah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 68

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Sayf ibn Umayrah from one of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Between every two Adhans (between the Adhan and the Iqamah) there is a sitting, except for Maghrib, for between them is only a brief pause.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« بَيْنَ كُلِّ أَذَانَيْنِ قَعْدَةٌ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّ بَيْنَهُمَا نَفَساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Sayf ibn Umayrah from one of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Between every two Adhans (between the Adhan and the Iqamah) there is a sitting, except for Maghrib, for between them is only a brief pause.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 68

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Rashid from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Yaqtin, who raised it to them:
(Imam (a.s)) said: “When a man finishes the Adhan and sits, he says: ‘O Allah (swt), make my heart righteous, and my sustenance flowing, and grant me a place and a settlement near the grave of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ رَفَعَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ:« يَقُولُ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ جَلَسَ اَللَّهُمَّ اِجْعَلْ قَلْبِي بَارّاً وَ رِزْقِي دَارّاً وَ اِجْعَلْ لِي عِنْدَ قَبْرِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَرَاراً وَ مُسْتَقَرّاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Rashid from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Yaqtin, who raised it to them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: “When a man finishes the Adhan and sits, he says: ‘O Allah (swt), make my heart righteous, and my sustenance flowing, and grant me a place and a settlement near the grave of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq al-Jariri:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever sits between the Adhan of Maghrib and the Iqamah, it is as if he were covered in his own blood in the path of Allah (swt).”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْجَرِيرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ قَالَ:« مَنْ جَلَسَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ أَذَانِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ كَانَ كَالْمُتَشَحِّطِ بِدَمِهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اَللَّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq al-Jariri:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever sits between the Adhan of Maghrib and the Iqamah, it is as if he were covered in his own blood in the path of Allah (swt).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on the Number of Phrases in the Adhan and Iqamah, and Their Description
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Adhan is to be recited with measured recitation (‘tartil’), and the Iqamah is to be recited quickly in a flowing manner (‘hadr’).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلسَّرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْأَذَانُ تَرْتِيلٌ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةُ حَدْرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Adhan is to be recited with measured recitation (‘tartil’), and the Iqamah is to be recited quickly in a flowing manner (‘hadr’).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you enter the mosque, praise Allah (swt) and extol Him (swt), and send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Then when you begin the prayer and pronounce the Takbir, do not raise your hands beyond your ears, and do not raise your hands in supplication during the obligatory prayer so that they go above your head.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَاحْمَدِ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنِ عَلَيْهِ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَإِذَا اِفْتَتَحْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَكَبَّرْتَ فَلاَ تُجَاوِزْ أُذُنَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَرْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ بِالدُّعَاءِ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ تُجَاوِزُ بِهِمَا رَأْسَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you enter the mosque, praise Allah (swt) and extol Him (swt), and send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Then when you begin the prayer and pronounce the Takbir, do not raise your hands beyond your ears, and do not raise your hands in supplication during the obligatory prayer so that they go above your head.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Fadhala from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) when He (a.s) began the prayer, He (a.s) would raise his hands slightly below his face.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ حِينَ اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ أَسْفَلَ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ قَلِيلاً
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Fadhala from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) when He (a.s) began the prayer, He (a.s) would raise his hands slightly below his face.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), when Imam (a.s) said the Takbir in prayer, He (a.s) would raise his hands until they nearly reached his ears.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا كَبَّرَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ حَتَّى تَكَادَ تَبْلُغُ أُذُنَيْهِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), when Imam (a.s) said the Takbir in prayer, He (a.s) would raise his hands until they nearly reached his ears.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadhala from Ibn Sinan who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) praying, He (a.s) would raise his hands in front of his face when He (a.s) began the prayer.
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ حِينَ اِسْتَفْتَحَ.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadhala from Ibn Sinan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) praying, He (a.s) would raise his hands in front of his face when He (a.s) began the prayer.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah Kawthar 108:2). Imam (a.s) said: “It is the raising of your hands in front of your face.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى« فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَ اِنْحَرْ» قَالَ «هُوَ رَفْعُ يَدَيْكَ حِذَاءَ وَجْهِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah Kawthar 108:2). Imam (a.s) said: “It is the raising of your hands in front of your face.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the minimum that suffices in prayer from the Takbir. Imam (a.s) said: “One Takbir.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ مِنَ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ قَالَ« تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the minimum that suffices in prayer from the Takbir. Imam (a.s) said: “One Takbir.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you begin the prayer, you may say the Takbir once if you wish, or three times if you wish, or five times if you wish, or seven times if you wish, all of that suffices for you. However, if you are an imam, you should not recite aloud except with one Takbir.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا اِفْتَتَحْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَكَبِّرْ إِنْ شِئْتَ وَاحِدَةً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ ثَلاَثاً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ خَمْساً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ سَبْعاً فَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ مُجْزٍ عَنْكَ غَيْرَ أَنَّكَ إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً لَمْ تَجْهَرْ إِلاَّ بِتَكْبِيرَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you begin the prayer, you may say the Takbir once if you wish, or three times if you wish, or five times if you wish, or seven times if you wish, all of that suffices for you. However, if you are an imam, you should not recite aloud except with one Takbir.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 70

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) begin the prayer, He (a.s) raised his hands in front of his face and directed the palms of his hands toward the Qiblah.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَرَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِبَطْنِ كَفَّيْهِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) begin the prayer, He (a.s) raised his hands in front of his face and directed the palms of his hands toward the Qiblah.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 71

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from al-Husayn from Zayd al-Shahham, and Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is the opening (of the prayer) with one Takbir?” Imam (a.s) said: “One Takbir suffices for you.” I asked: “And the seven (Takbirs)?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is extra merit.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلاِفْتِتَاحُ فَقَالَ« تَكْبِيرَةٌ تُجْزِيكَ» قُلْتُ فَالسَّبْعُ قَالَ« ذَلِكَ اَلْفَضْلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from al-Husayn from Zayd al-Shahham, and Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is the opening (of the prayer) with one Takbir?” Imam (a.s) said: “One Takbir suffices for you.” I asked: “And the seven (Takbirs)?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is extra merit.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The single Takbir at the opening of the prayer suffices, and three is better, and seven is the best of all.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرَةُ اَلْوَاحِدَةُ فِي اِفْتِتَاحِ اَلصَّلاَةِ تُجْزِي وَ اَلثَّلاَثُ أَفْضَلُ وَ اَلسَّبْعُ أَفْضَلُ كُلِّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The single Takbir at the opening of the prayer suffices, and three is better, and seven is the best of all.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 71

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr and Fadhala from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Hafs:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was in prayer, and beside Him (saws) was al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s), peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said the Takbir, but al-Husayn (a.s) did not follow with the Takbir. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said the Takbir again, but al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, still did not say the Takbir. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, continued to say the Takbir and was helping al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, to say the Takbir, but He (a.s) did not do so, until the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, completed seven Takbirs, and then al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, followed with the Takbir on the seventh.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “(Thus) So it became a Sunnah.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَكَبَّرَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَلَمْ يُحِرِ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَلَمْ يُحِرِ اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّكْبِيرَ وَ لَمْ يَزَلْ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُعَالِجُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّكْبِيرَ فَلَمْ يُحِرْ حَتَّى أَكْمَلَ سَبْعَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ فَأَحَارَ اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّكْبِيرَ فِي اَلسَّابِعَةِ» فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« فَصَارَتْ سُنَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr and Fadhala from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Hafs:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was in prayer, and beside Him (saws) was al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s), peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said the Takbir, but al-Husayn (a.s) did not follow with the Takbir. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said the Takbir again, but al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, still did not say the Takbir. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, continued to say the Takbir and was helping al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, to say the Takbir, but He (a.s) did not do so, until the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, completed seven Takbirs, and then al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, followed with the Takbir on the seventh.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “(Thus) So it became a Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 71

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you begin the prayer, raise your hands, then spread them open fully, then say Takbir three times, then say: ‘O Allah (swt), You are the True King. There is no god but You (azj). Glory be to You (azj). Indeed, I have wronged myself, so forgive me my sin. Surely, no one forgives sins except You (azj).’ Then say Takbir two times, then say: ‘Here I am, at Your (azj) service, and all goodness is in Your (azj) hands, and evil is not attributed to You (azj). The rightly guided is he whom You (azj) guide. There is no refuge from You (azj) except in You (azj). Glory be to You (azj) and to Your (azj) mercy. You (azj) are Blessed and Exalted. Glory be to You (azj), Lord (azj) of the House.’ Then say Takbir two times, then say: ‘I have turned my face to the One (azj) who created the heavens and the earth,’ the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, in pure devotion, submitting (to Him (azj)), ‘and I am not of the polytheists.’ Then seek refuge with Allah (swt) from the accursed Shaytan, then recite the Opening Chapter of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا اِفْتَتَحْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَارْفَعْ كَفَّيْكَ ثُمَّ اُبْسُطْهُمَا بَسْطاً ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ ثَلاَثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ اَلْمَلِكُ اَلْحَقُّ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي إِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ اَلذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قُلْ لَبَّيْكَ وَ سَعْدَيْكَ وَ اَلْخَيْرُ فِي يَدَيْكَ وَ اَلشَّرُّ لَيْسَ إِلَيْكَ وَ اَلْمَهْدِيُّ مَنْ هَدَيْتَ لاَ مَلْجَأَ مِنْكَ إِلاَّ إِلَيْكَ سُبْحَانَكَ وَ حَنَانَيْكَ تَبَارَكْتَ وَ تَعَالَيْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ رَبَّ اَلْبَيْتِ ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ« وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضَ» عَالِمِ اَلْغَيْبِ وَ اَلشَّهَادَةِ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِماً« وَ مٰا أَنَا مِنَ اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ» ثُمَّ تَعَوَّذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلشَّيْطَانِ اَلرَّجِيمِ ثُمَّ اِقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you begin the prayer, raise your hands, then spread them open fully, then say Takbir three times, then say: ‘O Allah (swt), You are the True King. There is no god but You (azj). Glory be to You (azj). Indeed, I have wronged myself, so forgive me my sin. Surely, no one forgives sins except You (azj).’ Then say Takbir two times, then say: ‘Here I am, at Your (azj) service, and all goodness is in Your (azj) hands, and evil is not attributed to You (azj). The rightly guided is he whom You (azj) guide. There is no refuge from You (azj) except in You (azj). Glory be to You (azj) and to Your (azj) mercy. You (azj) are Blessed and Exalted. Glory be to You (azj), Lord (azj) of the House.’ Then say Takbir two times, then say: ‘I have turned my face to the One (azj) who created the heavens and the earth,’ the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, in pure devotion, submitting (to Him (azj)), ‘and I am not of the polytheists.’ Then seek refuge with Allah (swt) from the accursed Shaytan, then recite the Opening Chapter of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 71

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It suffices you in prayer, in the words of directing yourself toward Allah (swt) (‘tawajjuh’), to say: ‘I turn my face toward the One (azj) who created the heavens and the earth, upon the creed of Abraham, upright and submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds. No partner has He (azj), and with this I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims.’ And one ‘takbirah’ (saying of ‘Allahu Akbar’) is sufficient for you.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ مِنَ اَلْكَلاَمِ فِي اَلتَّوَجُّهِ إِلَى اَللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولَ« وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضَ» عَلَى مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِماً «وَ مٰا أَنَا مِنَ اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ»« إِنَّ صَلاٰتِي وَ نُسُكِي وَ مَحْيٰايَ وَ مَمٰاتِي لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ` لاٰ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ بِذٰلِكَ أُمِرْتُ» وَ أَنَا مِنَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ يُجْزِيكَ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It suffices you in prayer, in the words of directing yourself toward Allah (swt) (‘tawajjuh’), to say: ‘I turn my face toward the One (azj) who created the heavens and the earth, upon the creed of Abraham, upright and submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds. No partner has He (azj), and with this I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims.’ And one ‘takbirah’ (saying of ‘Allahu Akbar’) is sufficient for you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 72

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) for several days. He (a.s) used to recite in Surah al-Fatiha: ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’, and when it was a prayer in which the recitation is not to be recited aloud, He (a.s) would recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ aloud and would conceal the rest (of the surahs).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّاماً كَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي فَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ «بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ فَإِذَا كَانَ صَلاَةٌ لاَ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ جَهَرَ بِ«بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ وَ أَخْفَى مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) for several days. He (a.s) used to recite in Surah al-Fatiha: ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’, and when it was a prayer in which the recitation is not to be recited aloud, He (a.s) would recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ aloud and would conceal the rest (of the surahs).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 72

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who is an imam and begins with (Surah) al-Hamd but does not recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’. Imam (a.s) said: “It does not harm him, and there is no problem with it.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ إِمَاماً فَيَسْتَفْتِحُ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ لاَ يَقْرَأُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَضُرُّهُ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynMatn: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who is an imam and begins with (Surah) al-Hamd but does not recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’. Imam (a.s) said: “It does not harm him, and there is no problem with it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 72

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Jarir Zakariyya ibn Idris al-Qummi who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a people in prayer who dislike that he recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ aloud. Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should not recite it aloud.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَرِيرٍ زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ اَلْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ يَكْرَهُونَ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بِ«بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَجْهَرْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Jarir Zakariyya ibn Idris al-Qummi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a people in prayer who dislike that he recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ aloud. Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should not recite it aloud.”
