chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man and Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Both of them (Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi) asked Him (a.s) about one who recites ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ when he wishes to recite Surah al-Fatiha. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he wishes, silently, and if he wishes, aloud.” So they asked: “Does he recite it with another Surah as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُمَا سَأَلاَهُ عَمَّنْ يَقْرَأُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ حِينَ يُرِيدُ يَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنْ شَاءَ سِرّاً وَ إِنْ شَاءَ جَهْراً» فَقَالاَ أَ فَيَقْرَؤُهَا مَعَ اَلسُّورَةِ اَلْأُخْرَى فَقَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man and Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Both of them (Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi) asked Him (a.s) about one who recites ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ when he wishes to recite Surah al-Fatiha. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he wishes, silently, and if he wishes, aloud.” So they asked: “Does he recite it with another Surah as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 73

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who begins the recitation in prayer, should he recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, when he begins the prayer, let him say it at the beginning of what he opens with, and thereafter it suffices him.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَفْتَتِحُ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ أَ يَقْرَأُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَلْيَقُلْهَا فِي أَوَّلِ مَا يَفْتَتِحُ ثُمَّ يَكْفِيهِ مَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who begins the recitation in prayer, should he recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, when he begins the prayer, let him say it at the beginning of what he opens with, and thereafter it suffices him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 73

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “When I stand for prayer, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ in Surah al-Fatiha?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Then when I have recited Surah al-Fatiha, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ with the next Surah?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا أَقَمْتُ لِلصَّلاَةِ أَقْرَأُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ فِي فَاتِحَةِ اَلْقُرْآنِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ فَإِذَا قَرَأْتُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْقُرْآنِ أَقْرَأُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ مَعَ اَلسُّورَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “When I stand for prayer, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ in Surah al-Fatiha?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Then when I have recited Surah al-Fatiha, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ with the next Surah?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 74

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Hamdani who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him; “May I be your ransom, what do you say about a man who begins with ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ in his prayer, alone, in Surah al-Fatiha, but when he reaches a different Surah after al-Fatiha, he omits it? The ‘Abbasid (official) said: ‘There is no harm in that.’” So He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in His (a.s) own handwriting: “He must repeat it twice, despite his nose.” This was meaning the ‘Abbasid (so the nose of that ‘Abbasid, who claimed there was no harm, be rubbed in the dust).
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ اَلْهَمْدَانِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي رَجُلٍ اِبْتَدَأَ بِ«بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ» فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ فِي أُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ فَلَمَّا صَارَ إِلَى غَيْرِ أُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ مِنَ اَلسُّورَةِ تَرَكَهَا فَقَالَ اَلْعَبَّاسِيُّ لَيْسَ بِذَلِكَ بَأْسٌ فَكَتَبَ بِخَطِّهِ «يُعِيدُهَا مَرَّتَيْنِ عَلَى رَغْمِ أَنْفِهِ» يَعْنِي اَلْعَبَّاسِيَّ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Hamdani who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him; “May I be your ransom, what do you say about a man who begins with ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ in his prayer, alone, in Surah al-Fatiha, but when he reaches a different Surah after al-Fatiha, he omits it? The ‘Abbasid (official) said: ‘There is no harm in that.’” So He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in His (a.s) own handwriting: “He must repeat it twice, despite his nose.” This was meaning the ‘Abbasid (so the nose of that ‘Abbasid, who claimed there was no harm, be rubbed in the dust).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 74

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not recite in the obligatory prayer less than one Surah, nor more.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِأَقَلَّ مِنْ سُورَةٍ وَ لاَ بِأَكْثَرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not recite in the obligatory prayer less than one Surah, nor more.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 74

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites two Surahs in one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: “No, for each Surah there is a rak‘ah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ اَلسُّورَتَيْنِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ لِكُلِّ سُورَةٍ رَكْعَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites two Surahs in one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: “No, for each Surah there is a rak‘ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 74

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan al-Sayqal who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is it sufficient for me to recite only Surah al-Fatiha in an obligatory prayer if I am in a hurry or something hastens me?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يُجْزِي عَنِّي أَنْ أَقُولَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا إِذَا كُنْتُ مُسْتَعْجِلاً أَوْ أَعْجَلَنِي شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan al-Sayqal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is it sufficient for me to recite only Surah al-Fatiha in an obligatory prayer if I am in a hurry or something hastens me?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is permissible for a sick person to recite only Surah al-Fatiha in the obligatory prayer, and it is also permissible for a healthy person when making up voluntary prayers, whether at night or during the day.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَجُوزُ لِلْمَرِيضِ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا وَ يَجُوزُ لِلصَّحِيحِ فِي قَضَاءِ صَلاَةِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is permissible for a sick person to recite only Surah al-Fatiha in the obligatory prayer, and it is also permissible for a healthy person when making up voluntary prayers, whether at night or during the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from al-Qarawi from Aban from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I recite two Surahs in one rak‘ah?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Is it not said that each Surah should be given its due in bowing and prostration?” Imam (a.s) said: “That applies in the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَرَوِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقْرَأُ سُورَتَيْنِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ أَ لَيْسَ يُقَالُ أَعْطِ كُلَّ سُورَةٍ حَقَّهَا مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَقَالَ« ذَاكَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَأَمَّا فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from al-Qarawi from Aban from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I recite two Surahs in one rak‘ah?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Is it not said that each Surah should be given its due in bowing and prostration?” Imam (a.s) said: “That applies in the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said: Zurarah said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يُجْمَعَ بَيْنَ اَلسُّورَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَأَمَّا اَلنَّافِلَةُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said: Zurarah said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Abdillah (a.s), he said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone is valid in the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ تَجُوزُ وَحْدَهَا فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Abdillah (a.s), he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone is valid in the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone suffices in the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا تُجْزِي فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone suffices in the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 76

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man recites only Surah al-Fatiha in the first two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer if a need hastens him or he fears something.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ إِذَا مَا أَعْجَلَتْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ أَوْ تَخَوَّفَ شَيْئاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man recites only Surah al-Fatiha in the first two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer if a need hastens him or he fears something.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 76

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan from al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May a man recite the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if it is more than three verses.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلسَّرِيِّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يَقْرَأُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلسُّورَةَ اَلْوَاحِدَةَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِذَا كَانَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثَلاَثِ آيَاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan from al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May a man recite the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if it is more than three verses.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 76

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them, said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer while he is able to recite others, if he does so, is there anything upon him? Imam (a.s) said: “If he can recite other than it, then he should not do it. But if he cannot recite other than it, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ سُورَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ هُوَ يُحْسِنُ غَيْرَهَا فَإِنْ فَعَلَ فَمَا عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« إِذَا أَحْسَنَ غَيْرَهَا فَلاَ يَفْعَلْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُحْسِنْ غَيْرَهَا فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer while he is able to recite others, if he does so, is there anything upon him? Imam (a.s) said: “If he can recite other than it, then he should not do it. But if he cannot recite other than it, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 76

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Fadhala from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in prayer and recited for us ‘Surah al- Duha’ and ‘Surah al-Sharh’.
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَرَأَ بِنَا بِالضُّحَى وَ أَ لَمْ نَشْرَحْ
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Fadhala from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in prayer and recited for us ‘Surah al- Duha’ and ‘Surah al-Sharh’.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 77

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This hadith was also narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from one of our companions from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) prayed and recited in the first rak‘ah ‘By the morning brightness” (Surah al-Duha)’ and in the second ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-Sharh)’.
arabicText: وَ رَوَى هَذَا اَلْحَدِيثَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَرَأَ فِي اَلْأُولَى« وَ اَلضُّحىٰ» وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ« أَ لَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: This hadith was also narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from one of our companions from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) prayed and recited in the first rak‘ah ‘By the morning brightness” (Surah al-Duha)’ and in the second ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-Sharh)’.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 77

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from al-‘Ala’ from Zayd al-Shahham who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in the Fajr prayer, and He (a.s) recited ‘By the morning brightness” (Surah al-Duha)’ and ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-Sharh)’ in one rak‘ah.
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْفَجْرَ فَقَرَأَ« وَ اَلضُّحىٰ» وَ« أَ لَمْ نَشْرَحْ» فِي رَكْعَةٍ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from al-‘Ala’ from Zayd al-Shahham who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in the Fajr prayer, and He (a.s) recited ‘By the morning brightness” (Surah al-Duha)’ and ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-Sharh)’ in one rak‘ah.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 77

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer), there is no harm.”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان عن ابن بكير عن زرارة قال قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام إنما يكره أن يجمع بين السورتين في الفريضة فاما النافلة فلا بأس
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer), there is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who joins two Surahs in one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: “Every Surah has a right, so give it its due in bowing and prostration.” I asked: “What if he cuts the Surah (splits it)?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرُنُ بَيْنَ اَلسُّورَتَيْنِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ لِكُلِّ سُورَةٍ حَقّاً فَأَعْطِهَا حَقَّهَا مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ» قُلْتُ فَيَقْطَعُ اَلسُّورَةَ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who joins two Surahs in one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: “Every Surah has a right, so give it its due in bowing and prostration.” I asked: “What if he cuts the Surah (splits it)?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim who said:
I asked the Righteous servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him: “Is it permissible to recite two or three Surahs in the night prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for the night prayer, recite two or three Surahs. But as for the daytime prayer, do not recite except one Surah (in each rak‘ah).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَبْداً صَالِحاً عَ هَ لْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِالسُّورَتَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثِ فَقَالَ« مَا كَانَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فَاقْرَأْ بِالسُّورَتَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثِ وَ مَا كَانَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ فَلاَ تَقْرَأْ إِلاَّ بِسُورَةٍ سُورَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous servant (Abd Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him: “Is it permissible to recite two or three Surahs in the night prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for the night prayer, recite two or three Surahs. But as for the daytime prayer, do not recite except one Surah (in each rak‘ah).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm in combining as many Surahs as you wish in the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer).”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تَجْمَعَ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ مِنَ اَلسُّوَرِ مَا شِئْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm in combining as many Surahs as you wish in the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from someone who informed him from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s): “May a Surah be divided between two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, divide it however you wish.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ تُقْسَمُ اَلسُّورَةُ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمِ اِقْسِمْهَا كَيْفَ شِئْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from someone who informed him from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s): “May a Surah be divided between two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, divide it however you wish.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn al-Tawil from Abu Dawud al-Munshid from Muhassin al-Mithami:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In ‘Zawal’ prayer (midday supererogatory), you recite in: - The first rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas), - The second rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun), - The third rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and Ayat al-Kursi, - The fourth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-Baqarah ‘Amana al-rasulu...’ to its end, - The fifth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and five verses from Aal ‘Imran starting from ‘Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...’ to ‘Indeed, You do not break the promise,’ - The sixth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and three verses of Surah al-A‘raf starting from ‘Indeed, your Lord is Allah (swt) who created the heavens and the earth...’ to ‘Indeed, the mercy of Allah (swt) is near to the doers of good,’ - The seventh rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the verses from Surah al-An‘am ‘And they assigned to Allah (swt) partners of the jinn...’ to ‘And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware,’ - The eighth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-Hashr from ‘If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain...’ to its end. Then when you finish, you say: ‘O Allah (swt), Turner of hearts and sights, make my heart firm upon Your (swt) religion, and do not let my heart deviate after You (swt) have guided me, and grant me from Yourself (swt) mercy, indeed, You (swt) are the Bestower’, seven times. Then you say: ‘I seek refuge with Allah (swt) from the Fire’, seven times.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَلطَّوِيلِ عَنْ أَبِي دَاوُدَ اَلْمُنْشِدِ عَنْ مُحَسِّنٍ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَقْرَأُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلزَّوَالِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلرَّابِعَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ آخِرَ اَلْبَقَرَةِ« آمَنَ اَلرَّسُولُ» إِلَى آخِرِهَا وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْخَامِسَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ اَلْخَمْسَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ آلِ عِمْرَانَ« إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضِ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ« إِنَّكَ لاٰ تُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلسَّادِسَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ ثَلاَثَ آيَاتِ اَلسُّخْرَةِ« إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اَللّٰهُ اَلَّذِي خَلَقَ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضَ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ« إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اَللّٰهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ اَلْمُحْسِنِينَ وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلسَّابِعَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ اَلْآيَاتِ مِنْ سُورَةِ اَلْأَنْعَامِ« وَ جَعَلُوا لِلّٰهِ شُرَكٰاءَ اَلْجِنَّ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ« وَ هُوَ اَللَّطِيفُ اَلْخَبِيرُ» وَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّامِنَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ» وَ آخِرَ سُورَةِ اَلْحَشْرِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ« لَوْ أَنْزَلْنٰا هٰذَا اَلْقُرْآنَ عَلىٰ جَبَلٍ» إِلَى آخِرِهَا فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ قُلْتَ اَللَّهُمَّ مُقَلِّبَ اَلْقُلُوبِ وَ اَلْأَبْصَارِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ وَ لاَ تُزِغْ قَلْبِي بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنِي وَ هَبْ لِي« مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْوَهّٰابُ» سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ أَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn al-Tawil from Abu Dawud al-Munshid from Muhassin al-Mithami:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In ‘Zawal’ prayer (midday supererogatory), you recite in: - The first rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas), - The second rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun), - The third rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and Ayat al-Kursi, - The fourth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-Baqarah ‘Amana al-rasulu...’ to its end, - The fifth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and five verses from Aal ‘Imran starting from ‘Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...’ to ‘Indeed, You do not break the promise,’ - The sixth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and three verses of Surah al-A‘raf starting from ‘Indeed, your Lord is Allah (swt) who created the heavens and the earth...’ to ‘Indeed, the mercy of Allah (swt) is near to the doers of good,’ - The seventh rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the verses from Surah al-An‘am ‘And they assigned to Allah (swt) partners of the jinn...’ to ‘And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware,’ - The eighth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-Hashr from ‘If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain...’ to its end. Then when you finish, you say: ‘O Allah (swt), Turner of hearts and sights, make my heart firm upon Your (swt) religion, and do not let my heart deviate after You (swt) have guided me, and grant me from Yourself (swt) mercy, indeed, You (swt) are the Bestower’, seven times. Then you say: ‘I seek refuge with Allah (swt) from the Fire’, seven times.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Mu‘adh ibn Muslim narrated to me:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not leave off reciting ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun) in seven places: - In the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, - The two rak‘ahs of Zawal (midday supererogatory prayer), - The two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, - The first two rak‘ahs of the Night Prayer (‘Salat al-Layl’), - The two rak‘ahs of ‘Ihram’ (entering prayer), - The two rak‘ahs of Fajr if you begin your day with them, - The two rak‘ahs of ‘Tawaf’ (circumambulation).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاذُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لاَ تَدَعْ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» فِي سَبْعِ مَوَاطِنَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي أَوَّلِ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْإِحْرَامِ وَ اَلْفَجْرِ إِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ بِهِمَا وَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلطَّوَافِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Mu‘adh ibn Muslim narrated to me:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not leave off reciting ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun) in seven places: - In the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, - The two rak‘ahs of Zawal (midday supererogatory prayer), - The two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, - The first two rak‘ahs of the Night Prayer (‘Salat al-Layl’), - The two rak‘ahs of ‘Ihram’ (entering prayer), - The two rak‘ahs of Fajr if you begin your day with them, - The two rak‘ahs of ‘Tawaf’ (circumambulation).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And in another narration: “In all of these (prayers), ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ is recited in the first rak‘ah and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ in the second, except in the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, in which ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ is recited first, and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ is recited in the second rak‘ah.”
arabicText: وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى:« يُقْرَأُ فِي هَذَا كُلِّهِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَفِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ بِ«قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» إِلاَّ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَإِنَّهُ يُبْدَأُ بِ«قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» ثُمَّ يُقْرَأُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ «قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynMatn: And in another narration: “In all of these (prayers), ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ is recited in the first rak‘ah and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ in the second, except in the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, in which ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ is recited first, and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ is recited in the second rak‘ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are behind an imam and he recites al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) and finishes its recitation, then you say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (All praise is due to Allah (swt), Lord of the worlds), and do not say ‘Amin’.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَقَرَأَ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ فَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهَا فَقُلْ أَنْتَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ اَلْعَالَمِينَ وَ لاَ تَقُلْ آمِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are behind an imam and he recites al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) and finishes its recitation, then you say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (All praise is due to Allah (swt), Lord of the worlds), and do not say ‘Amin’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Should I say ‘Amin’ when I finish reciting Surah al-Fatiha?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُولُ إِذَا فَرَغْتُ مِنْ فَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ آمِينَ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Should I say ‘Amin’ when I finish reciting Surah al-Fatiha?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the people saying ‘Amin’ together in prayer when Surah al-Fatiha is recited. He said: “How beautiful it is, but lower your voice with it.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَلنَّاسِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ جَمَاعَةً حِينَ تُقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةُ اَلْكِتَابِ آمِينَ قَالَ« مَا أَحْسَنَهَا وَ اِخْفِضِ اَلصَّوْتَ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the people saying ‘Amin’ together in prayer when Surah al-Fatiha is recited. He said: “How beautiful it is, but lower your voice with it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Should I say ‘Amin’ when the imam (of prayer) says: ‘ghayril-maghdubi ‘alayhim wa lad-dallin’?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are the Jews and the Christians.” And He (a.s) did not respond regarding this (He (a.s) gave no ruling about saying ‘Amin’).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُولُ آمِينَ إِذَا قَالَ اَلْإِمَامُ« غَيْرِ اَلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ لاَ اَلضّٰالِّينَ» قَالَ« هُمُ اَلْيَهُودُ وَ اَلنَّصَارَى وَ لَمْ يُجِبْ فِي هَذَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Should I say ‘Amin’ when the imam (of prayer) says: ‘ghayril-maghdubi ‘alayhim wa lad-dallin’?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are the Jews and the Christians.” And He (a.s) did not respond regarding this (He (a.s) gave no ruling about saying ‘Amin’).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) raising his hands when He (a.s) bowed (for ‘ruku’), and when He (a.s) raised his head from bowing, and when He (a.s) prostrated (‘sujud’), and when He (a.s) raised his head from prostration, and when He (a.s) intended to go into the second prostration.
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ إِذَا رَكَعَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ اَلثَّانِيَةَ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) raising his hands when He (a.s) bowed (for ‘ruku’), and when He (a.s) raised his head from bowing, and when He (a.s) prostrated (‘sujud’), and when He (a.s) raised his head from prostration, and when He (a.s) intended to go into the second prostration.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Muskan: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said regarding a man who raises his hands whenever he goes down for bowing (‘ruku’) and prostration (‘sujud’), and whenever he raises his head from bowing or prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “It is servitude (‘al-‘ubudiyyah’).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَرْفَعُ يَدَهُ كُلَّمَا أَهْوَى لِلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ كُلَّمَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنْ رُكُوعٍ أَوْ سُجُودٍ قَالَ« هِيَ اَلْعُبُودِيَّةُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Muskan: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said regarding a man who raises his hands whenever he goes down for bowing (‘ruku’) and prostration (‘sujud’), and whenever he raises his head from bowing or prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “It is servitude (‘al-‘ubudiyyah’).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq from Yunus from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Your raising of your hands in prayer is its adornment.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْوَرَّاقِ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: رَفْعُكَ يَدَيْكَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ زِينَتُهَا.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq from Yunus from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Your raising of your hands in prayer is its adornment.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, and al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Hisham ibn Salim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the ‘tasbih’ in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’. Imam (a.s) said: “In ‘ruku’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-‘Azim (Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Great)’, and in ‘sujud’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-A‘la (Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Most High)’. The obligation in that is one ‘tasbih’, the Sunnah is three, and the excellence is in saying it seven times.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ وَ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَقَالَ يَقُولُ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ« سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ فِي اَلسُّجُودِ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْأَعْلَى اَلْفَرِيضَةُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ تَسْبِيحَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ اَلسُّنَّةُ ثَلاَثٌ وَ اَلْفَضْلُ فِي سَبْعٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, and al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Hisham ibn Salim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the ‘tasbih’ in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’. Imam (a.s) said: “In ‘ruku’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-‘Azim (Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Great)’, and in ‘sujud’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-A‘la (Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Most High)’. The obligation in that is one ‘tasbih’, the Sunnah is three, and the excellence is in saying it seven times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 81

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) (peace be upon him), he said:
I said to Him (a.s): “What suffices in terms of what is to be said in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm recitation (‘tarassul’), and one complete (tasbihah) suffices.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَقَالَ« ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ فِي تَرَسُّلٍ وَ وَاحِدَةٌ تَامَّةً تُجْزِي»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) (peace be upon him), he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “What suffices in terms of what is to be said in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm recitation (‘tarassul’), and one complete (tasbihah) suffices.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 81

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh al-Nakha‘i from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked Him (a.s) about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Three, and one suffices you if you have firmly placed your forehead on the ground.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ اَلنَّخَعِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ كَمْ يُجْزِي فِيهِ مِنَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فَقَالَ« ثَلاَثَةٌ وَ تُجْزِيكَ وَاحِدَةٌ إِذَا أَمْكَنْتَ جَبْهَتَكَ مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh al-Nakha‘i from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (peace be upon him), he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Three, and one suffices you if you have firmly placed your forehead on the ground.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 81

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man in ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices him in his ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’? Imam (a.s) said: “Three, and one suffices him.”

thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man in ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices him in his ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’? Imam (a.s) said: “Three, and one suffices him.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Misma‘ Abi Sayyar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’ to say three ‘tasbihat’, or their equivalent with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’). But it is of no value, nor does it hold any merit, for one to say: ‘Subh... Subh... Subh’ (in a hurried manner).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, whether they were mentioned in the Qur’an. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, in the words of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘O you who believe, bow and prostrate’.” (Surah Hajj 22:77) I asked: “What is the minimum required for ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for what suffices you in ‘ruku’, it is to say three ‘tasbihat’, ‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’ three times. And whoever is able to lengthen the ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, let him lengthen them as much as he is able. That should be in glorifying Allah (swt), praising Him (swt), magnifying Him (swt), supplicating, and showing humility, for the closest a servant is to his Lord (azj) is when he is in ‘sujud’. As for the imam (of prayer), when he leads the people in prayer, he should not prolong it for them, for among them are the weak and those who have needs. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to lighten the prayer when leading the people.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ هَلْ نَزَلَ فِي اَلْقُرْآنِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اِرْكَعُوا وَ اُسْجُدُوا»» فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ حَدُّ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَا يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ ثَلاَثاً وَ مَنْ كَانَ يَقْوَى عَلَى أَنْ يُطَوِّلَ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ فَلْيُطَوِّلْ مَا اِسْتَطَاعَ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ فِي تَسْبِيحِ اَللَّهِ وَ تَحْمِيدِهِ وَ تَمْجِيدِهِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ وَ اَلتَّضَرُّعِ فَإِنَّ أَقْرَبَ مَا يَكُونُ اَلْعَبْدُ إِلَى رَبِّهِ وَ هُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَمَّا اَلْإِمَامُ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا قَامَ بِالنَّاسِ فَلاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُطَوِّلَ بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ فِي اَلنَّاسِ اَلضَّعِيفَ وَ مَنْ لَهُ اَلْحَاجَةُ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ إِذَا صَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ خَفَّ بِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, whether they were mentioned in the Qur’an. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, in the words of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘O you who believe, bow and prostrate’.” (Surah Hajj 22:77) I asked: “What is the minimum required for ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for what suffices you in ‘ruku’, it is to say three ‘tasbihat’, ‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’ three times. And whoever is able to lengthen the ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, let him lengthen them as much as he is able. That should be in glorifying Allah (swt), praising Him (swt), magnifying Him (swt), supplicating, and showing humility, for the closest a servant is to his Lord (azj) is when he is in ‘sujud’. As for the imam (of prayer), when he leads the people in prayer, he should not prolong it for them, for among them are the weak and those who have needs. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to lighten the prayer when leading the people.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the lightest (minimum) amount of ‘tasbih’ in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’), saying: ‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ أَخَفُّ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ مُتَرَسِّلاً تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the lightest (minimum) amount of ‘tasbih’ in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’), saying: ‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you intend to go into bowing (ruku‘), say while you are standing upright: ‘Allahu Akbar’, then bow and say: ‘My Lord (azj), for You (azj) have I bowed, to You (azj) have I submitted, in You (azj) have I believed, upon You (azj) have I relied, and You (azj) are my Lord (azj). My hearing, my sight, my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my brain, my nerves, my bones, and everything my feet carry have humbled themselves to You (azj), not arrogantly, nor proudly, nor with weariness. Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Mighty, and praise be to Him (azj)’, three times, in a calm and deliberate manner (tarassul). And in your bowing, align your feet, placing between them the distance of one span. Place your palms firmly on your knees. Put your right hand on your right knee before the left, press the tips of your fingers on the center of the kneecap, and spread your fingers when placing them on your knees. Keep your back straight and extend your neck, and let your gaze be between your feet. Then say: ‘Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah (swt) hears the one who praises Him (azj)), while you are upright standing, and say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (Praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord of the worlds), the One worthy of majesty, sovereignty, and greatness. ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’, say it aloud. Then raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration (sujud).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَقُلْ وَ أَنْتَ مُنْتَصِبٌ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ثُمَّ اِرْكَعْ وَ قُلْ رَبِّ لَكَ رَكَعْتُ وَ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَ بِكَ آمَنْتُ وَ عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَ أَنْتَ رَبِّي خَشَعَ لَكَ سَمْعِي وَ بَصَرِي وَ شَعْرِي وَ بَشَرِي وَ لَحْمِي وَ دَمِي وَ مُخِّي وَ عَصَبِي وَعِظَامِي وَمَا أَقَلَّتْهُ قَدَمَايَ غَيْرَ مُسْتَنْكِفٍ وَلاَ مُسْتَكْبِرٍ وَلاَ مُسْتَحْسِرٍ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي تَرَسُّلٍ وَ تَصُفُّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ تَضَعُ يَدَكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ اَلْيُسْرَى وَ تَلْقُمُ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ اَلرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَا عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنُقَكَ وَ لْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ ثُمَّ قُلْ سَمِعَ اَللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ وَ أَنْتَ مُنْتَصِبٌ قَائِمٌ «اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» أَهْلَ اَلْجَبَرُوتِ وَاَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَاَلْعَظَمَةِ« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» تَجْهَرُ بِهَا صَوْتَكَ ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ يَدَيْكَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَ تَخِرُّ سَاجِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you intend to go into bowing (ruku‘), say while you are standing upright: ‘Allahu Akbar’, then bow and say: ‘My Lord (azj), for You (azj) have I bowed, to You (azj) have I submitted, in You (azj) have I believed, upon You (azj) have I relied, and You (azj) are my Lord (azj). My hearing, my sight, my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my brain, my nerves, my bones, and everything my feet carry have humbled themselves to You (azj), not arrogantly, nor proudly, nor with weariness. Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Mighty, and praise be to Him (azj)’, three times, in a calm and deliberate manner (tarassul). And in your bowing, align your feet, placing between them the distance of one span. Place your palms firmly on your knees. Put your right hand on your right knee before the left, press the tips of your fingers on the center of the kneecap, and spread your fingers when placing them on your knees. Keep your back straight and extend your neck, and let your gaze be between your feet. Then say: ‘Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah (swt) hears the one who praises Him (azj)), while you are upright standing, and say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (Praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord of the worlds), the One worthy of majesty, sovereignty, and greatness. ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’, say it aloud. Then raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration (sujud).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you raise your head from bowing (ruku‘), straighten your back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَأَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لاَ يُقِيمُ صُلْبَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you raise your head from bowing (ruku‘), straighten your back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) placing his hands before his knees when He (a.s) went into prostration (sujud), and when He (a.s) wanted to rise, He (a.s) would raise his knees before his hands.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقُومَ رَفَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) placing his hands before his knees when He (a.s) went into prostration (sujud), and when He (a.s) wanted to rise, He (a.s) would raise his knees before his hands.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who places his hands before his knees during prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes (it is permissible).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who places his hands before his knees during prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes (it is permissible).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein

And from him, from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He (a.s) was asked about a man who places his hands on the ground before his knees. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes,” meaning in prayer.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» يَعْنِي فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (a.s) was asked about a man who places his hands on the ground before his knees. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes,” meaning in prayer.
