chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man, when praying, places his knees on the ground before his hands.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ إِذَا صَلَّى اَلرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَضَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man, when praying, places his knees on the ground before his hands.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 84

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you go into prostration (sujud), say the takbir (Allahu Akbar), and say: ‘O Allah (swt), to You (azj) I have prostrated, in You (azj) I have believed, to You (azj) I have submitted, upon You (azj) I have relied. You (azj) are my Lord (azj). My face has prostrated to the One (azj) who created it, and who split open its hearing and sight.’ ‘All praise belongs to Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds.’ ‘Blessed is Allah (swt), the best of creators.’ Then say: ‘Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Most High, and with His (azj) praise,’ three times. Then when you raise your head, say between the two prostrations: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive me, have mercy on me, mend me, repel from me (what harms me), and grant me well-being. Indeed, I am in need of whatever good You (azj) may send down to me.’ ‘Blessed is Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَكَبِّرْ وَ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ لَكَ سَجَدْتُ وَ بِكَ آمَنْتُ وَ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَ عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَ أَنْتَ رَبِّي سَجَدَ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي خَلَقَهُ وَ شَقَّ سَمْعَهُ وَ بَصَرَهُ« وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» تَبَارَكَ« اَللّٰهُ أَحْسَنُ اَلْخٰالِقِينَ» ثُمَّ قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ فَإِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ فَقُلْ بَيْنَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لِي وَ اِرْحَمْنِي وَ اُجْبُرْنِي وَ اِدْفَعْ عَنِّي وَ عَافِنِي« إِنِّي لِمٰا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ»« تَبٰارَكَ اَللّٰهُ رَبُّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you go into prostration (sujud), say the takbir (Allahu Akbar), and say: ‘O Allah (swt), to You (azj) I have prostrated, in You (azj) I have believed, to You (azj) I have submitted, upon You (azj) I have relied. You (azj) are my Lord (azj). My face has prostrated to the One (azj) who created it, and who split open its hearing and sight.’ ‘All praise belongs to Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds.’ ‘Blessed is Allah (swt), the best of creators.’ Then say: ‘Glory be to my Lord (azj), the Most High, and with His (azj) praise,’ three times. Then when you raise your head, say between the two prostrations: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive me, have mercy on me, mend me, repel from me (what harms me), and grant me well-being. Indeed, I am in need of whatever good You (azj) may send down to me.’ ‘Blessed is Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 84

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs al-A‘war:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, performed prostration, He (a.s) would collapse as the emaciated camel collapses, meaning the way it kneels down.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ حَفْصٍ اَلْأَعْوَرِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا سَجَدَ يَتَخَوَّى كَمَا يَتَخَوَّى اَلْبَعِيرُ اَلضَّامِرُ يَعْنِي بُرُوكَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs al-A‘war:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, performed prostration, He (a.s) would collapse as the emaciated camel collapses, meaning the way it kneels down.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 85

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan, from Misma‘:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It does not suffice a man in his prayer with less than three tasbihat or their equivalent.”
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مِسْمَعٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يُجْزِي اَلرَّجُلَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ أَقَلُّ مِنْ ثَلاَثِ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ أَوْ قَدْرِهِنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan, from Misma‘:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It does not suffice a man in his prayer with less than three tasbihat or their equivalent.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 85

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Dawud al-Abzari:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The minimum of tasbih is three times while you are in prostration, do not hasten through them.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ يَحْيَى اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلْأَبْزَارِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَدْنَى اَلتَّسْبِيحِ ثَلاَثُ مَرَّاتٍ وَ أَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ لاَ تَعْجَلْ بِهِنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Dawud al-Abzari:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The minimum of tasbih is three times while you are in prostration, do not hasten through them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 85

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the minimum that suffices of tasbih in bowing and prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “Three tasbihat.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَقَالَ« ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the minimum that suffices of tasbih in bowing and prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “Three tasbihat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 85

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I said to (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the limit of bowing and prostration?” Imam (a.s) said: “You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ three times in bowing, and ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ three times in prostration. So whoever omits one has omitted one-third of his prayer, and whoever omits two has omitted two-thirds of his prayer, and whoever does not perform tasbih, then he has no prayer.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ حَدُّ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ« تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثاً فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْأَعْلَى وَبِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثاً فِي اَلسُّجُودِ فَمَنْ نَقَصَ وَاحِدَةً نَقَصَ ثُلُثَ صَلاَتِهِ وَمَنْ نَقَصَ اِثْنَتَيْنِ نَقَصَ ثُلُثَيْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to (Imam) Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the limit of bowing and prostration?” Imam (a.s) said: “You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ three times in bowing, and ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ three times in prostration. So whoever omits one has omitted one-third of his prayer, and whoever omits two has omitted two-thirds of his prayer, and whoever does not perform tasbih, then he has no prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 86

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, who said:
One day, Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “O Hammad, do you know how to perform prayer properly?” I said: “O my master, I have memorized the book of Hariz regarding prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “It does not matter, O Hammad. Stand and pray.” So I stood before Him (a.s), facing the qiblah. I began the prayer, bowed, and prostrated. Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Hammad, you do not perform prayer properly. How unbecoming it is for a man like you, sixty or seventy years may pass over him, and he does not establish even one prayer with all of its boundaries complete?!” Hammad said: ‘So I felt humiliated within myself and I said; “May I be your ransom, then teach me the prayer.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) stood, facing the qiblah, upright. He (a.s) placed both his hands on his thighs, brought his fingers together, and positioned his feet close together until the distance between them was about the width of three spread-out fingers. He (a.s) pointed all the toes of his feet toward the qiblah, not turning them away from the qiblah, and Imam (a.s) said with humility: “Allahu Akbar.” Then He (a.s) recited al-Hamd with measured tone and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, then paused for a short moment, the amount of time one takes a breath, while standing. Then He (a.s) raised his hands in line with his face and said: “Allahu Akbar,” while still standing. Then He (a.s) bowed and filled his hands with his knees, spreading his fingers apart. He (a.s) pulled his knees backward and straightened his back until, had a drop of water or oil been poured on it, it would not have moved, due to the straightness of his back. He (a.s) extended his neck and closed his eyes. Then Imam (a.s) said tasbih three times with measured tone, saying: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih.’ Then He (a.s) stood up straight, and when He (a.s) became fully upright, Imam (a.s) said “‘Samia’a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah (swt) has heard the one who praises Him),” then Imam (a.s) said ‘Allahu Akbar’ while standing, and raised his hands in line with his face. Then He (a.s) went into prostration and placed his palms, with fingers joined together, between his knees, in line with his face, and said: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A’la wa bi-hamdih’ three times. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body on another part. He (a.s) prostrated on eight bones; the two palms, the two knees, the tips of the big toes, the forehead, and the nose. Imam (a.s) said: “Seven of them are obligatory to prostrate upon, and they are the ones Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His Book, where He (swt) said: ‘And that the masajid belong to Allah (swt), so do not call upon anyone with Allah (swt)’ (Surah Jinn 72:18). These are the forehead, the two palms, the two knees, and the two big toes. Placing the nose on the ground is a sunnah.” Then He (a.s) raised his head from prostration, and when He (a.s) was fully upright sitting, Imam (a.s) said: ‘Allahu Akbar’. Then He (a.s) sat on his left thigh, placing his right foot on the instep of his left foot, and said: “Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.” Then Imam (a.s) said takbir while sitting and performed the second prostration, saying as Imam (a.s) said in the first. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body upon another in bowing or in prostration. He (a.s) was balanced and did not place his forearms on the ground. He (a.s) prayed two rak’ahs in this manner, with his fingers joined together, and He (a.s) was seated during the tashahhud. When He (a.s) completed the tashahhud, He (a.s) gave salam and said: ‘O Hammad, pray like this.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْماً «يَا حَمَّادُ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا أَحْفَظُ كِتَابَ حَرِيزٍ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ عَلَيْكَ يَا حَمَّادُ قُمْ فَصَلِّ» قَالَ فَقُمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مُتَوَجِّهاً إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَاسْتَفْتَحْتُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَرَكَعْتُ وَ سَجَدْتُ فَقَالَ« يَا حَمَّادُ لاَ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ مَا أَقْبَحَ بِالرَّجُلِ مِنْكُمْ يَأْتِي عَلَيْهِ سِتُّونَ سَنَةً أَوْ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً فَلاَ يُقِيمُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً بِحُدُودِهَا تَامَّةً» قَالَ حَمَّادٌ فَأَصَابَنِي فِي نَفْسِي اَلذُّلُّ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَعَلِّمْنِي اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقَامَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ مُنْتَصِباً فَأَرْسَلَ يَدَيْهِ جَمِيعاً عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ قَدْ ضَمَّ أَصَابِعَهُ وَ قَرَّبَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهِ حَتَّى كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرُ ثَلاَثِ أَصَابِعَ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ بِأَصَابِعِ رِجْلَيْهِ جَمِيعاً اَلْقِبْلَةَ لَمْ يُحَرِّفْهَا عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَقَالَ بِخُشُوعٍ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ اَلْحَمْدَ بِتَرْتِيلٍ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ صَبَرَ هُنَيْئَةً بِقَدْرِ مَا يَتَنَفَّسُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ قَالَ «اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ مَلَأَ كَفَّيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ رَدَّ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى خَلْفِهِ ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى ظَهْرُهُ حَتَّى لَوْ صُبَّ عَلَيْهِ قَطْرَةٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ أَوْ دُهْنٍ لَمْ تَزُلْ لاِسْتِوَاءِ ظَهْرِهِ وَمَدَّ عُنُقَهُ وَغَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ ثَلاَثاً بِتَرْتِيلٍ فَقَالَ «سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ» ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى قَائِماً فَلَمَّا اِسْتَمْكَنَ مِنَ اَلْقِيَامِ قَالَ« سَمِعَ اَللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ ثُمَّ سَجَدَ وَ بَسَطَ كَفَّيْهِ مَضْمُومَتَيِ اَلْأَصَابِعِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ فَقَالَ« سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ» ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئاً مِنْ جَسَدِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ وَ سَجَدَ عَلَى ثَمَانِيَةِ أَعْظُمٍ اَلْكَفَّيْنِ وَ اَلرُّكْبَتَيْنِ وَ أَنَامِلِ إِبْهَامَيِ اَلرِّجْلَيْنِ وَ اَلْجَبْهَةِ وَ اَلْأَنْفِ وَ قَالَ« سَبْعٌ مِنْهَا فَرْضٌ يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهَا وَ هِيَ اَلَّتِي ذَكَرَهَا اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَ قَالَ« وَ أَنَّ اَلْمَسٰاجِدَ لِلّٰهِ فَلاٰ تَدْعُوا مَعَ اَللّٰهِ أَحَداً» وَ هِيَ اَلْجَبْهَةُ وَ اَلْكَفَّانِ وَ اَلرُّكْبَتَانِ وَ اَلْإِبْهَامَانِ وَ وَضْعُ اَلْأَنْفِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ سُنَّةٌ» ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَلَمَّا اِسْتَوَى جَالِساً قَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» ثُمَّ قَعَدَ عَلَى فَخِذِهِ اَلْأَيْسَرِ قَدْ وَضَعَ قَدَمَهُ اَلْأَيْمَنَ عَلَى بَطْنِ قَدَمِهِ اَلْأَيْسَرِ وَ قَالَ« أَسْتَغْفِرُ اَللَّهَ رَبِّي وَ أَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَ قَالَ كَمَا قَالَ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئاً مِنْ بَدَنِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فِي رُكُوعٍ وَلاَ سُجُودٍ وَ كَانَ مُجَّنِّحاً وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ عَلَى هَذَا وَ يَدَاهُ مَضْمُومَةُ اَلْأَصَابِعِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ سَلَّمَ فَقَالَ« يَا حَمَّادُ هَكَذَا صَلِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: One day, Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “O Hammad, do you know how to perform prayer properly?” I said: “O my master, I have memorized the book of Hariz regarding prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “It does not matter, O Hammad. Stand and pray.” So I stood before Him (a.s), facing the qiblah. I began the prayer, bowed, and prostrated. Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Hammad, you do not perform prayer properly. How unbecoming it is for a man like you, sixty or seventy years may pass over him, and he does not establish even one prayer with all of its boundaries complete?!” Hammad said: ‘So I felt humiliated within myself and I said; “May I be your ransom, then teach me the prayer.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) stood, facing the qiblah, upright. He (a.s) placed both his hands on his thighs, brought his fingers together, and positioned his feet close together until the distance between them was about the width of three spread-out fingers. He (a.s) pointed all the toes of his feet toward the qiblah, not turning them away from the qiblah, and Imam (a.s) said with humility: “Allahu Akbar.” Then He (a.s) recited al-Hamd with measured tone and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, then paused for a short moment, the amount of time one takes a breath, while standing. Then He (a.s) raised his hands in line with his face and said: “Allahu Akbar,” while still standing. Then He (a.s) bowed and filled his hands with his knees, spreading his fingers apart. He (a.s) pulled his knees backward and straightened his back until, had a drop of water or oil been poured on it, it would not have moved, due to the straightness of his back. He (a.s) extended his neck and closed his eyes. Then Imam (a.s) said tasbih three times with measured tone, saying: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih.’ Then He (a.s) stood up straight, and when He (a.s) became fully upright, Imam (a.s) said “‘Samia’a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah (swt) has heard the one who praises Him),” then Imam (a.s) said ‘Allahu Akbar’ while standing, and raised his hands in line with his face. Then He (a.s) went into prostration and placed his palms, with fingers joined together, between his knees, in line with his face, and said: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A’la wa bi-hamdih’ three times. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body on another part. He (a.s) prostrated on eight bones; the two palms, the two knees, the tips of the big toes, the forehead, and the nose. Imam (a.s) said: “Seven of them are obligatory to prostrate upon, and they are the ones Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His Book, where He (swt) said: ‘And that the masajid belong to Allah (swt), so do not call upon anyone with Allah (swt)’ (Surah Jinn 72:18). These are the forehead, the two palms, the two knees, and the two big toes. Placing the nose on the ground is a sunnah.” Then He (a.s) raised his head from prostration, and when He (a.s) was fully upright sitting, Imam (a.s) said: ‘Allahu Akbar’. Then He (a.s) sat on his left thigh, placing his right foot on the instep of his left foot, and said: “Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.” Then Imam (a.s) said takbir while sitting and performed the second prostration, saying as Imam (a.s) said in the first. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body upon another in bowing or in prostration. He (a.s) was balanced and did not place his forearms on the ground. He (a.s) prayed two rak’ahs in this manner, with his fingers joined together, and He (a.s) was seated during the tashahhud. When He (a.s) completed the tashahhud, He (a.s) gave salam and said: ‘O Hammad, pray like this.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 86

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I saw Him (a.s), when He (a.s) raised his head from the second prostration of the first rak‘ah, He (a.s) would sit until He (a.s) was at ease, then He (a.s) would stand.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُهُ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى جَلَسَ حَتَّى يَطْمَئِنَّ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Him (a.s), when He (a.s) raised his head from the second prostration of the first rak‘ah, He (a.s) would sit until He (a.s) was at ease, then He (a.s) would stand.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 88

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you raise your head from the second prostration in the first rak‘ah, when you intend to stand, then sit upright first, then stand.”
arabicText: سَمَاعَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى حِينَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقُومَ فَاسْتَوِ جَالِساً ثُمَّ قُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you raise your head from the second prostration in the first rak‘ah, when you intend to stand, then sit upright first, then stand.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 88

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rahim, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, I see you, when you pray and raise your head from prostration in the first and third rak‘ah, you sit upright before standing. So should we do as you do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not look at what I do, do what you have been commanded to do.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ رَحِيمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَرَاكَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَرَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَاَلثَّالِثَةِ تَسْتَوِي جَالِساً ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَنَصْنَعُ كَمَا تَصْنَعُ قَالَ« لاَ تَنْظُرُوا إِلَى مَا أَصْنَعُ أَنَا اِصْنَعُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rahim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, I see you, when you pray and raise your head from prostration in the first and third rak‘ah, you sit upright before standing. So should we do as you do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not look at what I do, do what you have been commanded to do.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 88

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, when they raised their heads from the second prostration, they stood up without sitting.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا رَفَعَا رُءُوسَهُمَا مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ نَهَضَا وَ لَمْ يَجْلِسَا
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, when they raised their heads from the second prostration, they stood up without sitting.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 89

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, Ibn Muslim, and al-Halabi said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Do not sit in prayer between the two prostrations like the sitting of a dog.”
arabicText: مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ وَ اِبْنُ مُسْلِمٍ وَ اَلْحَلَبِيُّ قَالُوا قَالَ:« لاَ تُقْعِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ بَيْنَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ كَإِقْعَاءِ اَلْكَلْبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, Ibn Muslim, and al-Halabi said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not sit in prayer between the two prostrations like the sitting of a dog.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 89

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
(Abu Abdillah (a.s) said) “When you sit in prayer, do not sit on your right side, rather, sit on your left side. And when you prostrate, spread your palms on the ground. And when you bow, place your knees into your palms.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you stand in prayer, do not place one foot directly against the other; rather, leave a gap between them, the minimum being the width of a finger, and the maximum up to a span. Let your shoulders hang down, release your arms, and do not interlock your fingers. Let your hands be upon your thighs, opposite your knees, and let your gaze be toward the place of your prostration. When you bow, align your position in bowing between your feet, making the distance between them about a span. Firmly place your palms upon your knees. Place your right hand on your right knee before the left, and let the tips of your fingers reach the center of the kneecap. Spread your fingers when placing them on your knees, and if the tips of your fingers reach in your bowing, reaching your kneecaps, that suffices you. But what is more beloved to me is that you firmly place your palms on your knees, so that your fingers are upon the center of the kneecap, and you spread them apart. Keep your back straight, stretch your neck, and let your gaze be directed to the space between your feet. When you intend to go into prostration, raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration, beginning with your hands, place them on the ground before your knees. Place them together. Do not spread your forearms on the ground like a beast spreads its forearms, and do not place your forearms on your knees or thighs. Rather, raise your elbows outward. Do not press your palms to your knees, nor bring them close to your face, let them be level with your shoulders. Do not place them in front of your knees, but turn them slightly away from that. Spread them flat on the ground and draw them toward yourself in a drawing motion. If there is a cloth beneath them, it does not harm you; but if you place them directly on the earth, that is better. Do not spread your fingers during prostration; rather, keep them joined together.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you sit in tashahhud, press your knees to the ground and spread them slightly. Let the top of your left foot be on the ground, and the top of your right foot on the sole of your left foot. Your buttocks should be on the ground, and the tip of your right big toe should be on the ground. Beware of sitting on your two feet, for that causes discomfort, and you will not truly be sitting on the ground, it would be as if you are sitting part of your body upon another part, and you will not be able to remain patient in the tashahhud and in supplication.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَلاَ تُلْصِقْ قَدَمَكَ بِالْأُخْرَى وَ دَعْ بَيْنَهُمَا فَصْلاً إِصْبَعاً أَقَلُّ ذَلِكَ إِلَى شِبْرٍ أَكْثَرُهُ وَاُسْدُلْ مَنْكِبَيْكَ وَأَرْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ وَلاَ تُشَبِّكْ أَصَابِعَكَ وَلْتَكُونَا عَلَى فَخِذَيْكَ قُبَالَةَ رُكْبَتِكَ وَلْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ فَإِذَا رَكَعْتَ فَصُفَّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ تَضَعُ يَدَكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ اَلْيُسْرَى وَ بَلِّغْ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ اَلرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَا عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَإِنْ وَصَلَتْ أَطْرَافُ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي رُكُوعِكَ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ أَجْزَأَكَ ذَلِكَ وَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ أَنْ تُمَكِّنَ كَفَّيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَتَجْعَلَ أَصَابِعَكَ فِي عَيْنِ اَلرُّكْبَةِ وَ تُفَرِّجَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنُقَكَ وَ لْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ فَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ فَارْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَخِرَّ سَاجِداً وَاِبْدَأْ بِيَدَيْكَ فَضَعْهُمَا عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْكَ تَضَعُهُمَا مَعاً وَ لاَ تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ اِفْتِرَاشَ اَلسَّبُعِ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ لاَ تَضَعَنَّ ذِرَاعَيْكَ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ فَخِذَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ تَجَنَّحْ بِمِرْفَقَيْكَ وَ لاَ تُلْزِقْ كَفَّيْكَ بِرُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لاَ تُدْنِهِمَا مِنْ وَجْهِكَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ حِيَالَ مَنْكِبَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْهُمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ تُحَرِّفُهُمَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئاً وَ اُبْسُطْهُمَا عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ بَسْطاً وَ اِقْبِضْهُمَا إِلَيْكَ قَبْضاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَحْتَهُمَا ثَوْبٌ فَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ وَ إِنْ أَفْضَيْتَ بِهِمَا إِلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَ لاَ تُفَرِّجَنَّ بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي سُجُودِكَ وَ لَكِنِ اُضْمُمْهُنَّ جَمِيعاً قَالَ فَإِذَا قَعَدْتَ فِي تَشَهُّدِكَ فَأَلْصِقْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَفَرِّجْ بَيْنَهُمَا شَيْئاً وَلْيَكُنْ ظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُسْرَى عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى بَاطِنِ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُسْرَى وَأَلْيَتَاكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَطَرَفُ إِبْهَامِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ إِيَّاكَ وَ اَلْقُعُودَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ فَتَتَأَذَّى بِذَلِكَ وَ لاَ تَكُونُ قَاعِداً عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ إِنَّمَا قَعَدَ بَعْضُكَ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَلاَ تَصْبِرَ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:

Let your shoulders hang down, release your arms, and do not interlock your fingers. Let your hands be upon your thighs, opposite your knees, and let your gaze be toward the place of your prostration. When you bow, align your position in bowing between your feet, making the distance between them about a span. Firmly place your palms upon your knees. Spread your fingers when placing them on your knees, and if the tips of your fingers reach in your bowing, reaching your kneecaps, that suffices you. But what is more beloved to me is that you firmly place your palms on your knees, so that your fingers are upon the center of the kneecap, and you spread them apart. Keep your back straight, stretch your neck, and let your gaze be directed to the space between your feet. When you intend to go into prostration, raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration, beginning with your hands, place them on the ground before your knees. Place them together. Spread them flat on the ground and draw them toward yourself in a drawing motion. If there is a cloth beneath them, it does not harm you; but if you place them directly on the earth, that is better. Let the top of your left foot be on the ground, and the top of your right foot on the sole of your left foot. Your buttocks should be on the ground, and the tip of your right big toe should be on the ground. Beware of sitting on your two feet, for that causes discomfort, and you will not truly be sitting on the ground, it would be as if you are sitting part of your body upon another part, and you will not be able to remain patient in the tashahhud and in supplication.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from a man, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s) regarding the verse: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah Kawthar 108:2). He (a.s) said: “The ‘nahr’ (sacrifice) is uprightness in standing, that one straightens his back and his neck.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Do not place your hands on your hips (takfir), for that is what the Magians do. Do not cover your mouth (talath-thum), do not squat (ihtifaz), do not sit on your feet (iq‘aʾ), and do not spread your forearms on the ground.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ« فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَ اِنْحَرْ» قَالَ« اَلنَّحْرُ اَلاِعْتِدَالُ فِي اَلْقِيَامِ أَنْ يُقِيمَ صُلْبَهُ وَ نَحْرَهُ» وَ قَالَ« لاَ تُكَفِّرْ إِنَّمَا يَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَجُوسُ وَ لاَ تَلَثَّمْ وَ لاَ تَحْتَفِزْ وَ لاَ تُقْعِ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from a man, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s) regarding the verse: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah Kawthar 108:2). He (a.s) said: “The ‘nahr’ (sacrifice) is uprightness in standing, that one straightens his back and his neck.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Do not place your hands on your hips (takfir), for that is what the Magians do. Do not cover your mouth (talath-thum), do not squat (ihtifaz), do not sit on your feet (iq‘aʾ), and do not spread your forearms on the ground.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked (Imam (a.s)): “A man places his hand in prayer, (and he demonstrated) the right over the left?. Imam (a.s) said: "That is takfeer (a gesture used by others), so do not do it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَضَعُ يَدَهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ حَكَى اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى اَلْيُسْرَى فَقَالَ« ذَلِكَ اَلتَّكْفِيرُ فَلاَ تَفْعَلْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam (a.s)): “A man places his hand in prayer, (and he demonstrated) the right over the left?. Imam (a.s) said: "That is takfeer (a gesture used by others), so do not do it."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja‘far ibn Ali, who said:
I saw Aba al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, and He (a.s) had performed a prostration after the prayer, and He (a.s) spread his forearms on the ground and pressed his chest to the ground, while still in his clothes.
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَبَسَطَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ أَلْصَقَ جُؤْجُؤَهُ بِالْأَرْضِ فِي ثِيَابِهِ
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja‘far ibn Ali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Aba al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, and He (a.s) had performed a prostration after the prayer, and He (a.s) spread his forearms on the ground and pressed his chest to the ground, while still in his clothes.
