author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan, who said:
I saw Aba al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, perform the prostration of gratitude (‘Sajdat al-Shukr’), and He (a.s) spread out his forearms and pressed his chest and stomach to the ground. So I asked Him (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “This is how it should be.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلشُّكْرِ فَافْتَرَشَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ أَلْصَقَ صَدْرَهُ وَ بَطْنَهُ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« كَذَا يَجِبُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Aba al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, perform the prostration of gratitude (‘Sajdat al-Shukr’), and He (a.s) spread out his forearms and pressed his chest and stomach to the ground. So I asked Him (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “This is how it should be.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 91

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the limit of prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever part is placed from the area between the hairline and the position of the eyebrows, it suffices you.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ حَدِّ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ« مَا بَيْنَ قُصَاصِ اَلشَّعْرِ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ اَلْحَاجِبِ مَا وَضَعْتَ مِنْهُ أَجْزَأَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the limit of prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever part is placed from the area between the hairline and the position of the eyebrows, it suffices you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 91

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked (Imam (a.s)) about a man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban. Imam (a.s) said: “If his forehead touches the ground in the area between his eyebrows and the hairline, then it suffices for him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَلَنْسُوَةٌ أَوْ عِمَامَةٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا مَسَّ جَبْهَتُهُ اَلْأَرْضَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ حَاجِبَيْهِ وَ قُصَاصِ شَعْرِهِ فَقَدْ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam (a.s)) about a man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban. Imam (a.s) said: “If his forehead touches the ground in the area between his eyebrows and the hairline, then it suffices for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 91

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating, can it be higher than the place where he stands? Imam (a.s) said: “No, but it should be level.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ مَوْضِعِ جَبْهَةِ اَلسَّاجِدِ أَ يَكُونُ أَرْفَعَ مِنْ مَقَامِهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ لِيَكُنْ مُسْتَوِياً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating, can it be higher than the place where he stands? Imam (a.s) said: “No, but it should be level.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 91

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from ‘Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who raises the place of his forehead in the mosque (during prostration). Imam (a.s) said: “I like to place my face where my feet stand,” and He (a.s) disliked (raising it).
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَرْفَعُ مَوْضِعَ جَبْهَتِهِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ« إِنِّي أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَضَعَ وَجْهِي فِي مَوْضِعِ قَدَمِي وَ كَرِهَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from ‘Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who raises the place of his forehead in the mosque (during prostration). Imam (a.s) said: “I like to place my face where my feet stand,” and He (a.s) disliked (raising it).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from one of his companions, from Musadif, who said:
A boil had appeared on me (forehead), so I was prostrating on one side. Abu Abdillah (a.s) saw its mark and said: “What is this?” I said: “I cannot prostrate because of the boil, so I prostrate while turned to the side.” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Do not do that. Dig a small pit and place the boil into the pit so that you may place your forehead on the ground.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ مُصَادِفٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ بِي دُمَّلٌ فَكُنْتُ أَسْجُدُ عَلَى جَانِبٍ فَرَأَى أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَثَرَهُ فَقَالَ« مَا هَذَا» فَقُلْتُ لاَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ مِنْ أَجْلِ اَلدُّمَّلِ فَإِنَّمَا أَسْجُدُ مُنْحَرِفاً فَقَالَ لِي« لاَ تَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ اِحْفِرْ حَفِيرَةً وَ اِجْعَلِ اَلدُّمَّلَ فِي اَلْحَفِيرَةِ حَتَّى تَضَعَ جَبْهَتَكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from one of his companions, from Musadif, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A boil had appeared on me (forehead), so I was prostrating on one side. Abu Abdillah (a.s) saw its mark and said: “What is this?” I said: “I cannot prostrate because of the boil, so I prostrate while turned to the side.” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Do not do that. Dig a small pit and place the boil into the pit so that you may place your forehead on the ground.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain of narration, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about someone who has an ailment on his forehead and is unable to prostrate upon it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should place his chin on the ground, for Allah (swt) the Exalted says: ‘They fall down upon their chins in prostration’.” (Surah Isra 17:107)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّنْ بِجَبْهَتِهِ عِلَّةٌ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلسُّجُودِ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ« يَضَعُ ذَقَنَهُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ« يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقٰانِ سُجَّداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain of narration, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about someone who has an ailment on his forehead and is unable to prostrate upon it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should place his chin on the ground, for Allah (swt) the Exalted says: ‘They fall down upon their chins in prostration’.” (Surah Isra 17:107)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prostrates while wearing a turban, such that his forehead does not touch the ground. Imam (a.s) said: “That does not suffice him until his forehead reaches the ground.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْعِمَامَةُ لاَ تُصِيبُ جَبْهَتُهُ اَلْأَرْضَ قَالَ« لاَ يُجْزِيهِ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى تَصِلَ جَبْهَتُهُ إِلَى اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prostrates while wearing a turban, such that his forehead does not touch the ground. Imam (a.s) said: “That does not suffice him until his forehead reaches the ground.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from prostration, say: ‘O Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), by Your (azj) power and strength I rise and I sit.’ And if you wish, you may also say: ‘…and I bow and I prostrate.’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قُلْتَ اَللَّهُمَّ رَبِّي بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قُلْتَ وَ أَرْكَعُ وَ أَسْجُدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from prostration, say: ‘O Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), by Your (azj) power and strength I rise and I sit.’ And if you wish, you may also say: ‘…and I bow and I prostrate.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a man rises from prostration, he says: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit).’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَامَ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a man rises from prostration, he says: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Khala:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you in qunut to say: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, You (azj) have power over all things.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ اُعْفُ عَنَّا فِي اَلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ« إِنَّكَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Khala:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you in qunut to say: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, You (azj) have power over all things.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The takbir in the obligatory prayer, in the five daily prayers, is ninety-five takbirs, among them are five takbirs of qunut.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرْضِ فِي اَلْخَمْسِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلْقُنُوتِ خَمْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The takbir in the obligatory prayer, in the five daily prayers, is ninety-five takbirs, among them are five takbirs of qunut.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah:
Imam (a.s) explained the (takbirs) as follows; In Dhuhr, twenty-one takbirs; in ‘Asr, twenty-one takbirs; in Maghrib, sixteen takbirs; in the last Isha, twenty-one takbirs; and in Fajr, eleven takbirs; and five takbirs of qunut in the five prayers.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ:« وَ فَسَّرَهُنَّ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْعَصْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي خَمْسِ صَلَوَاتٍُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) explained the (takbirs) as follows; In Dhuhr, twenty-one takbirs; in ‘Asr, twenty-one takbirs; in Maghrib, sixteen takbirs; in the last Isha, twenty-one takbirs; and in Fajr, eleven takbirs; and five takbirs of qunut in the five prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sabbah al-Muzani, who said
Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, said: “Ninety-five takbirs are (prescribed) in the day and night for the prayers, among them is the takbir of qunut.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْمُزَنِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً فِي اَلْيَوْمِ وَ اَللَّيْلَةِ لِلصَّلَوَاتِ مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلْقُنُوتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sabbah al-Muzani, who said
thaqalaynMatn: Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, said: “Ninety-five takbirs are (prescribed) in the day and night for the prayers, among them is the takbir of qunut.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit after the first two rak‘ahs and recite the tashahhud, then stand, say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ فَتَشَهَّدْتَ ثُمَّ قُمْتَ فَقُلْ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ وَ قُوَّتِهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit after the first two rak‘ahs and recite the tashahhud, then stand, say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “When (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, would rise from the first two rak‘ahs, He (a.s) would say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا نَهَضَ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ قَالَ« بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “When (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, would rise from the first two rak‘ahs, He (a.s) would say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from the two rak‘ahs, lean on your palms and say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.) for indeed (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to do that.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَمِدْ عَلَى كَفَّيْكَ وَ قُلْ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ فَإِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from the two rak‘ahs, lean on your palms and say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.) for indeed (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to do that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) for several days, and He (a.s) would perform ‘qunut’ in every prayer, whether it was one in which the recitation was audible or not.
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّاماً فَكَانَ يَقْنُتُ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا أَوْلاَ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) for several days, and He (a.s) would perform ‘qunut’ in every prayer, whether it was one in which the recitation was audible or not.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every prayer, in the second rak‘ah, before bowing.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every prayer, in the second rak‘ah, before bowing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘qunut’ in all five prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “Perform ‘qunut’ in all of them.” He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: “Then I later asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “As for the prayers in which you recite aloud, do not have any doubt about it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ اَلْخَمْسِ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ« اُقْنُتْ فِيهِنَّ جَمِيعاً» قَالَ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بَعْدُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَا جَهَرْتَ فِيهِ فَلاَ تَشُكَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘qunut’ in all five prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “Perform ‘qunut’ in all of them.” He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: “Then I later asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “As for the prayers in which you recite aloud, do not have any doubt about it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut in Maghrib is in the second rak‘ah, and in Isha and Ghadah (Fajr) it is the same. And in Witr it is in the third rak‘ah.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَ فِي اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ اَلْغَدَاةِ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ وَ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut in Maghrib is in the second rak‘ah, and in Isha and Ghadah (Fajr) it is the same. And in Witr it is in the third rak‘ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, about which prayer is it in? Imam (a.s) said: “Every prayer in which the recitation is done aloud has ‘qunut’ in it, and ‘qunut’ is before bowing and after the recitation.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ صَلاَةٍ هُوَ فَقَالَ« كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيهِ قُنُوتٌ وَ اَلْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, about which prayer is it in? Imam (a.s) said: “Every prayer in which the recitation is done aloud has ‘qunut’ in it, and ‘qunut’ is before bowing and after the recitation.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
One of our companions asked Him (a.s), and I (Abu Basir) was present, about ‘qunut’ in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said to him: “In the second rak‘ah.” So the man said to Him (a.s): “One of our companions narrated to us that you told him it is in the first rak‘ah.” Imam (a.s) said: “In the last.” Then, when He (a.s) saw that the man was confused, Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, (it is) in both the first and the last.” Then Abu Basir asked after that: “Is it before the bowing or after it?” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Every ‘qunut’ is before bowing, except in Friday prayer: in the first rak‘ah it is before bowing, and in the last it is after bowing.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ« فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ قَدْ حَدَّثَنَا بِهِ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَهُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فَقَالَ« فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» فَلَمَّا رَأَى غَفْلَةً مِنْهُ فَقَالَ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» فَقَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« كُلُّ قُنُوتٍ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ إِلاَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ فَإِنَّ اَلرَّكْعَةَ اَلْأُولَى فِيهَا قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةَ بَعْدَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: One of our companions asked Him (a.s), and I (Abu Basir) was present, about ‘qunut’ in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said to him: “In the second rak‘ah.” So the man said to Him (a.s): “One of our companions narrated to us that you told him it is in the first rak‘ah.” Imam (a.s) said: “In the last.” Then, when He (a.s) saw that the man was confused, Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, (it is) in both the first and the last.” Then Abu Basir asked after that: “Is it before the bowing or after it?” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Every ‘qunut’ is before bowing, except in Friday prayer: in the first rak‘ah it is before bowing, and in the last it is after bowing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut is in Friday prayer, Isha, ‘Atamah (night prayer), Witr, and Ghadah (Fajr). Whoever abandons qunut out of aversion to it, then he has no prayer.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَاَلْعِشَاءِ وَاَلْعَتَمَةِ وَاَلْوَتْرِ وَ اَلْغَدَاةِ فَمَنْ تَرَكَ اَلْقُنُوتَ رَغْبَةً عَنْهُ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut is in Friday prayer, Isha, ‘Atamah (night prayer), Witr, and Ghadah (Fajr). Whoever abandons qunut out of aversion to it, then he has no prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every two rak‘ahs, in supererogatory (nafl) and obligatory prayers.” Al-Hasan said: “And Abdullah ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in all prayers.” Muhammad ibn Muslim said: “So I mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (a.s), and Imam (a.s) said: “As for that in which there is no doubt, it is what is recited aloud.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلتَّطَوُّعِ وَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ» قَالَ اَلْحَسَنُ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: قَالَ« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَا لاَ يُشَكُّ فِيهِ فَمَا جُهِرَ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every two rak‘ahs, in supererogatory (nafl) and obligatory prayers.” Al-Hasan said: “And Abdullah ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in all prayers.” Muhammad ibn Muslim said: “So I mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (a.s), and Imam (a.s) said: “As for that in which there is no doubt, it is what is recited aloud.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is it before bowing or after? Imam (a.s) said: “Neither before it nor after it.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ« لاَ قَبْلَهُ وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is it before bowing or after? Imam (a.s) said: “Neither before it nor after it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is ‘qunut’ performed in all the prayers, or only in those in which the recitation is audible? Imam (a.s) said: “Qunut is only in Ghadah (Fajr), Jumu‘ah (Friday prayer), Witr, and Maghrib.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ هَلْ يُقْنَتُ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا أَمْ فِيمَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ قَالَ« لَيْسَ اَلْقُنُوتُ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْغَدَاةِ وَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ».
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is ‘qunut’ performed in all the prayers, or only in those in which the recitation is audible? Imam (a.s) said: “Qunut is only in Ghadah (Fajr), Jumu‘ah (Friday prayer), Witr, and Maghrib.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): In which prayers should I perform ‘qunut’? Imam (a.s) said: “Do not perform ‘qunut’ except in Fajr.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ أَقْنُتُ فَقَالَ« لاَ تَقْنُتْ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): In which prayers should I perform ‘qunut’? Imam (a.s) said: “Do not perform ‘qunut’ except in Fajr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding ‘qunut’: “If you wish, then perform qunut; and if you wish, do not perform it.” Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘And when there is taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), then do not perform qunut, and I adhere to this.’
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ:« إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْنُتْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لاَ تَقْنُتْ» قَالَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« وَ إِذَا كَانَتِ اَلتَّقِيَّةُ فَلاَ تَقْنُتْ وَ أَنَا أَتَقَلَّدُ هَذَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding ‘qunut’: “If you wish, then perform qunut; and if you wish, do not perform it.” Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘And when there is taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), then do not perform qunut, and I adhere to this.’

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’. Imam (a.s) said: “In that which you recite aloud.” So I said: “I asked your father (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘In all five prayers.’” Imam (a.s) said: “May Allah (swt) have mercy on my father (a.s). The companions of my father (a.s) came to him and asked him, so He (a.s) informed them of the truth. Then they came to me full of doubts, so I gave them a ruling based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فَقَالَ« فِيمَا تَجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُ أَبَاكَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« فِي اَلْخَمْسِ كُلِّهَا» فَقَالَ« رَحِمَ اَللَّهُ أَبِي إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ أَبِي أَتَوْهُ فَسَأَلُوهُ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ ثُمَّ أَتَوْنِي شُكَّاكاً فَأَفْتَيْتُهُمْ بِالتَّقِيَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’. Imam (a.s) said: “In that which you recite aloud.” So I said: “I asked your father (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘In all five prayers.’” Imam (a.s) said: “May Allah (swt) have mercy on my father (a.s). The companions of my father (a.s) came to him and asked him, so He (a.s) informed them of the truth. Then they came to me full of doubts, so I gave them a ruling based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mu‘awiyah narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ of ‘witr’: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.‘ And Imam (a.s) said: ‘Three tasbihat suffice for qunut.”’
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو اَلْقَاسِمِ مُعَاوِيَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّاكٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: فِي قُنُوتِ اَلْوَتْرِ« اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ اُعْفُ عَنَّا فِي اَلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ» وَ قَالَ« يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقُنُوتِ ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mu‘awiyah narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ of ‘witr’: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.‘ And Imam (a.s) said: ‘Three tasbihat suffice for qunut.”’

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Qunut is before bowing, and if you wish, then after it.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ وَمَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَبَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Qunut is before bowing, and if you wish, then after it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr al-Ahwal:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the first two rak‘ahs is: ‘Alhamdu lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept His (saws) intercession on behalf of His (saws) nation, and raise His (saws) rank.’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو اَلْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَقَبَّلْ شَفَاعَتَهُ فِي أُمَّتِهِ وَ اِرْفَعْ دَرَجَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr al-Ahwal:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the first two rak‘ahs is: ‘Alhamdu lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept His (saws) intercession on behalf of His (saws) nation, and raise His (saws) rank.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are leading a group in prayer, one ‘taslim’ to your right suffices. If you are praying behind an imam, then (you do) two ‘taslims’. And if you are alone, then one ‘taslim’ facing the qiblah suffices.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ كُنْتَ تَؤُمُّ قَوْماً أَجْزَأَكَ تَسْلِيمَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ فَتَسْلِيمَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَوَاحِدَةً مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are leading a group in prayer, one ‘taslim’ to your right suffices. If you are praying behind an imam, then (you do) two ‘taslims’. And if you are alone, then one ‘taslim’ facing the qiblah suffices.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The imam says one ‘taslim’, and those behind him say two ‘taslims’. But if there is no one on his left, then he says one ‘taslim’.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْإِمَامُ يُسَلِّمُ وَاحِدَةً وَمَنْ وَرَاءَهُ يُسَلِّمُ اِثْنَتَيْنِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ أَحَدٌ سَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The imam says one ‘taslim’, and those behind him say two ‘taslims’. But if there is no one on his left, then he says one ‘taslim’.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus‘ab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man standing in the row behind the imam and there is no one on his left, how should he perform the ‘taslim’? Imam (a.s) said: “One ‘taslim’ to his right.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَنْبَسَةَ بْنِ مُصْعَبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّفِّ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ أَحَدٌ كَيْفَ يُسَلِّمُ قَالَ« تَسْلِيمَةً عَنْ يَمِينِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus‘ab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man standing in the row behind the imam and there is no one on his left, how should he perform the ‘taslim’? Imam (a.s) said: “One ‘taslim’ to his right.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya, and Isma‘il:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “He performs one ‘taslim’, whether he is an imam or not.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُسَلِّمُ تَسْلِيمَةً وَاحِدَةً إِمَاماً كَانَ أَوْ غَيْرَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya, and Isma‘il:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “He performs one ‘taslim’, whether he is an imam or not.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are an imam, then the ‘taslim’ is that you send salam upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Once you say that, the prayer has ended. Then you inform the people by saying, while facing the qiblah, ‘Peace be upon you.’ And likewise, if you are praying alone, you say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt) ‘ just as you would say if you were the imam. But if you are in a congregation, then say what you have said, and send salam upon those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then send salam upon those on your right, and do not omit sending ‘taslim’ to your right even if there is no one on your left.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَإِنَّمَا اَلتَّسْلِيمُ أَنْ تُسَلِّمَ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَتَقُولَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ فَإِذَا قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدِ اِنْقَطَعَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ ثُمَّ تُؤْذِنُ اَلْقَوْمَ فَتَقُولُ وَ أَنْتَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ تَقُولُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ مِثْلَ مَا سَلَّمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ إِمَامٌ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقُلْ مِثْلَ مَا قُلْتَ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مَنْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ شِمَالِكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى اَلَّذِينَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ لاَ تَدَعِ اَلتَّسْلِيمَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are an imam, then the ‘taslim’ is that you send salam upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Once you say that, the prayer has ended. Then you inform the people by saying, while facing the qiblah, ‘Peace be upon you.’ And likewise, if you are praying alone, you say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt) ‘ just as you would say if you were the imam. But if you are in a congregation, then say what you have said, and send salam upon those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then send salam upon those on your right, and do not omit sending ‘taslim’ to your right even if there is no one on your left.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
(It was said) “When a woman stands for prayer, she joins her feet together and does not spread them apart, and she brings her hands close to her chest due to the presence of her breasts. When she bows, she places her hands above her knees, on her thighs, so that she does not bend too much and raise her backside. When she sits, she sits on her buttocks as a man does. When she moves into prostration, she begins by sitting and placing her knees down before her hands. Then she prostrates closely to the ground. When she is in her sitting posture, she brings her thighs together and lifts her knees off the ground. When she rises, she rises smoothly, without first lifting her backside.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَامَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ جَمَعَتْ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهَا وَ لاَ تُفَرِّجُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ تَضُمُّ يَدَيْهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهَا لِمَكَانِ ثَدْيَيْهَا فَإِذَا رَكَعَتْ وَضَعَتْ يَدَيْهَا فَوْقَ رُكْبَتَيْهَا عَلَى فَخِذَيْهَا لِئَلاَّ تَطَأْطَأَ كَثِيراً فَتَرْتَفِعَ عَجِيزَتُهَا فَإِذَا جَلَسَتْ فَعَلَى أَلْيَتَيْهَا كَمَا يَقْعُدُ اَلرَّجُلُ فَإِذَا سَقَطَتْ لِلسُّجُودِ بَدَأَتْ بِالْقُعُودِ وَ بِالرُّكْبَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْيَدَيْنِ ثُمَّ تَسْجُدُ لاَطِئَةً بِالْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ فِي جُلُوسِهَا ضَمَّتْ فَخِذَيْهَا وَ رَفَعَتْ رُكْبَتَيْهَا مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا نَهَضَتْ اِنْسَلَّتْ اِنْسِلاَلاً لاَ تَرْفَعُ عَجِيزَتَهَا أَوَّلاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: (It was said) “When a woman stands for prayer, she joins her feet together and does not spread them apart, and she brings her hands close to her chest due to the presence of her breasts. When she bows, she places her hands above her knees, on her thighs, so that she does not bend too much and raise her backside. When she sits, she sits on her buttocks as a man does. When she moves into prostration, she begins by sitting and placing her knees down before her hands. Then she prostrates closely to the ground. When she is in her sitting posture, she brings her thighs together and lifts her knees off the ground. When she rises, she rises smoothly, without first lifting her backside.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 100

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a woman prostrates, she spreads her forearms.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا سَجَدَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ بَسَطَتْ ذِرَاعَيْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a woman prostrates, she spreads her forearms.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 101

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the sitting posture of a woman in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “She brings her thighs together.”
arabicText: عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ جُلُوسِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« تَضُمُّ فَخِذَيْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the sitting posture of a woman in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “She brings her thighs together.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 101

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions:
(It was said): “When a woman prostrates, she gathers herself (draws herself in), and when a man prostrates, he spreads himself out.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ: «اَلْمَرْأَةُ إِذَا سَجَدَتْ تَضَمَّمَتْ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا سَجَدَ تَفَتَّحَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: (It was said): “When a woman prostrates, she gathers herself (draws herself in), and when a man prostrates, he spreads himself out.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is there anything specific or fixed regarding the recitation in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except for Jumu‘ah, ‘(Surah) al-Jumu‘ah’ and ‘(Surah) al-Munafiqin’ are to be recited.” I said to Him (a.s): “Then which surahs should be recited in the prayers?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, they are the same; and ‘Asr and Maghrib are the same. As for Ghadah (Fajr), it is the longest. As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, then (recite): ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la) and ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), and those like them. And as for ‘Asr and Maghrib, then (recite): ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah’ (Surah An-Nasr) and ‘Alhakum al-Takathur’ (Surah At-Takathur), and those like them. And as for Ghadah (Fajr), then (recite): ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba’), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and ‘Hal ata ‘ala’l-insani hinun mina’l-dahr’ (Surah Al-Insan).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ قَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ تُقْرَأُ بِالْجُمُعَةِ وَ اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ» قُلْتُ لَهُ فَأَيُّ اَلسُّوَرِ تُقْرَأُ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ قَالَ« أَمَّا اَلظُّهْرُ وَ اَلْعِشَاءُ اَلْآخِرَةُ تُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا سَوَاءً وَ اَلْعَصْرُ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ سَوَاءً وَ أَمَّا اَلْغَدَاةُ فَأَطْوَلُ وَ أَمَّا اَلظُّهْرُ وَ اَلْعِشَاءُ اَلْآخِرَةُ فَ«سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ رَبِّكَ اَلْأَعْلَى» وَ «اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» وَ نَحْوُهُمَا وَ أَمَّا اَلْعَصْرُ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ فَ«إِذٰا جٰاءَ نَصْرُ اَللّٰهِ» وَ «أَلْهٰاكُمُ اَلتَّكٰاثُرُ» وَ نَحْوُهُمَا وَ أَمَّا اَلْغَدَاةُ فَ«عَمَّ يَتَسٰاءَلُونَ» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ« لاٰ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ اَلْقِيٰامَةِ» وَ« هَلْ أَتىٰ عَلَى اَلْإِنْسٰانِ حِينٌ مِنَ اَلدَّهْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is there anything specific or fixed regarding the recitation in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except for Jumu‘ah, ‘(Surah) al-Jumu‘ah’ and ‘(Surah) al-Munafiqin’ are to be recited.” I said to Him (a.s): “Then which surahs should be recited in the prayers?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, they are the same; and ‘Asr and Maghrib are the same. As for Ghadah (Fajr), it is the longest. As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, then (recite): ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la) and ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), and those like them. And as for ‘Asr and Maghrib, then (recite): ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah’ (Surah An-Nasr) and ‘Alhakum al-Takathur’ (Surah At-Takathur), and those like them. And as for Ghadah (Fajr), then (recite): ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba’), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and ‘Hal ata ‘ala’l-insani hinun mina’l-dahr’ (Surah Al-Insan).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Isa ibn Abdillah al-Qummi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to pray Ghadah (Fajr) with: ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Dhuhr with: ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la), ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Maghrib with: ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah wa’l-fath’ (Surah An-Nasr), ‘Idha zulzilati’l-ardu zilzalaha’ (Surah Az-Zalzalah). And He (a.s) used to pray the final Isha similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Dhuhr, and ‘Asr similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Maghrib.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْقُمِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ بِ«عَمَّ يَتَسٰاءَلُونَ» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ «لاٰ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ اَلْقِيٰامَةِ» وَ شِبْهِهَا وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ بِ«سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ» وَ «اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ شِبْهِهَا وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلْمَغْرِبَ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «إِذٰا جٰاءَ نَصْرُ اَللّٰهِ وَ اَلْفَتْحُ» وَ «إِذٰا زُلْزِلَتِ» وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ بِنَحْوِ مَا يُصَلِّي فِي اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ بِنَحْوٍ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Isa ibn Abdillah al-Qummi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to pray Ghadah (Fajr) with: ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Dhuhr with: ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la), ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Maghrib with: ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah wa’l-fath’ (Surah An-Nasr), ‘Idha zulzilati’l-ardu zilzalaha’ (Surah Az-Zalzalah). And He (a.s) used to pray the final Isha similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Dhuhr, and ‘Asr similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Maghrib.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) instructed me to recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’) in the obligatory prayer.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: أَمَرَنِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) instructed me to recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’) in the obligatory prayer.

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Sabir, the freed slave of Bassam, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and He (a.s) recited ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’).
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ صَابِرٍ مَوْلَى بَسَّامٍ قَالَ: أَمَّنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَرَأَ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Sabir, the freed slave of Bassam, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and He (a.s) recited ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’).

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma‘il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, from Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Abi Talhah, the maternal uncle of Sahl ibn Abd Rabbih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “I recited in the Fajr prayer: ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al-Kafirun), and the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, also did that.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ خَالِ سَهْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «قَرَأْتُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ قَدْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma‘il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, from Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Abi Talhah, the maternal uncle of Sahl ibn Abd Rabbih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “I recited in the Fajr prayer: ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al-Kafirun), and the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, also did that.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Sa‘id al-Mukari and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah and Abu Ishaq Tha‘labah, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I pray using : ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, prayed in both rak‘ahs with ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’, and He (saws) did not pray before it or after it with anything more complete than it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ اَلْمُكَارِي وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ وَ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ ثَعْلَبَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ قَدْ صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي كِلْتَا اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ لَمْ يُصَلِّ قَبْلَهَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهَا بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» أَتَمَّ مِنْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Sa‘id al-Mukari and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah and Abu Ishaq Tha‘labah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I pray using : ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, prayed in both rak‘ahs with ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’, and He (saws) did not pray before it or after it with anything more complete than it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ suffices for fifty prayers.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:«« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» تُجْزِي فِي خَمْسِينَ صَلاَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ suffices for fifty prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 102

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “Do not recite anything from the ‘Azaʾim’ (chapters containing obligatory prostration) in the obligatory prayer, for prostration is an addition in the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ فَإِنَّ اَلسُّجُودَ زِيَادَةٌ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “Do not recite anything from the ‘Azaʾim’ (chapters containing obligatory prostration) in the obligatory prayer, for prostration is an addition in the obligatory prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yusuf ibn ‘Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) (peace be upon him), who said:
(imam (a.s) said) “Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, when He (a.s) prayed, would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ (glorification) in the last two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his ‘Asr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ in the last two rak‘ahs similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) used to say: ‘The beginning of the prayer of one of you is the bowing.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا صَلَّى يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلظُّهْرِ سِرّاً وَ يُسَبِّحُ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلظُّهْرِ عَلَى نَحْوٍ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعَصْرِ سِرّاً وَ يُسَبِّحُ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ عَلَى نَحْوٍ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ أَوَّلُ صَلاَةِ أَحَدِكُمُ اَلرُّكُوعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yusuf ibn ‘Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) (peace be upon him), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (imam (a.s) said) “Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, when He (a.s) prayed, would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ (glorification) in the last two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his ‘Asr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ in the last two rak‘ahs similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) used to say: ‘The beginning of the prayer of one of you is the bowing.’”
