chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: “Nothing of recitation or supplication is recorded except what he makes himself hear.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ وَ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يُكْتَبُ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا أَسْمَعَ نَفْسَهُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: “Nothing of recitation or supplication is recorded except what he makes himself hear.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem with that, as long as he makes his ears hear the murmur (of his recitation).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ يَقْرَأُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى فِيهِ قَالَ« فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ إِذَا أَسْمَعَ أُذُنَيْهِ اَلْهَمْهَمَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem with that, as long as he makes his ears hear the murmur (of his recitation).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man, is it permissible for him to recite in his prayer and move his tongue with the recitation only within his throat without making himself hear it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if he does not move his tongue and simply imagines (the recitation) as imagination.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ يُحَرِّكَ لِسَانَهُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِي لَهَوَاتِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ نَفْسَهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ لاَ يُحَرِّكَ لِسَانَهُ يَتَوَهَّمُ تَوَهُّماً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them both), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man, is it permissible for him to recite in his prayer and move his tongue with the recitation only within his throat without making himself hear it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if he does not move his tongue and simply imagines (the recitation) as imagination.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from someone who mentioned it:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you, when praying with them, to recite like the whispering of the soul (inner speech).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ مَعَهُمْ مِثْلُ حَدِيثِ اَلنَّفْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from someone who mentioned it:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you, when praying with them, to recite like the whispering of the soul (inner speech).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices in terms of recitation in the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “That you say: ‘Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar’, then you say the ‘takbir’ and bow.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ قَالَ« أَنْ تَقُولَ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ تُكَبِّرَ وَ تَرْكَعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices in terms of recitation in the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “That you say: ‘Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar’, then you say the ‘takbir’ and bow.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Halabi, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs of Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “You glorify (‘tusabbih’), praise Allah (swt) (‘tuhammid’), and seek forgiveness for your sins. And if you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), for it is praise and supplication.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلظُّهْرِ قَالَ« تُسَبِّحُ وَ تُحَمِّدُ اَللَّهَ وَ تَسْتَغْفِرُ لِذَنْبِكَ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ فَإِنَّهَا تَحْمِيدٌ وَ دُعَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Halabi, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs of Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “You glorify (‘tusabbih’), praise Allah (swt) (‘tuhammid’), and seek forgiveness for your sins. And if you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), for it is praise and supplication.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs, what should I do in them? Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), and if you wish, remember Allah (swt), it is the same.” I asked: “Which of the two is better?” Imam (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), they are the same. If you wish, you may glorify (‘tasbih’), and if you wish, you may recite.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مَا أَصْنَعُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ« إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاذْكُرِ اَللَّهَ فَهُوَ سَوَاءٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَأَيُّ ذَلِكَ أَفْضَلُ فَقَالَ« هُمَا وَ اَللَّهِ سَوَاءٌ إِنْ شِئْتَ سَبَّحْتَ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ قَرَأْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs, what should I do in them? Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), and if you wish, remember Allah (swt), it is the same.” I asked: “Which of the two is better?” Imam (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), they are the same. If you wish, you may glorify (‘tasbih’), and if you wish, you may recite.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Allan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “Which is better in the last two rak‘ahs, recitation or ‘tasbih’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recitation is better.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلاَّنٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ أَوِ اَلتَّسْبِيحُ فَقَالَ« اَلْقِرَاءَةُ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Allan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “Which is better in the last two rak‘ahs, recitation or ‘tasbih’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recitation is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are an imam (of prayer), then recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’) in the last two rak‘ahs. And if you are alone, then it is permissible whether you do so or not.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَاقْرَأْ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَيَسَعُكَ فَعَلْتَ أَوْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ»

englishText: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you stand for the last two rak‘ahs, do not recite in them. Rather, say: ‘al-hamdu lillah’, ‘subhan Allah’, and ‘Allahu akbar’.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا فَقُلِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ»

Rather, say: ‘al-hamdu lillah’, ‘subhan Allah’, and ‘Allahu akbar’.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur‘ah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit in the second rak‘ah, say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept his intercession for his nation, and raise his rank.) Then you praise Allah (swt) twice or three times, then rise. And when you sit in the fourth (rak‘ah), you say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tahiratu al-tayyibatu al-zakiyatu al-ghadiyatu al-raihat al-sabi ghat al-na'imatu lillah ma taba wa zaka wa tahura wa khalasa wa safa falillah wa ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah. Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu anna rabbi ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul wa ashhadu anna al-sa'ata atiyatun la rayba fiha wa anna Allah yab'athu man fi al-qubur’” (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. All greetings are for Allah (swt), and the pure, good, blessed, ascending and descending, complete and delightful prayers are for Allah (swt) whatever is good, pure, purified, sincere, and clear belongs to Allah (swt) and is for Allah (swt). And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner. And I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that my Lord (swt) is the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. And I bear witness “that the Hour is surely coming there is no doubt about it and that Allah (swt) will resurrect those who are in the graves.” All praise is due to Allah (swt) who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah (swt) not guided us. All praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord of the worlds." “O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and bless Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and send peace upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and have mercy on Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) sent blessings and bestowed favor and mercy upon Ibrahim (a.s) and upon the family of Ibrahim (a.s), indeed, You (azj) are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and Forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe, our Lord (azj), indeed You are Kind and Merciful. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me Paradise by Your (swt) grace and protect me from the Fire. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and forgive the believing men and believing women; And those who enter my house as believers, and the believing men and the believing women, and increase not the wrongdoers except in destruction."‘ Then say: ‘Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings.’ ‘Peace be upon the Prophets of Allah (swt) and His messengers.’ ‘Peace be upon Jibra’il (a.s) and Mika’il (a.s) and the close angels.’ ‘Peace be upon Muhammad ibn Abdillah (saws), the Seal of the Prophets, there is no prophet after him.’ ‘And peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Then you give the salam (salutation to conclude the prayer).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ خَيْرُ اَلْأَسْمَاءِ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَ نَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَقَبَّلْ شَفَاعَتَهُ فِي أُمَّتِهِ وَ اِرْفَعْ دَرَجَتَهُ ثُمَّ تَحْمَدُ اَللَّهَ مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَإِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قُلْتَ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ خَيْرُ اَلْأَسْمَاءِ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَ نَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلطَّاهِرَاتُ اَلطَّيِّبَاتُ اَلزَّاكِيَاتُ اَلْغَادِيَاتُ اَلرَّائِحَاتُ اَلسَّابِغَاتُ اَلنَّاعِمَاتُ لِلَّهِ مَا طَابَ وَ زَكَا وَ طَهُرَ وَ خَلَصَ وَ صَفَا فَلِلَّهِ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ رَبِّي نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ وَ أَشْهَدُ« أَنَّ اَلسّٰاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لاٰ رَيْبَ فِيهٰا وَ أَنَّ اَللّٰهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي اَلْقُبُورِ»« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ اَلَّذِي هَدٰانٰا لِهٰذٰا وَ مٰا كُنّٰا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلاٰ أَنْ هَدٰانَا اَللّٰهُ»« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَبَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَرَحَّمْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ وَ بَارَكْتَ وَ تَرَحَّمْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ« اِغْفِرْ لَنٰا وَ لِإِخْوٰانِنَا اَلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونٰا بِالْإِيمٰانِ وَ لاٰ تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنٰا غِلاًّ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنٰا إِنَّكَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ» اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اُمْنُنْ عَلَيَّ بِالْجَنَّةِ وَ عَافِنِي مِنَ اَلنَّارِ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اِغْفِرْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ« وَ لِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِناً وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَاَلْمُؤْمِنٰاتِ وَلاٰ تَزِدِ اَلظّٰالِمِينَ إِلاّٰ تَبٰاراً» ثُمَّ قُلِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى أَنْبِيَاءِ اَللَّهِ وَ رُسُلِهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى جَبْرَئِيلَ وَ مِيكَائِيلَ وَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ خَاتَمِ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ لاَ نَبِيَّ بَعْدَهُ وَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ ثُمَّ تُسَلِّمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur‘ah, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit in the second rak‘ah, say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept his intercession for his nation, and raise his rank.) Then you praise Allah (swt) twice or three times, then rise. And when you sit in the fourth (rak‘ah), you say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tahiratu al-tayyibatu al-zakiyatu al-ghadiyatu al-raihat al-sabi ghat al-na'imatu lillah ma taba wa zaka wa tahura wa khalasa wa safa falillah wa ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah. Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu anna rabbi ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul wa ashhadu anna al-sa'ata atiyatun la rayba fiha wa anna Allah yab'athu man fi al-qubur’” (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. All greetings are for Allah (swt), and the pure, good, blessed, ascending and descending, complete and delightful prayers are for Allah (swt) whatever is good, pure, purified, sincere, and clear belongs to Allah (swt) and is for Allah (swt). And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner. And I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that my Lord (swt) is the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. And I bear witness “that the Hour is surely coming there is no doubt about it and that Allah (swt) will resurrect those who are in the graves.” All praise is due to Allah (swt) who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah (swt) not guided us. All praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord of the worlds." “O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and bless Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and send peace upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and have mercy on Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) sent blessings and bestowed favor and mercy upon Ibrahim (a.s) and upon the family of Ibrahim (a.s), indeed, You (azj) are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and Forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe, our Lord (azj), indeed You are Kind and Merciful. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me Paradise by Your (swt) grace and protect me from the Fire. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and forgive the believing men and believing women; And those who enter my house as believers, and the believing men and the believing women, and increase not the wrongdoers except in destruction."‘ Then say: ‘Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings.’ ‘Peace be upon the Prophets of Allah (swt) and His messengers.’ ‘Peace be upon Jibra’il (a.s) and Mika’il (a.s) and the close angels.’ ‘Peace be upon Muhammad ibn Abdillah (saws), the Seal of the Prophets, there is no prophet after him.’ ‘And peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Then you give the salam (salutation to conclude the prayer).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 105

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdillah, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices to be said in the ‘tashahhud’ of the first two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah’.” I said: “And what suffices in the ‘tashahhud’ of the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ قَالَ« تَقُولُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ» قُلْتُ فَمَا يُجْزِي مِنْ تَشَهُّدِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« اَلشَّهَادَتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdillah, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices to be said in the ‘tashahhud’ of the first two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah’.” I said: “And what suffices in the ‘tashahhud’ of the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 106

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hajjal, from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun, from Yahya ibn Talhah, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the minimum that suffices for ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies (‘al-shahadatan’).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ طَلْحَةَ عَنْ سَوْرَةَ بْنِ كُلَيْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ قَالَ« اَلشَّهَادَتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hajjal, from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun, from Yahya ibn Talhah, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the minimum that suffices for ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies (‘al-shahadatan’).”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Bakr, from Habib al-Khath‘ami:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man sits for the ‘tashahhud’ and praises Allah (swt), it suffices him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ حَبِيبٍ اَلْخَثْعَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا جَلَسَ اَلرَّجُلُ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ أَجْزَأَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Bakr, from Habib al-Khath‘ami:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man sits for the ‘tashahhud’ and praises Allah (swt), it suffices him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 107

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the ‘tashahhud’ which is said in the second rak‘ah, is it sufficient if I say it in the fourth [rak‘ah] as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ اَلتَّشَهُّدُ اَلَّذِي فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ يُجْزِي أَنْ أَقُولَهُ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the ‘tashahhud’ which is said in the second rak‘ah, is it sufficient if I say it in the fourth [rak‘ah] as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “If it were as they say, obligatory upon the people, they would have perished. Rather, the people used to say the simplest of what they knew. If you praise Allah (swt), it suffices you.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فَقَالَ« لَوْ كَانَ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ وَاجِباً عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ هَلَكُوا إِنَّمَا كَانَ اَلْقَوْمُ يَقُولُونَ أَيْسَرَ مَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِذَا حَمِدْتَ اَللَّهَ أَجْزَأَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “If it were as they say, obligatory upon the people, they would have perished. Rather, the people used to say the simplest of what they knew. If you praise Allah (swt), it suffices you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 107

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The ‘tashahhud’ in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Twice.” I said: “And how is it said twice?” Imam (a.s) said: “When you sit upright, say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan Abduhu wa rasuluh,’ then you exit (complete the prayer).” I said: “What about the statement of the servant: ‘al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tayyibat lillah’?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is a graceful form of supplication, a kindness from the servant by which his Lord shows him grace.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« مَرَّتَيْنِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَالَ« إِذَا اِسْتَوَيْتَ جَالِساً فَقُلْ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ ثُمَّ تَنْصَرِفُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَوْلُ اَلْعَبْدِ اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلَّهِ قَالَ« هَذَا اَللُّطْفُ مِنَ اَلدُّعَاءِ يَلْطُفُ اَلْعَبْدَ رَبُّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The ‘tashahhud’ in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Twice.” I said: “And how is it said twice?” Imam (a.s) said: “When you sit upright, say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan Abduhu wa rasuluh,’ then you exit (complete the prayer).” I said: “What about the statement of the servant: ‘al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tayyibat lillah’?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is a graceful form of supplication, a kindness from the servant by which his Lord shows him grace.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 107

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Ali, from ‘Ubayd, from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, is in two parts.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ شَفْعٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Ali, from ‘Ubayd, from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, is in two parts.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What should I say in the ‘tashahhud’ and in the ‘qunut’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Say the best of what you know, for if it had been fixed (with strict wording), the people would have perished.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَقُولُ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ وَ اَلْقُنُوتِ قَالَ« قُلْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا عَلِمْتَ فَإِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ مُوَقَّتاً لَهَلَكَ اَلنَّاسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What should I say in the ‘tashahhud’ and in the ‘qunut’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Say the best of what you know, for if it had been fixed (with strict wording), the people would have perished.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Abbas, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Hammad, from Abu Basir, who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s), and when He (a.s) reached the final ‘tashahhud’, He (a.s) raised his voice until we could hear him. When He (a.s) finished the prayer, I said to him: “Is it appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make his ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ تَشَهُّدِهِ رَفَعَ صَوْتَهُ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَنَا فَلَمَّا اِنْصَرَفَ قُلْتُ كَذَا يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ تَشَهُّدَهُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Abbas, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Hammad, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s), and when He (a.s) reached the final ‘tashahhud’, He (a.s) raised his voice until we could hear him. When He (a.s) finished the prayer, I said to him: “Is it appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make his ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make audible to those behind him everything that he says, and it is not appropriate for those behind the imam (of prayer) to make anything they say audible to him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ كُلَّمَا يَقُولُ وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَهُ شَيْئاً مِمَّا يَقُولُ».
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make audible to those behind him everything that he says, and it is not appropriate for those behind the imam (of prayer) to make anything they say audible to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make the ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him, and they should not make anything audible to him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ اَلتَّشَهُّدَ وَ لاَ يُسْمِعُونَهُ شَيْئاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make the ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him, and they should not make anything audible to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-‘Ubaydi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man, whether it is proper for him to recite aloud the ‘tashahhud’ and the statements in ‘ruku’, ‘sujud’, and ‘qunut’. Imam (a.s) said: “If he wishes, he may recite aloud, and if he wishes, he may not recite aloud.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بِالتَّشَهُّدِ وَاَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَاَلسُّجُودِ وَاَلْقُنُوتِ قَالَ« إِنْ شَاءَ جَهَرَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يَجْهَرْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-‘Ubaydi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man, whether it is proper for him to recite aloud the ‘tashahhud’ and the statements in ‘ruku’, ‘sujud’, and ‘qunut’. Imam (a.s) said: “If he wishes, he may recite aloud, and if he wishes, he may not recite aloud.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to move (from his place) after the taslim until those behind him complete their prayer.” He (al-Halabi) said: “I asked Him (a.s) about the man who leads others in prayer, should he engage in ta‘qib with his companions after the taslim?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should recite tasbih, and whoever wishes may go to attend to his need, and no man should remain seated for the sake of the Imam’s ta‘qib.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَنْتَقِلَ إِذَا سَلَّمَ حَتَّى يُتِمَّ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ اَلصَّلاَةَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ هَلْ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يُعَقِّبَ بِأَصْحَابِهِ بَعْدَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ فَقَالَ« يُسَبِّحُ وَ يَذْهَبُ مَنْ شَاءَ لِحَاجَتِهِ وَ لاَ يُعَقِّبُ رَجُلٌ لِتَعْقِيبِ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to move (from his place) after the taslim until those behind him complete their prayer.” He (al-Halabi) said: “I asked Him (a.s) about the man who leads others in prayer, should he engage in ta‘qib with his companions after the taslim?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should recite tasbih, and whoever wishes may go to attend to his need, and no man should remain seated for the sake of the Imam’s ta‘qib.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Any man who leads a group (in prayer) is required to remain seated after the taslim and not leave that spot until those behind him who had missed part of their prayer have completed it. This is obligatory upon every imam (of prayer) when he knows that among them is someone who has missed part of the prayer. But if he knows that there is no one among them who has missed part of the prayer, then he may go wherever he wishes.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْعُدَ بَعْدَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ وَ لاَ يَخْرُجَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَوْضِعِ حَتَّى يُتِمَّ اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ اَلَّذِينَ سُبِقُوا صَلاَتَهُمْ ذَلِكَ عَلَى كُلِّ إِمَامٍ وَاجِبٌ إِذَا عَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيهِمْ مَسْبُوقاً وَ إِنْ عَلِمَ أَنْ لَيْسَ فِيهِمْ مَسْبُوقاً بِالصَّلاَةِ فَلْيَذْهَبْ حَيْثُ شَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Any man who leads a group (in prayer) is required to remain seated after the taslim and not leave that spot until those behind him who had missed part of their prayer have completed it. This is obligatory upon every imam (of prayer) when he knows that among them is someone who has missed part of the prayer. But if he knows that there is no one among them who has missed part of the prayer, then he may go wherever he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from the one who narrated it from him:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever performs an obligatory prayer and remains in ta‘qib until the (time of) the next (prayer), then he is the guest of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, and it is a right upon Allah (swt), the Exalted, to honor His (swt) guest.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ يُونُسَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى صَلاَةً فَرِيضَةً وَعَقَّبَ إِلَى أُخْرَى فَهُوَ ضَيْفُ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَ جَلَّ وَحَقٌّ عَلَى اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى أَنْ يُكْرِمَ ضَيْفَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from the one who narrated it from him:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever performs an obligatory prayer and remains in ta‘qib until the (time of) the next (prayer), then he is the guest of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, and it is a right upon Allah (swt), the Exalted, to honor His (swt) guest.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Supplication after the obligatory prayer is better than performing voluntary prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلدُّعَاءُ بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ تَنَفُّلاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Supplication after the obligatory prayer is better than performing voluntary prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Sama‘ah, who said:
(it was said) “It is appropriate for the Imam to remain (seated) before speaking to anyone until he sees that those behind him have completed their prayer, then he may depart.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَلْبَثَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَ أَحَداً حَتَّى يَرَى أَنَّ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ قَدْ أَتَمُّوا اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُ هُوَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (it was said) “It is appropriate for the Imam to remain (seated) before speaking to anyone until he sees that those behind him have completed their prayer, then he may depart.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Aban from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih and Abdullah ibn Sinan, both from al-Walid ibn Sabih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Ta‘qib is more effective in seeking sustenance than traveling through the lands (in search of it).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ شِهَابِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ كِلَيْهِمَا عَنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ بْنِ صَبِيحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّعْقِيبُ أَبْلَغُ فِي طَلَبِ اَلرِّزْقِ مِنَ اَلضَّرْبِ فِي اَلْبِلاَدِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Aban from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih and Abdullah ibn Sinan, both from al-Walid ibn Sabih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Ta‘qib is more effective in seeking sustenance than traveling through the lands (in search of it).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
(Imam (a.s) said) “Supplication after the obligatory prayer is better than supplication after the recommended prayer, just as the obligatory prayer is superior to the recommended one.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلدُّعَاءُ دُبُرَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ اَلدُّعَاءِ دُبُرَ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ كَفَضْلِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ عَلَى اَلتَّطَوُّعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “Supplication after the obligatory prayer is better than supplication after the recommended prayer, just as the obligatory prayer is superior to the recommended one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from al-Rabi‘ ibn Zakariyya al-Katib from Abdullah ibn Muhammad:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “People have not practiced anything more demanding than ta‘qib.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلرَّبِيعِ بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا اَلْكَاتِبِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَا عَالَجَ اَلنَّاسُ شَيْئاً أَشَدَّ مِنَ اَلتَّعْقِيبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from al-Rabi‘ ibn Zakariyya al-Katib from Abdullah ibn Muhammad:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “People have not practiced anything more demanding than ta‘qib.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Two men began the prayer at the same time. One of them recited the Qur’an, and his recitation was more than his supplication. The other supplicated more, and his supplication was more than his recitation. Then they both concluded (their prayers) at the same time. Which of them is superior?” Imam (a.s) said: “Each has merit. Each is good.” I asked: “I know that each is good and that each has merit, but..” Imam (a.s) said: “Supplication is superior. Have you not heard the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted: ‘And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Surely those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation’? (Surah Ghafir 40:60). By Allah (swt), it is worship! By Allah (swt), it is superior! By Allah (swt), it is superior! Is it not worship? By Allah (swt), it is worship! By Allah (swt), it is worship! Is it not the most intense of them? By Allah (swt), it is the most intense of them. By Allah (swt), it is the most intense of them.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلَيْنِ اِفْتَتَحَا اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي سَاعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَتَلاَ هَذَا اَلْقُرْآنَ فَكَانَتْ تِلاَوَتُهُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ دُعَائِهِ وَ دَعَا هَذَا أَكْثَرَ فَكَانَ دُعَاؤُهُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ تِلاَوَتِهِ ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفَا فِي سَاعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ أَيُّهُمَا أَفْضَلُ قَالَ« كُلٌّ فِيهِ فَضْلٌ كُلٌّ حَسَنٌ» قُلْتُ إِنِّي قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ كُلاًّ حَسَنٌ وَ أَنَّ كُلاًّ فِيهِ فَضْلٌ فَقَالَ« اَلدُّعَاءُ أَفْضَلُ أَ مَا سَمِعْتَ قَوْلَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« وَ قٰالَ رَبُّكُمُ اُدْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ اَلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبٰادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دٰاخِرِينَ» هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ اَلْعِبَادَةُ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ أَ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ اَلْعِبَادَةَ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ اَلْعِبَادَةُ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ اَلْعِبَادَةُ أَ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ أَشَدَّهُنَّ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ أَشَدُّهُنَّ هِيَ وَ اَللَّهِ أَشَدُّهُنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Two men began the prayer at the same time. One of them recited the Qur’an, and his recitation was more than his supplication. The other supplicated more, and his supplication was more than his recitation. Then they both concluded (their prayers) at the same time. Which of them is superior?” Imam (a.s) said: “Each has merit. Each is good.” I asked: “I know that each is good and that each has merit, but..” Imam (a.s) said: “Supplication is superior. Have you not heard the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted: ‘And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Surely those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation’? (Surah Ghafir 40:60). By Allah (swt), it is worship! By Allah (swt), it is superior! By Allah (swt), it is superior! Is it not worship? By Allah (swt), it is worship! By Allah (swt), it is worship! Is it not the most intense of them? By Allah (swt), it is the most intense of them. By Allah (swt), it is the most intense of them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever recites the Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a), peace be upon her, before folding his legs after the obligatory prayer will be forgiven. And he should begin with the takbir.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ سَبَّحَ تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ اَلزَّهْرَاءِ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَثْنِيَ رِجْلَيْهِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ غُفِرَ لَهُ وَ يَبْدَأُ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever recites the Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a), peace be upon her, before folding his legs after the obligatory prayer will be forgiven. And he should begin with the takbir.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Yahya ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Ibn Abi Najran from a man:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever glorifies Allah (swt) after the obligatory prayer with the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, one hundred times, and follows it with ‘La ilaha illallah ‘ (There is no god but Allah (swt)), Allah (swt) will forgive him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ سَبَّحَ اَللَّهَ فِي دُبُرِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْمِائَةَ وَ أَتْبَعَهَا بِلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ غَفَرَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Yahya ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Ibn Abi Najran from a man:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever glorifies Allah (swt) after the obligatory prayer with the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, one hundred times, and follows it with ‘La ilaha illallah ‘ (There is no god but Allah (swt)), Allah (swt) will forgive him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “O Abu Harun, we instruct our children to (recite) the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, just as we instruct them to perform the prayer. So adhere to it, for no servant adheres to it and becomes wretched.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ أَبِي هَارُونَ اَلْمَكْفُوفِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَا أَبَا هَارُونَ إِنَّا نَأْمُرُ صِبْيَانَنَا بِتَسْبِيحِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ كَمَا نَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَالْزَمْهُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَلْزَمْهُ عَبْدٌ فَشَقِيَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “O Abu Harun, we instruct our children to (recite) the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, just as we instruct them to perform the prayer. So adhere to it, for no servant adheres to it and becomes wretched.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And through this same chain of transmission, from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Allah (swt) has not been worshipped with anything of praise better than the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, and had there been anything better than it, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, would have gifted it to (Sayyida) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her.”
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَ قَالَ:« مَا عُبِدَ اَللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلتَّحْمِيدِ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ تَسْبِيحِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ لَوْ كَانَ شَيْءٌ أَفْضَلَ مِنْهُ لَنَحَلَهُ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And through this same chain of transmission, from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Allah (swt) has not been worshipped with anything of praise better than the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, and had there been anything better than it, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, would have gifted it to (Sayyida) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, every day after every prayer is more beloved to me than performing a thousand rak‘ahs of prayer each day.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي خَالِدٍ اَلْقَمَّاطِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« تَسْبِيحُ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ صَلاَةِ أَلْفِ رَكْعَةٍ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “The Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, every day after every prayer is more beloved to me than performing a thousand rak‘ahs of prayer each day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, who said:
I entered with my father upon Abu Abdillah (a.s), and my father asked Him (a.s) about the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her. Imam (a.s) said: ‘Allahu Akbar’ - Until He (a.s) counted thirty-four times. Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Alhamdulillah’ - Until He (a.s) reached sixty-eight. Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Subhanallah’ - Until He (a.s) completed one hundred. He (a.s) would count them with his hand all together as one sequence.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ قَالَ: دَخَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَسَأَلَهُ أَبِي عَنْ تَسْبِيحِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» حَتَّى أَ حْصَى أَرْبَعاً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ مَرَّةً ثُمَّ قَالَ« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» حَتَّى بَلَغَ سَبْعاً وَ سِتِّينَ ثُمَّ قَالَ« سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ» حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِائَةً يُحْصِيهَا بِيَدِهِ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I entered with my father upon Abu Abdillah (a.s), and my father asked Him (a.s) about the Tasbih of Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her. Imam (a.s) said: ‘Allahu Akbar’ - Until He (a.s) counted thirty-four times. Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Alhamdulillah’ - Until He (a.s) reached sixty-eight. Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Subhanallah’ - Until He (a.s) completed one hundred. He (a.s) would count them with his hand all together as one sequence.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “You begin with the takbir thirty-four times, then the tahmid thirty-three times, then the tasbih thirty-three times.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ:« تَبْدَأُ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ أَرْبَعاً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ ثُمَّ اَلتَّحْمِيدِ ثَلاَثاً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ ثُمَّ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ ثَلاَثاً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “You begin with the takbir thirty-four times, then the tahmid thirty-three times, then the tasbih thirty-three times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and al-Hasan ibn Sa‘id from Zur‘ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Say after the tasleem (concluding the prayer), ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah (swt), alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him (swt) belongs all praise. He (swt) gives life and causes death, and He (swt) is the Living who does not die. In His (swt) hand is all good, and He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah (swt), alone. He (swt) fulfilled His (swt) promise, and aided His (swt) servant, and defeated the confederates alone. O Allah (swt), guide me to the truth concerning that in which there is disagreement, by Your (swt) permission. Indeed, You (swt) guide whom You (swt) will to the straight path."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ وَاَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْ بَعْدَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ« لاٰ إِلٰهَ إِلاَّ اَللّٰهُ» وَحْدَهُ« لاٰ شَرِيكَ لَهُ»« لَهُ اَلْمُلْكُ وَ لَهُ اَلْحَمْدُ»« يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ» وَ هُوَ حَيٌّ لاَ يَمُوتُ بِيَدِهِ اَلْخَيْرُ« وَ هُوَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ صَدَقَ وَعْدَهُ وَ نَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ وَ هَزَمَ اَلْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ اَللَّهُمَّ اِهْدِنِي لِمَا اُخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ مِنَ اَلْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِكَ إِنَّكَ تَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and al-Hasan ibn Sa‘id from Zur‘ah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Say after the tasleem (concluding the prayer), ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah (swt), alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him (swt) belongs all praise. He (swt) gives life and causes death, and He (swt) is the Living who does not die. In His (swt) hand is all good, and He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah (swt), alone. He (swt) fulfilled His (swt) promise, and aided His (swt) servant, and defeated the confederates alone. O Allah (swt), guide me to the truth concerning that in which there is disagreement, by Your (swt) permission. Indeed, You (swt) guide whom You (swt) will to the straight path."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), when He (a.s) completed his prayer, raise both his hands above his head.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا صَلَّى فَفَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ جَمِيعاً فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), when He (a.s) completed his prayer, raise both his hands above his head.
