chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Mu‘awiyah ibn Shurayh from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb from ‘Amr ibn Nahik from Sallam al-Makki:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, whose name was Shaybah al-Hudhali, and he said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), I am an old man; my age has advanced, and my strength has weakened from the acts I had trained myself upon, prayer, fasting, Hajj, and jihad. So teach me, O Messenger of Allah (swt), some words by which Allah (swt) will benefit me and lighten (the burden) upon me, O Messenger of Allah (swt).” He (saws) replied: “Repeat (what you said).” So he repeated it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said to him: “There is not a tree or a clod of earth around you except that it has wept out of mercy for you. So when you have prayed the morning prayer, say ten times: ‘Subhana Allah al-azim wa bihamdih, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Aliyy al-‘Azim’ (Glory be to Allah (swt), the Almighty, and with His (swt) praise. There is no power and no strength except with Allah (swt), the Most High, the Most Great.) Indeed, with this Allah (swt) will protect you from blindness, insanity, leprosy, poverty, and decrepitude.” The man said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), that is for this world, so what about the Hereafter?” He (saws) said: “Say after every prayer: ‘O Allah (swt), guide me from Yourself (swt), pour upon me from Your (azj) bounty, spread upon me from Your (azj) mercy, and send down upon me from Your (azj) blessings.’” He (the narrator) said: So He (saws) grasped them in his hand and walked on. A man said to Ibn ‘Abbas: "How tightly your uncle clung to them!" He said: Then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: “Indeed, if he meets (his Lord (azj)) on the Day of Resurrection having preserved them and not having deliberately abandoned them, Allah (swt) will open for him eight gates from the gates of Paradise, and he will enter through whichever of them he wishes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ نَهِيكٍ عَنْ سَلاَّمٍ اَلْمَكِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتَى رَجُلٌ إِلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُقَالُ لَهُ شَيْبَةُ اَلْهُذَيْلِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنِّي شَيْخٌ قَدْ كَبِرَ سِنِّي وَ ضَعُفَتْ قُوَّتِي عَنْ عَمَلٍ كُنْتُ قَدْ عَوَّدْتُهُ نَفْسِي مِنْ صَلاَةٍ وَ صِيَامٍ وَ حَجٍّ وَ جِهَادٍ فَعَلِّمْنِي يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ كَلاَماً يَنْفَعُنِي اَللَّهُ بِهِ وَ خَفِّفْ عَلَيَّ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَقَالَ« أَعِدْ» فَأَعَادَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ« مَا حَوْلَكَ شَجَرَةٌ وَلاَ مَدَرَةٌ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ بَكَتْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِكَ فَإِذَا صَلَّيْتَ اَلصُّبْحَ فَقُلْ عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ اَلْعَلِيِّ اَلْعَظِيمِ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ يُعَافِيكَ بِذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلْعَمَى وَ اَلْجُنُونِ وَاَلْجُذَامِ وَ اَلْفَقْرِ وَ اَلْهَرَمِ» فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ هَذَا لِلدُّنْيَا فَمَا لِلْآخِرَةِ فَقَالَ« تَقُولُ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ اَللَّهُمَّ اِهْدِنِي مِنْ عِنْدِكَ وَ أَفِضْ عَلَيَّ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ وَ اُنْشُرْ عَلَيَّ مِنْ رَحْمَتِكَ وَ أَنْزِلْ عَلَيَّ مِنْ بَرَكَاتِكَ» قَالَ فَقَبَضَ عَلَيْهِنَّ بِيَدِهِ ثُمَّ مَضَى فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لاِبْنِ عَبَّاسٍ شَدَّ مَا قَبَضَ عَلَيْهَا خَالُكَ قَالَ فَقَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« أَمَا إِنَّهُ إِنْ وَافَى بِهَا يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ لَمْ يَدَعْهَا مُتَعَمِّداً فَتَحَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَبْوَابٍ مِنْ أَبْوَابِ اَلْجَنَّةِ يَدْخُلُ مِنْ أَيِّهَا شَاءَ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Mu‘awiyah ibn Shurayh from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb from ‘Amr ibn Nahik from Sallam al-Makki:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, whose name was Shaybah al-Hudhali, and he said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), I am an old man; my age has advanced, and my strength has weakened from the acts I had trained myself upon, prayer, fasting, Hajj, and jihad. So teach me, O Messenger of Allah (swt), some words by which Allah (swt) will benefit me and lighten (the burden) upon me, O Messenger of Allah (swt).” He (saws) replied: “Repeat (what you said).” So he repeated it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said to him: “There is not a tree or a clod of earth around you except that it has wept out of mercy for you. So when you have prayed the morning prayer, say ten times: ‘Subhana Allah al-azim wa bihamdih, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Aliyy al-‘Azim’ (Glory be to Allah (swt), the Almighty, and with His (swt) praise. There is no power and no strength except with Allah (swt), the Most High, the Most Great.) Indeed, with this Allah (swt) will protect you from blindness, insanity, leprosy, poverty, and decrepitude.” The man said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), that is for this world, so what about the Hereafter?” He (saws) said: “Say after every prayer: ‘O Allah (swt), guide me from Yourself (swt), pour upon me from Your (azj) bounty, spread upon me from Your (azj) mercy, and send down upon me from Your (azj) blessings.’” He (the narrator) said: So He (saws) grasped them in his hand and walked on. A man said to Ibn ‘Abbas: "How tightly your uncle clung to them!" He said: Then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: “Indeed, if he meets (his Lord (azj)) on the Day of Resurrection having preserved them and not having deliberately abandoned them, Allah (swt) will open for him eight gates from the gates of Paradise, and he will enter through whichever of them he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 113

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted: ‘Remember Allah (swt) with much remembrance’ (Surah Ahzab 33:41), what is meant by “much remembrance”? Imam (a.s) said: “That one says tasbih (subhanAllah) thirty times after the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَ جَلَّ« اُذْكُرُوا اَللّٰهَ ذِكْراً كَثِيراً» مَاذَا اَلذِّكْرُ اَلْكَثِيرُ قَالَ« أَنْ يُسَبِّحَ فِي دُبُرِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ ثَلاَثِينَ مَرَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted: ‘Remember Allah (swt) with much remembrance’ (Surah Ahzab 33:41), what is meant by “much remembrance”? Imam (a.s) said: “That one says tasbih (subhanAllah) thirty times after the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 114

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Ayyub, who said Abu Basir narrated to me:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said to his companions one day: ‘Do you think that if you gathered together all the clothing and vessels you possess, then placed them one on top of another, do you think it would reach the sky?’ They said: ‘No, O Messenger of Allah (swt).’ He (saws) said: ‘One of you says, when he finishes his prayer: ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wa Allahu Akbar’, thirty times. These repel destruction, drowning, burning, falling into a well, being devoured by a beast, a bad death, and the calamity that descends upon the servant on that day.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ« أَ رَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ جَمَعْتُمْ مَا عِنْدَكُمْ مِنَ اَلثِّيَابِ وَ اَلْآنِيَةِ ثُمَّ وَضَعْتُمْ بَعْضَهُ عَلَى بَعْضٍ تَرَوْنَهُ يَبْلُغُ اَلسَّمَاءَ» قَالُوا لاَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَقَالَ« يَقُولُ أَحَدُكُمْ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ثَلاَثِينَ مَرَّةً وَ هُنَّ يَدْفَعْنَ اَلْهَدْمَ وَ اَلْغَرَقَ وَ اَلْحَرَقَ وَ اَلتَّرَدِّيَ فِي اَلْبِئْرِ وَ أَكْلَ اَلسَّبُعِ وَ مِيتَةَ اَلسَّوْءِ وَ اَلْبَلِيَّةَ اَلَّتِي نَزَلَتْ عَلَى اَلْعَبْدِ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Ayyub, who said Abu Basir narrated to me:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said to his companions one day: ‘Do you think that if you gathered together all the clothing and vessels you possess, then placed them one on top of another, do you think it would reach the sky?’ They said: ‘No, O Messenger of Allah (swt).’ He (saws) said: ‘One of you says, when he finishes his prayer: ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wa Allahu Akbar’, thirty times. These repel destruction, drowning, burning, falling into a well, being devoured by a beast, a bad death, and the calamity that descends upon the servant on that day.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 114

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The least that suffices you from supplication after the obligatory prayer is to say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You for every good which Your knowledge encompasses, and I seek refuge in You from every evil which Your knowledge encompasses. O Allah (swt), I ask You for well-being in all my affairs, and I seek refuge in You from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «أَقَلُّ مَا يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلدُّعَاءِ بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ أَنْ تَقُولَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ كُلِّ خَيْرٍ أَحَاطَ بِهِ عِلْمُكَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ كُلِّ شَرٍّ أَحَاطَ بِهِ عِلْمُكَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عَافِيَتَكَ فِي أُمُورِي كُلِّهَا وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ خِزْيِ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ عَذَابِ اَلْآخِرَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The least that suffices you from supplication after the obligatory prayer is to say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You for every good which Your knowledge encompasses, and I seek refuge in You from every evil which Your knowledge encompasses. O Allah (swt), I ask You for well-being in all my affairs, and I seek refuge in You from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 114

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Do not forget the two obligations,” or Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon you to observe the two obligations after every prayer.” I asked: “And what are the two obligations?” Imam (a.s) said: “You ask Allah (swt) for Paradise and you seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the Fire.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «لاَ تَنْسَوُا اَلْمُوجِبَتَيْنِ» أَوْ قَالَ« عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْمُوجِبَتَيْنِ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا اَلْمُوجِبَتَانِ قَالَ« تَسْأَلُ اَللَّهَ اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ تَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Do not forget the two obligations,” or Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon you to observe the two obligations after every prayer.” I asked: “And what are the two obligations?” Imam (a.s) said: “You ask Allah (swt) for Paradise and you seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the Fire.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad al-Wasiti, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Do not leave, after every prayer, to say: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by Allah (swt), the One, the Self-Sufficient’, until you complete it, And: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by the Lord of al-Falaq’, until you complete it, And: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by the Lord of mankind’, until you complete it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْوَاسِطِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ تَدَعْ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ أُعِيذُ نَفْسِي وَ مَا رَزَقَنِي رَبِّي بِاللَّهِ اَلْوَاحِدِ اَلصَّمَدِ حَتَّى تَخْتِمَهَا وَ أُعِيذُ نَفْسِي وَ مَا رَزَقَنِي رَبِّي« بِرَبِّ اَلْفَلَقِ» حَتَّى تَخْتِمَهَا وَ أُعِيذُ نَفْسِي وَ مَا رَزَقَنِي رَبِّي« بِرَبِّ اَلنّٰاسِ» حَتَّى تَخْتِمَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad al-Wasiti, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Do not leave, after every prayer, to say: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by Allah (swt), the One, the Self-Sufficient’, until you complete it, And: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by the Lord of al-Falaq’, until you complete it, And: ‘I seek protection for myself and what my Lord has provided me with, by the Lord of mankind’, until you complete it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it has been narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever wishes to depart from this world having been cleansed of sins as pure gold is cleansed of impurities, and with no one seeking from him a right due to injustice, let him say after every prayer the ‘(Surah al-Ikhlas)’ twelve times. Then he should spread his hands and say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by Your hidden, treasured, pure, immaculate, and blessed Name. And I ask You (azj) by Your great Name and Your ancient authority, that You (azj) send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws). O Giver of gifts, O Liberator of captives, O Deliverer of necks from the Fire, I ask You (azj) to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and to free my neck from the Fire, and to cause me to leave this world in security, and to admit me into Paradise in peace. And that You (azj) make the beginning of my supplication success, and its middle acceptance, and its end righteousness. Indeed, You (azj) are the Knower of the unseen.’ Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: “This is from the hidden teachings which the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, taught me, and He (saws) commanded me to teach it to al-Hasan (a.s) and al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنَ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ قَدْ تَخَلَّصَ مِنَ اَلذُّنُوبِ كَمَا يَتَخَلَّصُ اَلذَّهَبُ اَلَّذِي لاَ كَدَرَ فِيهِ وَ لاَ يَطْلُبَهُ أَحَدٌ بِمَظْلِمَةٍ فَلْيَقُلْ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ نِسْبَةَ اَلرَّبِّ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى اِثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً» ثُمَّ يَبْسُطُ يَدَيْهِ فَيَقُولُ« اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِاسْمِكَ اَلْمَكْنُونِ اَلْمَخْزُونِ اَلطُّهْرِ اَلطَّاهِرِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ بِاسْمِكَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ سُلْطَانِكَ اَلْقَدِيمِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ يَا وَاهِبَ اَلْعَطَايَا يَا مُطْلِقَ اَلْأُسَارَى يَافَكَّاكَ اَلرِّقَابِ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تُعْتِقَ رَقَبَتِي مِنَ اَلنَّارِ وَ تُخْرِجَنِي مِنَ اَلدُّنْيَا آمِناً وَ تُدْخِلَنِي اَلْجَنَّةَ سَالِماً وَأَنْ تَجْعَلَ دُعَائِي أَوَّلَهُ فَلاَحاً وَأَوْسَطَهُ نَجَاحاً وَآخِرَهُ صَلاَحاً« إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلاّٰمُ اَلْغُيُوبِ»» ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« هَذَا مِنَ اَلْمَخْبِيَّاتِ مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أُعَلِّمَهُ اَلْحَسَنَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنَ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynMatn: And it has been narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever wishes to depart from this world having been cleansed of sins as pure gold is cleansed of impurities, and with no one seeking from him a right due to injustice, let him say after every prayer the ‘(Surah al-Ikhlas)’ twelve times. Then he should spread his hands and say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by Your hidden, treasured, pure, immaculate, and blessed Name. And I ask You (azj) by Your great Name and Your ancient authority, that You (azj) send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws). O Giver of gifts, O Liberator of captives, O Deliverer of necks from the Fire, I ask You (azj) to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and to free my neck from the Fire, and to cause me to leave this world in security, and to admit me into Paradise in peace. And that You (azj) make the beginning of my supplication success, and its middle acceptance, and its end righteousness. Indeed, You (azj) are the Knower of the unseen.’ Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: “This is from the hidden teachings which the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, taught me, and He (saws) commanded me to teach it to al-Hasan (a.s) and al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 115

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from al-Munakhkhal ibn Jamil from Jabir:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you turn away from an obligatory prayer, do not turn away except with the act of turning away accompanied by the cursing of the Banu Umayyah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْمُنَخَّلِ بْنِ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا اِنْحَرَفْتَ عَنْ صَلاَةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ فَلاَ تَنْحَرِفْ إِلاَّ بِانْصِرَافِ لَعْنِ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from al-Munakhkhal ibn Jamil from Jabir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you turn away from an obligatory prayer, do not turn away except with the act of turning away accompanied by the cursing of the Banu Umayyah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 116

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abu ‘Asim Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) and said: “May I be your ransom, your Shi‘a say that faith is ‘settled’ and ‘entrusted.’ Teach me something, that if I say it, I will have completed (perfected) faith.” Imam (a.s) said: “Say after every obligatory prayer: ‘I am pleased with Allah (swt) as Lord (azj), with Muhammad (saws) as Prophet, with Islam as religion, with the Qur’an as Book, with the Ka‘bah as qiblah, and with Ali (a.s) as guardian and Imam, and with al-Hasan (a.s) and al-Husayn (a.s) and the Imams (a.s), may Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon them. O Allah (swt), I am pleased with them as Imams (a.s), so be pleased with me for their sake. Indeed, You (swt) have power over all things.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلنَّهَاوَنْدِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَاصِمٍ يُوسُفَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلدَّيْلَمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ شِيعَتَكَ تَقُولُ إِنَّ اَلْإِيمَانَ مُسْتَقَرُّ« وَ مُسْتَوْدَعٌ» فَعَلِّمْنِي شَيْئاً إِذَا أَنَا قُلْتُهُ اِسْتَكْمَلْتُ اَلْإِيمَانَ قَالَ« قُلْ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبّاً وَ بِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيّاً وَ بِالْإِسْلاَمِ دِيناً وَ بِالْقُرْآنِ كِتَاباً وَ بِالْكَعْبَةِ قِبْلَةً وَ بِعَلِيٍّ وَلِيّاً وَ إِمَاماً وَ بِالْحَسَنِ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ وَ اَلْأَئِمَّةِ صَلَوَاتُُ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي رَضِيتُ بِهِمْ أَئِمَّةً فَارْضَنِي لَهُمْ« إِنَّكَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abu ‘Asim Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) and said: “May I be your ransom, your Shi‘a say that faith is ‘settled’ and ‘entrusted.’ Teach me something, that if I say it, I will have completed (perfected) faith.” Imam (a.s) said: “Say after every obligatory prayer: ‘I am pleased with Allah (swt) as Lord (azj), with Muhammad (saws) as Prophet, with Islam as religion, with the Qur’an as Book, with the Ka‘bah as qiblah, and with Ali (a.s) as guardian and Imam, and with al-Hasan (a.s) and al-Husayn (a.s) and the Imams (a.s), may Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon them. O Allah (swt), I am pleased with them as Imams (a.s), so be pleased with me for their sake. Indeed, You (swt) have power over all things.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 116

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr). Imam (a.s) said: “What is the prostration of gratitude?” So I said to Him (a.s): “Our companions perform one prostration after the obligatory prayer and say that it is the prostration of gratitude.” Imam (a.s) said: “Gratitude is only when Allah (swt), the Exalted, bestows a blessing upon His (a.s) servant, that he says: ‘Glory be to the One Who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of mastering it. And indeed, to our Lord (azj) we shall surely return.’ And all praise belongs to Allah (swt), Lord of the worlds.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ سَجْدَةِ اَلشُّكْرِ فَقَالَ« أَيُّ شَيْءٍ سَجْدَةُ اَلشُّكْرِ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا يَسْجُدُونَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ سَجْدَةً وَاحِدَةً وَ يَقُولُونَ هِيَ سَجْدَةُ اَلشُّكْرِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّمَا اَلشُّكْرُ إِذَا أَنْعَمَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَى عَبْدِهِ اَلنِّعْمَةَ أَنْ يَقُولَ« سُبْحٰانَ اَلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنٰا هٰذٰا وَ مٰا كُنّٰا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ` وَ إِنّٰا إِلىٰ رَبِّنٰا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ»« وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr). Imam (a.s) said: “What is the prostration of gratitude?” So I said to Him (a.s): “Our companions perform one prostration after the obligatory prayer and say that it is the prostration of gratitude.” Imam (a.s) said: “Gratitude is only when Allah (swt), the Exalted, bestows a blessing upon His (a.s) servant, that he says: ‘Glory be to the One Who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of mastering it. And indeed, to our Lord (azj) we shall surely return.’ And all praise belongs to Allah (swt), Lord of the worlds.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 116

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “(prophet) Musa ibn ‘Imran (a.s), when he prayed, would not turn away (from the prayer) until he had placed his right cheek on the ground and his left cheek on the ground.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ مُوسَى بْنُ عِمْرَانَ إِذَا صَلَّى لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ حَتَّى يُلْصِقَ خَدَّهُ اَلْأَيْمَنَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ خَدَّهُ اَلْأَيْسَرَ بِالْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “(prophet) Musa ibn ‘Imran (a.s), when he prayed, would not turn away (from the prayer) until he had placed his right cheek on the ground and his left cheek on the ground.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 117

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hariz from Murazim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The prostration of gratitude is obligatory upon every Muslim. With it, you complete your prayer, please your Lord (azj), and the angels are amazed at you. Indeed, when the servant prays and then performs the prostration of gratitude, the Lord (azj), Exalted is He (azj), lifts the veil between the servant and the angels and says: ‘O My (azj) angels, look at My (azj) servant, he has fulfilled My (azj) closeness, completed My (azj) covenant, and then prostrated to Me (azj) in gratitude for what I have bestowed upon him. O My (azj) angels, what does he deserve?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), Your mercy.’ Then the Lord (azj), Exalted is He (azj), says: ‘And what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), Your Paradise.’ Then the Lord (azj) says: ‘And what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), sufficiency in his needs.’ Then the Lord (azj) says: ‘And what else?’ And there remains nothing of good except that the angels mention it. Then Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘O My angels, and what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), we have no knowledge.’ Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘I shall thank him as he has thanked Me (azj), and I shall turn to him with My (azj) bounty and show him My (azj) mercy.’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُرَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «سَجْدَةُ اَلشُّكْرِ وَاجِبَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ تُتِمُّ بِهَا صَلاَتَكَ وَ تُرْضِي بِهَا رَبَّكَ وَ تَعْجَبُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مِنْكَ وَ إِنَّ اَلْعَبْدَ إِذَا صَلَّى ثُمَّ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلشُّكْرِ فَتَحَ اَلرَّبُّ تَعَالَى اَلْحِجَابَ بَيْنَ اَلْعَبْدِ وَ بَيْنَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ فَيَقُولُ« يَا مَلاَئِكَتِي اُنْظُرُوا إِلَى عَبْدِي أَدَّى قُرْبَتِي وَ أَتَمَّ عَهْدِي ثُمَّ سَجَدَ لِي شُكْراً عَلَى مَا أَنْعَمْتُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ مَلاَئِكَتِي مَاذَا لَهُ»» قَالَ« فَتَقُولُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يَا رَبَّنَا رَحْمَتُكَ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ اَلرَّبُّ تَعَالَى« ثُمَّ مَاذَا لَهُ»» قَالَ« فَتَقُولُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يَا رَبَّنَا جَنَّتُكَ فَيَقُولُ اَلرَّبُّ تَعَالَى« ثُمَّ مَاذَا» فَتَقُولُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يَا رَبَّنَا كِفَايَةُ مُهِمِّهِ فَيَقُولُ اَلرَّبُّ« ثُمَّ مَاذَا» فَلاَ يَبْقَى شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلْخَيْرِ إِلاَّ قَالَتْهُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ فَيَقُولُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى« يَا مَلاَئِكَتِي ثُمَّ مَاذَا» فَتَقُولُ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يَا رَبَّنَا لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَا فَيَقُولُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى« لَأَشْكُرَنَّهُ كَمَا شَكَرَنِي وَ أُقْبِلُ إِلَيْهِ بِفَضْلِي وَ أُرِيهِ رَحْمَتِي»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hariz from Murazim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The prostration of gratitude is obligatory upon every Muslim. With it, you complete your prayer, please your Lord (azj), and the angels are amazed at you. Indeed, when the servant prays and then performs the prostration of gratitude, the Lord (azj), Exalted is He (azj), lifts the veil between the servant and the angels and says: ‘O My (azj) angels, look at My (azj) servant, he has fulfilled My (azj) closeness, completed My (azj) covenant, and then prostrated to Me (azj) in gratitude for what I have bestowed upon him. O My (azj) angels, what does he deserve?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), Your mercy.’ Then the Lord (azj), Exalted is He (azj), says: ‘And what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), Your Paradise.’ Then the Lord (azj) says: ‘And what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), sufficiency in his needs.’ Then the Lord (azj) says: ‘And what else?’ And there remains nothing of good except that the angels mention it. Then Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘O My angels, and what else?’ The angels say: ‘Our Lord (azj), we have no knowledge.’ Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: ‘I shall thank him as he has thanked Me (azj), and I shall turn to him with My (azj) bounty and show him My (azj) mercy.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 117

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, about what I should say in the prostration of gratitude, for our companions have differed concerning it. Imam (a.s) said: “Say while you are in prostration: ‘O Allah (swt), I call You (azj) to witness, and I call Your (azj) angels, Your (azj) prophets, Your (azj) messengers, and all of Your (azj) creation to witness, that indeed You are Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), and Islam is my religion, and Muhammad (saws) is my Prophet, and Ali (a.s) and so-and-so (a.s) and so-and-so (a.s) until the last of them are my Imams (a.s). Through them I express loyalty, and from their enemies I disassociate. O Allah (swt), I implore You (azj) by the blood of the wronged one, three times. O Allah (swt), I implore You (azj) by Your (azj) commitment to Yourself (azj) for the sake of Your (azj) allies, that You (azj) will grant them victory over Your (azj) enemy and their enemy. I ask You (azj) to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and upon the entrusted ones among the family of Muhammad (saws). O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for ease after hardship, three times.’ Then place your right cheek on the ground and say: ‘O my refuge when paths fail me and the earth, despite its vastness, becomes narrow for me. O Creator (azj) of my form, have mercy on me, for You (azj) created me out of mercy, and You (azj) are independent of Your (azj) creation. Send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and upon the entrusted ones from the family of Muhammad (saws).’ Then place your left cheek on the ground and say: ‘O Subduer of every tyrant, O Honorer of every one brought low, by Your (azj) might, I have reached my limit, three times.’ Then say: ‘O Compassionate, O Bestower, O Remover of great hardships, three times.’ Then return to prostration and say one hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran (Thanks).’ Then ask Allah (swt) for your need, if Allah (swt) wills.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جُنْدَبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّا أَقُولُ فِي سَجْدَةِ اَلشُّكْرِ فَقَدِ اِخْتَلَفَ أَصْحَابُنَا فِيهِ فَقَالَ« قُلْ وَ أَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُكَ وَ أُشْهِدُ مَلاَئِكَتَكَ وَ أَنْبِيَاءَكَ وَ رُسُلَكَ وَ جَمِيعَ خَلْقِكَ أَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُ رَبِّي وَ اَلْإِسْلاَمُ دِينِي وَ مُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيِّي وَ عَلِيٌّ وَ فُلاَنٌ وَ فُلاَنٌ إِلَى آخِرِهِمْ أَئِمَّتِي بِهِمْ أَتَوَلَّى وَ مِنْ أَعْدَائِهِمْ أَتَبَرَّأُ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَنْشُدُكَ دَمَ اَلْمَظْلُومِ ثَلاَثاً اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَنْشُدُكَ بِإِيوَائِكَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ لِأَوْلِيَائِكَ لَتُظْفِرَنَّهُمْ بِعَدُوِّكَ وَعَدُوِّهِمْ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى اَلْمُسْتَحْفَظِينَ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ اَلْيُسْرَ بَعْدَ اَلْعُسْرِ ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ ضَعْ خَدَّكَ اَلْأَيْمَنَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ تَقُولُ يَا كَهْفِي حِينَ تُعْيِينِي اَلْمَذَاهِبُ وَ تَضِيقُ عَلَيَّ« اَلْأَرْضُ بِمٰا رَحُبَتْ» وَ يَا بَارِئَ خَلْقِي رَحْمَةً بِي وَ كَانَ عَنْ خَلْقِي غَنِيّاً صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى اَلْمُسْتَحْفَظِينَ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ ثُمَّ تَضَعُ خَدَّكَ اَلْأَيْسَرَ وَ تَقُولُ يَا مُذِلَّ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ وَ يَا مُعِزَّ كُلِّ ذَلِيلٍ قَدْ وَ عِزَّتِكَ بَلَغَ بِي مَجْهُودِي ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ تَقُولُ يَا حَنَّانُ يَا مَنَّانُ يَا كَاشِفَ اَلْكُرَبِ اَلْعِظَامِ ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ تَعُودُ لِلسُّجُودِ فَتَقُولُ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ شُكْراً شُكْراً ثُمَّ تَسْأَلُ اَللَّهَ حَاجَتَكَ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, about what I should say in the prostration of gratitude, for our companions have differed concerning it. Imam (a.s) said: “Say while you are in prostration: ‘O Allah (swt), I call You (azj) to witness, and I call Your (azj) angels, Your (azj) prophets, Your (azj) messengers, and all of Your (azj) creation to witness, that indeed You are Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), and Islam is my religion, and Muhammad (saws) is my Prophet, and Ali (a.s) and so-and-so (a.s) and so-and-so (a.s) until the last of them are my Imams (a.s). Through them I express loyalty, and from their enemies I disassociate. O Allah (swt), I implore You (azj) by the blood of the wronged one, three times. O Allah (swt), I implore You (azj) by Your (azj) commitment to Yourself (azj) for the sake of Your (azj) allies, that You (azj) will grant them victory over Your (azj) enemy and their enemy. I ask You (azj) to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and upon the entrusted ones among the family of Muhammad (saws). O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for ease after hardship, three times.’ Then place your right cheek on the ground and say: ‘O my refuge when paths fail me and the earth, despite its vastness, becomes narrow for me. O Creator (azj) of my form, have mercy on me, for You (azj) created me out of mercy, and You (azj) are independent of Your (azj) creation. Send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and upon the entrusted ones from the family of Muhammad (saws).’ Then place your left cheek on the ground and say: ‘O Subduer of every tyrant, O Honorer of every one brought low, by Your (azj) might, I have reached my limit, three times.’ Then say: ‘O Compassionate, O Bestower, O Remover of great hardships, three times.’ Then return to prostration and say one hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran (Thanks).’ Then ask Allah (swt) for your need, if Allah (swt) wills.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 118

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the prostration of gratitude He (a.s) wrote back to me: “One hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran (Thanks, thanks)’, and if you wish: ‘Afwan, ‘afwan (Pardon, pardon).’
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْقَاسَانِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي سَجْدَةِ اَلشُّكْرِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ« مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ شُكْراً شُكْراً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ عَفْواً عَفْواً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the prostration of gratitude He (a.s) wrote back to me: “One hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran (Thanks, thanks)’, and if you wish: ‘Afwan, ‘afwan (Pardon, pardon).’

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, who said:
I went out with Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them, to one of his properties. He (a.s) stood to perform the noon prayer, and when He (a.s) finished, He (a.s) fell in prostration to Allah (swt). I heard him, in a sorrowful voice, with tears choking him, saying: “My Lord (azj), I disobeyed You (azj) with my tongue, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have rendered me mute. I disobeyed You (azj) with my sight, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have blinded me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my hearing, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have made me deaf. I disobeyed You (azj) with my hand, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have crippled me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my foot, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have amputated me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my private part, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have made me barren. I disobeyed You (azj) with all of my limbs which You (azj) bestowed upon me, and this is not the proper response to Your (azj) favor upon me.” Then he (narrator) said: “I counted a thousand times as Imam (a.s) said: “‘Al-‘afw, al-‘afw (Forgiveness, forgiveness)’.” Then He (a.s) placed his right cheek on the ground, and I (narrator) heard Him (a.s) say in a sorrowful voice: “I return to You (azj) with my sin. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins but You (azj), O my Master.” (Three times) Then He (a.s) placed his left cheek on the ground, and I (narrator) heard Him (a.s) say: “Have mercy on one who has done wrong, committed sins, submitted himself in humility, and confessed.” (Three times) Then He (a.s) raised his head.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: خَرَجْتُ مَعَ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ ع إِلَى بَعْضِ أَمْوَالِهِ فَقَامَ إِلَى صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ خَرَّ لِلَّهِ سَاجِداً فَسَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ بِصَوْتٍ حَزِينٍ وَ تَغَرْغَرُ دُمُوعُهُ« رَبِّ عَصَيْتُكَ بِلِسَانِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَأَخْرَ سْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِبَصَرِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَأَ كْمَهْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِسَمْعِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَأَصْمَمْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِيَدِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَكَنَّعْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِرِجْلِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَجَذَمْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِفَرْجِي وَ لَوْ شِئْتَ وَ عِزَّتِكَ لَعَقَمْتَنِي وَ عَصَيْتُكَ بِجَمِيعِ جَوَارِحِي اَلَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ بِهَا عَلَيَّ وَ لَيْسَ هَذَا جَزَاءَكَ مِنِّي» ثُمَّ قَالَ أَحْصَيْتُ لَهُ أَلْفَ مَرَّةٍ وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ« اَلْعَفْوَ اَلْعَفْوَ» قَالَ ثُمَّ أَلْصَقَ خَدَّهُ اَلْأَيْمَنَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ بِصَوْتٍ حَزِينٍ« بُؤْتُ إِلَيْكَ بِذَنْبِي عَمِلْتُ سُوءاً وَ« ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي» فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ اَلذُّنُوبَ غَيْرُكَ يَا مَوْلاَيَ» ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ أَلْصَقَ خَدَّهُ اَلْأَيْسَرَ بِالْأَرْضِ فَسَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ« اِرْحَمْ مَنْ أَسَاءَ وَ اِقْتَرَفَ وَ اِسْتَكَانَ وَ اِعْتَرَفَ» ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I went out with Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them, to one of his properties. He (a.s) stood to perform the noon prayer, and when He (a.s) finished, He (a.s) fell in prostration to Allah (swt). I heard him, in a sorrowful voice, with tears choking him, saying: “My Lord (azj), I disobeyed You (azj) with my tongue, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have rendered me mute. I disobeyed You (azj) with my sight, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have blinded me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my hearing, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have made me deaf. I disobeyed You (azj) with my hand, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have crippled me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my foot, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have amputated me. I disobeyed You (azj) with my private part, and if You (azj) had willed, by Your (azj) might, You (azj) would have made me barren. I disobeyed You (azj) with all of my limbs which You (azj) bestowed upon me, and this is not the proper response to Your (azj) favor upon me.” Then he (narrator) said: “I counted a thousand times as Imam (a.s) said: “‘Al-‘afw, al-‘afw (Forgiveness, forgiveness)’.” Then He (a.s) placed his right cheek on the ground, and I (narrator) heard Him (a.s) say in a sorrowful voice: “I return to You (azj) with my sin. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins but You (azj), O my Master.” (Three times) Then He (a.s) placed his left cheek on the ground, and I (narrator) heard Him (a.s) say: “Have mercy on one who has done wrong, committed sins, submitted himself in humility, and confessed.” (Three times) Then He (a.s) raised his head.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 119

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ahmad ibn Muhammad raised it (in narration) to Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: “A supplication that is to be recited after every prayer you perform, and if you are afflicted with an illness, pain, or ailment, then when you complete your prayer, wipe your hand over the place of your prostration on the ground, and supplicate with this supplication. Then pass your hand over the place of your pain seven times, saying: ‘O He (azj) who pressed the earth upon the water, and sealed the air with the sky, and chose for Himself (azj) the most beautiful of names, send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and do for me such-and-such, and grant me such-and-such, and heal me from such-and-such.’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« دُعَاءً يُدْعَى بِهِ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ تُصَلِّيهَا فَإِذَا كَانَ بِكَ دَاءٌ مِنْ سَقَمٍ وَ وَجَعٍ فَإِذَا قَضَيْتَ صَلاَتَكَ فَامْسَحْ بِيَدِكَ عَلَى مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ وَ اُدْعُ بِهَذَا اَلدُّعَاءِ وَ أَمِرَّ يَدَكَ عَلَى مَوْضِعِ وَجَعِكَ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ تَقُولُ يَا مَنْ كَبَسَ اَلْأَرْضَ عَلَى اَلْمَاءِ وَ سَدَّ اَلْهَوَاءَ بِالسَّمَاءِ وَ اِخْتَارَ لِنَفْسِهِ أَحْسَنَ اَلْأَسْمَاءِ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اِفْعَلْ بِي كَذَا وَ كَذَا وَ اُرْزُقْنِي كَذَا وَ كَذَا وَعَافِنِي مِنْ كَذَا وَ كَذَا».
thaqalaynMatn: Ahmad ibn Muhammad raised it (in narration) to Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: “A supplication that is to be recited after every prayer you perform, and if you are afflicted with an illness, pain, or ailment, then when you complete your prayer, wipe your hand over the place of your prostration on the ground, and supplicate with this supplication. Then pass your hand over the place of your pain seven times, saying: ‘O He (azj) who pressed the earth upon the water, and sealed the air with the sky, and chose for Himself (azj) the most beautiful of names, send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and do for me such-and-such, and grant me such-and-such, and heal me from such-and-such.’”
