chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from a man: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are afflicted with distress, then wipe your hand over the place of your prostration, then pass your hand over your face” - meaning from the side of your left cheek, over your forehead, to the side of your right cheek. This is how Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid described it to us. Then (Imam (a.s) instructed) say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the One besides whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen… the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah (swt), remove from me distress and sorrow.’” (three times)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَصَابَكَ هَمٌّ فَامْسَحْ يَدَكَ عَلَى مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ ثُمَّ أَمِرَّ بِيَدِكَ عَلَى وَجْهِكَ» يَعْنِي مِنْ جَانِبِ خَدِّكَ اَلْأَيْسَرِ وَ عَلَى جَبْهَتِكَ إِلَى جَانِبِ خَدِّكَ اَلْأَيْمَنِ كَذَلِكَ وَصَفَهُ لَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ ثُمَّ قُلْ« بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ اَلَّذِي« لاٰ إِلٰهَ إِلاّٰ هُوَ عٰالِمُ اَلْغَيْبِ وَ اَلشَّهٰادَةِ»..« اَلرَّحْمٰنُ اَلرَّحِيمُ» اَللَّهُمَّ اِذْهَبْ عَنِّي بِالْهُمُومِ وَ اَلْحَزَنِ ثَلاَثاً»
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from a man: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are afflicted with distress, then wipe your hand over the place of your prostration, then pass your hand over your face” - meaning from the side of your left cheek, over your forehead, to the side of your right cheek. This is how Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid described it to us. Then (Imam (a.s) instructed) say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the One besides whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen… the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah (swt), remove from me distress and sorrow.’” (three times)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 120

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “When you remember the blessing of Allah (swt) upon you and you are in a place where no one sees you, then place your cheek on the ground. But if you are among a group of people, then place your hand on the lower part of your abdomen, bend your back slightly, and let it be an act of humility before Allah (swt), for that is more beloved. And let it appear as though it is a cramp you are feeling in your lower abdomen.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ اَلنَّهَاوَنْدِيِّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا ذَكَرْتَ نِعْمَةَ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَ كُنْتَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ لاَ يَرَاكَ أَحَدٌ فَأَلْصِقْ خَدَّكَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ إِذَا كُنْتَ فِي مَلَإٍ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ فَضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى أَسْفَلِ بَطْنِكَ وَ اِحْنِ ظَهْرَكَ وَ لْيَكُنْ تَوَاضُعاً لِلَّهِ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَحَبُّ وَ تُرِي أَنَّ ذَلِكَ غَمْزٌ وَجَدْتَهُ فِي أَسْفَلِ بَطْنِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “When you remember the blessing of Allah (swt) upon you and you are in a place where no one sees you, then place your cheek on the ground. But if you are among a group of people, then place your hand on the lower part of your abdomen, bend your back slightly, and let it be an act of humility before Allah (swt), for that is more beloved. And let it appear as though it is a cramp you are feeling in your lower abdomen.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 121

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja‘far from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-‘Ala’ al-Khaffaf:
(Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever performs the Maghrib prayer and then remains in ta‘qib without speaking until he performs two rak‘ahs, they will be recorded for him in ‘Illiyyin (those of elevated stations). And if he performs four (rak‘ahs), it will be recorded for him as an accepted Hajj.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ اَلْخَفَّافِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ عَقَّبَ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ كُتِبَتَا لَهُ فِي عِلِّيِّينَ فَإِنْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعاً كُتِبَتْ لَهُ حَجَّةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja‘far from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-‘Ala’ al-Khaffaf:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever performs the Maghrib prayer and then remains in ta‘qib without speaking until he performs two rak‘ahs, they will be recorded for him in ‘Illiyyin (those of elevated stations). And if he performs four (rak‘ahs), it will be recorded for him as an accepted Hajj.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 121

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not leave four rak‘ahs after Maghrib, whether you are traveling or at home, even if the cavalry is pursuing you.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تَدَعْ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ حَضَرٍ وَ إِنْ طَلَبَتْكَ اَلْخَيْلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Do not leave four rak‘ahs after Maghrib, whether you are traveling or at home, even if the cavalry is pursuing you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 121

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, mentioned and said:
(Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked: “Why is Maghrib three rak‘ahs, and why are there four rak‘ahs after it which are never shortened, whether at home or while traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, every prayer as two rak‘ahs. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, added two rak‘ahs to each prayer while in residence, and they were shortened during travel, except for Maghrib and the morning prayer. When He (saws), peace be upon him and his family, prayed Maghrib, the news of the birth of (Sayyidah) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, reached Him (saws). Thus, He (saws) added one rak‘ah to it out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, was born, He (saws) added two rak‘ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, was born, He (saws) added two more rak‘ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. So He (saws) said: ‘To the male belongs a share equal to that of two females’, and He (saws) left it in that state, both during travel and at home.”
arabicText: ذَكَرَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ بَابَوَيْهِ رَحِمَهُ اَللَّهُ فَقَالَ: سُئِلَ اَلصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لِمَ صَارَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ ثَلاَثَ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ أَرْبَعاً بَعْدَهَا لَيْسَ فِيهَا تَقْصِيرٌ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لاَ سَفَرٍ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَنْزَلَ عَلَى نَبِيِّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ كُلَّ صَلاَةٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ وَقَصَّرَ فِيهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ اَلْغَدَاةَ فَلَمَّا صَلَّى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ بَلَغَهُ مَوْلِدُ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً شُكْراً لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلَمَّا أَنْ وُلِدَ اَلْحَسَنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ شُكْراً لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلَمَّا أَنْ وُلِدَ اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ شُكْراً لِلَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ فَقَالَ« لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ اَلْأُنْثَيَيْنِ» فَتَرَكَهَا عَلَى حَالِهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ اَلْحَضَرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, mentioned and said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked: “Why is Maghrib three rak‘ahs, and why are there four rak‘ahs after it which are never shortened, whether at home or while traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, every prayer as two rak‘ahs. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, added two rak‘ahs to each prayer while in residence, and they were shortened during travel, except for Maghrib and the morning prayer. When He (saws), peace be upon him and his family, prayed Maghrib, the news of the birth of (Sayyidah) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, reached Him (saws). Thus, He (saws) added one rak‘ah to it out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, was born, He (saws) added two rak‘ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, was born, He (saws) added two more rak‘ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. So He (saws) said: ‘To the male belongs a share equal to that of two females’, and He (saws) left it in that state, both during travel and at home.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 121

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salamah from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hajjaj al-Khashshab from Abu al-Fawaris, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) forbade me from speaking between the four rak‘ahs that are after Maghrib.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حَجَّاجٍ اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْفَوَارِسِ قَالَ: نَهَانِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ بَيْنَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ اَلَّتِي بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salamah from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hajjaj al-Khashshab from Abu al-Fawaris, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) forbade me from speaking between the four rak‘ahs that are after Maghrib.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 122

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated from al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Hafs al-Jawhari, who said:
Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in the Maghrib prayer, then He (a.s) performed the prostration of gratitude after the seventh (rak‘ah). So I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): “Your forefathers (a.s) used to perform the prostration after the third (rak‘ah).” Imam (a.s) said: “None of my forefathers (a.s) performed the prostration except after the seventh.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ عَنِ اَلصَّفَّارِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَفْصٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلاَةَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَسَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلشُّكْرِ بَعْدَ اَلسَّابِعَةِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَانَ آبَاؤُكَ يَسْجُدُونَ بَعْدَ اَلثَّلاَثَةِ فَقَالَ« مَا كَانَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ آبَائِي يَسْجُدُ إِلاَّ بَعْدَ اَلسَّبْعَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated from al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Hafs al-Jawhari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in the Maghrib prayer, then He (a.s) performed the prostration of gratitude after the seventh (rak‘ah). So I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): “Your forefathers (a.s) used to perform the prostration after the third (rak‘ah).” Imam (a.s) said: “None of my forefathers (a.s) performed the prostration except after the seventh.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 122

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It was narrated by Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Babawayh, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him. He (Ibn Babawayn) said Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Jahm ibn Abi Jahm, who said:
I saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, and He (a.s) had prostrated after the three rak‘ahs of Maghrib. So I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I saw you prostrating after the three.” Imam (a.s) said: “And you saw me?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then do not abandon it, for supplication in it is answered.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَابَوَيْهِ رَحِمَهُ اَللَّهُ قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ جَهْمِ بْنِ أَبِي جَهْمٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ بَعْدَ اَلثَّلاَثِ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رَأَيْتُكَ سَجَدْتَ بَعْدَ اَلثَّلاَثِ فَقَالَ« وَ رَأَيْتَنِي» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« فَلاَ تَدَعْهَا فَإِنَّ اَلدُّعَاءَ فِيهَا مُسْتَجَابٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: It was narrated by Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Babawayh, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him. He (Ibn Babawayn) said Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Jahm ibn Abi Jahm, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, and He (a.s) had prostrated after the three rak‘ahs of Maghrib. So I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I saw you prostrating after the three.” Imam (a.s) said: “And you saw me?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then do not abandon it, for supplication in it is answered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 122

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Abu al-‘Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Supplication is answered in four times: during Witr, after Fajr, after Dhuhr, and after Maghrib.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يُسْتَجَابُ اَلدُّعَاءُ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاطِنَ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Abu al-‘Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Supplication is answered in four times: during Witr, after Fajr, after Dhuhr, and after Maghrib.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 123

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Abu Isma‘il al-Sarraj, from Ali ibn Shajarah, from Muhammad ibn Marwan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “You wipe your right hand over your forehead and your face after Maghrib and after the (other) prayers, and say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the One besides whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen… the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah (swt), I seek refuge in You (azj) from anxiety and grief, from sickness and poverty, from humiliation and disgrace, and from indecencies, both apparent and hidden.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلسَّرَّاجِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ شَجَرَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« تَمْسَحُ يَدَكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى جَبْهَتِكَ وَ وَجْهِكَ فِي دُبُرِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ وَ تَقُولُ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ« اَلَّذِي لاٰ إِلٰهَ إِلاّٰ هُوَ عٰالِمُ اَلْغَيْبِ وَ اَلشَّهٰادَةِ»..« اَلرَّحْمٰنُ اَلرَّحِيمُ» اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ اَلْهَمِّ وَ اَلْحَزَنِ وَ اَلسُّقْمِ وَ اَلْعُدْمِ وَ اَلصَّغَارِ وَ اَلذُّلِّ وَ اَلْفَوَاحِشِ« مٰا ظَهَرَ مِنْهٰا وَ مٰا بَطَنَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Abu Isma‘il al-Sarraj, from Ali ibn Shajarah, from Muhammad ibn Marwan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “You wipe your right hand over your forehead and your face after Maghrib and after the (other) prayers, and say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the One besides whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen… the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah (swt), I seek refuge in You (azj) from anxiety and grief, from sickness and poverty, from humiliation and disgrace, and from indecencies, both apparent and hidden.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 123

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever says after performing the Maghrib prayer, three times: ‘Alhamdu lillah alladhi yaf‘alu ma yasha’, wa la yaf‘alu ma yasha’u ghayruhu’ (Praise be to Allah (swt), the One who does whatever He wills, and no one else does what He wills) - will be granted abundant good.”
arabicText: وَ قَالَ اَلصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ قَالَ إِذَا صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَ لاَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ غَيْرُ هُ أُعْطِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً»
thaqalaynMatn: And (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever says after performing the Maghrib prayer, three times: ‘Alhamdu lillah alladhi yaf‘alu ma yasha’, wa la yaf‘alu ma yasha’u ghayruhu’ (Praise be to Allah (swt), the One who does whatever He wills, and no one else does what He wills) - will be granted abundant good.”

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Say in the final prostration of the nawafil of Maghrib on the night of Friday, seven times while you are in prostration: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by Your (azj) noble Face and Your (azj) great Name to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and to forgive me my great sin.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« قُلْ فِي آخِرِ اَلسَّجْدَةِ مِنَ اَلنَّوَافِلِ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ أَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِوَجْهِكَ اَلْكَرِيمِ وَ اِسْمِكَ اَلْعَظِيمِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تَغْفِرَ لِي ذَنْبِيَ اَلْعَظِيمَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Say in the final prostration of the nawafil of Maghrib on the night of Friday, seven times while you are in prostration: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by Your (azj) noble Face and Your (azj) great Name to send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and to forgive me my great sin.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 123

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It is narrated from (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Say after the two night prayers (‘al-Ishaayn’): ‘O Allah (swt), in Your hand are the measures of night and day, the measures of this world and the Hereafter, the measures of death and life, the measures of the sun and the moon, the measures of victory and defeat, and the measures of wealth and poverty. O Allah (swt), repel from me the evil of the wicked ones from among jinn and mankind, and make my return one of everlasting goodness and never-ending bliss.’”
arabicText: رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« تَقُولُ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءَيْنِ اَللَّهُمَّ بِيَدِكَ مَقَادِيرُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلْمَوْتِ وَ اَلْحَيَاةِ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ اَلْقَمَرِ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلنَّصْرِ وَ اَلْخِذْلاَنِ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلْغِنَى وَ اَلْفَقْرِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِدْرَأْ عَنِّي شَرَّ فَسَقَةِ اَلْجِنِّ وَ اَلْإِنْسِ وَ اِجْعَلْ مُنْقَلَبِي إِلَى خَيْرٍ دَائِمٍ وَ نَعِيمٍ لاَ يَزُولُ»
thaqalaynSanad: It is narrated from (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Say after the two night prayers (‘al-Ishaayn’): ‘O Allah (swt), in Your hand are the measures of night and day, the measures of this world and the Hereafter, the measures of death and life, the measures of the sun and the moon, the measures of victory and defeat, and the measures of wealth and poverty. O Allah (swt), repel from me the evil of the wicked ones from among jinn and mankind, and make my return one of everlasting goodness and never-ending bliss.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 123

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) used to recite in the two rak‘ahs after ‘al-‘Atamah’ (the Isha prayer): ‘Surat al-Waqi‘ah’ and ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas)’.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ اَلْوَاقِعَةَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) used to recite in the two rak‘ahs after ‘al-‘Atamah’ (the Isha prayer): ‘Surat al-Waqi‘ah’ and ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas)’.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 124

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
It is narrated from (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever performs purification (wudu) and then goes to his bed, his bed will be like his place of prayer. And if he remembers that he is not in a state of wudu and performs ‘tayammum’ from his blanket, whatever it may be, he will remain in a state of prayer as long as he remembers Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.”
arabicText: رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَنْ تَطَهَّرَ ثُمَّ أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ بَاتَ وَ فِرَاشُهُ كَمَسْجِدِهِ وَ إِنْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ فَتَيَمَّمَ مِنْ دِثَارِهِ كَائِناً مَا كَانَ لَمْ يَزَلْ فِي صَلاَةٍ مَا ذَكَرَ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: It is narrated from (Imam) Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever performs purification (wudu) and then goes to his bed, his bed will be like his place of prayer. And if he remembers that he is not in a state of wudu and performs ‘tayammum’ from his blanket, whatever it may be, he will remain in a state of prayer as long as he remembers Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 124

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said to me: “When a man lies down on his right side, let him say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), I submit my soul to You (azj), and I turn my face to You (azj), and I entrust my affairs to You (azj), and I rely upon You (azj). I seek refuge in You (azj) out of fear of You (azj) and longing toward You (azj). There is no refuge and no escape from You (azj) except to You (azj). I believe in Your (azj) Book which You (azj) have revealed, and in Your (azj) Messenger (saws) whom You have sent.’ Then let him recite the Tasbih of (Sayyidah) Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a), peace be upon her. And whoever experiences fear or disturbance at the time of sleep, let him recite, when he goes to his bed, the two Surahs of seeking refuge (‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’) and ‘Ayat al-Kursi’.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا تَوَسَّدَ اَلرَّجُلُ يَمِينَهُ فَلْيَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْلَمْتُ نَفْسِي إِلَيْكَ وَوَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَيْكَ رَهْبَةً مِنْكَ وَ رَغْبَةً إِلَيْكَ لاَ مَلْجَأَ وَ لاَ مَنْجَى مِنْكَ إِلاَّ إِلَيْكَ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ اَلَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ وَ بِرَسُولِكَ اَلَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ اَلزَّهْرَاءِ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ مَنْ أَصَابَهُ فَزَعٌ عِنْدَ مَنَامِهِ فَلْيَقْرَأْ إِذَا أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ وَ آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said to me: “When a man lies down on his right side, let him say: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), I submit my soul to You (azj), and I turn my face to You (azj), and I entrust my affairs to You (azj), and I rely upon You (azj). I seek refuge in You (azj) out of fear of You (azj) and longing toward You (azj). There is no refuge and no escape from You (azj) except to You (azj). I believe in Your (azj) Book which You (azj) have revealed, and in Your (azj) Messenger (saws) whom You have sent.’ Then let him recite the Tasbih of (Sayyidah) Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a), peace be upon her. And whoever experiences fear or disturbance at the time of sleep, let him recite, when he goes to his bed, the two Surahs of seeking refuge (‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’) and ‘Ayat al-Kursi’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 124

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
(Imams (a.s) said) “A man should not neglect to say at the time of sleep: ‘I seek protection for myself, my children, my family, and my wealth with the perfect words of Allah (swt) from every devil and harmful creature, and from every envious evil eye.’ This is what Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, used to use to seek protection for (Imam) al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَدَعُ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَقُولَ عِنْدَ مَنَامِهِ أُعِيذُ نَفْسِي وَ ذُرِّيَّتِي وَ أَهْلَ بَيْتِي وَ مَالِي بِكَلِمَاتِ اَللَّهِ اَلتَّامَّاتِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَ هَامَّةٍ وَ مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ فَذَلِكَ اَلَّذِي عَوَّذَ بِهِ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْحُسَيْنَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imams (a.s) said) “A man should not neglect to say at the time of sleep: ‘I seek protection for myself, my children, my family, and my wealth with the perfect words of Allah (swt) from every devil and harmful creature, and from every envious evil eye.’ This is what Jibra’il (a.s), peace be upon him, used to use to seek protection for (Imam) al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 124

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “Recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ at the time of sleep, for indeed, it is a declaration of disassociation from shirk. And ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ is the description of the Lord (azj).”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِقْرَأْ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» عِنْدَ مَنَامِكَ فَإِنَّهَا بَرَاءَةٌ مِنَ اَلشِّرْكِ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ» نِسْبَةُ اَلرَّبِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “Recite ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ at the time of sleep, for indeed, it is a declaration of disassociation from shirk. And ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ is the description of the Lord (azj).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 125

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Him, peace be upon him: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says, when he lies down to sleep, three times: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who is exalted and thus overpowered, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who is hidden and thus aware, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who possesses and thus decreed, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who gives life to the dead and causes the living to die, and He has power over all things’, (this person) will emerge from his sins like the day his mother gave birth to him.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى بَكْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَنْ قَالَ حِينَ يَأْخُذُ مَضْجَعَهُ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي عَلاَ فَقَهَرَ وَاَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي بَطَنَ فَخَبَرَ وَاَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي مَلَكَ فَقَدَرَ وَاَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي« يُحْيِ اَلْمَوْتىٰ» وَ يُمِيتُ اَلْأَحْيَاءَ «وَ هُوَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» خَرَجَ مِنَ اَلذُّنُوبِ كَيَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Him, peace be upon him: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says, when he lies down to sleep, three times: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who is exalted and thus overpowered, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who is hidden and thus aware, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who possesses and thus decreed, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), the One who gives life to the dead and causes the living to die, and He has power over all things’, (this person) will emerge from his sins like the day his mother gave birth to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 125

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d al-Iskaf narrated from Abu Ja‘far (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says these words, I guarantee that no scorpion nor harmful creature will harm him until morning: ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah (swt), which no righteous or wicked person can surpass, from the evil of what He (azj) has created, and from the evil of what He (azj) has formed, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock He (azj) holds. Indeed, my Lord (azj) is on a straight path.’”
arabicText: وَرَوَى سَعْدٌ اَلْإِسْكَافُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَنْ قَالَ هَذِهِ اَلْكَلِمَاتِ فَأَنَا ضَامِنٌ أَنْ لاَ يُصِيبَهُ عَقْرَبٌ وَ لاَ هَامَّةٌ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اَللَّهِ اَلتَّامَّاتِ اَلَّتِي لاَ يُجَاوِزُهُنَّ بَرٌّ وَ لاَ فَاجِرٌ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا ذَرَأَ وَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا بَرَأَ وَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ هُوَ« آخِذٌ بِنٰاصِيَتِهٰا إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلىٰ صِرٰاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d al-Iskaf narrated from Abu Ja‘far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says these words, I guarantee that no scorpion nor harmful creature will harm him until morning: ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah (swt), which no righteous or wicked person can surpass, from the evil of what He (azj) has created, and from the evil of what He (azj) has formed, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock He (azj) holds. Indeed, my Lord (azj) is on a straight path.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 125

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Abbas ibn Hilal narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, from his father, peace be upon them both:
Imam (a.s) said: “No one has ever said, when intending to sleep: ‘Indeed, Allah (swt) holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist, and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him (azj). Indeed, He (azj) is Most Forbearing, Most Forgiving’, and then had the house collapse upon him.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْعَبَّاسُ بْنُ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَمْ يَقُلْ أَحَدٌ قَطُّ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَنَامَ «إِنَّ اَللّٰهَ يُمْسِكُ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولاٰ وَ لَئِنْ زٰالَتٰا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمٰا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ إِنَّهُ كٰانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً» فَسَقَطَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْبَيْتُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Abbas ibn Hilal narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, from his father, peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “No one has ever said, when intending to sleep: ‘Indeed, Allah (swt) holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist, and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him (azj). Indeed, He (azj) is Most Forbearing, Most Forgiving’, and then had the house collapse upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 125

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, in the night there is a moment in which no Muslim servant coincides with it while praying and supplicating to Allah (swt) except that He (azj) answers him, in every night.” I asked: “May Allah (swt) set you right, which moment of the night is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “When half the night has passed, until the last third remaining.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ فِي اَللَّيْلِ لَسَاعَةً لاَ يُوَافِقُهَا عَبْدٌ مُسْلِمٌ يُصَلِّي وَ يَدْعُو اَللَّهَ فِيهَا إِلاَّ اِسْتَجَابَ لَهُ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ» قُلْتُ أَصْلَحَكَ اَللَّهُ فَأَيَّةُ سَاعَةٍ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« إِذَا مَضَى نِصْفُ اَللَّيْلِ إِلَى اَلثُّلُثِ اَلْبَاقِي»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, in the night there is a moment in which no Muslim servant coincides with it while praying and supplicating to Allah (swt) except that He (azj) answers him, in every night.” I asked: “May Allah (swt) set you right, which moment of the night is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “When half the night has passed, until the last third remaining.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl, from one of the two (Imams):
Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs after the middle of the night.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ فُضَيْلٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ يُصَلِّي بَعْدَمَا يَنْتَصِفُ اَللَّيْلُ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl, from one of the two (Imams):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to pray thirteen rak‘ahs after the middle of the night.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 125

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, when He (saws) prayed the final night prayer (‘Isha al-akhirah’), would go to his bed and would not perform any prayer until after the middle of the night, neither in the month of Ramadan nor outside of it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ اَلطَّائِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذَا صَلَّى اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ لاَ يُصَلِّي شَيْئاً إِلاَّ بَعْدَ اِنْتِصَافِ اَللَّيْلِ لاَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ لاَ فِي غَيْرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, when He (saws) prayed the final night prayer (‘Isha al-akhirah’), would go to his bed and would not perform any prayer until after the middle of the night, neither in the month of Ramadan nor outside of it.”
