chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdah al-Saburi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, people narrate from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family; ‘Indeed, in the night there is an hour in which no believing servant supplicates with a supplication except that it is answered for him.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “When is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Between the middle of the night and the remaining third.” I asked: “On one of the nights or every night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Every night.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدَةَ اَلسَّابُورِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ اَلنَّاسَ يَرْوُونَ عَنِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ« إِنَّ فِي اَللَّيْلِ لَسَاعَةً لاَ يَدْعُو فِيهَا عَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ بِدَعْوَةٍ إِلاَّ اُسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ» قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ مَتَى هِيَ قَالَ« مَابَيْنَ نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ إِلَى اَلثُّلُثِ اَلْبَاقِي» قُلْتُ لَيْلَةً مِنَ اَللَّيَالِي أَوْ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ« كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdah al-Saburi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May I be your ransom, people narrate from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family; ‘Indeed, in the night there is an hour in which no believing servant supplicates with a supplication except that it is answered for him.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “When is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Between the middle of the night and the remaining third.” I asked: “On one of the nights or every night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Every night.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 126

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, from the man of al-‘Askar, peace be upon him.
Imam (a.s) said: “When the night reaches its midpoint, a whiteness appears in the middle of the sky resembling an iron pillar, by which the world becomes illuminated. It remains for an hour and then disappears. Then darkness returns. When the final third of the night remains, a whiteness appears from the direction of the east, and the world is illuminated by it. It remains for an hour and then disappears. And that is the time of the night prayer. Then darkness returns before the true dawn, then the true dawn rises from the direction of the east.” Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever wishes to pray at the middle of the night and prolong (his prayer), then that is for him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْقَاسَانِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ اَلْعَسْكَرِيِّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ اَللَّيْلُ ظَهَرَ بَيَاضٌ فِي وَسَطِ اَلسَّمَاءِ شِبْهُ عَمُودٍ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ تُضِيءُ لَهُ اَلدُّنْيَا فَيَكُونُ سَاعَةً وَ يَذْهَبُ ثُمَّ تُظْلِمُ فَإِذَا بَقِيَ ثُلُثُ اَللَّيْلِ اَلْأَخِيرُ ظَهَرَ بَيَاضٌ مِنْ قِبَلِ اَلْمَشْرِقِ فَأَضَاءَتْ لَهُ اَلدُّنْيَا فَيَكُونُ سَاعَةً ثُمَّ يَذْهَبُ وَ هُوَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ تُظْلِمُ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ يَطْلُعُ اَلْفَجْرُ اَلصَّادِقُ مِنْ قِبَلِ اَلْمَشْرِقِ» قَالَ« مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ فَيُطَوِّلَ فَذَلِكَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, from the man of al-‘Askar, peace be upon him.
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When the night reaches its midpoint, a whiteness appears in the middle of the sky resembling an iron pillar, by which the world becomes illuminated. It remains for an hour and then disappears. Then darkness returns. When the final third of the night remains, a whiteness appears from the direction of the east, and the world is illuminated by it. It remains for an hour and then disappears. And that is the time of the night prayer. Then darkness returns before the true dawn, then the true dawn rises from the direction of the east.” Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever wishes to pray at the middle of the night and prolong (his prayer), then that is for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 126

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Abdullah ibn Muskan from Layth al-Muradi. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the prayer in the summer during the short nights, (specifically) the night prayer being performed at the beginning of the night. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, excellent is what you observed, and excellent is what you did.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ لَيْثٍ اَلْمُرَادِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلصَّيْفِ فِي اَللَّيَالِي اَلْقِصَارِ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ نِعْمَ مَا رَأَيْتَ وَ نِعْمَ مَا صَنَعْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Abdullah ibn Muskan from Layth al-Muradi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the prayer in the summer during the short nights, (specifically) the night prayer being performed at the beginning of the night. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, excellent is what you observed, and excellent is what you did.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 127

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb: from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
I asked (Imam (a.s)): “One of your followers from among the righteous has complained to me about what he experiences from sleep. He (follower) said, ‘I want to rise for prayer at night, but sleep overcomes me until morning, so I sometimes make up my prayer for a month consecutively, or even two months. I endure its burden.’” Imam (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), it is a source of delight for him.” Yet He (a.s) did not grant him a concession to pray at the beginning of the night, and Imam (a.s) said: “Making it up during the day is better.” I asked: “Among our women are young maidens, who love goodness and its people and are eager for prayer, but sleep overcomes them to the extent that they sometimes make up the prayer and sometimes are too weak to make it up. Yet they are capable of performing it at the beginning of the night.” So He (a.s) granted them a concession: “They may pray at the beginning of the night if they are weak and neglect making it up.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ حَمَّادُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ إِنَّ رَجُلاً مِنْ مَوَالِيكَ مِنْ صُلَحَائِهِمْ شَكَا إِلَيَّ مَا يَلْقَى مِنَ اَلنَّوْمِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ اَلْقِيَامَ لِلصَّلاَةِ بِاللَّيْلِ فَيَغْلِبُنِي اَلنَّوْمُ حَتَّى أُصْبِحَ فَرُبَّمَا قَضَيْتُ صَلاَتِيَ اَلشَّهْرَ اَلْمُتَتَابِعَ وَ اَلشَّهْرَيْنِ أَصْبِرُ عَلَى ثِقْلِهِ قَالَ« قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لَهُ وَ اَللَّهِ وَ لَمْ يُرَخِّصْ لَهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ» وَ قَالَ« اَلْقَضَاءُ بِالنَّهَارِ أَفْضَلُ» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّ مِنْ نِسَائِنَا أَبْكَاراً اَلْجَارِيَةَ تُحِبُّ اَلْخَيْرَ وَ أَهْلَهُ وَ تَحْرِصُ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيَغْلِبُهَا اَلنَّوْمُ حَتَّى رُبَّمَا قَضَتْ وَ رُبَّمَا ضَعُفَتْ مِنْ قَضَائِهِ وَ هِيَ تَقْوَى عَلَيْهِ أَوَّلَ اَللَّيْلِ فَرَخَّصَ لَهُنَّ« فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ أَوَّلَ اَللَّيْلِ إِذَا ضَعُفْنَ وَ ضَيَّعْنَ اَلْقَضَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb: from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam (a.s)): “One of your followers from among the righteous has complained to me about what he experiences from sleep. He (follower) said, ‘I want to rise for prayer at night, but sleep overcomes me until morning, so I sometimes make up my prayer for a month consecutively, or even two months. I endure its burden.’” Imam (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), it is a source of delight for him.” Yet He (a.s) did not grant him a concession to pray at the beginning of the night, and Imam (a.s) said: “Making it up during the day is better.” I asked: “Among our women are young maidens, who love goodness and its people and are eager for prayer, but sleep overcomes them to the extent that they sometimes make up the prayer and sometimes are too weak to make it up. Yet they are capable of performing it at the beginning of the night.” So He (a.s) granted them a concession: “They may pray at the beginning of the night if they are weak and neglect making it up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 127

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not wake up at the end of the night until ten or fifteen nights pass in this state, so he prays at the beginning of the night. Is that more beloved to you, or that he makes it up? Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather, that he makes it up is more beloved to me. I dislike that he should take that as a habit.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَسْتَيْقِظُ مِنْ آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ لِذَلِكَ اَلْعَشْرُ وَ اَلْخَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ فَيُصَلِّي أَوَّلَ اَللَّيْلِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ أَمْ يَقْضِي قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ يَقْضِي أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ إِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ ذَلِكَ خُلُقاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not wake up at the end of the night until ten or fifteen nights pass in this state, so he prays at the beginning of the night. Is that more beloved to you, or that he makes it up? Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather, that he makes it up is more beloved to me. I dislike that he should take that as a habit.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 127

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who raised it (to the Prophet (saws)). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever prays at night, his face will be alluring (attractive) during the day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ اَلرَّازِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ صَلَّى بِاللَّيْلِ حَسُنَ وَجْهُهُ بِالنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who raised it (to the Prophet (saws)). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever prays at night, his face will be alluring (attractive) during the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Hisham ibn Salim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘Indeed, the rising by night is the firmest in tread and most upright in speech’ (Surah Muzzammil 73:6) Imam (a.s) said: “His rising from his bed, desiring none but Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «إِنَّ نٰاشِئَةَ اَللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً وَ أَقْوَمُ قِيلاً» قَالَ« قِيَامُهُ عَنْ فِرَاشِهِ لاَ يُرِيدُ إِلاَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Hisham ibn Salim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘Indeed, the rising by night is the firmest in tread and most upright in speech’ (Surah Muzzammil 73:6) Imam (a.s) said: “His rising from his bed, desiring none but Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The honor of the believer is the night prayer, and the dignity of the believer is his refraining from (speaking about) the reputations of people.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «شَرَفُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِ صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ عِزُّ اَلْمُؤْمِنِ كَفُّهُ عَنْ أَعْرَاضِ اَلنَّاسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The honor of the believer is the night prayer, and the dignity of the believer is his refraining from (speaking about) the reputations of people.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu al-Hasan (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them, except (that they did it) seeking the pleasure of Allah (swt)”’ (Surah Hadid 57:27) Imam (a.s) said: “(It refers to) the night prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ« وَرَهْبٰانِيَّةً اِبْتَدَعُوهٰا مٰا كَتَبْنٰاهٰا عَلَيْهِمْ إِلاَّ اِبْتِغٰاءَ رِضْوٰانِ اَللّٰهِ» قَالَ «صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them, except (that they did it) seeking the pleasure of Allah (swt)”’ (Surah Hadid 57:27) Imam (a.s) said: “(It refers to) the night prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Zuhayr al-Nahdi, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from some of his companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Hold fast to the night prayer, for it is the practice of your Prophet (saws), the way of the righteous before you, and a repellent of illness from your bodies.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي زُهَيْرٍ اَلنَّهْدِيِّ عَنْ آدَمَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« عَلَيْكُمْ بِصَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فَإِنَّهَا سُنَّةُ نَبِيِّكُمْ وَ دَأْبُ اَلصَّالِحِينَ قَبْلَكُمْ وَ مَطْرَدَةُ اَلدَّاءِ عَنْ أَجْسَادِكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Zuhayr al-Nahdi, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from some of his companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Hold fast to the night prayer, for it is the practice of your Prophet (saws), the way of the righteous before you, and a repellent of illness from your bodies.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Zuhayr, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “The night prayer brightens the face, the night prayer sweetens the scent, and the night prayer brings sustenance.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي زُهَيْرٍ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ تُبَيِّضُ اَلْوَجْهَ وَ صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ تُطَيِّبُ اَلرِّيحَ وَ صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ تَجْلِبُ اَلرِّزْقَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Zuhayr, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The night prayer brightens the face, the night prayer sweetens the scent, and the night prayer brings sustenance.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from someone who narrated to him:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, if Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has said: ‘Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world’ (Surah Kahf 18:46), then surely eight rak‘ahs which the servant prays at the end of the night are the adornment of the Hereafter.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَمِّهِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِنْ كَانَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَالَ« اَلْمٰالُ وَ اَلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ اَلْحَيٰاةِ اَلدُّنْيٰا» إِنَّ اَلثَّمَانِيَةَ رَكَعَاتٍ يُصَلِّيهَا اَلْعَبْدُ آخِرَ اَللَّيْلِ زِينَةُ اَلْآخِرَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from someone who narrated to him:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, if Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has said: ‘Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world’ (Surah Kahf 18:46), then surely eight rak‘ahs which the servant prays at the end of the night are the adornment of the Hereafter.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle, from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
A man came to Him (a.s) and complained about poverty and went to extremes in his complaint to the point that he nearly complained of hunger. Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to him: “O this one, do you pray at night?” The man replied: “Yes.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) turned to his companions and said: “He has lied, the one who claims that he prays at night and goes hungry during the day. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, has guaranteed with the night prayer the sustenance of the day.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمِّهِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ جَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ اَلْحَاجَةَ وَ أَفْرَطَ فِي اَلشِّكَايَةِ حَتَّى كَادَ أَنْ يَشْكُوَ اَلْجُوعَ قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَا هَذَا تُصَلِّي بِاللَّيْلِ» قَالَ فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ نَعَمْ قَالَ فَالْتَفَتَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ« كَذَبَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّهُ يُصَلِّي بِاللَّيْلِ وَ يَجُوعُ بِالنَّهَارِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى ضَمِنَ بِصَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ قُوتَ اَلنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle, from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: A man came to Him (a.s) and complained about poverty and went to extremes in his complaint to the point that he nearly complained of hunger. Abu Abdillah (a.s), said to him: “O this one, do you pray at night?” The man replied: “Yes.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) turned to his companions and said: “He has lied, the one who claims that he prays at night and goes hungry during the day. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, has guaranteed with the night prayer the sustenance of the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s) narrated to me from my grandfather (a.s) from his forefathers (a.s), from (Imam) Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him. He (Imam Ali (a.s)) said: ‘Rising for prayer at night is health for the body, the pleasure of the Lord (azj), adherence to the morals of the prophets, and an exposure to His (azj) mercy.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي عَنْ جَدِّي عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« قِيَامُ اَللَّيْلِ مَصَحَّةُ اَلْبَدَنِ وَرِضَا اَلرَّبِّ وَ تَمَسُّكٌ بِأَخْلاَقِ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ وَ تَعَرُّضٌ لِرَحْمَتِهِ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s) narrated to me from my grandfather (a.s) from his forefathers (a.s), from (Imam) Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him. He (Imam Ali (a.s)) said: ‘Rising for prayer at night is health for the body, the pleasure of the Lord (azj), adherence to the morals of the prophets, and an exposure to His (azj) mercy.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi. He said:
I asked him about the night prayer and the witr prayer. He said: “It is obligatory.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« هِيَ وَاجِبَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about the night prayer and the witr prayer. He said: “It is obligatory.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 130

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from ‘Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu‘man, from his father, from some of his companions. He said:
A man came to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said: ‘O Commander of the Faithful, I have been deprived of the night prayer.’ Commander of the Faithful (a.s) said: “You are a man whose sins have shackled you.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي قَدْ حُرِمْتُ اَلصَّلاَةَ بِاللَّيْلِ قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ« أَنْتَ رَجُلٌ قَدْ قَيَّدَتْكَ ذُنُوبُكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from ‘Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu‘man, from his father, from some of his companions. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said: ‘O Commander of the Faithful, I have been deprived of the night prayer.’ Commander of the Faithful (a.s) said: “You are a man whose sins have shackled you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 130

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Musa ibn Ja‘far al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali. He said:
I heard him say: “Indeed, the servant stands for prayer at night, and drowsiness causes him to sway right and left, and his chin has fallen onto his chest. Then Allah (swt), the Exalted, commands the gates of the heavens to open, then says to the angels: ‘Look at My (azj) servant, what he suffers in drawing near to Me (azj) with that which I have not made obligatory upon him, hoping from Me (azj) for one of three things: A sin I (azj) may forgive for him, or a repentance I (azj) may renew for him, or a sustenance I (azj) may increase for him. Bear witness, O My (azj) angels, that I have granted him all three.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْبَغْدَادِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ شَمُّونٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ اَلْعَبْدَ لَيَقُومُ فِي اَللَّيْلِ فَيَمِيلُ بِهِ اَلنُّعَاسُ يَمِيناً وَ شِمَالاً وَ قَدْ وَقَعَ ذَقَنُهُ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ فَيَأْمُرُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَبْوَابَ اَلسَّمَاءِ فَتَنْفَتِحُ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ« اُنْظُرُوا إِلَى عَبْدِي مَا يُصِيبُهُ فِي اَلتَّقَرُّبِ إِلَيَّ بِمَا لَمْ أَفْتَرِضْ عَلَيْهِ رَاجِياً مِنِّي لِثَلاَثِ خِصَالٍ ذَنْباً أَغْفِرُهُ لَهُ أَوْ تَوْبَةً أُجَدِّدُهَا لَهُ أَوْ رِزْقاً أَزِيدُهُ فِيهِ اِشْهَدُوا مَلاَئِكَتِي أَنِّي قَدْ جَمَعْتُهُنَّ لَهُ»».
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Musa ibn Ja‘far al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard him say: “Indeed, the servant stands for prayer at night, and drowsiness causes him to sway right and left, and his chin has fallen onto his chest. Then Allah (swt), the Exalted, commands the gates of the heavens to open, then says to the angels: ‘Look at My (azj) servant, what he suffers in drawing near to Me (azj) with that which I have not made obligatory upon him, hoping from Me (azj) for one of three things: A sin I (azj) may forgive for him, or a repentance I (azj) may renew for him, or a sustenance I (azj) may increase for him. Bear witness, O My (azj) angels, that I have granted him all three.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 130

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi ‘Uthman, and Abu ‘Uthman’s name is Abdulwahid ibn Habib. He said Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali claimed to us, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar al-Duhni:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The night prayer improves the face, removes worry, and clears the eyesight.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ وَ أَبُو عُثْمَانَ اِسْمُهُ عَبْدُ اَلْوَاحِدِ بْنُ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ زَعَمَ لَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ اَلثُّمَالِيِّ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ اَلدُّهْنِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ تُحَسِّنُ اَلْوَجْهَ وَ تُذْهِبُ اَلْهَمَّ وَ تَجْلُو اَلْبَصَرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi ‘Uthman, and Abu ‘Uthman’s name is Abdulwahid ibn Habib. He said Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali claimed to us, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar al-Duhni:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The night prayer improves the face, removes worry, and clears the eyesight.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 130

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “O Sulayman, do not abandon the night prayer, for the one who is truly deprived is the one who is deprived of the night prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلدَّيْلَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا سُلَيْمَانُ لاَ تَدَعْ قِيَامَ اَللَّيْلِ فَإِنَّ اَلْمَغْبُونَ مَنْ حُرِمَ قِيَامَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “O Sulayman, do not abandon the night prayer, for the one who is truly deprived is the one who is deprived of the night prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Kindi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, a man may utter a lie, and because of it he is deprived of the night prayer; and when he is deprived of the night prayer, he is deprived thereby of sustenance.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْكِنْدِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ لَيَكْذِبُ اَلْكَذِبَةَ فَيُحْرَمُ بِهَا صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فَإِذَا حُرِمَ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ حُرِمَ بِهَا اَلرِّزْقَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Kindi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, a man may utter a lie, and because of it he is deprived of the night prayer; and when he is deprived of the night prayer, he is deprived thereby of sustenance.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the houses in which the Qur’an is recited and prayer is performed shine for the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars of the sky shine for the inhabitants of the earth.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى فُضَيْلُ بْنُ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ اَلْبُيُوتَ اَلَّتِي يُصَلَّى فِيهَا بِتِلاَوَةِ اَلْقُرْآنِ تُضِيءُ لِأَهْلِ اَلسَّمَاءِ كَمَا تُضِيءُ نُجُومُ اَلسَّمَاءِ لِأَهْلِ اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Indeed, the houses in which the Qur’an is recited and prayer is performed shine for the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars of the sky shine for the inhabitants of the earth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Abu Dharr in his will to him: “O Abu Dharr, preserve the will of your Prophet (saws); Whoever’s end comes while he was engaged in the night prayer, then Paradise is for him.” (This was mentioned in a lengthy narration.)
arabicText: وَ قَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ [صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ خ ل] لِأَبِي ذَرٍّ فِي وَصِيَّتِهِ لَهُ: «يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ اِحْفَظْ وَصِيَّةَ نَبِيِّكَ مَنْ خُتِمَ لَهُ بِقِيَامِ اَللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ مَاتَ فَلَهُ اَلْجَنَّةُ» فِي حَدِيثٍ طَوِيلٍ.
thaqalaynMatn: And the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Abu Dharr in his will to him: “O Abu Dharr, preserve the will of your Prophet (saws); Whoever’s end comes while he was engaged in the night prayer, then Paradise is for him.” (This was mentioned in a lengthy narration.)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani, from someone who narrated to him:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds”’ (Surah Hud 11:114) Imam (a.s) said: “The believer’s prayer at night removes what he has committed of sins during the day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عُمَرَ اَلْيَمَانِيِّ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« إِنَّ اَلْحَسَنٰاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ اَلسَّيِّئٰاتِ» قَالَ« صَلاَةُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِ بِاللَّيْلِ تَذْهَبُ بِمَا عَمِلَ مِنْ ذَنْبٍ بِالنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani, from someone who narrated to him:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds”’ (Surah Hud 11:114) Imam (a.s) said: “The believer’s prayer at night removes what he has committed of sins during the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you rise at night from your sleep, say: ‘Praise be to Allah (swt) who returned my soul to me so that I may praise Him (azj) and worship Him (azj).’ And when you hear the sound of the roosters, say: ‘Holy, Holy, is our Lord (azj) and the Lord (azj) of the angels and the Spirit. Your (azj) mercy has preceded Your (azj) wrath. There is no god but You (azj), alone with no partner. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me. Indeed, none forgives sins except You (azj).’ Then when you stand up, look at the horizons of the sky and say: ‘O Allah (swt), there is no night in prostration that is hidden from You (azj), nor a sky with towers, nor an earth with bedding, nor ‘layers of darkness, some above others’, nor a deep sea in which travellers travel during the night from among Your (azj) creation. You (azj) know ‘the betrayal of the eyes and what the breasts conceal’. The stars have disappeared, and the eyes have slept, and yet You (azj) are ‘the Ever-Living, the Sustainer’, neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You (azj). Glory be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds. And the God (azj) of the Messengers, and praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.” Then recite the five verses from Surah Aal Imran: ‘Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…’ until His (azj) saying: ‘Indeed, You do not break the promise.”’ Then use the siwak (toothstick) and perform wudu (ablution). When you place your hand in the water, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt) and by Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), make me among those who repent often and make me among those who purify themselves.’ When you finish, say: ‘Praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.’ When you stand for your prayer, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and to Allah (swt), and from Allah (swt), and whatever Allah (swt) wills. There is no power and no strength except through Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), make me among Your (azj) visitors and among the frequenters of Your (azj) mosques. O Lord (azj), open for me the door of Your (azj) repentance, and close from me the door of Your (azj) disobedience and every act of disobedience. Praise be to Allah (swt), who made me among those who converse with Him (azj). O Allah (swt), turn Your (azj) face toward me, Exalted is Your (azj) praise!’ Then begin the prayer with the takbir.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُمْتَ بِاللَّيْلِ مِنْ مَنَامِكَ فَقُلِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي رَدَّ عَلَيَّ رُوحِي لِأَحْمَدَهُ وَ أَعْبُدَهُ فَإِذَا سَمِعْتَ صَوْتَ اَلدُّيُوكِ فَقُلْ سُبُّوحٌ قُدُّوسُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ وَاَلرُّوحِ سَبَقَتْ رَحْمَتُكَ غَضَبَكَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ وَحْدَكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ عَمِلْتُ سُوءاً وَ« ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي» وَ اِرْحَمْنِي إِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ اَلذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ فَإِذَا قُمْتَ فَانْظُرْ فِي آفَاقِ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّهُ لاَ يُوَارِي عَنْكَ لَيْلٌ سَاجٍ وَ لاَ سَمَاءٌ ذَاتُ أَبْرَاجٍ وَ لاَ أَرْضٌ ذَاتُ مِهَادٍ وَ لاَ« ظُلُمٰاتٌ بَعْضُهٰا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ» وَ لاَ بَحْرٌ لُجِّيٌّ تُدْلِجُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلْمُدْلِجِ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ تَعْلَمُ« خٰائِنَةَ اَلْأَعْيُنِ وَ مٰا تُخْفِي اَلصُّدُورُ» غَارَتِ اَلنُّجُومُ وَ نَامَتِ اَلْعُيُونُ وَ أَنْتَ« اَلْحَيُّ اَلْقَيُّومُ» لاَ تَأْخُذُكَ« سِنَةٌ وَ لاٰ نَوْمٌ»« سُبْحٰانَ اَللّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» وَ إِلَهِ اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ« وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» ثُمَّ اِقْرَأِ اَلْخَمْسَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ آلِ عِمْرَانَ« إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَاَلْأَرْضِ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ« إِنَّكَ لاٰ تُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» ثُمَّ اِسْتَكْ وَ تَوَضَّأْ فَإِذَا وَضَعْتَ يَدَكَ فِي اَلْمَاءِ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِجْعَلْنِي مِنَ اَلتَّوَّابِينَ وَ اِجْعَلْنِي مِنَ اَلْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَقُلْ« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» فَإِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى صَلاَتِكَ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ إِلَى اَللَّهِ وَ مِنَ اَللَّهِ وَ مَا شَاءَ اَللَّهُ وَ لاَ حَوْلَ وَ لاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِجْعَلْنِي مِنْ زُوَّارِكَ وَ عُمَّارِ مَسَاجِدِكَ وَ اِفْتَحْ لِي يَا رَبِّ بَابَ تَوْبَتِكَ وَ أَغْلِقْ عَنِّي بَابَ مَعْصِيَتِكَ وَ كُلِّ مَعْصِيَةٍ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي جَعَلَنِي مِمَّنْ يُنَاجِيهِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَقْبِلْ عَلَيَّ بِوَجْهِكَ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ ثُمَّ اِفْتَتِحِ اَلصَّلاَةَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you rise at night from your sleep, say: ‘Praise be to Allah (swt) who returned my soul to me so that I may praise Him (azj) and worship Him (azj).’ And when you hear the sound of the roosters, say: ‘Holy, Holy, is our Lord (azj) and the Lord (azj) of the angels and the Spirit. Your (azj) mercy has preceded Your (azj) wrath. There is no god but You (azj), alone with no partner. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me. Indeed, none forgives sins except You (azj).’ Then when you stand up, look at the horizons of the sky and say: ‘O Allah (swt), there is no night in prostration that is hidden from You (azj), nor a sky with towers, nor an earth with bedding, nor ‘layers of darkness, some above others’, nor a deep sea in which travellers travel during the night from among Your (azj) creation. You (azj) know ‘the betrayal of the eyes and what the breasts conceal’. The stars have disappeared, and the eyes have slept, and yet You (azj) are ‘the Ever-Living, the Sustainer’, neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You (azj). Glory be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds. And the God (azj) of the Messengers, and praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.” Then recite the five verses from Surah Aal Imran: ‘Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…’ until His (azj) saying: ‘Indeed, You do not break the promise.”’ Then use the siwak (toothstick) and perform wudu (ablution). When you place your hand in the water, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt) and by Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), make me among those who repent often and make me among those who purify themselves.’ When you finish, say: ‘Praise be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.’ When you stand for your prayer, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and to Allah (swt), and from Allah (swt), and whatever Allah (swt) wills. There is no power and no strength except through Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), make me among Your (azj) visitors and among the frequenters of Your (azj) mosques. O Lord (azj), open for me the door of Your (azj) repentance, and close from me the door of Your (azj) disobedience and every act of disobedience. Praise be to Allah (swt), who made me among those who converse with Him (azj). O Allah (swt), turn Your (azj) face toward me, Exalted is Your (azj) praise!’ Then begin the prayer with the takbir.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 131

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to recite fifteen verses in every rak‘ah, and His (saws) bowing (ruku‘) would be equal in length to His (saws) standing, and His (saws) prostration would be equal to His (saws) bowing, and His (saws) raising of His (saws) head from bowing and from prostration were all equal.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ آيَةً وَ يَكُونُ رُكُوعُهُ مِثْلَ قِيَامِهِ وَ سُجُودُهُ مِثْلَ رُكُوعِهِ وَ رَفْعُ رَأْسِهِ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ سَوَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to recite fifteen verses in every rak‘ah, and His (saws) bowing (ruku‘) would be equal in length to His (saws) standing, and His (saws) prostration would be equal to His (saws) bowing, and His (saws) raising of His (saws) head from bowing and from prostration were all equal.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 132

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Mas‘ud al-Ta’i:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to recite in the final rak‘ah of the night prayer: ‘Has there come upon man…’ (Surah al-Insan 76:1).” Ali ibn al-Nu‘man said, and al-Harith said: I heard Him (a.s) while He (a.s) was saying: ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ is one-third of the Qur’an, and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’ equals one-fourth of it. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to combine ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ in the witr prayer in order to encompass the entire Qur’an.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَسْعُودٍ اَلطَّائِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي آخِرِ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ« هَلْ أَتىٰ عَلَى اَلْإِنْسٰانِ» قَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلنُّعْمَانِ وَ قَالَ اَلْحَارِثُ سَمِعْتُهُ وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ«« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُلُثُ اَلْقُرْآنِ وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» تَعْدِلُ رُبُعَهُ وَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَجْمَعُ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فِي اَلْوَتْرِ لِكَيْ يَجْمَعَ اَلْقُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Mas‘ud al-Ta’i:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to recite in the final rak‘ah of the night prayer: ‘Has there come upon man…’ (Surah al-Insan 76:1).” Ali ibn al-Nu‘man said, and al-Harith said: I heard Him (a.s) while He (a.s) was saying: ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ is one-third of the Qur’an, and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’ equals one-fourth of it. And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to combine ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ in the witr prayer in order to encompass the entire Qur’an.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 132

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it has been narrated: “That whoever recites in the first two rak‘ahs of the night prayer, ‘Al-Hamdulillah’ once in each rak‘ah, and ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ thirty times, then he finishes his prayer, there will remain no sin between him and Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, except that it will be forgiven for him.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ:« أَنَّ مَنْ قَرَأَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ مِنْهَا اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ مَرَّةً وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثَلاَثِينَ مَرَّةً اِنْفَتَلَ وَ لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ذَنْبٌ إِلاَّ غُفِرَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynMatn: And it has been narrated: “That whoever recites in the first two rak‘ahs of the night prayer, ‘Al-Hamdulillah’ once in each rak‘ah, and ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ thirty times, then he finishes his prayer, there will remain no sin between him and Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, except that it will be forgiven for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 133

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Barqi and Abu Ahmad, from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is proper for the servant, when he prays, to recite with measured tone (tartil). And when he passes by a verse that mentions Paradise or the Fire, he should ask Allah (swt) for Paradise and seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the Fire. And when he passes by ‘O people’ and ‘O you who believe’, he should say: ‘Labbayk, our Lord (azj).’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ وَ أَبِي أَحْمَدَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْعَبْدِ إِذَا صَلَّى أَنْ يُرَتِّلَ فِي قِرَاءَتِهِ فَإِذَا مَرَّ بِآيَةٍ فِيهَا ذِكْرُ اَلْجَنَّةِ وَ ذِكْرُ اَلنَّارِ سَأَلَ اَللَّهَ اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ تَعَوَّذَ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ وَ إِذَا مَرَّ بِ«يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلنّٰاسُ» وَ «يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا» يَقُولُ لَبَّيْكَ رَبَّنَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Barqi and Abu Ahmad, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is proper for the servant, when he prays, to recite with measured tone (tartil). And when he passes by a verse that mentions Paradise or the Fire, he should ask Allah (swt) for Paradise and seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the Fire. And when he passes by ‘O people’ and ‘O you who believe’, he should say: ‘Labbayk, our Lord (azj).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 133

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya‘qub ibn Salim:
He asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who rises at the end of the night and raises his voice with the Qur’an. Imam (a.s) said: “It is proper for a man, when he prays at night, to make his voice heard by his family, so that the one who is already awake may rise and the one stirring may become active.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَمِّهِ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ سَالِمٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ مِنْ آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ فَيَرْفَعُ صَوْتَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ فَقَالَ« يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ إِذَا صَلَّى فِي اَللَّيْلِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ أَهْلَهُ لِكَيْ يَقُومَ اَلْقَائِمُ وَ يَتَحَرَّكَ اَلْمُتَحَرِّكُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya‘qub ibn Salim:
thaqalaynMatn: He asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who rises at the end of the night and raises his voice with the Qur’an. Imam (a.s) said: “It is proper for a man, when he prays at night, to make his voice heard by his family, so that the one who is already awake may rise and the one stirring may become active.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 133

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Isma‘il ibn Jabir or Abdullah ibn Sinan. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise at the end of the night and I fear that dawn will come.” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite al-Hamd and hurry, hurry.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ اَلْكِنْدِيِّ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ أَوْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَقُومُ آخِرَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَخَافُ اَلصُّبْحَ قَالَ« اِقْرَأِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ اِعْجَلِ اِعْجَلْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Isma‘il ibn Jabir or Abdullah ibn Sinan. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise at the end of the night and I fear that dawn will come.” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite al-Hamd and hurry, hurry.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 133

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far. said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who rises at the end of the night and fears that dawn might surprise him, should he begin with the witr prayer or perform the prayer in its proper sequence so that the witr would be the last of it? Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, he should begin with the witr.” And he (narrator) said: “I used to do that myself.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ آخِرَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ هُوَ يَخْشَى أَنْ يَفْجَأَهُ اَلصُّبْحُ أَ يَبْدَأُ بِالْوَتْرِ أَوْ يُصَلِّي اَلصَّلاَةَ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا حَتَّى يَكُونَ اَلْوَتْرُ آخِرَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ« بَلْ يَبْدَأُ بِالْوَتْرِ» وَ قَالَ« أَنَا كُنْتُ فَاعِلاً ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far. said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who rises at the end of the night and fears that dawn might surprise him, should he begin with the witr prayer or perform the prayer in its proper sequence so that the witr would be the last of it? Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, he should begin with the witr.” And he (narrator) said: “I used to do that myself.”
