chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Fadl al-Nahwi, from Abu Ja‘far al-Ahwal Muhammad ibn al-Nu‘man. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “If you have prayed four rak‘ahs of the night prayer before the rising of dawn, then complete the prayer, whether dawn has risen or not.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْفَضْلِ اَلنَّحْوِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ اَلْأَحْوَلِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ صَلَّيْتَ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَأَتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ طَلَعَ أَمْ لَمْ يَطْلُعْ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Fadl al-Nahwi, from Abu Ja‘far al-Ahwal Muhammad ibn al-Nu‘man. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “If you have prayed four rak‘ahs of the night prayer before the rising of dawn, then complete the prayer, whether dawn has risen or not.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 134

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ya‘qub al-Bazzaz. He said:
I said to Him (a.s): “I rise shortly before Fajr and pray four rak‘ahs, then I fear that dawn will break, should I begin with the witr or complete the rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather perform the witr and delay the rak‘ahs until you make them up in the early part of the day.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ اَلْبَزَّازِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَقُومُ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ بِقَلِيلٍ فَأُصَلِّي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ يَنْفَجِرَ اَلْفَجْرُ أَبْدَأُ بِالْوَتْرِ أَوْ أُتِمُّ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ أَوْتِرْ وَ أَخِّرِ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ حَتَّى تَقْضِيَهَا فِي صَدْرِ اَلنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ya‘qub al-Bazzaz. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “I rise shortly before Fajr and pray four rak‘ahs, then I fear that dawn will break, should I begin with the witr or complete the rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather perform the witr and delay the rak‘ahs until you make them up in the early part of the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 134

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Marzuban ibn ‘Imran, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise and the dawn has already appeared. If I begin with the Fajr prayer, I perform it at its earliest time; but if I begin with the night prayer and the witr, I end up praying Fajr at the time these people do (later).” So Imam (a.s) said: “Begin with the night prayer and the witr, but do not make that a habit.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اَلْمَرْزُبَانِ بْنِ عِمْرَانَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُومُ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَإِنْ أَنَا بَدَأْتُ بِالْفَجْرِ صَلَّيْتُهَا فِي أَوَّلِ وَقْتِهَا وَ إِنْ بَدَأْتُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ صَلَّيْتُ اَلْفَجْرَ فِي وَقْتِ هَؤُلاَءِ فَقَالَ« اِبْدَأْ بِصَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْ ذَلِكَ عَادَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Marzuban ibn ‘Imran, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise and the dawn has already appeared. If I begin with the Fajr prayer, I perform it at its earliest time; but if I begin with the night prayer and the witr, I end up praying Fajr at the time these people do (later).” So Imam (a.s) said: “Begin with the night prayer and the witr, but do not make that a habit.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 134

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from ‘Ammar ibn al-Mubarak, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise and the dawn has already appeared, and I have not yet performed the night prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Perform the night prayer, and perform the witr, and perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُومُ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ لَمْ أُصَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَوْتِرْ وَ صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from ‘Ammar ibn al-Mubarak, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I rise and the dawn has already appeared, and I have not yet performed the night prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Perform the night prayer, and perform the witr, and perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Hammad, from Isma‘il ibn Jabir. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I perform the witr after the dawn has risen?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُوتِرُ بَعْدَ مَا يَطْلُعُ اَلْفَجْرُ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Hammad, from Isma‘il ibn Jabir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I perform the witr after the dawn has risen?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from ‘Amr ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the night prayer and the witr after the rising of dawn. Imam (a.s) said: “Pray it after Fajr, so long as it is still within the time when you can pray the morning prayer at its latest time. But do not make that your habit every night.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Also perform the witr after you finish it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَاَلْوَتْرِ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« صَلِّهَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَكُونَ فِي وَقْتٍ تُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ فِي آخِرِ وَقْتِهَا وَ لاَ تَعَمَّدْ ذَلِكَ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ» وَ قَالَ« أَوْتِرْ أَيْضاً بَعْدَ فَرَاغِكَ مِنْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from ‘Amr ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the night prayer and the witr after the rising of dawn. Imam (a.s) said: “Pray it after Fajr, so long as it is still within the time when you can pray the morning prayer at its latest time. But do not make that your habit every night.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Also perform the witr after you finish it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the recitation in the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “There was a door between me and my father (a.s), and when my father (a.s) would pray, He (a.s) would recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in the three rak‘ahs of the witr. And when He (a.s) finished reciting it, He (a.s) would say: ‘Thus, Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj),’ or ‘That is how Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj).’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ «كَانَ بَيْنِي وَ بَيْنَ أَبِي بَابٌ فَكَانَ أَبِي إِذَا صَلَّى يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فِي ثَلاَثَتِهِنَّ وَ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فَإِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْهَا قَالَ« كَذَلِكَ اَللَّهُ رَبِّي أَوْ كَذَاكَ اَللَّهُ رَبِّي»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the recitation in the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “There was a door between me and my father (a.s), and when my father (a.s) would pray, He (a.s) would recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in the three rak‘ahs of the witr. And when He (a.s) finished reciting it, He (a.s) would say: ‘Thus, Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj),’ or ‘That is how Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from al-Halabi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ is equal to one-third of the Qur’an, and He (a.s) used to love to combine it in the witr so that the entire Qur’an would be encompassed.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ كَانَ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:«« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» تَعْدِلُ ثُلُثَ اَلْقُرْآنِ وَ كَانَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَجْمَعَهَا فِي اَلْوَتْرِ لِيَكُونَ اَلْقُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from al-Halabi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “My father (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ is equal to one-third of the Qur’an, and He (a.s) used to love to combine it in the witr so that the entire Qur’an would be encompassed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yaqtin. He said:
I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd al-Salih (a.s)) about the recitation in the witr prayer. I asked: “Some have narrated ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in all three rak‘ahs, and some have narrated the ‘Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (Surah al-Falaq and Surah al-Nas) in the first two, and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in the third.” Imam (a.s) said: “Act upon the ‘Mu‘awwidhatayn’ and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلْعَبْدَ اَلصَّالِحَ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ وَ قُلْتُ إِنَّ بَعْضاً رَوَى« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فِي اَلثَّلاَثِ وَبَعْضاً رَوَى فِي اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ وَفِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فَقَالَ« اِعْمَلْ بِالْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yaqtin. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd al-Salih (a.s)) about the recitation in the witr prayer. I asked: “Some have narrated ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in all three rak‘ahs, and some have narrated the ‘Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (Surah al-Falaq and Surah al-Nas) in the first two, and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ in the third.” Imam (a.s) said: “Act upon the ‘Mu‘awwidhatayn’ and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The witr is three rak‘ahs, separated from one another, and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ is recited in all of them.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْوَتْرُ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ يُفْصَلُ بَيْنَهُنَّ وَ يُقْرَأُ فِيهِنَّ جَمِيعاً بقل هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The witr is three rak‘ahs, separated from one another, and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ is recited in all of them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The witr is three rak‘ahs, two separated and one (by itself).”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْوَتْرُ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ ثِنْتَيْنِ مَفْصُولَةً وَ وَاحِدَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The witr is three rak‘ahs, two separated and one (by itself).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), regarding the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of witr. Imam (a.s) said: “You may wake the one who is sleeping and speak regarding a need.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّسْلِيمُ فِي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« تُوقِظُ اَلرَّاقِدَ وَ تُكَلِّمُ بِالْحَاجَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), regarding the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of witr. Imam (a.s) said: “You may wake the one who is sleeping and speak regarding a need.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Walad Hafs ibn Salim. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. And if you have a need, then go out and take care of it, then return and perform one rak‘ah.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي وَلاَّدٍ حَفْصِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكَ حَاجَةٌ فَاخْرُجْ وَ اِقْضِهَا ثُمَّ عُدْ فَارْكَعْ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Walad Hafs ibn Salim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. And if you have a need, then go out and take care of it, then return and perform one rak‘ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
Imam (a.s) said to me: “Recite in the witr, in all three rak‘ahs, ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’, and perform taslim in the two rak‘ahs. Wake the one who is asleep and command (them) to pray.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: «اِقْرَأْ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فِي ثَلاَثَتِهِنَّ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ سَلِّمْ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ تُوقِظُ اَلرَّاقِدَ وَ تَأْمُرُ بِالصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me: “Recite in the witr, in all three rak‘ahs, ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’, and perform taslim in the two rak‘ahs. Wake the one who is asleep and command (them) to pray.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 136

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Abu Walad:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man prays the two rak‘ahs of the witr, then departs to fulfill his need.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي وَلاَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْوَتْرِ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفَ فَيَقْضِيَ حَاجَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Abu Walad:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man prays the two rak‘ahs of the witr, then departs to fulfill his need.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, or someone else, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
I said to Him (a.s): “Shall I separate the witr (into parts)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said to Him (a.s): “Sometimes I become thirsty, may I drink water (in between)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَفْصِلُ اَلْوَتْرَ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي رُبَّمَا عَطِشْتُ أَ فَأَشْرَبُ اَلْمَاءَ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, or someone else, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “Shall I separate the witr (into parts)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said to Him (a.s): “Sometimes I become thirsty, may I drink water (in between)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding someone who leaves after the second rak‘ah of the witr, whether it is permissible for him to speak or leave the mosque and then return to complete the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, you may do as you wish, you may speak, perform wudu again, and then complete it before you pray the morning (Fajr) prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ: فِيمَنِ اِنْصَرَفَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ اَلْوَتْرِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ أَوْ يَخْرُجَ مِنَ اَلْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ يَعُودَ فَيُوتِرَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ تَصْنَعُ مَا تَشَاءُ وَ تَتَكَلَّمُ وَ تُحْدِثُ وُضُوءَكَ ثُمَّ تُتِمُّهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ اَلْغَدَاةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, from Muhammad ibn ‘Udhafir, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding someone who leaves after the second rak‘ah of the witr, whether it is permissible for him to speak or leave the mosque and then return to complete the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, you may do as you wish, you may speak, perform wudu again, and then complete it before you pray the morning (Fajr) prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the witr, should it be separated or connected? Imam (a.s) said: “Separated.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ أَ فَصْلٌ أَمْ وَصْلٌ قَالَ« فَصْلٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the witr, should it be separated or connected? Imam (a.s) said: “Separated.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah and others, from some of his teachers. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I separate (the rak‘ahs) in the witr?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Sometimes I become thirsty, so I drink water.” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and (even) marry (if you wish).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ بَعْضِ مَشِيخَتِهِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَفْصِلُ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي رُبَّمَا عَطِشْتُ فَأَشْرَبُ اَلْمَاءَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ اِنْكِحْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah and others, from some of his teachers. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I separate (the rak‘ahs) in the witr?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “Sometimes I become thirsty, so I drink water.” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and (even) marry (if you wish).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, you may say the taslim, and if you wish, you may omit it.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ فِي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ شِئْتَ سَلَّمْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لَمْ تُسَلِّمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the taslim (salutation) in the two rak‘ahs of the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, you may say the taslim, and if you wish, you may omit it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I say the taslim in the two rak‘ahs of the witr?” Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, you may say the taslim, and if you wish, you may omit it.”
arabicText: وعنه عن النضر عن محمد بن أبي حمزة عن معاوية بن عمار قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام اسلم في ركعتي الوتر؟ فقال إن شئت سلمت وإن شئت لم تسلم
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Shall I say the taslim in the two rak‘ahs of the witr?” Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, you may say the taslim, and if you wish, you may omit it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 137

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdawayh al-Hamdani. He said:
I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, about the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Connect it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ كُرْدَوَيْهِ اَلْهَمْدَانِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلْعَبْدَ اَلصَّالِحَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« صِلْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdawayh al-Hamdani. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, about the witr. Imam (a.s) said: “Connect it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 138

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur, from a servant of Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The two rak‘ahs of the witr, if he wishes, he may speak between them and the third rak‘ah, and if he wishes, he may not separate them.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ مَوْلًى لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« رَكْعَتَا اَلْوَتْرِ إِنْ شَاءَ تَكَلَّمَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ بَيْنَ اَلثَّالِثَةِ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يَفْصِلْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur, from a servant of Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The two rak‘ahs of the witr, if he wishes, he may speak between them and the third rak‘ah, and if he wishes, he may not separate them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 138

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘And in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness’ (Surah Dhariyat 51:18), this refers to the witr, at the end of the night, seventy times.
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« وَ بِالْأَسْحٰارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ» فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فِي آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘And in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness’ (Surah Dhariyat 51:18), this refers to the witr, at the end of the night, seventy times.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl. He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about what I should say in my witr. He said: “Whatever Allah (swt) causes to be spoken on your tongue and has decreed.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّا أَقُولُ فِي وَتْرِي فَقَالَ «مَا قَضَى اَللَّهُ عَلَى لِسَانِكَ وَ قَدَّرَهُ»
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl. He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about what I should say in my witr. He said: “Whatever Allah (swt) causes to be spoken on your tongue and has decreed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
Imam (a.s) said to me: “Seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in the witr seventy times.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِيَ:« اِسْتَغْفِرِ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s). He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me: “Seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in the witr seventy times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir who said:
I said to him: “(about) Those who seek forgiveness at dawn” (Surah Aal ‘Imran 3:17) & (Surah Dhariyat 51:18). He said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family, sought forgiveness in his Witr prayer seventy times.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ« اَلْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحٰارِ» فَقَالَ «اِسْتَغْفَرَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي وَتْرِهِ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to him: “(about) Those who seek forgiveness at dawn” (Surah Aal ‘Imran 3:17) & (Surah Dhariyat 51:18). He said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family, sought forgiveness in his Witr prayer seventy times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the Qunoot in Witr, is there anything fixed in it that should be followed and said? Imam (a.s) said: “No. Praise Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family, and seek forgiveness for your great sins.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Every sin is great.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ هَلْ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ يُتَّبَعُ وَ يُقَالُ فَقَالَ« لاَ أَثْنِ عَلَى اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اِسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ اَلْعَظِيمِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« كُلُّ ذَنْبٍ عَظِيمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the Qunoot in Witr, is there anything fixed in it that should be followed and said? Imam (a.s) said: “No. Praise Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family, and seek forgiveness for your great sins.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Every sin is great.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Qunoot in Witr is seeking forgiveness, and in the obligatory prayer it is supplication.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ اَلاِسْتِغْفَارُ وَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ اَلدُّعَاءُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Qunoot in Witr is seeking forgiveness, and in the obligatory prayer it is supplication.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In the Witr, you supplicate against the enemy, and if you wish, you may mention them by name. And you seek forgiveness, and you raise your hands in the Witr in front of your face, and if you wish, under your garment.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَدْعُو فِي اَلْوَتْرِ عَلَى اَلْعَدُوِّ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ سَمَّيْتَهُمْ وَ تَسْتَغْفِرُ وَ تَرْفَعُ يَدَيْكَ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِكَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ تَحْتَ ثَوْبِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In the Witr, you supplicate against the enemy, and if you wish, you may mention them by name. And you seek forgiveness, and you raise your hands in the Witr in front of your face, and if you wish, under your garment.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 139

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Hadid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from some of our companions:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: “Five Tasbihs with calm recitation suffice you for Qunoot.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلْقُنُوتِ خَمْسُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ فِي تَرَسُّلٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Hadid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: “Five Tasbihs with calm recitation suffice you for Qunoot.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 140

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Aban ibn Uthman narrated from Al-Halabi:
He (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "I mention the names of the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, in the prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "Summarize them."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ: أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُسَمِّي اَلْأَئِمَّةَ عَلَيهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« أَجْمِلْهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And Aban ibn Uthman narrated from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "I mention the names of the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, in the prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "Summarize them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 140

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding the man who forgets the Qunoot in the Witr prayer or in other than the Witr. Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon him." And Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it while he has already moved toward the bowing (ruku‘) before placing his hands on his knees, then let him return to a standing position and recite the Qunoot, then bow. But if he has placed his hands on his knees, then let him continue in his prayer, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى اَلْقُنُوتَ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ أَوْ غَيْرِ اَلْوَتْرِ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ» وَ قَالَ« إِنْ ذَكَرَهُ وَ قَدْ أَهْوَى إِلَى اَلرُّكُوعِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَضَعَ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى اَلرُّكْبَتَيْنِ فَلْيَرْجِعْ قَائِماً وَ لْيَقْنُتْ ثُمَّ يَرْكَعُ وَ إِنْ وَضَعَ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى اَلرُّكْبَتَيْنِ فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding the man who forgets the Qunoot in the Witr prayer or in other than the Witr. Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon him." And Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it while he has already moved toward the bowing (ruku‘) before placing his hands on his knees, then let him return to a standing position and recite the Qunoot, then bow. But if he has placed his hands on his knees, then let him continue in his prayer, and there is nothing upon him."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Abdul-Aziz, who said: One of our companions narrated to me, saying:
Abu al-Hasan al Awwal (the First) (a.s), peace be upon him, when He (a.s) raised his head from the final rak‘ah of the Witr prayer, used to say: "This is the position of one whose good deeds are a blessing from You, and whose gratitude is weak, and whose sin is great, and there is no refuge for that except in Your (azj) gentleness and Your (azj) mercy. For indeed, You (azj) said in Your (azj) revealed Book, which was sent down upon Your (azj) sent Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family: ‘They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness’ (Surah Dhariyat 51:17–18). My sleep has been long, and my standing (in prayer) has been little, and now is the time before dawn, and I am seeking Your (azj) forgiveness for my sins, seeking forgiveness like one who finds no harm or benefit for his own self, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection." Then He (a.s) would fall into prostration.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْعَزِيزِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ عَنْ آخِرِ رَكْعَةِ اَلْوَتْرِ قَالَ« هَذَا مَقَامُ مَنْ حَسَنَاتُهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْكَ وَ شُكْرُهُ ضَعِيفٌ وَ ذَنْبُهُ عَظِيمٌ وَ لَيْسَ لِذَلِكَ إِلاَّ رِفْقُكَ وَ رَحْمَتُكَ فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ فِي كِتَابِكَ اَلْمُنْزَلِ عَلَى نَبِيِّكَ اَلْمُرْسَلِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ« كٰانُوا قَلِيلاً مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ مٰا يَهْجَعُونَ` وَ بِالْأَسْحٰارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ» طَالَ هُجُوعِي وَ قَلَّ قِيَامِي وَ هَذَا اَلسَّحَرُ وَ أَنَا أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لِذُنُوبِي اِسْتِغْفَارَ مَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ ضَرّاً وَ لاَ نَفْعاً وَ لاَ مَوْتاً وَ لاَ حَيَاةً وَ لاَ نُشُوراً ثُمَّ يَخِرُّ سَاجِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Abdul-Aziz, who said: One of our companions narrated to me, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan al Awwal (the First) (a.s), peace be upon him, when He (a.s) raised his head from the final rak‘ah of the Witr prayer, used to say: "This is the position of one whose good deeds are a blessing from You, and whose gratitude is weak, and whose sin is great, and there is no refuge for that except in Your (azj) gentleness and Your (azj) mercy. For indeed, You (azj) said in Your (azj) revealed Book, which was sent down upon Your (azj) sent Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family: ‘They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness’ (Surah Dhariyat 51:17–18). My sleep has been long, and my standing (in prayer) has been little, and now is the time before dawn, and I am seeking Your (azj) forgiveness for my sins, seeking forgiveness like one who finds no harm or benefit for his own self, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection." Then He (a.s) would fall into prostration.

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: "The two rak‘ahs that are before the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer, what is their time?" Imam (a.s) said: "Before the rising of the dawn. So when the dawn rises, then the time of the dawn prayer has entered."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَللَّتَانِ قَبْلَ اَلْغَدَاةِ أَيْنَ مَوْضِعُهُمَا فَقَالَ« قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَإِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْغَدَاةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: "The two rak‘ahs that are before the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer, what is their time?" Imam (a.s) said: "Before the rising of the dawn. So when the dawn rises, then the time of the dawn prayer has entered."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I (Ali ibn Mahziyar) read in the letter of a man to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, asking: "The two rak‘ahs before the Fajr prayer, are they from the night prayer or from the day prayer? And at what time should I perform them?" So He (a.s) wrote in his own handwriting: "Insert them into the night prayer as an insertion."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: قَرَأْتُ فِي كِتَابِ رَجُلٍ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَللَّتَانِ قَبْلَ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَمْ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ فِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ أُصَلِّيهِمَا فَكَتَبَ بِخَطِّهِ« اُحْشُوهُمَا فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ حَشْواً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Ali ibn Mahziyar) read in the letter of a man to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, asking: "The two rak‘ahs before the Fajr prayer, are they from the night prayer or from the day prayer? And at what time should I perform them?" So He (a.s) wrote in his own handwriting: "Insert them into the night prayer as an insertion."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Insert them into the night prayer."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« اُحْشُوا بِهِمَا صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Insert them into the night prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked (Imam (a.s)): "Are the two rak‘ahs of Fajr from the night prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ رَكْعَتَا اَلْفَجْرِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ هِيَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam (a.s)): "Are the two rak‘ahs of Fajr from the night prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 141

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, are they before the Fajr or after the Fajr? Imam (a.s) said: "Before the Fajr, for they are from the night prayer. Thirteen rak‘ahs is the night prayer. Do you want to compare? If there was something due upon you from the month of Ramadan, would you perform voluntary prayers after the time of the obligatory prayer has entered? Begin with the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ أَوْ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ إِنَّهُمَا مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ أَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُقَايِسَ لَوْ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَ كُنْتَ تَتَطَوَّعُ إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْكَ وَقْتُ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَابْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, are they before the Fajr or after the Fajr? Imam (a.s) said: "Before the Fajr, for they are from the night prayer. Thirteen rak‘ahs is the night prayer. Do you want to compare? If there was something due upon you from the month of Ramadan, would you perform voluntary prayers after the time of the obligatory prayer has entered? Begin with the obligatory prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "You perform them when you are about to leave off the dawn prayer; indeed, they are before the dawn prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ قَالَ« تَرْكَعُهُمَا حِينَ تَتْرُكُ اَلْغَدَاةَ إِنَّهُمَا قَبْلَ اَلْغَدَاةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "You perform them when you are about to leave off the dawn prayer; indeed, they are before the dawn prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 142

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn Bayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the beginning time of the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "The last sixth of the night."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمْزَةَ بْنِ بِيضٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَوَّلِ وَقْتِ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« سُدُسُ اَللَّيْلِ اَلْبَاقِي»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn Bayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the beginning time of the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "The last sixth of the night."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 142

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: "The two rak‘ahs of Fajr, should I perform them before Fajr or after Fajr?" He (narrator) said: “Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Insert them into the night prayer, and perform them before Fajr."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ أُصَلِّيهِمَا قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ أَوْ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اُحْشُ بِهِمَا صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ صَلِّهِمَا قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: "The two rak‘ahs of Fajr, should I perform them before Fajr or after Fajr?" He (narrator) said: “Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Insert them into the night prayer, and perform them before Fajr."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 142

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: "When should I perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr?" Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn appears across the horizon, and that is what the Arabs call 'al-Sadi‘ (the splitter of the night).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقُلْتُ مَتَى أُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« حِينَ يَعْتَرِضُ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ هُوَ اَلَّذِي تُسَمِّيهِ اَلْعَرَبُ اَلصَّدِيعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: "When should I perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr?" Imam (a.s) said: "When the dawn appears across the horizon, and that is what the Arabs call 'al-Sadi‘ (the splitter of the night).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 142

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "Perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr before the Fajr, and after it, and at its time."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ بَعْدَهُ وَ عِنْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "Perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr before the Fajr, and after it, and at its time."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And it has been narrated from Safwan from al-‘Alaa from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, and from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, when should I perform them? Imam (a.s) said: "Before the Fajr, and with it, and after it."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ مَتَى أُصَلِّيهِمَا فَقَالَ« قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ مَعَهُ وَ بَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And it has been narrated from Safwan from al-‘Alaa from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, and from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, when should I perform them? Imam (a.s) said: "Before the Fajr, and with it, and after it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Perform them with the Fajr, and before it, and after it."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلِّهِمَا مَعَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ قَبْلَهُ وَ بَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Perform them with the Fajr, and before it, and after it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Muskan from Ya‘qub ibn Salim al-Bazzaz, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Perform them after the Fajr, and recite in the first one ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’ and in the second one ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’."
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ سَالِمٍ اَلْبَزَّازِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلِّهِمَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ اِقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا فِي اَلْأُولَى« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Muskan from Ya‘qub ibn Salim al-Bazzaz, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Perform them after the Fajr, and recite in the first one ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’ and in the second one ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Perform them before the Fajr, and with the Fajr, and after the Fajr."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ قَالَ« صَلِّهِمَا قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ مَعَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Perform them before the Fajr, and with the Fajr, and after the Fajr."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Perform them after the Fajr has risen."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلِّهِمَا بَعْدَ مَا يَطْلُعُ اَلْفَجْرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Perform them after the Fajr has risen."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 143

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from someone who informed him:
He, peace be upon him, said: "Perform the two rak‘ahs while the light is still between you and being level with your head. If it is after that, then begin with the Fajr prayer."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلِّ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مَا بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَكُونَ اَلضَّوْءُ حِذَاءَ رَأْسِكَ فَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَابْدَأْ بِالْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from someone who informed him:
thaqalaynMatn: He, peace be upon him, said: "Perform the two rak‘ahs while the light is still between you and being level with your head. If it is after that, then begin with the Fajr prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 144

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "A man rises and the light of dawn has already appeared." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him perform the two prostrations (the two rak‘ahs) that are before the dawn prayer, and then let him perform the dawn (Fajr) prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ وَ قَدْ نَوَّرَ بِالْغَدَاةِ قَالَ« فَلْيُصَلِّ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ اَلْغَدَاةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "A man rises and the light of dawn has already appeared." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him perform the two prostrations (the two rak‘ahs) that are before the dawn prayer, and then let him perform the dawn (Fajr) prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 144

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "When should I perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr?" Imam (a.s) said to me: "After the rising of the Fajr." I said to Him (a.s): "Abu Ja‘far (a.s) instructed me to perform them before the rising of the Fajr." So He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: "O Abu Muhammad, the Shia came to my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) seeking guidance, so He (a.s) gave them a fatwa with the pure truth. But they came to me full of doubt, so I gave them a fatwa based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation)."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَتَى أُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ قَالَ فَقَالَ لِي« بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ» قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أُصَلِّيَهُمَا قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ إِنَّ اَلشِّيعَةَ أَتَوْا أَبِي مُسْتَرْشِدِينَ فَأَفْتَاهُمْ بِمُرِّ اَلْحَقِّ وَأَتَوْنِي شُكَّاكاً فَأَفْتَيْتُهُمْ بِالتَّقِيَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "When should I perform the two rak‘ahs of Fajr?" Imam (a.s) said to me: "After the rising of the Fajr." I said to Him (a.s): "Abu Ja‘far (a.s) instructed me to perform them before the rising of the Fajr." So He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: "O Abu Muhammad, the Shia came to my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) seeking guidance, so He (a.s) gave them a fatwa with the pure truth. But they came to me full of doubt, so I gave them a fatwa based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 145

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Sometimes I perform them while it is still night upon me, so if I rise and the Fajr has not yet appeared, I repeat them."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« رُبَّمَا صَلَّيْتُهُمَا وَ عَلَيَّ لَيْلٌ فَإِنْ قُمْتُ وَ لَمْ يَطْلُعِ اَلْفَجْرُ أَعَدْتُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Sometimes I perform them while it is still night upon me, so if I rise and the Fajr has not yet appeared, I repeat them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 145

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "Indeed, I perform the night prayer, and I finish my prayer and perform the two rak‘ahs, then I sleep for as long as Allah (swt) wills before the Fajr rises. Then if I wake at the time of Fajr, I repeat them."
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ صَفْوَانُ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنِّي لَأُصَلِّي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فَأَفْرُغُ مِنْ صَلاَتِي وَ أُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَنَامُ مَا شَاءَ اَللَّهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظْتُ عِنْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ أَعَدْتُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "Indeed, I perform the night prayer, and I finish my prayer and perform the two rak‘ahs, then I sleep for as long as Allah (swt) wills before the Fajr rises. Then if I wake at the time of Fajr, I repeat them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 145

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Recite in the two rak‘ahs of Fajr any two Surahs that you love." And Imam (a.s) said: "As for me, I love to recite in them ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِقْرَأْ فِي رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ بِأَيِّ سُورَتَيْنِ أَحْبَبْتَ» وَ قَالَ «أَمَّا أَنَا فَأُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِيهِمَا بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ»
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Recite in the two rak‘ahs of Fajr any two Surahs that you love." And Imam (a.s) said: "As for me, I love to recite in them ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 145

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan, and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) what I should say when I lie on my right side after the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Recite the five verses at the end of Surah Al ‘Imran, until ‘'Indeed, You do not break the promise.'‘ (Surah Al-'Imran 3:190-194). Then say: I have held fast to the firm handhold of Allah (swt) which ‘never breaks’, and I have taken refuge with the strong rope of Allah (swt). I seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the evil of the wicked among the Arabs and non-Arabs. I believe in Allah (swt). I have placed my trust in Allah (swt). I turn my back to Allah (swt). I have entrusted my affair to Allah (swt). And whoever relies upon Allah (swt), then He (swt) is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah (swt) will accomplish His (swt) purpose. Allah (swt) has set a measure for everything. Allah (swt) is sufficient for me, and He (swt) is the best disposer of affairs. O Allah (swt), whoever begins his morning in need of the creation, then indeed my need and my longing is toward You (swt). Praise be to the Lord (swt) of the morning! Praise be to the cleaver of the dawn!" (Repeat this three times).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّا أَقُولُ إِذَا اِضْطَجَعْتُ عَلَى يَمِينِي بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اِقْرَأِ اَلْخَمْسَ آيَاتٍ اَلَّتِي فِي آخِرِ آلِ عِمْرَانَ إِلَى« إِنَّكَ لاٰ تُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» وَ قُلِ اِسْتَمْسَكْتُ بِعُرْوَةِ اَللَّهِ اَلْوُثْقَى اَلَّتِي« لاَ اِنْفِصٰامَ لَهٰا» وَ اِعْتَصَمْتُ بِحَبْلِ اَللَّهِ اَلْمَتِينِ وَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَرِّ فَسَقَةِ اَلْعَرَبِ وَ اَلْعَجَمِ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ« تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اَللّٰهِ» أَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَى اَللَّهِ فَوَّضْتُ« أَمْرِي إِلَى اَللّٰهِ»« وَ مَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اَللّٰهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ إِنَّ اَللّٰهَ بٰالِغُ أَمْرِهِ قَدْ جَعَلَ اَللّٰهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً» حَسْبِيَ« اَللّٰهُ وَ نِعْمَ اَلْوَكِيلُ» اَللَّهُمَّ مَنْ أَصْبَحَتْ حَاجَتُهُ إِلَى مَخْلُوقٍ فَإِنَّ حَاجَتِي وَ رَغْبَتِي إِلَيْكَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِرَبِّ اَلصَّبَاحِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِفَالِقِ اَلْإِصْبَاحِ ثَلاَثاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan, and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) what I should say when I lie on my right side after the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Recite the five verses at the end of Surah Al ‘Imran, until ‘'Indeed, You do not break the promise.'‘ (Surah Al-'Imran 3:190-194). Then say: I have held fast to the firm handhold of Allah (swt) which ‘never breaks’, and I have taken refuge with the strong rope of Allah (swt). I seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the evil of the wicked among the Arabs and non-Arabs. I believe in Allah (swt). I have placed my trust in Allah (swt). I turn my back to Allah (swt). I have entrusted my affair to Allah (swt). And whoever relies upon Allah (swt), then He (swt) is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah (swt) will accomplish His (swt) purpose. Allah (swt) has set a measure for everything. Allah (swt) is sufficient for me, and He (swt) is the best disposer of affairs. O Allah (swt), whoever begins his morning in need of the creation, then indeed my need and my longing is toward You (swt). Praise be to the Lord (swt) of the morning! Praise be to the cleaver of the dawn!" (Repeat this three times).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 146

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I performed the night prayer behind (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). When He (a.s) finished, He (a.s) placed a prostration (sajdah) in place of lying down (al-daj‘ah).
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْبِلاَدِ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ جَعَلَ مَكَانَ اَلضَّجْعَةِ سَجْدَةً
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I performed the night prayer behind (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). When He (a.s) finished, He (a.s) placed a prostration (sajdah) in place of lying down (al-daj‘ah).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 146

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-Husayn ibn Uthman by a man:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Standing, sitting, and speaking after the two rak’ahs of Fajr suffice you in place of lying down."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلاِضْطِجَاعِ بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ اَلْقِيَامُ وَ اَلْقُعُودُ وَ اَلْكَلاَمُ بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-Husayn ibn Uthman by a man:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Standing, sitting, and speaking after the two rak’ahs of Fajr suffice you in place of lying down."
