gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "It is only required of one of you, when midnight arrives, to rise and perform his prayer all at once, thirteen rak‘ahs. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and supplicate; if he wishes, he may sleep; if he wishes, he may go wherever he wishes."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِبْنَيْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّمَا عَلَى أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ اَللَّيْلُ أَنْ يَقُومَ فَيُصَلِّيَ صَلاَتَهُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ إِنْ شَاءَ جَلَسَ فَدَعَا وَ إِنْ شَاءَ نَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ ذَهَبَ حَيْثُ شَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "It is only required of one of you, when midnight arrives, to rise and perform his prayer all at once, thirteen rak‘ahs. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and supplicate; if he wishes, he may sleep; if he wishes, he may go wherever he wishes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Akhir (the Last), peace be upon him, said: "Beware of sleeping between the night prayer and the Fajr prayer. Rather, lie down without sleeping, for the one who sleeps at that time is not praised for what he has performed of his prayer."
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْقَاسَانِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَخِيرُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِيَّاكَ وَ اَلنَّوْمَ بَيْنَ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ لَكِنْ ضَجْعَةً بِلاَ نَوْمٍ فَإِنَّ صَاحِبَهُ لاَ يُحْمَدُ عَلَى مَا قَدَّمَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan al-Akhir (the Last), peace be upon him, said: "Beware of sleeping between the night prayer and the Fajr prayer. Rather, lie down without sleeping, for the one who sleeps at that time is not praised for what he has performed of his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja‘far al-Nahwi from Abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khallad from ‘Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Asadi from Ibn ‘Umar:
(Imam) al-Hasan ibn Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “I heard my father (Imam) Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "Any Muslim who sits in his prayer place, in which he performed the Fajr prayer, remembering Allah (swt) until the sun rises, will have the reward of one who has performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and he will be forgiven. And if he remains sitting there until the time comes in which prayer is permitted, and he then performs two rak‘ahs or four, he will be forgiven for what has passed, and he will have the reward of one who has performed Hajj to the House of Allah (swt)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ اَلنَّحْوِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلنَّجُودِ اَلْأَسَدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ عُمَرَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« أَيُّمَا اِمْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ جَلَسَ فِي مُصَلاَّهُ اَلَّذِي صَلَّى فِيهِ اَلْفَجْرَ يَذْكُرُ اَللَّهَ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ اَلْأَجْرِ كَحَاجِّ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ غُفِرَ لَهُ فَإِنْ جَلَسَ فِيهِ حَتَّى تَكُونَ سَاعَةٌ تَحِلُّ فِيهَا اَلصَّلاَةُ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ أَرْبَعاً غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَ كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ اَلْأَجْرِ كَحَاجِّ بَيْتِ اَللَّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja‘far al-Nahwi from Abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khallad from ‘Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Asadi from Ibn ‘Umar:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) al-Hasan ibn Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “I heard my father (Imam) Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "Any Muslim who sits in his prayer place, in which he performed the Fajr prayer, remembering Allah (swt) until the sun rises, will have the reward of one who has performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and he will be forgiven. And if he remains sitting there until the time comes in which prayer is permitted, and he then performs two rak‘ahs or four, he will be forgiven for what has passed, and he will have the reward of one who has performed Hajj to the House of Allah (swt)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Allah (swt) said; "O son of Adam, remember Me (azj) for one hour after Fajr, and remember Me (azj) for one hour after ‘Asr, I will suffice you concerning that which troubles you."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« قَالَ اَللَّهُ« يَا اِبْنَ آدَمَ اُذْكُرْنِي بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ سَاعَةً وَ اُذْكُرْنِي بَعْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ سَاعَةً أَكْفِكَ مَا أَهَمَّكَ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Allah (swt) said; "O son of Adam, remember Me (azj) for one hour after Fajr, and remember Me (azj) for one hour after ‘Asr, I will suffice you concerning that which troubles you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Mu’awiyah ibn Hakim from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad from al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: "It is proper for a man, when he begins his morning, to recite fifty verses after the ‘ta’qib’ (post-prayer supplication and remembrance)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ بَعْدَ اَلتَّعْقِيبِ خَمْسِينَ آيَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Mu’awiyah ibn Hakim from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad from al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: "It is proper for a man, when he begins his morning, to recite fifty verses after the ‘ta’qib’ (post-prayer supplication and remembrance)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And al-’Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about sleeping after the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, sustenance is distributed during that hour, so I dislike for a man to sleep at that time."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلنَّوْمِ بَعْدَ اَلْغَدَاةِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ اَلرِّزْقَ يُبْسَطُ تِلْكَ اَلسَّاعَةَ فَأَنَا أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَنَامَ اَلرَّجُلُ تِلْكَ اَلسَّاعَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And al-’Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about sleeping after the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, sustenance is distributed during that hour, so I dislike for a man to sleep at that time."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Sitting after the dawn prayer in ‘ta’qib’ and supplication until the sun rises is more effective in seeking sustenance than striking the earth (engaging in work and travel)."
arabicText: وَقَالَ اَلصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْجُلُوسُ بَعْدَ صَلاَةِ اَلْغَدَاةِ فِي اَلتَّعْقِيبِ وَاَلدُّعَاءِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ أَبْلَغُ فِي طَلَبِ اَلرِّزْقِ مِنَ اَلضَّرْبِ فِي اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Sitting after the dawn prayer in ‘ta’qib’ and supplication until the sun rises is more effective in seeking sustenance than striking the earth (engaging in work and travel)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The sleep of the early morning is ominous, it drives away sustenance, makes the complexion pale, uglifies and alters it. It is the sleep of every unfortunate one. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, distributes sustenance between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So beware of that sleep. The manna and quails used to descend upon the Children of Israel between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever slept during that hour, his portion would not descend, and when he awoke, he would not find his portion, and would be in need of begging and seeking."
arabicText: وَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« نَوْمَةُ اَلْغَدَاةِ مَشُومَةٌ تَطْرُدُ اَلرِّزْقَ وَ تُصَفِّرُ اَللَّوْنَ وَ تُقَبِّحُهُ وَ تُغَيِّرُهُ وَ هُوَ نَوْمُ كُلِّ مَشُومٍ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقْسِمُ اَلْأَرْزَاقَ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ إِيَّاكُمْ وَ تِلْكَ اَلنَّوْمَةَ وَ كَانَ اَلْمَنُّ وَ اَلسَّلْوَى يَنْزِلُ عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَمَنْ نَامَ تِلْكَ اَلسَّاعَةَ لَمْ يَنْزِلْ نَصِيبُهُ وَ كَانَ إِذَا اِنْتَبَهَ فَلاَ يَرَى نَصِيبَهُ اِحْتَاجَ إِلَى اَلسُّؤَالِ وَ اَلطَّلَبِ»
thaqalaynMatn: And (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The sleep of the early morning is ominous, it drives away sustenance, makes the complexion pale, uglifies and alters it. It is the sleep of every unfortunate one. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, distributes sustenance between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So beware of that sleep. The manna and quails used to descend upon the Children of Israel between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever slept during that hour, his portion would not descend, and when he awoke, he would not find his portion, and would be in need of begging and seeking."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Majestic: ‘"By those who distribute [affairs] by command"‘: (Surah Dhariyat 51:4). (Imam (a.s) said) "The angels distribute the sustenance of the children of Adam between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever sleeps during that time has slept away his sustenance."
arabicText: وَ قَالَ اَلصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« فَالْمُقَسِّمٰاتِ أَمْراً» قَالَ« اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ تُقَسِّمُ أَرْزَاقَ بَنِي آدَمَ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَمَنْ نَامَ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمَا نَامَ عَنْ رِزْقِهِ»
thaqalaynMatn: And (Imam) al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Majestic: ‘"By those who distribute [affairs] by command"‘: (Surah Dhariyat 51:4). (Imam (a.s) said) "The angels distribute the sustenance of the children of Adam between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever sleeps during that time has slept away his sustenance."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Explanation of the Fifty-One Rak‘ahs; The Order, Recitation, Tasbih in Bowing and Prostration, Qunut, and What is Obligatory and Recommended Therein
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "Whoever sits in his prayer place from the Fajr prayer until the rising of the sun, Allah (swt) will shield him from the Fire."
arabicText: وَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَ:« مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي مُصَلاَّهُ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ سَتَرَهُ اَللَّهُ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ»
thaqalaynMatn: And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "Whoever sits in his prayer place from the Fajr prayer until the rising of the sun, Allah (swt) will shield him from the Fire."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "What has Allah (swt) made obligatory in the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "The time, purification, bowing, prostration, facing the Qiblah, supplication, and direction (intention)." I asked: "And what about everything else?" Imam (a.s) said: "It is Sunnah within the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« اَلْوَقْتَ وَ اَلطَّهُورَ وَ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ وَ اَلْقِبْلَةَ وَ اَلدُّعَاءَ وَ اَلتَّوَجُّهَ» قُلْتُ فَمَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« سُنَّةٌ فِي فَرِيضَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "What has Allah (swt) made obligatory in the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "The time, purification, bowing, prostration, facing the Qiblah, supplication, and direction (intention)." I asked: "And what about everything else?" Imam (a.s) said: "It is Sunnah within the obligatory prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: "Prayer is made up of three thirds: one third is purification, one third is bowing, and one third is prostration."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ ثَلاَثَةُ أَثْلاَثٍ ثُلُثٌ طَهُورٌ وَ ثُلُثٌ رُكُوعٌ وَ ثُلُثٌ سُجُودٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: "Prayer is made up of three thirds: one third is purification, one third is bowing, and one third is prostration."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), said: "There is no prayer without purification."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ إِلاَّ بِطَهُورٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), said: "There is no prayer without purification."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "When the time (for prayer) enters, purification and prayer become obligatory, and there is no prayer without purification."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلْوَقْتُ وَجَبَ اَلطَّهُورُ وَ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ لاَ صَلاَةَ إِلاَّ بِطَهُورٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "When the time (for prayer) enters, purification and prayer become obligatory, and there is no prayer without purification."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from his father from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Whoever performs the prayer outside of its appointed time, there is no prayer for him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْبِلاَدِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتٍ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from his father from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Whoever performs the prayer outside of its appointed time, there is no prayer for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) (said) concerning a man who performed the dawn prayer at night, deceived by the moonlight, and then slept until the sun rose, and was informed that he had prayed during the night. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "He must repeat his prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى اَلْغَدَاةَ بِلَيْلٍ غَرَّهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلْقَمَرُ وَ نَامَ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَأُخْبِرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى بِلَيْلٍ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) (said) concerning a man who performed the dawn prayer at night, deceived by the moonlight, and then slept until the sun rose, and was informed that he had prayed during the night. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "He must repeat his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari said: Abdullah ibn Waddah narrated to me from Sama’ah ibn Mihran, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: "Beware of praying before the sun passes the meridian (before noon), for you would be praying in the time of ‘Asr. It is better for you to pray in the time of ‘Asr than to pray before the sun has passed the meridian."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ وَضَّاحٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ فَإِنَّكَ تُصَلِّي فِي وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ خَيْرٌ لَكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari said: Abdullah ibn Waddah narrated to me from Sama’ah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: "Beware of praying before the sun passes the meridian (before noon), for you would be praying in the time of ‘Asr. It is better for you to pray in the time of ‘Asr than to pray before the sun has passed the meridian."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Isma‘il ibn Riyah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you perform the prayer while thinking that you are within the time, but the time had not yet entered, and then the time enters while you are still in the prayer, it suffices for you."
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى عن الحسين بن سعيد عن محمد بن أبي عمير عن اسماعيل بن رياح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا صليت وانت ترى انك في وقت ولم يدخل الوقت فدخل الوقت وأنت في الصلاة فقد اجزأت عنك
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Isma‘il ibn Riyah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you perform the prayer while thinking that you are within the time, but the time had not yet entered, and then the time enters while you are still in the prayer, it suffices for you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you perform part of the prayer during travel outside of its prescribed time, it does not harm (it is not invalid)."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِهَا فَلاَ يَضُرُّ» فان المراد به جواز تأخير الصلاة عن وقتها عند العارض والعذر والاضطرار فأما تقديمها فانه لا يجوز على كل حال
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you perform part of the prayer during travel outside of its prescribed time, it does not harm (it is not invalid)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked the Righteous servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)): “About a man who prays on a cloudy day not facing the Qiblah, then the sun appears while he is still within the prayer time, should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the Qiblah? And if he had made every effort to determine the Qiblah, does his prayer suffice?” Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat it as long as the time remains. But if the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him."
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن يعقوب بن يقطين قال سألت عبدا صالحا عليه السلام عن رجل يصلي في يوم سحاب على غير القبلة ثم تطلع الشمس وهو في وقت أيعيد الصلاة إذا كان قد صلى على غير القبلة؟ وان كان قد تحرى القبلة بجهده أتجزيه صلاته؟ فقال يعيد ما كان في وقت فإذا ذهب الوقت فلا اعادة عليه
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)): “About a man who prays on a cloudy day not facing the Qiblah, then the sun appears while he is still within the prayer time, should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the Qiblah? And if he had made every effort to determine the Qiblah, does his prayer suffice?” Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat it as long as the time remains. But if the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man is in a deserted land on a cloudy day and he prays not facing the Qiblah. Then it clears up, and he comes to know that he had prayed not facing the Qiblah, what should he do?" Imam (a.s) said: "If the time remains, then let him repeat his prayer. But if the time has passed, then his effort suffices him."
arabicText: وعنه عن النضر بن سويد عن هشام بن سالم عن سليمان ابن خالد قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام الرجل يكون في قفر من الارض في يوم غيم فيصلي لغير القبلة ثم يصحي فيعلم انه قد صلى لغير القبلة كيف يصنع؟ فقال إن كان في وقت فليعد صلاته وإن كان قد مضى الوقت فحسبه اجتهاده
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "A man is in a deserted land on a cloudy day and he prays not facing the Qiblah. Then it clears up, and he comes to know that he had prayed not facing the Qiblah, what should he do?" Imam (a.s) said: "If the time remains, then let him repeat his prayer. But if the time has passed, then his effort suffices him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you prayed while not facing the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed not facing the Qiblah while you are still within the time, then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن الحسين بن محمد عن عبد الله بن عامر عن علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة بن أيوب عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الله عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا صليت وأنت على غير القبلة واستبان لك انك صليت على غير القبلة وانت في وقت فأعد وان فاتك الوقت فلا تعد
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you prayed while not facing the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed not facing the Qiblah while you are still within the time, then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who prays not facing the Qiblah and then realizes while he is still in the prayer before finishing it. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is facing a direction between the east and the west, then let him turn his face toward the Qiblah as soon as he realizes. But if he is facing the rear of the Qiblah, then he must break the prayer, turn his face toward the Qiblah, and then begin the prayer anew."
arabicText: وعنه عن أحمد بن ادريس عن أحمد بن محمد ومحمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن أحمد بن الحسن بن علي عن عمرو بن سعيد عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار الساباطي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في رجل صلى على غير القبلة فيعلم وهو في الصلاة قبل أن يفرغ من صلاته قال ان كان متوجها فيما بين المشرق والمغرب فليحول وجهه الى القبلة حين يعلم وان كان متوجها الى دبر القبلة فليقطع الصلاة ثم يحول وجهه الى القبلة ثم يفتتح الصلاة
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who prays not facing the Qiblah and then realizes while he is still in the prayer before finishing it. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is facing a direction between the east and the west, then let him turn his face toward the Qiblah as soon as he realizes. But if he is facing the rear of the Qiblah, then he must break the prayer, turn his face toward the Qiblah, and then begin the prayer anew."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 151

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who gave the ‘Iqamah’ for prayer but forgot to say the Takbirat al-Ihram (opening Takbir) and began the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَقَامَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who gave the ‘Iqamah’ for prayer but forgot to say the Takbirat al-Ihram (opening Takbir) and began the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about a man who forgets the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir). Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat (the prayer)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلاِفْتِتَاحِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about a man who forgets the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir). Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat (the prayer)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah from Safwan from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
(Imam (a.s)) was asked regarding the one who remembers that he did not say the Takbir at the beginning of his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain that he did not say the Takbir, then he must repeat (the prayer); but how can he be certain?”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلَّذِي يَذْكُرُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ فِي أَوَّلِ صَلاَتِهِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا اِسْتَيْقَنَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ لَكِنْ كَيْفَ يَسْتَيْقِنُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah from Safwan from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) was asked regarding the one who remembers that he did not say the Takbir at the beginning of his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain that he did not say the Takbir, then he must repeat (the prayer); but how can he be certain?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dhurayh ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets to say the Takbir until he has already recited (Qur’an). Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say the Takbir."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْمُحَارِبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى قَرَأَ قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dhurayh ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets to say the Takbir until he has already recited (Qur’an). Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say the Takbir."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgets to begin the prayer (with the opening Takbir) until he has bowed. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat the prayer."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَفْتَتِحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgets to begin the prayer (with the opening Takbir) until he has bowed. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Barqi from Dhurayh al-Muharibi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already recited (Qur’an). Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say the Takbir."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ اَلْمُحَارِبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى قَرَأَ قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Barqi from Dhurayh al-Muharibi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already recited (Qur’an). Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say the Takbir."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik and Ibn Abi Ya’fur:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who performs prayer but does not begin with the Takbir, does the Takbir of bowing suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: "No. Rather, he must repeat his prayer if he remembers that he did not say the Takbir."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَلَمْ يَفْتَتِحْ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ هَلْ يُجْزِيهِ تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلرُّكُوعِ قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ إِذَا حَفِظَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik and Ibn Abi Ya’fur:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who performs prayer but does not begin with the Takbir, does the Takbir of bowing suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: "No. Rather, he must repeat his prayer if he remembers that he did not say the Takbir."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 152

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who transmitted it with an elevated chain from al-Ridha (a.s):
(Imam (a.s)) said: "The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes of those behind him, except for the Takbirat al-Iftitah (the opening Takbir)."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى رَفَعَهُ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْإِمَامُ يَحْمِلُ أَوْهَامَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ إِلاَّ تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلاِفْتِتَاحِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who transmitted it with an elevated chain from al-Ridha (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: "The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes of those behind him, except for the Takbirat al-Iftitah (the opening Takbir)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 153

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "If at the beginning of your prayer, after the opening (du’a’), you said the first of the twenty-one Takbirs, then forgot all the rest of the Takbirs and did not say them, that first Takbir suffices you for all the Takbirs of the prayer."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا أَنْتَ كَبَّرْتَ فِي أَوَّلِ صَلاَتِكَ بَعْدَ اَلاِسْتِفْتَاحِ بِإِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً ثُمَّ نَسِيتَ اَلتَّكْبِيرَ كُلَّهُ وَ لَمْ تُكَبِّرْ أَجْزَأَكَ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ اَلْأَوَّلُ عَنْ تَكْبِيرِ اَلصَّلاَةِ كُلِّهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "If at the beginning of your prayer, after the opening (du’a’), you said the first of the twenty-one Takbirs, then forgot all the rest of the Takbirs and did not say them, that first Takbir suffices you for all the Takbirs of the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 153

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already entered into the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Was it not his intention to say the Takbir?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him continue with his prayer."
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« أَ لَيْسَ كَانَ مِنْ نِيَّتِهِ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already entered into the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Was it not his intention to say the Takbir?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him continue with his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 153

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "A man forgot to say the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir) until he said the Takbir for bowing." Imam (a.s) said: "It suffices him."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلاِفْتِتَاحِ حَتَّى كَبَّرَ لِلرُّكُوعِ فَقَالَ« أَجْزَأَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "A man forgot to say the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir) until he said the Takbir for bowing." Imam (a.s) said: "It suffices him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 153

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "A man forgets the first Takbir of the opening (Takbirat al-Iftitah)." Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it before bowing, let him say the Takbir, then recite, then bow. And if he remembers it during the prayer, let him say it while standing, in the place of the Takbir, before the recitation and after the recitation." I asked: "And if he remembers it after the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him make it up, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَنْسَى أَوَّلَ تَكْبِيرَةٍ مِنَ اَلاِفْتِتَاحِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ ذَكَرَهَا قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ كَبَّرَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ إِنْ ذَكَرَهَا فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ كَبَّرَهَا فِي قِيَامِهِ فِي مَوْضِعِ اَلتَّكْبِيرَةِ قَبْلَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ ذَكَرَهَا بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« فَلْيَقْضِهَا وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "A man forgets the first Takbir of the opening (Takbirat al-Iftitah)." Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it before bowing, let him say the Takbir, then recite, then bow. And if he remembers it during the prayer, let him say it while standing, in the place of the Takbir, before the recitation and after the recitation." I asked: "And if he remembers it after the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him make it up, and there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 154

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah ibn Mihran from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who stood in prayer and forgot to say the Takbir, so he began with the recitation. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it while he is still standing and before he bows, then let him say the Takbir. But if he has already bowed, then let him continue with his prayer."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَامَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ فَبَدَأَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ ذَكَرَهَا وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ فَلْيُكَبِّرْ وَ إِنْ رَكَعَ فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ» فهذا الخبر ايضا مثل الاولين لان تقدير الكلام في الخبر إن ذكرها وهو قائم قبل أن يركع فليكبر وإن ركع من غير أن يذكر فليمض في صلاته وليس في الخبر انه إذا ركع وهو ذاكر انه لم يكبر فليمض في صلاته وإذا احتمل ما قلناه لم يناف ما قدمناه
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah ibn Mihran from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who stood in prayer and forgot to say the Takbir, so he began with the recitation. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers it while he is still standing and before he bows, then let him say the Takbir. But if he has already bowed, then let him continue with his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 154

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’i ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
(Imams (a.s) said) "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made bowing and prostration obligatory, and the recitation is Sunnah. So whoever leaves the recitation deliberately must repeat the prayer, but whoever forgets the recitation, his prayer is valid, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَرَضَ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ وَ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ سُنَّةٌ فَمَنْ تَرَكَ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ مُتَعَمِّداً أَعَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ مَنْ نَسِيَ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’i ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imams (a.s) said) "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made bowing and prostration obligatory, and the recitation is Sunnah. So whoever leaves the recitation deliberately must repeat the prayer, but whoever forgets the recitation, his prayer is valid, and there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 155

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "I performed the obligatory prayer but forgot to recite anything in my entire prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "Did you not complete the bowing and the prostration?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then your prayer is complete, if it was out of forgetfulness."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي صَلَّيْتُ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ فَنَسِيتُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَتِي كُلِّهَا فَقَالَ« أَ لَيْسَ قَدْ أَتْمَمْتَ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ» قُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ« فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُكَ إِذَا كَانَ نِسْيَاناً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "I performed the obligatory prayer but forgot to recite anything in my entire prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "Did you not complete the bowing and the prostration?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then your prayer is complete, if it was out of forgetfulness."

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa and Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked: "A man forgets the recitation in the first two rak’ahs, and then remembers during the last two that he did not recite." Imam (a.s) said: "Did he complete the bowing and the prostration?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "I dislike to make the end of my prayer the beginning of it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَسْهُو عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ فَيَذْكُرُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْرَأْ قَالَ« أَتَمَّ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« إِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَجْعَلَ آخِرَ صَلاَتِي أَوَّلَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa and Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked: "A man forgets the recitation in the first two rak’ahs, and then remembers during the last two that he did not recite." Imam (a.s) said: "Did he complete the bowing and the prostration?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "I dislike to make the end of my prayer the beginning of it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 155

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir, who said:
(It was said) "If one forgets to recite in the first and second rak’ahs, the glorification in the bowing and prostration suffices him. And if it is the dawn (Fajr) prayer and he forgets to recite in it, then let him continue with his prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ:« إِذَا نَسِيَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلثَّانِيَةِ أَجْزَأَهُ تَسْبِيحُ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اَلْغَدَاةُ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِيهَا فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (It was said) "If one forgets to recite in the first and second rak’ahs, the glorification in the bowing and prostration suffices him. And if it is the dawn (Fajr) prayer and he forgets to recite in it, then let him continue with his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 155

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no prayer for him unless he recites it, whether aloud or silently."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَقْرَأُ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« لاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخْفَاتٍ
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no prayer for him unless he recites it, whether aloud or silently."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 156

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who stands in prayer and forgets Surat al-Fatihah. Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say: ‘I seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the accursed Shaytan. Indeed, Allah (swt) is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,’ then let him recite it as long as he has not bowed. For there is no (valid) recitation until he begins with it, whether aloud or silently. But if he has bowed, it suffices him, if Allah (swt), the Exalted, wills."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيَنْسَى فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ قَالَ« فَلْيَقُلْ أَسْتَعِيذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلشَّيْطَانِ اَلرَّجِيمِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ« هُوَ اَلسَّمِيعُ اَلْعَلِيمُ» ثُمَّ لْيَقْرَأْهَا مَادَامَ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ قِرَاءَةَ حَتَّى يَبْدَأَ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخْفَاتٍ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا رَكَعَ أَجْزَأَهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who stands in prayer and forgets Surat al-Fatihah. Imam (a.s) said: "Let him say: ‘I seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the accursed Shaytan. Indeed, Allah (swt) is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,’ then let him recite it as long as he has not bowed. For there is no (valid) recitation until he begins with it, whether aloud or silently. But if he has bowed, it suffices him, if Allah (swt), the Exalted, wills."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 156

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt) has made bowing and prostration obligatory in the prayer. Do you not see that if a man enters Islam and does not know how to recite the Qur’an, it suffices him to say the Takbir, to glorify (Allah (swt)), and to pray?"
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ فَرَضَ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ أَ لاَ تَرَى لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً دَخَلَ فِي اَلْإِسْلاَمِ لاَ يُحْسِنُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ اَلْقُرْآنَ أَجْزَأَهُ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ وَ يُسَبِّحَ وَ يُصَلِّيَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt) has made bowing and prostration obligatory in the prayer. Do you not see that if a man enters Islam and does not know how to recite the Qur’an, it suffices him to say the Takbir, to glorify (Allah (swt)), and to pray?"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 156

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no prayer for him unless he begins with it, whether aloud or silently." I said: "Which of the two do you prefer: if he is fearful or in a hurry, should he recite a (different) Surah or Surat al-Fatihah?" Imam (a.s) said: "Surat al-Fatihah."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَقْرَأُ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« لاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَبْدَأَ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخْفَاتٍ» قُلْتُ أَيُّهُمَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَ خَائِفاً أَوْ مُسْتَعْجِلاً يَقْرَأُ بِسُورَةٍ أَوْ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ قَالَ« بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no prayer for him unless he begins with it, whether aloud or silently." I said: "Which of the two do you prefer: if he is fearful or in a hurry, should he recite a (different) Surah or Surat al-Fatihah?" Imam (a.s) said: "Surat al-Fatihah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 156

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "A man recites aloud in a place where he should not recite aloud, and recites silently where he should not recite silently, or he omits recitation where recitation is required, or he recites where recitation is not required." Imam (a.s) said: "If he did any of that out of forgetfulness or inattentiveness, then there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ جَهَرَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيمَا لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلْجَهْرُ فِيهِ وَأَخْفَى فِيمَا لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلْإِخْفَاتُ فِيهِ وَ تَرَكَ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ فِيمَا يَنْبَغِي اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهِ أَوْ قَرَأَ فِيمَا لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« أَيَّ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَ نَاسِياً أَوْ سَاهِياً فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "A man recites aloud in a place where he should not recite aloud, and recites silently where he should not recite silently, or he omits recitation where recitation is required, or he recites where recitation is not required." Imam (a.s) said: "If he did any of that out of forgetfulness or inattentiveness, then there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 157

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu al-Jawzaʾ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid:
Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: “I performed the Maghrib prayer with my father (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)), peace be upon him, and He (a.s) forgot Surat al-Fatihah in the first rak’ah, so He (a.s) recited it in the second.”
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَنَسِيَ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فَقَرَأَهَا فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu al-Jawzaʾ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: “I performed the Maghrib prayer with my father (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)), peace be upon him, and He (a.s) forgot Surat al-Fatihah in the first rak’ah, so He (a.s) recited it in the second.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 157

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "I forget the recitation in the first rak’ah." Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the second." I said: "I forget in the second." Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the third." I said: "I forget in my entire prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "If you have maintained the bowing and the prostration, then your prayer is complete."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَسْهُو عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى قَالَ« اِقْرَأْ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ» قُلْتُ أَسْهُو فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ قَالَ «اِقْرَأْ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ» قُلْتُ أَسْهُو فِي صَلاَتِي كُلِّهَا قَالَ« إِذَا حَفِظْتَ اَلرُّكُوعَ وَ اَلسُّجُودَ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُكَ» قوله عليه السلام إذا فاتك في الاولى فاقرأ في الثانية لم يرد أن يعيد قراءة ما قد فاته في الاوله وإنما أراد أن يقرأ في الثانية والثالثة ما يخصهما من القراءة فأما الاولة فقد مضى حكمها
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "I forget the recitation in the first rak’ah." Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the second." I said: "I forget in the second." Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the third." I said: "I forget in my entire prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "If you have maintained the bowing and the prostration, then your prayer is complete."

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If a man is certain that he has left out a rak’ah from the prayer, and he has already performed two prostrations but omitted the bowing, then he must begin the prayer anew."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَيْقَنَ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنَّهُ تَرَكَ رَكْعَةً مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ تَرَكَ اَلرُّكُوعَ اِسْتَأْنَفَ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If a man is certain that he has left out a rak’ah from the prayer, and he has already performed two prostrations but omitted the bowing, then he must begin the prayer anew."
