chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets to recite the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw) in which he recites the tashahhud."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَتَشَهَّدَ قَالَ «يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ يَتَشَهَّدُ فِيهِمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets to recite the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw) in which he recites the tashahhud."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 168

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who errs in prayer and forgets the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: "He should return and recite the tashahhud." I asked: “Should he perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, there are no prostrations of forgetfulness in this case."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْهُو فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيَنْسَى اَلتَّشَهُّدَ فَقَالَ «يَرْجِعُ فَيَتَشَهَّدُ» قُلْتُ أَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ فَقَالَ« لاَ لَيْسَ فِي هَذَا سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ» ف أ
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who errs in prayer and forgets the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: "He should return and recite the tashahhud." I asked: “Should he perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, there are no prostrations of forgetfulness in this case."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 168

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit until he bows in the third (rak‘ah). Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer, then give the salam, and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw) while he is seated, before he speaks."
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان بن يحيى عن الحسين بن أبي العلا قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن الرجل يصلي ركعتين من المكتوبة فلا يجلس حتى يركع الثالثة فقال يتم صلاته ثم يسلم ويسجد سجدتي السهو وهو جالس قبل أن يتكلم
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit until he bows in the third (rak‘ah). Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer, then give the salam, and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw) while he is seated, before he speaks."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 169

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit in them. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers while he is standing in the third (rak‘ah), let him sit. But if he does not remember until he bows, then let him complete his prayer, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw) while he is seated, before he speaks."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَلاَ يَجْلِسُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ ذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ فَلْيَجْلِسْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit in them. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers while he is standing in the third (rak‘ah), let him sit. But if he does not remember until he bows, then let him complete his prayer, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw) while he is seated, before he speaks."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 169

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, from Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Part of the completion of fasting is the giving of zakat, just as sending blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is part of the completion of prayer. And whoever fasts but does not give it (zakat), his fast is not accepted if he deliberately leaves it. And whoever prays but does not send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and deliberately leaves that out, then he has no prayer. Indeed, Allah (swt) the Exalted began with it before the prayer, as He (swt) said: ‘Indeed successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and then prays.’" (Surah A'la 87:14 -15)
arabicText: اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مِنْ تَمَامِ اَلصَّوْمِ إِعْطَاءُ اَلزَّكَاةِ كَالصَّلاَةِ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ مِنْ تَمَامِ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ مَنْ صَامَ وَ لَمْ يُؤَدِّهَا فَلاَ صَوْمَ لَهُ إِذَا تَرَكَهَا مُتَعَمِّداً وَ مَنْ صَلَّى وَ لَمْ يُصَلِّ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ تَرَكَ ذَلِكَ مُتَعَمِّداً فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى بَدَأَ بِهَا قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّٰى` وَ ذَكَرَ اِسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلّٰى»
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Part of the completion of fasting is the giving of zakat, just as sending blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is part of the completion of prayer. And whoever fasts but does not give it (zakat), his fast is not accepted if he deliberately leaves it. And whoever prays but does not send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and deliberately leaves that out, then he has no prayer. Indeed, Allah (swt) the Exalted began with it before the prayer, as He (swt) said: ‘Indeed successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and then prays.’" (Surah A'la 87:14 -15)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 169

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man forgets to say the salam, then when he turns his face away from the qiblah and says ‘al-salamu ‘alayna wa ‘ala ‘ibadillah al-salihin’, he has completed his prayer."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا نَسِيَ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ فَإِذَا وَلَّى وَجْهَهُ عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ قَالَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ فَقَدْ فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man forgets to say the salam, then when he turns his face away from the qiblah and says ‘al-salamu ‘alayna wa ‘ala ‘ibadillah al-salihin’, he has completed his prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 170

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If one forgets to say the salam behind the imam, the salam of the imam suffices for him."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا نَسِيَ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَجْزَأَهُ تَسْلِيمُ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If one forgets to say the salam behind the imam, the salam of the imam suffices for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 170

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah ibn A‘yan, who said:
We asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ until he bows. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘qunut’ after the bowing, and if he does not remember, then there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَزُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ قَالاَ: سَأَلْنَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى اَلْقُنُوتَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ قَالَ« يَقْنُتُ بَعْدَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah ibn A‘yan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ until he bows. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘qunut’ after the bowing, and if he does not remember, then there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 170

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘qunut’, if a man forgets it. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘qunut’ after he bows, and if he does not remember until after he finishes the prayer, then there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ يَنْسَاهُ اَلرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ« يَقْنُتُ بَعْدَمَا يَرْكَعُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘qunut’, if a man forgets it. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘qunut’ after he bows, and if he does not remember until after he finishes the prayer, then there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 171

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man remembers that he did not perform the ‘qunut’ until after he bowed.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should perform the ‘qunut’ when he raises his head."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْنُتْ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ قَالَ فَقَالَ« يَقْنُتُ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man remembers that he did not perform the ‘qunut’ until after he bowed.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should perform the ‘qunut’ when he raises his head."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 171

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard it mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who forgets the ‘qunut’, he should perform the ‘qunut’ after he finishes (the prayer), while he is seated."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ يُذْكَرُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ «فِي اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا سَهَا فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ قَنَتَ بَعْدَمَا يَنْصَرِفُ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard it mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who forgets the ‘qunut’, he should perform the ‘qunut’ after he finishes (the prayer), while he is seated."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 171

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Yasa‘, from his father, who said:
I asked Abul Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ in the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no redoing (the prayer) upon him."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلِ بْنِ يَسَعَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ اَلْقُنُوتَ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ قَالَ« لاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Yasa‘, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abul Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ in the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no redoing (the prayer) upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 171

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ until he bows, should he perform the ‘qunut’? Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى اَلْقُنُوتَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ أَ يَقْنُتُ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgets the ‘qunut’ until he bows, should he perform the ‘qunut’? Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 171

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from him, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ in the Fajr prayer: "If you wish, then perform the ‘qunut’, and if you wish, then do not perform it." And Imam (a.s) said: "When there is ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation), then do not perform the ‘qunut’, and I personally adopt this."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْهُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْنُتْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَلاَ تَقْنُتْ وَ قَالَ« هُوَ إِذَا كَانَ تَقِيَّةً فَلاَ تَقْنُتْ وَ أَنَا أَتَقَلَّدُ هَذَا» وقد استوفينا القنوت وما يتعلق باحكامه فيما مضى مستوفى وفيه غنى ان شاء الله تعالى
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ in the Fajr prayer: "If you wish, then perform the ‘qunut’, and if you wish, then do not perform it." And Imam (a.s) said: "When there is ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation), then do not perform the ‘qunut’, and I personally adopt this."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 172

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hariz narrated from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who recites aloud in what should not be recited aloud, or recites silently in what should not be recited silently. Imam (a.s) said: "Whichever of these he does deliberately, he has invalidated his prayer and must repeat it. But if he did it forgetfully, out of inattentiveness, or not knowing, then there is nothing upon him, and his prayer is complete."
arabicText: رَوَى حَرِيزٌ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ جَهَرَ فِيمَا لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلْإِجْهَارُ فِيهِ أَوْ أَخْفَى فِيمَا لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلْإِخْفَاءُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« أَيَّ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَ مُتَعَمِّداً فَقَدْ نَقَضَ صَلاَتَهُ وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ وَ إِنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ نَاسِياً أَوْ سَاهِياً أَوْلاَ يَدْرِي فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Hariz narrated from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who recites aloud in what should not be recited aloud, or recites silently in what should not be recited silently. Imam (a.s) said: "Whichever of these he does deliberately, he has invalidated his prayer and must repeat it. But if he did it forgetfully, out of inattentiveness, or not knowing, then there is nothing upon him, and his prayer is complete."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 172

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is praying one of the obligatory prayers in which the recitation is normally to be done aloud, is it required of him not to recite aloud? Imam (a.s) said: "If he wishes, he may recite aloud, and if he wishes, he may refrain from doing so."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ مَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لاَ يَجْهَرَ قَالَ« إِنْ شَاءَ جَهَرَ وَإِنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ» فهذا الخبر موافق للعامة لانهم الذين بخيرون في ذلك والذي نعمل عليه ما قدمناه
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is praying one of the obligatory prayers in which the recitation is normally to be done aloud, is it required of him not to recite aloud? Imam (a.s) said: "If he wishes, he may recite aloud, and if he wishes, he may refrain from doing so."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 172

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, by Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Make up what you have missed of the day prayer during the day, and what you have missed of the night prayer during the night." I said: “Should I make up two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, always make up ‘witr’."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اِقْضِ مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِاللَّيْلِ» قُلْتُ أَقْضِي وَتْرَيْنِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ اِقْضِ وَتْراً أَبَداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, by Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Make up what you have missed of the day prayer during the day, and what you have missed of the night prayer during the night." I said: “Should I make up two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, always make up ‘witr’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 173

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isma’il al-Ju’fi, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The best way to make up the recommended prayers (‘nawafil’) is to make up the night prayer during the night, and the day prayer during the day." I said: “So there would be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "No." I said: “Then why do you command me to perform two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "One of them is a make-up."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَفْضَلُ قَضَاءِ اَلنَّوَافِلِ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَصَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ بِالنَّهَارِ» قُلْتُ فَيَكُونُ وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ قَالَ« لاَ» قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ تَأْمُرُنِي أَنْ أُوتِرَ وَتْرَيْنِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَحَدُهُمَا قَضَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isma’il al-Ju’fi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "The best way to make up the recommended prayers (‘nawafil’) is to make up the night prayer during the night, and the day prayer during the day." I said: “So there would be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "No." I said: “Then why do you command me to perform two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "One of them is a make-up."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 173

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about a man who misses a day prayer, when should he make it up? Imam (a.s) said: "Whenever he wishes, if he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after ‘Ishaʾ."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ فَاتَتْهُ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ مَتَى يَقْضِيهَا قَالَ« مَتَى مَا شَاءَ إِنْ شَاءَ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about a man who misses a day prayer, when should he make it up? Imam (a.s) said: "Whenever he wishes, if he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after ‘Ishaʾ."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 173

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who misses a day prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He may make it up, if he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after Isha."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ تَفُوتُهُ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ قَالَ« يَقْضِيهَا إِنْ شَاءَ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who misses a day prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He may make it up, if he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after Isha."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you have the strength, then make up the day prayer during the night."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «إِنْ قَوِيتَ فَاقْضِ صَلاَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you have the strength, then make up the day prayer during the night."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Hammad, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you miss anything from the recommended prayers of the day or night, then make it up at the time of the sun’s zenith, after Dhuhr, at ‘Asr, after Maghrib, after ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ), and at the end of the night before dawn (sahar)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ:« إِنْ فَاتَكَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ تَطَوُّعِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ اَللَّيْلِ فَاقْضِهِ عِنْدَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ عِنْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ وَ مِنْ آخِرِ اَلسَّحَرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Hammad, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you miss anything from the recommended prayers of the day or night, then make it up at the time of the sun’s zenith, after Dhuhr, at ‘Asr, after Maghrib, after ‘Atamah (‘Ishaʾ), and at the end of the night before dawn (sahar)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "The best way to make up the recommended prayers (‘nawafil’) is to perform the night prayer during the night and the day prayer during the day." I said: “Will there be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "No." I said: “Then why do you command me to perform two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "One of them is a make-up."
arabicText: وعنه عن الحسن عن فضالة عن أبان عن إسماعيل الجعفي قال قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام أفضل قضاء النوافل صلاة الليل بالليل وصلاة النهار بالنهار قلت ويكون وتران في ليلة؟ قال لا قلت ولم تأمرني ان اوتر وترين في ليلة؟ فقال أحدهما قضاء
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "The best way to make up the recommended prayers (‘nawafil’) is to perform the night prayer during the night and the day prayer during the day." I said: “Will there be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "No." I said: “Then why do you command me to perform two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "One of them is a make-up."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, (Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), whenever He (a.s) missed something from the night (prayers), He (a.s) would make it up during the day. And if He (a.s) missed something from the day, He (a.s) would make it up the next day, or on Friday, or within the month. And when many such things accumulated upon Him, He (a.s) would make them up during Sha’ban, so that the complete year’s deeds would be complete for him."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ:« إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ إِذَا فَاتَهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ قَضَاهُ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ إِنْ فَاتَهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلْيَوْمِ قَضَاهُ مِنَ اَلْغَدِ أَوْ فِي اَلْجُمْعَةِ أَوْ فِي اَلشَّهْرِ وَ كَانَ إِذَا اِجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْأَشْيَاءُ قَضَاهَا فِي شَعْبَانَ حَتَّى يَكْمُلَ لَهُ عَمَلُ اَلسَّنَةِ كُلِّهَا كَامِلَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Indeed, (Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), whenever He (a.s) missed something from the night (prayers), He (a.s) would make it up during the day. And if He (a.s) missed something from the day, He (a.s) would make it up the next day, or on Friday, or within the month. And when many such things accumulated upon Him, He (a.s) would make them up during Sha’ban, so that the complete year’s deeds would be complete for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about making up the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’). Imam (a.s) said: "Make it up at the same time in which you used to perform it." I asked: “Will there be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "It is not considered two ‘witrs’ in one night, one of them is for what you missed."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَضَاءِ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ «اِقْضِهَا فِي وَقْتِهَا اَلَّذِي صَلَّيْتَ فِيهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ يَكُونُ وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ قَالَ« لَيْسَ هُوَ وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ أَحَدُهُمَا لِمَا فَاتَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s) about making up the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’). Imam (a.s) said: "Make it up at the same time in which you used to perform it." I asked: “Will there be two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "It is not considered two ‘witrs’ in one night, one of them is for what you missed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 174

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "Indeed, the servant stands and makes up the ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer), and the Lord (azj) causes His (swt) angels to marvel at him. He (AZJ) says: 'My angels, My servant is making up what I (azj) did not make obligatory upon him.'"
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ اَلْعَبْدَ يَقُومُ فَيَقْضِي اَلنَّافِلَةَ فَيُعَجِّبُ اَلرَّبُّ مَلاَئِكَتَهُ مِنْهُ فَيَقُولُ« مَلاَئِكَتِي عَبْدِي يَقْضِي مَا لَمْ أَفْتَرِضْهُ عَلَيْهِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "Indeed, the servant stands and makes up the ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer), and the Lord (azj) causes His (swt) angels to marvel at him. He (AZJ) says: 'My angels, My servant is making up what I (azj) did not make obligatory upon him.'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Fadalah from Aban, both from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about making up ‘witr’ after Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: "Make it up as ‘witr’, always, just as you missed it." I asked: “Two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, is not one of them a make-up?"
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَضَاءِ اَلْوَتْرِ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ فَقَالَ« اِقْضِهِ وَتْراً أَبَداً كَمَا فَاتَكَ» قُلْتُ وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ أَ لَيْسَ إِنَّمَا أَحَدُهُمَا قَضَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Fadalah from Aban, both from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about making up ‘witr’ after Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: "Make it up as ‘witr’, always, just as you missed it." I asked: “Two ‘witr’ prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, is not one of them a make-up?"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Nu’man, and Muhammad ibn Sinan, and Fadalah from al-Husayn, all from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the making up of ‘witr’. Imam (a.s) said: "Always make it up as ‘witr’."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ وَفَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَضَاءِ اَلْوَتْرِ قَالَ« اِقْضِهِ وَتْراً أَبَداً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Nu’man, and Muhammad ibn Sinan, and Fadalah from al-Husayn, all from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding the making up of ‘witr’. Imam (a.s) said: "Always make it up as ‘witr’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about ‘witr’ that a man misses. Imam (a.s) said: "He should always make it up as ‘witr’."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ يَفُوتُ اَلرَّجُلَ قَالَ« يَقْضِي وَتْراً أَبَداً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘witr’ that a man misses. Imam (a.s) said: "He should always make it up as ‘witr’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:
I asked Aba Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who misses the ‘witr’ prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should always make it up as ‘witr’."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَفُوتُهُ اَلْوَتْرُ قَالَ« يَقْضِيهِ وَتْراً أَبَداً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who misses the ‘witr’ prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should always make it up as ‘witr’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked (Imam (a.s)): “I reach the night without having performed the ‘witr’, how should I make it up?” Imam (a.s) said: "Like for like."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أُصْبِحُ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ إِلَى اَللَّيْلِ كَيْفَ أَقْضِي قَالَ« مِثْلاً بِمِثْلٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam (a.s)): “I reach the night without having performed the ‘witr’, how should I make it up?” Imam (a.s) said: "Like for like."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 175

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from al-Fudayl, who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: "You make it up during the day as ‘witr’ as long as the sun has not passed its zenith (before Dhuhr). But once the sun has passed its zenith, then it is (made up) as pairs, two by two."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« تَقْضِيهِ مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ مَا لَمْ تَزُلِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَتْراً فَإِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَمَثْنَى مَثْنَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from al-Fudayl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: "You make it up during the day as ‘witr’ as long as the sun has not passed its zenith (before Dhuhr). But once the sun has passed its zenith, then it is (made up) as pairs, two by two."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama’ah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "‘Witr’ is (prayed as) three rak’ahs until the sun passes its zenith (zawal), but once it has passed, then it is (prayed as) four rak’ahs."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْوَتْرُ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ إِلَى زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَإِذَا زَالَتْ فَأَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama’ah, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "‘Witr’ is (prayed as) three rak’ahs until the sun passes its zenith (zawal), but once it has passed, then it is (prayed as) four rak’ahs."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdaywayh al-Hamdani, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about making up the ‘witr’ prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever is after the sun’s zenith (‘zawal’) is to be prayed as ‘shaf’, two rak’ahs by two rak’ahs."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ كُرْدَوَيْهِ اَلْهَمْدَانِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَضَاءِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« مَا كَانَ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ فَهُوَ شَفْعٌ رَكْعَتَيْنِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdaywayh al-Hamdani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about making up the ‘witr’ prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever is after the sun’s zenith (‘zawal’) is to be prayed as ‘shaf’, two rak’ahs by two rak’ahs."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who feels lazy or weak and prays the recommended (‘nafl’) prayer while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "He should double, two rak’ahs in place of one."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَكْسَلُ أَوْ يَضْعُفُ فَيُصَلِّي اَلتَّطَوُّعَ جَالِساً قَالَ« يُضَعِّفُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِرَكْعَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who feels lazy or weak and prays the recommended (‘nafl’) prayer while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "He should double, two rak’ahs in place of one."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: "If a man prays while sitting and he is able to stand, then let him double (the prayer)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :«إِذَا صَلَّى اَلرَّجُلُ جَالِساً وَ هُوَ يَسْتَطِيعُ اَلْقِيَامَ فَلْيُضَعِّفْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: "If a man prays while sitting and he is able to stand, then let him double (the prayer)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who misses the ‘witr’ prayer at night. Imam (a.s) said: "He should make it up as ‘witr’ whenever he remembers, even if the sun has passed its zenith."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَفُوتُهُ اَلْوَتْرُ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« يَقْضِيهِ وَتْراً مَتَى مَا ذَكَرَ وَ إِنْ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who misses the ‘witr’ prayer at night. Imam (a.s) said: "He should make it up as ‘witr’ whenever he remembers, even if the sun has passed its zenith."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 176

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
(It was said) "If you miss your ‘witr’ from the night, then whenever you make it up the next day before the sun’s zenith, you make it up as ‘witr’. And whenever you make it up at night, you make it up as ‘witr’. But whenever you make it up during the day after that (after that day), you make it up as ‘shaf’, you add to it another rak’ah so that it becomes even." I asked: “Why is it made ‘shaf’?” Imam (a.s) said: "As a punishment for neglecting the ‘witr’."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ:« إِذَا فَاتَكَ وَتْرُكَ مِنْ لَيْلَتِكَ فَمَتَى مَا قَضَيْتَهُ مِنَ اَلْغَدِ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ قَضَيْتَهُ وَتْراً وَ مَتَى مَا قَضَيْتَهُ لَيْلاً قَضَيْتَهُ وَتْراً وَ مَتَى مَا قَضَيْتَهُ نَهَاراً بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ قَضَيْتَهُ شَفْعاً تُضِيفُ إِلَيْهِ أُخْرَى حَتَّى تَكُونَ شَفْعاً» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ جُعِلَ اَلشَّفْعَ قَالَ« عُقُوبَةً لِتَضْيِيعِهِ اَلْوَتْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (It was said) "If you miss your ‘witr’ from the night, then whenever you make it up the next day before the sun’s zenith, you make it up as ‘witr’. And whenever you make it up at night, you make it up as ‘witr’. But whenever you make it up during the day after that (after that day), you make it up as ‘shaf’, you add to it another rak’ah so that it becomes even." I asked: “Why is it made ‘shaf’?” Imam (a.s) said: "As a punishment for neglecting the ‘witr’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 177

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sa’d ibn Isma’il, from his father Isma’il ibn ‘Isa, who said:
I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays the Dhuhr prayer, then begins his ‘nafilah’, and the time for ‘Asr comes upon him before he finishes his ‘nafilah’. So he delays the ‘Asr prayer and then makes up his ‘nafilah’ after ‘Asr, or delays the ‘nafilah’ until he performs it in another time. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘Asr prayer and make up his ‘nafilah’ on another day."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى ثُمَّ يَتَنَفَّلُ فَيُدْرِكُهُ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ مِنَ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ مِنْ نَافِلَتِهِ فَيُبْطِئُ بِالْعَصْرِ ثُمَّ يَقْضِي نَافِلَتَهُ بَعْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ أَوْ يُؤَخِّرُهَا حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَهَا فِي وَقْتٍ آخَرَ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ وَ يَقْضِي نَافِلَتَهُ فِي يَوْمٍ آخَرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sa’d ibn Isma’il, from his father Isma’il ibn ‘Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays the Dhuhr prayer, then begins his ‘nafilah’, and the time for ‘Asr comes upon him before he finishes his ‘nafilah’. So he delays the ‘Asr prayer and then makes up his ‘nafilah’ after ‘Asr, or delays the ‘nafilah’ until he performs it in another time. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the ‘Asr prayer and make up his ‘nafilah’ on another day."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 177

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from Abi Bakr:
(Imam) Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When the time of an obligatory prayer enters, there is no (valid) supererogatory (‘tatawwu’) prayer (to be performed)."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةٍ مَفْرُوضَةٍ فَلاَ تَطَوُّعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from Abi Bakr:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When the time of an obligatory prayer enters, there is no (valid) supererogatory (‘tatawwu’) prayer (to be performed)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 177

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Tatari, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
(Imam) Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “A man from the people of Madinah said to me, ‘O Aba Ja’far, why do I not see you performing supererogatory (‘tatawwu’) prayers between the adhan and the iqamah as the people do?’” He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said: "So I replied, 'When we want to perform supererogatory prayers, we do so outside the time of the obligatory prayer. Once the time of the obligatory prayer enters, there is no supererogatory prayer (to be performed).'"
arabicText: اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« قَالَ لِي رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْمَدِينَةِ يَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ مَا لِي لاَ أَرَاكَ تَطَوَّعُ بَيْنَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ كَمَا يَصْنَعُ اَلنَّاسُ» قَالَ« فَقُلْتُ إِنَّا إِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَطَوَّعَ كَانَ تَطَوُّعُنَا فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ فَإِذَا دَخَلَتِ اَلْفَرِيضَةُ فَلاَ تَطَوُّعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Tatari, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “A man from the people of Madinah said to me, ‘O Aba Ja’far, why do I not see you performing supererogatory (‘tatawwu’) prayers between the adhan and the iqamah as the people do?’” He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said: "So I replied, 'When we want to perform supererogatory prayers, we do so outside the time of the obligatory prayer. Once the time of the obligatory prayer enters, there is no supererogatory prayer (to be performed).'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 177

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, from Najiyyah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "The time of the prayer reaches me or enters while I have not yet prayed, should I begin with the ‘nafilah’ (supererogatory prayer)?" Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "No. Rather, begin with the obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), and make up the ‘nafilah’ afterward."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ نَجِيَّةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تُدْرِكُنِي اَلصَّلاَةُ أَوْ يَدْخُلُ وَقْتُهَا فَأَبْدَأُ بِالنَّافِلَةِ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ اِبْدَأْ بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ وَ اِقْضِ اَلنَّافِلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, from Najiyyah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): "The time of the prayer reaches me or enters while I have not yet prayed, should I begin with the ‘nafilah’ (supererogatory prayer)?" Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: "No. Rather, begin with the obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), and make up the ‘nafilah’ afterward."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 178

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Udim ibn al-Hurr, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "A man should not perform supererogatory (‘nafilah’) prayer once the time of an obligatory (‘faridah’) prayer has entered." And Imam (a.s) said: "When the time of an obligatory prayer enters, begin with it."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أُدَيْمِ بْنِ اَلْحُرِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ يَتَنَفَّلُ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ فَرِيضَةٍ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ« إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ فَرِيضَةٍ فَابْدَأْ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Udim ibn al-Hurr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "A man should not perform supererogatory (‘nafilah’) prayer once the time of an obligatory (‘faridah’) prayer has entered." And Imam (a.s) said: "When the time of an obligatory prayer enters, begin with it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 178

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about performing the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’) and ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night while traveling, if I fear the cold or there is an illness. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm, I do it myself."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ إِذَا تَخَوَّفْتُ اَلْبَرْدَ أَوْ كَانَتْ عِلَّةٌ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنَا أَفْعَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about performing the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’) and ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night while traveling, if I fear the cold or there is an illness. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm, I do it myself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 178

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Tatari, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ya’qub ibn Salim, from Abdullah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who fears becoming in a state of janabah during travel, or fears the cold, should he hasten to perform the night prayer and ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: اَلطَّاطَرِيُّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخَافُ اَلْجَنَابَةَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ أَوِ اَلْبَرْدَ أَ يُعَجِّلُ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Tatari, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ya’qub ibn Salim, from Abdullah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who fears becoming in a state of janabah during travel, or fears the cold, should he hasten to perform the night prayer and ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 178

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the night prayer, may I perform it at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, I do that myself. When the camel driver hastens me, I perform it in the howdah (riding carriage)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ أُصَلِّيهَا أَوَّلَ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنِّي لَأَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ فَإِذَا أَعْجَلَنِي اَلْجَمَّالُ صَلَّيْتُهَا فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the night prayer, may I perform it at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, I do that myself. When the camel driver hastens me, I perform it in the howdah (riding carriage)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 178

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you fear that you will not be able to rise at the end of the night, or if you have an illness, or are afflicted by cold, then perform your prayer and your ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ:« إِذَا خَشِيتَ أَنْ لاَ تَقُومَ آخِرَ اَللَّيْلِ أَوْ كَانَتْ بِكَ عِلَّةٌ أَوْ أَصَابَكَ بَرْدٌ فَصَلِّ صَلاَتَكَ وَ أَوْتِرْ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If you fear that you will not be able to rise at the end of the night, or if you have an illness, or are afflicted by cold, then perform your prayer and your ‘witr’ at the beginning of the night."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about prayer during the summer, in the short nights, may I pray at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: صَفْوَانُ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ لَيْثٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلصَّيْفِ فِي اَللَّيَالِي اَلْقِصَارِ أُصَلِّي فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about prayer during the summer, in the short nights, may I pray at the beginning of the night? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Muskan, from Ya’qub al-Ahmar, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about performing the night prayer at the beginning of the night. Imam (a.s) said: "Excellent is what you have seen, and excellent is what you have done." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, the youth sleeps a lot, so I command you to do this."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ اَلْأَحْمَرِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ« نِعْمَ مَا رَأَيْتَ وَ نِعْمَ مَا صَنَعْتَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّ اَلشَّابَّ يُكْثِرُ اَلنَّوْمَ فَأَنَا آمُرُكَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Muskan, from Ya’qub al-Ahmar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about performing the night prayer at the beginning of the night. Imam (a.s) said: "Excellent is what you have seen, and excellent is what you have done." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, the youth sleeps a lot, so I command you to do this."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Nadr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Sa’id, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about performing the night prayer and ‘witr’ during travel at the beginning of the night if one is unable to pray at its end. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ إِذَا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي آخِرِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Nadr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Sa’id, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about performing the night prayer and ‘witr’ during travel at the beginning of the night if one is unable to pray at its end. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from someone who narrated to him:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The sick person should pray while sitting, and if he is unable, he should pray lying on his back. He should pronounce the ‘takbir’, then recite. When he wants to perform ‘ruku’, he should close his eyes, then say the ‘tasbih’; then he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes will count as raising his head from ‘ruku’. When he wants to prostrate, he closes his eyes, then recites the ‘tasbih’, and when he has done so, he opens his eyes, the opening of his eyes will count as raising his head from ‘sujud’. Then he recites the ‘tashahhud’ and concludes the prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُصَلِّي اَلْمَرِيضُ قَاعِداً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ صَلَّى مُسْتَلْقِياً يُكَبِّرُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ اَلرُّكُوعَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتْحُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَ رَأْسِهِ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَبَّحَ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتْحُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَ رَأْسِهِ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from someone who narrated to him:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "The sick person should pray while sitting, and if he is unable, he should pray lying on his back. He should pronounce the ‘takbir’, then recite. When he wants to perform ‘ruku’, he should close his eyes, then say the ‘tasbih’; then he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes will count as raising his head from ‘ruku’. When he wants to prostrate, he closes his eyes, then recites the ‘tasbih’, and when he has done so, he opens his eyes, the opening of his eyes will count as raising his head from ‘sujud’. Then he recites the ‘tashahhud’ and concludes the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamzah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Those who remember Allah (swt) standing, and sitting’ (Surah Al ‘Imran 3:191). Imam (a.s) said: "The healthy one prays standing, and sitting refers to the sick person who prays while seated. ‘And on their sides’ refers to the one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «اَلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اَللّٰهَ قِيٰاماً وَقُعُوداً» قَالَ« اَلصَّحِيحُ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً وَقُعُوداً اَلْمَرِيضُ يُصَلِّي جَالِساً« وَعَلىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ» اَلَّذِي يَكُونُ أَضْعَفَ مِنَ اَلْمَرِيضِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي جَالِساً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamzah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) (was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Those who remember Allah (swt) standing, and sitting’ (Surah Al ‘Imran 3:191). Imam (a.s) said: "The healthy one prays standing, and sitting refers to the sick person who prays while seated. ‘And on their sides’ refers to the one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 179

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj:
That he asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the condition of the sick person who should pray sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: "A man may feel pain and discomfort, but he knows himself best. However, when he regains strength, then let him stand."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرِيضِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي قَاعِداً فَقَالَ« إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ لَيُوعَكُ وَ يَحْرَجُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا قَوِيَ فَلْيَقُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj:
thaqalaynMatn: That he asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What is the condition of the sick person who should pray sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: "A man may feel pain and discomfort, but he knows himself best. However, when he regains strength, then let him stand."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): “Do you pray the supererogatory prayers while seated?” Imam (a.s) said: "I have not performed them except while sitting since I carried this flesh and reached this age."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ تُصَلِّي اَلنَّوَافِلَ وَ أَنْتَ قَاعِدٌ فَقَالَ« مَا أُصَلِّيهَا إِلاَّ وَ أَنَا قَاعِدٌ مُنْذُ حَمَلْتُ هَذَا اَللَّحْمَ وَ بَلَغْتُ هَذَا اَلسِّنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): “Do you pray the supererogatory prayers while seated?” Imam (a.s) said: "I have not performed them except while sitting since I carried this flesh and reached this age."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “A man prays while sitting and recites a surah, then when he wishes to conclude it, he stands and bows (‘rak’ah’) at its end.” Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is considered the prayer of one who stands."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ فَيَقْرَأُ اَلسُّورَةَ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْتِمَهَا قَامَ فَرَكَعَ بِآخِرِهَا قَالَ« صَلاَتُهُ صَلاَةُ اَلْقَائِمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “A man prays while sitting and recites a surah, then when he wishes to conclude it, he stands and bows (‘rak’ah’) at its end.” Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is considered the prayer of one who stands."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "If you want to pray while sitting and have it counted for you as the prayer of one who stands, then recite while sitting. When you reach the end of the surah, stand up, complete it, and bow. That will be counted for you as the prayer of one who stands."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ وَ يُكْتَبَ لَكَ بِصَلاَةِ اَلْقَائِمِ فَاقْرَأْ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِي آخِرِ اَلسُّورَةِ فَقُمْ فَأَتِمَّهَا وَ اِرْكَعْ فَتِلْكَ تُحْسَبُ لَكَ بِصَلاَةِ اَلْقَائِمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "If you want to pray while sitting and have it counted for you as the prayer of one who stands, then recite while sitting. When you reach the end of the surah, stand up, complete it, and bow. That will be counted for you as the prayer of one who stands."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Detailed Explanation of Prayer, Including the Obligatory and Recommended, and What is Permissible and Not Permissible.
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “We commonly say that whoever prays while sitting without an excuse, his prayer counts as two rak’ahs for one, and two prostrations for one.” Imam (a.s) said: "It is not like that, it is complete for you."
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّا نَتَحَدَّثُ نَقُولُ مَنْ صَلَّى وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ كَانَتْ صَلاَتُهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بِسَجْدَةٍ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ هُوَ هَكَذَا هِيَ تَامَّةٌ لَكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “We commonly say that whoever prays while sitting without an excuse, his prayer counts as two rak’ahs for one, and two prostrations for one.” Imam (a.s) said: "It is not like that, it is complete for you."
