chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, who said: Ali bin al-Husayn and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from al-‘Ubaydi, from Yunus, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
He (a.s) was asked about a man who joined the imam (of prayer) in prayer while the imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah before him. When the imam finished the prayer, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has completely turned his face away, then he must start the prayer anew from the beginning."
arabicText: اَلْعَيَّاشِيُّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ وَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَقَدْ سَبَقَهُ بِرَكْعَةٍ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ اَلْإِمَامُ خَرَجَ مَعَ اَلنَّاسِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَةٌ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً يَجُوزُ لَهُ إِذَا لَمْ يُحَوِّلْ وَجْهَهُ عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَإِذَا حَوَّلَ وَجْهَهُ بِكُلِّيَّةٍ اِسْتَقْبَلَ اَلصَّلاَةَ اِسْتِقْبَالاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, who said: Ali bin al-Husayn and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from al-‘Ubaydi, from Yunus, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (a.s) was asked about a man who joined the imam (of prayer) in prayer while the imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah before him. When the imam finished the prayer, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has completely turned his face away, then he must start the prayer anew from the beginning."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 195

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman bin Sayabah and Abu al-‘Abbas:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and your inclination falls upon three, then build upon three. And if your inclination falls upon four, then give the taslim and depart. But if your doubt is balanced (with no inclination toward either), then depart and pray two rak‘ahs while sitting."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ وَ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ ثَلاَثاً صَلَّيْتَ أَوْ أَرْبَعاً وَ وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى اَلثَّلاَثِ فَابْنِ عَلَى اَلثَّلاَثِ وَإِنْ وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْبَعِ فَسَلِّمْ وَاِنْصَرِفْ وَإِنِ اِعْتَدَلَ وَهْمُكَ فَانْصَرِفْ وَ صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman bin Sayabah and Abu al-‘Abbas:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and your inclination falls upon three, then build upon three. And if your inclination falls upon four, then give the taslim and depart. But if your doubt is balanced (with no inclination toward either), then depart and pray two rak‘ahs while sitting."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 196

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Hadid, from Jamil, from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding someone who does not know whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and his doubt between them is equal. Imam (a.s) said: "When the doubt is equal between three and four, then he has a choice: if he wishes, he may pray one rak‘ah while standing, and if he wishes, he may pray two rak‘ahs with four prostrations."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِيمَنْ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ ثَلاَثاً صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً وَ وَهْمُهُ فِي ذَلِكَ سَوَاءٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا اِعْتَدَلَ اَلْوَهْمُ فِي اَلثَّلاَثِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Hadid, from Jamil, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding someone who does not know whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and his doubt between them is equal. Imam (a.s) said: "When the doubt is equal between three and four, then he has a choice: if he wishes, he may pray one rak‘ah while standing, and if he wishes, he may pray two rak‘ahs with four prostrations."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed and did not know whether he was in the third rak‘ah or the fourth. Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever his assumption inclines toward, if he thinks he is in the third and there is still something in his heart about the fourth, then he should conclude (the prayer) between himself and his Lord (azj), then pray two rak‘ahs in which he recites the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى فَلَمْ يَدْرِ أَ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ هُوَ أَمْ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ« فَمَا ذَهَبَ وَهْمُهُ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ رَأَى أَنَّهُ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ وَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنَ اَلرَّابِعَةِ شَيْءٌ سَلَّمَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed and did not know whether he was in the third rak‘ah or the fourth. Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever his assumption inclines toward, if he thinks he is in the third and there is still something in his heart about the fourth, then he should conclude (the prayer) between himself and his Lord (azj), then pray two rak‘ahs in which he recites the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin Abi al-‘Ala’:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If his doubt is equal between three and four, then he should give the taslim and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, while he is seated, shortening the tashahhud."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنِ اِسْتَوَى وَهْمُهُ فِي اَلثَّلاَثِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ سَلَّمَ وَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ يُقَصِّرُ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin Abi al-‘Ala’:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If his doubt is equal between three and four, then he should give the taslim and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, while he is seated, shortening the tashahhud."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and does not know whether they were two or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, perform the tashahhud, and then conclude (the prayer), and nothing is required of him."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَلاَ يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَانِ هِيَ أَوْ أَرْبَعٌ قَالَ« يُسَلِّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and does not know whether they were two or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, perform the tashahhud, and then conclude (the prayer), and nothing is required of him."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, from Hammad, from Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four rak‘ahs or two, then stand and perform two rak‘ahs, then give the taslim. Then perform two more rak‘ahs, then give the taslim, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatayn) while sitting, and then give the taslim after them."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَرْبَعاً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقُمْ وَ اِرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلِّمْ وَ اِرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلِّمْ وَاُسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ ثُمَّ تُسَلِّمُ بَعْدَهُمَا»
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, from Hammad, from Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four rak‘ahs or two, then stand and perform two rak‘ahs, then give the taslim. Then perform two more rak‘ahs, then give the taslim, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatayn) while sitting, and then give the taslim after them."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Maskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite the tashahhud and give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both of them, then recite the tashahhud and give the taslim. If he had already prayed four, then these two are (counted as) recommended prayers (nafilah), and if he had only prayed two, then these complete the four. And if he spoke (during this state), then he must perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ« يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَأَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعاً كَانَتْ هَاتَانِ نَافِلَةً وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَاتَانِ إِتْمَامَ اَلْأَرْبَعَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَكَلَّمَ فَلْيَسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Maskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite the tashahhud and give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both of them, then recite the tashahhud and give the taslim. If he had already prayed four, then these two are (counted as) recommended prayers (nafilah), and if he had only prayed two, then these complete the four. And if he spoke (during this state), then he must perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 197

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “A person does not know whether he is in the fourth rak‘ah or the second, but he is certain that he has completed two rak‘ahs.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations while standing, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha), and perform the tashahhud, and nothing is upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in the third or the fourth, and he is certain he has completed three rak‘ahs, then he should stand and add one more, and nothing is upon him. One does not nullify certainty with doubt, and one should not insert doubt into certainty, nor mix the two together. Rather, doubt is nullified by certainty, and he completes the prayer based on what is certain and builds upon it, and doubt is not to be regarded in any situation."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَنْ لَمْ يَدْرِ فِي أَرْبَعٍ هُوَ أَوْ فِي ثِنْتَيْنِ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ اَلثِّنْتَيْنِ قَالَ« رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِذَا لَمْ يَدْرِ فِي ثَلاَثٍ هُوَ أَوْ فِي أَرْبَعٍ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ اَلثَّلاَثَ قَامَ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا أُخْرَى وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لاَ يَنْقُضِ اَلْيَقِينَ بِالشَّكِّ وَ لاَ يُدْخِلِ اَلشَّكَّ فِي اَلْيَقِينِ وَ لاَ يَخْلِطْ أَحَدَهُمَا بِالْآخَرِ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يَنْقُضُ اَلشَّكَّ بِالْيَقِينِ وَ يُتِمُّ عَلَى اَلْيَقِينِ فَيَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ وَ لاَ يَعْتَدُّ بِالشَّكِّ فِي حَالٍ مِنَ اَلْحَالاَتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “A person does not know whether he is in the fourth rak‘ah or the second, but he is certain that he has completed two rak‘ahs.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations while standing, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha), and perform the tashahhud, and nothing is upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in the third or the fourth, and he is certain he has completed three rak‘ahs, then he should stand and add one more, and nothing is upon him. One does not nullify certainty with doubt, and one should not insert doubt into certainty, nor mix the two together. Rather, doubt is nullified by certainty, and he completes the prayer based on what is certain and builds upon it, and doubt is not to be regarded in any situation."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 197

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat the prayer."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَدْرِي صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ« يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 197

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed and did not know whether he had prayed two, three, or four rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should stand and pray two rak‘ahs while standing and give the taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs while sitting and give the taslim. If he had actually prayed four rak‘ahs, then the two rak‘ahs are counted as recommended (nafilah), and if not, then the four rak‘ahs are completed."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثاً أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ« فَيَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ وَ يُسَلِّمُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ جُلُوسٍ وَ يُسَلِّمُ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ كَانَتِ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ نَافِلَةً وَ إِلاَّ تَمَّتِ اَلْأَرْبَعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed and did not know whether he had prayed two, three, or four rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should stand and pray two rak‘ahs while standing and give the taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs while sitting and give the taslim. If he had actually prayed four rak‘ahs, then the two rak‘ahs are counted as recommended (nafilah), and if not, then the four rak‘ahs are completed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 198

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ali bin Isma‘il, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful and do not know whether you are in the third, or the second, or the first, or the fourth, then repeat (the prayer), and do not proceed based on doubt."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ شَكَكْتَ وَ لَمْ تَدْرِ أَ فِي ثَلاَثٍ أَنْتَ أَمْ فِي اِثْنَتَيْنِ أَمْ فِي وَاحِدَةٍ أَوْ فِي أَرْبَعٍ فَأَعِدْ وَ لاَ تَمْضِ عَلَى اَلشَّكِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ali bin Isma‘il, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful and do not know whether you are in the third, or the second, or the first, or the fourth, then repeat (the prayer), and do not proceed based on doubt."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 198

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from ‘Abbad bin Sulayman, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d, from Safwan:
Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know how many rak‘ahs you have prayed, and your assumption does not settle upon anything, then repeat the prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ كُنْتَ لاَ تَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّيْتَ وَ لَمْ يَقَعْ وَهْمُكَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ فَأَعِدِ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from ‘Abbad bin Sulayman, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d, from Safwan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know how many rak‘ahs you have prayed, and your assumption does not settle upon anything, then repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 198

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn bin Ali, from their father Ali bin Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know how many rak‘ahs he has prayed, one, or two, or three. Imam (a.s) said: “He should build upon what he is certain of, and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw), and recite a light tashahhud."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى وَاحِدَةً أَوِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ أَمْ ثَلاَثاً قَالَ« يَبْنِي عَلَى اَلْجَزْمِ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ خَفِيفاً»
thaqalaynMatn: As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn bin Ali, from their father Ali bin Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know how many rak‘ahs he has prayed, one, or two, or three. Imam (a.s) said: “He should build upon what he is certain of, and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw), and recite a light tashahhud."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 198

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah bin Hakim, from Abdillah bin al-Mughirah, from Ali bin Abi Hamzah, from a righteous man, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who doubts and does not know whether he has prayed one, two, three, or four rak‘ahs, his prayer becomes confused for him. Imam (a.s) said: "All of that?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him continue in his prayer and seek refuge with Allah (swt) from Shaytan, for soon it will leave him."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَالِحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَشُكُّ فَلاَ يَدْرِي وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى أَوِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً أَوْ أَرْبَعاً تَلْتَبِسُ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَتُهُ قَالَ« كُلُّ ذَا» قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ يَتَعَوَّذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ اَلشَّيْطَانِ فَإِنَّهُ يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ عَنْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah bin Hakim, from Abdillah bin al-Mughirah, from Ali bin Abi Hamzah, from a righteous man, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who doubts and does not know whether he has prayed one, two, three, or four rak‘ahs, his prayer becomes confused for him. Imam (a.s) said: "All of that?" I said: "Yes." Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him continue in his prayer and seek refuge with Allah (swt) from Shaytan, for soon it will leave him."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Abu Basir, who said:
We said to Him (a.s): “A man frequently doubts in his prayer to the extent that he no longer knows how much he has prayed or what remains upon him.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat (the prayer)." We asked: “But it happens to him frequently, every time he repeats, he doubts again.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should proceed with his doubt." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do not accustom the evil one (‘al-khabith’), meaning the Shaytan, from yourselves to breaking the prayer, lest you encourage him, for Shaytan is wicked and becomes accustomed to whatever he is trained with. So let one of you proceed in his assumption and not frequently invalidate the prayer, for if he does that repeatedly, the doubt will not return to him." Zurarah said: “Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Indeed, the evil one only wants to be obeyed; so when he is disobeyed, he does not return to any one of you.’"
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالاَ: قُلْنَا لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَشُكُّ كَثِيراً فِي صَلاَتِهِ حَتَّى لاَ يَدْرِيَ كَمْ صَلَّى وَ لاَ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ» قُلْنَا فَإِنَّهُ يَكْثُرُ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ كُلَّمَا أَعَادَ شَكَّ قَالَ« يَمْضِي فِي شَكِّهِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« لاَ تُعَوِّدُوا اَلْخَبِيثَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ نَقْضَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَتُطْمِعُوهُ فَإِنَّ اَلشَّيْطَانَ خَبِيثٌ مُعْتَادٌ لِمَا عُوِّدَ بِهِ فَلْيَمْضِ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي اَلْوَهْمِ وَلاَ يُكْثِرَنَّ نَقْضَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مَرَّاتٍ لَمْ يَعُدْ إِلَيْهِ اَلشَّكُّ» قَالَ زُرَارَةُ ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اَلْخَبِيثُ أَنْ يُطَاعَ فَإِذَا عُصِيَ لَمْ يَعُدْ إِلَى أَحَدِكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We said to Him (a.s): “A man frequently doubts in his prayer to the extent that he no longer knows how much he has prayed or what remains upon him.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat (the prayer)." We asked: “But it happens to him frequently, every time he repeats, he doubts again.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then he should proceed with his doubt." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do not accustom the evil one (‘al-khabith’), meaning the Shaytan, from yourselves to breaking the prayer, lest you encourage him, for Shaytan is wicked and becomes accustomed to whatever he is trained with. So let one of you proceed in his assumption and not frequently invalidate the prayer, for if he does that repeatedly, the doubt will not return to him." Zurarah said: “Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘Indeed, the evil one only wants to be obeyed; so when he is disobeyed, he does not return to any one of you.’"

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali bin Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa bin Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who stands in prayer and does not know whether he has prayed anything or not. Imam (a.s) said: "He should start over."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَلاَ يَدْرِي صَلَّى شَيْئاً أَمْ لاَ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali bin Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa bin Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who stands in prayer and does not know whether he has prayed anything or not. Imam (a.s) said: "He should start over."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal, from ‘Uqbah bin Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who prayed the Night Prayer and performed the ‘Witr’, then remembered that he had forgotten two rak‘ahs from his prayer, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should stand and pray the two rak‘ahs that he forgot at that place, then perform the ‘Witr’ again."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَوْتَرَ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ نَسِيَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ اَلَّتِي نَسِيَ مَكَانَهُ ثُمَّ يُوتِرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal, from ‘Uqbah bin Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who prayed the Night Prayer and performed the ‘Witr’, then remembered that he had forgotten two rak‘ahs from his prayer, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should stand and pray the two rak‘ahs that he forgot at that place, then perform the ‘Witr’ again."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who, in a two-rak‘ah recommended prayer (‘nafilah’), forgot and did not sit between the two rak‘ahs, and then stood and performed the ‘ruku’ in the third. Imam (a.s) said: "He should abandon that rak‘ah, sit down, recite the ‘tashahhud’, and give the ‘taslim’. Then he may begin a new prayer afterward."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَهَا فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلنَّافِلَةِ فَلَمْ يَجْلِسْ بَيْنَهُمَا حَتَّى قَامَ فَرَكَعَ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ قَالَ «يَدَعُ رَكْعَةً وَ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَأْنِفُ اَلصَّلاَةَ» بَعْدُ
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who, in a two-rak‘ah recommended prayer (‘nafilah’), forgot and did not sit between the two rak‘ahs, and then stood and performed the ‘ruku’ in the third. Imam (a.s) said: "He should abandon that rak‘ah, sit down, recite the ‘tashahhud’, and give the ‘taslim’. Then he may begin a new prayer afterward."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Mas‘ud al-‘Ayyashi said: Hamdawayh bin Nusair narrated to me, who said: Ayyub bin Nuh narrated to us, from Abdillah bin al-Mughirah, who said: Ibn Maskan informed us, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who is praying the two rak‘ahs of ‘Witr’, and he stands up and forgets the ‘tashahhud’ until he performs ‘ruku’, and then remembers while he is in ‘ruku’. Imam (a.s) said: "He should sit from his ‘ruku’, recite the ‘tashahhud’, then stand and complete (his prayer)." He (narrator) said: “I asked (Imam (a.s)) ‘Did you not say concerning the obligatory prayer, that if one remembers after performing ‘ruku’, he should continue and then perform two prostrations (of forgetfulness) after completing the prayer, and recite the ‘tashahhud’ in them?’ Imam (a.s) said: "The ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer) is not like the ‘faridah’ (obligatory prayer)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ اَلْعَيَّاشِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي حَمْدَوَيْهِ بْنُ نُصَيْرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ بْنُ نُوحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْوَتْرِ يَقُومُ فَيَنْسَى اَلتَّشَهُّدَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ فَيَذْكُرُ وَ هُوَ رَاكِعٌ قَالَ« يَجْلِسُ مِنْ رُكُوعِهِ فَيَتَشَهَّدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُتِمُّ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَ لَيْسَ قُلْتَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ إِذَا ذَكَرَ بَعْدَ مَا يَرْكَعُ مَضَى ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ مَا يَنْصَرِفُ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ اَلنَّافِلَةُ مِثْلَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Mas‘ud al-‘Ayyashi said: Hamdawayh bin Nusair narrated to me, who said: Ayyub bin Nuh narrated to us, from Abdillah bin al-Mughirah, who said: Ibn Maskan informed us, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who is praying the two rak‘ahs of ‘Witr’, and he stands up and forgets the ‘tashahhud’ until he performs ‘ruku’, and then remembers while he is in ‘ruku’. Imam (a.s) said: "He should sit from his ‘ruku’, recite the ‘tashahhud’, then stand and complete (his prayer)." He (narrator) said: “I asked (Imam (a.s)) ‘Did you not say concerning the obligatory prayer, that if one remembers after performing ‘ruku’, he should continue and then perform two prostrations (of forgetfulness) after completing the prayer, and recite the ‘tashahhud’ in them?’ Imam (a.s) said: "The ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer) is not like the ‘faridah’ (obligatory prayer)."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn bin Muhammad, from Abdillah bin ‘Amir, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Amr bin Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to recite a surah, and he begins with ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’”. Imam (a.s) said: "He may return (change to another surah) from any surah except ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun’."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيُرِيدُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ سُورَةً فَيَقْرَأُ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» فَقَالَ« يَرْجِعُ مِنْ كُلِّ سُورَةٍ إِلاَّ مِنْ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn bin Muhammad, from Abdillah bin ‘Amir, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Amr bin Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to recite a surah, and he begins with ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’”. Imam (a.s) said: "He may return (change to another surah) from any surah except ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun’."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Ibn Maskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ in the Fajr prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem. And whoever begins with a surah and then decides to switch to another surah, there is no problem, except for ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’, from which he may not switch to another, and likewise ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ قَرَأَ فِي اَلْغَدَاةِ سُورَةَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ وَ مَنِ اِفْتَتَحَ بِسُورَةٍ ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِي سُورَةٍ غَيْرِهَا فَلاَ بَأْسَ إِلاَّ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فَلاَ يَرْجِعُ مِنْهَا إِلَى غَيْرِهَا وَ كَذَلِكَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Ibn Maskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ in the Fajr prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem. And whoever begins with a surah and then decides to switch to another surah, there is no problem, except for ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’, from which he may not switch to another, and likewise ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi; and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani; and Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, all from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (said) regarding a man who, in an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), begins reciting from the middle of a surah, then forgets and begins another surah until he completes it, and then remembers before going into ‘ruku’. Imam (a.s) said: "He should go into ‘ruku’, and it does not harm him."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْكِنَانِيِّ وَأَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْمُثَنَّى اَلْحَنَّاطِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِنِصْفِ اَلسُّورَةِ ثُمَّ يَنْسَى فَيَأْخُذُ فِي أُخْرَى حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْهَا ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ قَالَ« يَرْكَعُ وَ لاَ يَضُرُّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi; and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani; and Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, all from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (said) regarding a man who, in an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), begins reciting from the middle of a surah, then forgets and begins another surah until he completes it, and then remembers before going into ‘ruku’. Imam (a.s) said: "He should go into ‘ruku’, and it does not harm him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 203

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn and Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Safwan bin Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who speaks forgetfully during the prayer and says, ‘Straighten your rows.’ Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer, then perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw)." I asked: "Are the two prostrations of forgetfulness before the ‘taslim’ or after it?" Imam (a.s) said: "After it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَكَلَّمُ نَاسِياً فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ يَقُولُ أَقِيمُوا صُفُوفَكُمْ قَالَ« يُتِمُّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ» فَقُلْتُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ قَبْلَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ هُمَا أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ «بَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn and Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Safwan bin Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who speaks forgetfully during the prayer and says, ‘Straighten your rows.’ Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer, then perform two prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw)." I asked: "Are the two prostrations of forgetfulness before the ‘taslim’ or after it?" Imam (a.s) said: "After it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 203

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who is forgetful in the first two rak‘ahs and speaks. Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, whether he spoke or did not speak, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْهُو فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَيَتَكَلَّمُ قَالَ« يُتِمُّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ تَكَلَّمَ أَوْ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who is forgetful in the first two rak‘ahs and speaks. Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, whether he spoke or did not speak, and there is nothing upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 203

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Qasim bin Burayd, from Muhammad bin Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), then gave the ‘taslim’ thinking that he had completed the prayer and spoke, then remembered that he had only prayed two rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَسَلَّمَ وَ هُوَ يَرَى أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَتَمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ تَكَلَّمَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُصَلِّ غَيْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ «يُتِمُّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Qasim bin Burayd, from Muhammad bin Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), then gave the ‘taslim’ thinking that he had completed the prayer and spoke, then remembered that he had only prayed two rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, and there is nothing upon him."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from ‘Amr bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who forgot the ‘tashahhud’ in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers that he at least said ‘Bismillah’, then his prayer is valid. But if he does not remember anything from ‘tashahhud’, he must repeat prayer." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who remembers after having stood up, spoken, and gone about his affairs, that he had only prayed two rak‘ahs in Dhuhr, ‘Asr, Isha, or Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "He builds upon his prayer and completes it, even if he had reached China, and he does not need to repeat the prayer."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ اَلتَّشَهُّدَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« إِنْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ فَقَطْ فَقَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ أَعَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ» وَ اَلرَّجُلِ يَذْكُرُ بَعْدَمَا قَامَ وَ تَكَلَّمَ وَمَضَى فِي حَوَائِجِهِ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ وَاَلْعَصْرِ وَاَلْعَتَمَةِ وَاَلْمَغْرِبِ قَالَ« يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ فَيُتِمُّهَا وَ لَوْ بَلَغَ اَلصِّينَ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from ‘Amr bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who forgot the ‘tashahhud’ in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he remembers that he at least said ‘Bismillah’, then his prayer is valid. But if he does not remember anything from ‘tashahhud’, he must repeat prayer." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who remembers after having stood up, spoken, and gone about his affairs, that he had only prayed two rak‘ahs in Dhuhr, ‘Asr, Isha, or Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "He builds upon his prayer and completes it, even if he had reached China, and he does not need to repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 204

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “A man does not know whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat (the prayer)." I asked: “A man does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three.” Imam (a.s) said: "If the doubt enters after he has already begun the third rak‘ah, then he should continue in the third, then pray the next rak‘ah (the fourth), and there is nothing upon him, and he should give the taslim."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى أَمِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ» قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ لَمْ يَدْرِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثاً قَالَ« إِنْ دَخَلَهُ اَلشَّكُّ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهِ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ مَضَى فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلْأُخْرَى وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ يُسَلِّمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “A man does not know whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat (the prayer)." I asked: “A man does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three.” Imam (a.s) said: "If the doubt enters after he has already begun the third rak‘ah, then he should continue in the third, then pray the next rak‘ah (the fourth), and there is nothing upon him, and he should give the taslim."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 204

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja‘far, from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from ‘Ubayd bin Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat (the prayer)." I asked: “Is it not said that a jurist does not repeat the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "That is only in the case of doubt between three and four (rak‘ahs)."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَمْ يَدْرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثاً قَالَ« يُعِيدُ» قُلْتُ أَ لَيْسَ يُقَالُ لاَ يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقِيهٌ فَقَالَ« إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ فِي اَلثَّلاَثِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja‘far, from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from ‘Ubayd bin Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat (the prayer)." I asked: “Is it not said that a jurist does not repeat the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "That is only in the case of doubt between three and four (rak‘ahs)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 205

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Sahl, from his father, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or two. Imam (a.s) said: "He should build upon the lesser number and act according to what he is certain of. After finishing his prayer, he should recite a light tashahhud. This is to be done both at the beginning of the prayer and at its end."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ ثَلاَثاً صَلَّى أَمِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ قَالَ« يَبْنِي عَلَى اَلنُّقْصَانِ وَ يَأْخُذُ بِالْجَزْمِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ بَعْدَ اِنْصِرَافِهِ تَشَهُّداً خَفِيفاً كَذَلِكَ فِي أَوَّلِ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ آخِرِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Sahl, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or two. Imam (a.s) said: "He should build upon the lesser number and act according to what he is certain of. After finishing his prayer, he should recite a light tashahhud. This is to be done both at the beginning of the prayer and at its end."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 205

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Khalid, from al-Hasan bin Ali, from Mu‘adh bin Muslim, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whenever doubt enters upon you in your prayer, then act according to the greater number." Imam (a.s) said: "Then, after you finish, complete what you think you may have left out."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ اَلشَّكِّ فِي صَلاَتِكَ فَاعْمَلْ عَلَى اَلْأَكْثَرِ» قَالَ« فَإِذَا اِنْصَرَفْتَ فَأَتِمَّ مَا ظَنَنْتَ أَنَّكَ نَقَصْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Khalid, from al-Hasan bin Ali, from Mu‘adh bin Muslim, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whenever doubt enters upon you in your prayer, then act according to the greater number." Imam (a.s) said: "Then, after you finish, complete what you think you may have left out."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 205

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the sons of A‘yan:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man is certain that he has added something to his obligatory prayer, then he should not count it (as valid), and he must start his prayer over from the beginning, if he has attained definite certainty."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ بُكَيْرٍ اِبْنَيْ أَعْيَنَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا اِسْتَيْقَنَ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنَّهُ زَادَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ لَمْ يَعْتَدَّ بِهَا وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ صَلاَتَهُ اِسْتِقْبَالاً إِذَا كَانَ قَدِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ يَقِيناً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the sons of A‘yan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man is certain that he has added something to his obligatory prayer, then he should not count it (as valid), and he must start his prayer over from the beginning, if he has attained definite certainty."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 206

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban bin ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever adds to his prayer, it is obligatory upon him to repeat it."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ زَادَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban bin ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever adds to his prayer, it is obligatory upon him to repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 206

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about a man who, after finishing the Dhuhr prayer, becomes certain that he had prayed five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "And how did he become certain?" I said: “He knows it (to be certain).” Imam (a.s) said: "If he knows that he had sat in the fourth rak‘ah, then his Dhuhr prayer is complete, and he should stand and add to the fifth rak‘ah another rak‘ah and two prostrations, so they will become two (extra) rak‘ahs as ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer), and nothing is upon him."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ اِسْتَيْقَنَ بَعْدَ مَا صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى خَمْساً قَالَ «وَ كَيْفَ اِسْتَيْقَنَ» قُلْتُ عَلِمَ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ جَلَسَ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ فَصَلاَةُ اَلظُّهْرِ تَامَّةٌ وَ لْيَقُمْ فَلْيُضِفْ إِلَى اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْخَامِسَةِ رَكْعَةً وَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ فَيَكُونَانِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about a man who, after finishing the Dhuhr prayer, becomes certain that he had prayed five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "And how did he become certain?" I said: “He knows it (to be certain).” Imam (a.s) said: "If he knows that he had sat in the fourth rak‘ah, then his Dhuhr prayer is complete, and he should stand and add to the fifth rak‘ah another rak‘ah and two prostrations, so they will become two (extra) rak‘ahs as ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer), and nothing is upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 206

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil bin Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "If he sat in the fourth rak‘ah for the duration of the tashahhud, then his prayer is complete."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى خَمْساً فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ جَلَسَ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قَدْرَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil bin Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "If he sat in the fourth rak‘ah for the duration of the tashahhud, then his prayer is complete."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 206

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub narrated from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus bin Abd al-Rahman, from Abdillah bin Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four or five rak‘ahs, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’) after your ‘taslim’, then give the ‘taslim’ again after them."
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ لاَ تَدْرِي أَرْبَعاً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ خَمْساً فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ بَعْدَ تَسْلِيمِكَ ثُمَّ سَلِّمْ بَعْدَهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub narrated from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus bin Abd al-Rahman, from Abdillah bin Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four or five rak‘ahs, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’) after your ‘taslim’, then give the ‘taslim’ again after them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 206

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Musa bin al-Hasan, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Abdillah bin Maymun al-Qaddah, from (Imam) Ja‘far bin Muhammad (a.s), from his father (Imam al Baqir (a.s)):
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdata al-sahw’) are to be performed after the ‘taslim’ and before speaking."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ اَلْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ بَعْدَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ وَ قَبْلَ اَلْكَلاَمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Musa bin al-Hasan, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Abdillah bin Maymun al-Qaddah, from (Imam) Ja‘far bin Muhammad (a.s), from his father (Imam al Baqir (a.s)):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdata al-sahw’) are to be performed after the ‘taslim’ and before speaking."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 207

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "In the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), if there was a deficiency (in the prayer), then they are before the ‘taslim’; and if there was an addition, then they are after it."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «فِي سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ إِذَا نَقَصْتَ قَبْلَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ وَ إِذَا زِدْتَ فَبَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "In the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), if there was a deficiency (in the prayer), then they are before the ‘taslim’; and if there was an addition, then they are after it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 207

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “When should I perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Before the ‘taslim’, for if you give the ‘taslim’, the sanctity of your prayer has ended."
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَارُودِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَتَى أَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ قَالَ« قَبْلَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا سَلَّمْتَ بَعْدُ ذَهَبَتْ حُرْمَةُ صَلاَتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “When should I perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Before the ‘taslim’, for if you give the ‘taslim’, the sanctity of your prayer has ended."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 207

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And as for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from ‘Amr bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s) (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), is there in them any ‘takbir’ (saying "Allahu Akbar") or ‘tasbih’ (glorification)? Imam (a.s) said: "No, they are only two prostrations. But if the one who erred is the imam (of prayer), then he says ‘takbir’ when he goes into prostration and when he raises his head, in order to inform those behind him that he has made an error. He is not required to say ‘tasbih’ in them, and there is no ‘tashahhud’ after the two prostrations."
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ هَلْ فِيهِمَا تَكْبِيرٌ أَوْ تَسْبِيحٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ إِنَّهُمَا سَجْدَتَانِ فَقَطْ فَإِنْ كَانَ اَلَّذِي سَهَا هُوَ اَلْإِمَامَ كَبَّرَ إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ لِيُعْلِمَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْسَهَا وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُسَبِّحَ فِيهِمَا وَ لاَ فِيهِمَا تَشَهُّدٌ بَعْدَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And as for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from ‘Amr bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s) (peace be upon him), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), is there in them any ‘takbir’ (saying "Allahu Akbar") or ‘tasbih’ (glorification)? Imam (a.s) said: "No, they are only two prostrations. But if the one who erred is the imam (of prayer), then he says ‘takbir’ when he goes into prostration and when he raises his head, in order to inform those behind him that he has made an error. He is not required to say ‘tasbih’ in them, and there is no ‘tashahhud’ after the two prostrations."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 208

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have prayed four rak‘ahs or five, or whether you have omitted or added something, then perform the tashahhud, give the salam, and perform two prostrations (‘sajdatayn’) without bowing (‘ruku’) or recitation, and in them recite a light tashahhud."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَرْبَعاً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ خَمْساً أَمْ نَقَصْتَ أَمْ زِدْتَ فَتَشَهَّدْ وَ سَلِّمْ وَ اُسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بِغَيْرِ رُكُوعٍ وَ لاَ قِرَاءَةٍ تَتَشَهَّدُ فِيهِمَا تَشَهُّداً خَفِيفاً»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have prayed four rak‘ahs or five, or whether you have omitted or added something, then perform the tashahhud, give the salam, and perform two prostrations (‘sajdatayn’) without bowing (‘ruku’) or recitation, and in them recite a light tashahhud."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abi Ja‘far, from his father, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say regarding the two prostrations of forgetfulness: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and may Allah (swt) send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and upon the family of Muhammad (saws).’ He (narrator) said: “And I heard Him (a.s) on another occasion say in them: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and peace be upon you, O Prophet (saws), and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings.’
arabicText: فَمَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: فِي سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ« بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَبِاللَّهِ وَصَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ» قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى يَقُولُ فِيهِمَا« بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abi Ja‘far, from his father, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washsha’, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: "Whoever forgets one of the prayers of his day and does not know which prayer it is, he should perform two rak’ahs, three, and four."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ نَسِيَ صَلاَةً مِنْ صَلاَةِ يَوْمِهِ وَاحِدَةً وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيُّ صَلاَةٍ هِيَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ ثَلاَثاً وَ أَرْبَعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washsha’, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: "Whoever forgets one of the prayers of his day and does not know which prayer it is, he should perform two rak’ahs, three, and four."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 209

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):, the same (narration).
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مِثْلَهُ
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):, the same (narration).
