chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, said Ali bin al-Hasan and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Mu‘awiyah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who stood to pray an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), then became confused and thought it was a recommended prayer (‘nafilah’), or he stood to pray a ‘nafilah’ and thought it was an obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is according to what he began the prayer with.”
arabicText: اَلْعَيَّاشِيُّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ وَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَامَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَسَهَا فَظَنَّ أَنَّهَا نَافِلَةٌ أَوْ قَامَ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ فَظَنَّ أَنَّهَا مَكْتُوبَةٌ قَالَ« هِيَ عَلَى مَا اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, said Ali bin al-Hasan and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Mu‘awiyah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who stood to pray an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), then became confused and thought it was a recommended prayer (‘nafilah’), or he stood to pray a ‘nafilah’ and thought it was an obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is according to what he began the prayer with.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 209

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Nusayr, who said: Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
And I asked Him (a.s) about a man who led a group in prayer for ‘Asr, then remembered while he was praying with them that he had not yet prayed Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should count it as the Dhuhr which he had missed, and begin ‘Asr anew. As for the people, they have completed their prayer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: وَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فِي اَلْعَصْرِ فَذَكَرَ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ صَلَّى اَلْأُولَى قَالَ« فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا اَلْأُولَى اَلَّتِي فَاتَتْهُ وَ اِسْتَأْنَفَ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ قَدْ قَضَى اَلْقَوْمُ صَلاَتَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad bin Nusayr, who said: Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: And I asked Him (a.s) about a man who led a group in prayer for ‘Asr, then remembered while he was praying with them that he had not yet prayed Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should count it as the Dhuhr which he had missed, and begin ‘Asr anew. As for the people, they have completed their prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 209

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ali bin Abdillah, from Abdillah bin Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), and also from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ibrahim bin Abdillah bin Sam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man has upon him such a great number of missed ‘nafilah’ prayers that he does not know what they are due to their amount, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should pray until he no longer knows how many he has prayed because of their abundance, and that way he will have fulfilled what was upon him.” I asked: “Suppose he left them and is not able to make them up due to being busy?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he was busy (occupied) in the pursuit of livelihood that is necessary, or a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if he was busy (occupied) for worldly affairs and he occupied himself with them instead of prayer, then he must make them up, otherwise he will meet Allah (swt) having shown negligence, disrespect, and disregard for Sunnah of Messenger of Allah (swt).” I asked: “If he is unable to make them up, is it acceptable for him to give charity?” He (a.s) was silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.” I asked: “And what amount of charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “According to his ability, and the minimum is a ‘mudd’.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for every poor person in place of each prayer.” I asked: “And how many prayers would require a ‘mudd’ for each?” Imam (a.s) said: “For every two rak’ahs of night prayer, and every two rak’ahs of daytime prayer.” I asked: “Suppose he is unable?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for every four rak’ahs.” I asked: “Suppose he is still unable?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for the night prayer and a ‘mudd’ for the daytime prayer. And the prayer is better, the prayer is better, the prayer is better.”
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن علي بن ابراهيم عن أبيه عن عمرو ابن عثمان عن علي بن عبد الله عن عبد الله بن سنان قال قلت لابي عبد الله ومحمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن أبى اسحاق عن عمرو بن عثمان عن ابراهيم بن عبد الله ابن سام قال قلت لابي عبد الله رجل عليه من صلاة النوافل ما لا يدري ما هو من كثرته كيف يصنع؟ قال فيصلي حتى لا يدري كم صلى من كثرته فيكون قد قضى بقدر ما عليه قلت فانه ترك ولا يقدر على القضاء من شغله قال ان كان شغله في طلب معيشة لا بد منها أو حاجة لاخ مؤمن فلا شئ عليه وان كان شغله للدنيا وتشاغل بها عن الصلاة فعليه القضاء والا لقي الله مستخفا متهاونا مضيعا لسنة رسول الله ص قلت فانه لا يقدر على القضاء فهل يصلح أن يتصدق فسكت مليا ثم قال نعم ليتصدق بصدقة قلت وما يتصدق؟ قال بقدر قوته وأدنى ذلك مد فقال مد لكل مسكين مكان كل صلاة قلت وكم الصلاة التي يجب فيها لكل مسكين مد؟ فقال لكل ركعتين من صلاة الليل وكل ركعتين من صلاة النهار فقلت لا يقدر فقال مد لكل أربع ركعات فقلت لا يقدر فقال مد لصلاة الليل ومد لصلاة النهار والصلاة أفضل والصلاة أفضل والصلاة أفضل
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ali bin Abdillah, from Abdillah bin Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), and also from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ibrahim bin Abdillah bin Sam, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “A man has upon him such a great number of missed ‘nafilah’ prayers that he does not know what they are due to their amount, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should pray until he no longer knows how many he has prayed because of their abundance, and that way he will have fulfilled what was upon him.” I asked: “Suppose he left them and is not able to make them up due to being busy?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he was busy (occupied) in the pursuit of livelihood that is necessary, or a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if he was busy (occupied) for worldly affairs and he occupied himself with them instead of prayer, then he must make them up, otherwise he will meet Allah (swt) having shown negligence, disrespect, and disregard for Sunnah of Messenger of Allah (swt).” I asked: “If he is unable to make them up, is it acceptable for him to give charity?” He (a.s) was silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.” I asked: “And what amount of charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “According to his ability, and the minimum is a ‘mudd’.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for every poor person in place of each prayer.” I asked: “And how many prayers would require a ‘mudd’ for each?” Imam (a.s) said: “For every two rak’ahs of night prayer, and every two rak’ahs of daytime prayer.” I asked: “Suppose he is unable?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for every four rak’ahs.” I asked: “Suppose he is still unable?” Imam (a.s) said: “A ‘mudd’ for the night prayer and a ‘mudd’ for the daytime prayer. And the prayer is better, the prayer is better, the prayer is better.”

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Marazim, who said:
Isma‘il bin Jabir asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), saying: "May Allah (swt) set you right, I have many missed ‘nafilah’ prayers, what should I do?" Imam (a.s) said: "Make them up (as qadha)." I asked: "They are more than that (too many)." Imam (a.s) said: "Make them up." I said: "I cannot count them." Imam (a.s) said: "Approximate (estimate)." Marazim said: I was ill for four months and did not perform ‘nafilah’ prayers during that time, so I asked (Imam (a.s): "May Allah (swt) set you right or may I be your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not perform any ‘nafilah’ prayers during that time." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no ‘qadha’ upon you. The sick is not like the healthy. Whatever overcomes one by Allah’s (swt) will, then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse him in it."
arabicText: لي بن ابراهيم عن أبيه عن ابن أبي عمير عن مرازم قال سأل إسماعيل بن جابر أبا عبد الله عليه السلام فقال اصلحك الله ان علي نوافل كثيره فكيف اصنع؟ فقال اقضها فقال له انها اكثر من ذلك قال اقضها قال لا احصيها قال توخ قال مرازم وكنت مرضت أربعة اشهر لم اتنفل فيها فقلت أصلحك الله أو جعلت فداك إني مرضت أربعة أشهر لم اصل فيها نافلة فقال ليس عليك قضاء إن المريض ليس كالصحيح كلما غلب الله عليه فالله أولى بالعذر فيه
thaqalaynSanad: Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Marazim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Isma‘il bin Jabir asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), saying: "May Allah (swt) set you right, I have many missed ‘nafilah’ prayers, what should I do?" Imam (a.s) said: "Make them up (as qadha)." I asked: "They are more than that (too many)." Imam (a.s) said: "Make them up." I said: "I cannot count them." Imam (a.s) said: "Approximate (estimate)." Marazim said: I was ill for four months and did not perform ‘nafilah’ prayers during that time, so I asked (Imam (a.s): "May Allah (swt) set you right or may I be your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not perform any ‘nafilah’ prayers during that time." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no ‘qadha’ upon you. The sick is not like the healthy. Whatever overcomes one by Allah’s (swt) will, then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse him in it."

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhayna, from Zurarah, who said:
He (Zurarah) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: ‘"Turning (the head) invalidates the prayer when it is with the whole (of the body)."‘
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «اَلاِلْتِفَاتُ يَقْطَعُ اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا كَانَ بِكُلِّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhayna, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (Zurarah) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s) say: ‘"Turning (the head) invalidates the prayer when it is with the whole (of the body)."‘

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 211

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from al-’Alaʾ, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s): "May a man turn his head during his prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, and he should not crack his fingers either."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ يَلْتَفِتُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لاَ يَنْقُضُ أَصَابِعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from al-’Alaʾ, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s): "May a man turn his head during his prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, and he should not crack his fingers either."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 212

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you face the qiblah with your face, do not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest your prayer become invalid. For indeed, Allah (swt) the Exalted said to His Prophet (saws), peace be upon him, regarding the obligatory prayer: ‘So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it’ (Surah Baqarah 2:144 & 2:150). And lower your gaze, and do not raise it to the sky, but rather let it be aligned with your face at the place of your prostration."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتَ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِوَجْهِكَ فَلاَ تَقْلِبْ وَجْهَكَ عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَتَفْسُدَ صَلاَتُكَ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى قَالَ لِنَبِيِّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ« فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرٰامِ وَ حَيْثُ مٰا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ» وَ اِخْشَعْ بَصَرَكَ وَ لاَ تَرْفَعْهُ إِلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ لَكِنْ حِذَاءَ وَجْهِكَ فِي مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you face the qiblah with your face, do not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest your prayer become invalid. For indeed, Allah (swt) the Exalted said to His Prophet (saws), peace be upon him, regarding the obligatory prayer: ‘So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it’ (Surah Baqarah 2:144 & 2:150). And lower your gaze, and do not raise it to the sky, but rather let it be aligned with your face at the place of your prostration."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 212

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who experiences nosebleed (‘ru’af’) while in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is able to find water near him, whether to his right, left, or in front of him, while still facing the qiblah, then let him wash it off and continue with the remainder of his prayer. But if he is not able to find water without turning his face away or speaking, then his prayer is invalidated."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُهُ اَلرُّعَافُ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ قَدَرَ عَلَى مَاءٍ عِنْدَهُ يَمِيناً أَوْ شِمَالاً بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَلْيَغْسِلْهُ عَنْهُ ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَاءٍ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ بِوَجْهِهِ أَوْ يَتَكَلَّمَ فَقَدْ قَطَعَ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who experiences nosebleed (‘ru’af’) while in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is able to find water near him, whether to his right, left, or in front of him, while still facing the qiblah, then let him wash it off and continue with the remainder of his prayer. But if he is not able to find water without turning his face away or speaking, then his prayer is invalidated."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 212

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d bin Abdillah, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far bin Bashir, from Hammad bin Uthman, from Abd al-Hamid, from Abd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about turning the head in prayer, does it invalidate the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "No, but I do not like it to be done."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلاِلْتِفَاتِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ أَ يَقْطَعُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يُفْعَلَ» فالمراد بهذا الخبر هو انه إذا لم يلتفت الى ورائه وإنما يلتفت يمينا وشمالا فان ذلك لا يقطع الصلاة وإن كان منقصا لها فأما إذا كان الالتفات بالكلية فانه يقطع الصلاة حسب ما قدمناه
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa’d bin Abdillah, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far bin Bashir, from Hammad bin Uthman, from Abd al-Hamid, from Abd al-Malik, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about turning the head in prayer, does it invalidate the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "No, but I do not like it to be done."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 212

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Muhammad bin al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who performed ablution but forgot to wipe over his head until he had already stood for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: ‘"Then he should leave (the prayer), wipe over his head, and repeat the prayer."‘
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْكِنَانِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَوَضَّأَ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يَمْسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ حَتَّى قَامَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ فَلْيَمْسَحْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ لْيُعِدِ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Muhammad bin al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who performed ablution but forgot to wipe over his head until he had already stood for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: ‘"Then he should leave (the prayer), wipe over his head, and repeat the prayer."‘

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 213

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Uthman, from Sama’ah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: ‘"Whoever forgets to wipe his head or his feet, or forgets any part of the ablution that Allah (swt) the Exalted has mentioned in the Qur’an, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the ablution and the prayer."‘
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ نَسِيَ مَسْحَ رَأْسِهِ أَوْ قَدَمَيْهِ أَوْ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلْوُضُوءِ اَلَّذِي ذَكَرَهُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي اَلْقُرْآنِ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ اَلْوُضُوءِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Uthman, from Sama’ah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: ‘"Whoever forgets to wipe his head or his feet, or forgets any part of the ablution that Allah (swt) the Exalted has mentioned in the Qur’an, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the ablution and the prayer."‘

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 213

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who forgot to wipe over his head and remembered while he was in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain of that, then he should leave the prayer, wipe over his head and his feet, and then start the prayer anew. But if he is uncertain and does not know whether he wiped or not, then let him take from his beard if it is moist and wipe with it over his head; and if there is water in front of him, let him take from it and wipe his head with it."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يَمْسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ فَذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ قَدِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ ذَلِكَ اِنْصَرَفَ وَ مَسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهِ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ إِنْ شَكَّ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ مَسَحَ أَوْ لَمْ يَمْسَحْ فَلْيَتَنَاوَلْ مِنْ لِحْيَتِهِ إِنْ كَانَتْ مُبْتَلَّةً وَ لْيَمْسَحْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَمَامَهُ مَاءٌ فَلْيَتَنَاوَلْ مِنْهُ فَلْيَمْسَحْ بِهِ رَأْسَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who forgot to wipe over his head and remembered while he was in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain of that, then he should leave the prayer, wipe over his head and his feet, and then start the prayer anew. But if he is uncertain and does not know whether he wiped or not, then let him take from his beard if it is moist and wipe with it over his head; and if there is water in front of him, let him take from it and wipe his head with it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 213

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik bin A’yan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Whoever forgets to wipe his head, then remembers that he did not wipe his head, if there is moisture in his beard, then let him take from it and wipe his head. But if there is no moisture in his beard, then he should leave (his prayer) and repeat the ablution."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ نَسِيَ مَسْحَ رَأْسِهِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَمْسَحْ رَأْسَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِي لِحْيَتِهِ بَلَلٌ فَلْيَأْخُذْ مِنْهُ وَ لْيَمْسَحْ رَأْسَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي لِحْيَتِهِ بَلَلٌ فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ وَ لْيُعِدِ اَلْوُضُوءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik bin A’yan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Whoever forgets to wipe his head, then remembers that he did not wipe his head, if there is moisture in his beard, then let him take from it and wipe his head. But if there is no moisture in his beard, then he should leave (his prayer) and repeat the ablution."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 213

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far bin Bashir, from Hammad bin Uthman, from ‘Ammar bin Musa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "If a man were to forget to perform istinjaʾ (cleansing) after defecation until he prayed, he does not have to repeat the prayer."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً نَسِيَ أَنْ يَسْتَنْجِيَ مِنَ اَلْغَائِطِ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ لَمْ يُعِدِ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far bin Bashir, from Hammad bin Uthman, from ‘Ammar bin Musa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "If a man were to forget to perform istinjaʾ (cleansing) after defecation until he prayed, he does not have to repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 213

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya from al-’Amraki from Ali bin Ja’far from his brother (Imam) Musa bin Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who remembered, while he was in his prayer, that he had not performed ‘istinjaʾ’ after relieving himself. Imam (a.s) said: "He should leave, perform ‘istinja’ after relieving himself, and repeat the prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَسْتَنْجِ مِنَ اَلْخَلاَءِ قَالَ« يَنْصَرِفُ وَ لْيَسْتَنْجِ مِنَ اَلْخَلاَءِ وَ يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya from al-’Amraki from Ali bin Ja’far from his brother (Imam) Musa bin Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who remembered, while he was in his prayer, that he had not performed ‘istinjaʾ’ after relieving himself. Imam (a.s) said: "He should leave, perform ‘istinja’ after relieving himself, and repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 214

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad bin Ya’qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abdillah, from Abdillah bin Jabalah, from Sayf, from Maymun al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “A man experienced janabah (ritual impurity) during the night, so he performed ghusl, and in the morning he looked and saw janabah (impurity) on his clothing.” Imam (a.s) said: "Praise be to Allah (swt), who has not left anything without assigning a rule for it. If, when he stood for prayer, he looked and did not see anything, then there is no repetition (of prayer) required of him. But if, when he stood, he did not look, then he must repeat the prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ مَيْمُونٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ فَاغْتَسَلَ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ نَظَرَ فَإِذَا فِي ثَوْبِهِ جَنَابَةٌ فَقَالَ« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي لَمْ يَدَعْ شَيْئاً إِلاَّ وَ لَهُ حَدٌّ إِنْ كَانَ حِينَ قَامَ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ نَظَرَ فَلَمْ يَرَ شَيْئاً فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ حِينَ قَامَ فَلَمْ يَنْظُرْ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad bin Ya’qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abdillah, from Abdillah bin Jabalah, from Sayf, from Maymun al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “A man experienced janabah (ritual impurity) during the night, so he performed ghusl, and in the morning he looked and saw janabah (impurity) on his clothing.” Imam (a.s) said: "Praise be to Allah (swt), who has not left anything without assigning a rule for it. If, when he stood for prayer, he looked and did not see anything, then there is no repetition (of prayer) required of him. But if, when he stood, he did not look, then he must repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 214

chapter: Chapter on Rulings on Forgetfulness (Sahw) in Prayer and What Requires Repeating of Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Wahb bin Hafs, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed while there was urine or janabah (impurity) on his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "Whether he knew of it or not, if he comes to know of it, then he must repeat the prayer."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ فِي ثَوْبِهِ بَوْلٌ أَوْ جَنَابَةٌ فَقَالَ« عَلِمَ بِهِ أَوْ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فَعَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ اَلصَّلاَةِ إِذَا عَلِمَ» قوله عليه السلام علم به أو لم يعلم يريد به في حال قيامه الى الصلاة بعد أن يكون قد تقدمه العلم بحصول النجاسة في الثوب ولم يعلم في حال قيامه الى الصلاة لسهو عرض أو نسيان ولو لم يتقدمه علم اصلا بحصول النجاسة قبل ذلك لما وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة على كل حال بدلالة الخبر الاول وإلا تناقضت الاخبار
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Wahb bin Hafs, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed while there was urine or janabah (impurity) on his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "Whether he knew of it or not, if he comes to know of it, then he must repeat the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 214

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from more than one person:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding the carcass (maytah). Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in anything from it, not even a sandal strap."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْمَيْتَةِ قَالَ «لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ وَ لاَ شِسْعٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from more than one person:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (said) regarding the carcass (maytah). Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in anything from it, not even a sandal strap."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 215

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the skin of a dead animal, can it be worn in prayer if it has been tanned? Imam (a.s) said: "No, even if it is tanned seventy times."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْجِلْدِ اَلْمَيِّتِ أَ يُلْبَسُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ إِذَا دُبِغَ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَوْ دُبِغَ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the skin of a dead animal, can it be worn in prayer if it has been tanned? Imam (a.s) said: "No, even if it is tanned seventy times."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 215

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad: the same (narration).
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ: مِثْلَهُ.
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad: the same (narration).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 216

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from ‘Aytham ibn Aslam al-Najashi, from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about praying in fur garments. Imam (a.s) said: "(Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s) was a man sensitive to cold, and the furs of the Hijaz would not keep him warm because their tanning was done with qaraz (a plant extract). So He (a.s) would send to Iraq and He (a.s) would be brought fur from your region, and He (a.s) would wear it. But when the time for prayer arrived, He (a.s) would take it off, and also take off the shirt that was in contact with it. He (a.s) was asked about that, and He (Imam Husayn (a.s)) said: 'Indeed, the people of Iraq deem it permissible to wear the skins of dead animals, and they claim that tanning it is its purification (that tanning makes it lawful).’"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلدَّيْلَمِيِّ عَنْ عَيْثَمِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ اَلنَّجَاشِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْفِرَاءِ فَقَالَ« كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلاً صَرِداً فَلاَ تُدْفِئُهُ فِرَاءُ اَلْحِجَازِ لِأَنَّ دِبَاغَهَا بِالْقَرَظِ فَكَانَ يَبْعَثُ إِلَى اَلْعِرَاقِ فَيُؤْتَى مِمَّا قِبَلَكُمْ بِالْفَرْوِ فَيَلْبَسُهُ فَإِذَا حَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ أَلْقَاهُ وَ أَلْقَى اَلْقَمِيصَ اَلَّذِي يَلِيهِ فَكَانَ يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَيَقُولُ« إِنَّ أَهْلَ اَلْعِرَاقِ يَسْتَحِلُّونَ لِبَاسَ اَلْجُلُودِ اَلْمَيْتَةِ وَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ دِبَاغَهُ ذَكَاتُهُ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from ‘Aytham ibn Aslam al-Najashi, from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about praying in fur garments. Imam (a.s) said: "(Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s) was a man sensitive to cold, and the furs of the Hijaz would not keep him warm because their tanning was done with qaraz (a plant extract). So He (a.s) would send to Iraq and He (a.s) would be brought fur from your region, and He (a.s) would wear it. But when the time for prayer arrived, He (a.s) would take it off, and also take off the shirt that was in contact with it. He (a.s) was asked about that, and He (Imam Husayn (a.s)) said: 'Indeed, the people of Iraq deem it permissible to wear the skins of dead animals, and they claim that tanning it is its purification (that tanning makes it lawful).’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 216

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
With this same chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about wearing fur garments and praying in them. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them except in what has been ritually slaughtered." I asked: "Isn’t dhakiyy what is slaughtered with iron (a blade)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if it is from that which its meat is eaten." So I asked: "What about what is not eaten from animals other than sheep?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with (wearing) squirrel (al-sinjab), for it is a creature that does not eat meat, and it is not from those things which the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, prohibited when He (saws) prohibited all animals with fangs or talons."
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ لِبَاسِ اَلْفِرَاءِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهَا إِلاَّ فِيمَا كَانَ مِنْهُ ذَكِيّاً» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَ وَ لَيْسَ اَلذَّكِيُّ مَا ذُكِّيَ بِالْحَدِيدِ فَقَالَ «بَلَى إِذَا كَانَ مِمَّا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ» فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا لاَ يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ اَلْغَنَمِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالسِّنْجَابِ فَإِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ لاَ تَأْكُلُ اَللَّحْمَ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ مِمَّا نَهَى عَنْهُ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذْ نَهَى عَنْ كُلِّ ذِي نَابٍ أَوْ مِخْلَبٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: With this same chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about wearing fur garments and praying in them. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them except in what has been ritually slaughtered." I asked: "Isn’t dhakiyy what is slaughtered with iron (a blade)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if it is from that which its meat is eaten." So I asked: "What about what is not eaten from animals other than sheep?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with (wearing) squirrel (al-sinjab), for it is a creature that does not eat meat, and it is not from those things which the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, prohibited when He (saws) prohibited all animals with fangs or talons."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 216

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "I enter the market of the Muslims, I mean this group who ‘claim’ Islam, and I buy fur garments from them for trade. So I say to the seller: 'Is it not from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?' And he (seller) replies: 'Yes.' So is it permissible for me to sell it on the basis that it is dhakiyyah?" Imam (a.s) said: "No. But there is no harm in selling them if you say: ‘The one I bought them from claimed they were from a slaughtered animal.’” I asked: “What invalidates that? (makes it impermissible to sell as definitely pure)” Imam (a.s) said: "The people of Iraq making carrion (maytah) lawful, and they claimed that the tanning of the skin of carrion renders it ritually pure (as its slaughter). Then they were not content with lying about that except by attributing it to the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَدْخُلُ سُوقَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ أَعْنِي هَذَا اَلْخَلْقَ اَلَّذِي يَدَّعُونَ اَلْإِسْلاَمَ فَأَشْتَرِي مِنْهُمُ اَلْفِرَاءَ لِلتِّجَارَةِ فَأَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهَا أَ لَيْسَ هِيَ ذَكِيَّةً فَيَقُولُ بَلَى فَهَلْ يَصْلُحُ لِي أَنْ أَبِيعَهَا عَلَى أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تَبِيعَهَا وَ تَقُولَ قَدْ شَرَطَ اَلَّذِي اِشْتَرَيْتُهَا مِنْهُ أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا أَفْسَدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ« اِسْتِحْلاَلُ أَهْلِ اَلْعِرَاقِ لِلْمَيْتَةِ وَ زَعَمُوا أَنَّ دِبَاغَ جِلْدِ اَلْمَيْتَةِ ذَكَاتُهُ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْضَوْا أَنْ يَكْذِبُوا فِي ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ عَلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "I enter the market of the Muslims, I mean this group who ‘claim’ Islam, and I buy fur garments from them for trade. So I say to the seller: 'Is it not from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?' And he (seller) replies: 'Yes.' So is it permissible for me to sell it on the basis that it is dhakiyyah?" Imam (a.s) said: "No. But there is no harm in selling them if you say: ‘The one I bought them from claimed they were from a slaughtered animal.’” I asked: “What invalidates that? (makes it impermissible to sell as definitely pure)” Imam (a.s) said: "The people of Iraq making carrion (maytah) lawful, and they claimed that the tanning of the skin of carrion renders it ritually pure (as its slaughter). Then they were not content with lying about that except by attributing it to the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 216

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Asim ibn Humaid, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "May I be ransomed for you, can anything from a dead animal (maytah) be benefitted from?" Imam (a.s) said: "No." I asked: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dead sheep and said: 'What would have been upon the people of this sheep if they could not benefit from its meat, to at least benefit from its hide?'" Imam (a.s) said: "That was a sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it was an emaciated sheep whose meat was of no benefit, so they left it until it died. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: 'What would have been upon its people, if they could not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its hide, that is, by making it ritually slaughtered (tudhakka)'."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ اَلْمَيْتَةُ يُنْتَفَعُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهَا قَالَ« لاَ» قُلْتُ بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ مَرَّ بِشَاةٍ مَيْتَةٍ فَقَالَ« مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَهْلِ هَذِهِ اَلشَّاةِ إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِإِهَابِهَا» فَقَالَ« تِلْكَ شَاةٌ لِسَوْدَةَ بِنْتِ زَمْعَةَ زَوْجِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ كَانَتْ شَاةً مَهْزُولَةً لاَ يُنْتَفَعُ بِلَحْمِهَا فَتَرَكُوهَا حَتَّى مَاتَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« مَاكَانَ عَلَى أَهْلِهَا إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِإِهَابِهَا أَيْ تُذَكَّى»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Asim ibn Humaid, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: "May I be ransomed for you, can anything from a dead animal (maytah) be benefitted from?" Imam (a.s) said: "No." I asked: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dead sheep and said: 'What would have been upon the people of this sheep if they could not benefit from its meat, to at least benefit from its hide?'" Imam (a.s) said: "That was a sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it was an emaciated sheep whose meat was of no benefit, so they left it until it died. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: 'What would have been upon its people, if they could not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its hide, that is, by making it ritually slaughtered (tudhakka)'."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama’ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing a sword in prayer when it contains fur or ‘kaymukht’ (a type of soft leather). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it as long as it is not known to be from a dead animal."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ تَقْلِيدِ اَلسَّيْفِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ اَلْفِرَاءُ وَ اَلْكَيْمُخْتُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ مَا لَمْ يُعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مَيْتَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama’ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing a sword in prayer when it contains fur or ‘kaymukht’ (a type of soft leather). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it as long as it is not known to be from a dead animal."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 217

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d ibn al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in the skins of wild beasts. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Him (a.s): ‘Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?’" Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدِ بْنِ اَلْأَحْوَصِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جُلُودِ اَلسِّبَاعِ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهَا» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمٍ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d ibn al-Ahwas, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in the skins of wild beasts. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Him (a.s): ‘Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?’" Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 217

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the meat of wild beasts and their skins. Imam (a.s) said: "As for the meat of wild beasts, from birds and animals, we dislike it. And as for the skins, ride upon them, but do not wear anything from them in which you pray."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ لُحُومِ اَلسِّبَاعِ وَ جُلُودِهَا فَقَالَ« أَمَّا لُحُومُ اَلسِّبَاعِ مِنَ اَلطَّيْرِ وَ اَلدَّوَابِّ فَإِنَّا نَكْرَهُهُ وَ أَمَّا اَلْجُلُودُ فَارْكَبُوا عَلَيْهَا وَ لاَ تَلْبَسُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئاً تُصَلُّونَ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the meat of wild beasts and their skins. Imam (a.s) said: "As for the meat of wild beasts, from birds and animals, we dislike it. And as for the skins, ride upon them, but do not wear anything from them in which you pray."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 218

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the skins of foxes, can one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "I do not like to pray in them."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ جُلُودِ اَلثَّعَالِبِ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا فَقَالَ« مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the skins of foxes, can one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "I do not like to pray in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 218

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said:
I wrote to Him (a.s) asking about prayer in the skins of rabbits. Imam (a.s) wrote in reply: "It is makrooh (disliked)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جُلُودِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ« مَكْرُوهَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him (a.s) asking about prayer in the skins of rabbits. Imam (a.s) wrote in reply: "It is makrooh (disliked)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 218

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Bunan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:
I wrote to Him (a.s): "May I be ransomed for you, we have socks and padding that are made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or taqiyyah?" Imam (a.s) wrote in reply, peace be upon him: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْأَبْهَرِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عِنْدَنَا جَوَارِبُ وَ تِكَكٌ تُعْمَلُ مِنْ وَبَرِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ فَهَلْ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ مِنْ غَيْرِ ضَرُورَةٍ وَ لاَ تَقِيَّةٍ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Bunan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him (a.s): "May I be ransomed for you, we have socks and padding that are made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or taqiyyah?" Imam (a.s) wrote in reply, peace be upon him: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
