chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ali ibn Mahziyar said Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to Imam (a.s): "We have socks and padding that are made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or taqiyyah?" Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
arabicText: علي بن مهزيار قال كتب إليه ابراهيم بن عقبة عندنا جوارب وتكك تعمل من وبر الارانب فهل تجوز الصلاة في وبر الارانب من غير ضرورة ولا تقية؟ فكتب عليه السلام لا تجوز الصلاة فيها
thaqalaynMatn: Ali ibn Mahziyar said Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to Imam (a.s): "We have socks and padding that are made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or taqiyyah?" Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 218

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي زَيْدٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ جُلُودِ اَلثَّعَالِبِ اَلذَّكِيَّةِ قَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 219

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man:
He asked (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes. He (a.s) forbade praying in them and in what is next to them. But I (narrator) did not know which of the two garments He (a.s) meant, was it the one that is in contact with the fur or the one that is in contact with the skin? So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: "The one that is in contact with the skin." And Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned that He (a.s) was asked about this matter, and Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in what is above it, nor in what is beneath it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ: سَأَلَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جُلُودِ اَلثَّعَالِبِ فَنَهَى عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا وَ فِي اَلَّذِي يَلِيهِ فَلَمْ أَدْرِ أَيُّ اَلثَّوْبَيْنِ اَلَّذِي يَلْصَقُ بِالْوَبَرِ أَوِ اَلَّذِي يَلْصَقُ بِالْجِلْدِ فَوَقَّعَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِخَطِّهِ« اَلَّذِي يَلْصَقُ بِالْجِلْدِ» وَ ذَكَرَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ هَذِهِ اَلْمَسْأَلَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي اَلَّذِي فَوْقَهُ وَ لاَ فِي اَلَّذِي تَحْتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man:
thaqalaynMatn: He asked (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes. He (a.s) forbade praying in them and in what is next to them. But I (narrator) did not know which of the two garments He (a.s) meant, was it the one that is in contact with the fur or the one that is in contact with the skin? So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: "The one that is in contact with the skin." And Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned that He (a.s) was asked about this matter, and Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in what is above it, nor in what is beneath it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 219

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And as for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about prayer in the skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "If they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then there is no problem."
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جُلُودِ اَلثَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And as for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about prayer in the skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "If they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 219

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, asking: "Is it permissible to pray in a cap that has upon it the fur of an animal whose meat is not permissible to eat, or in a waistband of silk, or in a waistband made from rabbit fur?" Imam (a.s) wrote: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk. And if the fur is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then prayer in it is permissible, Allah (swt) willing."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي قَلَنْسُوَةٍ عَلَيْهَا وَبَرُ مَالاَ يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ أَوْ تِكَّةِ حَرِيرٍ أَوْ تِكَّةٍ مِنْ وَبَرِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلْحَرِيرِ اَلْمَحْضِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ اَلْوَبَرُ ذَكِيّاً حَلَّتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, asking: "Is it permissible to pray in a cap that has upon it the fur of an animal whose meat is not permissible to eat, or in a waistband of silk, or in a waistband made from rabbit fur?" Imam (a.s) wrote: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk. And if the fur is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then prayer in it is permissible, Allah (swt) willing."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 219

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Walid ibn Aban, who said:
I said to (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: "May I pray in the fur of the fennec and the squirrel?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." So I asked: "Is it permissible to pray in fox skins if they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ بْنِ أَبَانٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي فِي اَلْفَنَكِ وَاَلسِّنْجَابِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقُلْتُ يُصَلَّى فِي اَلثَّعَالِبِ إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً قَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Walid ibn Aban, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: "May I pray in the fur of the fennec and the squirrel?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." So I asked: "Is it permissible to pray in fox skins if they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?" Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 220

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Him (a.s): "Is it permissible to pray in a cap made of pure silk or a cap made of brocade (dibaj)?" Imam (a.s) wrote in reply: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي قَلَنْسُوَةِ حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ أَوْ قَلَنْسُوَةِ دِيبَاجٍ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Him (a.s): "Is it permissible to pray in a cap made of pure silk or a cap made of brocade (dibaj)?" Imam (a.s) wrote in reply: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 220

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a garment made of silk, can men pray in it? He said: "No."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلثَّوْبِ اَلْإِبْرِيسَمِ هَلْ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ اَلرِّجَالُ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a garment made of silk, can men pray in it? He said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 220

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from a group of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Harith, who said:
I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: "Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَارِثِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمٍ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from a group of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Harith, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: "Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 221

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him ,about prayer in a garment of brocade (dibaj), and he said: "As long as it does not have images (tamathil), then there is no problem."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي ثَوْبِ دِيبَاجٍ فَقَالَ« مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him ,about prayer in a garment of brocade (dibaj), and he said: "As long as it does not have images (tamathil), then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 221

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing silk and brocade. Imam (a.s) said: "As for during war, there is no problem, even if it contains images (tamathil)."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ لِبَاسِ اَلْحَرِيرِ وَاَلدِّيبَاجِ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا فِي اَلْحَرْبِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ تَمَاثِيلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing silk and brocade. Imam (a.s) said: "As for during war, there is no problem, even if it contains images (tamathil)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 221

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with a garment whose warp, buttons, and embroidery are of silk. What is disliked for men is pure silk (al-harir al-buhm)."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالثَّوْبِ أَنْ يَكُونَ سَدَاهُ وَ زِرُّهُ وَ عَلَمُهُ حَرِيراً وَ إِنَّمَا كُرِهَ اَلْحَرِيرُ اَلْبُهْمُ لِلرِّجَالِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with a garment whose warp, buttons, and embroidery are of silk. What is disliked for men is pure silk (al-harir al-buhm)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 222

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
Zurarah asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes, fennec, squirrels, and other types of fur. So He (a.s) took out a book, which He (a.s) claimed was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, (and it said): "Indeed, prayer in the fur of every animal whose meat is forbidden to eat, then prayer in its fur, hair, skin, urine, feces, and everything from it, is invalid. That prayer is not accepted until one prays in something other than it, from that which Allah (swt) has permitted its meat to be eaten." Then Imam (a.s) said: "O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, by Allah (swt). So preserve it, O Zurarah. For if it is from that whose meat is permissible to eat, then prayer in its fur, urine, hair, feces, milk, and everything from it is permissible, if you know that it is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyy), slaughtered by the proper method. But if it is other than that, from what you have been prohibited from eating or what is forbidden for you to eat, then prayer in anything from it is invalid, whether it was ritually slaughtered or not."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ زُرَارَةُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلثَّعَالِبِ وَ اَلْفَنَكِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ اَلْوَبَرِ فَأَخْرَجَ كِتَاباً زَعَمَ أَنَّهُ إِمْلاَءُ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« أَنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي وَبَرِ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَرَامٍ أَكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ شَعْرِهِ وَ جِلْدِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ وَ رَوْثِهِ وَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ لاَ تُقْبَلُ تِلْكَ اَلصَّلاَةُ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ فِي غَيْرِهِ مِمَّا أَحَلَّ اَللَّهُ أَكْلَهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« يَا زُرَارَةُ هَذَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اَللَّهِ فَاحْفَظْ ذَلِكَ يَا زُرَارَةُ فَإِنْ كَانَ مِمَّا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ وَ شَعْرِهِ وَ رَوْثِهِ وَ أَلْبَانِهِ وَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ جَائِزَةٌ إِذَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ ذَكِيٌّ قَدْ ذَكَّاهُ اَلذَّبْحُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا قَدْ نُهِيتَ عَنْ أَكْلِهِ أَوْ حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكَ أَكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ ذَكَّاهُ اَلذَّبْحُ أَوْ لَمْ يُذَكِّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Zurarah asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes, fennec, squirrels, and other types of fur. So He (a.s) took out a book, which He (a.s) claimed was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, (and it said): "Indeed, prayer in the fur of every animal whose meat is forbidden to eat, then prayer in its fur, hair, skin, urine, feces, and everything from it, is invalid. That prayer is not accepted until one prays in something other than it, from that which Allah (swt) has permitted its meat to be eaten." Then Imam (a.s) said: "O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, by Allah (swt). So preserve it, O Zurarah. For if it is from that whose meat is permissible to eat, then prayer in its fur, urine, hair, feces, milk, and everything from it is permissible, if you know that it is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyy), slaughtered by the proper method. But if it is other than that, from what you have been prohibited from eating or what is forbidden for you to eat, then prayer in anything from it is invalid, whether it was ritually slaughtered or not."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 222

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said:
I wrote to Him (a.s): "Fur and hair from animals whose meat is not lawful to eat fall onto my garment, without any taqiyyah or necessity, what is the ruling?" He (a.s) wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْهَمَذَانِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ يَسْقُطُ عَلَى ثَوْبِيَ اَلْوَبَرُ وَ اَلشَّعْرُ مِمَّا لاَ يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ وَ لاَ ضَرُورَةٍ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him (a.s): "Fur and hair from animals whose meat is not lawful to eat fall onto my garment, without any taqiyyah or necessity, what is the ruling?" He (a.s) wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 223

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a man, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to dislike prayer in the fur of anything whose meat is not lawful to eat.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْوَشَّاءِ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَكْرَهُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي وَبَرِ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لاَ يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a man, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to dislike prayer in the fur of anything whose meat is not lawful to eat.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 223

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from someone who mentioned it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in garments made from sable, squirrel, and fox. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no good in any of that, except for the squirrel, for it is a creature that does not eat meat."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ مُقَاتِلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّمُّورِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ اَلثَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ« لاَ خَيْرَ فِي ذَا كُلِّهِ مَا خَلاَ اَلسِّنْجَابَ فَإِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ لاَ تَأْكُلُ اَللَّحْمَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from someone who mentioned it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in garments made from sable, squirrel, and fox. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no good in any of that, except for the squirrel, for it is a creature that does not eat meat."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 223

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: "What do you say about fur garments, can one pray in them?" Imam (a.s) said: "Which fur garments?" I said: "The fennec, the squirrel, and the sable." Imam (a.s) said: "Then pray in the fennec and the squirrel. As for the sable, do not pray in it." I said: "Can one pray in fox furs?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, but they may be worn after the prayer." I said: "Can I pray in the garment that touches it (worn underneath it)?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيِّ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلْفِرَاءِ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ قَالَ« أَيُّ اَلْفِرَاءِ» قُلْتُ اَلْفَنَكَ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابَ وَ اَلسَّمُّورَ قَالَ« فَصَلِّ فِي اَلْفَنَكِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ فَأَمَّا اَلسَّمُّورُ فَلاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ» قُلْتُ فَالثَّعَالِبُ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا قَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ تُلْبَسُ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ» قُلْتُ أُصَلِّي فِي اَلثَّوْبِ اَلَّذِي يَلِيهِ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: "What do you say about fur garments, can one pray in them?" Imam (a.s) said: "Which fur garments?" I said: "The fennec, the squirrel, and the sable." Imam (a.s) said: "Then pray in the fennec and the squirrel. As for the sable, do not pray in it." I said: "Can one pray in fox furs?" Imam (a.s) said: "No, but they may be worn after the prayer." I said: "Can I pray in the garment that touches it (worn underneath it)?" Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 223

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said Bashir ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying:
I asked Him (a.s) about prayer in garments made from fennec, fur, squirrel, sable, and decorative collars (hawasil) that are hunted in the lands of polytheism or the lands of Islam, whether I may pray in them when not under taqiyyah. Imam (a.s) said: "Pray in the squirrel and the Khwarazmian collars, and do not pray in foxes or sable."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْفَنَكِ وَ اَلْفِرَاءِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ اَلسَّمُّورِ وَ اَلْحَوَاصِلِ اَلَّتِي تُصَادُ بِبِلاَدِ اَلشِّرْكِ أَوْ بِلاَدِ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ لِغَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ فِي اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ اَلْحَوَاصِلِ اَلْخُوارَزْمِيَّةِ وَ لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي اَلثَّعَالِبِ وَ لاَ اَلسَّمُّورِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said Bashir ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about prayer in garments made from fennec, fur, squirrel, sable, and decorative collars (hawasil) that are hunted in the lands of polytheism or the lands of Islam, whether I may pray in them when not under taqiyyah. Imam (a.s) said: "Pray in the squirrel and the Khwarazmian collars, and do not pray in foxes or sable."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 223

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن جعفر بن محمد بن أبي زيد قال سئل الرضا عليه السلام عن جلود الثعالب الذكية قال لا تصل فيها
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 224

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about garments made from furs, sable, squirrel, foxes, and similar things. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with praying in them."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِرَاءِ وَ اَلسَّمُّورِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ اَلثَّعَالِبِ وَ أَشْبَاهِهِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about garments made from furs, sable, squirrel, foxes, and similar things. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with praying in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 224

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing garments made from fur, sable, fennec, foxes, and all types of skins. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ لِبَاسِ اَلْفِرَاءِ وَ اَلسَّمُّورِ وَ اَلْفَنَكِ وَ اَلثَّعَالِبِ وَ جَمِيعِ اَلْجُلُودِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about wearing garments made from fur, sable, fennec, foxes, and all types of skins. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 224

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the skins of sable (sammur). Imam (a.s) said: "What is that? The dark one?" I said: "It is the black one." Imam (a.s) said: "Does it hunt?" I said: "Yes, it takes chickens and pigeons." Imam (a.s) said: "No (do not pray in it)."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ جُلُودِ اَلسَّمُّورِ فَقَالَ« أَيُّ شَيْءٍ هُوَ ذَاكَ اَلْأَدْبَسُ» فَقُلْتُ هُوَ اَلْأَسْوَدُ فَقَالَ« يَصِيدُ» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ يَأْخُذُ اَلدَّجَاجَ وَاَلْحَمَامَ قَالَ «لاَ» ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون أراد بغي على حسب ما قدمناه قبل هذا الموضع ويجوز ايضا أن يكون أراد إذا كان على قلنسوة أو ثوب لايتم الصلاة به وكل ما ورد من الاخبار في رخص لبس هذه الاشياء في حال الصلاة فالكلام عليه ما ذكرناه
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the skins of sable (sammur). Imam (a.s) said: "What is that? The dark one?" I said: "It is the black one." Imam (a.s) said: "Does it hunt?" I said: "Yes, it takes chickens and pigeons." Imam (a.s) said: "No (do not pray in it)."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Furayt, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man from the dealers in khazz (a type of fine fabric) entered and said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, what do you say about prayer in khazz?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with praying in it." The man said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, it is from a dead animal, and I prepare it myself, I know it." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: "I know it better than you." The man said to Him (a.s): "It is my work, and no one knows it better than me." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, smiled and then said to him: "Do you say it is a creature that is brought out from the water, or is caught from the water, and when water is lost, it dies?" The man said: "You have spoken the truth, may I be your ransom, that is how it is." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Then you are saying it is a creature that walks on four legs, and it is not considered among the category of fish so that its slaughter would be its exit from water?" The man said: "Yes, by Allah (swt), that is what I say." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: "Indeed Allah (swt), the Exalted, has made it lawful and has made its death its slaughter, just as He (swt) has made fish lawful and made their death their slaughter."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلدَّيْلَمِيِّ عَنْ فُرَيْتٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ مِنَ اَلْخَزَّازِينَ فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْخَزِّ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ مَيِّتٌ وَ هُوَ عِلاَجِي وَ أَنَا أَعْرِفُهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَنَا أَعْرَفُ بِهِ مِنْكَ» فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ إِنَّهُ عِلاَجِي وَ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ أَعْرَفَ بِهِ مِنِّي فَتَبَسَّمَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ« تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ تُخْرَجُ مِنَ اَلْمَاءِ أَوْ تُصَادُ مِنَ اَلْمَاءِ فَتُخْرَجُ فَإِذَا فُقِدَ اَلْمَاءُ مَاتَ» فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ صَدَقْتَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ هَكَذَا هُوَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« فَإِنَّكَ تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ تَمْشِي عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ فِي حَدِّ اَلْحِيتَانِ فَتَكُونَ ذَكَاتُهُ خُرُوجَهُ مِنَ اَلْمَاءِ» فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِي وَ اَللَّهِ هَكَذَا أَقُولُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَحَلَّهُ وَ جَعَلَ ذَكَاتَهُ مَوْتَهُ كَمَا أَحَلَّ اَلْحِيتَانَ وَ جَعَلَ ذَكَاتَهَا مَوْتَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Furayt, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man from the dealers in khazz (a type of fine fabric) entered and said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, what do you say about prayer in khazz?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with praying in it." The man said to Him (a.s): "May I be your ransom, it is from a dead animal, and I prepare it myself, I know it." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: "I know it better than you." The man said to Him (a.s): "It is my work, and no one knows it better than me." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, smiled and then said to him: "Do you say it is a creature that is brought out from the water, or is caught from the water, and when water is lost, it dies?" The man said: "You have spoken the truth, may I be your ransom, that is how it is." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Then you are saying it is a creature that walks on four legs, and it is not considered among the category of fish so that its slaughter would be its exit from water?" The man said: "Yes, by Allah (swt), that is what I say." So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: "Indeed Allah (swt), the Exalted, has made it lawful and has made its death its slaughter, just as He (swt) has made fish lawful and made their death their slaughter."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim, from Mu‘ammar ibn Khallad, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in khazz (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "Pray in it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْخَزِّ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim, from Mu‘ammar ibn Khallad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in khazz (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "Pray in it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding prayer in pure khazz (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it. But as for that which is mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar to it, do not pray in it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْخَزِّ اَلْخَالِصِ« أَنَّهُ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ فَأَمَّا اَلَّذِي يُخْلَطُ فِيهِ وَبَرُ اَلْأَرَانِبِ أَوْ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يُشْبِهُ هَذَا فَلاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding prayer in pure khazz (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it. But as for that which is mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar to it, do not pray in it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who raised it (to the Imam (a.s)), who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer in pure khazz is not a problem. But as for that which is mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar to it, do not pray in it."
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن محمد بن عيسى عن أيوب بن نوح رفعه قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام الصلاة في الخز الخالص لا بأس به فأما الذي يخلط فيه وبر الارانب أو غير ذلك مما يشبه هذا فلا تصل فيه
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who raised it (to the Imam (a.s)), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer in pure khazz is not a problem. But as for that which is mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar to it, do not pray in it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, who said:
I saw Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, praying in a cloak made of khazz (a type of fine fabric).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْجَعْفَرِيِّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي فِي جُبَّةِ خَزٍّ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, praying in a cloak made of khazz (a type of fine fabric).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 226

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
I asked him about prayer in khazz that is lined with rabbit fur. And he wrote in reply: "That is permissible."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْخَزِّ يُغَشُّ بِوَبَرِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ« يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about prayer in khazz that is lined with rabbit fur. And he wrote in reply: "That is permissible."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
A man asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in khazz (a fine fabric) that is lined with rabbit fur. He wrote in reply: "That is permissible."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَعَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِبْنَيْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْخَزِّ يُغَشُّ بِوَبَرِ اَلْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ« يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ» فذكر على ما ترى في هذه الرواية ان السائل كان غيره وسمى المسؤول وهذا ظاهر التناقض لانه لو كان السائل هو نفسه لوجب أن تكون الرواية الاخيرة كذبا ولو كان السائل غيره لوجب أن تكون الاولى كذبا وإذا تقابل الروايتان ولم يكن هناك ما يعضد أحداهما وجب اطراحهما مع أنه لو صح هذا الحديث لم يكن معترضا على ما ذكرناه من الاحاديث ويحتمل أن يكون ورد هذا الخبر مورد التقية كما وردت أخبار كثيرة في مثله
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in khazz (a fine fabric) that is lined with rabbit fur. He wrote in reply: "That is permissible."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) "Black is disliked except in three things; the shoes, the turban, and the cloak."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُكْرَهُ اَلسَّوَادُ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثَةٍ اَلْخُفِّ وَ اَلْعِمَامَةِ وَ اَلْكِسَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) "Black is disliked except in three things; the shoes, the turban, and the cloak."

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from someone who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "Shall I pray in a black cap?" Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in it, for it is the clothing of the people of the Fire."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَسِّنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أُصَلِّي فِي اَلْقَلَنْسُوَةِ اَلسَّوْدَاءِ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهَا فَإِنَّهَا لِبَاسُ أَهْلِ اَلنَّارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from someone who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "Shall I pray in a black cap?" Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in it, for it is the clothing of the people of the Fire."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Hammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) "Do not pray in what is transparent or see-through" (meaning a garment that is thin and clings to the body)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلسَّيَّارِيِّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيمَا شَفَّ أَوْصَفَّ يَعْنِي اَلثَّوْبَ اَلْمُصَقَّلَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Hammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) "Do not pray in what is transparent or see-through" (meaning a garment that is thin and clings to the body)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 227

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who raised it (to the Imam (a.s)), who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in what is transparent or revealing" (meaning a garment that is thin and clings to the body).
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن محمد بن يحيى رفعه قال أبو عبد الله لا تصل فيما شف أوصف يعني الثوب المصقل
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who raised it (to the Imam (a.s)), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in what is transparent or revealing" (meaning a garment that is thin and clings to the body).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from some of our companions, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
(Imam (a.s) said) "Wearing a cloak (irtida’) over a wrapped garment (tawashshuh; piece of cloth over one's shoulder) in prayer is disliked, and wrapping a garment (tawashshuh) over a shirt is also disliked."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« اَلاِرْتِدَاءُ فَوْقَ اَلتَّوَشُّحِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ مَكْرُوهٌ وَ اَلتَّوَشُّحُ فَوْقَ اَلْقَمِيصِ مَكْرُوهٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from some of our companions, from one of them (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) "Wearing a cloak (irtida’) over a wrapped garment (tawashshuh; piece of cloth over one's shoulder) in prayer is disliked, and wrapping a garment (tawashshuh) over a shirt is also disliked."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is not appropriate to wrap yourself with an izar over the shirt when you pray, for that is from the dress of the Days of Ignorance."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَتَوَشَّحَ بِإِزَارٍ فَوْقَ اَلْقَمِيصِ إِذَا أَنْتَ صَلَّيْتَ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ زِيِّ اَلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is not appropriate to wrap yourself with an izar over the shirt when you pray, for that is from the dress of the Days of Ignorance."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Beware wrapping yourself in ‘al-samma’." I asked: "What is the ‘al-samma’ wrap?" Imam (a.s) said: "It is to insert the garment from beneath your arms and place it over one shoulder."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِيَّاكَ وَ اِلْتِحَافَ اَلصَّمَّاءِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا اِلْتِحَافُ اَلصَّمَّاءِ قَالَ« أَنْ تُدْخِلَ اَلثَّوْبَ مِنْ تَحْتِ جَنَاحَيْكَ فَتَجْعَلَهُ عَلَى مَنْكِبٍ وَاحِدٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Beware wrapping yourself in ‘al-samma’." I asked: "What is the ‘al-samma’ wrap?" Imam (a.s) said: "It is to insert the garment from beneath your arms and place it over one shoulder."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Bazi‘, who said:
I said to Al-Ridha (a.s): "I tie the izar or the scarf over my shirt during prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَشُدُّ اَلْإِزَارَ أَوِ اَلْمِنْدِيلَ فَوْقَ قَمِيصِي فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Bazi‘, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Al-Ridha (a.s): "I tie the izar or the scarf over my shirt during prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far al-Thani (a.s), peace be upon him, praying in a shirt, and He (a.s) had wrapped a cloth (mindil) over it as a waist-wrapper (izar) while he was praying.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ اَلْبَجَلِيِّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ اَلثَّانِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيصٍ قَدِ اِتَّزَرَ فَوْقَهُ بِمِنْدِيلٍ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja‘far, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja‘far al-Thani (a.s), peace be upon him, praying in a shirt, and He (a.s) had wrapped a cloth (mindil) over it as a waist-wrapper (izar) while he was praying.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 228

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin wrote to the Righteous Servant (al-Abd al-Salih (a.s)) asking: "Can a man pray while wearing an izar wrapped over his shirt?" He (a.s) wrote in reply: "Yes."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ كَتَبَ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ إِلَى اَلْعَبْدِ اَلصَّالِحِ: هَلْ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ عَلَيْهِ إِزَارٌ مُتَوَشِّحٌ بِهِ فَوْقَ اَلْقَمِيصِ فَكَتَبَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin wrote to the Righteous Servant (al-Abd al-Salih (a.s)) asking: "Can a man pray while wearing an izar wrapped over his shirt?" He (a.s) wrote in reply: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 229

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who wraps himself in a single garment during prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not wrap himself in a single garment completely. But if he wraps it across himself (tawashshaha) and covers his shoulders, then there is no problem."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَشْتَمِلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ بِثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ قَالَ« لاَ يَشْتَمِلُ بِثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ فَأَمَّا أَنْ يَتَوَشَّحَ فَيُغَطِّيَ مَنْكِبَيْهِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who wraps himself in a single garment during prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not wrap himself in a single garment completely. But if he wraps it across himself (tawashshaha) and covers his shoulders, then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 229

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from someone who mentioned it:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not wrap it under the chin (yatanahhak), and then suffers from an illness for which there is no cure, let him blame no one but himself."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ تَعَمَّمَ وَ لَمْ يَتَحَنَّكْ فَأَصَابَهُ دَاءٌ لاَ دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلاَ يَلُومَنَّ إِلاَّ نَفْسَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from someone who mentioned it:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not wrap it under the chin (yatanahhak), and then suffers from an illness for which there is no cure, let him blame no one but himself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 229

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja‘far, from Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Isa ibn Hamzah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not wrap the turban under his chin (hanak), and then is afflicted with a pain for which there is no cure, let him blame no one but himself."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنِ اِعْتَمَّ فَلَمْ يُدِرِ اَلْعِمَامَةَ تَحْتَ حَنَكِهِ فَأَصَابَهُ أَلَمٌ لاَ دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلاَ يَلُومَنَّ إِلاَّ نَفْسَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja‘far, from Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Isa ibn Hamzah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not wrap the turban under his chin (hanak), and then is afflicted with a pain for which there is no cure, let him blame no one but himself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 230

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from his father, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) led us in prayer wearing a single garment.
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) led us in prayer wearing a single garment.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 230

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Safwan, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
Someone who asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated to me (Rifa‘ah ibn Musa), about a man who prays in a single garment, wrapping it around his lower body. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it if he raises it up to his chest."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي مَنْ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ يَأْتَزِرُ بِهِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَهُ إِلَى اَلثَّدْيَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Safwan, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Someone who asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated to me (Rifa‘ah ibn Musa), about a man who prays in a single garment, wrapping it around his lower body. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it if he raises it up to his chest."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 230

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from Ziyad ibn Suqah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if one of you prays in a single garment with its buttons undone. Indeed, the religion of Muhammad (saws) (peace be upon him and his family) is upright and simple (hanif)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ سُوقَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي اَلثَّوْبِ اَلْوَاحِدِ وَ أَزْرَارُهُ مَحْلُولَةٌ إِنَّ دِينَ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حَنِيفٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from Ziyad ibn Suqah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if one of you prays in a single garment with its buttons undone. Indeed, the religion of Muhammad (saws) (peace be upon him and his family) is upright and simple (hanif)."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far, peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed while his private part was exposed, and he did not know about it. Does he have to repeat the prayer, or what is his situation? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no repetition upon him, and his prayer is complete."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ صَلَّى وَ فَرْجُهُ خَارِجٌ لاَ يَعْلَمُ بِهِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةٌ أَوْ مَا حَالُهُ قَالَ« لاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far, peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed while his private part was exposed, and he did not know about it. Does he have to repeat the prayer, or what is his situation? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no repetition upon him, and his prayer is complete."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 230

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, by Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays in a single shirt, or a narrow-sleeved robe (qabaʾ taq), or a padded robe, and he is not wearing an izar (waist wrap). Imam (a.s) said: "If the shirt is thick, and the robe (qabaʾ) is not split wide open in the front, and the single garment if he wraps it across himself, and the trousers (sarawil) are of that same type, then there is no problem with all of that. But when he wears trousers, he should put something over his shoulders, even if it is just a rope."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيصٍ وَاحِدٍ أَوْ قَبَاءٍ طَاقٍ أَوْ قَبَاءٍ مَحْشُوٍّ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِزَارٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْقَمِيصُ صَفِيقاً وَ اَلْقَبَاءُ لَيْسَ بِطَوِيلِ اَلْفُرَجِ وَ اَلثَّوْبُ اَلْوَاحِدُ إِذَا كَانَ يَتَوَشَّحُ بِهِ وَ اَلسَّرَاوِيلُ بِتِلْكَ اَلْمَنْزِلَةِ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا لَبِسَ اَلسَّرَاوِيلَ جَعَلَ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ شَيْئاً وَ لَوْ حَبْلاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, by Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays in a single shirt, or a narrow-sleeved robe (qabaʾ taq), or a padded robe, and he is not wearing an izar (waist wrap). Imam (a.s) said: "If the shirt is thick, and the robe (qabaʾ) is not split wide open in the front, and the single garment if he wraps it across himself, and the trousers (sarawil) are of that same type, then there is no problem with all of that. But when he wears trousers, he should put something over his shoulders, even if it is just a rope."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 230

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the minimum clothing in which a woman may pray. Imam (a.s) said: "A long shirt (dir‘) and an large wrap (milhafah), which she spreads over her head and covers herself with."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا تُصَلِّي فِيهِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ قَالَ« دِرْعٌ وَ مِلْحَفَةٌ فَتَنْشُرُهَا عَلَى رَأْسِهَا وَ تَتَجَلَّلُ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the minimum clothing in which a woman may pray. Imam (a.s) said: "A long shirt (dir‘) and an large wrap (milhafah), which she spreads over her head and covers herself with."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 231

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj:
Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is not obligatory for slave women to cover their heads in prayer, and it is not appropriate for a woman to pray except in two garments."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَاءِ أَنْ يَتَقَنَّعْنَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ إِلاَّ فِي ثَوْبَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is not obligatory for slave women to cover their heads in prayer, and it is not appropriate for a woman to pray except in two garments."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) praying in a single izar (waist wrap) that was not wide, and He (a.s) had tied it around His (a.s) neck. I said to Him (a.s): "What do you say about a man who prays in a single shirt?" Imam (a.s) said: "If it is thick, then there is no problem with it. And a woman prays in a long shirt (dir‘) and a head covering (miqna‘ah), if the shirt is thick, meaning if it is concealing." I asked: "May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, does a slave woman cover her head when she prays?" Imam (a.s) said: "A slave woman is not required to wear a head covering."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّى فِي إِزَارٍ وَاحِدٍ لَيْسَ بِوَاسِعٍ قَدْ عَقَدَهُ عَلَى عُنُقِهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا تَرَى لِلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيصٍ وَاحِدٍ فَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ كَثِيفاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَاَلْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي فِي اَلدِّرْعِ وَاَلْمِقْنَعَةِ إِذَا كَانَ اَلدِّرْعُ كَثِيفاً يَعْنِي إِذَا كَانَ سَتِيراً» قُلْتُ رَحِمَكَ اَللَّهُ اَلْأَمَةُ تُغَطِّي رَأْسَهَا إِذَا صَلَّتْ فَقَالَ لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْأَمَةِ قِنَاعٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) praying in a single izar (waist wrap) that was not wide, and He (a.s) had tied it around His (a.s) neck. I said to Him (a.s): "What do you say about a man who prays in a single shirt?" Imam (a.s) said: "If it is thick, then there is no problem with it. And a woman prays in a long shirt (dir‘) and a head covering (miqna‘ah), if the shirt is thick, meaning if it is concealing." I asked: "May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, does a slave woman cover her head when she prays?" Imam (a.s) said: "A slave woman is not required to wear a head covering."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 231

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "A woman prays in three garments: an izar (waist wrap), a dir‘ (long shirt), and a khimar (head covering). It does not harm her to wrap herself with the khimar. But if she does not find (all three), then two garments: she wraps the lower part of her body with one and covers her head with the other." I asked: "And if it is a dir‘ and a milhafah (outer wrap) and she does not have a miqna‘ah (headscarf)?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem if she covers her head with the milhafah. If it does not suffice her, then she should wear it lengthwise."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« تُصَلِّي اَلْمَرْأَةُ فِي ثَلاَثَةِ أَثْوَابٍ إِزَارٍ وَدِرْعٍ وَخِمَارٍ وَلاَ يَضُرُّهَا بِأَنْ تَقَنَّعَ بِالْخِمَارِ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ فَثَوْبَيْنِ تَأْتَزِرُ بِأَحَدِهِمَا وَ تَقَنَّعُ بِالْآخَرِ» قُلْتُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ دِرْعاً وَ مِلْحَفَةً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا مِقْنَعَةٌ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِذَا تَقَنَّعَتْ بِالْمِلْحَفَةِ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكْفِهَا فَلْتَلْبَسْهَا طُولاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "A woman prays in three garments: an izar (waist wrap), a dir‘ (long shirt), and a khimar (head covering). It does not harm her to wrap herself with the khimar. But if she does not find (all three), then two garments: she wraps the lower part of her body with one and covers her head with the other." I asked: "And if it is a dir‘ and a milhafah (outer wrap) and she does not have a miqna‘ah (headscarf)?" Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem if she covers her head with the milhafah. If it does not suffice her, then she should wear it lengthwise."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem for a free Muslim woman to pray with her head uncovered."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَنْصَارِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالْمَرْأَةِ اَلْمُسْلِمَةِ اَلْحُرَّةِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ هِيَ مَكْشُوفَةُ اَلرَّأْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem for a free Muslim woman to pray with her head uncovered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 232

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, from Abu Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Ayyub al-Makki, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if a Muslim woman prays and there is no head covering (qina‘) on her head."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْمَكِّيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ اَلْمُسْلِمَةُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى رَأْسِهَا قِنَاعٌ»
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, from Abu Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Ayyub al-Makki, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if a Muslim woman prays and there is no head covering (qina‘) on her head."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 232

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): "Does the slave woman (amah) cover her head?" Imam (a.s) said: "No. And it is not obligatory for umm al-walad (a slave woman who has borne a child) to cover her head, if she has not borne a child."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِبْنَيْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلْأَمَةُ تُغَطِّي رَأْسَهَا فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لاَ عَلَى أُمِّ اَلْوَلَدِ أَنْ تُغَطِّيَ رَأْسَهَا إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Him (a.s): "Does the slave woman (amah) cover her head?" Imam (a.s) said: "No. And it is not obligatory for umm al-walad (a slave woman who has borne a child) to cover her head, if she has not borne a child."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman praying in a dir‘ (long shirt) and a khimar (head covering). Imam (a.s) said: "There should be over her a milhafah (outer wrap) that she gathers around herself."
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي فِي دِرْعٍ وَ خِمَارٍ فَقَالَ« تَكُونُ عَلَيْهَا مِلْحَفَةٌ تَضُمُّهَا عَلَيْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman praying in a dir‘ (long shirt) and a khimar (head covering). Imam (a.s) said: "There should be over her a milhafah (outer wrap) that she gathers around herself."
