chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “Can a man pray while he is veiled (covering his face with a cloth)?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for on the ground, then no; but as for on a riding animal, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ مُتَلَثِّمٌ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَلاَ وَ أَمَّا عَلَى اَلدَّابَّةِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “Can a man pray while he is veiled (covering his face with a cloth)?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for on the ground, then no; but as for on a riding animal, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 245

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is veiled (covering his face with a cloth). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ يَقْرَأُ اَلْقُرْآنَ وَ هُوَ مُتَلَثِّمٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is veiled (covering his face with a cloth). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 245

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja‘far from Abu Abdillah from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from someone he mentioned among our companions from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man recites (the Qur’an) in prayer while his garment is over his mouth.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَقْرَأَ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى فِيهِ
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja‘far from Abu Abdillah from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from someone he mentioned among our companions from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if a man recites (the Qur’an) in prayer while his garment is over his mouth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 245

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Al-Halabi:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Can a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that if he can hear the murmuring (of his own recitation).”
arabicText: ما رواه سعد عن أحمد بن محمد عن الحسن بن محبوب عن علي بن رئاب عن الحلبي قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام هل يقرأ الرجل في صلاته وثوبه على فيه؟ فقال لا بأس بذلك إذا سمع الهمهمة
thaqalaynSanad: Narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Can a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that if he can hear the murmuring (of his own recitation).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 246

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is veiled (covering his face). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it, but if he uncovers his mouth, that is better.” He (Sama’ah) said: “And I asked Him (a.s) about a woman who prays while wearing a niqab”. Imam (a.s) said: “If she uncovers the place of prostration, then there is no harm in it, and if she unveils (her face), that is better.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَيَتْلُو اَلْقُرْآنَ وَهُوَ مُتَلَثِّمٌ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ كَشَفَ عَنْ فِيهِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي مُتَنَقِّبَةً قَالَ« إِذَا كَشَفَتْ عَنْ مَوْضِعِ اَلسُّجُودِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ أَسْفَرَتْ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is veiled (covering his face). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it, but if he uncovers his mouth, that is better.” He (Sama’ah) said: “And I asked Him (a.s) about a woman who prays while wearing a niqab”. Imam (a.s) said: “If she uncovers the place of prostration, then there is no harm in it, and if she unveils (her face), that is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 246

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays in one corner of the room and his wife or daughter prays beside him in the other corner. Imam (a.s) said: “That is not appropriate. But if there is a span (shibr) of distance between them, it is sufficient” (meaning if the man is ahead of the woman by a span).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي زَاوِيَةِ اَلْحُجْرَةِ وَاِمْرَأَتُهُ أَوِ اِبْنَتُهُ تُصَلِّي بِحِذَاهُ فِي اَلزَّاوِيَةِ اَلْأُخْرَى قَالَ« لاَ يَنْبَغِي ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا شِبْرٌ أَجْزَأَهُ يَعْنِي إِذَا كَانَ اَلرَّجُلُ مُتَقَدِّماً لِلْمَرْأَةِ بِشِبْرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prays in one corner of the room and his wife or daughter prays beside him in the other corner. Imam (a.s) said: “That is not appropriate. But if there is a span (shibr) of distance between them, it is sufficient” (meaning if the man is ahead of the woman by a span).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 246

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man and a woman who pray in the same house, with the woman at the man's right side, aligned with him. Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless there is between them a span (shibr) or an arm’s length (dhira‘).” Then Imam (a.s) said: “The length of the mount of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was an arm’s length, and He (saws) used to place it in front of him when He (saws) prayed to screen himself from those who might pass in front of him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةِ يُصَلِّيَانِ فِي بَيْتٍ وَاحِدٍ اَلْمَرْأَةُ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلرَّجُلِ بِحِذَاهُ قَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُمَا شِبْرٌ أَوْ ذِرَاعٌ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «كَانَ طُولُ رَحْلِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذِرَاعاً فَكَانَ يَضَعُهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ إِذَا صَلَّى لِيَسْتُرَهُ مِمَّنْ يَمُرُّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man and a woman who pray in the same house, with the woman at the man's right side, aligned with him. Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless there is between them a span (shibr) or an arm’s length (dhira‘).” Then Imam (a.s) said: “The length of the mount of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was an arm’s length, and He (saws) used to place it in front of him when He (saws) prayed to screen himself from those who might pass in front of him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan and Fadalah from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a woman who shares a howdah (a carriage on a riding animal) with a man, and they both pray together. Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather the man should pray, and when he finishes, the woman should pray.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُزَامِلُ اَلرَّجُلَ فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ يُصَلِّيَانِ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ صَلَّتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan and Fadalah from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a woman who shares a howdah (a carriage on a riding animal) with a man, and they both pray together. Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather the man should pray, and when he finishes, the woman should pray.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man and a woman who pray together in a house, with the woman at the man's right side, aligned with him. Imam (a.s) said: “No, not unless there is between them a span (shibr), or an arm’s length (dhira‘), or something like that.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةِ يُصَلِّيَانِ جَمِيعاً فِي بَيْتٍ اَلْمَرْأَةُ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلرَّجُلِ بِحِذَاهُ قَالَ« لاَ حَتَّى يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُمَا شِبْرٌ أَوْ ذِرَاعٌ أَوْ نَحْوُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man and a woman who pray together in a house, with the woman at the man's right side, aligned with him. Imam (a.s) said: “No, not unless there is between them a span (shibr), or an arm’s length (dhira‘), or something like that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Sindi ibn Muhammad Al-Bazzaz from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I pray and a woman is beside me, and she is also praying.” Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless she moves forward or you do. But there is no harm if she is beside you while sitting or standing (and not praying).”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ سِنْدِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْبَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي وَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ إِلَى جَنْبِي وَ هِيَ تُصَلِّي فَقَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَتَقَدَّمَ هِيَ أَوْ أَنْتَ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ هِيَ بِحِذَاكَ جَالِسَةٌ أَوْ قَائِمَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Sindi ibn Muhammad Al-Bazzaz from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I pray and a woman is beside me, and she is also praying.” Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless she moves forward or you do. But there is no harm if she is beside you while sitting or standing (and not praying).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Idris ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who is praying while directly in line with him is a woman standing, in a state of janabah, on her bed. Imam (a.s) said: “If she is sitting, she does not harm you; but if she is praying, then no (it is not permissible).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِدْرِيسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ بِحِيَالِهِ اِمْرَأَةٌ قَائِمَةٌ جُنُبٌ عَلَى فِرَاشِهَا فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَتْ قَاعِدَةً فَلاَ تَضُرُّكَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي فَلاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Idris ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who is praying while directly in line with him is a woman standing, in a state of janabah, on her bed. Imam (a.s) said: “If she is sitting, she does not harm you; but if she is praying, then no (it is not permissible).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id Al-Mada’ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about a man who is able to pray while in front of him a woman is also praying. Imam (a.s) said: “He should not pray until he places between himself and her more than ten arm-lengths (adhru‘). And if she is on his right or on his left, he should place the same distance between himself and her. But if she is praying behind him, then there is no harm, even if she touches his garment. And if the woman is sitting, or sleeping, or standing without praying, then there is no harm wherever she may be.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْتَقِيمُ لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ اِمْرَأَةٌ تُصَلِّي قَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي حَتَّى يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ أَذْرُعٍ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ جَعَلَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَهَا مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ تُصِيبُ ثَوْبَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ قَاعِدَةً أَوْ نَائِمَةً أَوْ قَائِمَةً فِي غَيْرِ صَلاَةٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ حَيْثُ كَانَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id Al-Mada’ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about a man who is able to pray while in front of him a woman is also praying. Imam (a.s) said: “He should not pray until he places between himself and her more than ten arm-lengths (adhru‘). And if she is on his right or on his left, he should place the same distance between himself and her. But if she is praying behind him, then there is no harm, even if she touches his garment. And if the woman is sitting, or sleeping, or standing without praying, then there is no harm wherever she may be.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from someone who informed him from Jamil ibn Darraj:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who is praying and a woman is praying beside him. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي بِحِذَاهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from someone who informed him from Jamil ibn Darraj:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who is praying and a woman is praying beside him. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about an Imam (of prayer) who was leading the noon prayer, and his wife stood beside him and prayed with him, thinking it was the afternoon (‘Asr) prayer. Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation? And what is the ruling of the woman’s prayer with them, considering she had already prayed the noon prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer.”
arabicText: اَلْعَيَّاشِيُّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي اَلْعَمْرَكِيُّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ إِمَامٍ كَانَ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ فَقَامَتِ اِمْرَأَتُهُ بِحِيَالِهِ تُصَلِّي مَعَهُ وَ هِيَ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّهَا اَلْعَصْرُ هَلْ يُفْسِدُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اَلْقَوْمِ وَ مَا حَالُ اَلْمَرْأَةِ فِي صَلاَتِهَا مَعَهُمْ وَ قَدْ كَانَتْ صَلَّتِ اَلظُّهْرَ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُفْسِدُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اَلْقَوْمِ وَ تُعِيدُ اَلْمَرْأَةُ صَلاَتَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about an Imam (of prayer) who was leading the noon prayer, and his wife stood beside him and prayed with him, thinking it was the afternoon (‘Asr) prayer. Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation? And what is the ruling of the woman’s prayer with them, considering she had already prayed the noon prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
(a type of non-leather or stitched footwear)Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Musadif:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who performed an obligatory prayer while his hair was tied up. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُصَادِفٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى صَلاَةً فَرِيضَةً وَ هُوَ مَعْقُوصُ اَلشَّعْرِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: (a type of non-leather or stitched footwear)Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Musadif:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (was asked) regarding a man who performed an obligatory prayer while his hair was tied up. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, who said:
I saw him praying in his sandals; he did not remove them, and I think he said: "The two rak‘ahs of ṭawaf”.
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ: رَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي فِي نَعْلَيْهِ لَمْ يَخْلَعْهُمَا وَ أَحْسَبُهُ قَالَ« رَكْعَتَيِ اَلطَّوَافِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw him praying in his sandals; he did not remove them, and I think he said: "The two rak‘ahs of ṭawaf”.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) praying in his sandals on more than one occasion, and I never saw him remove them at all.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي فِي نَعْلَيْهِ غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ وَ لَمْ أَرَهُ يَنْزِعُهُمَا قَطُّ
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s) praying in his sandals on more than one occasion, and I never saw him remove them at all.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, who said: “When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for that is from the Sunnah.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَصَلِّ فِي نَعْلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَتْ طَاهِرَةً فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ»
thaqalaynMatn: Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, who said: “When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for that is from the Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) pray when the sun had passed its zenith on the Day of Tarwiyah, six units of prayer behind the Maqam, and He (a.s) had his sandals on; He (a.s) did not remove them.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّى حِينَ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ يَوْمَ اَلتَّرْوِيَةِ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ خَلْفَ اَلْمَقَامِ وَ عَلَيْهِ نَعْلاَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِعْهُمَا
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) pray when the sun had passed its zenith on the Day of Tarwiyah, six units of prayer behind the Maqam, and He (a.s) had his sandals on; He (a.s) did not remove them.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Aban from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for it is said that this is from the Sunnah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَصَلِّ فِي نَعْلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَتْ طَاهِرَةً فَإِنَّهُ يُقَالُ ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Aban from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for it is said that this is from the Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the leather socks (khifaf) that are sold in the market. Imam (a.s) said: “Buy them and pray in them unless you come to know that it is (from) a dead animal with certainty.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْخِفَافِ اَلَّتِي تُبَاعُ فِي اَلسُّوقِ فَقَالَ« اِشْتَرِ وَ صَلِّ فِيهَا حَتَّى تَعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ مَيِّتٌ بِعَيْنِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the leather socks (khifaf) that are sold in the market. Imam (a.s) said: “Buy them and pray in them unless you come to know that it is (from) a dead animal with certainty.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Sahl from some of his companions from Al-Hasan Al-Jahm, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pass through the market and buy leather socks (khuff), and I do not know whether they are from a ritually slaughtered animal (dhaki) or not.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray in them.” I asked: “And what about sandals?” Imam (a.s) said: “The same applies.” I said: “This makes me uneasy.” (concerning the purity of the leather) Imam (a.s) said: “Do you turn away from us? Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him used to do that.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ سَهْلٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْجَهْمِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَعْتَرِضُ اَلسُّوقَ فَأَشْتَرِي خُفّاً لاَ أَدْرِي أَ ذَكِيٌّ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ قَالَ« صَلِّ فِيهِ» قُلْتُ وَ اَلنَّعْلُ قَالَ« مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ» قُلْتُ إِنِّي أَضِيقُ مِنْ هَذَا قَالَ« أَ تَرْغَبُ عَنَّا كَانَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَفْعَلُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Sahl from some of his companions from Al-Hasan Al-Jahm, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pass through the market and buy leather socks (khuff), and I do not know whether they are from a ritually slaughtered animal (dhaki) or not.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray in them.” I asked: “And what about sandals?” Imam (a.s) said: “The same applies.” I said: “This makes me uneasy.” (concerning the purity of the leather) Imam (a.s) said: “Do you turn away from us? Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him used to do that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Isma‘il ibn Al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about wearing leather garments, leather socks (khiffaf), and sandals, and praying in them if they are not from the land of the Muslims. Imam (a.s) said: “As for the sandals and the leather socks, there is no harm in them.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ لِبَاسِ اَلْجُلُودِ وَ اَلْخِفَافِ وَ اَلنِّعَالِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا إِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ أَرْضِ اَلْمُصَلِّينَ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا اَلنِّعَالُ وَ اَلْخِفَافُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Isma‘il ibn Al-Fudayl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about wearing leather garments, leather socks (khiffaf), and sandals, and praying in them if they are not from the land of the Muslims. Imam (a.s) said: “As for the sandals and the leather socks, there is no harm in them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I asked him about praying in a jurmuq (a type of overshoe), and I brought him a jurmuq which I sent to him. He said: “It is permissible to pray in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جُرْمُوقٍ وَ أَتَيْتُهُ بِجُرْمُوقٍ بَعَثْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ« يُصَلَّى فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about praying in a jurmuq (a type of overshoe), and I brought him a jurmuq which I sent to him. He said: “It is permissible to pray in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad ibn Uthman narrated:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Prostration is (to be done) upon that which the earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى حَمَّادُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« اَلسُّجُودُ عَلَى مَا أَنْبَتَتِ اَلْأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا أُكِلَ أَوْ لُبِسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad ibn Uthman narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Prostration is (to be done) upon that which the earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And Hisham ibn Al-Hakam said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Inform me about what is permissible to prostrate upon and what is not permissible.” Imam (a.s) said: “Prostration is not permissible except upon the earth or that which the earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”
arabicText: وَ قَالَ هِشَامُ بْنُ اَلْحَكَمِ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَخْبِرْنِي عَمَّا يَجُوزُ اَلسُّجُودُ عَلَيْهِ وَ عَمَّا لاَ يَجُوزُ قَالَ «اَلسُّجُودُ لاَ يَجُوزُ إِلاَّ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ أَوْ عَلَى مَا أَنْبَتَتِ اَلْأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا أُكِلَ أَوْ لُبِسَ»
thaqalaynMatn: And Hisham ibn Al-Hakam said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Inform me about what is permissible to prostrate upon and what is not permissible.” Imam (a.s) said: “Prostration is not permissible except upon the earth or that which the earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it was narrated from Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said: “Prostration upon the earth is an obligation, and upon other than the earth is a Sunnah.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« اَلسُّجُودُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَرِيضَةٌ وَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْأَرْضِ سُنَّةٌ»
thaqalaynMatn: And it was narrated from Al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said: “Prostration upon the earth is an obligation, and upon other than the earth is a Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And it was narrated from Yasir, the servant, that he said:
Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by me while I was praying on a piece of tabari (a type of mat or plant material), and I had placed something over it. Imam (a.s) said: “Why do you not prostrate upon it? Is it not from vegetation of earth?”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ يَاسِرٍ اَلْخَادِمِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: مَرَّ بِي أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا أُصَلِّي عَلَى اَلطَّبَرِيِّ وَ قَدْ أَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ شَيْئاً فَقَالَ« مَالَكَ لاَ تَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ أَ لَيْسَ هُوَ مِنْ نَبَاتِ اَلْأَرْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And it was narrated from Yasir, the servant, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by me while I was praying on a piece of tabari (a type of mat or plant material), and I had placed something over it. Imam (a.s) said: “Why do you not prostrate upon it? Is it not from vegetation of earth?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about gypsum (jiss) that had been fired using excrement and the bones of the dead, and then the mosque was plastered with it, whether it is permissible to prostrate upon it. So Imam (a.s) wrote to him in His (a.s) own handwriting: “Indeed, water and fire have purified it.”
arabicText: وَسَأَلَ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلْجِصِّ يُوقَدُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَذِرَةِ وَعِظَامِ اَلْمَوْتَى ثُمَّ يُجَصَّصُ بِهِ اَلْمَسْجِدُ أَ يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ بِخَطِّهِ« أَنَّ اَلْمَاءَ وَ اَلنَّارَ قَدْ طَهَّرَاهُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about gypsum (jiss) that had been fired using excrement and the bones of the dead, and then the mosque was plastered with it, whether it is permissible to prostrate upon it. So Imam (a.s) wrote to him in His (a.s) own handwriting: “Indeed, water and fire have purified it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Dawud ibn Yazid asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him, about paper (qaratis) and parchment (kawaghidh) that have writing on them, whether it is permissible to prostrate upon them. So He (a.s) wrote: “It is permissible.”
arabicText: وَ سَأَلَ دَاوُدُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلْقَرَاطِيسِ وَ اَلْكَوَاغِذِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ عَلَيْهَا هَلْ يَجُوزُ اَلسُّجُودُ عَلَيْهَا فَكَتَبَ« يَجُوزُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Dawud ibn Yazid asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him, about paper (qaratis) and parchment (kawaghidh) that have writing on them, whether it is permissible to prostrate upon them. So He (a.s) wrote: “It is permissible.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, about a man who prostrates on a covering (mishh) or a carpet (bisat). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it if it is in a situation of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), and there is no harm in prostrating on clothes in a situation of taqiyyah.”
arabicText: وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ يَقْطِينٍ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ عَلَى اَلْمِسْحِ وَ اَلْبِسَاطِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي حَالِ اَلتَّقِيَّةِ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِالسُّجُودِ عَلَى اَلثِّيَابِ فِي حَالِ اَلتَّقِيَّةِ»
thaqalaynMatn: Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, about a man who prostrates on a covering (mishh) or a carpet (bisat). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it if it is in a situation of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), and there is no harm in prostrating on clothes in a situation of taqiyyah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible to Pray in, from Clothing and Place, and What is Not Permissible to Pray in, from That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it was narrated from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said: I said: "A man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban?" He said: “If something from his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows and the beginning of his hairline, then it is sufficient for him."
arabicText: وروي عن أحدهما عليه السلام قال قلت الرجل يسجد وعليه قلنسوة أو عمامة؟ فقال إذا مس شئ من جبهته الارض فيما بين حاجبيه وقصاص شعره فقد اجزاءه عنه
thaqalaynMatn: And it was narrated from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said: I said: "A man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban?" He said: “If something from his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows and the beginning of his hairline, then it is sufficient for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb:
He asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best thing by which the servants may draw near to their Lord (azj). Imam (a.s) said: “I do not know anything, after recognition (of Allah (azj)), better than prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ مَا يَتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ اَلْعِبَادُ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ فَقَالَ« لاَ أَعْلَمُ شَيْئاً بَعْدَ اَلْمَعْرِفَةِ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb:
thaqalaynMatn: He asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best thing by which the servants may draw near to their Lord (azj). Imam (a.s) said: “I do not know anything, after recognition (of Allah (azj)), better than prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili from his father, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Satan remains fearful of the believer and in awe of him as long as he maintains the five daily prayers. But when he neglects them, Satan becomes bold against him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« لاَ يَزَالُ اَلشَّيْطَانُ ذَعِراً مِنْ أَمْرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِ هَائِباً لَهُ مَا حَافَظَ عَلَى اَلصَّلَوَاتِ اَلْخَمْسِ فَإِذَا ضَيَّعَهُنَّ اِجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Satan remains fearful of the believer and in awe of him as long as he maintains the five daily prayers. But when he neglects them, Satan becomes bold against him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: “Pray to Allah (swt) for me that He (azj) admits me into Paradise.” He (saws) said: “Help me by increasing your prostration.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتَى رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ اُدْعُ اَللَّهَ لِي أَنْ يُدْخِلَنِي اَلْجَنَّةَ فَقَالَ« أَعِنِّي بِكَثْرَةِ اَلسُّجُودِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: “Pray to Allah (swt) for me that He (azj) admits me into Paradise.” He (saws) said: “Help me by increasing your prostration.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Isma‘il ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “One obligatory prayer is better than twenty pilgrimages, and one pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given away in charity until nothing remains of it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةٌ فَرِيضَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عِشْرِينَ حَجَّةً وَ حَجَّةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ بَيْتٍ مَمْلُوٍّ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ يُتَصَدَّقُ مِنْهُ حَتَّى يَفْنَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Isma‘il ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “One obligatory prayer is better than twenty pilgrimages, and one pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given away in charity until nothing remains of it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah from Isa ibn Abdullah Al-Hashimi from his father from his grandfather:
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, the pillar of the religion is prayer, and it is the first thing from the deeds of the son of Adam that will be looked into. If it is sound, the rest of his deeds will be examined, and if it is not sound, none of his other deeds will be looked at.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« إِنَّ عَمُودَ اَلدِّينِ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ هِيَ أَوَّلُ مَا يُنْظَرُ فِيهِ مِنْ عَمَلِ اِبْنِ آدَمَ فَإِنْ صَحَّتْ نُظِرَ فِي عَمَلِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَصِحَّ لَمْ يُنْظَرْ فِي بَقِيَّةِ عَمَلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah from Isa ibn Abdullah Al-Hashimi from his father from his grandfather:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, the pillar of the religion is prayer, and it is the first thing from the deeds of the son of Adam that will be looked into. If it is sound, the rest of his deeds will be examined, and if it is not sound, none of his other deeds will be looked at.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And through this same chain of transmission:
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Waiting for the prayer after the prayer is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.’”
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« اِنْتِظَارُ اَلصَّلاَةِ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ كَنْزٌ مِنْ كُنُوزِ اَلْجَنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And through this same chain of transmission:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Waiting for the prayer after the prayer is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Wuhaib ibn Hafs from Abu Basir:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘If there were a river at the door of one of you, and he bathed in it five times a day, would there remain any filth on his body?’” (His companions) said: “No.” He (saws) said: “Then the likeness of prayer is that of a flowing river, whenever a person prays, it expiates the sins committed between the two prayers.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ وُهَيْبِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« لَوْ كَانَ عَلَى بَابِ دَارِ أَحَدِكُمْ نَهَرٌ فَاغْتَسَلَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مِنْهُ خَمْسَ مَرَّاتٍ أَ كَانَ يَبْقَى فِي جَسَدِهِ مِنَ اَلدَّرَنِ شَيْءٌ» قُلْنَا لاَ قَالَ« فَإِنَّ مَثَلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ كَمَثَلِ اَلنَّهَرِ اَلْجَارِي كُلَّمَا صَلَّى صَلاَةً كَفَّرَتْ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا مِنَ اَلذُّنُوبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Wuhaib ibn Hafs from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘If there were a river at the door of one of you, and he bathed in it five times a day, would there remain any filth on his body?’” (His companions) said: “No.” He (saws) said: “Then the likeness of prayer is that of a flowing river, whenever a person prays, it expiates the sins committed between the two prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu‘man, who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to me from ‘Urwah, the son of the sister of Shu‘ayb Al-‘Aqarqufi, from his uncle Shu‘ayb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever feels hunger, let him perform ablution and pray two units of prayer, then say: ‘O Lord, I am hungry, so feed me’. And he will be fed at that very moment.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عُرْوَةَاِ بْنِ أُخْتِ شُعَيْبٍ اَلْعَقَرْقُوفِيِّ عَنْ خَالِهِ شُعَيْبٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ جَاعَ فَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ وَ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ إِنِّي جَائِعٌ فَأَطْعِمْنِي فَإِنَّهُ يُطْعَمُ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu‘man, who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to me from ‘Urwah, the son of the sister of Shu‘ayb Al-‘Aqarqufi, from his uncle Shu‘ayb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever feels hunger, let him perform ablution and pray two units of prayer, then say: ‘O Lord, I am hungry, so feed me’. And he will be fed at that very moment.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Musa ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sa‘id from Isma‘il ibn Muslim from Ja‘far from his father (peace be upon them), who said:
(Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said): “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Everything has a face, and the face of your religion is prayer, so let none of you disgrace the face of his religion. And everything has a nose, and the nose of prayer is the takbir (saying Allahu Akbar).’”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَجْهٌ وَ وَجْهُ دِينِكُمُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَلاَ يَشِينَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ وَجْهَ دِينِهِ وَ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْفٌ وَ أَنْفُ اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Musa ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sa‘id from Isma‘il ibn Muslim from Ja‘far from his father (peace be upon them), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said): “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Everything has a face, and the face of your religion is prayer, so let none of you disgrace the face of his religion. And everything has a nose, and the nose of prayer is the takbir (saying Allahu Akbar).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Isma‘il ibn Yasar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Beware of laziness. Indeed, your Lord (azj) is Merciful and He (azj) rewards even a little. A man may pray two units of voluntary prayer, seeking by them the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of them. And he may give one dirham in charity, voluntarily, seeking by it the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of it. And he may fast a single day, voluntarily, seeking by it the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِيَّاكُمْ وَ اَلْكَسَلَ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ رَحِيمٌ يَشْكُرُ اَلْقَلِيلَ إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ لَيُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ تَطَوُّعاً يُرِيدُ بِهِمَا وَجْهَ اَللَّهِ فَيُدْخِلُهُ اَللَّهُ بِهِمَا اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ إِنَّهُ لَيَتَصَدَّقُ بِالدِّرْهَمِ تَطَوُّعاً يُرِيدُ بِهِ وَجْهَ اَللَّهِ فَيُدْخِلُهُ اَللَّهُ بِهِ اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ إِنَّهُ لَيَصُومُ اَلْيَوْمَ تَطَوُّعاً يُرِيدُ بِهِ وَجْهَ اَللَّهِ فَيُدْخِلُهُ اَللَّهُ بِهِ اَلْجَنَّةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Isma‘il ibn Yasar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Beware of laziness. Indeed, your Lord (azj) is Merciful and He (azj) rewards even a little. A man may pray two units of voluntary prayer, seeking by them the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of them. And he may give one dirham in charity, voluntarily, seeking by it the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of it. And he may fast a single day, voluntarily, seeking by it the Face (favour) of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) will admit him to Paradise because of it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Hamzah ibn Humran from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The likeness of prayer is that of the central pole of a tent; if the pole stands firm, the ropes, the pegs, and the covering are all of benefit; but if the pole breaks, then neither ropes, nor pegs, nor covering are of any benefit.’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ حَمْزَةَ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَثَلُ اَلصَّلاَةِ مَثَلُ عَمُودِ اَلْفُسْطَاطِ إِذَا ثَبَتَ اَلْعَمُودُ نَفَعَتِ اَلْأَطْنَابُ وَ اَلْأَوْتَادُ وَ اَلْغِشَاءُ وَ إِذَا اِنْكَسَرَ لَمْ يَنْفَعْ طُنُبٌ وَ لاَ وَتِدٌ وَ لاَ غِشَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Hamzah ibn Humran from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The likeness of prayer is that of the central pole of a tent; if the pole stands firm, the ropes, the pegs, and the covering are all of benefit; but if the pole breaks, then neither ropes, nor pegs, nor covering are of any benefit.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn Al-Bukhtari:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, accepts a single prayer from, He (swt) will not punish him. And whoever He (azj) accepts a good deed from, He (azj) will not punish him.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ قَبِلَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْهُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً لَمْ يُعَذِّبْهُ وَ مَنْ قَبِلَ مِنْهُ حَسَنَةً لَمْ يُعَذِّبْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn Al-Bukhtari:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Whoever Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, accepts a single prayer from, He (swt) will not punish him. And whoever He (azj) accepts a good deed from, He (azj) will not punish him.”

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Musa ibn Ja‘far from some of our companions from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah al-Dihqan from Wasil ibn Sulayman from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) said: ‘There is no prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before Allah (swt): ‘O people, rise to the fires you have kindled upon your backs and extinguish them with your prayer.’”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عُبَيْدِاَللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلدِّهْقَانِ عَنْ وَاصِلِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:« مَا مِنْ صَلاَةٍ يَحْضُرُ وَقْتُهَا إِلاَّ نَادَى مَلَكٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَللَّهِ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّاسُ قُومُوا إِلَى نِيرَانِكُمُ اَلَّتِي أَوْقَدْتُمُوهَا عَلَى ظُهُورِكُمْ فَأَطْفِئُوهَا بِصَلاَتِكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Musa ibn Ja‘far from some of our companions from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah al-Dihqan from Wasil ibn Sulayman from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) said: ‘There is no prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before Allah (swt): ‘O people, rise to the fires you have kindled upon your backs and extinguish them with your prayer.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abdillah from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) at al-Muzdalifah, and when we finished, He (a.s) turned to me and said: “O Aban, the five obligatory prayers, whoever upholds their limits and preserves their timings shall meet Allah (swt) on the Day of Judgment with a covenant by which He (azj) will admit him into Paradise. But whoever does not uphold their limits and does not preserve their timings shall meet Allah (swt) without a covenant; if He (azj) wills, He (azj) will punish him, and if He (azj) wills, He (azj) will forgive him.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِالْمُزْدَلِفَةِ فَلَمَّا اِنْصَرَفْتُ اِلْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ فَقَالَ« يَا أَبَانُ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلْخَمْسُ اَلْمَفْرُوضَاتُ مَنْ أَقَامَ حُدُودَهُنَّ وَ حَافَظَ عَلَى مَوَاقِيتِهِنَّ لَقِيَ اَللَّهَ يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ وَ لَهُ عِنْدَهُ عَهْدٌ يُدْخِلُهُ بِهِ اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُقِمْ حُدُودَهُنَّ وَ لَمْ يُحَافِظْ عَلَى مَوَاقِيتِهِنَّ لَقِيَ اَللَّهَ وَ لاَ عَهْدَ لَهُ إِنْ شَاءَ عَذَّبَهُ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ غَفَرَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abdillah from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) at al-Muzdalifah, and when we finished, He (a.s) turned to me and said: “O Aban, the five obligatory prayers, whoever upholds their limits and preserves their timings shall meet Allah (swt) on the Day of Judgment with a covenant by which He (azj) will admit him into Paradise. But whoever does not uphold their limits and does not preserve their timings shall meet Allah (swt) without a covenant; if He (azj) wills, He (azj) will punish him, and if He (azj) wills, He (azj) will forgive him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: “Indeed, the first thing by which the servant is taken to account is the prayer. If it is accepted, then everything else will be accepted; and if the prayer is raised at its appointed time, it returns to its owner white and radiant, saying, ‘You preserved me, may Allah (swt) preserve you.’ But if it is raised at other than its time and without fulfilling its limits, it returns to its owner black and dark, saying; ‘You neglected me, may Allah (swt) neglect you.’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ اَلْعَبْدُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَإِنْ قُبِلَتْ قُبِلَ مَا سِوَاهَا وَ إِنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا اِرْتَفَعَتْ فِي وَقْتِهَا رَجَعَتْ إِلَى صَاحِبِهَا وَهِيَ بَيْضَاءُ مُشْرِقَةٌ تَقُولُ حَفِظْتَنِي حَفِظَكَ اَللَّهُ وَإِذَا اِرْتَفَعَتْ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِهَا بِغَيْرِ حُدُودِهَا رَجَعَتْ إِلَى صَاحِبِهَا وَ هِيَ سَوْدَاءُ مُظْلِمَةٌ تَقُولُ ضَيَّعْتَنِي ضَيَّعَكَ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: “Indeed, the first thing by which the servant is taken to account is the prayer. If it is accepted, then everything else will be accepted; and if the prayer is raised at its appointed time, it returns to its owner white and radiant, saying, ‘You preserved me, may Allah (swt) preserve you.’ But if it is raised at other than its time and without fulfilling its limits, it returns to its owner black and dark, saying; ‘You neglected me, may Allah (swt) neglect you.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked the Righteous Servant (al Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Those who are heedless of their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘un 107:5). Imam (a.s) said: “It means neglecting (and wasting) it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَبْداً صَالِحاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« اَلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاٰتِهِمْ سٰاهُونَ» قَالَ« هُوَ اَلتَّضْيِيعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked the Righteous Servant (al Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Those who are heedless of their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘un 107:5). Imam (a.s) said: “It means neglecting (and wasting) it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was sitting in the mosque when a man entered, stood, and prayed. He (the man) did not perfect his bowing (ruku‘) or his prostration (sujud). So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If this man dies while continuing to pray like that, he will surely die upon a religion other than mine.’”
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« بَيْنَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ جَالِسٌ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ إِذْ دَخَلَ رَجُلٌ فَقَامَ فَصَلَّى فَلَمْ يُتِمَّ رُكُوعَهُ وَ لاَ سُجُودَهُ فَقَالَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« نَقَرَ كَنَقْرِ اَلْغُرَابِ لَئِنْ مَاتَ هَذَا وَ هَكَذَا صَلاَتُهُ لَيَمُوتَنَّ عَلَى غَيْرِ دِينِي»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was sitting in the mosque when a man entered, stood, and prayed. He (the man) did not perfect his bowing (ruku‘) or his prostration (sujud). So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If this man dies while continuing to pray like that, he will surely die upon a religion other than mine.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-‘Is ibn Al-Qasim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), fifty years may pass over a man, and Allah (swt) has not accepted from him a single prayer. So what could be more severe than this? By Allah (swt), you indeed know among your neighbors and your companions those whom, if they were to pray for one of you, you would not accept it from them due to their belittling of the prayer. Indeed, Allah (swt) does not accept except that which is good, so how can He (azj) accept that which is taken lightly?”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« وَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَيَأْتِي عَلَى اَلرَّجُلِ خَمْسُونَ سَنَةً مَا قَبِلَ اَللَّهُ مِنْهُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً فَأَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَشَدُّ مِنْ هَذَا وَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَعْرِفُونَ مِنْ جِيرَانِكُمْ وَ أَصْحَابِكُمْ مَنْ لَوْ كَانَ يُصَلِّي لِبَعْضِكُمْ مَا قَبِلَهَا مِنْهُ لاِسْتِخْفَافِهِ بِهَا إِنَّ اَللَّهَ لاَ يَقْبَلُ إِلاَّ اَلْحَسَنَ فَكَيْفَ يَقْبَلُ مَا اُسْتُخِفَّ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-‘Is ibn Al-Qasim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), fifty years may pass over a man, and Allah (swt) has not accepted from him a single prayer. So what could be more severe than this? By Allah (swt), you indeed know among your neighbors and your companions those whom, if they were to pray for one of you, you would not accept it from them due to their belittling of the prayer. Indeed, Allah (swt) does not accept except that which is good, so how can He (azj) accept that which is taken lightly?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the servant rises from prayer and performs it lightly (hastily), Allah (swt), the Exalted, says to His (azj) angels: ‘Do you not see My (azj) servant? It is as if he thinks the fulfillment of his needs lies in the hands of someone other than Me (azj). Does he not know that the fulfillment of his needs is in My (azj) hand?’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَامَ اَلْعَبْدُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَخَفَّفَ صَلاَتَهُ قَالَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِمَلاَئِكَتِهِ« أَ مَا تَرَوْنَ إِلَى عَبْدِي كَأَنَّهُ يَرَى أَنَّ قَضَاءَ حَوَائِجِهِ بِيَدِ غَيْرِي أَ مَا يَعْلَمُ أَنَّ قَضَاءَ حَوَائِجِهِ بِيَدِي»»
thaqalaynMatn: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the servant rises from prayer and performs it lightly (hastily), Allah (swt), the Exalted, says to His (azj) angels: ‘Do you not see My (azj) servant? It is as if he thinks the fulfillment of his needs lies in the hands of someone other than Me (azj). Does he not know that the fulfillment of his needs is in My (azj) hand?’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: “Those who guard their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘arij 70:34) & (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:9). Imam (a.s) said: “That refers to the obligatory prayers.” I asked: (about) “Those who are constant in their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘arij 70:23). Imam (a.s) said: “That refers to the supererogatory (nafilah) prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى« اَلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلىٰ صَلاٰتِهِمْ يُحٰافِظُونَ» قَالَ« هِيَ اَلْفَرِيضَةُ» قُلْتُ« اَلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلىٰ صَلاٰتِهِمْ دٰائِمُونَ» قَالَ« هِيَ اَلنَّافِلَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: “Those who guard their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘arij 70:34) & (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:9). Imam (a.s) said: “That refers to the obligatory prayers.” I asked: (about) “Those who are constant in their prayers” (Surah Al-Ma‘arij 70:23). Imam (a.s) said: “That refers to the supererogatory (nafilah) prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Isma‘il ibn Abi Ziyad from Ja‘far from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever recites a verse of obscene poetry during the day, his prayer will not be accepted from him that day; and whoever recites it at night, his prayer will not be accepted from him that night.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ تَمَثَّلَ بِبَيْتِ شِعْرٍ مِنَ اَلْخَنَا لَمْ يُقْبَلْ مِنْهُ صَلاَةٌ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ مَنْ تَمَثَّلَ بِاللَّيْلِ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ مِنْهُ صَلاَةٌ تِلْكَ اَللَّيْلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Isma‘il ibn Abi Ziyad from Ja‘far from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever recites a verse of obscene poetry during the day, his prayer will not be accepted from him that day; and whoever recites it at night, his prayer will not be accepted from him that night.”

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ahmad ibn Abdillah Al-Karkhi from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “One hajj is better than the world and all that is in it, and one obligatory prayer is better than a thousand hajj.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْكَرْخِيِّ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« حَجَّةٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ مَا فِيهَا وَ صَلاَةٌ فَرِيضَةٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ أَلْفِ حَجَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ahmad ibn Abdillah Al-Karkhi from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “One hajj is better than the world and all that is in it, and one obligatory prayer is better than a thousand hajj.”
