chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about what Allah (swt) has made obligatory in terms of prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Five prayers during the night and day." So I asked: "Has Allah (swt) named them and clarified them in His Book?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (saws); ‘Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:78)’ - And its decline (duluk) is its zenith. And between the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night are four prayers that He (azj) named, clarified, and set their times. And the darkness of the night is its midpoint. Then Imam (a.s) said: “And ‘(establish) the recitation of the dawn; indeed, the recitation of the dawn is ever witnessed’, this is (about) the fifth.” And He (azj) said in that; ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day’, and its two ends are Maghrib and Ghadah (fajr, morning). And ‘in the early part of the night’, this is the night prayer (Isha). And He (azj) said; ‘Guard strictly [five] the prayers, especially the middle prayer’, and that is the Dhuhr prayer, and it was the first prayer that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed. It is the middle of the day and the middle of the two daytime prayers: the morning and the ‘Asr prayers.” And in some recitations it is; ‘Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the ‘Asr prayer, and stand before Allah (swt) devoutly.’" Imam (a.s) said: "This verse was revealed on the day of Jumu‘ah while the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was on a journey, and he performed qunut in it and left it as it was in travel and in residence. And He (saws) added two rak‘ahs for the resident, and the two rak‘ahs that the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, added on the day of Jumu‘ah for the resident were because of the two sermons with the Imam (of prayer). So whoever prays on the day of Jumu‘ah not in congregation, let him pray it four rak‘ahs like the Dhuhr prayer on the other days."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« خَمْسُ صَلَوَاتٍُ فِي اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ» فَقُلْتُ هَلْ سَمَّاهُنَّ اَللَّهُ وَ بَيَّنَهُنَّ فِي كِتَابِهِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ قَالَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لِنَبِيِّهِ« أَقِمِ اَلصَّلاٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلىٰ غَسَقِ اَللَّيْلِ» وَ دُلُوكُهَا زَوَالُهَا فَفِيمَا بَيْنَ دُلُوكِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى غَسَقِ اَللَّيْلِ أَرْبَعُ صَلَوَاتٍُ سَمَّاهُنَّ وَبَيَّنَهُنَّ وَوَقَّتَهُنَّ وَ غَسَقُ اَللَّيْلِ اِنْتِصَافُهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ« وَقُرْآنَ اَلْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ اَلْفَجْرِ كٰانَ مَشْهُوداً» فَهَذِهِ اَلْخَامِسَةُ وَقَالَ فِي ذَلِكَ« وَأَقِمِ اَلصَّلاٰةَ طَرَفَيِ اَلنَّهٰارِ» وَطَرَفَاهُ اَلْمَغْرِبُ وَاَلْغَدَاةُ« وَزُلَفاً مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ» وَ هِيَ صَلاَةُ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ قَالَ« حٰافِظُوا عَلَى اَلصَّلَوٰاتِ وَ اَلصَّلاٰةِ اَلْوُسْطىٰ» وَ هِيَ صَلاَةُ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ هِيَ أَوَّلُ صَلاَةٍ صَلاَّهَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ هِيَ وَسَطُ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ وَسَطُ صَلاَتَيْنِ بِالنَّهَارِ صَلاَةِ اَلْغَدَاةِ وَ صَلاَةِ اَلْعَصْرِ» وَ فِي بَعْضِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ«« حٰافِظُوا عَلَى اَلصَّلَوٰاتِ وَ اَلصَّلاٰةِ اَلْوُسْطىٰ» صَلاَةِ اَلْعَصْرِ« وَ قُومُوا لِلّٰهِ قٰانِتِينَ»» قَالَ« فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ اَلْآيَةُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي سَفَرٍ فَقَنَتَ فِيهَا وَ تَرَكَهَا عَلَى حَالِهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ اَلْحَضَرِ وَ أَضَافَ لِلْمُقِيمِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ إِنَّمَا وُضِعَتِ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَللَّتَانِ أَضَافَهُمَا اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ لِلْمُقِيمِ لِمَكَانِ اَلْخُطْبَتَيْنِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَمَنْ صَلَّى يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي غَيْرِ جَمَاعَةٍ فَلْيُصَلِّهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ كَصَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْأَيَّامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about what Allah (swt) has made obligatory in terms of prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Five prayers during the night and day." So I asked: "Has Allah (swt) named them and clarified them in His Book?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (saws); ‘Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:78)’ - And its decline (duluk) is its zenith. And between the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night are four prayers that He (azj) named, clarified, and set their times. And the darkness of the night is its midpoint. Then Imam (a.s) said: “And ‘(establish) the recitation of the dawn; indeed, the recitation of the dawn is ever witnessed’, this is (about) the fifth.” And He (azj) said in that; ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day’, and its two ends are Maghrib and Ghadah (fajr, morning). And ‘in the early part of the night’, this is the night prayer (Isha). And He (azj) said; ‘Guard strictly [five] the prayers, especially the middle prayer’, and that is the Dhuhr prayer, and it was the first prayer that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed. It is the middle of the day and the middle of the two daytime prayers: the morning and the ‘Asr prayers.” And in some recitations it is; ‘Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the ‘Asr prayer, and stand before Allah (swt) devoutly.’" Imam (a.s) said: "This verse was revealed on the day of Jumu‘ah while the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was on a journey, and he performed qunut in it and left it as it was in travel and in residence. And He (saws) added two rak‘ahs for the resident, and the two rak‘ahs that the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, added on the day of Jumu‘ah for the resident were because of the two sermons with the Imam (of prayer). So whoever prays on the day of Jumu‘ah not in congregation, let him pray it four rak‘ahs like the Dhuhr prayer on the other days."

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about what is obligatory (fardh) in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “The time, purification, the qiblah, facing the direction (of Qibla), bowing, prostration, and supplication.” I asked: “And what about everything else besides that?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is Sunnah within the obligatory (prayer).”
arabicText: حَمَّادٌ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْفَرْضِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« اَلْوَقْتُ وَ اَلطَّهُورُ وَ اَلْقِبْلَةُ وَ اَلتَّوَجُّهُ وَ اَلرُّكُوعُ وَ اَلسُّجُودُ وَ اَلدُّعَاءُ» قُلْتُ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« سُنَّةٌ فِي فَرِيضَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s) about what is obligatory (fardh) in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “The time, purification, the qiblah, facing the direction (of Qibla), bowing, prostration, and supplication.” I asked: “And what about everything else besides that?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is Sunnah within the obligatory (prayer).”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Hammad ibn Isa:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Prayer has four thousand boundaries (limits).”
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« لِلصَّلاَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ حَدٍّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Hammad ibn Isa:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Prayer has four thousand boundaries (limits).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it was narrated from (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “Prayer has four thousand gates (aspects/rulings).”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« لِلصَّلاَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ بَابٍ»
thaqalaynMatn: And it was narrated from (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “Prayer has four thousand gates (aspects/rulings).”

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah said: Ibn Ribat narrated to me from Ibn Miskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family,) and said; “O Messenger of Allah (swt), inform me about Islam, its root, its branch, its peak, and its summit.” He (saws) said: “Its root is prayer, its branch is zakat, and its peak and summit is striving in the way of Allah (swt), the Exalted.” He (the man) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), inform me about the gates of goodness.” He (saws) said: “Fasting is a shield, charity erases sin, and the standing of a man in the depths of the night while he privately converses with his Lord (azj).” Then the Prophet (saws) recited: ‘Their sides forsake their beds, they call upon their Lord (azj) in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them, they spend’ (Surah Al-Sajdah 32:16).
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي اِبْنُ رِبَاطٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَقَالَ يَارَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ أَصْلِهِ وَ فَرْعِهِ وَ ذِرْوَتِهِ وَ سَنَامِهِ فَقَالَ« أَصْلُهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ فَرْعُهُ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ ذِرْوَتُهُ وَ سَنَامُهُ اَلْجِهَادُ فِي سَبِيلِ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى» قَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَبْوَابِ اَلْخَيْرِ قَالَ« اَلصِّيَامُ جُنَّةٌ وَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ تُذْهِبُ اَلْخَطِيئَةَ وَ قِيَامُ اَلرَّجُلِ فِي جَوْفِ اَللَّيْلِ يُنَاجِي رَبَّهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ«« تَتَجٰافىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ اَلْمَضٰاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَمِمّٰا رَزَقْنٰاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah said: Ibn Ribat narrated to me from Ibn Miskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family,) and said; “O Messenger of Allah (swt), inform me about Islam, its root, its branch, its peak, and its summit.” He (saws) said: “Its root is prayer, its branch is zakat, and its peak and summit is striving in the way of Allah (swt), the Exalted.” He (the man) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), inform me about the gates of goodness.” He (saws) said: “Fasting is a shield, charity erases sin, and the standing of a man in the depths of the night while he privately converses with his Lord (azj).” Then the Prophet (saws) recited: ‘Their sides forsake their beds, they call upon their Lord (azj) in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them, they spend’ (Surah Al-Sajdah 32:16).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Ibn Faddal from Marwan from ‘Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
We were sitting with Abu Abdillah (a.s) at Mina when a man said to him: “What do you say about the nawafil (supererogatory prayers)?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are obligatory (faridah).” We were alarmed, and the man was alarmed too. Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “I only mean the night prayer upon the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Indeed, Allah (swt) says: ‘And in the night, keep vigil with it as a supererogatory act for you’” (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:79).
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: كُنَّا جُلُوساً عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِمِنًى فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلنَّوَافِلِ فَقَالَ« فَرِيضَةٌ» قَالَ فَفَزِعْنَا وَفَزِعَ اَلرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« إِنَّمَا أَعْنِي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ عَلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ يَقُولُ« وَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نٰافِلَةً لَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Ibn Faddal from Marwan from ‘Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We were sitting with Abu Abdillah (a.s) at Mina when a man said to him: “What do you say about the nawafil (supererogatory prayers)?” Imam (a.s) said: “They are obligatory (faridah).” We were alarmed, and the man was alarmed too. Then Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “I only mean the night prayer upon the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Indeed, Allah (swt) says: ‘And in the night, keep vigil with it as a supererogatory act for you’” (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:79).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 259

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl Al-Kufi from Sa‘d ibn Abi ‘Amr al-Jallab, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The two units of the Fajr prayer (the supererogatory rak‘ahs before the obligatory Fajr), if I miss them, should I make them up?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said: “Why? Are they obligatory?” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, established them as a Sunnah. And whatever the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, establishes as a Sunnah is an obligation.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي عَمْرٍو اَلْجَلاَّبِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَكْعَتَا اَلْفَجْرِ تَفُوتُنِي أَ فَأُصَلِّيهِمَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ لِمَ أَ فَرِيضَةٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ« رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ سَنَّهُمَا فَمَا سَنَّ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَهُوَ فَرْضٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl Al-Kufi from Sa‘d ibn Abi ‘Amr al-Jallab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The two units of the Fajr prayer (the supererogatory rak‘ahs before the obligatory Fajr), if I miss them, should I make them up?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said: “Why? Are they obligatory?” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, established them as a Sunnah. And whatever the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, establishes as a Sunnah is an obligation.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 259

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is a Sunnah, not an obligation (faridah).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« سُنَّةٌ لَيْسَتْ بِفَرِيضَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “It is a Sunnah, not an obligation (faridah).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 260

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from ‘Ubayd from his father:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The witr prayer is recorded in the Book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, as obligatory (wajib); it is the witr of the night, and the Maghrib prayer is the witr of the day.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْوَتْرُ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَاجِبٌ وَ هُوَ وَتْرُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ وَتْرُ اَلنَّهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from ‘Ubayd from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The witr prayer is recorded in the Book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, as obligatory (wajib); it is the witr of the night, and the Maghrib prayer is the witr of the day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 260

chapter: Chapter on the Merit of Prayer, and What is Obligatory and Recommended from It
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Wahb or from Al-Sakuni from Ja‘far from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Perform voluntary prayers during the hour of heedlessness, even if it is only two light rak‘ahs, for they will bring about the abode of honor.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), what is the hour of heedlessness?” He (saws) said: “It is the time between Maghrib and Isha.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ وَهْبٍ أَوْ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« تَنَفَّلُوا فِي سَاعَةِ اَلْغَفْلَةِ وَ لَوْ بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ خَفِيفَتَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُمَا يُورِثَانِ دَارَ اَلْكَرَامَةِ» قِيلَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ وَ مَا سَاعَةُ اَلْغَفْلَةِ قَالَ« مَابَيْنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Wahb or from Al-Sakuni from Ja‘far from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Perform voluntary prayers during the hour of heedlessness, even if it is only two light rak‘ahs, for they will bring about the abode of honor.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), what is the hour of heedlessness?” He (saws) said: “It is the time between Maghrib and Isha.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 260

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to me from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to me from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 260

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Miskan from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مَالِكٍ اَلْجُهَنِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Miskan from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn Yunus from the Righteous Servant (al Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن زياد عن منصور بن يونس عن العبد الصالح عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول إذا زالت الشمس فقد دخل وقت الصلاتين
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn Yunus from the Righteous Servant (al Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Miskan from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن أبي حمزة عن ابن مسكان عن مالك الجهني قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن وقت الظهر فقال إذا زالت الشمس فقد دخل وقت الصلاتين
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Miskan from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Mithami and others from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed Dhuhr when the sun had just passed its zenith. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ وَغَيْرِهِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ حِينَ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Mithami and others from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who prayed Dhuhr when the sun had just passed its zenith. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from ‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who intends to tend to a need or to sleep when the sun passes its zenith, so he begins to pray Dhuhr at that time. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ عَلاَءٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ اَلْحَاجَةَ أَوِ اَلنَّوْمَ حِينَ تَزُولُ اَلشَّمْسُ فَجَعَلَ يُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى حِينَئِذٍ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from ‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who intends to tend to a need or to sleep when the sun passes its zenith, so he begins to pray Dhuhr at that time. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ali ibn Al-Nu‘man and Ibn Ribat from Sa‘id al-A‘raj from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer, is it when the sun passes its zenith? Imam (a.s) said: “After the zenith by the measure of a footstep (qadam) or so, except in travel or on the day of Jumu‘ah, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ وَ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلْأَعْرَجِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ أَهُوَ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ« بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ بِقَدَمٍ أَوْ نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ أَوْ يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَإِنَّ وَقْتَهَا إِذَا زَالَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ali ibn Al-Nu‘man and Ibn Ribat from Sa‘id al-A‘raj from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer, is it when the sun passes its zenith? Imam (a.s) said: “After the zenith by the measure of a footstep (qadam) or so, except in travel or on the day of Jumu‘ah, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan from Ibn Miskan from Isma‘il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “After the sun’s zenith by a footstep (qadam) or so, except on the day of Jumu‘ah or while traveling, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.”
arabicText: عنه عن صفوان عن ابن مسكان عن إسماعيل بن عبد الخالق قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن وقت الظهر قال بعد الزوال بقدم أو نحو ذلك إلا في يوم الجمعة أو في السفر فان وقتها حين تزول الشمس
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan from Ibn Miskan from Isma‘il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “After the sun’s zenith by a footstep (qadam) or so, except on the day of Jumu‘ah or while traveling, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn ibn Hashim and Ibn Ribat and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the shadow is the length of one arm's span (dhira‘).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ وَ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ وَ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ وَ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn ibn Hashim and Ibn Ribat and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the time of Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “When the shadow is the length of one arm's span (dhira‘).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The time of Dhuhr is when the shadow reaches one arm's span (dhira‘).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ عَلَى ذِرَاعٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The time of Dhuhr is when the shadow reaches one arm's span (dhira‘).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do you know why the arm's span (dhira‘) and two arm's spans were set?" I asked: "Why?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer. You are allowed to perform supererogatory (nafilah) prayers from the sun's zenith until the shadow reaches an arm's span. When it reaches an arm's span, you must begin with the obligatory (faridah) prayer and leave the supererogatory."
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: أَ تَدْرِي لِمَ جُعِلَ اَلذِّرَاعُ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَانِ قُلْتُ لِمَ قَالَ« لِمَكَانِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ لَكَ أَنْ تَتَنَفَّلَ مِنْ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى أَنْ يَبْلُغَ ذِرَاعاً فَإِذَا بَلَغَ ذِرَاعاً بَدَأْتَ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ تَرَكْتَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do you know why the arm's span (dhira‘) and two arm's spans were set?" I asked: "Why?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer. You are allowed to perform supererogatory (nafilah) prayers from the sun's zenith until the shadow reaches an arm's span. When it reaches an arm's span, you must begin with the obligatory (faridah) prayer and leave the supererogatory."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Al-Mithami from Aban from Isma‘il Al-Ju‘fi:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do you know why the arm's span (dhira‘) and the two arm's spans were set?" I asked: "Why?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer, so that time would not be taken from this (obligatory prayer) and entered into that (supererogatory prayer)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتَدْرِي لِمَ جُعِلَ اَلذِّرَاعُ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَانِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ لِمَ قَالَ« لِمَكَانِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ لِئَلاَّ يُؤْخَذَ مِنْ وَقْتِ هَذِهِ وَ يُدْخَلَ فِي وَقْتِ هَذِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Al-Mithami from Aban from Isma‘il Al-Ju‘fi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do you know why the arm's span (dhira‘) and the two arm's spans were set?" I asked: "Why?" Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer, so that time would not be taken from this (obligatory prayer) and entered into that (supererogatory prayer)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ja‘far ibn Muthanna al-‘Attar from Husayn ibn Uthman al-Rawwasi from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “When the sun passes its zenith, pray eight rak‘ahs, then pray the obligatory Dhuhr prayer, four rak‘ahs. When you finish your ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), whether you shortened or prolonged it, then pray the ‘Asr prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُثَنًّى اَلْعَطَّارِ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ اَلرَّوَّاسِيِّ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَصَلِّ ثَمَانَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ صَلِّ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ أَرْبَعاً فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ قَصَّرْتَ أَوْ طَوَّلْتَ فَصَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ja‘far ibn Muthanna al-‘Attar from Husayn ibn Uthman al-Rawwasi from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “When the sun passes its zenith, pray eight rak‘ahs, then pray the obligatory Dhuhr prayer, four rak‘ahs. When you finish your ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), whether you shortened or prolonged it, then pray the ‘Asr prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-Harith ibn Mughirah from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said:
I was measuring the position of the sun before Abu Abdillah (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: “O ‘Umar, shall I inform you of something clearer than this?” I said: “Yes, may I be ransomed for you.” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of Dhuhr has entered, except that before it is the ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), and that is up to you, if you shorten it, then when you finish your ‘subhah’, and if you lengthen it, then when you finish your ‘subhah’.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ بْنِ مُغِيرَةَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ قَالَ: كُنْتُ أَقِيسُ اَلشَّمْسَ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ« يَا عُمَرُ أَ لاَ أُنَبِّئُكَ بِأَبْيَنَ مِنْ هَذَا» قَالَ قُلْتُ بَلَى جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ اَلظُّهْرُ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا سُبْحَةً وَ ذَلِكَ إِلَيْكَ فَإِنْ أَنْتَ خَفَّفْتَ فَحِينَ تَفْرُغُ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ وَ إِنْ طَوَّلْتَ فَحِينَ تَفْرُغُ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-Harith ibn Mughirah from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was measuring the position of the sun before Abu Abdillah (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: “O ‘Umar, shall I inform you of something clearer than this?” I said: “Yes, may I be ransomed for you.” Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, the time of Dhuhr has entered, except that before it is the ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), and that is up to you, if you shorten it, then when you finish your ‘subhah’, and if you lengthen it, then when you finish your ‘subhah’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Dhurayh al-Muharibi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Some people asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) while I was present. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, it is the time (for prayer); nothing holds you back from it except your subhah (supererogatory prayer), whether you lengthen it or shorten it.” Then some of the people said: “We pray the Dhuhr when the shadow is two feet in length and the ‘Asr when it is four feet.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Half of that is more beloved to me.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ اَلْمُحَارِبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُنَاسٌ وَأَنَا حَاضِرٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَهُوَ وَقْتٌ لاَ يَحْبِسُكَ مِنْهَا إِلاَّ سُبْحَتُكَ تُطِيلُهَا أَوْ تَقْصُرُهَا» فَقَالَ بَعْضُ اَلْقَوْمِ إِنَّا نُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى إِذَا كَانَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْنِ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اَلنِّصْفُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Dhurayh al-Muharibi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Some people asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) while I was present. Imam (a.s) said: “When the sun passes its zenith, it is the time (for prayer); nothing holds you back from it except your subhah (supererogatory prayer), whether you lengthen it or shorten it.” Then some of the people said: “We pray the Dhuhr when the shadow is two feet in length and the ‘Asr when it is four feet.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Half of that is more beloved to me.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Ibn Bukayr from his father from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “I prayed Dhuhr on a cloudy day, and then the sky cleared, and I realized that I had prayed just as the day had started to decline.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not repeat it, (but) do not do it again.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ فِي يَوْمِ غَيْمٍ فَانْجَلَتْ فَوَجَدْتُنِي صَلَّيْتُ حِينَ زَالَ اَلنَّهَارُ قَالَ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُعِدْ وَ لاَ تَعُدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Ibn Bukayr from his father from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “I prayed Dhuhr on a cloudy day, and then the sky cleared, and I realized that I had prayed just as the day had started to decline.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not repeat it, (but) do not do it again.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Abi Bishr from Ma‘bad ibn Maysarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “When the sun passes its zenith during the length of the day, is it permissible for a man to pray Dhuhr and ‘Asr (immediately)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but I do not like that he should do so every day.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بِشْرٍ عَنْ مَعْبَدِ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فِي طُولِ اَلنَّهَارِ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ ذَلِكَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Abi Bishr from Ma‘bad ibn Maysarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “When the sun passes its zenith during the length of the day, is it permissible for a man to pray Dhuhr and ‘Asr (immediately)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but I do not like that he should do so every day.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I fast, and I do not take a midday nap until the sun passes its zenith. When it passes, I pray my supererogatory prayers, then I pray Dhuhr, then I pray my supererogatory prayers, then I pray ‘Asr, and then I sleep, and this is before the people pray.” Imam (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, when the sun passes its zenith, the time has entered. But I dislike for you to take that (early time) as a constant habit.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَصُومُ فَلاَ أَقِيلُ حَتَّى تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ صَلَّيْتُ نَوَافِلِي ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتُ نَوَافِلِي ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتُ اَلْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ نِمْتُ وَ ذَلِكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلنَّاسُ فَقَالَ« يَا زُرَارَةُ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ اَلْوَقْتُ وَ لَكِنِّي أَكْرَهُ لَكَ أَنْ تَتَّخِذَهُ وَقْتاً دَائِماً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I fast, and I do not take a midday nap until the sun passes its zenith. When it passes, I pray my supererogatory prayers, then I pray Dhuhr, then I pray my supererogatory prayers, then I pray ‘Asr, and then I sleep, and this is before the people pray.” Imam (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, when the sun passes its zenith, the time has entered. But I dislike for you to take that (early time) as a constant habit.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from ‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: A man from the people of Madinah said to me: “O Aba Ja‘far, why do I not see you performing voluntary prayers between the adhan and the iqamah as the people do?” I (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said: “When we want to perform voluntary prayers, we perform them at a time other than the time of an obligatory prayer. Once the time for an obligatory prayer enters, there is no voluntary prayer.”
arabicText: روى ذلك الحسن بن محمد بن سماعة عن عبد الله بن جبلة عن علا عن محمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قال لي رجل من أهل المدينة يا أبا جعفر مالي لا أراك تتطوع بين الاذان والاقامة كما يصنع الناس؟ قال قلت إنا إذا أردنا أن نتطوع كان تطوعنا في غير وقت فريضة فإذا دخلت الفريضة لا تطوع
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from ‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: A man from the people of Madinah said to me: “O Aba Ja‘far, why do I not see you performing voluntary prayers between the adhan and the iqamah as the people do?” I (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said: “When we want to perform voluntary prayers, we perform them at a time other than the time of an obligatory prayer. Once the time for an obligatory prayer enters, there is no voluntary prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar narrated from Najiyyah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “The time for prayer comes upon me, should I begin with the supererogatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, begin with the obligatory prayer and make up the supererogatory prayer afterward.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ نَجِيَّةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تُدْرِكُنِي اَلصَّلاَةُ فَأَبْدَأُ بِالنَّافِلَةِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« لاَ اِبْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ اِقْضِ اَلنَّافِلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar narrated from Najiyyah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “The time for prayer comes upon me, should I begin with the supererogatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, begin with the obligatory prayer and make up the supererogatory prayer afterward.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Khalid and ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Thabit from Ziyad ibn Abi Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “When the obligatory prayer is present, begin with it; it will not harm you if you leave the supererogatory prayer that comes before it.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ وَ عُبَيْسِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ عَنْ ثَابِتٍ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ أَبِي غِيَاثٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا حَضَرَتِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةُ فَابْدَأْ بِهَا فَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ مَا قَبْلَهَا مِنَ اَلنَّافِلَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Khalid and ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Thabit from Ziyad ibn Abi Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “When the obligatory prayer is present, begin with it; it will not harm you if you leave the supererogatory prayer that comes before it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Wuhaib ibn Hafs from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In residence (when not traveling), the prayer is eight rak‘ahs after the sun has passed its zenith, during the time between you and when two-thirds of a shadow’s length (qamah) passes. When two-thirds of the qamah have passed, you must begin with the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ وُهَيْبِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ ثَمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ مَا بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ ثُلُثَا اَلْقَامَةِ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ ثُلُثَا اَلْقَامَةِ بَدَأْتَ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Wuhaib ibn Hafs from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “In residence (when not traveling), the prayer is eight rak‘ahs after the sun has passed its zenith, during the time between you and when two-thirds of a shadow’s length (qamah) passes. When two-thirds of the qamah have passed, you must begin with the obligatory prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Jabalah from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The prayer in residence (not while traveling) is eight rak‘ahs after the sun has passed its zenith, during the time between you and when two-thirds of a shadow’s length (qamah) passes. When two-thirds of the qamah have passed, you must begin with the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: عنه عن ابن جبلة عن علي بن أبي حمزة عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال الصلاة في الحضر ثماني ركعات إذا زالت الشمس ما بينك وبين أن يذهب ثلثا القامة فإذا ذهب ثلثا القامة بدأت بالفريضة
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Jabalah from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The prayer in residence (not while traveling) is eight rak‘ahs after the sun has passed its zenith, during the time between you and when two-thirds of a shadow’s length (qamah) passes. When two-thirds of the qamah have passed, you must begin with the obligatory prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim from Ibn Miskan from Al-Halabi: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray Dhuhr when the shadow reached an arm’s span (dhira‘) and ‘Asr at about the same measure.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ عَلَى ذِرَاعٍ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ عَلَى نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynMatn: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim from Ibn Miskan from Al-Halabi: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray Dhuhr when the shadow reached an arm’s span (dhira‘) and ‘Asr at about the same measure.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mithami from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best time for Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "An arm’s span (dhira‘) after the sun’s zenith." I asked: "Is it the same in winter and summer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ قَالَ« ذِرَاعٌ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فِي اَلشِّتَاءِ وَ اَلصَّيْفِ سَوَاءٌ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mithami from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the best time for Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "An arm’s span (dhira‘) after the sun’s zenith." I asked: "Is it the same in winter and summer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who said:
I wrote to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom. Our companions have narrated from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them, that they both said: ‘When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered, except that before them is a subhah (supererogatory prayer), which if you wish, you may lengthen, and if you wish, you may shorten.’ And some of your followers have narrated from them (Imams (a.s)) that: ‘The time of Dhuhr is after two footsteps from the zenith, and the time of ‘Asr is after four footsteps from the zenith. If you pray before that, it does not suffice; and some say it does suffice, but the preference is in waiting for two or four footsteps.’ And I wished, may I be your ransom, to know the correct position regarding the virtue of the timing.” So Imam (a.s) wrote: “The two footsteps and the four footsteps are both correct.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رَوَى أَصْحَابُنَا عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِمَا سُبْحَةً إِنْ شِئْتَ طَوَّلْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَصَّرْتَ» وَ رَوَى بَعْضُ مَوَالِيكَ عَنْهُمَا« أَنَّ وَقْتَ اَلظُّهْرِ عَلَى قَدَمَيْنِ مِنَ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ وَقْتَ اَلْعَصْرِ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ مِنَ اَلزَّوَالِ فَإِنْ صَلَّيْتَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يُجْزِكَ وَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ يُجْزِي وَ لَكِنَّ اَلْفَضْلَ فِي اِنْتِظَارِ اَلْقَدَمَيْنِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ» وَ قَدْ أَحْبَبْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مَوْضِعَ اَلْفَضْلِ فِي اَلْوَقْتِ فَكَتَبَ« اَلْقَدَمَانِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ صَوَابٌ جَمِيعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom. Our companions have narrated from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them, that they both said: ‘When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered, except that before them is a subhah (supererogatory prayer), which if you wish, you may lengthen, and if you wish, you may shorten.’ And some of your followers have narrated from them (Imams (a.s)) that: ‘The time of Dhuhr is after two footsteps from the zenith, and the time of ‘Asr is after four footsteps from the zenith. If you pray before that, it does not suffice; and some say it does suffice, but the preference is in waiting for two or four footsteps.’ And I wished, may I be your ransom, to know the correct position regarding the virtue of the timing.” So Imam (a.s) wrote: “The two footsteps and the four footsteps are both correct.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said:
One of our companions wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “It has been narrated from your forefathers regarding ‘one footstep, two footsteps, four footsteps, one height (qamah), two heights, a shadow equal to yourself, one arm’s span, and two arm’s spans.’” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: “Neither one footstep nor two footsteps (are required). When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered, and before them is a ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer) which is eight rak‘ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray the Dhuhr prayer. When you finish, between Dhuhr and ‘Asr there is a ‘subhah’ as well, which is eight rak‘ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray the ‘Asr prayer.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: كَتَبَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رُوِيَ عَنْ آبَائِكَ« اَلْقَدَمِ وَ اَلْقَدَمَيْنِ وَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ وَ اَلْقَامَةِ وَ اَلْقَامَتَيْنِ وَ ظِلِّ مِثْلِكَ وَ اَلذِّرَاعِ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَيْنِ» فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ اَلْقَدَمِ وَ لاَ اَلْقَدَمَيْنِ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا سُبْحَةٌ وَ هِيَ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِنْ شِئْتَ طَوَّلْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَصَّرْتَ ثُمَّ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَلظُّهْرِ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ كَانَ بَيْنَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ سُبْحَةٌ وَ هِيَ ثَمَانُ رَكَعَاتٍ إِنْ شِئْتَ طَوَّلْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَصَّرْتَ ثُمَّ صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: One of our companions wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “It has been narrated from your forefathers regarding ‘one footstep, two footsteps, four footsteps, one height (qamah), two heights, a shadow equal to yourself, one arm’s span, and two arm’s spans.’” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in reply: “Neither one footstep nor two footsteps (are required). When the sun passes its zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered, and before them is a ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer) which is eight rak‘ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray the Dhuhr prayer. When you finish, between Dhuhr and ‘Asr there is a ‘subhah’ as well, which is eight rak‘ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray the ‘Asr prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’d from Musa ibn Ja’far from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Maymun ibn Yusuf al-Nahhas from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, who said:
I wrote asking about the times of prayer, and he replied: "When the sun passes its zenith, pray your ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), and I prefer that you complete your obligatory prayer while the sun is at two footsteps (above the horizon). Then pray your ‘subhah’, and I prefer that you complete your ‘Asr prayer while the sun is at four footsteps. But if some urgent matter hastens you, then begin with the two obligatory prayers and make up the supererogatory afterward. And when the dawn rises, pray the obligatory (Fajr) prayer first, then afterward make up as much as you wish (of supererogatory prayers)."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ يُوسُفَ اَلنَّحَّاسِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفَرَجِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ أَسْأَلُ عَنْ أَوْقَاتِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَأَجَابَ« إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَصَلِّ سُبْحَتَكَ وَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَكُونَ فَرَاغُكَ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ اَلشَّمْسُ عَلَى قَدَمَيْنِ ثُمَّ صَلِّ سُبْحَتَكَ وَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَكُونَ فَرَاغُكَ مِنَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ اَلشَّمْسُ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ فَإِنْ عَجَّلَ بِكَ أَمْرٌ فَابْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَتَيْنِ وَ اِقْضِ اَلنَّافِلَةَ بَعْدَهُمَا فَإِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَصَلِّ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ ثُمَّ اِقْضِ بَعْدُ مَا شِئْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’d from Musa ibn Ja’far from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Maymun ibn Yusuf al-Nahhas from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote asking about the times of prayer, and he replied: "When the sun passes its zenith, pray your ‘subhah’ (supererogatory prayer), and I prefer that you complete your obligatory prayer while the sun is at two footsteps (above the horizon). Then pray your ‘subhah’, and I prefer that you complete your ‘Asr prayer while the sun is at four footsteps. But if some urgent matter hastens you, then begin with the two obligatory prayers and make up the supererogatory afterward. And when the dawn rises, pray the obligatory (Fajr) prayer first, then afterward make up as much as you wish (of supererogatory prayers)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ibn Ribat from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was the height of one qamah (the height of a man). When a shadow the length of one arm’s span (dhira‘) had passed, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr; when two arm’s spans had passed, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know why one arm’s span and two arm’s spans were set?" I said: "No." Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer: when the time of one arm’s span and two arm’s spans arrives, you must begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer."
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ حَائِطُ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَامَةً فَإِذَا مَضَى مِنْ فَيْئِهِ ذِرَاعٌ صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ إِذَا مَضَى مِنْ فَيْئِهِ ذِرَاعَانِ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« أَ تَدْرِي لِمَ جُعِلَ اَلذِّرَاعُ وَاَلذِّرَاعَانِ» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« مِنْ أَجْلِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلذِّرَاعِ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَيْنِ بَدَأْتَ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ تَرَكْتَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ibn Ribat from Ibn Miskan from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja‘far (a.s) say: "The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was the height of one qamah (the height of a man). When a shadow the length of one arm’s span (dhira‘) had passed, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr; when two arm’s spans had passed, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know why one arm’s span and two arm’s spans were set?" I said: "No." Imam (a.s) said: "Because of the obligatory prayer: when the time of one arm’s span and two arm’s spans arrives, you must begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn ‘Udays from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the shadow on the wall measured one arm’s span (dhira‘), would pray Dhuhr, and when it reached two arm’s spans, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr." I asked: "The walls differ; some are short and some are tall." Imam (a.s) said: "The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at that time was the height of a man (qamah). And the one arm’s span and two arm’s spans were set so that no supererogatory prayer would be performed during the time of an obligatory prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عُدَيْسٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفَيْءُ فِي اَلْجِدَارِ ذِرَاعاً صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ وَ إِذَا كَانَ ذِرَاعَيْنِ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ» قُلْتُ اَلْجُدْرَانُ تَخْتَلِفُ مِنْهَا قَصِيرٌ وَمِنْهَا طَوِيلٌ قَالَ« إِنَّ جِدَارَ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ كَانَ يَوْمَئِذٍ قَامَةً وَ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ اَلذِّرَاعُ وَ اَلذِّرَاعَانِ لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ تَطَوُّعٌ فِي وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn ‘Udays from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the shadow on the wall measured one arm’s span (dhira‘), would pray Dhuhr, and when it reached two arm’s spans, He (saws) would pray ‘Asr." I asked: "The walls differ; some are short and some are tall." Imam (a.s) said: "The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at that time was the height of a man (qamah). And the one arm’s span and two arm’s spans were set so that no supererogatory prayer would be performed during the time of an obligatory prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from ‘Ubays from Hammad from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
I heard the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, saying: "Indeed, the beginning of the time for Dhuhr is when the sun passes its zenith, and the end of its time is one height (qamah) from the zenith. The beginning of the time for ‘Asr is at one height, and the end of its time is two heights." I asked: "Is it the same in winter and summer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عُبَيْسٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ اَلْعَبْدَ اَلصَّالِحَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ أَوَّلَ وَقْتِ اَلظُّهْرِ زَوَالُ اَلشَّمْسِ وَآخِرَ وَقْتِهَا قَامَةٌ مِنَ اَلزَّوَالِ وَأَوَّلَ وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ قَامَةٌ وَآخِرَ وَقْتِهَا قَامَتَانِ» قُلْتُ فِي اَلشِّتَاءِ وَ اَلصَّيْفِ سَوَاءٌ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from ‘Ubays from Hammad from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, saying: "Indeed, the beginning of the time for Dhuhr is when the sun passes its zenith, and the end of its time is one height (qamah) from the zenith. The beginning of the time for ‘Asr is at one height, and the end of its time is two heights." I asked: "Is it the same in winter and summer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Khalil al-Abdi from Ziyad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Hanzalah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "In the Book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, it is stated: 'One qamah is one arm’s span (dhira‘), and two qamahs are two arm’s spans (dhira‘ayn).'"
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ خَلِيلٍ اَلْعَبْدِيِّ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اَلْقَامَةُ ذِرَاعٌ وَ اَلْقَامَتَانِ ذِرَاعَانِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Khalil al-Abdi from Ziyad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Hanzalah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "In the Book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, it is stated: 'One qamah is one arm’s span (dhira‘), and two qamahs are two arm’s spans (dhira‘ayn).'"

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn ibn Hashim and Ali ibn Ribat and Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "When the shadow is one arm’s span (dhira‘)." I asked: "An arm’s span from what?" Imam (a.s) said: "An arm’s span from your own shadow." I asked: "And the ‘Asr prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Half of that." I asked: "That is one hand-span (shibr)." Imam (a.s) said: "A hand-span, and is a hand-span not considerable?"
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ وَ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِبَاطٍ وَ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعاً» قُلْتُ ذِرَاعاً مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ قَالَ «ذِرَاعاً مِنْ فَيْئِكَ» قُلْتُ فَالْعَصْرُ قَالَ« اَلشَّطْرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ» قُلْتُ هَذَا شِبْرٌ قَالَ« شِبْرٌ أَ وَ لَيْسَ شِبْرٌ كَثِيراً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn ibn Hashim and Ali ibn Ribat and Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the Dhuhr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "When the shadow is one arm’s span (dhira‘)." I asked: "An arm’s span from what?" Imam (a.s) said: "An arm’s span from your own shadow." I asked: "And the ‘Asr prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "Half of that." I asked: "That is one hand-span (shibr)." Imam (a.s) said: "A hand-span, and is a hand-span not considerable?"

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ali ibn Shajarah from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I said to Him (a.s): "Our companions may be gathered in one place, and some of them get up to pray Dhuhr while others get up to pray ‘Asr." Imam (a.s) said: "All of that is permissible (wasi‘)."
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ شَجَرَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ يَكُونُ أَصْحَابُنَا فِي اَلْمَكَانِ مُجْتَمِعِينَ فَيَقُومُ بَعْضُهُمْ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ وَ بَعْضُهُمْ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ قَالَ« كُلُّ ذَلِكَ وَاسِعٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ali ibn Shajarah from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): "Our companions may be gathered in one place, and some of them get up to pray Dhuhr while others get up to pray ‘Asr." Imam (a.s) said: "All of that is permissible (wasi‘)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, by Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir by Hammad ibn Abi Talhah, who said Zurarah ibn A‘yan narrated to me:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Two men are praying at the same time, one of them hastens the ‘Asr prayer while the other delays the Dhuhr prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي زُرَارَةُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلاَنِ يُصَلِّيَانِ فِي وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ وَ أَحَدُهُمَا يُعَجِّلُ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ اَلْآخَرُ يُؤَخِّرُ اَلظُّهْرَ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, by Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir by Hammad ibn Abi Talhah, who said Zurarah ibn A‘yan narrated to me:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "Two men are praying at the same time, one of them hastens the ‘Asr prayer while the other delays the Dhuhr prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Ribat from Ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Sometimes I would enter upon Abu Ja‘far (a.s) after I had prayed Dhuhr and ‘Asr, and Imam (a.s) would say: "Have you prayed Dhuhr?" And I would say: "Yes, and (also) ‘Asr." Then Imam (a.s) would say: "I have not yet prayed Dhuhr." He (a.s) would then rise, calmly and without haste, perform ghusl (ritual bath) or perform wudu’ (ablution), then pray Dhuhr and then pray ‘Asr. And sometimes I would enter upon Him (a.s) while I had not yet prayed Dhuhr, and He would say: "Have you prayed Dhuhr?" And I would say: "No" Then Imam (a.s) would say: "I have already prayed Dhuhr and ‘Asr."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: رُبَّمَا دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ فَيَقُولُ« صَلَّيْتَ اَلظُّهْرَ» فَأَقُولُ نَعَمْ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ فَيَقُولُ« مَا صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ» فَيَقُومُ مُتَرَسِّلاً غَيْرَ مُسْتَعْجِلٍ فَيَغْتَسِلُ أَوْ يَتَوَضَّأُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ وَ رُبَّمَا دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَمْ أُصَلِّ اَلظُّهْرَ فَيَقُولُ« قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ اَلظُّهْرَ» فَأَقُولُ لاَ فَيَقُولُ« قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Ribat from Ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Sometimes I would enter upon Abu Ja‘far (a.s) after I had prayed Dhuhr and ‘Asr, and Imam (a.s) would say: "Have you prayed Dhuhr?" And I would say: "Yes, and (also) ‘Asr." Then Imam (a.s) would say: "I have not yet prayed Dhuhr." He (a.s) would then rise, calmly and without haste, perform ghusl (ritual bath) or perform wudu’ (ablution), then pray Dhuhr and then pray ‘Asr. And sometimes I would enter upon Him (a.s) while I had not yet prayed Dhuhr, and He would say: "Have you prayed Dhuhr?" And I would say: "No" Then Imam (a.s) would say: "I have already prayed Dhuhr and ‘Asr."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim Al-Bajali, from Salim Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
A man asked (Imam (a.s)) while I was present, and he said: "Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying Asr while others are praying Dhuhr." Imam (a.s) said: "I am the one who ordered them to do this. If they were to pray at the same time, they would be recognized and seized by their necks."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ اَلْبَجَلِيِّ عَنْ سَالِمٍ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَ إِنْسَانٌ وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ فَقَالَ رُبَّمَا دَخَلْتُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ وَ بَعْضُهُمْ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ فَقَالَ« أَنَا أَمَرْتُهُمْ بِهَذَا لَوْ صَلَّوْا عَلَى وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ لَعُرِفُوا فَأُخِذُوا بِرِقَابِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim Al-Bajali, from Salim Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked (Imam (a.s)) while I was present, and he said: "Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying Asr while others are praying Dhuhr." Imam (a.s) said: "I am the one who ordered them to do this. If they were to pray at the same time, they would be recognized and seized by their necks."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "(Archangel) Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, with the timings of the prayer. He (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the sun had passed the meridian and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Dhuhr. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the shadow had increased by the length of a span and ordered him, so he prayed Asr. Then he came to him when the sun had set and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Maghrib. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the twilight had disappeared and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Isha. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the dawn had risen and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Subh. Then he {Jibrail) came to Him (saws) on the next day when the shadow had increased by the length of a span and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Dhuhr. Then he {Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the shadow had increased by the length of two spans and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Asr. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the sun had set and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Maghrib. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when a third of the night had passed and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Isha. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the light of dawn had spread and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Subh." Then Imam (a.s) said: "What is between these two times is (considered) time (for the prayer)."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «أَتَى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِمَوَاقِيتِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَأَتَاهُ حِينَ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ زَادَ اَلظِّلُّ قَامَةً فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ سَقَطَ اَلشَّفَقُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْعِشَاءَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلصُّبْحَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ مِنَ اَلْغَدِ حِينَ زَادَ فِي اَلظِّلِّ قَامَةٌ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ زَادَ فِي اَلظِّلِّ قَامَتَانِ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ ذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ اَللَّيْلِ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلْعِشَاءَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ نَوَّرَ اَلصُّبْحُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى اَلصُّبْحَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« مَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَقْتٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "(Archangel) Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, with the timings of the prayer. He (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the sun had passed the meridian and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Dhuhr. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the shadow had increased by the length of a span and ordered him, so he prayed Asr. Then he came to him when the sun had set and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Maghrib. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the twilight had disappeared and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Isha. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the dawn had risen and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Subh. Then he {Jibrail) came to Him (saws) on the next day when the shadow had increased by the length of a span and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Dhuhr. Then he {Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the shadow had increased by the length of two spans and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Asr. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the sun had set and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Maghrib. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when a third of the night had passed and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Isha. Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) when the light of dawn had spread and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He (saws) prayed Subh." Then Imam (a.s) said: "What is between these two times is (considered) time (for the prayer)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir, from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, came", and he mentioned the narration similar to that of Abu Khadijah, except that instead of saying "one span and two spans (qamah and qamatayn)," he said "one forearm length and two forearm lengths (dhiraʿ and dhira’ayn)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَشِيرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتَى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» وَ ذَكَرَ مِثْلَ حَدِيثِ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ إِلاَّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ بَدَلَ اَلْقَامَةِ وَاَلْقَامَتَيْنِ« ذِرَاعٍ وَ ذِرَاعَيْنِ».
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir, from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, came", and he mentioned the narration similar to that of Abu Khadijah, except that instead of saying "one span and two spans (qamah and qamatayn)," he said "one forearm length and two forearm lengths (dhiraʿ and dhira’ayn)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, descended upon the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family," And he continued the narration similar to the first one, and he mentioned in place of "one span and two spans" (qamah wa qamatayn), "two feet and four feet" (qadamayn wa arbaʿat aqdam).
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ مُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« نَزَلَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ» وَ سَاقَ اَلْحَدِيثَ مِثْلَ اَلْأَوَّلِ وَ ذَكَرَ بَدَلَ اَلْقَامَةِ وَ اَلْقَامَتَيْنِ «قَدَمَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَةَ أَقْدَامٍ».
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, descended upon the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family," And he continued the narration similar to the first one, and he mentioned in place of "one span and two spans" (qamah wa qamatayn), "two feet and four feet" (qadamayn wa arbaʿat aqdam).
