chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Dharih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and informed him of the timings of the prayer. He (Jibrail) said: “Pray Fajr when the dawn breaks, and pray the first prayer (Dhuhr) when the sun passes the meridian, and pray Asr shortly after it, and pray Maghrib when the disk (of the sun) sets, and pray the night prayer (Isha) when the twilight disappears.” Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) on the next day and said: “Brighten the Fajr (delay it until the light is widespread), so He (saws) delayed it until the light spread. Then He (saws) delayed Dhuhr until the time when He (saws) had prayed Asr on the previous day, and He (saws) prayed Asr shortly after it, and He (saws) prayed Maghrib before the twilight disappeared, and He (saws) prayed the night prayer (Isha) when a third of the night had passed. Then he (Jibrail) said: “Between these two times there is time, and the best time is its beginning." Then He (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I dislike to burden my nation, I would have delayed it (Isha) until the middle of the night.’ And he (Dhurayh) said: "I said to Him (a.s);There are people among the companions of Abu Al-Khattab who delay Maghrib until the stars become entangled." He (Dhurayh) said: "He, (Imam al Sadiq (a.s)), said: ‘I disassociate myself before Allah (swt) from whoever does this intentionally.’"
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتَى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ مَوَاقِيتَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ صَلِّ اَلْفَجْرَ حِينَ يَنْشَقُّ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ صَلِّ اَلْأُولَى إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ بُعَيْدَهَا وَ صَلِّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ إِذَا سَقَطَ اَلْقُرْصُ وَ صَلِّ اَلْعَتَمَةَ إِذَا غَابَ اَلشَّفَقُ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ مِنَ اَلْغَدِ فَقَالَ أَسْفِرْ بِالْفَجْرِ فَأَسْفَرَ ثُمَّ أَخَّرَ اَلظُّهْرَ حَتَّى كَانَ اَلْوَقْتُ اَلَّذِي صَلَّى فِيهِ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ بُعَيْدَهَا وَ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ وَ صَلَّى اَلْعَتَمَةَ حِينَ ذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ اَللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا بَيْنَ هَذَيْنِ اَلْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتٌ وَ أَفْضَلُ اَلْوَقْتِ أَوَّلُهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« لَوْلاَ أَنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَى أُمَّتِي لَأَخَّرْتُهَا إِلَى نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ»» وَ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ أُنَاساً مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ يُمَسُّونَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ حَتَّى تَشْتَبِكَ اَلنُّجُومُ قَالَ فَقَالَ« أَبْرَأُ إِلَى اَللَّهِ مِمَّنْ يَفْعَلُ هَذَا مُتَعَمِّداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Dharih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and informed him of the timings of the prayer. He (Jibrail) said: “Pray Fajr when the dawn breaks, and pray the first prayer (Dhuhr) when the sun passes the meridian, and pray Asr shortly after it, and pray Maghrib when the disk (of the sun) sets, and pray the night prayer (Isha) when the twilight disappears.” Then he (Jibrail) came to Him (saws) on the next day and said: “Brighten the Fajr (delay it until the light is widespread), so He (saws) delayed it until the light spread. Then He (saws) delayed Dhuhr until the time when He (saws) had prayed Asr on the previous day, and He (saws) prayed Asr shortly after it, and He (saws) prayed Maghrib before the twilight disappeared, and He (saws) prayed the night prayer (Isha) when a third of the night had passed. Then he (Jibrail) said: “Between these two times there is time, and the best time is its beginning." Then He (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I dislike to burden my nation, I would have delayed it (Isha) until the middle of the night.’ And he (Dhurayh) said: "I said to Him (a.s);There are people among the companions of Abu Al-Khattab who delay Maghrib until the stars become entangled." He (Dhurayh) said: "He, (Imam al Sadiq (a.s)), said: ‘I disassociate myself before Allah (swt) from whoever does this intentionally.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mitami from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays outside of the (prescribed) time, his prayer is not considered a prayer.”
arabicText: الحسن بن محمد عن الميثمي عن معاوية بن وهب عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من صلى في غير وقت فلا صلاة له
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mitami from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays outside of the (prescribed) time, his prayer is not considered a prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from his father:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of Asr, it will be counted for me."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْعَطَّارِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَأَنْ أُصَلِّيَ اَلظُّهْرَ فِي وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُ صَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِنِّي إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ لَمْ تُحْتَسَبْ لِي وَإِذَا صَلَّيْتُ فِي وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ حُسِبَتْ لِي»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of Asr, it will be counted for me."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of Asr, it will be counted for me."
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن الحسن العطار عن عبد الله بن سليمان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال لان أصلي الظهر في وقت العصر أحب إلي من أن أصلي قبل أن تزول الشمس فاني إذا صليت قبل أن تزول الشمس لم تحسب لي وإذا صليت في وقت العصر حسبت لي
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of Asr, it will be counted for me."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prayed the morning prayer during the night, being deceived by the moon, and then slept until the sun rose, and was informed that he had prayed during the night. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his prayer.”
arabicText: علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة عن أبان عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في رجل صلى الغداة بليل غره من ذلك القمر ونام حتى طلعت الشمس فاخبر انه صلى بليل قال يعيد صلاته
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prayed the morning prayer during the night, being deceived by the moon, and then slept until the sun rose, and was informed that he had prayed during the night. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about praying during the night and day when neither the sun nor the moon nor the stars are visible. Imam (a.s) said: “Exert your judgment and face the qiblah as best as you can.”
arabicText: محمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن الحسين عن عثمان بن عيسى عن سماعة قال سألته عن الصلاة بالليل والنهار إذا لم تر الشمس ولا القمر ولا النجوم قال اجتهد رأيك وتعمد القبلة جهدك
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about praying during the night and day when neither the sun nor the moon nor the stars are visible. Imam (a.s) said: “Exert your judgment and face the qiblah as best as you can.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Abdillah Al-Farra' from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
A man from among our companions said to Imam (a.s): “Sometimes the time becomes unclear to us on a cloudy day.” Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know those birds you have in Iraq that are called roosters?" I said: “Yes”. Imam (a.s) said: "When their voices rise and they call to each other, then the sun has passed the meridian," or Imam (a.s) said: "then pray."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْفَرَّاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا رُبَّمَا اِشْتَبَهَ اَلْوَقْتُ عَلَيْنَا فِي يَوْمِ اَلْغَيْمِ فَقَالَ« تَعْرِفُ هَذِهِ اَلطُّيُورَ اَلَّتِي عِنْدَكُمْ بِالْعِرَاقِ يُقَالُ لَهَا اَلدِّيَكَةُ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« إِذَا اِرْتَفَعَتْ أَصْوَاتُهَا وَ تَجَاوَبَتْ فَقَدْ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ» أَوْ قَالَ« فَصَلِّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Abdillah Al-Farra' from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man from among our companions said to Imam (a.s): “Sometimes the time becomes unclear to us on a cloudy day.” Imam (a.s) said: "Do you know those birds you have in Iraq that are called roosters?" I said: “Yes”. Imam (a.s) said: "When their voices rise and they call to each other, then the sun has passed the meridian," or Imam (a.s) said: "then pray."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from Al-Nawfali from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar from a man who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I am a man who gives the call to prayer, and when it is a cloudy day, I do not know the time.” Imam (a.s) said: "When the rooster crows three continuous times, then the sun has passed the meridian and the time of prayer has entered."
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ مُؤَذِّنٌ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ اَلْغَيْمِ لَمْ أَعْرِفِ اَلْوَقْتَ قَالَ« إِذَا صَاحَ اَلدِّيكُ ثَلاَثَةَ أَصْوَاتٍ وِلاَءً فَقَدْ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from Al-Nawfali from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar from a man who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I am a man who gives the call to prayer, and when it is a cloudy day, I do not know the time.” Imam (a.s) said: "When the rooster crows three continuous times, then the sun has passed the meridian and the time of prayer has entered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Zurarah ibn A'yan and Bukayr ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah Al-Ijli who said:
Abu Ja'far (a.s) and Abu Abdullah (a.s), peace be upon them, said: "The time of Dhuhr is after the sun has passed the meridian by two feet, and the time of Asr is after that by two feet, and this is the beginning of the time until four feet have passed for Asr."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ وَ زُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ وَ بُكَيْرِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ اَلْعِجْلِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:« وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ قَدَمَانِ وَ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَدَمَانِ وَ هَذَا أَوَّلُ وَقْتٍ إِلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ لِلْعَصْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Zurarah ibn A'yan and Bukayr ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah Al-Ijli who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far (a.s) and Abu Abdullah (a.s), peace be upon them, said: "The time of Dhuhr is after the sun has passed the meridian by two feet, and the time of Asr is after that by two feet, and this is the beginning of the time until four feet have passed for Asr."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (a.s): “Is there a known limit between Dhuhr and Asr?” Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بَيْنَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ حَدٌّ مَعْرُوفٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja'far (a.s): “Is there a known limit between Dhuhr and Asr?” Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ubaydi from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said:
Al-Faqīh (the Jurist) said: "The end of the time for Asr is six and a half feet."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ قَالَ اَلْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« آخِرُ وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ سِتَّةُ أَقْدَامٍ وَ نِصْفٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ubaydi from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Faqīh (the Jurist) said: "The end of the time for Asr is six and a half feet."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Ya'qub Al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The prayer is not missed by one who intends to pray. The prayer of the day is not missed until the sun sets, and the prayer of the night is not missed until the dawn rises, and the prayer of Fajr is not missed until the sun rises."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَفُوتُ اَلصَّلاَةُ مَنْ أَرَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ لاَ يَفُوتُ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ حَتَّى تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ لاَ صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ لاَ صَلاَةُ اَلْفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Ya'qub Al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The prayer is not missed by one who intends to pray. The prayer of the day is not missed until the sun sets, and the prayer of the night is not missed until the dawn rises, and the prayer of Fajr is not missed until the sun rises."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Asr is at two arm's lengths, and whoever delays it until it reaches six feet, then he is the one who has neglected it."
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْعَصْرُ عَلَى ذِرَاعَيْنِ فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا حَتَّى تَصِيرَ عَلَى سِتَّةِ أَقْدَامٍ فَذَلِكَ اَلْمُضَيِّعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Asr is at two arm's lengths, and whoever delays it until it reaches six feet, then he is the one who has neglected it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ja'far, from Mathna, from Mansur ibn Hazim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Pray Asr at four feet (of shadow)." Mathna said: “Abu Basir said to me that Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Pray Asr on the day of Friday at six feet (of shadow).’"
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُثَنًّى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ »قَالَ مُثَنًّى قَالَ لِي أَبُو بَصِيرٍ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ عَلَى سِتَّةِ أَقْدَامٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ja'far, from Mathna, from Mansur ibn Hazim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Pray Asr at four feet (of shadow)." Mathna said: “Abu Basir said to me that Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Pray Asr on the day of Friday at six feet (of shadow).’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The one deprived of his family and his wealth is the one who neglects the Asr prayer." I asked: “What does 'deprived' mean?” Imam (a.s) said: "He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise." I asked: “And what is the neglect of it?” Imam (a.s) said: "He delays it until the sun yellows and sets."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنَّ اَلْمَوْتُورَ أَهْلَهُ وَ مَالَهُ مَنْ ضَيَّعَ صَلاَةَ اَلْعَصْرِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا اَلْمَوْتُورُ قَالَ« لاَ يَكُونُ لَهُ أَهْلٌ وَ لاَ مَالٌ فِي اَلْجَنَّةِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا تَضْيِيعُهَا قَالَ« يَدَعُهَا حَتَّى تَصْفَرَّ وَ تَغِيبَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The one deprived of his family and his wealth is the one who neglects the Asr prayer." I asked: “What does 'deprived' mean?” Imam (a.s) said: "He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise." I asked: “And what is the neglect of it?” Imam (a.s) said: "He delays it until the sun yellows and sets."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned the beginning of the time and its virtue. So I asked: “How should I manage the eight rak'ahs (of recommended prayers before Dhuhr)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Lighten them as much as you are able."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: ذَكَرَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَوَّلَ اَلْوَقْتِ وَ فَضْلَهُ فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ بِالثَّمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ« خَفِّفْ مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned the beginning of the time and its virtue. So I asked: “How should I manage the eight rak'ahs (of recommended prayers before Dhuhr)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Lighten them as much as you are able."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Safwan Al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked: “When should I pray Asr if I am not traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: "After Dhuhr by the measure of two-thirds of a foot (of shadow)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلْعَصْرُ مَتَى أُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا كُنْتُ فِي غَيْرِ سَفَرٍ قَالَ« عَلَى قَدْرِ ثُلُثَيْ قَدَمٍ بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Safwan Al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked: “When should I pray Asr if I am not traveling?” Imam (a.s) said: "After Dhuhr by the measure of two-thirds of a foot (of shadow)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Faddal from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Burayd from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) said: "When the redness disappears from the east, then the sun has set from the east of the earth and its west."
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا غَابَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ مِنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ فَقَدْ غَابَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ مِنْ شَرْقِ اَلْأَرْضِ وَ غَرْبِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Faddal from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Burayd from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: "When the redness disappears from the east, then the sun has set from the east of the earth and its west."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Dharih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the second time for Maghrib before the disappearance of the twilight."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَتَى اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي اَلْوَقْتِ اَلثَّانِي فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Dharih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at the second time for Maghrib before the disappearance of the twilight."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is from when the sun sets until the stars become intertwined."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ مِنْ حِينِ تَغِيبُ اَلشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَشْتَبِكَ اَلنُّجُومُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is from when the sun sets until the stars become intertwined."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ali ibn Al-Harith, from Bakkar, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "When the redness in the horizon changes and the yellowness disappears, and before the stars become intertwined."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَارِثِ عَنْ بَكَّارٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا تَغَيَّرَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ فِي اَلْأُفُقِ وَ ذَهَبَتِ اَلصُّفْرَةُ وَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَشْتَبِكَ اَلنُّجُومُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ali ibn Al-Harith, from Bakkar, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "When the redness in the horizon changes and the yellowness disappears, and before the stars become intertwined."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Mitami, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashimi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray Maghrib when the sun set, when its edge disappeared."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي اَلْمَغْرِبَ حِينَ تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ حَيْثُ يَغِيبُ حَاجِبُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Mitami, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashimi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to pray Maghrib when the sun set, when its edge disappeared."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the sun sets."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ حِينَ تَغِيبُ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the sun sets."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, by Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, byIbrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah and Abu Usamah:
They asked the Shaykh about Maghrib, and some of them said: “May I be your ransom, we wait until a star appears.” Imam (a.s) said: “This is (the practice of) the Khattabiyyah. Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, brought it (the timing of Maghrib) to Muhammad, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the disk (of the sun) had set."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنِ اَلصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ وَ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ قَالاَ: سَأَلُوا اَلشَّيْخَ عَنِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ جَعَلَنِيَ اَللَّهُ فِدَاكَ نَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ كَوْكَبٌ« فَقَالَ خَطَّابِيَّةٌ إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ نَزَلَ بِهَا عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حِينَ سَقَطَ اَلْقُرْصُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, by Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, byIbrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah and Abu Usamah:
thaqalaynMatn: They asked the Shaykh about Maghrib, and some of them said: “May I be your ransom, we wait until a star appears.” Imam (a.s) said: “This is (the practice of) the Khattabiyyah. Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, brought it (the timing of Maghrib) to Muhammad, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when the disk (of the sun) had set."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hammad ibn Udays, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Al-Qasim ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Abu Al-Khattab was mentioned, so Imam (a.s) cursed him, then said: "He did not retain anything (correctly). I had narrated to him (Abu Al-Khattab) that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, had the sun set for Him (a.s) in such-and-such a place, and He (a.s) prayed Maghrib at Al-Shajarah, and the distance between them was six miles. I informed him (Abu Al-Khattab) of this regarding travel, but he applied it to a state of residence."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ[ حُسَيْنِ خ ل] بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُدَيْسٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: ذُكِرَ أَبُو اَلْخَطَّابِ فَلَعَنَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَحْفَظُ شَيْئاً حَدَّثْتُهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ غَابَتْ لَهُ اَلشَّمْسُ فِي مَكَانِ كَذَا وَ كَذَا وَ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ بِالشَّجَرَةِ وَ بَيْنَهُمَا سِتَّةُ أَمْيَالٍ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِذَلِكَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَوَضَعَهُ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Husayn ibn Hammad ibn Udays, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Al-Qasim ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Al-Khattab was mentioned, so Imam (a.s) cursed him, then said: "He did not retain anything (correctly). I had narrated to him (Abu Al-Khattab) that the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, had the sun set for Him (a.s) in such-and-such a place, and He (a.s) prayed Maghrib at Al-Shajarah, and the distance between them was six miles. I informed him (Abu Al-Khattab) of this regarding travel, but he applied it to a state of residence."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him::
I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "It is from the setting of the sun until the disappearance of the twilight."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ قَالَ« مَا بَيْنَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى سُقُوطِ اَلشَّفَقِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him::
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "It is from the setting of the sun until the disappearance of the twilight."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said to me: "Delay Maghrib a little, for the sun sets from your location before it sets from ours."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي:« مَسُّوا بِالْمَغْرِبِ قَلِيلاً فَإِنَّ اَلشَّمْسَ تَغِيبُ مِنْ عِنْدِكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me: "Delay Maghrib a little, for the sun sets from your location before it sets from ours."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 276

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Waddah who said:
I wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him: “The disk disappears and the night approaches, then the night continues to rise, and the sun is hidden from us, and above the mountain a redness appears, and the callers to prayer make the Adhan among us; should I pray at that time and break my fast if I am fasting, or should I wait until the redness above the mountain disappears?” So Imam (a.s) wrote to me: "I see for you that you should wait until the redness disappears and take precaution for your religion."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ وَضَّاحٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلْعَبْدِ اَلصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَتَوَارَى اَلْقُرْصُ وَ يُقْبِلُ اَللَّيْلُ ثُمَّ يَزِيدُ اَللَّيْلُ اِرْتِفَاعاً وَ تَسْتَتِرُ عَنَّا اَلشَّمْسُ وَ تَرْتَفِعُ فَوْقَ اَلْجَبَلِ حُمْرَةٌ وَ يُؤَذِّنَ عِنْدَنَا اَلْمُؤَذِّنُونَ فَأُصَلِّي حِينَئِذٍ وَ أُفْطِرُ إِنْ كُنْتُ صَائِماً أَوْ أَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى تَذْهَبَ اَلْحُمْرَةُ اَلَّتِي فَوْقَ اَلْجَبَلِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ« أَرَى لَكَ أَنْ تَنْتَظِرَ حَتَّى تَذْهَبَ اَلْحُمْرَةُ وَ تَأْخُذَ بِالْحَائِطَةِ لِدِينِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Waddah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him: “The disk disappears and the night approaches, then the night continues to rise, and the sun is hidden from us, and above the mountain a redness appears, and the callers to prayer make the Adhan among us; should I pray at that time and break my fast if I am fasting, or should I wait until the redness above the mountain disappears?” So Imam (a.s) wrote to me: "I see for you that you should wait until the redness disappears and take precaution for your religion."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 276

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Jarud or Isma'il ibn Abi Sammal from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Jarud who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: "O Jarud, they are advised, but they do not accept. And when they hear something, they cry out about it, or if they are told something, they spread it. I (Imam al Sadiq (a.s)) said to them: ‘Delay Maghrib a little, but they abandoned it until the stars became intertwined. Now I pray it when the disk (of the sun) sets.’"
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ جَارُودٍ أَوْ[ أَوْ خ ل] إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ جَارُودٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَا جَارُودُ يُنْصَحُونَ فَلاَ يَقْبَلُونَ وَ إِذَا سَمِعُوا بِشَيْءٍ نَادَوْا بِهِ أَوْ حُدِّثُوا بِشَيْ ءٍأَذَاعُوهُ قُلْتُ لَهُمْ مَسُّوا بِالْمَغْرِبِ قَلِيلاً فَتَرَكُوهَا حَتَّى اِشْتَبَكَتِ اَلنُّجُومُ فَأَنَا اَلْآنَ أُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا سَقَطَ اَلْقُرْصُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Jarud or Isma'il ibn Abi Sammal from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Jarud who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: "O Jarud, they are advised, but they do not accept. And when they hear something, they cry out about it, or if they are told something, they spread it. I (Imam al Sadiq (a.s)) said to them: ‘Delay Maghrib a little, but they abandoned it until the stars became intertwined. Now I pray it when the disk (of the sun) sets.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 277

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan from Ali ibn Ya'qub from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ammar Al-Sabati: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "I had commanded Abu Al-Khattab to pray Maghrib when the redness had disappeared, but he took it to mean the redness from the direction of the west, and he would pray when the twilight disappeared."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّمَا أَمَرْتُ أَبَا اَلْخَطَّابِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ حِينَ زَالَتِ اَلْحُمْرَةُ فَجَعَلَ هُوَ اَلْحُمْرَةَ اَلَّتِي مِنْ قِبَلِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي حِينَ يَغِيبُ اَلشَّفَقُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan from Ali ibn Ya'qub from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ammar Al-Sabati: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "I had commanded Abu Al-Khattab to pray Maghrib when the redness had disappeared, but he took it to mean the redness from the direction of the west, and he would pray when the twilight disappeared."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 277

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdul Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is easier for you and more suitable for your prayer, and you are occupied with your needs, then you have until a quarter of the night." He (Umar ibn Yazid) said: “and that was while He (Imam (a.s)) was present in his hometown.”
arabicText: محمد بن علي بن محبوب عن محمد بن عبد الحميد عن محمد ابن عمر بن يزيد عن محمد بن عذافر عن عمر بن يزيد قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن وقت المغرب فقال إذا كان ارفق بك وأمكن لك في صلاتك وكنت في حوائجك فلك الى ربع الليل قال فقال لي وهو شاهد في بلده
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdul Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is easier for you and more suitable for your prayer, and you are occupied with your needs, then you have until a quarter of the night." He (Umar ibn Yazid) said: “and that was while He (Imam (a.s)) was present in his hometown.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 278

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Udym ibn Al-Hurr who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, (conveyed the) command to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, regarding all the prayers, and assigned for each prayer two times, except for Maghrib, for he (Jibrail) assigned for it only one time."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ أُدَيْمِ بْنِ اَلْحُرِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَمَرَ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِالصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا فَجَعَلَ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَقْتَيْنِ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّهُ جَعَلَ لَهَا وَقْتاً وَاحِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Udym ibn Al-Hurr who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, (conveyed the) command to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, regarding all the prayers, and assigned for each prayer two times, except for Maghrib, for he (Jibrail) assigned for it only one time."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zayd Al-Shahham who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, for each prayer with two times, except for the Maghrib prayer, for its time is one, and its time is its obligation."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَتَى اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ بِوَقْتَيْنِ غَيْرَ صَلاَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَإِنَّ وَقْتَهَا وَاحِدٌ وَ وَقْتَهَا وُجُوبُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zayd Al-Shahham who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib. Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, for each prayer with two times, except for the Maghrib prayer, for its time is one, and its time is its obligation."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 278

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Isma'il ibn Mihran who said:
I wrote to (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioning that: “Our companions say that when the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr and Asr has entered, and when it sets, the time for Maghrib and Isha enters, except that Maghrib is before Isha, whether in travel or residence, and that the time for Maghrib extends until a quarter of the night.” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: "Such is the time, except that the time for Maghrib is narrow, and its end is when the redness disappears and it turns into whiteness in the western horizon."
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ ذَكَرَ أَصْحَابُنَا أَنَّهُ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ إِذَا غَرَبَتْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ اَلْحَضَرِ وَ أَنَّ وَقْتَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِلَى رُبُعِ اَللَّيْلِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« كَذَلِكَ اَلْوَقْتُ غَيْرَ أَنَّ وَقْتَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ ضَيِّقٌ وَ آخِرَ وَقْتِهَا ذَهَابُ اَلْحُمْرَةِ وَ مَصِيرُهَا إِلَى اَلْبَيَاضِ فِي أُفُقِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Isma'il ibn Mihran who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioning that: “Our companions say that when the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr and Asr has entered, and when it sets, the time for Maghrib and Isha enters, except that Maghrib is before Isha, whether in travel or residence, and that the time for Maghrib extends until a quarter of the night.” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: "Such is the time, except that the time for Maghrib is narrow, and its end is when the redness disappears and it turns into whiteness in the western horizon."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Rayan who said:
I wrote to Imam (a.s), asking; “About a man who is inside a house, and its walls prevent him from seeing the redness of the Maghrib and from knowing the disappearance of the twilight and the time for the Isha prayer; when should he pray it, and what should he do?” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in response: "He should pray it, in this case, when the stars begin to scatter and Isha when they become intertwined and the whiteness of the sunset appears."
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلرَّيَّانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ فِي اَلدَّارِ تَمْنَعُهُ حِيطَانُهَا اَلنَّظَرَ إِلَى حُمْرَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ مَعْرِفَةَ مَغِيبِ اَلشَّفَقِ وَ وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ مَتَى يُصَلِّيهَا وَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَوَقَّعَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا كَانَ عَلَى هَذِهِ اَلصِّفَةِ عِنْدَ قَصْرِ اَلنُّجُومِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءَ عِنْدَ اِشْتِبَاكِهَا وَ بَيَاضِ مَغِيبِ اَلشَّمْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Rayan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Imam (a.s), asking; “About a man who is inside a house, and its walls prevent him from seeing the redness of the Maghrib and from knowing the disappearance of the twilight and the time for the Isha prayer; when should he pray it, and what should he do?” So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in response: "He should pray it, in this case, when the stars begin to scatter and Isha when they become intertwined and the whiteness of the sunset appears."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the disk (of the sun) disappears. If you see it after that and you have already prayed, you must repeat the prayer, but your fast remains valid, and you must refrain from food if you have eaten anything."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا غَابَ اَلْقُرْصُ فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ أَعَدْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ مَضَى صَوْمُكَ وَ تَكُفُّ عَنِ اَلطَّعَامِ إِنْ كُنْتَ أَصَبْتَ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the disk (of the sun) disappears. If you see it after that and you have already prayed, you must repeat the prayer, but your fast remains valid, and you must refrain from food if you have eaten anything."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 279

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O Shihab, I like that when I pray Maghrib, I see a star in the sky."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ شِهَابِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا شِهَابُ إِنِّي أُحِبُّ إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ أَنْ أَرَى فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ كَوْكَباً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O Shihab, I like that when I pray Maghrib, I see a star in the sky."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Basir:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I fear burdening my nation, I would have delayed the night prayer (Isha) until a third of the night. And you are in a state of concession until midnight, and that is the darkening of the night. When the darkening has passed, two angels call out: Whoever has slept through the obligatory prayer after midnight, may his eyes never taste sleep.’"
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« لَوْلاَ أَنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَى أُمَّتِي لَأَخَّرْتُ اَلْعَتَمَةَ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَنْتَ فِي رُخْصَةٍ إِلَى نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ غَسَقُ اَللَّيْلِ فَإِذَا مَضَى اَلْغَسَقُ نَادَى مَلَكَانِ مَنْ رَقَدَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بَعْدَ نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ فَلاَ رَقَدَتْ عَيْنَاهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I fear burdening my nation, I would have delayed the night prayer (Isha) until a third of the night. And you are in a state of concession until midnight, and that is the darkening of the night. When the darkening has passed, two angels call out: Whoever has slept through the obligatory prayer after midnight, may his eyes never taste sleep.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The end of the time for the night prayer (Isha) is midnight."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مُعَلًّى أَبِي عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« آخِرُ وَقْتِ اَلْعَتَمَةِ نِصْفُ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The end of the time for the night prayer (Isha) is midnight."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for the night prayer (Isha) extends until a third of the night or until midnight, and that (delay) is considered negligence."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْعَتَمَةُ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اَللَّيْلِ أَوْ إِلَى نِصْفِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ ذَلِكَ اَلتَّضْيِيعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The time for the night prayer (Isha) extends until a third of the night or until midnight, and that (delay) is considered negligence."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s) said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is overcome by sleep or prevented by something from praying Fajr on time. Imam (a.s) said: "He may pray Fajr any time between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun, and that is specifically for the obligatory prayer. So if he has prayed one rakʿah of the dawn prayer and then the sun rises, he should complete the prayer, and his prayer is valid. But if the sun rises before he has prayed a single rakʿah, then he should break off the prayer and not pray until the sun has risen and its glare has passed."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا غَلَبَتْهُ عَيْنُهُ أَوْ عَاقَهُ أَمْرٌ« أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْفَجْرَ مَا بَيْنَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ خَاصَّةً فَإِنْ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً مِنَ اَلْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَلْيُتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ إِنْ طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَةً فَلْيَقْطَعِ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّي حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ يَذْهَبَ شُعَاعُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s) said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is overcome by sleep or prevented by something from praying Fajr on time. Imam (a.s) said: "He may pray Fajr any time between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun, and that is specifically for the obligatory prayer. So if he has prayed one rakʿah of the dawn prayer and then the sun rises, he should complete the prayer, and his prayer is valid. But if the sun rises before he has prayed a single rakʿah, then he should break off the prayer and not pray until the sun has risen and its glare has passed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would not pray anything during the day until the sun had passed the meridian. When the day had declined by about half a finger's width, He (saws) would pray eight rak'ahs. When the shadow extended to the length of one arm, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr, then He (saws) would pray two rak'ahs after Dhuhr. He (saws) would pray two rak'ahs before the time of Asr. When the shadow extended to two arms' length, He (saws) would pray Asr. He (saws) would pray Maghrib when the sun set. When the twilight disappeared, the time for Isha would begin. The end of the time for Maghrib is the return of the twilight. When the twilight returns, the time for Isha enters. The end of the time for Isha is a third of the night. He would not pray after Isha until midnight; then he would pray thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr prayer and including the two rak'ahs of Fajr before the morning prayer. When the dawn rose and became bright, he would pray the morning (Fajr) prayer."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لاَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ شَيْئاً حَتَّى تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا زَالَ اَلنَّهَارُ قَدْرَ نِصْفِ إِصْبَعٍ صَلَّى ثَمَانَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا فَاءَ اَلْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعاً صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُصَلِّي قَبْلَ وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا فَاءَ اَلْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعَيْنِ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ وَ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ حِينَ تَغِيبُ اَلشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا غَابَ اَلشَّفَقُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ آخِرُ وَقْتِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِيَابُ اَلشَّفَقِ فَإِذَا آبَ اَلشَّفَقُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ آخِرُ وَقْتِ اَلْعِشَاءِ ثُلُثُ اَللَّيْلِ وَ كَانَ لاَ يُصَلِّي بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اَللَّيْلُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنْهَا اَلْوَتْرُ وَ مِنْهَا رَكْعَتَا اَلْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ اَلْغَدَاةِ فَإِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ أَضَاءَ صَلَّى اَلْغَدَاةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would not pray anything during the day until the sun had passed the meridian. When the day had declined by about half a finger's width, He (saws) would pray eight rak'ahs. When the shadow extended to the length of one arm, He (saws) would pray Dhuhr, then He (saws) would pray two rak'ahs after Dhuhr. He (saws) would pray two rak'ahs before the time of Asr. When the shadow extended to two arms' length, He (saws) would pray Asr. He (saws) would pray Maghrib when the sun set. When the twilight disappeared, the time for Isha would begin. The end of the time for Maghrib is the return of the twilight. When the twilight returns, the time for Isha enters. The end of the time for Isha is a third of the night. He would not pray after Isha until midnight; then he would pray thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr prayer and including the two rak'ahs of Fajr before the morning prayer. When the dawn rose and became bright, he would pray the morning (Fajr) prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with the people when the sun had passed the meridian, in congregation, without any excuse. And He (saws) prayed Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha) with them before the twilight disappeared, without any excuse, in congregation. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, only did that to widen the time for his nation."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِالنَّاسِ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ حِينَ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ وَ صَلَّى بِهِمُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ اَلشَّفَقِ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ إِنَّمَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لِيَتَّسِعَ اَلْوَقْتُ عَلَى أُمَّتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with the people when the sun had passed the meridian, in congregation, without any excuse. And He (saws) prayed Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha) with them before the twilight disappeared, without any excuse, in congregation. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, only did that to widen the time for his nation."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Musa ibn Umar from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May we combine between Maghrib and Isha while residing, before the twilight disappears, without any excuse?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ نَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ قَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Musa ibn Umar from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May we combine between Maghrib and Isha while residing, before the twilight disappears, without any excuse?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali from Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad from Yahya ibn Abi Zakariyya from Al-Walid ibn Aban from Safwan Al-Jammal who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with us when the sun had passed the meridian, with one Adhan and two Iqamahs. Then Imam (a.s) said: "I have something I need to attend to, so offer your recommended prayers."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي زَكَرِيَّا عَنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ بْنِ أَبَانٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ عِنْدَ مَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ بِأَذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنِّي عَلَى حَاجَةٍ فَتَنَفَّلُوا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali from Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad from Yahya ibn Abi Zakariyya from Al-Walid ibn Aban from Safwan Al-Jammal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with us when the sun had passed the meridian, with one Adhan and two Iqamahs. Then Imam (a.s) said: "I have something I need to attend to, so offer your recommended prayers."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Abbas Al-Naqid who said:
My possessions were scattered, and the craftsmen working for me dispersed, so I complained about that to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. Imam (a.s) said to me: "Combine between the two prayers, Dhuhr and Asr, and you will see what you love (desire)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَبَّاسٍ اَلنَّاقِدِ قَالَ: تَفَرَّقَ مَا كَانَ فِي يَدِي وَ تَفَرَّقَ عَنِّي حُرَفَائِي فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لِي« اِجْمَعْ بَيْنَ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ تَرَى مَا تُحِبُّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Abbas Al-Naqid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: My possessions were scattered, and the craftsmen working for me dispersed, so I complained about that to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. Imam (a.s) said to me: "Combine between the two prayers, Dhuhr and Asr, and you will see what you love (desire)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah ibn Al-Khattab from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: "If you combine between the two prayers, then do not offer any supererogatory prayer between them."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا جَمَعْتَ بَيْنَ اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ فَلاَ تَطَوَّعْ بَيْنَهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah ibn Al-Khattab from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: "If you combine between the two prayers, then do not offer any supererogatory prayer between them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who comes to the mosque and the people there have already prayed. Should he start with the obligatory prayer or with a supererogatory prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "If it is within a good time, then there is no harm in performing the supererogatory prayer before the obligatory one. But if he fears missing the obligatory prayer because a lot of time has passed, then he should start with the obligatory prayer, as it is the right of Allah (swt). Then he may pray as many supererogatory prayers as he wishes. The matter is flexible; a person may pray at the beginning of the obligatory prayer’s time. And it is better, if a person is praying alone, to begin with the obligatory prayer once its time has entered, so that the best part of the time is devoted to the obligatory prayer. However, it is not prohibited for him to perform supererogatory prayers from the beginning of the time until near the end of the time."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَهْلُهُ أَ يَبْتَدِئُ بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ أَوْ يَتَطَوَّعُ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ حَسَنٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِالتَّطَوُّعِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ خَافَ اَلْفَوْتَ مِنْ أَجْلِ مَا مَضَى مِنَ اَلْوَقْتِ فَلْيَبْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ هُوَ حَقُّ اَللَّهِ ثُمَّ لْيَتَطَوَّعْ مَا شَاءَ اَلْأَمْرُ مُوَسَّعٌ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْإِنْسَانُ فِي أَوَّلِ وَقْتِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَاَلْفَضْلُ إِذَا صَلَّى اَلْإِنْسَانُ وَحْدَهُ أَنْ يَبْدَأَ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا لِيَكُونَ فَضْلُ اَلْوَقْتِ لِلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ لَيْسَ بِمَحْظُورٍ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلنَّوَافِلَ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلْوَقْتِ إِلَى قَرِيبٍ مِنْ آخِرِ اَلْوَقْتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who comes to the mosque and the people there have already prayed. Should he start with the obligatory prayer or with a supererogatory prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "If it is within a good time, then there is no harm in performing the supererogatory prayer before the obligatory one. But if he fears missing the obligatory prayer because a lot of time has passed, then he should start with the obligatory prayer, as it is the right of Allah (swt). Then he may pray as many supererogatory prayers as he wishes. The matter is flexible; a person may pray at the beginning of the obligatory prayer’s time. And it is better, if a person is praying alone, to begin with the obligatory prayer once its time has entered, so that the best part of the time is devoted to the obligatory prayer. However, it is not prohibited for him to perform supererogatory prayers from the beginning of the time until near the end of the time."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
I asked: “May I pray a supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer?” He said: "Yes, at the beginning of the time, if you are with an Imam whom you follow. But if you are alone, then start with the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أُصَلِّي فِي وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ نَافِلَةً قَالَ« نَعَمْ فِي أَوَّلِ اَلْوَقْتِ إِذَا كُنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ تَقْتَدِي بِهِ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَابْدَأْ بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked: “May I pray a supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer?” He said: "Yes, at the beginning of the time, if you are with an Imam whom you follow. But if you are alone, then start with the obligatory prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 283

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd narrated from Ahmad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Usamah or someone else who said:
I once climbed Mount Abu Qubays while the people were praying Maghrib, and I saw that the sun had not actually set; it had only been concealed behind the mountain from the people. I then met Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and informed him of this. Imam (a.s) said to me: "And why did you do that? What a bad thing you have done! You should pray it when you do not see it, whether it has set behind a mountain or disappeared, so long as it is not hidden by a cloud or darkness that covers it. What is required of you is your east and your west, and it is not upon the people to investigate further."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ قَالَ صَعِدْتُ مَرَّةً جَبَلَ أَبِي قُبَيْسٍ وَاَلنَّاسُ يُصَلُّونَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَرَأَيْتُ اَلشَّمْسَ لَمْ تَغِبْ إِنَّمَا تَوَارَتْ خَلْفَ اَلْجَبَلِ عَنِ اَلنَّاسِ فَلَقِيتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِي وَلِمَ فَعَلْتَ ذَلِكَ بِئْسَ مَا صَنَعْتَ إِنَّمَا تُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا لَمْ تَرَهَا خَلْفَ جَبَلٍ غَابَتْ أَوْ غَارَتْ مَا لَمْ يُجَلِّلْهَا سَحَابٌ أَوْ ظُلَمٌ تُظِلُّهَا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ مَشْرِقُكَ وَمَغْرِبُكَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ أَنْ يَبْحَثُوا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Usamah or someone else who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I once climbed Mount Abu Qubays while the people were praying Maghrib, and I saw that the sun had not actually set; it had only been concealed behind the mountain from the people. I then met Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and informed him of this. Imam (a.s) said to me: "And why did you do that? What a bad thing you have done! You should pray it when you do not see it, whether it has set behind a mountain or disappeared, so long as it is not hidden by a cloud or darkness that covers it. What is required of you is your east and your west, and it is not upon the people to investigate further."
