chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Musa ibn Al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mehran who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding Maghrib: “Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun might still be behind the mountain or that the mountain has hidden it from us.” Imam (a.s) said: "You are not required to climb the mountain."
arabicText: عنه عن موسى بن الحسن عن أحمد بن هلال عن محمد ابن أبي عمير عن جعفر بن عثمان عن سماعة بن مهران قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام في المغرب انا ربما صلينا ونحن نخاف ان تكون الشمس خلف الجبل أو قد سترنا منها الجبل قال فقال ليس عليك صعود الجبل
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Musa ibn Al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mehran who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding Maghrib: “Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun might still be behind the mountain or that the mountain has hidden it from us.” Imam (a.s) said: "You are not required to climb the mountain."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about the Maghrib prayer when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay it for a while? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm if he is fasting, he should break his fast and then pray, and if he has a need, he should fulfill it and then pray."
arabicText: عنه عن أحمد بن الحسن بن علي بن فضال عن عمرو ابن سعيد المدائني عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار بن موسى الساباطي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن صلاة المغرب إذا حضرت هل يجوز أن تؤخر ساعة؟ قال لا بأس ان كان صائما افطر ثم صلى وان كانت له حاجة قضاها ثم صلى
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about the Maghrib prayer when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay it for a while? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm if he is fasting, he should break his fast and then pray, and if he has a need, he should fulfill it and then pray."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises, should he pray as soon as he wakes up or wait until the sun has risen fully? Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray as soon as he wakes up." I asked: “Should he perform the Witr prayer or the two rak'ahs (of Nafila)?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather he should begin with the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنَامُ عَنِ اَلْغَدَاةِ حَتَّى تَبْزُغَ اَلشَّمْسُ أَيُصَلِّي حِينَ يَسْتَيْقِظُ أَوْ يَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى تَنْبَسِطَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ يُصَلِّي حِينَ يَسْتَيْقِظُ» قُلْتُ يُوتِرُ أَوْ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ لاَ بَلْ يَبْدَأُ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises, should he pray as soon as he wakes up or wait until the sun has risen fully? Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray as soon as he wakes up." I asked: “Should he perform the Witr prayer or the two rak'ahs (of Nafila)?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather he should begin with the obligatory prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray the two rak'ahs and then pray the morning (Fajr) prayer."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَامَ عَنِ اَلْغَدَاةِ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray the two rak'ahs and then pray the morning (Fajr) prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, once slept and his eyes were overcome by sleep, and He (saws) did not wake up until the heat of the sun troubled him. Then He (saws) awoke, called his group for a moment, prayed two rak'ahs, and then prayed the morning (Fajr) prayer. He (saws) said: 'O Bilal, what happened to you?' Bilal replied: 'The one who caused you to sleep, O Messenger of Allah (swt), also caused me to sleep.' He (saws) disliked staying in that place and said: 'You (Bilal) have slept in the valley of Shaytan.'"
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ رَقَدَ فَغَلَبَتْهُ عَيْنَاهُ فَلَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظْ حَتَّى آذَاهُ حَرُّ اَلشَّمْسِ ثُمَّ اِسْتَيْقَظَ فَعَادَ نَادِيَهُ سَاعَةً وَ رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلصُّبْحَ وَقَالَ يَا بِلاَلُ مَالَكَ» فَقَالَ بِلاَلٌ أَرْقَدَنِي اَلَّذِي أَرْقَدَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ قَالَ وَكَرِهَ اَلْمُقَامَ وَقَالَ نِمْتُمْ بِوَادِي اَلشَّيْطَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, once slept and his eyes were overcome by sleep, and He (saws) did not wake up until the heat of the sun troubled him. Then He (saws) awoke, called his group for a moment, prayed two rak'ahs, and then prayed the morning (Fajr) prayer. He (saws) said: 'O Bilal, what happened to you?' Bilal replied: 'The one who caused you to sleep, O Messenger of Allah (swt), also caused me to sleep.' He (saws) disliked staying in that place and said: 'You (Bilal) have slept in the valley of Shaytan.'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who prayed without purification, or forgot prayers and did not perform them, or slept through them. Imam (a.s) said: "He must make them up whenever he remembers them, at whatever time he remembers, by night or by day. If the time of a present prayer comes and he has not yet finished making up what he missed, then he should make up what he can without fearing that the time of the present prayer will expire. The present prayer has greater right to its time, so he should perform it first. When he has prayed it, he should then complete whatever he had missed from before. And he should not perform even a single rak'ah of supererogatory prayer until he has made up the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن ابن أبي عمير عن عمر بن اذينة عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام انه سئل عن رجل صلى بغير طهور أو نسي صلوات لم يصلها أو نام عنها فقال يقضيها إذا ذكرها في أي ساعة ذكرها من ليل أو نهار فإذا دخل وقت صلاة ولم يتم ما قد فاته فليقض ما لم يتخوف أن يذهب وقت هذه الصلاة التي قد حضرت وهذه أحق بوقتها فليصلها فإذا قضاها فليصل ما قد فاته مما قد مضى ولا يتطوع بركعة حتى يقضي الفريضة
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who prayed without purification, or forgot prayers and did not perform them, or slept through them. Imam (a.s) said: "He must make them up whenever he remembers them, at whatever time he remembers, by night or by day. If the time of a present prayer comes and he has not yet finished making up what he missed, then he should make up what he can without fearing that the time of the present prayer will expire. The present prayer has greater right to its time, so he should perform it first. When he has prayed it, he should then complete whatever he had missed from before. And he should not perform even a single rak'ah of supererogatory prayer until he has made up the obligatory prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from a group of our companions:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian, nor at night after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّهُمْ سَمِعُوا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لاَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ حَتَّى تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَلاَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ بَعْدَ مَا يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اَللَّيْلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from a group of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian, nor at night after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "(Imam (a.s)) Ali, peace be upon him, would not pray anything during the night after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight, and He (a.s) would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لاَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ شَيْئاً إِذَا صَلَّى اَلْعَتَمَةَ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اَللَّيْلُ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ حَتَّى تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "(Imam (a.s)) Ali, peace be upon him, would not pray anything during the night after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight, and He (a.s) would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 286

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I get occupied (and cannot pray at the usual time)”. Imam (a.s) said: "Then do as we do, pray six rak'ahs when the sun is at the same position it is at during the Asr prayer,” (meaning at the height of the greater forenoon ‘al-duha al-akbar’), “and count them as if you had performed them at zawal (midday)."
arabicText: رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَشْتَغِلُ قَالَ فَاصْنَعْ كَمَا نَصْنَعُ صَلِّ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ إِذَا كَانَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فِي مِثْلِ مَوْضِعِهَا صَلاَةَ اَلْعَصْرِ يَعْنِي اِرْتِفَاعَ اَلضُّحَى اَلْأَكْبَرِ وَاِعْتَدَّ بِهَا مِنَ اَلزَّوَالِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I get occupied (and cannot pray at the usual time)”. Imam (a.s) said: "Then do as we do, pray six rak'ahs when the sun is at the same position it is at during the Asr prayer,” (meaning at the height of the greater forenoon ‘al-duha al-akbar’), “and count them as if you had performed them at zawal (midday)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 286

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ammar ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid Al-Ghassani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “May I be your ransom, the daytime prayer, the prayer of the supererogatory (nawafil), how many are they?” Imam (a.s) said: "Sixteen. You may pray them at any hour of the day you wish, but if you pray them at their proper times, it is better."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ ظَرِيفِ بْنِ نَاصِحٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ اَلْغَسَّانِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّهَارِ صَلاَةُ اَلنَّوَافِلِ فِي كَمْ هِيَ قَالَ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ أَيَّ سَاعَاتِ اَلنَّهَارِ شِئْتَ تُصَلِّيهَا صَلَّيْتَهَا إِلاَّ أَنَّكَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَهَا فِي مَوَاقِيتِهَا أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ammar ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid Al-Ghassani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said to me: "The daytime prayer is sixteen rak'ahs, whichever part of the day you wish, if you wish at its beginning, or if you wish in its middle, or if you wish at its end."
arabicText: عنه عن علي بن الحكم عن بعض أصحابه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال لي صلاة النهار ست عشرة ركعة أي النهار شئت ان شئت في أوله وإن شئت في وسطه وإن شئت في آخره
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to me: "The daytime prayer is sixteen rak'ahs, whichever part of the day you wish, if you wish at its beginning, or if you wish in its middle, or if you wish at its end."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Sayf, from Abd al-A‘la who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the daytime supererogatory prayer (nafila). Imam (a.s) said: "Sixteen rak‘ahs, whenever you feel active. Indeed, (Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, had specific hours during the day in which he would pray them. If he was preoccupied by his land or by a ruler, He (a.s) would make them up. The supererogatory prayer is like a gift, whenever it is offered, it is accepted."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The supererogatory prayer is like a gift, whenever it is offered, it is accepted. So offer from it whatever you wish earlier, and delay from it whatever you wish."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلاَةُ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلْهَدِيَّةِ مَتَى مَا أُتِيَ بِهَا قُبِلَتْ فَقَدِّمْ مِنْهَا مَا شِئْتَ وَأَخِّرْ مِنْهَا مَا شِئْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The supererogatory prayer is like a gift, whenever it is offered, it is accepted. So offer from it whatever you wish earlier, and delay from it whatever you wish."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Yazid ibn Dumrah Al-Laythi from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, about a man who is preoccupied at the time of the meridian, may he perform the (supererogatory prayers) early in the day? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if he knows that he will be preoccupied, then he may perform them all at the beginning of the day."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يَزِيدَ [يَزِيدَخ ل] بْنِ ضَمْرَةَ اَللَّيْثِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَشْتَغِلُ عَنِ اَلزَّوَالِ أَ يَتَعَجَّلُ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلنَّهَارِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ يَشْتَغِلُ فَيُعَجِّلُهَا فِي صَدْرِ اَلنَّهَارِ كُلَّهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Yazid ibn Dumrah Al-Laythi from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, about a man who is preoccupied at the time of the meridian, may he perform the (supererogatory prayers) early in the day? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if he knows that he will be preoccupied, then he may perform them all at the beginning of the day."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, who raised it (the chain of narration) and said:
A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Indeed, the sun rises between the two horns of Satan.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, indeed, Iblis has taken for himself a throne between the heaven and the earth. So when the sun rises and people prostrate at that time, Iblis says to his devils: 'Indeed, the children of Adam are praying to me.'"
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ اَلشَّمْسَ تَطْلُعُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيِ اَلشَّيْطَانِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنَّ إِبْلِيسَ اِتَّخَذَ عَرْشاً بَيْنَ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ اَلْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ سَجَدَ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْوَقْتِ اَلنَّاسُ قَالَ إِبْلِيسُ لِشَيَاطِينِهِ إِنَّ بَنِي آدَمَ يُصَلُّونَ لِي»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, who raised it (the chain of narration) and said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Indeed, the sun rises between the two horns of Satan.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, indeed, Iblis has taken for himself a throne between the heaven and the earth. So when the sun rises and people prostrate at that time, Iblis says to his devils: 'Indeed, the children of Adam are praying to me.'"

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot Dhuhr until the time of Asr entered. Imam (a.s) said: "He should begin with the obligatory prayer. Likewise with the other prayers, begin with the one that was missed, unless you fear that the time for the current prayer will expire, then you should begin with the one whose time you are currently in, and afterwards make up the one you missed."
arabicText: سهل بن زياد عن محمد بن سنان عن ابن مسكان عن أبي بصير قال سألته عن رجل نسي الظهر حتى دخل وقت العصر قال يبدأ بالمكتوبة وكذلك الصلوات وتبدأ بالتي نسيت إلا أن تخاف أن يخرج وقت الصلاة فتبدأ بالتي أنت في وقتها ثم تقضي التي نسيت
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot Dhuhr until the time of Asr entered. Imam (a.s) said: "He should begin with the obligatory prayer. Likewise with the other prayers, begin with the one that was missed, unless you fear that the time for the current prayer will expire, then you should begin with the one whose time you are currently in, and afterwards make up the one you missed."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from his father:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "If a prayer passes you by and you remember it during the time of another prayer, then if you know that by praying the one that you missed you will still have time to perform the current one within its time, begin with the one you missed, for Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says: “And establish the prayer for My remembrance” (Surah Taha 20:14). But if you know that by praying the one you missed you will miss the current prayer, then begin with the one whose time you are in, and then perform the one you missed afterward."
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن القاسم بن عروة عن عبيد بن زرارة عن أبيه عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إذا فاتتك صلاة فذكرتها في وقت اخرى فان كنت تعلم أنك إذا صليت التي قد فاتتك كنت من الاخرى في وقت فابدأ بالتي فاتتك فان الله عزوجل يقول وأقم الصلاة لذكري وإن كنت تعلم إذا صليت التي فاتتك فاتتك التي بعدها فابدأ بالتي انت في وقتها وأقم الاخرى
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "If a prayer passes you by and you remember it during the time of another prayer, then if you know that by praying the one that you missed you will still have time to perform the current one within its time, begin with the one you missed, for Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says: “And establish the prayer for My remembrance” (Surah Taha 20:14). But if you know that by praying the one you missed you will miss the current prayer, then begin with the one whose time you are in, and then perform the one you missed afterward."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Aban from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot a prayer until the time of another prayer entered. Imam (a.s) said: "If he forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, he should pray it as soon as he remembers it. If he remembers it while he is in the middle of another prayer, he should begin with the one he missed. And if he remembers it while he is with an Imam (of prayer) in the Maghrib prayer, he should complete it with a rak'ah and then pray Maghrib, and after that he should pray the Isha. If he had already prayed the Isha alone and had performed two rak'ahs of it and then remembered that he had forgotten Maghrib, he should complete it with a rak'ah so that it becomes the Maghrib prayer of three rak'ahs, and then he should pray the Isha after that."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْمُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ صَلاَةً حَتَّى دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةٍ أُخْرَى فَقَالَ« إِذَا نَسِيَ اَلصَّلاَةَ أَوْ نَامَ عَنْهَا صَلَّى حِينَ يَذْكُرُهَا فَإِنْ ذَكَرَهَا وَهُوَ فِي صَلاَةٍ بَدَأَ بِالَّتِي نَسِيَ وَإِنْ ذَكَرَهَا وَهُوَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ أَتَمَّهَا بِرَكْعَةٍ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلْعَتَمَةَ بَعْدُ فَإِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى اَلْعَتَمَةَ وَحْدَهُ فَصَلَّى مِنْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ نَسِيَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ أَتَمَّهَا بِرَكْعَةٍ فَتَكُونُ صَلاَةُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ ثَلاَثَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَتَمَةَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Aban from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot a prayer until the time of another prayer entered. Imam (a.s) said: "If he forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, he should pray it as soon as he remembers it. If he remembers it while he is in the middle of another prayer, he should begin with the one he missed. And if he remembers it while he is with an Imam (of prayer) in the Maghrib prayer, he should complete it with a rak'ah and then pray Maghrib, and after that he should pray the Isha. If he had already prayed the Isha alone and had performed two rak'ahs of it and then remembered that he had forgotten Maghrib, he should complete it with a rak'ah so that it becomes the Maghrib prayer of three rak'ahs, and then he should pray the Isha after that."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who led a group of people in the Asr prayer and then, while praying, remembered that he had not prayed the Dhuhr prayer. He said: "He should make the prayer he is currently in the Dhuhr prayer which he had missed, and then after completing it, he should newly begin the Asr prayer. As for the people, their prayer remains valid."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فِي اَلْعَصْرِ فَذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ صَلَّى اَلْأُولَى قَالَ« فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا اَلْأُولَى اَلَّتِي فَاتَتْهُ وَ يَسْتَأْنِفُ بَعْدُ صَلاَةَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ قَدْ قَضَى اَلْقَوْمُ صَلاَتَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who led a group of people in the Asr prayer and then, while praying, remembered that he had not prayed the Dhuhr prayer. He said: "He should make the prayer he is currently in the Dhuhr prayer which he had missed, and then after completing it, he should newly begin the Asr prayer. As for the people, their prayer remains valid."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 288

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the sun had set, while he had already prayed Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (or my father (a.s), peace be upon him), used to say: 'If he is able to pray it before Maghrib escapes him, he should begin with it; otherwise, he should pray Maghrib first and then pray it.'"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ اَلظُّهْرَ حَتَّى غَرَبَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ قَدْ كَانَ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ فَقَالَ« كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَوْ كَانَ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ« إِذَا أَمْكَنَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَفُوتَهُ اَلْمَغْرِبُ بَدَأَ بِهَا وَ إِلاَّ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ صَلاَّهَا»»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the sun had set, while he had already prayed Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (or my father (a.s), peace be upon him), used to say: 'If he is able to pray it before Maghrib escapes him, he should begin with it; otherwise, he should pray Maghrib first and then pray it.'"

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked him about a man who forgot to pray Dhuhr until he had already prayed Asr. He said: "He should consider the prayer he has performed as Dhuhr, and then begin Asr anew." I asked: “What if he forgot both Dhuhr and Asr together, and then remembered them at sunset?” He said: "If there is still enough time and he does not fear missing either of them, he should pray Dhuhr first and then Asr. But if he fears that he will miss it, then he should begin with Asr and not delay it so that it would not be missed, resulting in missing both prayers. Rather, he should pray Asr within what remains of its time, and then afterward pray Dhuhr immediately after it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْأُولَى حَتَّى صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ قَالَ« فَلْيَجْعَلْ صَلاَتَهُ اَلَّتِي صَلَّى اَلْأُولَى ثُمَّ لْيَسْتَأْنِفِ اَلْعَصْرَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ نَسِيَ اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلْعَصْرَ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ لاَ يَخَافُ فَوْتَ إِحْدَاهُمَا فَلْيُصَلِّ اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ إِنْ هُوَ خَافَ أَنْ يَفُوتَهُ فَلْيَبْدَأْ بِالْعَصْرِ وَ لاَ يُؤَخِّرْهَا فَتَفُوتَهُ فَيَكُونَ قَدْ فَاتَتَاهُ جَمِيعاً وَ لَكِنْ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ فِيمَا قَدْ بَقِيَ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ اَلْأُولَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى أَثَرِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about a man who forgot to pray Dhuhr until he had already prayed Asr. He said: "He should consider the prayer he has performed as Dhuhr, and then begin Asr anew." I asked: “What if he forgot both Dhuhr and Asr together, and then remembered them at sunset?” He said: "If there is still enough time and he does not fear missing either of them, he should pray Dhuhr first and then Asr. But if he fears that he will miss it, then he should begin with Asr and not delay it so that it would not be missed, resulting in missing both prayers. Rather, he should pray Asr within what remains of its time, and then afterward pray Dhuhr immediately after it."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot Dhuhr until he had already prayed two rak'ahs of Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "He should consider it as Dhuhr and then newly begin Asr." I said: “What if he forgot Maghrib until he had prayed two rak'ahs of Isha, and then he remembered?” Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer and then afterward make up Maghrib." I said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, you said that when one forgets Dhuhr and then remembers during Asr, he should consider it Dhuhr and then start Asr anew, but here you said he should complete his prayer and afterward make up Maghrib.” Imam (a.s) said: "This is not like that, for after Asr there is no other prayer, but after Isha there is still another prayer (Maghrib that was missed)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ اَلْأُولَى حَتَّى صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْعَصْرِ قَالَ« فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا اَلْأُولَى وَ لْيَسْتَأْنِفِ اَلْعَصْرَ» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ نَسِيَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ حَتَّى صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْعِشَاءِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ قَالَ« فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ لْيَقْضِ بَعْدُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قُلْتَ حِينَ نَسِيَ اَلظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلْعَصْرِ يَجْعَلُهَا اَلْأُولَى ثُمَّ لْيَسْتَأْنِفْ وَ قُلْتَ لِهَذَا يُتِمُّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ لْيَقْضِ بَعْدُ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ هَذَا مِثْلَ هَذَا إِنَّ اَلْعَصْرَ لَيْسَ بَعْدَهَا صَلاَةٌ وَ اَلْعِشَاءُ بَعْدَهَا صَلاَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot Dhuhr until he had already prayed two rak'ahs of Asr. Imam (a.s) said: "He should consider it as Dhuhr and then newly begin Asr." I said: “What if he forgot Maghrib until he had prayed two rak'ahs of Isha, and then he remembered?” Imam (a.s) said: "He should complete his prayer and then afterward make up Maghrib." I said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, you said that when one forgets Dhuhr and then remembers during Asr, he should consider it Dhuhr and then start Asr anew, but here you said he should complete his prayer and afterward make up Maghrib.” Imam (a.s) said: "This is not like that, for after Asr there is no other prayer, but after Isha there is still another prayer (Maghrib that was missed)."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man sleeps or forgets to pray Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha), and he wakes up before Fajr with enough time to pray both of them, then he should pray them both. But if he fears that one of them will be missed, then he should begin with Isha. And if he wakes up after Fajr, then he should pray the morning prayer (Fajr) first, then Maghrib, and then Isha before the rising of the sun."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ نَامَ رَجُلٌ أَوْ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظَ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ قَدْرَ مَا يُصَلِّيهِمَا كِلْتَيْهِمَا فَلْيُصَلِّهِمَا وَ إِنْ خَافَ أَنْ تَفُوتَهُ إِحْدَاهُمَا فَلْيَبْدَأْ بِالْعِشَاءِ وَ إِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَلْيُصَلِّ اَلصُّبْحَ ثُمَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ اَلْعِشَاءَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man sleeps or forgets to pray Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha), and he wakes up before Fajr with enough time to pray both of them, then he should pray them both. But if he fears that one of them will be missed, then he should begin with Isha. And if he wakes up after Fajr, then he should pray the morning prayer (Fajr) first, then Maghrib, and then Isha before the rising of the sun."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If a man sleeps and does not pray the Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha), or forgets them, and he wakes up before Fajr with enough time to pray both of them, then he should pray them both. But if he fears that one of them will be missed, then he should begin with the night prayer (Isha). And if he wakes up after Fajr, then he should begin by praying the morning prayer (Fajr), then Maghrib, then the night prayer (Isha) before the rising of the sun. But if he fears that the sun will rise and he will miss one of the two prayers, then he should pray Maghrib and leave the night prayer (Isha) until after the sun rises and its rays disappear, then he should pray it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ نَامَ رَجُلٌ وَلَمْ يُصَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ أَوْ نَسِيَ فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظَ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ قَدْرَ مَا يُصَلِّيهِمَا كِلْتَيْهِمَا فَلْيُصَلِّهِمَا وَ إِنْ خَشِيَ أَنْ تَفُوتَهُ إِحْدَاهُمَا فَلْيَبْدَأْ بِالْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ إِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ فَلْيَبْدَأْ فَلْيُصَلِّ اَلْفَجْرَ ثُمَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَإِنْ خَافَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ فَتَفُوتَهُ إِحْدَى اَلصَّلاَتَيْنِ فَلْيُصَلِّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ يَدَعُ اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ يَذْهَبَ شُعَاعُهَا ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "If a man sleeps and does not pray the Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha), or forgets them, and he wakes up before Fajr with enough time to pray both of them, then he should pray them both. But if he fears that one of them will be missed, then he should begin with the night prayer (Isha). And if he wakes up after Fajr, then he should begin by praying the morning prayer (Fajr), then Maghrib, then the night prayer (Isha) before the rising of the sun. But if he fears that the sun will rise and he will miss one of the two prayers, then he should pray Maghrib and leave the night prayer (Isha) until after the sun rises and its rays disappear, then he should pray it."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who entered with a group of people while he had not yet prayed Dhuhr, and the people were praying Asr, should he pray with them? Imam (a.s) said: "He should consider the prayer he performed with them as Dhuhr, and then he should pray Asr afterward."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ صَلَّى هُوَ اَلظُّهْرَ وَاَلْقَوْمُ يُصَلُّونَ اَلْعَصْرَ يُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ قَالَ« يَجْعَلُ صَلاَتَهُ اَلَّتِي صَلَّى مَعَهُمُ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ يُصَلِّي هُوَ بَعْدُ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who entered with a group of people while he had not yet prayed Dhuhr, and the people were praying Asr, should he pray with them? Imam (a.s) said: "He should consider the prayer he performed with them as Dhuhr, and then he should pray Asr afterward."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who missed Maghrib until the time for Isha (the night prayer) had arrived. Imam (a.s) said: "If the time for Isha has come and he remembers that he has the Maghrib prayer pending, then if he wishes, he may begin with Maghrib, and if he wishes, he may begin with Isha and then pray Maghrib afterward."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَفُوتُهُ اَلْمَغْرِبُ حَتَّى تَحْضُرَ اَلْعَتَمَةُ فَقَالَ «إِنْ حَضَرَتِ اَلْعَتَمَةُ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَإِنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَبْدَأَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ بَدَأَ وَ إِنْ أَحَبَّ بَدَأَ بِالْعَتَمَةِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ بَعْدُ»
thaqalaynMatn: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who missed Maghrib until the time for Isha (the night prayer) had arrived. Imam (a.s) said: "If the time for Isha has come and he remembers that he has the Maghrib prayer pending, then if he wishes, he may begin with Maghrib, and if he wishes, he may begin with Isha and then pray Maghrib afterward."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Abbas from Isma'il ibn Hammam:
Abu Al-Hasan (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who delays the Dhuhr prayer until the time of Asr enters: he should begin with Asr, then pray Dhuhr."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ هَمَّامٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُؤَخِّرُ اَلظُّهْرَ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ وَقْتُ اَلْعَصْرِ إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ بِالْعَصْرِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Abbas from Isma'il ibn Hammam:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Al-Hasan (a.s) said: "Regarding a man who delays the Dhuhr prayer until the time of Asr enters: he should begin with Asr, then pray Dhuhr."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the Fajr prayer until the sun rises while he is traveling, what should he do? Is it permissible for him to make it up during the day? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not make up either a supererogatory or an obligatory prayer during the day, and it is not permissible for him, nor is it established for him. Rather, he should delay it and make it up at night."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنَامُ عَنِ اَلْفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ هُوَ فِي سَفَرٍ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ بِالنَّهَارِ قَالَ« لاَ يَقْضِي صَلاَةً نَافِلَةً وَ لاَ فَرِيضَةً بِالنَّهَارِ وَ لاَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ وَ لاَ يَثْبُتُ لَهُ وَ لَكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهَا فَيَقْضِيهَا بِاللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who sleeps through the Fajr prayer until the sun rises while he is traveling, what should he do? Is it permissible for him to make it up during the day? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not make up either a supererogatory or an obligatory prayer during the day, and it is not permissible for him, nor is it established for him. Rather, he should delay it and make it up at night."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad narrated from Al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O so-and-so, when the time enters upon you, then pray them both, for you do not know what may happen."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ قَالَ قَالَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا فُلاَنُ إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلْوَقْتُ عَلَيْكَ فَصَلِّهِمَا فَإِنَّكَ لاَ تَدْرِي مَا يَكُونُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad narrated from Al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O so-and-so, when the time enters upon you, then pray them both, for you do not know what may happen."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habib who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, asking: “The supererogatory (nafila) prayers that are due upon me, when should I make them up?” So Imam (a.s) wrote: "At any hour you wish, whether by night or by day."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تَكُونُ عَلَيَّ اَلصَّلاَةُ اَلنَّافِلَةُ مَتَى أَقْضِيهَا فَكَتَبَ« فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habib who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, asking: “The supererogatory (nafila) prayers that are due upon me, when should I make them up?” So Imam (a.s) wrote: "At any hour you wish, whether by night or by day."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Sayf from Hassan ibn Mihran who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about making up the supererogatory (nafila) prayers. Imam (a.s) said: "Anytime between the rising of the sun and its setting."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ حَسَّانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَضَاءِ اَلنَّوَافِلِ قَالَ« مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Sayf from Hassan ibn Mihran who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about making up the supererogatory (nafila) prayers. Imam (a.s) said: "Anytime between the rising of the sun and its setting."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Zur'ah from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the night prayer sometimes escapes me, so I pray Fajr, is it permissible for me to pray after the Fajr prayer what I missed of the night prayer while I am still in my prayer place before the sun rises?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but do not let your family know about it, lest they take it as a regular practice."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ مُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ تَفُوتُنِي صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ فَأُصَلِّي اَلْفَجْرَ فَلِي أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ بَعْدَ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ مَا فَاتَنِي مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَنَا فِي مُصَلاَّيَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ تُعْلِمْ بِهِ أَهْلَكَ فَيَتَّخِذُونَهُ سُنَّةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Zur'ah from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the night prayer sometimes escapes me, so I pray Fajr, is it permissible for me to pray after the Fajr prayer what I missed of the night prayer while I am still in my prayer place before the sun rises?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but do not let your family know about it, lest they take it as a regular practice."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For every obligatory prayer there are two rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer except for Asr, for its supererogatory prayer is performed beforehand, thus they become two rak'ahs before it, and they are the two rak'ahs that complete the eight rak'ahs after Dhuhr. So if you want to make up any prayer, obligatory or other than it, do not pray anything until you first perform two rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer before the obligatory prayer that has arrived, then make up whatever you wish. And begin the night prayer with the verses: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...’ until ‘Indeed, You do not fail in (Your) promise’ (Surah Aali Imran 3:190-194). And on the day of Friday, you begin with the verses before the two rak'ahs before the zenith (zawal). And Imam (a.s) said: 'The time for the Friday prayer is when the sun has passed its zenith, by the measure of a strap (shiraak) or half of it.' And Imam (a.s) said: 'It is permissible for a man to pray at zawal from the time the sun has passed its zenith until two footsteps (qadaman) have passed. So if there remains time after the zenith for one rak‘ah or before two footsteps have passed, he should complete the prayer until he finishes the full rak‘ahs. But if two footsteps have passed before he prays one rak‘ah, then he should begin with the first (obligatory prayer) and not pray the zawal supererogatory prayer except after that. And it is permissible for a man to pray the supererogatory prayers of the first (part of the day) from the beginning of the first until four footsteps have passed. If the four footsteps pass and he has not prayed anything from the supererogatory prayers, then he should not pray the supererogatory prayers. But if he has prayed one rak‘ah, then he should complete the supererogatory prayers until he finishes them, then he should pray the Asr prayer." And Imam (a.s) said: "It is permissible for a man to pray if there remains something from the prayer of the zenith (zawal) until half a foot has passed after the arrival of Dhuhr. And if a man has already prayed something from the supererogatory prayers of Dhuhr before Asr arrives, it is permissible for him to complete the supererogatory prayers of Dhuhr until a foot has passed after the arrival of Asr." And Imam (a.s) said: "A footstep after the arrival of Asr is like half a footstep after the arrival of Dhuhr, they are the same in terms of time." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom are many missed night prayers; is it permissible for him to make up the prayers of many nights along with their witr, following one after the other? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, it is permissible for him to do so at the beginning of the night. But if half the night has passed until the rising of Fajr, then neither a man nor a woman is to perform witr except the witr of that specific night. And if he wishes to make up a missed prayer, then let him pray eight rak‘ahs from the prayer of that night and delay the witr, then make up whatever he wishes without witr, then pray the witr of that specific night alone." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom is a missed prayer from the time of being present (hadar), is it permissible for him to make it up while traveling? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, he may make it up at night on the ground. As for on the back of a mount, then no. And he should pray it as he would pray it in the state of presence (hadar)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ لَهَا نَافِلَةُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ إِلاَّ اَلْعَصْرَ فَإِنَّهُ تُقَدَّمُ نَافِلَتُهَا فَيَصِيرَانِ قَبْلَهَا وَهِيَ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَللَّتَانِ تَمَّتْ بِهِمَا اَلثَّمَانِي بَعْدَ اَلظُّهْرِ فَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَقْضِيَ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ مَكْتُوبَةً أَوْ غَيْرَهَا فَلاَ تُصَلِّ شَيْئاً حَتَّى تَبْدَأَ فَتُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ اَلَّتِي حَضَرَتْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً لَهَا ثُمَّ اِقْضِ مَا شِئْتَ وَ اِبْدَأْ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِالْآيَاتِ تَقْرَأُ« إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضِ» إِلَى« إِنَّكَ لاٰ تُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» وَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ تَبْدَأُ بِالْآيَاتِ قَبْلَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ» وَ قَالَ« وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِذَا زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ شِرَاكٌ أَوْ نِصْفٌ» وَ قَالَ «لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلزَّوَالَ مَا بَيْنَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ إِلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ قَدَمَانِ فَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ بَقِيَ مِنَ اَ لزَّوَالِ رَكْعَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ أَوْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَمْضِيَ قَدَمَانِ أَتَمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ تَمَامَ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ وَ إِنْ مَضَى قَدَمَانِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَةً بَدَأَ بِالْأُولَى وَ لَمْ يُصَلِّ اَلزَّوَالَ إِلاَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ مِنْ نَوَافِلِ اَلْأُولَى مَا بَيْنَ اَلْأُولَى إِلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ فَإِنْ مَضَتِ اَلْأَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ وَ لَمْ يُصَلِّ مِنَ اَلنَّوَافِلِ شَيْئاً فَلاَ يُصَلِّي اَلنَّوَافِلَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً فَلْيُتِمَّ اَلنَّوَافِلَ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْهَا ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ» وَ قَالَ« لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ إِنْ بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلزَّوَالِ إِلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ بَعْدَ حُضُورِ اَلْأُولَى نِصْفُ قَدَمٍ وَ لِلرَّجُلِ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى مِنْ نَوَافِلِ اَلْأُولَى شَيْئاً قَبْلَ أَنْ يَحْضُرَ اَلْعَصْرُ فَلَهُ أَنْ يُتِمَّ نَوَافِلَ اَلْأُولَى إِلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ بَعْدَ حُضُورِ اَلْعَصْرِ قَدَمٌ» وَ قَالَ« اَلْقَدَمُ بَعْدَ حُضُورِ اَلْعَصْرِ مِثْلُ نِصْفِ قَدَمٍ بَعْدَ حُضُورِ اَلْأُولَى فِي اَلْوَقْتِ سَوَاءً» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةُ لَيَالٍ كَثِيرَةٍ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ صَلاَةَ لَيَالٍ كَثِيرَةٍ بِأَوْتَارِهَا يُتْبِعُ بَعْضُهَا بَعْضاً قَالَ« نَعَمْ كَذَلِكَ لَهُ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَمَّا إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ إِلَى أَنْ يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَلَيْسَ لِلرَّجُلِ وَ لاَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ يُوتِرَ إِلاَّ وَتْرَ صَلاَةِ تِلْكَ اَللَّيْلَةِ فَإِنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ صَلاَةً عَلَيْهِ صَلَّى ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتٍ مِنْ صَلاَةِ تِلْكَ اَللَّيْلَةِ وَأَخَّرَ اَلْوَتْرَ ثُمَّ يَقْضِي مَا بَدَا لَهُ بِلاَ وَتْرٍ ثُمَّ يُوتِرُ اَلْوَتْرَ اَلَّذِي لِتِلْكَ اَللَّيْلَةِ خَاصَّةً» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةٌ فِي اَلْحَضَرِ هَلْ يَقْضِيهَا وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ قَالَ« نَعَمْ يَقْضِيهَا بِاللَّيْلِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَأَمَّا عَلَى اَلظَّهْرِ فَلاَ وَ يُصَلِّي كَمَا يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْحَضَرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "For every obligatory prayer there are two rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer except for Asr, for its supererogatory prayer is performed beforehand, thus they become two rak'ahs before it, and they are the two rak'ahs that complete the eight rak'ahs after Dhuhr. So if you want to make up any prayer, obligatory or other than it, do not pray anything until you first perform two rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer before the obligatory prayer that has arrived, then make up whatever you wish. And begin the night prayer with the verses: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...’ until ‘Indeed, You do not fail in (Your) promise’ (Surah Aali Imran 3:190-194). And on the day of Friday, you begin with the verses before the two rak'ahs before the zenith (zawal). And Imam (a.s) said: 'The time for the Friday prayer is when the sun has passed its zenith, by the measure of a strap (shiraak) or half of it.' And Imam (a.s) said: 'It is permissible for a man to pray at zawal from the time the sun has passed its zenith until two footsteps (qadaman) have passed. So if there remains time after the zenith for one rak‘ah or before two footsteps have passed, he should complete the prayer until he finishes the full rak‘ahs. But if two footsteps have passed before he prays one rak‘ah, then he should begin with the first (obligatory prayer) and not pray the zawal supererogatory prayer except after that. And it is permissible for a man to pray the supererogatory prayers of the first (part of the day) from the beginning of the first until four footsteps have passed. If the four footsteps pass and he has not prayed anything from the supererogatory prayers, then he should not pray the supererogatory prayers. But if he has prayed one rak‘ah, then he should complete the supererogatory prayers until he finishes them, then he should pray the Asr prayer." And Imam (a.s) said: "It is permissible for a man to pray if there remains something from the prayer of the zenith (zawal) until half a foot has passed after the arrival of Dhuhr. And if a man has already prayed something from the supererogatory prayers of Dhuhr before Asr arrives, it is permissible for him to complete the supererogatory prayers of Dhuhr until a foot has passed after the arrival of Asr." And Imam (a.s) said: "A footstep after the arrival of Asr is like half a footstep after the arrival of Dhuhr, they are the same in terms of time." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom are many missed night prayers; is it permissible for him to make up the prayers of many nights along with their witr, following one after the other? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, it is permissible for him to do so at the beginning of the night. But if half the night has passed until the rising of Fajr, then neither a man nor a woman is to perform witr except the witr of that specific night. And if he wishes to make up a missed prayer, then let him pray eight rak‘ahs from the prayer of that night and delay the witr, then make up whatever he wishes without witr, then pray the witr of that specific night alone." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom is a missed prayer from the time of being present (hadar), is it permissible for him to make it up while traveling? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, he may make it up at night on the ground. As for on the back of a mount, then no. And he should pray it as he would pray it in the state of presence (hadar)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 292

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali narrated from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "If two witr prayers, or three, or more than that have accumulated upon you, then make them up in the same order in which you missed them. Separate between each two witr prayers with a (supererogatory) prayer. Do not perform anything before the first one. The first, then the first, you begin by making up the prayer of your own night, then the witr." He said, and Abu Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: "There are not two Witrs in one night except that one of them is a makeup." And Imam (a.s) said: "If you performed Witr at the beginning of the night and then you rise at the end of the night, then your first Witr is a makeup. And whatever you have prayed from the prayers during your entire night, let them be considered as makeup until the end of your prayers, for they are for your night. And let the last of your prayers be the Witr of your night."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا اِجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْكَ وَتْرَانِ أَوْ ثَلاَثَةٌ أَوْ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَاقْضِ ذَلِكَ كَمَا فَاتَكَ تَفْصِلُ بَيْنَ كُلِّ وَتْرَيْنِ بِصَلاَةٍ لاَ تُقَدِّمَنَّ شَيْئاً قَبْلَ أَوَّلِهِ اَلْأَوَّلَ فَالْأَوَّلَ تَبْدَأُ إِذَا أَنْتَ قَضَيْتَ صَلاَةَ لَيْلَتِكَ ثُمَّ اَلْوَتْرَ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ إِلاَّ وَ أَحَدُهُمَا قَضَاءٌ» وَقَالَ« إِنْ أَوْتَرْتَ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ وَقُمْتَ فِي آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ فَوَتْرُكَ اَلْأَوَّلُ قَضَاءٌ وَمَا صَلَّيْتَ مِنْ صَلاَةٍ فِي لَيْلَتِكَ كُلِّهَا فَلْيَكُنْ قَضَاءً إِلَى آخِرِ صَلاَتِكَ فَإِنَّهَا لِلَيْلَتِكَ وَ لْيَكُنْ آخِرُ صَلاَتِكَ وَتْرَ لَيْلَتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali narrated from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "If two witr prayers, or three, or more than that have accumulated upon you, then make them up in the same order in which you missed them. Separate between each two witr prayers with a (supererogatory) prayer. Do not perform anything before the first one. The first, then the first, you begin by making up the prayer of your own night, then the witr." He said, and Abu Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: "There are not two Witrs in one night except that one of them is a makeup." And Imam (a.s) said: "If you performed Witr at the beginning of the night and then you rise at the end of the night, then your first Witr is a makeup. And whatever you have prayed from the prayers during your entire night, let them be considered as makeup until the end of your prayers, for they are for your night. And let the last of your prayers be the Witr of your night."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Abbas from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "Do not make up the Witr of your night if you have missed it until after you have prayed the prayer of the zenith (zawal) on the day of the two Eids."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لاَ تَقْضِ وَتْرَ لَيْلَتِكَ إِنْ كَانَ فَاتَكَ حَتَّى تُصَلِّيَ اَلزَّوَالَ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Abbas from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "Do not make up the Witr of your night if you have missed it until after you have prayed the prayer of the zenith (zawal) on the day of the two Eids."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Isa ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Abu Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to make up twenty Witrs in one night."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْقُمِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقْضِي عِشْرِينَ وَتْراً فِي لَيْلَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Isa ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Abu Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to make up twenty Witrs in one night."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays two rak'ahs of the Witr and forgets the third until morning comes. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the Witr when he wakes up with one rak'ah immediately."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْوَتْرِ وَ يَنْسَى اَلثَّالِثَةَ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ قَالَ« يُوتِرُ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ بِرَكْعَةٍ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays two rak'ahs of the Witr and forgets the third until morning comes. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the Witr when he wakes up with one rak'ah immediately."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar from Maymun from Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj who said:
I wrote to the Righteous servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about some matters. Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "Pray after Asr from the supererogatory prayers as much as you wish, and pray after Fajr from the supererogatory prayers as much as you wish."
arabicText: سعد عن موسى بن جعفر بن أبي جعفر عن محمد بن عبد الجبار عن ميمون عن محمد بن الفرج قال كتبت الى العبد الصالح عليه السلام اسأله عن مسائل فكتب إلي وصل بعد العصر من النوافل ما شئت وصل بعد الغداة من النوافل ما شئت
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar from Maymun from Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to the Righteous servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about some matters. Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "Pray after Asr from the supererogatory prayers as much as you wish, and pray after Fajr from the supererogatory prayers as much as you wish."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father Isma'il ibn Isa who said:
I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about a man who prays the Dhuhr prayer and then engages in supererogatory prayers, but the time for Asr comes before he completes his supererogatory prayers. Should he delay the Asr prayer in order to complete his supererogatory prayers, or should he pray the Asr and then complete the supererogatory prayers after Asr, or should he delay them until another time? Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray the Asr and make up his supererogatory prayers on another day."
arabicText: فأما ما رواه أحمد بن محمد عن سعد بن إسماعيل عن أبيه اسماعيل بن عيسى قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن الرجل يصلي الاولى ثم يتنفل فيدركه وقت العصر من قبل أن يفرغ من نافلته فيبطئ بالعصر يقضي نافلته أو يصليها بعد العصر أو يؤخرها حتى يصليها في وقت آخر؟ قال يصلي العصر ويقضي نافلته في يوم آخر
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father Isma'il ibn Isa who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about a man who prays the Dhuhr prayer and then engages in supererogatory prayers, but the time for Asr comes before he completes his supererogatory prayers. Should he delay the Asr prayer in order to complete his supererogatory prayers, or should he pray the Asr and then complete the supererogatory prayers after Asr, or should he delay them until another time? Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray the Asr and make up his supererogatory prayers on another day."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Mansur ibn Yunus from Anbasa Al-Abid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, "And He it is Who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude." (Surah Furqan 25:62) Imam (a.s) said: "Making up the prayer of the night during the day, and making up the prayer of the day during the night."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ يُونُسَ عَنْ عَنْبَسَةَ اَلْعَابِدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« وَ هُوَ اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ اَللَّيْلَ وَ اَلنَّهٰارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَنْ أَرٰادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرٰادَ شُكُوراً» قَالَ« قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ بِاللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Mansur ibn Yunus from Anbasa Al-Abid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, "And He it is Who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude." (Surah Furqan 25:62) Imam (a.s) said: "Making up the prayer of the night during the day, and making up the prayer of the day during the night."

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer Times (Mawaqit)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about (abundance of) prayers that have accumulated upon me. Imam (a.s) said: "Make an effort and make them up."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ تَجْتَمِعُ عَلَيَّ قَالَ« تَحَرَّ وَ اِقْضِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about (abundance of) prayers that have accumulated upon me. Imam (a.s) said: "Make an effort and make them up."
