chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is proper for one who recites the Qur'an, when he passes by a verse in the Qur'an that contains a supplication or a warning, that he should ask at that moment for the best of what he hopes for, and seek safety from the Fire and from punishment."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ قَرَأَ اَلْقُرْآنَ إِذَا مَرَّ بِآيَةٍ مِنَ اَلْقُرْآنِ فِيهَا مَسْأَلَةٌ أَوْ تَخْوِيفٌ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَيْرَ مَا يَرْجُو وَ يَسْأَلَ اَلْعَافِيَةَ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ وَ مِنَ اَلْعَذَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "It is proper for one who recites the Qur'an, when he passes by a verse in the Qur'an that contains a supplication or a warning, that he should ask at that moment for the best of what he hopes for, and seek safety from the Fire and from punishment."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla from Al-Washsha' from Hammad ibn Uthman from Sa'id, the seller of Al-Sabiri (a type of delicate cloth), who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Should a man force himself to weep during the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "Excellent, excellent (is such action); even if it is as little as the size of a fly's head."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلًّى عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ بَيَّاعِ اَلسَّابِرِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَتَبَاكَى اَلرَّجُلُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« بَخْ بَخْ وَ لَوْ مِثْلَ رَأْسِ اَلذُّبَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla from Al-Washsha' from Hammad ibn Uthman from Sa'id, the seller of Al-Sabiri (a type of delicate cloth), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Should a man force himself to weep during the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "Excellent, excellent (is such action); even if it is as little as the size of a fly's head."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban and Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When you stand for prayer, say: 'O Allah (swt), indeed I present Muhammad (saws) before my need and I turn towards You (azj) through Him (saws), so make me, through Him (saws), honorable in Your (azj) presence in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near. Make my prayer accepted, my sin forgiven, and my supplication through Him (saws) answered. Surely You (azj) are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'"
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ وَ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالاَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُقَدِّمُ إِلَيْكَ مُحَمَّداً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ حَاجَتِي وَ أَتَوَجَّهُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ فَاجْعَلْنِي بِهِ وَجِيهاً عِنْدَكَ« فِي اَلدُّنْيٰا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ مِنَ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ» اِجْعَلْ صَلاَتِي مَقْبُولَةً وَ ذَنْبِي مَغْفُوراً وَ دُعَائِي بِهِ مُسْتَجَاباً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْغَفُورُ اَلرَّحِيمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban and Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When you stand for prayer, say: 'O Allah (swt), indeed I present Muhammad (saws) before my need and I turn towards You (azj) through Him (saws), so make me, through Him (saws), honorable in Your (azj) presence in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near. Make my prayer accepted, my sin forgiven, and my supplication through Him (saws) answered. Surely You (azj) are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Imam (of prayer) suffices with one Takbir, and it suffices for you to say it three times calmly if you are alone."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْإِمَامُ يُجْزِيهِ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ يُجْزِيكَ ثَلاَثٌ مُتَرَسِّلاً إِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Imam (of prayer) suffices with one Takbir, and it suffices for you to say it three times calmly if you are alone."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the lightest form of Takbir in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Three Takbirs; and if there is recitation, then you should recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al Kafirun’. And if you are the Imam (of prayer), it suffices for you to pronounce one Takbir aloud and to say six (Takbirs) quietly."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَخَفِّ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ قِرَاءَةٌ قَرَأْتَ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَإِنَّهُ يُجْزِيكَ أَنْ تُكَبِّرَ وَاحِدَةً تَجْهَرُ فِيهَا وَ تُسِرُّ سِتّاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the lightest form of Takbir in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Three Takbirs; and if there is recitation, then you should recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al Kafirun’. And if you are the Imam (of prayer), it suffices for you to pronounce one Takbir aloud and to say six (Takbirs) quietly."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
I saw Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, or he said: “I heard Imam (a.s), begin the prayer with seven consecutive Takbirs.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَوْ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ اِسْتَفْتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ بِسَبْعِ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وِلاَءً
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, or he said: “I heard Imam (a.s), begin the prayer with seven consecutive Takbirs.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Abu Ja'far from Musa ibn Al-Qasim Al-Bajali and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them both:
(Imam (a.s)) said: "It is upon the Imam (of prayer) to raise his hand during the prayer; it is not upon anyone else to raise his hand during the prayer."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ اَلْبَجَلِيِّ وَ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ يَدَهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ لَيْسَ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ يَدَهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Abu Ja'far from Musa ibn Al-Qasim Al-Bajali and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: "It is upon the Imam (of prayer) to raise his hand during the prayer; it is not upon anyone else to raise his hand during the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Misma‘ Al-Basri who said:
I prayed with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Imam (a.s) recited "In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate” and then ‘Surah Al Fatiha’. Then Imam (a.s) recited the Surah after Al-Hamd and did not recite "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim." Then Imam (a.s) stood in the second unit and recited Al-Hamd and did not recite "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim" and then recited another Surah.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مِسْمَعٍ اَلْبَصْرِيِّ قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَرَأَ«« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ` اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ»» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ اَلسُّورَةَ اَلَّتِي بَعْدَ اَلْحَمْدِ وَلَمْ يَقْرَأْ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ» ثُمَّ قَامَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَقَرَأَ اَلْحَمْدَ وَلَمْ يَقْرَأْ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ بِسُورَةٍ أُخْرَى
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Misma‘ Al-Basri who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Imam (a.s) recited "In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate” and then ‘Surah Al Fatiha’. Then Imam (a.s) recited the Surah after Al-Hamd and did not recite "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim." Then Imam (a.s) stood in the second unit and recited Al-Hamd and did not recite "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim" and then recited another Surah.

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in prayer at the mosque of Banu Kahil, and Imam (a.s) recited aloud twice "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim", and Imam (a.s) performed the Qunoot in the Fajr prayer, and Imam (a.s) gave one salutation (salam) toward the Qiblah side.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي مَسْجِدِ بَنِي كَاهِلٍ فَجَهَرَ مَرَّتَيْنِ بِ«بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ وَ قَنَتَ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ وَ سَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً مِمَّا يَلِي اَلْقِبْلَةَ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in prayer at the mosque of Banu Kahil, and Imam (a.s) recited aloud twice "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim", and Imam (a.s) performed the Qunoot in the Fajr prayer, and Imam (a.s) gave one salutation (salam) toward the Qiblah side.

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is an Imam (of prayer) and begins with Al-Hamd without saying "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim". Imam (a.s) said: "It does not harm him, and there is no problem with that."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ إِمَاماً يَسْتَفْتِحُ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ لاَ يَقُولُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ قَالَ« لاَ يَضُرُّهُ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is an Imam (of prayer) and begins with Al-Hamd without saying "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim". Imam (a.s) said: "It does not harm him, and there is no problem with that."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-Abbas from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the seven oft-repeated verses’ (al-Sab‘ al-Mathani) and ‘the Great Qur'an’ (al-Qur’an al-‘Azim), is it Al-Fatiha? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: “Is ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ among the seven (al-Sab‘ al-Mathani)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, it is the best of them."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلسَّبْعِ اَلْمَثٰانِي وَ اَلْقُرْآنَ اَلْعَظِيمَ هِيَ اَلْفَاتِحَةُ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ:« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ مِنَ اَلسَّبْعِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ هِيَ أَفْضَلُهُنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-Abbas from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the seven oft-repeated verses’ (al-Sab‘ al-Mathani) and ‘the Great Qur'an’ (al-Qur’an al-‘Azim), is it Al-Fatiha? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: “Is ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ among the seven (al-Sab‘ al-Mathani)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, it is the best of them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdul-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Imam (a.s) sought refuge (with Allah (swt)) aloud, then Imam (a.s) recited aloud “Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلصَّمَدِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَتَعَوَّذَ بِإِجْهَارٍ ثُمَّ جَهَرَ بِِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdul-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Imam (a.s) sought refuge (with Allah (swt)) aloud, then Imam (a.s) recited aloud “Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), said: “Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim” is closer to the Greatest Name of Allah (swt) (al-Ism al-A'zam) than the pupil of the eye is to its white.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ:«« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ أَقْرَبُ إِلَى اِسْمِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَعْظَمِ مِنْ نَاظِرِ اَلْعَيْنِ إِلَى بَيَاضِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abdullah ibn Yahya Al-Kahili:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), said: “Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim” is closer to the Greatest Name of Allah (swt) (al-Ism al-A'zam) than the pupil of the eye is to its white.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, should he recite aloud in his voluntary (nafl) prayers during the day? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يَجْهَرُ بِقِرَاءَتِهِ فِي اَلتَّطَوُّعِ بِالنَّهَارِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, should he recite aloud in his voluntary (nafl) prayers during the day? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah in the daytime prayer is to recite quietly, and the Sunnah in the nighttime prayer is to recite aloud."
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلسُّنَّةُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ بِالْإِخْفَاتِ وَ اَلسُّنَّةُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِالْإِجْهَارِ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah in the daytime prayer is to recite quietly, and the Sunnah in the nighttime prayer is to recite aloud."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Sabbah Al-Hadhdha’ from a man from Abu Hamzah who said:
(Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them, said: "O Thumali, when the prayer is established, Satan comes to the companion of the Imam (of prayer) and says: 'Has he (Imam of Prayer) remembered his Lord (azj)?' If he says, ‘Yes,’ he (Satan) departs. But if he says, ‘No,’ he (Satan) mounts upon his shoulders and becomes the leader of the people until they finish." He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘May I be your ransom, do they not recite the Qur'an?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but not in the way you think, O Thumali. What is meant is reciting aloud ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’".
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَبَّاحٍ اَلْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ قَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا ثُمَالِيُّ إِنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا أُقِيمَتْ جَاءَ اَلشَّيْطَانُ إِلَى قَرِينِ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيَقُولُ هَلْ ذَكَرَ رَبَّهُ فَإِنْ قَالَ نَعَمْ ذَهَبَ وَ إِنْ قَالَ لاَ رَكِبَ عَلَى كَتِفَيْهِ فَكَانَ إِمَامَ اَلْقَوْمِ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفُوا» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَ لَيْسَ يَقْرَءُونَ اَلْقُرْآنَ قَالَ« بَلَى لَيْسَ حَيْثُ تَذْهَبُ يَا ثُمَالِيُّ إِنَّمَا هُوَ اَلْجَهْرُ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Sabbah Al-Hadhdha’ from a man from Abu Hamzah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them, said: "O Thumali, when the prayer is established, Satan comes to the companion of the Imam (of prayer) and says: 'Has he (Imam of Prayer) remembered his Lord (azj)?' If he says, ‘Yes,’ he (Satan) departs. But if he says, ‘No,’ he (Satan) mounts upon his shoulders and becomes the leader of the people until they finish." He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘May I be your ransom, do they not recite the Qur'an?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but not in the way you think, O Thumali. What is meant is reciting aloud ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’".

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 313

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zadawayh from Ibn Rashid who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, you wrote to Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj informing him that the best of what is recited in the obligatory prayers is ‘Surah Al-Qadr’ and ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’, but my chest feels tight when reciting them at Fajr.” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not let your chest be tight with them, for by Allah (swt), the virtue lies within them."
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبْدُوسٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زَادَوَيْهِ[ زَادَوَيْهِ خ ل] عَنِ اِبْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّكَ كَتَبْتَ إِلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفَرَجِ تُعْلِمُهُ أَنَّ أَفْضَلَ مَا يُقْرَأُ فِي اَلْفَرَائِضِ« إِنّٰا أَنْزَلْنٰاهُ» وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ إِنَّ صَدْرِي لَيَضِيقُ بِقِرَاءَتِهِمَا فِي اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ يَضِيقَنَّ صَدْرُكَ بِهِمَا فَإِنَّ اَلْفَضْلَ وَ اَللَّهِ فِيهِمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zadawayh from Ibn Rashid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, you wrote to Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj informing him that the best of what is recited in the obligatory prayers is ‘Surah Al-Qadr’ and ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’, but my chest feels tight when reciting them at Fajr.” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not let your chest be tight with them, for by Allah (swt), the virtue lies within them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 313

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, "And do not raise your voice in your prayer nor lower it too much" (Surah Al-Isra, 17:110). Imam (a.s) said: "Lowering the voice (mukhafatah) is to recite below the level of your own hearing, and raising the voice (jahr) is to raise your voice loudly and strongly."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« وَ لاٰ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاٰتِكَ وَ لاٰ تُخٰافِتْ بِهٰا» قَالَ« اَلْمُخَافَتَةُ مَا دُونَ سَمْعِكَ وَ اَلْجَهْرُ أَنْ تَرْفَعَ صَوْتَكَ شَدِيداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, "And do not raise your voice in your prayer nor lower it too much" (Surah Al-Isra, 17:110). Imam (a.s) said: "Lowering the voice (mukhafatah) is to recite below the level of your own hearing, and raising the voice (jahr) is to raise your voice loudly and strongly."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 313

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Al-Nawfali from Al-Sakuni:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who is praying in a place and then wishes to move forward. Imam (a.s) said: "He should stop reciting while walking until he reaches the place he intends, then he should resume his recitation."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي مَوْضِعٍ ثُمَّ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ قَالَ« يَكُفُّ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي مَشْيِهِ حَتَّى يَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَى اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي يُرِيدُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Al-Nawfali from Al-Sakuni:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who is praying in a place and then wishes to move forward. Imam (a.s) said: "He should stop reciting while walking until he reaches the place he intends, then he should resume his recitation."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 313

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Amr ibn Abi Nasr who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to recite a Surah, but he recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’. Imam (a.s) said: "He may turn back from any Surah except from ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."
arabicText: الحسين بن محمد عن عبد الله بن عامر عن علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة بن أيوب عن الحسين بن عثمان عن عمرو بن أبى نصر قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام الرجل يقوم في الصلاة فيريد أن يقرأ سورة فيقرأ قل هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون فقال يرجع من كل سورة إلا من قل هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Amr ibn Abi Nasr who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to recite a Surah, but he recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’. Imam (a.s) said: "He may turn back from any Surah except from ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 313

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who recites a verse of prostration (sajdah) at the end of a Surah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the prostration, then stand, recite the ‘Surah Al-Fatiha’, then bow (for Ruku') and prostrate."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ بِالسَّجْدَةِ فِي آخِرِ اَلسُّورَةِ قَالَ« يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ يَرْكَعُ وَ يَسْجُدُ
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who recites a verse of prostration (sajdah) at the end of a Surah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform the prostration, then stand, recite the ‘Surah Al-Fatiha’, then bow (for Ruku') and prostrate."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 314

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you pray with a group and the Imam (of prayer) recites ‘Surah Al-‘Alaq’ or something from the obligatory verses of prostration (al-‘Aza’im), and he finishes his recitation without performing a prostration, then you should gesture with an indication (for the prostration), and a woman in menstruation should prostrate if she hears the verse of prostration."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فَقَرَأَ اَلْإِمَامُ اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ اَلَّذِي خَلَقَ أَوْ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ وَ فَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهِ وَ لَمْ يَسْجُدْ فَأَوْمِ إِيمَاءً وَ اَلْحَائِضُ تَسْجُدُ إِذَا سَمِعَتِ اَلسَّجْدَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you pray with a group and the Imam (of prayer) recites ‘Surah Al-‘Alaq’ or something from the obligatory verses of prostration (al-‘Aza’im), and he finishes his recitation without performing a prostration, then you should gesture with an indication (for the prostration), and a woman in menstruation should prostrate if she hears the verse of prostration."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 314

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who hears a verse of prostration being recited. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not prostrate unless he is attentively listening to the recitation or praying behind the one who is reciting. But if he is praying in one area and you are in another, then do not prostrate for what you heard."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَمِعَ اَلسَّجْدَةَ تُقْرَأُ قَالَ« لاَ يَسْجُدُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُنْصِتاً لِلْقِرَاءَةِ مُسْتَمِعاً لَهَا أَوْ يُصَلِّي بِصَلاَتِهِ فَأَمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ يُصَلِّي فِي نَاحِيَةٍ وَ أَنْتَ فِي نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى فَلاَ تَسْجُدْ لِمَا سَمِعْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who hears a verse of prostration being recited. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not prostrate unless he is attentively listening to the recitation or praying behind the one who is reciting. But if he is praying in one area and you are in another, then do not prostrate for what you heard."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 315

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When you recite something from the obligatory verses of prostration (al-‘Aza’im) in which prostration is required, do not say the Takbir before your prostration, but say Takbir when you lift your head. And obligatory prostrations are four; Surah Fussilat, Surah As-Sajdah, Surah An-Najm, and Surah Al-‘Alaq."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ اَلَّتِي يُسْجَدُ فِيهَا فَلاَ تُكَبِّرْ قَبْلَ سُجُودِكَ وَ لَكِنْ تُكَبِّرُ حِينَ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ وَ اَلْعَزَائِمُ أَرْبَعَةٌ حم اَلسَّجْدَةُ وَ الم تَنْزِيلٌ وَ اَلنَّجْمُ وَ اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "When you recite something from the obligatory verses of prostration (al-‘Aza’im) in which prostration is required, do not say the Takbir before your prostration, but say Takbir when you lift your head. And obligatory prostrations are four; Surah Fussilat, Surah As-Sajdah, Surah An-Najm, and Surah Al-‘Alaq."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 315

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
He said: "When something from the four obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im) is recited and you hear it, then prostrate, even if you are without ablution, even if you are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), and even if it is a woman who is not praying. As for the rest of the Qur'an, you have a choice: if you wish, you may prostrate, and if you wish, you may not prostrate."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُرِئَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ اَلْأَرْبَعَةِ فَسَمِعْتَهَا فَاسْجُدْ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ جُنُباً وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ لاَ تُصَلِّي وَ سَائِرُ اَلْقُرْآنِ أَنْتَ فِيهِ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شِئْتَ سَجَدْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لَمْ تَسْجُدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He said: "When something from the four obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im) is recited and you hear it, then prostrate, even if you are without ablution, even if you are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), and even if it is a woman who is not praying. As for the rest of the Qur'an, you have a choice: if you wish, you may prostrate, and if you wish, you may not prostrate."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 315

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a menstruating woman, does she recite the Qur'an and perform the prostration if she hears a verse of prostration? Imam (a.s) said: "She may recite but she does not prostrate."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْحَائِضِ هَلْ تَقْرَأُ اَلْقُرْآنَ وَتَسْجُدُ سَجْدَةً إِذَا سَمِعَتِ اَلسَّجْدَةَ قَالَ« تَقْرَأُ وَلاَ تَسْجُدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a menstruating woman, does she recite the Qur'an and perform the prostration if she hears a verse of prostration? Imam (a.s) said: "She may recite but she does not prostrate."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 315

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abu Al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (narrated) from his father (a.s), from (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If the prostration is at the end of the Surah, it suffices you to bow (perform Ruku') for it."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ وَهْبِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَانَ آخِرُ اَلسُّورَةِ اَلسَّجْدَةَ أَجْزَأَكَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abu Al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (narrated) from his father (a.s), from (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If the prostration is at the end of the Surah, it suffices you to bow (perform Ruku') for it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 316

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah:
He said: "Whoever recites ‘Iqra' bismi Rabbik’ (Surah Al-‘Alaq), when he finishes it, he should prostrate, and when he stands up, he should recite the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and then bow." He said: "And if you are tested with this situation while praying behind an Imam who does not perform the prostration, then gesturing and bowing suffices for you, and do not recite it in an obligatory prayer; recite it in a voluntary prayer."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ:« مَنْ قَرَأَ اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِذَا خَتَمَهَا فَلْيَسْجُدْ فَإِذَا قَامَ فَلْيَقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ لْيَرْكَعْ» قَالَ« وَ إِنِ اُبْتُلِيتَ بِهَا مَعَ إِمَامٍ لاَ يَسْجُدُ فَيُجْزِيكَ اَلْإِيمَاءُ وَ اَلرُّكُوعُ وَ لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ اِقْرَأْ فِي اَلتَّطَوُّعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah:
thaqalaynMatn: He said: "Whoever recites ‘Iqra' bismi Rabbik’ (Surah Al-‘Alaq), when he finishes it, he should prostrate, and when he stands up, he should recite the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and then bow." He said: "And if you are tested with this situation while praying behind an Imam who does not perform the prostration, then gesturing and bowing suffices for you, and do not recite it in an obligatory prayer; recite it in a voluntary prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 316

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When you recite a verse of prostration, then prostrate, and do not say the Takbir until you lift your head."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا قَرَأْتَ اَلسَّجْدَةَ فَاسْجُدْ وَ لاَ تُكَبِّرْ حَتَّى تَرْفَعَ رَأْسَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When you recite a verse of prostration, then prostrate, and do not say the Takbir until you lift your head."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 316

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites a verse of prostration and forgets it until he bows and prostrates. Imam (a.s) said: "He should prostrate when he remembers, if it was from the obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ اَلسَّجْدَةَ فَيَنْسَاهَا حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ وَ يَسْجُدَ قَالَ« يَسْجُدُ إِذَا ذَكَرَ إِذَا كَانَتْ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites a verse of prostration and forgets it until he bows and prostrates. Imam (a.s) said: "He should prostrate when he remembers, if it was from the obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 316

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who hears a verse of prostration at a time when prayer is not valid, before the setting of the sun and after the prayer of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not prostrate." And (Imam (a.s) said) regarding a man who recites in an obligatory prayer a Surah that contains a verse of prostration from the obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im). Imam (a.s) said: "When he reaches the place of the prostration, he should not recite it, and if he wishes, he may go back and recite another Surah and leave the one that contains the prostration, thus turning to another one." And (Imam (a.s) said) regarding a man who prays among a group without following them and prays for himself, and they might recite a verse from the obligatory prostrations but they do not prostrate therein, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He does not prostrate."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْمَعُ اَلسَّجْدَةَ فِي اَلسَّاعَةِ اَلَّتِي لاَ يَسْتَقِيمُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهَا قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَسْجُدُ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ سُورَةً فِيهَا سَجْدَةٌ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا بَلَغَ مَوْضِعَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ فَلاَ يَقْرَأْهَا وَ إِنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فَيَقْرَأَ سُورَةً غَيْرَهَا وَ يَدَعَ اَلَّتِي فِيهَا اَلسَّجْدَةُ فَيَرْجِعُ إِلَى غَيْرِهَا» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ قَوْمٍ لاَ يَقْتَدِي بِهِمْ فَيُصَلِّي لِنَفْسِهِ وَ رُبَّمَا قَرَءُوا آيَةً مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ فَلاَ يَسْجُدُونَ فِيهَا فَكَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« لاَ يَسْجُدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who hears a verse of prostration at a time when prayer is not valid, before the setting of the sun and after the prayer of Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not prostrate." And (Imam (a.s) said) regarding a man who recites in an obligatory prayer a Surah that contains a verse of prostration from the obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im). Imam (a.s) said: "When he reaches the place of the prostration, he should not recite it, and if he wishes, he may go back and recite another Surah and leave the one that contains the prostration, thus turning to another one." And (Imam (a.s) said) regarding a man who prays among a group without following them and prays for himself, and they might recite a verse from the obligatory prostrations but they do not prostrate therein, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He does not prostrate."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 317

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn Al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who recites a verse of prostration and then becomes impure (loses his ablution) before he performs the prostration, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should appoint another person to lead; that person should perform the tashahhud, prostrate, and then they should all finish their prayer, and the Imam (of prayer) who became impure should withdraw, and the prayer of the congregation is complete."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ إِمَامٍ قَرَأَ اَلسَّجْدَةَ فَأَحْدَثَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يُقَدِّمُ غَيْرَهُ فَيَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَسْجُدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ هُوَ وَ قَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn Al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who recites a verse of prostration and then becomes impure (loses his ablution) before he performs the prostration, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should appoint another person to lead; that person should perform the tashahhud, prostrate, and then they should all finish their prayer, and the Imam (of prayer) who became impure should withdraw, and the prayer of the congregation is complete."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 317

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is being taught a Surah that contains an obligatory prostration (from the 'Aza’im), and it is repeated to him several times in a single sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "It is obligatory upon him to prostrate each time he hears it, and it is also obligatory upon the one teaching him to prostrate."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُعَلَّمُ اَلسُّورَةَ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ فَتُعَادُ عَلَيْهِ مِرَاراً فِي اَلْمَقْعَدِ اَلْوَاحِدِ قَالَ« عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ كُلَّمَا سَمِعَهَا وَ عَلَى اَلَّذِي يُعَلِّمُهُ أَيْضاً أَنْ يَسْجُدَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is being taught a Surah that contains an obligatory prostration (from the 'Aza’im), and it is repeated to him several times in a single sitting. Imam (a.s) said: "It is obligatory upon him to prostrate each time he hears it, and it is also obligatory upon the one teaching him to prostrate."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 317

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who intends to recite a Surah but then recites another one instead. Imam (a.s) said: "He is allowed to return (to the intended Surah) as long as he has not recited two-thirds of it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ اَلسُّورَةَ فَيَقْرَأُ غَيْرَهَا فَقَالَ« لَهُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ ثُلُثَيْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who intends to recite a Surah but then recites another one instead. Imam (a.s) said: "He is allowed to return (to the intended Surah) as long as he has not recited two-thirds of it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 317

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man recites a Surah in a rak'ah and makes a mistake, should he leave the place where he made the mistake and continue in his recitation, or should he leave that Surah and move to another Surah?” Imam (a.s) said: "All of that is permissible; and if he recites even a single verse and then wishes to bow with it, he may bow."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ قَرَأَ سُورَةً فِي رَكْعَةٍ فَغَلِطَ أَ يَدَعُ اَلْمَكَانَ اَلَّذِي غَلِطَ فِيهِ وَ يَمْضِي فِي قِرَاءَتِهِ أَوْ يَدَعُ تِلْكَ اَلسُّورَةَ وَ يَتَحَوَّلُ مِنْهَا إِلَى غَيْرِهَا فَقَالَ« كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ قَرَأَ آيَةً وَاحِدَةً فَشَاءَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ بِهَا رَكَعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man recites a Surah in a rak'ah and makes a mistake, should he leave the place where he made the mistake and continue in his recitation, or should he leave that Surah and move to another Surah?” Imam (a.s) said: "All of that is permissible; and if he recites even a single verse and then wishes to bow with it, he may bow."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 317

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin Al-Basri from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a Surah, can a man pray with it in the two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if it consists of six verses, he may recite half of it in the first rak'ah and the other half in the second rak'ah."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يَاسِينَ اَلْبَصْرِيِّ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلسُّورَةِ أَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ بِهَا فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَتْ سِتَّ آيَاتٍ قَرَأَ بِالنِّصْفِ مِنْهَا فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلنِّصْفِ اَلْآخَرِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin Al-Basri from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a Surah, can a man pray with it in the two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if it consists of six verses, he may recite half of it in the first rak'ah and the other half in the second rak'ah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 318

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, prayed with us, and they (a.s) recited the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and the end of Surah Al-Ma'idah. When they finished and gave the salam, they turned to us and said: "Indeed, I only intended to teach you."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَرَأَ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ آخِرِ سُورَةِ اَلْمَائِدَةِ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ اِلْتَفَتَ إِلَيْنَا فَقَالَ «أَمَا إِنِّي إِنَّمَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُعَلِّمَكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, prayed with us, and they (a.s) recited the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and the end of Surah Al-Ma'idah. When they finished and gave the salam, they turned to us and said: "Indeed, I only intended to teach you."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What do you say about a man who is praying while looking into the Mushaf, reading from it, and placing a lamp close to him?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ يَنْظُرُ فِي اَلْمُصْحَفِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِ يَضَعُ اَلسِّرَاجَ قَرِيباً مِنْهُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What do you say about a man who is praying while looking into the Mushaf, reading from it, and placing a lamp close to him?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about reciting behind the Imam (of prayer) in the last two rak'ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "The Imam (of prayer) recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha), and those behind him should glorify (say tasbih). If you are praying alone, then you may either recite (Surah Al-Fatiha) in them or, if you wish, you may glorify."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« اَلْإِمَامُ يَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَمَنْ خَلْفَهُ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَاقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَسَبِّحْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about reciting behind the Imam (of prayer) in the last two rak'ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "The Imam (of prayer) recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha), and those behind him should glorify (say tasbih). If you are praying alone, then you may either recite (Surah Al-Fatiha) in them or, if you wish, you may glorify."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about what the Imam (of prayer) recites in the last two rak'ahs of the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha), and those behind him do not recite. And a man who is praying alone recites Al-Fatiha in them."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّا يَقْرَأُ اَلْإِمَامُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فِي آخِرِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ لاَ يَقْرَأُ اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ وَ يَقْرَأُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِيهِمَا إِذَا صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about what the Imam (of prayer) recites in the last two rak'ahs of the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha), and those behind him do not recite. And a man who is praying alone recites Al-Fatiha in them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 319

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever makes a mistake in a Surah, let him recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and then bow."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ غَلِطَ فِي سُورَةٍ فَلْيَقْرَأْ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ لْيَرْكَعْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever makes a mistake in a Surah, let him recite ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and then bow."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 319

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Sometimes standing in prayer becomes difficult for me.” Imam (a.s) said: "If you want to attain the reward of the one who stands in prayer, then recite while you are sitting, and when only two verses remain from the Surah, then stand up, complete what remains, bow, and prostrate, that will be counted as the prayer of one who stood."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَدْ يَشْتَدُّ عَلَيَّ اَلْقِيَامُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُدْرِكَ صَلاَةَ اَلْقَائِمِ فَاقْرَأْ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ فَإِذَا بَقِيَ مِنَ اَلسُّورَةِ آيَتَانِ فَقُمْ فَأَتِمَّ مَا بَقِيَ وَ اِرْكَعْ وَ اُسْجُدْ فَذَلِكَ صَلاَةُ اَلْقَائِمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Sometimes standing in prayer becomes difficult for me.” Imam (a.s) said: "If you want to attain the reward of the one who stands in prayer, then recite while you are sitting, and when only two verses remain from the Surah, then stand up, complete what remains, bow, and prostrate, that will be counted as the prayer of one who stood."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 319

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Amir ibn Abdullah who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Whoever recites something from the Hawamim (the Surahs beginning with 'Ha Mim') in the Fajr prayer, for he will miss the time (of the prayer due to length of the Surahs)."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ عَامِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« مَنْ قَرَأَ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلْحَوَامِيمِ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَاتَهُ اَلْوَقْتُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Amir ibn Abdullah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Whoever recites something from the Hawamim (the Surahs beginning with 'Ha Mim') in the Fajr prayer, for he will miss the time (of the prayer due to length of the Surahs)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 319

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Isma'il ibn Abd Al-Khaliq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Talhah, from Abd Al-Khaliq:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to recite in the two rak'ahs after the night prayer (Al-Atamah) ‘Surah Al-Waqi'ah’ and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْعَتَمَةِ بِالْوَاقِعَةِ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Isma'il ibn Abd Al-Khaliq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Talhah, from Abd Al-Khaliq:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to recite in the two rak'ahs after the night prayer (Al-Atamah) ‘Surah Al-Waqi'ah’ and ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 319

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd Al-Ash'ari, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recited Al-Hamd and half of a Surah in one rak'ah, would it suffice in the second rak'ah not to recite Al-Hamd and only recite what remains of the Surah? Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite Al-Hamd, then recite what remains of the Surah."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ قَرَأَ فِي رَكْعَةٍ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ نِصْفَ سُورَةٍ هَلْ يُجْزِيهِ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ أَنْ لاَ يَقْرَأَ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ يَقْرَأَ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ اَلسُّورَةِ فَقَالَ« يَقْرَأُ اَلْحَمْدَ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ اَلسُّورَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd Al-Ash'ari, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recited Al-Hamd and half of a Surah in one rak'ah, would it suffice in the second rak'ah not to recite Al-Hamd and only recite what remains of the Surah? Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite Al-Hamd, then recite what remains of the Surah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 320

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from their father Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about combining two Surahs in the obligatory and the supererogatory prayers. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about reciting part of a Surah. Imam (a.s) said: "I dislike that, but there is no harm in it for the supererogatory prayers." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about the two rak'ahs in which the Imam (of prayer) remains silent, should ‘Surah Al-Hamd’ be recited in them when one is following an Imam (of prayer)? Imam (a.s) said: "If you recite, there is no harm; and if you remain silent, there is no harm."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقِرَانِ بَيْنَ اَلسُّورَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ وَ اَلنَّافِلَةِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» وَ عَنْ تَبْعِيضِ اَلسُّورَةِ قَالَ« أَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ يَصْمُتُ فِيهِمَا اَلْإِمَامُ أَ يُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِالْحَمْدِ وَ هُوَ إِمَامٌ يُقْتَدَى بِهِ قَالَ« إِنْ قَرَأْتَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ سَكَتَّ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from their father Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about combining two Surahs in the obligatory and the supererogatory prayers. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about reciting part of a Surah. Imam (a.s) said: "I dislike that, but there is no harm in it for the supererogatory prayers." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about the two rak'ahs in which the Imam (of prayer) remains silent, should ‘Surah Al-Hamd’ be recited in them when one is following an Imam (of prayer)? Imam (a.s) said: "If you recite, there is no harm; and if you remain silent, there is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 320

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Al-‘Amraki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites in an obligatory prayer the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and another Surah in one breath. Imam (a.s) said: "If he wishes, he may recite them in one breath, and if he wishes, he may recite them in separate breaths."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى ع قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ سُورَةٍ أُخْرَى فِي اَلنَّفَسِ اَلْوَاحِدِ قَالَ« إِنْ شَاءَ قَرَأَ فِي نَفَسٍ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ فِي غَيْرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Al-‘Amraki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who recites in an obligatory prayer the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and another Surah in one breath. Imam (a.s) said: "If he wishes, he may recite them in one breath, and if he wishes, he may recite them in separate breaths."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about joining the prayer behind someone while I am reciting behind him in the second rak'ah, and he bows just as I finish reciting the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha). Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the last two rak'ahs so that you will have recited in two rak'ahs."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ دُخُولِي مَعَ مَنْ أَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَيَرْكَعُ عِنْدَ فَرَاغِي مِنْ قِرَاءَةِ أُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ فَقَالَ« تَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأُخْرَاوَيْنِ كَيْ تَكُونَ قَدْ قَرَأْتَ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about joining the prayer behind someone while I am reciting behind him in the second rak'ah, and he bows just as I finish reciting the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha). Imam (a.s) said: "Recite in the last two rak'ahs so that you will have recited in two rak'ahs."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who forgets a letter from the Qur'an and remembers it while he is bowing, is it permissible for him to recite it? Imam (a.s) said: "No, but when he prostrates, let him recite it." And Imam (a.s) said: "When a man recites ‘By the sun and its brightness’ (Surah Al-Shams), upon completing it, he should say: 'Allah (swt) and His Messenger (saws) have spoken the truth.' And when a man recites ‘Is Allah (swt) better, or what they associate with Him?’ (Surah An-Naml 27:59), he should say: 'Allah (swt) is better, Allah (swt) is better, Allah (swt) is greater.' And when he recites ‘Then those who disbelieve set equals with their Lord’ (Surah Al-An‘am 6:1), he should say: 'Those who set equals with Allah (swt) have lied.' And when he recites ‘Praise be to Allah (swt), who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in His dominion, nor any protector out of weakness, and glorify Him with great glorification’ (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:111), he should say: 'Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest.'" I asked: “What if a man does not say anything of this when he recites?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon him."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى حَرْفاً مِنَ اَلْقُرْآنِ فَذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ رَاكِعٌ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَهُ قَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا سَجَدَ فَلْيَقْرَأْهُ» وَ قَالَ« اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا قَرَأَ« وَ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» فَيَخْتِمُهَا أَنْ يَقُولَ صَدَقَ اَللَّهُ وَ صَدَقَ رَسُولُهُ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا قَرَأَ« آللّٰهُ خَيْرٌ أَمّٰا يُشْرِكُونَ» أَنْ يَقُولَ اَللَّهُ خَيْرٌ اَللَّهُ خَيْرٌ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ إِذَا قَرَأَ« ثُمَّ اَلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ» أَنْ يَقُولَ كَذَبَ اَلْعَادِلُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا قَرَأَ« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ اَلَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَداً وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي اَلْمُلْكِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ مِنَ اَلذُّلِّ وَ كَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيراً» أَنْ يَقُولَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقُلِ اَلرَّجُلُ شَيْئاً مِنْ هَذَا إِذَا قَرَأَ قَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who forgets a letter from the Qur'an and remembers it while he is bowing, is it permissible for him to recite it? Imam (a.s) said: "No, but when he prostrates, let him recite it." And Imam (a.s) said: "When a man recites ‘By the sun and its brightness’ (Surah Al-Shams), upon completing it, he should say: 'Allah (swt) and His Messenger (saws) have spoken the truth.' And when a man recites ‘Is Allah (swt) better, or what they associate with Him?’ (Surah An-Naml 27:59), he should say: 'Allah (swt) is better, Allah (swt) is better, Allah (swt) is greater.' And when he recites ‘Then those who disbelieve set equals with their Lord’ (Surah Al-An‘am 6:1), he should say: 'Those who set equals with Allah (swt) have lied.' And when he recites ‘Praise be to Allah (swt), who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in His dominion, nor any protector out of weakness, and glorify Him with great glorification’ (Surah Al-Isra’ 17:111), he should say: 'Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest.'" I asked: “What if a man does not say anything of this when he recites?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon him."
