chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Abdullah ibn Ali Al-Zarrad who said:
Abu Kahmas asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Should a man perform his nawafil prayers (supererogatory prayers) in one place or should he distribute them in different places?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather here and there, for indeed they will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلزَّرَّادِ قَالَ: سَأَلَ أَبُو كَهْمَسٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ نَوَافِلَهُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ أَوْ يُفَرِّقُهَا قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ هَاهُنَا وَ هَاهُنَا فَإِنَّهَا تَشْهَدُ لَهُ يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Abdullah ibn Ali Al-Zarrad who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Kahmas asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Should a man perform his nawafil prayers (supererogatory prayers) in one place or should he distribute them in different places?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather here and there, for indeed they will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 360

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Harun from Murazim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “When should I pray the night prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray it at the end of the night." I said: “But I do not wake up.” Imam (a.s) said: "You will wake up once, so pray it, then if you sleep, you can make it up. When you become concerned with making it up during the day, you will wake up (at night)."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ هَارُونَ عَنْ مُرَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَتَى أُصَلِّي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ« صَلِّهَا آخِرَ اَللَّيْلِ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ فَإِنِّي لاَ أَسْتَنْبِهُ فَقَالَ« تَسْتَنْبِهُ مَرَّةً فَتُصَلِّيهَا وَ تَنَامُ فَتَقْضِيهَا فَإِذَا اِهْتَمَمْتَ بِقَضَائِهَا بِالنَّهَارِ اِسْتَنْبَهْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Harun from Murazim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “When should I pray the night prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray it at the end of the night." I said: “But I do not wake up.” Imam (a.s) said: "You will wake up once, so pray it, then if you sleep, you can make it up. When you become concerned with making it up during the day, you will wake up (at night)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 360

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa Al-Ubaydi from Ali and Ishaq, the two sons of Sulayman ibn Dawud, that Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed them, saying:
I wrote to the Faqih (jurist): "O my master, I made a vow that whenever I miss the night prayer, I would fast the following morning. If he misses it, what should he do? Is there a way out for him, and how much expiation is due upon him for each day he misses if he chooses to offer expiation?" So He wrote: "For each day, he should give a mudd of food as expiation."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ وَ إِسْحَاقَ اِبْنَيْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ أَنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ أَخْبَرَهُمَا قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلْفَقِيهِ يَا مَوْلاَيَ نَذَرْتُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَتَى فَاتَتْنِي صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ صُمْتُ فِي صَبِيحَتِهَا فَفَاتَهُ ذَلِكَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَهَلْ لَهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَخْرَجٌ وَ كَمْ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ فِي صَوْمِ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ تَرَكَهُ إِنْ كَفَّرَ إِنْ أَرَادَ ذَلِكَ فَكَتَبَ« يُفَرِّقُ عَنْ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ بِمُدٍّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ كَفَّارَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa Al-Ubaydi from Ali and Ishaq, the two sons of Sulayman ibn Dawud, that Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed them, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to the Faqih (jurist): "O my master, I made a vow that whenever I miss the night prayer, I would fast the following morning. If he misses it, what should he do? Is there a way out for him, and how much expiation is due upon him for each day he misses if he chooses to offer expiation?" So He wrote: "For each day, he should give a mudd of food as expiation."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Al-Abbas ibn Amir from Jabir from Abu Basir:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said regarding the verse: "They used to sleep but little of the night" (Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:17) Imam (a.s) said: "The people used to sleep, but whenever one of them turned over, he would say, 'Praise be to Allah (swt), there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest.'"
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:«« كٰانُوا قَلِيلاً مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ مٰا يَهْجَعُونَ»» قَالَ« كَانَ اَلْقَوْمُ يَنَامُونَ وَ لَكِنْ كُلَّمَا اِنْقَلَبَ أَحَدُهُمْ قَالَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Al-Abbas ibn Amir from Jabir from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said regarding the verse: "They used to sleep but little of the night" (Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:17) Imam (a.s) said: "The people used to sleep, but whenever one of them turned over, he would say, 'Praise be to Allah (swt), there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest.'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 360

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best in speech," (Surah Muzzammil 73:6). Imam (a.s) said: "By His (azj) saying 'and the best in speech', He (azj) means the rising of a man from his bed intending by it Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and intending no one other than Him (azj)."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« إِنَّ نٰاشِئَةَ اَللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً وَ أَقْوَمُ قِيلاً» قَالَ« يَعْنِي بِقَوْلِهِ« وَ أَقْوَمُ قِيلاً» قِيَامَ اَلرَّجُلِ عَنْ فِرَاشِهِ يُرِيدُ بِهِ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لاَ يُرِيدُ بِهِ غَيْرَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best in speech," (Surah Muzzammil 73:6). Imam (a.s) said: "By His (azj) saying 'and the best in speech', He (azj) means the rising of a man from his bed intending by it Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and intending no one other than Him (azj)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 361

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: "They used to sleep but little of the night" (Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:17) Imam (a.s) said: "The nights in which they missed getting up were very few; they would stand in prayer in most of the nights."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ« كٰانُوا قَلِيلاً مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ مٰا يَهْجَعُونَ» قَالَ« كَانُوا أَقَلَّ اَللَّيَالِي تَفُوتُهُمْ لاَ يَقُومُونَ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: "They used to sleep but little of the night" (Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:17) Imam (a.s) said: "The nights in which they missed getting up were very few; they would stand in prayer in most of the nights."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 361

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Ibn Muskan from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him (a.s): “A man prays the two rak'ahs of witr, then he stands and forgets the tashahhud until he bows, and remembers while bowing.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should sit from his bowing, perform the tashahhud, then stand and complete (his prayer)." I asked: “Did you not say regarding the obligatory prayer that if he remembers after bowing, he should continue, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness after he finishes and recite the tashahhud in them?” Imam (a.s) said: "The supererogatory prayer (nafila) is not like the obligatory prayer (faridah)."
arabicText: علي بن ابراهيم عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن المغيرة عن ابن مسكان عن الحسن الصيقل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له الرجل يصلي الركعتين من الوتر ثم يقوم فينسى التشهد حتى يركع فيذكر وهو راكع قال يجلس من ركوعه ويتشهد ثم يقوم فيتم قال قلت أليس قلت في الفريضة إذا ذكره بعدما ركع مضى ثم سجد سجدتي السهو بعدما ينصرف يتشهد فيهما؟ قال ليس النافلة مثل الفريضة
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Ibn Muskan from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Him (a.s): “A man prays the two rak'ahs of witr, then he stands and forgets the tashahhud until he bows, and remembers while bowing.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should sit from his bowing, perform the tashahhud, then stand and complete (his prayer)." I asked: “Did you not say regarding the obligatory prayer that if he remembers after bowing, he should continue, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness after he finishes and recite the tashahhud in them?” Imam (a.s) said: "The supererogatory prayer (nafila) is not like the obligatory prayer (faridah)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 361

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the best time for the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "The beginning of dawn is the best for that."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ سَاعَاتِ اَلْوَتْرِ فَقَالَ« اَلْفَجْرُ أَوَّلُ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the best time for the witr prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "The beginning of dawn is the best for that."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 361

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him: “The two rak'ahs before the morning prayer (Fajr), when is their time?” Imam (a.s) said: "Before the rising of the dawn; and when the dawn rises, then the time for the morning prayer has entered."
arabicText: علي عن أبيه عن ابن أبي عمير عن ابن اذينة عن زرارة قال قلت لابي جعفر عليه السلام الركعتان اللتان قبل الغداة أين موضعهما؟ فقال قبل طلوع الفجر فإذا طلع الفجر فقد دخل وقت الغداة
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him: “The two rak'ahs before the morning prayer (Fajr), when is their time?” Imam (a.s) said: "Before the rising of the dawn; and when the dawn rises, then the time for the morning prayer has entered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn from Al-Nadr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Al-Jarud from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Him (a.s) say: "(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to perform the witr prayer with nine surahs."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَارُودِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُوتِرُ بِتِسْعِ سُوَرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn from Al-Nadr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Al-Jarud from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Him (a.s) say: "(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to perform the witr prayer with nine surahs."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Is it not enough for one of you to stand before dawn, perform the witr prayer, and pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr, and have it written for him as the prayer of the night?"
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« أَ مَا يَرْضَى أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَقُومَ قَبْلَ اَلصُّبْحِ فَيُوتِرَ وَ يُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ يُكْتَبَ لَهُ بِصَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "Is it not enough for one of you to stand before dawn, perform the witr prayer, and pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr, and have it written for him as the prayer of the night?"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Bilal who said:
I wrote to Him (a.s) regarding the time of the night prayer. He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote back: "At the decline of the night, which is its middle, is best; but if that is missed, then its beginning and its end are both permissible."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِي وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« عِنْدَ زَوَالِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ هُوَ نِصْفُهُ أَفْضَلُ فَإِنْ فَاتَ فَأَوَّلَهُ وَ آخِرَهُ جَائِزٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Bilal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him (a.s) regarding the time of the night prayer. He (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote back: "At the decline of the night, which is its middle, is best; but if that is missed, then its beginning and its end are both permissible."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Muhammad ibn Isa who said:
I wrote to Him asking: “O my master, it has been narrated from your grandfather that he said, "There is no harm if a man prays the night prayer at the beginning of the night." So He wrote: "At whatever time he prays, it is permissible, Allah (swt) willing."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ يَا سَيِّدِي رُوِيَ عَنْ جَدِّكَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُصَلِّيَ اَلرَّجُلُ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ» فَكَتَبَ« فِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ صَلَّى فَهُوَ جَائِزٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Muhammad ibn Isa who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him asking: “O my master, it has been narrated from your grandfather that he said, "There is no harm if a man prays the night prayer at the beginning of the night." So He wrote: "At whatever time he prays, it is permissible, Allah (swt) willing."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ja'far ibn Uthman from Sama'ah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no harm in performing the night prayer from the beginning of the night until its end, except that the best of that is when the night has reached its midpoint."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لاَ بَأْسَ بِصَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ إِلاَّ أَنَّ أَفْضَلَ ذَلِكَ إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ اَللَّيْلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ja'far ibn Uthman from Sama'ah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no harm in performing the night prayer from the beginning of the night until its end, except that the best of that is when the night has reached its midpoint."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 362

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Al-Ala' from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A man who is accustomed to standing for the night prayer, a night, two nights, or three pass and he does not stand; is it more beloved to you that he performs the witr prayer early at the beginning of the night, or that he makes it up?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather he should make it up, even if it is for thirty nights."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ اَلْقِيَامُ بِاللَّيْلِ تَمْضِي عَلَيْهِ اَللَّيْلَةُ وَ اَللَّيْلَتَانِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثُ لاَ يَقُومُ فَيَقْضِي أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ أَمْ يُعَجِّلُ اَلْوَتْرَ أَوَّلَ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ يَقْضِي وَ إِنْ كَانَ ثَلاَثِينَ لَيْلَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Al-Ala' from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A man who is accustomed to standing for the night prayer, a night, two nights, or three pass and he does not stand; is it more beloved to you that he performs the witr prayer early at the beginning of the night, or that he makes it up?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, rather he should make it up, even if it is for thirty nights."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd Al-Hamid from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and I think it was Ishaq ibn Ghalib, who said:
He (ibn Ghalib) said: “When a man stands up during the night and thinks that dawn has arrived, so he performs the witr prayer, then he looks and realizes that it is still night” Imam (a.s) said: "He should add a rak'ah to the witr, then resume the night prayer, and then perform the witr prayer after it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَظُنُّهُ إِسْحَاقَ بْنَ غَالِبٍ قَالَ قَالَ: إِذَا قَامَ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي اَللَّيْلِ فَظَنَّ أَنَّ اَلصُّبْحَ قَدْ أَضَاءَ فَأَوْتَرَ ثُمَّ نَظَرَ فَرَأَى أَنَّ عَلَيْهِ لَيْلاً قَالَ« يُضِيفُ إِلَى اَلْوَتْرِ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ يَسْتَقْبِلُ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ يُوتِرُ بَعْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd Al-Hamid from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and I think it was Ishaq ibn Ghalib, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (ibn Ghalib) said: “When a man stands up during the night and thinks that dawn has arrived, so he performs the witr prayer, then he looks and realizes that it is still night” Imam (a.s) said: "He should add a rak'ah to the witr, then resume the night prayer, and then perform the witr prayer after it."

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him by Bunan ibn Muhammad by Sa'd ibn Al-Sindi by Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Imran by Imam Al-Ridha (a.s):
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s) said: "If you are in Fajr prayer and you went out and saw the dawn, then add a rak'ah to the two rak'ahs you prayed before, and make it the witr prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عِمْرَانَ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَخَرَجْتَ وَ رَأَيْتَ اَلصُّبْحَ فَزِدْ رَكْعَةً إِلَى اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ صَلَّيْتَهُمَا قَبْلُ وَ اِجْعَلْهُ وَتْراً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him by Bunan ibn Muhammad by Sa'd ibn Al-Sindi by Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Imran by Imam Al-Ridha (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s) said: "If you are in Fajr prayer and you went out and saw the dawn, then add a rak'ah to the two rak'ahs you prayed before, and make it the witr prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 363

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you fear being noticed (public attention) when leaning (in prayer), it is sufficient for you to place your hand on the ground without lying down." Then He (a.s) gestured with the tips of his fingers from his right hand and placed them lightly on the ground. And Abu Ja'far (a.s) also narrated that.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنْ خِفْتَ اَلشُّهْرَةَ فِي اَلتُّكَأَةِ فَقَدْ يُجْزِيكَ أَنْ تَضَعَ يَدَكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ لاَ تَضْطَجِعَ وَ أَوْمَأَ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِهِ مِنْ كَفِّهِ اَلْيُمْنَى فَوَضَعَهَا فِي اَلْأَرْضِ قَلِيلاً» وَ حَكَى أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ذَلِكَ
thaqalaynSanad: From him from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you fear being noticed (public attention) when leaning (in prayer), it is sufficient for you to place your hand on the ground without lying down." Then He (a.s) gestured with the tips of his fingers from his right hand and placed them lightly on the ground. And Abu Ja'far (a.s) also narrated that.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 363

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad from Musa ibn Al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who forgot to lie down on his right side after the two rak'ahs of Fajr and remembered when the iqamah (call to prayer) had already begun, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should proceed with the iqamah and perform the prayer, and leave that (lying on the right side); there is no harm."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ وَ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ نَسِيَ أَنْ يَضْطَجِعَ عَلَى يَمِينِهِ بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَذَكَرَ حِينَ أَخَذَ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يُقِيمُ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يَدَعُ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad from Musa ibn Al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who forgot to lie down on his right side after the two rak'ahs of Fajr and remembered when the iqamah (call to prayer) had already begun, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should proceed with the iqamah and perform the prayer, and leave that (lying on the right side); there is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 364

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only required of one of you, when midnight has passed, to rise and perform his prayer all at once, thirteen rak‘ahs in total. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and supplicate, or if he wishes, he may sleep, or if he wishes, he may go wherever he wants.”
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن عبد الله بن بكير عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إنما على أحدكم إذا انتصف الليل أن يقوم فيصلي صلاته جملة واحدة ثلاث عشرة ركعة ثم إن شاء جلس فدعا وإن شاء نام وإن شاء ذهب حيث شاء
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “It is only required of one of you, when midnight has passed, to rise and perform his prayer all at once, thirteen rak‘ahs in total. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and supplicate, or if he wishes, he may sleep, or if he wishes, he may go wherever he wants.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 364

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about the times for Witr. Imam (a.s) said: "The most beloved of them to me is the first dawn." And I asked Him (a.s) about the best hours of the night. Imam (a.s) said: "The last third." And I asked Him (a.s) about performing Witr after the dawn of morning has broken. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, my father would sometimes perform Witr after the dawn had broken."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ سَاعَاتِ اَلْوَتْرِ قَالَ «أَحَبُّهَا إِلَيَّ اَلْفَجْرُ اَلْأَوَّلُ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَفْضَلِ سَاعَاتِ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ« اَلثُّلُثُ اَلْبَاقِي» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْوَتْرِ بَعْدَ فَجْرِ اَلصُّبْحِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ قَدْ كَانَ أَبِي رُبَّمَا أَوْتَرَ بَعْدَمَا اِنْفَجَرَ اَلصُّبْحُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about the times for Witr. Imam (a.s) said: "The most beloved of them to me is the first dawn." And I asked Him (a.s) about the best hours of the night. Imam (a.s) said: "The last third." And I asked Him (a.s) about performing Witr after the dawn of morning has broken. Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, my father would sometimes perform Witr after the dawn had broken."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 364

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Zur‘ah, from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I rise while I am uncertain about the time of dawn.” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray based on your uncertainty. Then, when dawn appears, perform the Witr, and pray the two rak‘ahs. And if you rise and the dawn has already appeared, then begin with the obligatory prayer and do not perform anything else. Then, once you have finished, make up what you missed. And do not make this a habit. And beware of letting your family become aware of this, so that they pray in this manner and abandon the night prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ اَلْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُومُ وَ أَنَا أَشُكُّ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ عَلَى شَكِّكَ فَإِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَأَوْتِرْ وَ صَلِّ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ إِذَا أَنْتَ قُمْتَ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَابْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ لاَ تُصَلِّ غَيْرَهَا فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَاقْضِ مَا فَاتَكَ وَ لاَ تَكُونُ هَذِهِ عَادَةً وَ إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُطْلِعَ عَلَى هَذَا أَهْلَكَ فَيُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَ لاَ يُصَلُّونَ بِاللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Zur‘ah, from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I rise while I am uncertain about the time of dawn.” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray based on your uncertainty. Then, when dawn appears, perform the Witr, and pray the two rak‘ahs. And if you rise and the dawn has already appeared, then begin with the obligatory prayer and do not perform anything else. Then, once you have finished, make up what you missed. And do not make this a habit. And beware of letting your family become aware of this, so that they pray in this manner and abandon the night prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 364

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Barqi, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: "It may happen that I rise and the dawn has already appeared, so I perform the night prayer, and the Witr, and the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, then I perform the Fajr prayer." He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘May I do the same?’" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but do not make it a habit."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« رُبَّمَا قُمْتُ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَأُصَلِّي صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلْوَتْرَ وَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ أُصَلِّي اَلْفَجْرَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَفْعَلُ أَنَاذَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ لاَ يَكُونُ مِنْكَ عَادَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Barqi, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: "It may happen that I rise and the dawn has already appeared, so I perform the night prayer, and the Witr, and the two rak‘ahs before Fajr, then I perform the Fajr prayer." He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘May I do the same?’" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, but do not make it a habit."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 365

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is in his house, praying, while he believes it is still night. Then another person enters upon him from the door and says, "The morning has come." Should he repeat the Witr or not, or should he repeat any part of his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat it if he prayed it after morning had arrived."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي بَيْتِهِ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ يَرَى أَنَّ عَلَيْهِ لَيْلاً ثُمَّ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْآخَرُ مِنَ اَلْبَابِ فَقَالَ قَدْ أَصْبَحْتَ هَلْ يُعِيدُ اَلْوَتْرَ أَمْ لاَ أَوْ يُعِيدُ شَيْئاً مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ إِنْ صَلاَّهَا مُصْبِحاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man who is in his house, praying, while he believes it is still night. Then another person enters upon him from the door and says, "The morning has come." Should he repeat the Witr or not, or should he repeat any part of his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat it if he prayed it after morning had arrived."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 365

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr from (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “When the time for an obligatory prayer enters, do not perform supererogatory prayers.”
arabicText: ما رواه أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن سيف بن عميرة عن أبي بكر عن جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام قال إذا دخل وقت صلاة مفروضة فلا تطوع
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr from (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When the time for an obligatory prayer enters, do not perform supererogatory prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 365

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abdul-Aziz, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I rise while I fear that dawn may have arrived.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then perform the Witr." I asked: “Then I look and find that it is still night upon me.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then perform the night prayer."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْعَزِيزِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُومُ وَ أَنَا أَتَخَوَّفُ اَلْفَجْرَ قَالَ« فَأَوْتِرْ» قُلْتُ فَأَنْظُرُ وَ إِذَا عَلَيَّ لَيْلٌ قَالَ« فَصَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abdul-Aziz, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I rise while I fear that dawn may have arrived.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then perform the Witr." I asked: “Then I look and find that it is still night upon me.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then perform the night prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 365

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "If you rise and the dawn has already appeared, then begin with the Witr, then pray the two rak‘ahs, then pray the rak‘ahs when the morning has come."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِنْتِ إِلْيَاسَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَابْدَأْ بِالْوَتْرِ ثُمَّ صَلِّ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ صَلِّ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ إِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: "If you rise and the dawn has already appeared, then begin with the Witr, then pray the two rak‘ahs, then pray the rak‘ahs when the morning has come."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 365

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Allan, who said: Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar narrated to me, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Just before Fajr, with it, and after it." I asked: “When do I leave them in order to make them up later?” Imam (a.s) said: "When the mu’adhdhin says: ‘Qad qamatis salah’ (The prayer has been established)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلاَّنٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ قَالَ« قُبَيْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ مَعَهُ وَ بَعْدَهُ» قُلْتُ فَمَتَى أَدَعُهَا حَتَّى أَقْضِيَهَا قَالَ قَالَ« إِذَا قَالَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ قَدْ قَامَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Allan, who said: Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar narrated to me, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the two rak‘ahs before Fajr. Imam (a.s) said: "Just before Fajr, with it, and after it." I asked: “When do I leave them in order to make them up later?” Imam (a.s) said: "When the mu’adhdhin says: ‘Qad qamatis salah’ (The prayer has been established)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 366

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him. about a man who does not pray the morning prayer until it becomes bright and the redness appears, and he has not yet performed the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Should he perform them or delay them? Imam (a.s) said: "He should delay them."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ حَتَّى تُسْفِرَ وَ تَظْهَرَ اَلْحُمْرَةُ وَ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلْفَجْرِ أَيَرْكَعُهُمَا أَوْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمَا قَالَ «يُؤَخِّرُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him. about a man who does not pray the morning prayer until it becomes bright and the redness appears, and he has not yet performed the two rak‘ahs of Fajr. Should he perform them or delay them? Imam (a.s) said: "He should delay them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 366

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Abu Abdullah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, would perform two rak‘ahs after the ‘Isha prayer, in which He (a.s) would recite one hundred verses, and He (a.s) would not count them as part of anything. And He (a.s) would perform two rak‘ahs while sitting, in which He (a.s) would recite (Surah Al Ikhlas) and (Surah Al Kafirun). Then if He (a.s) woke up during the night, He (a.s) would perform the night prayer and the Witr. And if He (a.s) did not wake up until the dawn had risen, He (a.s) would perform two rak‘ahs, and they would count as the Shaf‘, and He (a.s) would count the two rak‘ahs He (a.s) had prayed after ‘Isha as the Witr.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِمِائَةِ آيَةٍ وَ لاَ يَحْتَسِبُ بِهِمَا وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ صَلَّى صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ أَوْتَرَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظْ حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ اَلْفَجْرُ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَصَارَتْ شَفْعاً وَ اِحْتَسَبَ بِالرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَللَّتَيْنِ صَلاَّهُمَا بَعْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَتْراً
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Abu Abdullah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, would perform two rak‘ahs after the ‘Isha prayer, in which He (a.s) would recite one hundred verses, and He (a.s) would not count them as part of anything. And He (a.s) would perform two rak‘ahs while sitting, in which He (a.s) would recite (Surah Al Ikhlas) and (Surah Al Kafirun). Then if He (a.s) woke up during the night, He (a.s) would perform the night prayer and the Witr. And if He (a.s) did not wake up until the dawn had risen, He (a.s) would perform two rak‘ahs, and they would count as the Shaf‘, and He (a.s) would count the two rak‘ahs He (a.s) had prayed after ‘Isha as the Witr.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 366

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Is it not sufficient for one of you to rise shortly before dawn, perform the Witr, and pray the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, and it will be recorded for him as the night prayer?”
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن الحسين عن ابن محبوب عن معاوية ابن وهب قال: سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول: أما يرضى أحدكم أن يقوم قبيل الصبح ويوتر ويصلي ركعتي الفجر وتكتب له صلاة الليل
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Is it not sufficient for one of you to rise shortly before dawn, perform the Witr, and pray the two rak‘ahs of Fajr, and it will be recorded for him as the night prayer?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 366

chapter: Chapter on the Manner of Prayer, Its Description and What is Obligatory and Recommended
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Whoever believes in Allah (swt) and the Last Day (Qiyama) should not pass the night without performing Witr."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:«« مَنْ كٰانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللّٰهِ وَ اَلْيَوْمِ اَلْآخِرِ» فَلاَ يَبِيتَنَّ إِلاَّ بِوَتْرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: "Whoever believes in Allah (swt) and the Last Day (Qiyama) should not pass the night without performing Witr."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 366

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, a servant’s prayer may be raised up for him as half of it, or a third of it, or a fourth of it, or a fifth of it. Only that part of it is raised up in which his heart is truly present. And they were commanded to perform supererogatory prayers so that with them, what was lacking from the obligatory prayers could be completed."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ اَلْعَبْدَ لَيُرْفَعُ لَهُ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ نِصْفُهَا وَ ثُلُثُهَا وَ رُبُعُهَا وَ خُمُسُهَا فَمَا يُرْفَعُ إِلاَّ مَا أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْهَا بِقَلْبِهِ وَ إِنَّمَا أُمِرُوا بِالنَّوَافِلِ لِيُتَمَّمَ لَهُمْ بِهَا مَا نَقَصُوا مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, a servant’s prayer may be raised up for him as half of it, or a third of it, or a fourth of it, or a fifth of it. Only that part of it is raised up in which his heart is truly present. And they were commanded to perform supererogatory prayers so that with them, what was lacking from the obligatory prayers could be completed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 367

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Faddalah from someone who narrated it from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him said: "A man’s prayer may be raised up for him as a fourth of it, or an eighth of it, or a half of it, or more, according to how much he was heedless. But Allah (swt), the Exalted, completes that through the supererogatory prayers."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يُرْفَعُ لِلرَّجُلِ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ رُبُعُهَا أَوْ ثُمُنُهَا أَوْ نِصْفُهَا أَوْ أَكْثَرُ بِقَدْرِ مَا سَهَا وَ لَكِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يُتِمُّ ذَلِكَ بِالنَّوَافِلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Faddalah from someone who narrated it from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him said: "A man’s prayer may be raised up for him as a fourth of it, or an eighth of it, or a half of it, or more, according to how much he was heedless. But Allah (swt), the Exalted, completes that through the supererogatory prayers."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, by Hammad ibn ‘Isa, said: One of our companions narrated to me from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali:
I (Abu Hamza) saw (Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, praying, and His (a.s) cloak fell from His (a.s) shoulders. Imam (a.s) did not adjust it until He (a.s) had completed His (a.s) prayer. I asked Imam (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: "Woe to you! Do you know before whom I was standing? Indeed, a servant’s prayer is not accepted from him except that part of it in which he was fully attentive." I (Abu Hamza) asked: “May I be your ransom! Then we are doomed.” Imam (a.s) said: "No, indeed Allah (swt), the Exalted, completes that with the supererogatory prayers."

thaqalaynSanad: From him, by Hammad ibn ‘Isa, said: One of our companions narrated to me from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Abu Hamza) saw (Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, praying, and His (a.s) cloak fell from His (a.s) shoulders. Imam (a.s) did not adjust it until He (a.s) had completed His (a.s) prayer. I asked Imam (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: "Woe to you! Do you know before whom I was standing? chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:
A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was listening: "May I be your ransom! I am very forgetful in prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "And is there anyone who is safe from it?" I said: "I do not think anyone is more forgetful than I am." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O Aba Muhammad, a servant’s prayer may be raised for him as a third, or a half, or three-quarters, or less, or more, according to the extent of his forgetfulness in it. But it is completed for him through the supererogatory prayers." Then Abu Basir said to Imam (a.s): "I see that the supererogatory prayers should never be abandoned under any circumstance." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Yes, indeed."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي كَثِيرُ اَلسَّهْوِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« وَ هَلْ يَسْلَمُ مِنْهُ أَحَدٌ» فَقُلْتُ مَا أَظُنُّ أَحَداً أَكْثَرَ سَهْواً مِنِّي فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ إِنَّ اَلْعَبْدَ يُرْفَعُ لَهُ ثُلُثُ صَلاَتِهِ وَ نِصْفُهَا وَ ثَلاَثَةُ أَرْبَاعِهَا وَ أَقَلُّ وَ أَكْثَرُ عَلَى قَدْرِ سَهْوِهِ فِيهِ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يُتَمُّ لَهُ مِنَ اَلنَّوَافِلِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ مَا أَرَى اَلنَّوَافِلَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُتْرَكَ عَلَى حَالٍ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَجَلْ لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was listening: "May I be your ransom! I am very forgetful in prayer." Imam (a.s) said: "And is there anyone who is safe from it?" I said: "I do not think anyone is more forgetful than I am." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "O Aba Muhammad, a servant’s prayer may be raised for him as a third, or a half, or three-quarters, or less, or more, according to the extent of his forgetfulness in it. But it is completed for him through the supererogatory prayers." Then Abu Basir said to Imam (a.s): "I see that the supererogatory prayers should never be abandoned under any circumstance." Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Yes, indeed."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both:
(Imam (a.s)) said: "You are granted from your prayer only that portion of it to which you give your attention. So if you are heedless of it entirely, or neglect its performance, it is wrapped up and struck against the face of its performer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ:« إِنَّمَا لَكَ مِنْ صَلاَتِكَ مَا أَقْبَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْهَا فَإِنْ أَوْهَمَهَا كُلَّهَا أَوْ غَفَلَ عَنْ أَدَائِهَا لُفَّتْ فَضُرِبَ بِهَا وَجْهُ صَاحِبِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: "You are granted from your prayer only that portion of it to which you give your attention. So if you are heedless of it entirely, or neglect its performance, it is wrapped up and struck against the face of its performer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:
In the book of Hariz, he said: “I forgot that I was in an obligatory prayer until I had already bowed, and I had intended it as a supererogatory prayer.” He said: "It is according to what you stood for, if you stood with the intention of an obligatory prayer and then doubt entered upon you, then you are in the obligatory prayer. But if you began with the intention of a supererogatory prayer and then intended it to be obligatory, then you are in the supererogatory prayer. And if you began in an obligatory prayer and then remembered a supererogatory prayer that was due upon you, then proceed with the obligatory prayer."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ فِي كِتَابِ حَرِيزٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: إِنِّي نَسِيتُ أَنِّي فِي صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ حَتَّى رَكَعْتُ وَ أَنَا أَنْوِيهَا تَطَوُّعاً قَالَ فَقَالَ« هِيَ اَلَّتِي قُمْتَ فِيهَا إِنْ كُنْتَ قُمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ تَنْوِي فَرِيضَةً ثُمَّ دَخَلَكَ اَلشَّكُّ فَأَنْتَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ دَخَلْتَ فِي نَافِلَةٍ فَتَنْوِيهَا فَرِيضَةً فَأَنْتَ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ دَخَلْتَ فِي فَرِيضَةٍ ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتَ نَافِلَةً كَانَتْ عَلَيْكَ فَامْضِ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: In the book of Hariz, he said: “I forgot that I was in an obligatory prayer until I had already bowed, and I had intended it as a supererogatory prayer.” He said: "It is according to what you stood for, if you stood with the intention of an obligatory prayer and then doubt entered upon you, then you are in the obligatory prayer. But if you began with the intention of a supererogatory prayer and then intended it to be obligatory, then you are in the supererogatory prayer. And if you began in an obligatory prayer and then remembered a supererogatory prayer that was due upon you, then proceed with the obligatory prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who stood for an obligatory prayer but due to forgetfulness thought it was a supererogatory one, or was in a supererogatory prayer and thought it was an obligatory one. Imam (a.s) said: "It is according to what he began the prayer upon."
arabicText: محمد بن مسعود العياشي عن جعفر بن أحمد عن علي بن الحسن عن محمد بن عيسى عن يونس عن معاوية قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن رجل قام في الصلاة المكتوبة فسها فظن انها نافلة أو كان في النافلة فظن انها مكتوبة قال هي ما أفتتح الصلاة عليه
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who stood for an obligatory prayer but due to forgetfulness thought it was a supererogatory one, or was in a supererogatory prayer and thought it was an obligatory one. Imam (a.s) said: "It is according to what he began the prayer upon."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Hamdawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdul-Aziz, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who stood for an obligatory prayer and prayed one rak‘ah while intending it to be a supererogatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "It is according to what you stood for and intended." And Imam (a.s) said: "If you stood while intending an obligatory prayer, and then doubt entered upon you afterward, then you are in the obligatory prayer according to what you stood for. But if you began it while intending it as a supererogatory prayer, and then afterward you intend it as obligatory, then you are in the supererogatory prayer. Indeed, what is counted for the servant from his prayer is what he began with at the start of his prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمْدَوَيْهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْعَزِيزِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَامَ فِي صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَ هُوَ يَنْوِي أَنَّهَا نَافِلَةٌ قَالَ «هِيَ اَلَّتِي قُمْتَ فِيهَا وَ لَهَا» وَ قَالَ« إِذَا قُمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ تَنْوِي اَلْفَرِيضَةَ فَدَخَلَكَ اَلشَّكُّ بَعْدُ فَأَنْتَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ عَلَى اَلَّذِي قُمْتَ لَهُ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ دَخَلْتَ فِيهَا وَأَنْتَ تَنْوِي نَافِلَةً ثُمَّ إِنَّكَ تَنْوِيهَا بَعْدُ فَرِيضَةً فَأَنْتَ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ وَإِنَّمَا يُحْسَبُ لِلْعَبْدِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلَّتِي اِبْتَدَأَ فِي أَوَّلِ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Hamdawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdul-Aziz, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who stood for an obligatory prayer and prayed one rak‘ah while intending it to be a supererogatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "It is according to what you stood for and intended." And Imam (a.s) said: "If you stood while intending an obligatory prayer, and then doubt entered upon you afterward, then you are in the obligatory prayer according to what you stood for. But if you began it while intending it as a supererogatory prayer, and then afterward you intend it as obligatory, then you are in the supererogatory prayer. Indeed, what is counted for the servant from his prayer is what he began with at the start of his prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who intends to pray eight rak‘ahs but ends up praying ten rak‘ahs, are the two extra rak‘ahs counted as part of another prayer upon him? Imam (a.s) said: "No, unless he deliberately intends that. But if he did not intend it, then no."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَيُصَلِّي عَشْرَ رَكَعَاتٍ أَيَحْتَسِبُ بِالرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةٍ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَهَا عَمْداً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْوِ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who intends to pray eight rak‘ahs but ends up praying ten rak‘ahs, are the two extra rak‘ahs counted as part of another prayer upon him? Imam (a.s) said: "No, unless he deliberately intends that. But if he did not intend it, then no."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah and Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about forgetfulness in the supererogatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon you."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسَّهْوِ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah and Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about forgetfulness in the supererogatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "There is nothing upon you."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Faddalah, from Ibn Sinan, from more than one person:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If forgetfulness becomes frequent for you, then proceed with your prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَثُرَ عَلَيْكَ اَلسَّهْوُ فَامْضِ فِي صَلاَتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Faddalah, from Ibn Sinan, from more than one person:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If forgetfulness becomes frequent for you, then proceed with your prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Faddalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If forgetfulness becomes frequent for you, then proceed with your prayer, for it is likely to leave you. Indeed, it is from Shaytan."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَثُرَ عَلَيْكَ اَلسَّهْوُ فَامْضِ عَلَى صَلاَتِكَ فَإِنَّهُ يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَدَعَكَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ مِنَ اَلشَّيْطَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Faddalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If forgetfulness becomes frequent for you, then proceed with your prayer, for it is likely to leave you. Indeed, it is from Shaytan."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Bukayr from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about forgetfulness (in prayer), for it occurs frequently with me. Imam (a.s) said: "Merge your prayer with merging (idraj)." I asked: “What is merging?” Imam (a.s) said: "Three tasbihat (glorifications) in the bowing and prostration."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلسَّهْوِ فَإِنَّهُ يَكْثُرُ عَلَيَّ فَقَالَ« أَدْرِجْ صَلاَتَكَ إِدْرَاجاً» قُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ اَلْإِدْرَاجُ قَالَ« ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Bukayr from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about forgetfulness (in prayer), for it occurs frequently with me. Imam (a.s) said: "Merge your prayer with merging (idraj)." I asked: “What is merging?” Imam (a.s) said: "Three tasbihat (glorifications) in the bowing and prostration."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Everything you doubt from what has already passed, proceed with it as it is."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كُلُّ مَا شَكَكْتَ فِيهِ مِمَّا قَدْ مَضَى فَامْضِهِ كَمَا هُوَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Everything you doubt from what has already passed, proceed with it as it is."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 370

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Ali:
Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "You build upon certainty, act upon what is firm, and apply precaution to the entire prayer."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ وَ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلسَّهْوِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« تَبْنِي عَلَى اَلْيَقِينِ وَ تَأْخُذُ بِالْجَزْمِ وَ تَحْتَاطُ بِالصَّلاَةِ كُلِّهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Ali:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "You build upon certainty, act upon what is firm, and apply precaution to the entire prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no forgetfulness upon the Imam (of prayer), nor upon the one who is behind the Imam (of prayer). There is no forgetfulness upon forgetfulness, and there is no repetition upon repetition."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ سَهْوٌ وَ لاَ عَلَى مَنْ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ سَهْوٌ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلسَّهْوِ سَهْوٌ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْإِعَادَةِ إِعَادَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no forgetfulness upon the Imam (of prayer), nor upon the one who is behind the Imam (of prayer). There is no forgetfulness upon forgetfulness, and there is no repetition upon repetition."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you stand up after the two rak‘ahs of Dhuhr or any other prayer and did not recite the tashahhud in them, and you remember that in the third rak‘ah before bowing, then sit and recite the tashahhud, then stand and complete your prayer. But if you do not remember until after you have bowed, then proceed with your prayer until you complete it. Once you have finished, perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness after the taslim and before you speak."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلظُّهْرِ أَوْ غَيْرِهِمَا وَ لَمْ تَتَشَهَّدْ فِيهِمَا فَذَكَرْتَ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَاجْلِسْ فَتَشَهَّدْ وَ قُمْ فَأَتِمَّ صَلاَتَكَ وَ إِنْ أَنْتَ لَمْ تَذْكُرْ حَتَّى تَرْكَعَ فَامْضِ فِي صَلاَتِكَ حَتَّى تَفْرُغَ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ بَعْدَ اَلتَّسْلِيمِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you stand up after the two rak‘ahs of Dhuhr or any other prayer and did not recite the tashahhud in them, and you remember that in the third rak‘ah before bowing, then sit and recite the tashahhud, then stand and complete your prayer. But if you do not remember until after you have bowed, then proceed with your prayer until you complete it. Once you have finished, perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness after the taslim and before you speak."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you stand up after the first two rak‘ahs and did not recite the tashahhud, and you remember before you bow, then sit and recite the tashahhud. But if you do not remember until after you have bowed, then proceed with your prayer as you are. Then, when you have finished, perform two prostrations in which there is no bowing, then recite the tashahhud that you missed."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ وَ لَمْ تَتَشَهَّدْ فَذَكَرْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَاقْعُدْ فَتَشَهَّدْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَذْكُرْ حَتَّى تَرْكَعَ فَامْضِ فِي صَلاَتِكَ كَمَا أَنْتَ فَإِذَا اِنْصَرَفْتَ سَجَدْتَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ لاَ رُكُوعَ فِيهِمَا ثُمَّ تَتَشَهَّدُ اَلتَّشَهُّدَ اَلَّذِي فَاتَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you stand up after the first two rak‘ahs and did not recite the tashahhud, and you remember before you bow, then sit and recite the tashahhud. But if you do not remember until after you have bowed, then proceed with your prayer as you are. Then, when you have finished, perform two prostrations in which there is no bowing, then recite the tashahhud that you missed."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prays the first two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer, then forgets and stands up before sitting between them. Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him sit down as long as he has not yet bowed, and his prayer is complete. But if he does not remember until after he has bowed, then let him continue in his prayer. When he finishes with the salam, he should peck out (quickly perform) two (rak‘ahs) while sitting."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ ثُمَّ يَنْسَى فَيَقُومُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ« فَلْيَجْلِسْ مَا لَمْ يَرْكَعْ وَ قَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ فَلْيَمْضِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ نَقَرَ ثِنْتَيْنِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prays the first two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer, then forgets and stands up before sitting between them. Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him sit down as long as he has not yet bowed, and his prayer is complete. But if he does not remember until after he has bowed, then let him continue in his prayer. When he finishes with the salam, he should peck out (quickly perform) two (rak‘ahs) while sitting."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqah:
I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s), peace be upon him: “Did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, ever end his prayer with the taslīm after only the first two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: “Even in his state, as he was?” Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, only intended to teach them (people around Him (saws)) jurisprudence."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْبَرْقِيُّ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ سَلَّمَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ وَ حَالُهُ حَالُهُ قَالَ« إِنَّمَا أَرَادَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ أَنْ يُفَقِّهَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqah:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s), peace be upon him: “Did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, ever end his prayer with the taslīm after only the first two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." I asked: “Even in his state, as he was?” Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, only intended to teach them (people around Him (saws)) jurisprudence."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Sa‘id al-A‘raj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once prayed and then performed the salam after two rak‘ahs. Those behind Him (saws) said: 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something occurred in the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' They said: 'You only prayed two rak‘ahs.' He (saws) said: 'Is that so, O Dhu al-Yadayn?', as he used to be called Dhu al-Shimalayn. He (Dhu al-Shimalayn) replied: 'Yes.' So the Prophet (saws) continued from where He (saws) had left off, completed the prayer as four rak‘ahs, and said: 'Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, is the One (azj) who made me forget, as a mercy to the ummah. Do you not see that if a man were to do this, he would be reproached, and it would be said to him: ‘Your prayer is not accepted?' But whoever experiences this now, let him know that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, has already established the precedent and it has become a model to follow.' And He (saws) performed two prostrations (sajdatayn) because of the speech that took place."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلْأَعْرَجِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَسَأَلَهُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَحَدَثَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ شَيْءٌ قَالَ« وَ مَا ذَاكَ» قَالُوا إِنَّمَا صَلَّيْتَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« أَ كَذَاكَ يَا ذَا اَلْيَدَيْنِ» وَ كَانَ يُدْعَى ذَا اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَبَنَى عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ فَأَتَمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ أَرْبَعاً وَ قَالَ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ هُوَ اَلَّذِي أَنْسَاهُ رَحْمَةً لِلْأُمَّةِ أَ لاَ تَرَى لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً صَنَعَ هَذَا لَعُيِّرَ»» وَ قِيلَ مَا تُقْبَلُ صَلاَتُكَ فَمَنْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْيَوْمَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ« قَدْ سَنَّ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ صَارَتْ أُسْوَةً وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ لِمَكَانِ اَلْكَلاَمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Sa‘id al-A‘raj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once prayed and then performed the salam after two rak‘ahs. Those behind Him (saws) said: 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something occurred in the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' They said: 'You only prayed two rak‘ahs.' He (saws) said: 'Is that so, O Dhu al-Yadayn?', as he used to be called Dhu al-Shimalayn. He (Dhu al-Shimalayn) replied: 'Yes.' So the Prophet (saws) continued from where He (saws) had left off, completed the prayer as four rak‘ahs, and said: 'Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, is the One (azj) who made me forget, as a mercy to the ummah. Do you not see that if a man were to do this, he would be reproached, and it would be said to him: ‘Your prayer is not accepted?' But whoever experiences this now, let him know that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, has already established the precedent and it has become a model to follow.' And He (saws) performed two prostrations (sajdatayn) because of the speech that took place."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who had prayed two rak‘ahs and then stood up. Imam (a.s) said: "He must start over." I asked: “What about what people narrate, then I mentioned to him the narration of Dhu al-Shimalayn.” Imam (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did not leave His (saws) place, and had He (saws) left it, He (saws) would have had to start over."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قَامَ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ» قُلْتُ فَمَا يَرْوِي اَلنَّاسُ فَذَكَرَ لَهُ حَدِيثَ ذِي اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَمْ يَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ وَ لَوْ بَرِحَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ»

thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who had prayed two rak‘ahs and then stood up. Imam (a.s) said: "He must start over."
