chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Faddalah, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and then got up and went about his need. Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer anew." I asked: “Why is it that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did not restart the prayer when He (saws) had prayed two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, had not left his place."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَذَهَبَ فِي حَاجَتِهِ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلصَّلاَةَ» فَقُلْتُ مَا بَالُ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَمْ يَسْتَقْبِلْ حِينَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ مِنْ مَوْضِعِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Faddalah, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and then got up and went about his need. Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer anew." I asked: “Why is it that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did not restart the prayer when He (saws) had prayed two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, had not left his place."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan by al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad by Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who joined the Imam (of prayer) in prayer while the Imam (of prayer) had already performed one rak‘ah before him. When the Imam completed the prayer, the man left with the people, then afterward remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat it as one rak‘ah."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَهُ بِرَكْعَةٍ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ اَلْإِمَامُ خَرَجَ مَعَ اَلنَّاسِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَةٌ قَالَ« يُعِيدُهَا رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan by al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad by Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who joined the Imam (of prayer) in prayer while the Imam (of prayer) had already performed one rak‘ah before him. When the Imam completed the prayer, the man left with the people, then afterward remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should repeat it as one rak‘ah."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs the morning prayer as one rak‘ah, recites the tashahhud, then finishes, leaves, and goes about, and afterward remembers that he had only prayed one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should add one rak‘ah to it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ رَكْعَةً وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُ وَ يَذْهَبُ وَ يَجِيءُ ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ بَعْدُ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا صَلَّى رَكْعَةً قَالَ« يُضِيفُ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs the morning prayer as one rak‘ah, recites the tashahhud, then finishes, leaves, and goes about, and afterward remembers that he had only prayed one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "He should add one rak‘ah to it."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever remembers his forgetfulness and completes the prayer, then there are no two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw) required upon him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once led the people in Dhuhr prayer, prayed two rak‘ahs, then due to forgetfulness stopped. Dhu al-Shimalayn said to Him (saws): 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something new been revealed in the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' He (Dhu al-Shimalayn) said: 'You only prayed two rak‘ahs.' The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: 'Do you all say what he (Dhu al-Shimalayn) is saying?' They said: 'Yes.' So He (saws) stood up and completed the prayer with them and performed two prostrations of forgetfulness." He (Sama‘ah) said: “I asked, ‘What about someone who prays two rak‘ahs and thinks they were four, so he gives salam and leaves, then afterward remembers that he only prayed two rak‘ahs?’" Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer from the start." I (Sama‘ah) asked: "Then why did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, not restart the prayer, and instead just completed what remained of it?" Imam (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, had not left His (saws) place. So if one has not left his place, then let him complete what is missing from his prayer, so long as he has retained the two initial rak‘ahs."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ حَفِظَ سَهْوَهُ فَأَتَمَّهُ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ صَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ اَلظُّهْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ ذُو اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ يَارَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَ نَزَلَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ« وَ مَا ذَاكَ» قَالَ إِنَّمَا صَلَّيْتَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« أَتَقُولُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِ» قَالُوا نَعَمْ فَقَامَ فَأَتَمَّ بِهِمُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَ رَأَيْتَ مَنْ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ ظَنَّ أَنَّهَا أَرْبَعٌ فَسَلَّمَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ بَعْدَمَا ذَهَبَ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلصَّلاَةَ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَا بَالُ اَلرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لَمْ يَسْتَقْبِلِ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَإِنَّمَا أَتَمَّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَمْ يَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ فَلْيُتِمَّ مَا نَقَصَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ حَفِظَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whoever remembers his forgetfulness and completes the prayer, then there are no two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw) required upon him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once led the people in Dhuhr prayer, prayed two rak‘ahs, then due to forgetfulness stopped. Dhu al-Shimalayn said to Him (saws): 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something new been revealed in the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' He (Dhu al-Shimalayn) said: 'You only prayed two rak‘ahs.' The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: 'Do you all say what he (Dhu al-Shimalayn) is saying?' They said: 'Yes.' So He (saws) stood up and completed the prayer with them and performed two prostrations of forgetfulness." He (Sama‘ah) said: “I asked, ‘What about someone who prays two rak‘ahs and thinks they were four, so he gives salam and leaves, then afterward remembers that he only prayed two rak‘ahs?’" Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer from the start." I (Sama‘ah) asked: "Then why did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, not restart the prayer, and instead just completed what remained of it?" Imam (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, had not left His (saws) place. So if one has not left his place, then let him complete what is missing from his prayer, so long as he has retained the two initial rak‘ahs."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performed one rak‘ah of the morning prayer, then finished and went out to attend to his needs, then remembered that he had only prayed one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him complete what remains."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً مِنَ اَلْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفَ وَ خَرَجَ فِي حَوَائِجِهِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً قَالَ« فَلْيُتِمَّ مَا بَقِيَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performed one rak‘ah of the morning prayer, then finished and went out to attend to his needs, then remembered that he had only prayed one rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "Then let him complete what remains."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ibn Abi Najran from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs in Kufa, then remembered, while he was in Mecca, or in Medina, or in Basra, or in another town among the towns, that he had only prayed two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى بِالْكُوفَةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ وَهُوَ بِمَكَّةَ أَوْ بِالْمَدِينَةِ أَوِ اَلْبَصْرَةِ أَوْ بِبَلْدَةٍ مِنَ اَلْبُلْدَانِ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ibn Abi Najran from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs in Kufa, then remembered, while he was in Mecca, or in Medina, or in Basra, or in another town among the towns, that he had only prayed two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad, who said: Ali ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to me by al-‘Ubaydi from Yunus from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
He was asked about a man who joined the Imam (of prayer) in prayer after the Imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah. When the Imam (of prayer) finished, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. He said: “He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has turned his face away, then he must begin the prayer anew from the start.”
arabicText: ما رواه محمد بن مسعود عن جعفر بن أحمد قال حدثني علي ابن الحسن وعلي بن محمد عن العبيدي عن يونس عن العلا عن محمد بن مسلم عن احدهما عليهما السلام قال سئل عن رجل دخل مع الامام في صلاته وقد سبقه بركعة فلما فرغ الامام خرج مع الناس ثم ذكر أنه قد فاتته ركعة قال يعيد ركعة واحدة يجوز له ذلك إذا لم يحول وجهه عن القبلة فإذا حول وجهه فعليه أن يستقبل الصلاة استقبالا
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad, who said: Ali ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to me by al-‘Ubaydi from Yunus from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)):
thaqalaynMatn: He was asked about a man who joined the Imam (of prayer) in prayer after the Imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah. When the Imam (of prayer) finished, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed a rak‘ah. He said: “He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has turned his face away, then he must begin the prayer anew from the start.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “I led a group in prayer, and I sat for the tashahhud, then stood up and forgot to offer the salam to them.” So they said (to narrator): "You did not offer salam to us." Imam (a.s) said: "Did you not offer salam while you were sitting?" I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then there is no harm upon you. And even if you had forgotten, when they said that to you, and you turned your face to them and said, 'Peace be upon you,' it would have been acceptable."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّيْتُ بِقَوْمٍ صَلاَةً فَقَعَدْتُ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ ثُمَّ قُمْتُ وَ نَسِيتُ أَنْ أُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا مَا سَلَّمْتَ عَلَيْنَا فَقَالَ« أَ لَمْ تُسَلِّمْ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ» قُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ« فَلاَ بَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ وَلَوْ نَسِيتَ حِينَ قَالُوا لَكَ ذَلِكَ اِسْتَقْبَلْتَهُمْ بِوَجْهِكَ فَقُلْتَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “I led a group in prayer, and I sat for the tashahhud, then stood up and forgot to offer the salam to them.” So they said (to narrator): "You did not offer salam to us." Imam (a.s) said: "Did you not offer salam while you were sitting?" I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: "Then there is no harm upon you. And even if you had forgotten, when they said that to you, and you turned your face to them and said, 'Peace be upon you,' it would have been acceptable."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who has doubt after he has finished his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not repeat it, and there is nothing upon him."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَشُكُّ بَعْدَمَا يَنْصَرِفُ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُعِيدُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who has doubt after he has finished his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not repeat it, and there is nothing upon him."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Abu Isma‘il al-Sarraj from Habib al-Khath‘ami, who said:
I complained to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about frequent forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Count your prayers with pebbles," or Imam (a.s) said: "Keep track of them with pebbles."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلسَّرَّاجِ عَنْ حَبِيبٍ اَلْخَثْعَمِيِّ قَالَ: شَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَثْرَةَ اَلسَّهْوِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« أَحْصِ صَلاَتَكَ بِالْحَصَى» أَوْ قَالَ« اِحْفَظْهَا بِالْحَصَى»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Abu Isma‘il al-Sarraj from Habib al-Khath‘ami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I complained to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about frequent forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Count your prayers with pebbles," or Imam (a.s) said: "Keep track of them with pebbles."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is standing behind the Imam (of prayer) and the Imam (of prayer) prolongs the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: “He may give salam behind him and go about his need if he wishes.”
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن ابن أبي عمير عن حماد بن عثمان عن عبيد الله الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في الرجل يكون خلف الامام فيطيل الامام التشهد فقال يسلم من خلفه ويمضي في حاجته ان أحب
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is standing behind the Imam (of prayer) and the Imam (of prayer) prolongs the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: “He may give salam behind him and go about his need if he wishes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is behind the Imam (of prayer), and the Imam (of prayer) prolongs the tashahhud, and the man is taken by the need to urinate, or he fears something may be missed, or he experiences pain, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite the tashahhud himself and leave, and leave the Imam."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيُطَوِّلُ اَلْإِمَامُ اَلتَّشَهُّدَ فَيَأْخُذُ اَلرَّجُلَ اَلْبَوْلُ أَوْ يَتَخَوَّفُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ يَفُوتُ أَوْ يَعْرِضُ لَهُ وَجَعٌ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يَتَشَهَّدُ هُوَ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ وَ يَدَعُ اَلْإِمَامَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is behind the Imam (of prayer), and the Imam (of prayer) prolongs the tashahhud, and the man is taken by the need to urinate, or he fears something may be missed, or he experiences pain, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should recite the tashahhud himself and leave, and leave the Imam."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Abu al-Maghra, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is behind the Imam (of prayer) and, due to forgetfulness, gives salam before the Imam (of prayer) does. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْمَغْرَاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيَسْهُو فَيُسَلِّمُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Abu al-Maghra, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is behind the Imam (of prayer) and, due to forgetfulness, gives salam before the Imam (of prayer) does. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn ‘Umar from Musa ibn Isa from Marwan ibn Muslim from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about something regarding forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Shall I not teach you something that, if you do it, and then afterward remember that you either completed or left something out, there will be nothing upon you?" I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: "If you forget, then build upon the greater number (of rak‘ahs). Then, when you finish and give salam, stand and pray what you thought you had left out. If it turns out that you had completed the prayer, then what you prayed afterward is not counted against you. And if you remember that you had actually missed something, then what you prayed afterward completes what was missing."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلسَّهْوِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« أَ لاَ أُعَلِّمُكَ شَيْئاً إِذَا فَعَلْتَهُ ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتَ أَنَّكَ أَتْمَمْتَ أَوْ نَقَصْتَ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ» قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ« إِذَا سَهَوْتَ فَابْنِ عَلَى اَلْأَكْثَرِ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ وَ سَلَّمْتَ فَقُمْ فَصَلِّ مَا ظَنَنْتَ أَنَّكَ نَقَصْتَ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ أَتْمَمْتَ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْكَ فِي هَذِهِ شَيْءٌ وَ إِنْ ذَكَرْتَ أَنَّكَ كُنْتَ نَقَصْتَ كَانَ مَا صَلَّيْتَ تَمَامَ مَا نَقَصْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn ‘Umar from Musa ibn Isa from Marwan ibn Muslim from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about something regarding forgetfulness in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "Shall I not teach you something that, if you do it, and then afterward remember that you either completed or left something out, there will be nothing upon you?" I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: "If you forget, then build upon the greater number (of rak‘ahs). Then, when you finish and give salam, stand and pray what you thought you had left out. If it turns out that you had completed the prayer, then what you prayed afterward is not counted against you. And if you remember that you had actually missed something, then what you prayed afterward completes what was missing."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Alwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers:
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, led us in the Dhuhr prayer and prayed five rak‘ahs. Then He (saws) finished, and one of the people said to Him (saws), 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something been added to the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' He (the man) said: 'You (saws) prayed five rak‘ahs with us.' So He (saws) turned to face the qiblah, said takbir while seated, then performed two prostrations in which there was no recitation and no bowing, then gave salam. And He (saws) used to say: "They (sajda tu sahw) are the two that humiliate Satan (al-murghimatan).’"
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلَّى بِنَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَلظُّهْرَ خَمْسَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ اِنْفَتَلَ فَقَالَ لَهُ بَعْضُ اَلْقَوْمِ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ هَلْ زِيدَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ« وَ مَا ذَاكَ» قَالَ صَلَّيْتَ بِنَا خَمْسَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ فَاسْتَقْبَلَ اَلْقِبْلَةَ وَ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ ثُمَّ سَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا قِرَاءَةٌ وَ لاَ رُكُوعٌ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ« هُمَا اَلْمُرْغِمَتَانِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Alwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, led us in the Dhuhr prayer and prayed five rak‘ahs. Then He (saws) finished, and one of the people said to Him (saws), 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something been added to the prayer?' He (saws) said: 'What is that?' He (the man) said: 'You (saws) prayed five rak‘ahs with us.' So He (saws) turned to face the qiblah, said takbir while seated, then performed two prostrations in which there was no recitation and no bowing, then gave salam. And He (saws) used to say: "They (sajda tu sahw) are the two that humiliate Satan (al-murghimatan).’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 375

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you forget something from the prayer, whether bowing, prostration, or takbir, and then you remember it, then perform whatever you missed, just the same."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا نَسِيتَ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ رُكُوعاً أَوْ سُجُوداً أَوْ تَكْبِيراً ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتَ فَاصْنَعِ اَلَّذِي فَاتَكَ سَوَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If you forget something from the prayer, whether bowing, prostration, or takbir, and then you remember it, then perform whatever you missed, just the same."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 376

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from al-‘Ayyas, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot a rak‘ah from his prayer until he finished it, then remembered that he had not bowed. Imam (a.s) said: "He should stand, perform the bowing, and then perform two prostrations."
arabicText: عنه عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي نجران عن صفوان عن العيص قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن رجل نسي ركعة من صلاته حتى فرغ منها ثم ذكر انه لم يركع قال يقوم فيركع ويسجد سجدتين
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from al-‘Ayyas, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who forgot a rak‘ah from his prayer until he finished it, then remembered that he had not bowed. Imam (a.s) said: "He should stand, perform the bowing, and then perform two prostrations."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 376

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Hamzah ibn Ya‘la from Ali ibn Idris from Muhammad from his brother Abu Jarir:
Abu al-Hasan (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When a man is in prayer and his father calls him, he should glorify (say tasbih); but if his mother calls him, he should respond by saying, 'Here I am (labbayk).'"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ حَمْزَةَ بْنِ يَعْلَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ أَبِي جَرِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَدَعَاهُ اَلْوَالِدُ فَلْيُسَبِّحْ وَإِذَا دَعَتْهُ اَلْوَالِدَةُ فَلْيَقُلْ لَبَّيْكِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Hamzah ibn Ya‘la from Ali ibn Idris from Muhammad from his brother Abu Jarir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu al-Hasan (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "When a man is in prayer and his father calls him, he should glorify (say tasbih); but if his mother calls him, he should respond by saying, 'Here I am (labbayk).'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 376

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is praying behind an Imam (of prayer) and does not know how many rak‘ahs have been prayed, does he have to perform anything for forgetfulness? Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ لاَ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى هَلْ عَلَيْهِ سَهْوٌ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is praying behind an Imam (of prayer) and does not know how many rak‘ahs have been prayed, does he have to perform anything for forgetfulness? Imam (a.s) said: "No."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 377

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, ever perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness? Imam (a.s) said: "No, and no Faqih (Jurist) performs them."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ سَجَدَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ قَطُّ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لاَ يَسْجُدُهُمَا فَقِيهٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Did the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, ever perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness? Imam (a.s) said: "No, and no Faqih (Jurist) performs them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 377

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjal from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari from Hamzah ibn Humran:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "No Faqih (Jurist) has ever repeated a prayer; rather, he finds a solution and manages it so that he does not have to repeat it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ حَمْزَةَ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ:« مَا أَعَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقِيهٌ قَطُّ يَحْتَالُ لَهَا وَ يُدَبِّرُهَا حَتَّى لاَ يُعِيدَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjal from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari from Hamzah ibn Humran:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "No Faqih (Jurist) has ever repeated a prayer; rather, he finds a solution and manages it so that he does not have to repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 377

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) (said) regarding a man who was called by someone while he was praying, and due to forgetfulness, he answered him for his need, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should continue with his prayer and perform a lot of takbirs (saying 'Allahu Akbar')."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ دَعَاهُ رَجُلٌ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي فَسَهَا فَأَجَابَهُ لِحَاجَتِهِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يَمْضِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ وَ يُكَبِّرُ تَكْبِيراً كَثِيراً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) (said) regarding a man who was called by someone while he was praying, and due to forgetfulness, he answered him for his need, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should continue with his prayer and perform a lot of takbirs (saying 'Allahu Akbar')."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 377

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Sometimes I doubt in the surah, I do not know whether I have recited it or not, so I repeat it.” Imam (a.s) said: "If it is a long surah, then no, do not repeat it. But if it is a short surah, then repeat it."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي رُبَّمَا شَكَكْتُ فِي اَلسُّورَةِ فَلاَ أَدْرِي قَرَأْتُهَا أَمْ لاَ فَأُعِيدُهَا قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَتْ طَوِيلَةً فَلاَ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ قَصِيرَةً فَأَعِدْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Sometimes I doubt in the surah, I do not know whether I have recited it or not, so I repeat it.” Imam (a.s) said: "If it is a long surah, then no, do not repeat it. But if it is a short surah, then repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 378

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I recite a surah and then, due to forgetfulness, realize it when I am at its end, should I return to the beginning of the surah or continue?” Imam (a.s) said: "Rather, continue."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقْرَأُ سُورَةً فَأَسْهُو فَأَنْتَبِهُ وَ أَنَا فِي آخِرِهَا فَأَرْجِعُ إِلَى أَوَّلِ اَلسُّورَةِ أَوْ أَمْضِي قَالَ« بَلِ اِمْضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I recite a surah and then, due to forgetfulness, realize it when I am at its end, should I return to the beginning of the surah or continue?” Imam (a.s) said: "Rather, continue."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 378

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man doubts about the adhan while he has already entered into the iqamah.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “A man doubts about the adhan and the iqamah and he has already said the takbir.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “A man doubts about the takbir and he has already begun the recitation.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “He doubts about the recitation and he has already bowed.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “He doubts about the bowing and he has already prostrated.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues with his prayer." Then Imam (a.s) said: "O Zurarah, when you have left something and moved on to something else, your doubt regarding the former is of no consequence."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ شَكَّ فِي اَلْأَذَانِ وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ فِي اَلْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ« يَمْضِي» قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ شَكَّ فِي اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ وَ قَدْ كَبَّرَ قَالَ« يَمْضِي» قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ شَكَّ فِي اَلتَّكْبِيرِ وَ قَدْ قَرَأَ قَالَ« يَمْضِي» قُلْتُ شَكَّ فِي اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ قَدْ رَكَعَ قَالَ «يَمْضِي» قُلْتُ شَكَّ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ قَالَ« يَمْضِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« يَا زُرَارَةُ إِذَا خَرَجْتَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ثُمَّ دَخَلْتَ فِي غَيْرِهِ فَشَكُّكَ لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man doubts about the adhan while he has already entered into the iqamah.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “A man doubts about the adhan and the iqamah and he has already said the takbir.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “A man doubts about the takbir and he has already begun the recitation.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “He doubts about the recitation and he has already bowed.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues." I asked: “He doubts about the bowing and he has already prostrated.” Imam (a.s) said: "He continues with his prayer." Then Imam (a.s) said: "O Zurarah, when you have left something and moved on to something else, your doubt regarding the former is of no consequence."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 378

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whenever you have doubt about something after you have finished your prayer, proceed and do not repeat it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كُلُّمَا شَكَكْتَ فِيهِ بَعْدَمَا تَفْرُغُ مِنْ صَلاَتِكَ فَامْضِ وَ لاَ تَعُدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Whenever you have doubt about something after you have finished your prayer, proceed and do not repeat it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 378

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham Abu Usamah, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed ‘Asr with six rak‘ahs or five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain that he prayed five or six, then he must repeat it. But if he does not know whether he added or shortened, then he should say the takbir while sitting, then perform two rak‘ahs, reciting in them the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), at the end of his prayer, then perform the tashahhud. And if he is certain that he prayed only two or three rak‘ahs, and then left and spoke without realizing that he had not completed the prayer, then he must complete what remains of the prayer. For indeed, the Prophet of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once prayed two rak‘ahs with the people, then forgot until He (saws) finished. Dhu al-Shimalayn said to Him (saws): 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something happened in the prayer?' So He (saws) said: 'O people, did Dhu al-Shimalayn speak the truth?' They said: 'Yes, you only prayed two rak‘ahs.' So He (saws) stood and completed what remained of His (saws) prayer."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ أَوْ خَمْسَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ« إِنِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى خَمْساً أَوْ سِتّاً فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ زَادَ أَمْ نَقَصَ فَلْيُكَبِّرْ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ ثُمَّ لْيَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي آخِرِ صَلاَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ إِنْ هُوَ اِسْتَيْقَنَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفَ فَتَكَلَّمَ فَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَائِماً عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّ نَبِيَّ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ صَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ نَسِيَ حَتَّى اِنْصَرَفَ فَقَالَ لَهُ ذُو اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَحَدَثَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ« أَيُّهَا اَلنَّاسُ أَ صَدَقَ ذُو اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ» فَقَالُوا نَعَمْ لَمْ تُصَلِّ إِلاَّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَامَ فَأَتَمَّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham Abu Usamah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed ‘Asr with six rak‘ahs or five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is certain that he prayed five or six, then he must repeat it. But if he does not know whether he added or shortened, then he should say the takbir while sitting, then perform two rak‘ahs, reciting in them the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), at the end of his prayer, then perform the tashahhud. And if he is certain that he prayed only two or three rak‘ahs, and then left and spoke without realizing that he had not completed the prayer, then he must complete what remains of the prayer. For indeed, the Prophet of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, once prayed two rak‘ahs with the people, then forgot until He (saws) finished. Dhu al-Shimalayn said to Him (saws): 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something happened in the prayer?' So He (saws) said: 'O people, did Dhu al-Shimalayn speak the truth?' They said: 'Yes, you only prayed two rak‘ahs.' So He (saws) stood and completed what remained of His (saws) prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from a man from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A man misses the Dhuhr, ‘Asr, and Maghrib prayers, and he remembers them at the time of the last Isha prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should begin with the prayer whose time he is currently in, because he does not know if death might come to him and he would have left an obligatory prayer within its time. Then he should make up what he missed, starting with the earliest first."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ يَفُوتُ اَلرَّجُلَ اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلْعَصْرُ وَاَلْمَغْرِبُ وَذَكَرَهَا عِنْدَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ قَالَ« يَبْدَأُ بِالْوَقْتِ اَلَّذِي هُوَ فِيهِ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَأْمَنُ اَلْمَوْتَ فَيَكُونُ قَدْ تَرَكَ صَلاَةً فَرِيضَةً فِي وَقْتٍ قَدْ دَخَلَتْ ثُمَّ يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ اَلْأُولَى فَالْأُولَى»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from a man from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A man misses the Dhuhr, ‘Asr, and Maghrib prayers, and he remembers them at the time of the last Isha prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should begin with the prayer whose time he is currently in, because he does not know if death might come to him and he would have left an obligatory prayer within its time. Then he should make up what he missed, starting with the earliest first."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan from ‘Anbasah, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he performed two rak‘ahs, one rak‘ah, or three. Imam (a.s) said: "He should build his prayer upon one rak‘ah, recite in it the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), and perform two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَنْبَسَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ رَكَعَ أَوْ وَاحِدَةً أَوْ ثَلاَثاً قَالَ« يَبْنِي صَلاَتَهُ عَلَى رَكْعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ يَقْرَأُ فِيهَا بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan from ‘Anbasah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who does not know whether he performed two rak‘ahs, one rak‘ah, or three. Imam (a.s) said: "He should build his prayer upon one rak‘ah, recite in it the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), and perform two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Yunus from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I experience forgetfulness in prayer while I am behind the Imam (of prayer)”. Imam (a.s) said: "When the Imam gives salam, then perform two prostrations of forgetfulness, and do not worry."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مِنْهَالٍ اَلْقَصَّابِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْهُو فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ أَنَا خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا سَلَّمَ فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ لاَ تَهُبَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Yunus from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I experience forgetfulness in prayer while I am behind the Imam (of prayer)”. Imam (a.s) said: "When the Imam gives salam, then perform two prostrations of forgetfulness, and do not worry."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abdul-Karim from al-Husayn ibn Hammad:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man senses moisture on his garment while he is praying, then let him take hold of his private part with the edge of his garment and wipe it against his thigh. If it turns out to be a moisture he recognizes (actual impurity), then let him perform ablution and repeat the prayer. But if it is not a known moisture, then that is from Shaytan."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْكَرِيمِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَحَسَّ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنَّ بِثَوْبِهِ بَلَلاً وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي فَلْيَأْخُذْ ذَكَرَهُ بِطَرَفِ ثَوْبِهِ فَيَمْسَحُهُ بِفَخِذِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَ بَلَلاً يَعْرِفُ فَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ وَ لْيُعِدِ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بَلَلاً فَذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلشَّيْطَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abdul-Karim from al-Husayn ibn Hammad:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "If a man senses moisture on his garment while he is praying, then let him take hold of his private part with the edge of his garment and wipe it against his thigh. If it turns out to be a moisture he recognizes (actual impurity), then let him perform ablution and repeat the prayer. But if it is not a known moisture, then that is from Shaytan."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
By him, by Ahmad ibn al-Hasan by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah by ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about forgetfulness, what cases require two prostrations of forgetfulness. Imam (a.s) said: "If you intended to sit but stood, or intended to stand but sat, or intended to recite but instead glorified, or intended to glorify but instead recited, then you must perform two prostrations of forgetfulness. But in anything that completes the prayer, there is no forgetfulness." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who intended to sit but stood up, and then remembered before initiating anything further or committing any additional act. Imam (a.s) said: "There are no two prostrations of forgetfulness upon him until he speaks something." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who forgets to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform them whenever he remembers." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who prayed three rak‘ahs thinking that they were four, and after giving salam remembered that they were only three. Imam (a.s) said: "He builds upon his prayer whenever he remembers, performs one more rak‘ah, then recites the tashahhud, gives salam, and performs two prostrations of forgetfulness, and his prayer is valid." And Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who forgets the bowing or forgets a prostration, whether he must perform a prostration of forgetfulness. Imam (a.s) said: "No, he has completed the prayer." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who joins the Imam (of prayer) in prayer after the Imam (of prayer) has already prayed one rak‘ah or more, and then the Imam (of prayer) makes a mistake, what should the man do? Imam (a.s) said: "When the Imam (of prayer) gives salam and performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness, the man who joined him does not perform the prostrations. But when the man stands, continues his prayer, completes it, and gives salam, then he must perform two prostrations of forgetfulness." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who makes a mistake in his prayer and does not remember it until he has prayed the Fajr prayer, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness until the sun rises and its glare disappears." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who makes a mistake behind the Imam (of prayer) and does not perform the opening takbir of prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat prayer, for there is no prayer without opening takbir." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom prayer is obligatory in a sitting position, but he forgets and stands to initiates prayer while standing, then remembers. Imam (a.s) said: "He must sit down and initiate the prayer while sitting. Likewise, if the prayer was obligatory upon him while standing, but he forgot and initiated the prayer while sitting, then he must cut off his prayer, stand, and initiate the prayer while standing. The initial opening (takbir) he made while sitting is not counted."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلسَّهْوِ مَا يَجِبُ فِيهِ سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَقْعُدَ فَقُمْتَ أَوْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَقُومَ فَقَعَدْتَ أَوْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ فَسَبَّحْتَ أَوْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُسَبِّحَ فَقَرَأْتَ فَعَلَيْكَ سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ وَلَيْسَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِمَّا يَتِمُّ بِهِ اَلصَّلاَةُ سَهْوٌ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقْعُدَ فَقَامَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقَدِّمَ شَيْئاً أَوْ يُحْدِثَ شَيْئاً قَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ حَتَّى يَتَكَلَّمَ بِشَيْءٍ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا سَهَا فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيَنْسَى أَنْ يَسْجُدَ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ قَالَ «يَسْجُدُهُمَا مَتَى ذَكَرَ» وَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى ثَلاَثَ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ هُوَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهَا أَرْبَعٌ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهَا ثَلاَثٌ قَالَ« يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ مَتَى مَا ذَكَرَ وَ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ وَ قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ» وَ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى اَلرُّكُوعَ أَوْ يَنْسَى سَجْدَةً هَلْ عَلَيْهِ سَجْدَةُ اَلسَّهْوِ قَالَ« لاَ قَدْ أَتَمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَدْخُلُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى اَلْإِمَامُ رَكْعَةً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ فَسَهَا اَلْإِمَامُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ اَلرَّجُلُ قَالَ« إِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَسَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ فَلاَ يَسْجُدُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلَّذِي دَخَلَ مَعَهُ وَإِذَا قَامَ وَبَنَى عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ وَأَتَمَّهَا وَسَلَّمَ سَجَدَ اَلرَّجُلُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ» وَعَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْهُو فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَلاَ يَذْكُرُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ اَلْفَجْرَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« لاَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيِ اَلسَّهْوِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ يَذْهَبَ شُعَاعُهَا» وَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَهَا خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَلَمْ يَفْتَتِحِ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ لاَ صَلاَةَ بِغَيْرِ اِفْتِتَاحٍ» وَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةٌ مِنْ قُعُودٍ فَنَسِيَ حَتَّى قَامَ وَ اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ قَالَ «يَقْعُدُ وَ يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ وَ كَذَلِكَ إِنْ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ اَلصَّلاَةُ مِنْ قِيَامٍ فَنَسِيَ حَتَّى اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْطَعَ صَلاَتَهُ وَ يَقُومَ فَيَفْتَتِحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ لاَ يَعْتَدَّ بِافْتِتَاحِهِ وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: By him, by Ahmad ibn al-Hasan by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah by ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about forgetfulness, what cases require two prostrations of forgetfulness. Imam (a.s) said: "If you intended to sit but stood, or intended to stand but sat, or intended to recite but instead glorified, or intended to glorify but instead recited, then you must perform two prostrations of forgetfulness. But in anything that completes the prayer, there is no forgetfulness." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who intended to sit but stood up, and then remembered before initiating anything further or committing any additional act. Imam (a.s) said: "There are no two prostrations of forgetfulness upon him until he speaks something." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who forgets to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness in the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He should perform them whenever he remembers." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who prayed three rak‘ahs thinking that they were four, and after giving salam remembered that they were only three. Imam (a.s) said: "He builds upon his prayer whenever he remembers, performs one more rak‘ah, then recites the tashahhud, gives salam, and performs two prostrations of forgetfulness, and his prayer is valid." And Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who forgets the bowing or forgets a prostration, whether he must perform a prostration of forgetfulness. Imam (a.s) said: "No, he has completed the prayer." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who joins the Imam (of prayer) in prayer after the Imam (of prayer) has already prayed one rak‘ah or more, and then the Imam (of prayer) makes a mistake, what should the man do? Imam (a.s) said: "When the Imam (of prayer) gives salam and performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness, the man who joined him does not perform the prostrations. But when the man stands, continues his prayer, completes it, and gives salam, then he must perform two prostrations of forgetfulness." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who makes a mistake in his prayer and does not remember it until he has prayed the Fajr prayer, what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness until the sun rises and its glare disappears." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who makes a mistake behind the Imam (of prayer) and does not perform the opening takbir of prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He must repeat prayer, for there is no prayer without opening takbir." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man upon whom prayer is obligatory in a sitting position, but he forgets and stands to initiates prayer while standing, then remembers. Imam (a.s) said: "He must sit down and initiate the prayer while sitting. Likewise, if the prayer was obligatory upon him while standing, but he forgot and initiated the prayer while sitting, then he must cut off his prayer, stand, and initiate the prayer while standing. The initial opening (takbir) he made while sitting is not counted."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 380

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from ‘Abbad ibn Sulayman from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed Dhuhr or ‘Asr and experienced an invalidating event (hadath) while sitting in the fourth rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "If he had already said “Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wa anna Muhammada Rasulullah” (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) and that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt)), then he does not need to repeat the prayer. But if he had not yet recited the tashahhud before the invalidating event occurred, then he must repeat the prayer."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْجَهْمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى اَلظُّهْرَ أَوِ اَلْعَصْرَ فَأَحْدَثَ حِينَ جَلَسَ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ فَلاَ يُعِيدُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَتَشَهَّدْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُحْدِثَ فَلْيُعِدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from ‘Abbad ibn Sulayman from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed Dhuhr or ‘Asr and experienced an invalidating event (hadath) while sitting in the fourth rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "If he had already said “Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wa anna Muhammada Rasulullah” (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) and that Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt)), then he does not need to repeat the prayer. But if he had not yet recited the tashahhud before the invalidating event occurred, then he must repeat the prayer."

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings on Forgetfulness (Ahkam al-Sahw)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid from Ibn Sinan from Abu Sa‘id al-Qammat, who said:
I heard a man asking Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who experiences cramping in his stomach, discomfort, or pressure from urine while he is in an obligatory prayer during the first, second, third, or fourth rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "If something like that happens to him, there is no harm in him leaving for his need, then performing ablution, and returning to his place of prayer where he was praying, and he should continue his prayer from the point where he left for his need, as long as he has not invalidated the prayer by speaking." He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Even if he turned to the right or left, or turned away from the qiblah?’" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, all of that is permissible. It is like the case of a man who forgets and leaves during one rak‘ah, or two, or three of an obligatory prayer. All that is required of him is to continue his prayer based on what he had already prayed." Then Imam (a.s) mentioned the forgetfulness of the Prophet (saws). peace be upon him and his family.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ اَلْقَمَّاطِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَجُلاً يَسْأَلُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَجَدَ غَمْزاً فِي بَطْنِهِ أَوْ أَذًى أَوْ عَصْراً مِنَ اَلْبَوْلِ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى أَوِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ أَوِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ أَوِ اَلرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا أَصَابَ شَيْئاً مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَخْرُجَ لِحَاجَتِهِ تِلْكَ فَيَتَوَضَّأَ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفَ إِلَى مُصَلاَّهُ اَلَّذِي كَانَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ فَيَبْنِيَ عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ مِنَ اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي خَرَجَ مِنْهُ لِحَاجَتِهِ مَا لَمْ يَنْقُضِ اَلصَّلاَةَ بِكَلاَمٍ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ إِنِ اِلْتَفَتَ يَمِيناً أَوْ شِمَالاً أَوْ وَلَّى عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ وَاسِعٌ إِنَّمَا هُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ رَجُلٍ سَهَا فَانْصَرَفَ فِي رَكْعَةٍ أَوْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثٍ مِنَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَبْنِيَ عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ» ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ سَهْوَ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid from Ibn Sinan from Abu Sa‘id al-Qammat, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard a man asking Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who experiences cramping in his stomach, discomfort, or pressure from urine while he is in an obligatory prayer during the first, second, third, or fourth rak‘ah. Imam (a.s) said: "If something like that happens to him, there is no harm in him leaving for his need, then performing ablution, and returning to his place of prayer where he was praying, and he should continue his prayer from the point where he left for his need, as long as he has not invalidated the prayer by speaking." He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Even if he turned to the right or left, or turned away from the qiblah?’" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, all of that is permissible. It is like the case of a man who forgets and leaves during one rak‘ah, or two, or three of an obligatory prayer. All that is required of him is to continue his prayer based on what he had already prayed." Then Imam (a.s) mentioned the forgetfulness of the Prophet (saws). peace be upon him and his family.

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is praying while wearing his dye (khidab). Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray while it is on him, but he should remove it when he wants to pray." I said: "His henna and cloth are clean." Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray while it is on him. Likewise, a woman also should not pray while her dye (khidab) is on her."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ عَلَيْهِ خِضَابُهُ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَكِنْ يَنْزِعُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ» قُلْتُ إِنَّ حِنَّاءَهُ وَ خِرْقَتَهُ نَظِيفَةٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ عَلَيْهِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ أَيْضاً لاَ تُصَلِّي وَ عَلَيْهَا خِضَابُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is praying while wearing his dye (khidab). Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray while it is on him, but he should remove it when he wants to pray." I said: "His henna and cloth are clean." Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray while it is on him. Likewise, a woman also should not pray while her dye (khidab) is on her."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifa‘ah, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a person who is dyed with henna, if he is able to perform sujud and recite properly, can he pray while wearing his henna? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if his cloth is pure and he is in a state of ablution."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمُخْتَضِبِ إِذَا تَمَكَّنَ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ أَيْضاً أَ يُصَلِّي فِي حِنَّائِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَ خِرْقَتُهُ طَاهِرَةً وَ كَانَ مُتَوَضِّئاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifa‘ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a person who is dyed with henna, if he is able to perform sujud and recite properly, can he pray while wearing his henna? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if his cloth is pure and he is in a state of ablution."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa‘ al-Ash‘ari from his father from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s): "May a man pray while wearing his dye (khidab) if he is in a state of purity?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلِ بْنِ اَلْيَسَعِ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ أَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ فِي خِضَابِهِ إِذَا كَانَ عَلَى طُهْرٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa‘ al-Ash‘ari from his father from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s): "May a man pray while wearing his dye (khidab) if he is in a state of purity?" Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 382

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman who prays while her hands are tied with henna. Imam (a.s) said: "If she had performed ablution for the prayer before that, then there is no harm in her praying while she is dyed with henna and her hands are tied."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي وَ يَدَاهَا مَرْبُوطَتَانِ بِالْحِنَّاءِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَتْ تَوَضَّأَتْ لِلصَّلاَةِ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ وَ هِيَ مُخْتَضِبَةٌ وَ يَدَاهَا مَرْبُوطَتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman who prays while her hands are tied with henna. Imam (a.s) said: "If she had performed ablution for the prayer before that, then there is no harm in her praying while she is dyed with henna and her hands are tied."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ja‘far from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man and a woman who apply henna or wasmah (a type of dye), can they pray while having it on? Imam (a.s) said: "If they leave the mouth and the nostrils uncovered, then there is no harm."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةِ يَخْتَضِبَانِ أَ يُصَلِّيَانِ وَ هُمَا بِالْحِنَّاءِ وَ اَلْوَسِمَةِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا أَبْرَزَا اَلْفَمَ وَ اَلْمَنْخِرَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ja‘far from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man and a woman who apply henna or wasmah (a type of dye), can they pray while having it on? Imam (a.s) said: "If they leave the mouth and the nostrils uncovered, then there is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays without taking his hands out from his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "If he takes his hands out, it is good; but if he does not, there is no harm."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ لاَ يُخْرِجُ يَدَيْهِ مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ أَخْرَجَ يَدَيْهِ فَحَسَنٌ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُخْرِجْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays without taking his hands out from his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "If he takes his hands out, it is good; but if he does not, there is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays while inserting his hands into his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is wearing another garment, such as an izar (a waist wrap) or trousers, then there is no harm. But if he is not, then it is not permissible for him to do so. And if he inserts one hand and not the other, there is no harm."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَيُدْخِلُ يَدَيْهِ فِي ثَوْبِهِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ ثَوْبٌ آخَرُ إِزَارٌ أَوْ سَرَاوِيلُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فَلاَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَ إِنْ أَدْخَلَ يَداً وَاحِدَةً وَ لَمْ يُدْخِلِ اَلْأُخْرَى فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays while inserting his hands into his garment. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is wearing another garment, such as an izar (a waist wrap) or trousers, then there is no harm. But if he is not, then it is not permissible for him to do so. And if he inserts one hand and not the other, there is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both:
(Imam (a.s)) said: "A man should not pray with his buttons undone if he is not wearing an izar (waist wrap)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لاَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ مَحْلُولَ اَلْأَزْرَارِ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ إِزَارٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: "A man should not pray with his buttons undone if he is not wearing an izar (waist wrap)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 383

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Ziyad ibn Suwayqah:
Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "There is no harm if one of you prays in a single garment with its buttons undone. Indeed, the religion of Muhammad (saws), peace be upon him and his family, is upright and easy (hanif)."
arabicText: سعد عن أحمد بن محمد عن الحسن بن محبوب عن علي ابن رئاب عن زياد بن سوقة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قال لا بأس أن يصلي أحدكم في الثوب الواحد وازراره محلولة إن دين محمد صلى الله عليه وآله حنيف
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Ziyad ibn Suwayqah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "There is no harm if one of you prays in a single garment with its buttons undone. Indeed, the religion of Muhammad (saws), peace be upon him and his family, is upright and easy (hanif)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 383

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Everything in which prayer is not valid if worn alone, there is no harm in praying while wearing it along with other garments, such as a silk belt, a cap (qalansuwah), leather socks (khuff), and a belt (zunnar) that may be in trousers, and he may pray while wearing it."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «كُلُّمَا لاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ وَحْدَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ مِثْلُ اَلتِّكَّةِ اَلْإِبْرِيسَمِ وَ اَلْقَلَنْسُوَةِ وَ اَلْخُفِّ وَ اَلزُّنَّارِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلسَّرَاوِيلِ وَ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Everything in which prayer is not valid if worn alone, there is no harm in praying while wearing it along with other garments, such as a silk belt, a cap (qalansuwah), leather socks (khuff), and a belt (zunnar) that may be in trousers, and he may pray while wearing it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 383

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi from Hammad ibn Uthman from someone who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who prays in leather socks (khuff) that have been soiled. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is something in which the prayer is not completed (meaning it is not considered a complete garment by itself), then there is no harm."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلصَّيْرَفِيِّ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْخُفِّ اَلَّذِي قَدْ أَصَابَهُ قَذَرٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ مِمَّا لاَ يَتِمُّ فِيهِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi from Hammad ibn Uthman from someone who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who prays in leather socks (khuff) that have been soiled. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is something in which the prayer is not completed (meaning it is not considered a complete garment by itself), then there is no harm."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 384

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibn Abi Layla from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “My cap (qalansuwah) fell into urine, so I picked it up and placed it on my head, and then I prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ قَلَنْسُوَتِي وَقَعَتْ فِي بَوْلٍ فَأَخَذْتُهَا فَوَضَعْتُهَا عَلَى رَأْسِي ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibn Abi Layla from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “My cap (qalansuwah) fell into urine, so I picked it up and placed it on my head, and then I prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
