chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from someone who narrated to them:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no harm in praying in something that, if worn alone, prayer is not valid in it, even if it is soiled, such as a cap (qalansuwah), a belt (tikkah), or socks (jawrab)."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْبِلاَدِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُمْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلشَّيْءِ اَلَّذِي لاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ وَحْدَهُ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْقَذَرُ مِثْلِ اَلْقَلَنْسُوَةِ وَ اَلتِّكَّةِ وَ اَلْجَوْرَبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from someone who narrated to them:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no harm in praying in something that, if worn alone, prayer is not valid in it, even if it is soiled, such as a cap (qalansuwah), a belt (tikkah), or socks (jawrab)."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Zurarah from one of the two (Imam (a.s) Abu Ja‘far or Abu Abdullah, peace be upon them):
(Imam (a.s)) said: "Everything in which prayer is not valid if worn alone, there is no harm if such a thing is worn during prayer, such as a cap (qalansuwah), a belt (tikkah), or socks (jawrab)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «كُلُّمَا كَانَ لاَ تَجُوزُ فِيهِ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَحْدَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ اَلشَّيْءُ مِثْلِ اَلْقَلَنْسُوَةِ وَ اَلتِّكَّةِ وَ اَلْجَوْرَبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Zurarah from one of the two (Imam (a.s) Abu Ja‘far or Abu Abdullah, peace be upon them):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s)) said: "Everything in which prayer is not valid if worn alone, there is no harm if such a thing is worn during prayer, such as a cap (qalansuwah), a belt (tikkah), or socks (jawrab)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 384

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti from Qasim al-Sayqal, who said:
I wrote to (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I work in making scabbards for swords from the skins of dead donkeys, and these skins touch my clothes, can I pray in them?” Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "Designate a specific garment for your prayer." Then I wrote to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I had written to your father (a.s), peace be upon him, about such-and-such, and it was difficult for me, so I began to make them from the skins of wild donkeys that had been slaughtered according to proper Islamic method (dhakiyyah).” Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "All righteous deeds are accompanied by patience, may Allah (swt) have mercy on you. If what you work with is from wild animals properly slaughtered (dhakiyyah), then there is no harm."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْوَاسِطِيِّ عَنْ قَاسِمٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَعْمَلُ أَغْمَادَ اَلسُّيُوفِ مِنْ جُلُودِ اَلْحُمُرِ اَلْمَيْتَةِ فَتُصِيبُ ثِيَابِي أَ فَأُصَلِّي فِيهَا فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ« اِتَّخِذْ ثَوْباً لِصَلاَتِكَ» فَكَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كُنْتُ كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِيكَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا فَصَعَّبَ عَلَيَّ ذَلِكَ فَصِرْتُ أَعْمَلُهَا مِنْ جُلُودِ اَلْحُمُرِ اَلْوَحْشِيَّةِ اَلذَّكِيَّةِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ« كُلُّ أَعْمَالِ اَلْبِرِّ بِالصَّبْرِ يَرْحَمُكَ اَللَّهُ فَإِنْ كَانَ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُ وَحْشِيّاً ذَكِيّاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti from Qasim al-Sayqal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to (Imam) al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I work in making scabbards for swords from the skins of dead donkeys, and these skins touch my clothes, can I pray in them?” Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "Designate a specific garment for your prayer." Then I wrote to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I had written to your father (a.s), peace be upon him, about such-and-such, and it was difficult for me, so I began to make them from the skins of wild donkeys that had been slaughtered according to proper Islamic method (dhakiyyah).” Imam (a.s) wrote back to me: "All righteous deeds are accompanied by patience, may Allah (swt) have mercy on you. If what you work with is from wild animals properly slaughtered (dhakiyyah), then there is no harm."

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad by Ahmad ibn al-Hasan by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah by ‘Ammar:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who vomits on his garment, can he pray in it without washing it? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَقَيَّأُ فِي ثَوْبِهِ أَ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ وَ لاَ يَغْسِلَهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad by Ahmad ibn al-Hasan by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah by ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who vomits on his garment, can he pray in it without washing it? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Khayran the servant, who said:
I wrote to Him (a.s) asking about a garment that is soiled by wine or the flesh of swine, should one pray in it or not? For indeed our companions have differed about it; some of them said: "Pray in it, for Allah (swt) has only forbidden drinking it," and some said: "Do not pray in it." So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote back: "Do not pray in it, for it is impurity (rijs)."
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ خَيْرَ انَ اَلْخَادِمِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلرَّجُلِ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلثَّوْبِ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْخَمْرُ وَ لَحْمُ اَلْخِنْزِيرِ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ أَمْ لاَ فَإِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا قَدِ اِخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ صَلِّ فِيهِ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ شُرْبَهَا وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Khayran the servant, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Him (a.s) asking about a garment that is soiled by wine or the flesh of swine, should one pray in it or not? For indeed our companions have differed about it; some of them said: "Pray in it, for Allah (swt) has only forbidden drinking it," and some said: "Do not pray in it." So Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote back: "Do not pray in it, for it is impurity (rijs)."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan, who said:
I sent a question to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, through Ibrahim ibn Maymun. I said to (ibn Maymun): “Ask Imam (a.s) about a man who urinates and small drop of his urine touches his thigh, and he prays, then after remembers that he did not wash it.” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "He must wash it and repeat his prayer."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ قَالَ: بَعَثْتُ بِمَسْأَلَةٍ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَعَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قُلْتُ سَلْهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَبُولُ فَيُصِيبُ فَخِذَهُ قَدْرُ نُكْتَةٍ مِنْ بَوْلِهِ فَيُصَلِّي وَ يَذْكُرُهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَغْسِلْهَا قَالَ« يَغْسِلُهَا وَ يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I sent a question to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, through Ibrahim ibn Maymun. I said to (ibn Maymun): “Ask Imam (a.s) about a man who urinates and small drop of his urine touches his thigh, and he prays, then after remembers that he did not wash it.” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "He must wash it and repeat his prayer."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Faddalah from Aban from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while there is excrement (‘adhirah) of a human, or a cat, or a dog on his garment, does he have to repeat his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "If he did not know about it, then he does not have to repeat."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ فِي ثَوْبِهِ عَذِرَةٌ مِنْ إِنْسَانٍ أَوْ سِنَّوْرٍ أَوْ كَلْبٍ أَ يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فَلاَ يُعِيدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Faddalah from Aban from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while there is excrement (‘adhirah) of a human, or a cat, or a dog on his garment, does he have to repeat his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "If he did not know about it, then he does not have to repeat."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man whose garment was soiled by janabah (semen) or blood. Imam (a.s) said: "If he knew that janabah or blood had touched his garment before he prayed, and then he prayed in it without washing it, he must repeat whatever prayers he performed. But if he suspected that something had touched him and he inspected it and did not see anything, it suffices for him to sprinkle it with water."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَصَابَ ثَوْبَهُ جَنَابَةٌ أَوْ دَمٌ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ أَصَابَ ثَوْبَهُ جَنَابَةٌ أَوْ دَمٌ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى فِيهِ وَ لَمْ يَغْسِلْهُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ مَا صَلَّى وَ إِنْ كَانَ يَرَى أَنَّهُ أَصَابَهُ شَيْءٌ فَنَظَرَ فَلَمْ يَرَ شَيْئاً أَجْزَأَهُ أَنْ يَنْضَحَهُ بِالْمَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man whose garment was soiled by janabah (semen) or blood. Imam (a.s) said: "If he knew that janabah or blood had touched his garment before he prayed, and then he prayed in it without washing it, he must repeat whatever prayers he performed. But if he suspected that something had touched him and he inspected it and did not see anything, it suffices for him to sprinkle it with water."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prayed two rak‘ahs in a garment that had janabah on it, and then he became aware of it. Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer anew." He (Abu Basir) said: “I also asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays while there is janabah or blood on his garment, and he only realizes it after he finishes his prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is valid and nothing is required of him."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى فِي ثَوْبٍ فِيهِ جَنَابَةٌ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ عَلِمَ بِهِ قَالَ« عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَبْتَدِئَ اَلصَّلاَةَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يُصَلِّي وَ فِي ثَوْبِهِ جَنَابَةٌ أَوْ دَمٌ حَتَّى فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ ثُمَّ عَلِمَ قَالَ« قَدْ مَضَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prayed two rak‘ahs in a garment that had janabah on it, and then he became aware of it. Imam (a.s) said: "He must begin the prayer anew." He (Abu Basir) said: “I also asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays while there is janabah or blood on his garment, and he only realizes it after he finishes his prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: "His prayer is valid and nothing is required of him."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Safwan from al-‘Ayyas ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed for several days wearing another man’s garment, and then the owner of the garment informed him that it was not suitable for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not have to repeat any of his prayers."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى فِي ثَوْبِ رَجُلٍ أَيَّاماً ثُمَّ إِنَّ صَاحِبَ اَلثَّوْبِ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ لاَ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ قَالَ« لاَ يُعِيدُ شَيْئاً مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Safwan from al-‘Ayyas ibn al-Qasim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed for several days wearing another man’s garment, and then the owner of the garment informed him that it was not suitable for prayer. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not have to repeat any of his prayers."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding janabah that affects a garment and its owner is unaware of it, and then he prays in it and learns of it afterward. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not have to repeat the prayer if he was not aware of it."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :فِي اَلْجَنَابَةِ تُصِيبُ اَلثَّوْبَ وَ لاَ يَعْلَمُ بِهَا صَاحِبُهُ فَيُصَلِّي فِيهِ ثُمَّ يَعْلَمُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ« لاَ يُعِيدُ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلِمَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding janabah that affects a garment and its owner is unaware of it, and then he prays in it and learns of it afterward. Imam (a.s) said: "He does not have to repeat the prayer if he was not aware of it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 387

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man whose garment is soiled by something that renders it impure, and he forgets to wash it, then he prays in it, and afterward remembers that he had not washed it, does he have to repeat the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "He does not repeat it. His prayer has passed and has been recorded for him."
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُ ثَوْبَهُ اَلشَّيْءُ فَيُنَجِّسُهُ فَيَنْسَى أَنْ يَغْسِلَهُ فَيُصَلِّي فِيهِ ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ غَسَلَهُ أَ يُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُعِيدُ قَدْ مَضَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ كُتِبَتْ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man whose garment is soiled by something that renders it impure, and he forgets to wash it, then he prays in it, and afterward remembers that he had not washed it, does he have to repeat the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: "He does not repeat it. His prayer has passed and has been recorded for him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 387

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imam Abu Ja‘far (a.s) or Imam Abu Abdullah (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who sees blood on the garment of his brother while he is praying. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not disturb him until he finishes."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَرَى فِي ثَوْبِ أَخِيهِ دَماً وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« لاَ يُؤْذِيهِ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imam Abu Ja‘far (a.s) or Imam Abu Abdullah (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who sees blood on the garment of his brother while he is praying. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not disturb him until he finishes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 387

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Faddalah from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
My father asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about someone who lends his garment to a person whom he knows eats catfish (jirri) and drinks wine, and then the garment is returned, should he pray in it before washing it? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray in it until he washes it."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ أَبِي أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلَّذِي يُعِيرُ ثَوْبَهُ لِمَنْ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ يَأْكُلُ اَلْجِرِّيَّ وَ يَشْرَبُ اَلْخَمْرَ فَيَرُدُّهُ أَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَغْسِلَهُ قَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ حَتَّى يَغْسِلَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Faddalah from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: My father asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about someone who lends his garment to a person whom he knows eats catfish (jirri) and drinks wine, and then the garment is returned, should he pray in it before washing it? Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray in it until he washes it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 388

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
My father asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), and I was present, saying: “I lend my garment to a dhimmi (non-Muslim under protection), and I know that he drinks wine and eats pork. When he returns it to me, I wash it before praying in it.” Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Pray in it and do not wash it because of that. You lent it to him while it was pure, and you have no certainty that he made it impure. So there is no harm in praying in it until you are certain that he has made it impure."
arabicText: رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ أَبِي أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ أَنِّي أُعِيرُ اَلذِّمِّيَّ ثَوْبِي وَ أَنَا أَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ يَشْرَبُ اَلْخَمْرَ وَ يَأْكُلُ لَحْمَ اَلْخِنْزِيرِ فَيَرُدُّ عَلَيَّ فَأَغْسِلُهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« صَلِّ فِيهِ وَ لاَ تَغْسِلْهُ مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّكَ أَعَرْتَهُ إِيَّاهُ وَ هُوَ طَاهِرٌ وَ لَمْ تَسْتَيْقِنْ أَنَّهُ نَجَّسَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ حَتَّى تَسْتَيْقِنَ أَنَّهُ نَجَّسَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: My father asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), and I was present, saying: “I lend my garment to a dhimmi (non-Muslim under protection), and I know that he drinks wine and eats pork. When he returns it to me, I wash it before praying in it.” Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: "Pray in it and do not wash it because of that. You lent it to him while it was pure, and you have no certainty that he made it impure. So there is no harm in praying in it until you are certain that he has made it impure."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 388

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Jamil ibn Darraj from al-Mu‘alla ibn Khunays, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "There is no harm in praying in garments made by the Magians, the Christians, and the Jews."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنِ اَلْمُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلثِّيَابِ اَلَّتِي يَعْمَلُهَا اَلْمَجُوسُ وَ اَلنَّصَارَى وَ اَلْيَهُودُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Faddalah from Jamil ibn Darraj from al-Mu‘alla ibn Khunays, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: "There is no harm in praying in garments made by the Magians, the Christians, and the Jews."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 388

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about Sabiriyyah garments (a type of fabric) made by the Magians, while they are impure and they drink wine, and their women are also in that state, can I wear such clothes without washing them and pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." Mu‘awiyah (ibn Ammar) asked: “So I made a shirt for Imam (a.s), sewed it, fashioned buttons for it, and a cloak from the Sabiriyyah cloth, then sent it to Imam (a.s) on a Friday during the day. It was as if Imam (a.s) knew what I intended, so He (a.s) came out for Friday prayer wearing it.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْبِلاَدِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلثِّيَابِ اَلسَّابِرِيَّةِ يَعْمَلُهَا اَلْمَجُوسُ وَ هُمْ أَخْبَاثٌ وَ هُمْ يَشْرَبُونَ اَلْخَمْرَ وَ نِسَاؤُهُمْ عَلَى تِلْكَ اَلْحَالِ أَلْبَسُهَا وَ لاَ أَغْسِلُهَا وَ أُصَلِّي فِيهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قَالَ مُعَاوِيَةُ فَقَطَعْتُ لَهُ قَمِيصاً وَ خِطْتُهُ وَ فَتَلْتُ لَهُ أَزْرَاراً وَ رِدَاءً مِنَ اَلسَّابِرِيِّ ثُمَّ بَعَثْتُ بِهَا إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمِ جُمُعَةٍ حِينَ اِرْتَفَعَ اَلنَّهَارُ فَكَأَنَّهُ عَرَفَ مَا أُرِيدُ فَخَرَجَ فِيهَا إِلَى اَلْجُمُعَةِ
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about Sabiriyyah garments (a type of fabric) made by the Magians, while they are impure and they drink wine, and their women are also in that state, can I wear such clothes without washing them and pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." Mu‘awiyah (ibn Ammar) asked: “So I made a shirt for Imam (a.s), sewed it, fashioned buttons for it, and a cloak from the Sabiriyyah cloth, then sent it to Imam (a.s) on a Friday during the day. It was as if Imam (a.s) knew what I intended, so He (a.s) came out for Friday prayer wearing it.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 388

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Aban ibn Uthman from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about praying in the garment of a Magian. Imam (a.s) said: "It should be sprinkled with water."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي ثَوْبِ اَلْمَجُوسِيِّ فَقَالَ« يُرَشُّ بِالْمَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Aban ibn Uthman from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about praying in the garment of a Magian. Imam (a.s) said: "It should be sprinkled with water."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 389

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and Ahmad ibn Hilal from Musa ibn al-Qasim from 'Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the musk pod (fa'rat al-misk) that a man may have with him while praying, in his pocket or in his clothes. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm in that."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ وَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ فَأْرَةِ اَلْمِسْكِ تَكُونُ مَعَ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَهِيَ مَعَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ أَوْ ثِيَابِهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and Ahmad ibn Hilal from Musa ibn al-Qasim from 'Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the musk pod (fa'rat al-misk) that a man may have with him while praying, in his pocket or in his clothes. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm in that."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 389

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, said:
I wrote to Imam (a.s), meaning Abu Muhammad, peace be upon him, asking: “Is it permissible for a man to pray while he has with him a musk pod?” So Imam (a.s) wrote: "There is no problem with it if it has been purified (slaughtered according to Islamic law)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ يَعْنِي أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَجُوزُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَ مَعَهُ فَأْرَةُ مِسْكٍ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِذَا كَانَ ذَكِيّاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Imam (a.s), meaning Abu Muhammad, peace be upon him, asking: “Is it permissible for a man to pray while he has with him a musk pod?” So Imam (a.s) wrote: "There is no problem with it if it has been purified (slaughtered according to Islamic law)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 389

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while wearing a burtulah (a type of garment or woolen cloak). Imam (a.s) said: "It does not harm him."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْبُرْطُلَةُ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَضُرُّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while wearing a burtulah (a type of garment or woolen cloak). Imam (a.s) said: "It does not harm him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 389

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad, peace be upon him, asking Him (a.s) about praying in crimson-dyed cloth, and that our companions refrain from praying in it. So Imam (a.s) wrote: "There is no problem with it at all. ‘And all praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.’"
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْقِرْمِزِ وَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا يَتَوَقَّفُونَ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ مُطْلَقٌ« وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Muhammad, peace be upon him, asking Him (a.s) about praying in crimson-dyed cloth, and that our companions refrain from praying in it. So Imam (a.s) wrote: "There is no problem with it at all. ‘And all praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 389

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if there are figures on the cloth, as long as the image has been altered."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تَكُونَ اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ فِي اَلثَّوْبِ إِذَا غُيِّرَتِ اَلصُّورَةُ مِنْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if there are figures on the cloth, as long as the image has been altered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 390

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The cushions that are in the house which have figures on them, whether on the right or the left” So Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem as long as they are not facing the Qiblah. But if any of them is in front of you, in the direction of the Qiblah, then cover it and pray. And if you have with you black coins that have figures on them, then do not place them in front of you; rather, place them behind you."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ لَيْثٍ اَلْمُرَادِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْوَسَائِدُ تَكُونُ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ فِيهَا اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ عَنْ يَمِينٍ أَوْ شِمَالٍ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ تُجَاهَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ كَانَ شَيْءٌ مِنْهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ مِمَّا يَلِي اَلْقِبْلَةَ فَغَطِّهِ وَ صَلِّ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ مَعَكَ دَرَاهِمُ سُودٌ فِيهَا تَمَاثِيلُ فَلاَ تَجْعَلْهَا مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْكَ وَ اِجْعَلْهَا مِنْ خَلْفِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The cushions that are in the house which have figures on them, whether on the right or the left” So Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem as long as they are not facing the Qiblah. But if any of them is in front of you, in the direction of the Qiblah, then cover it and pray. And if you have with you black coins that have figures on them, then do not place them in front of you; rather, place them behind you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 390

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem in praying over all kinds of figures if you place them beneath you."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى كُلِّ اَلتَّمَاثِيلِ إِذَا جَعَلْتَهَا تَحْتَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem in praying over all kinds of figures if you place them beneath you."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 390

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about figures that are on a rug, which have two eyes, while you are praying. Imam (a.s) said: "If it has one eye, there is no problem; but if it has two eyes, then no."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلتَّمَاثِيلِ تَكُونُ فِي اَلْبِسَاطِ لَهَا عَيْنَانِ وَ أَنْتَ تُصَلِّي فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَتْ لَهَا عَيْنٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ عَيْنَانِ فَلاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about figures that are on a rug, which have two eyes, while you are praying. Imam (a.s) said: "If it has one eye, there is no problem; but if it has two eyes, then no."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 390

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, about a man who prays while in his garment there are coins that have figures on them. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ فِي ثَوْبِهِ دَرَاهِمُ فِيهَا تَمَاثِيلُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, about a man who prays while in his garment there are coins that have figures on them. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 390

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about black coins (oxidised silver dirhams during that time) that have figures on them, may a man pray while they are with him? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that if they are concealed."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلدَّرَاهِمِ اَلسُّودِ فِيهَا اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ أَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هِيَ مَعَهُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَتْ مُوَارَاةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about black coins (oxidised silver dirhams during that time) that have figures on them, may a man pray while they are with him? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with that if they are concealed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 391

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id said: I read the letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, in which he asked Imam (a.s) about praying in a garment whose lining is made of silk. So Imam (a.s) wrote to him: "I have read it. There is no problem in praying in it."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ قَالَ: قَرَأْتُ كِتَابَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي ثَوْبٍ حَشْوُهُ قَزٌّ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ« قَرَأْتُهُ لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id said: I read the letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, in which he asked Imam (a.s) about praying in a garment whose lining is made of silk. So Imam (a.s) wrote to him: "I have read it. There is no problem in praying in it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 391

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Barqi, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Mada’ini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
"He used to dislike wearing a shirt trimmed with brocade, and he disliked wearing silk and wearing embroidered garments, and he disliked the red saddle-cloth (‘mitharah’), for it is the saddle-cloth of Iblis."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْبَرْقِيُّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ جَرَّاحٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَلْبَسَ اَلْقَمِيصَ اَلْمَكْفُوفَ بِالدِّيبَاجِ وَ يَكْرَهُ لِبَاسَ اَلْحَرِيرِ وَ لِبَاسَ اَلْوَشْيِ وَ يَكْرَهُ اَلْمِيثَرَةَ اَلْحَمْرَاءَ فَإِنَّهَا مِيثَرَةُ إِبْلِيسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Barqi, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Mada’ini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: "He used to dislike wearing a shirt trimmed with brocade, and he disliked wearing silk and wearing embroidered garments, and he disliked the red saddle-cloth (‘mitharah’), for it is the saddle-cloth of Iblis."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 391

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-‘Ayyas ibn Al-Qasim, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays in a woman's garment, or in her izar (lower wrap), and wraps himself with her khimar (head covering). Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if she is trustworthy (in her cleanliness)."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي ثَوْبِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ وَ فِي إِزَارِهَا وَ يَعْتَمُّ بِخِمَارِهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَتْ مَأْمُونَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-‘Ayyas ibn Al-Qasim, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays in a woman's garment, or in her izar (lower wrap), and wraps himself with her khimar (head covering). Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, if she is trustworthy (in her cleanliness)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 392

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: “A man came out of a ship naked, or his clothes were taken from him, and he did not find anything to pray in.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray by signaling (with gestures), and if it is a woman, she should place her hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he should place his hand over his private part. Then they both should sit and perform prayer by gesturing, without bowing and without prostrating, so that what is behind them does not become exposed. Their prayer should be by gesturing with their heads." Imam (a.s) said: "And if they are in water or in a deep sea, they should not prostrate upon it, and the requirement of facing the Qiblah is lifted from them in that situation. They should gesture therein, raising their heads counts as turning (toward Qiblah), and lowering them counts as turning (toward Qiblah)."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ مِنْ سَفِينَةٍ عُرْيَاناً أَوْ سُلِبَ ثِيَابُهُ وَ لَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئاً يُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي إِيمَاءً وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اِمْرَأَةً جَعَلَتْ يَدَهَا عَلَى فَرْجِهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَ رَجُلاً وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى سَوْأَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسَانِ فَيُومِئَانِ إِيمَاءً وَلاَ يَرْكَعَانِ وَلاَ يَسْجُدَانِ فَيَبْدُوَ مَا خَلْفَهُمَا تَكُونُ صَلاَتُهُمَا إِيمَاءً بِرُءُوسِهِمَا» قَالَ« وَ إِنْ كَانَا فِي مَاءٍ أَوْ بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ لَمْ يَسْجُدَا عَلَيْهِ وَ مَوْضُوعٌ عَنْهُمَا اَلتَّوَجُّهُ فِيهِ فَيُومِئَانِ فِي ذَلِكَ إِيمَاءً رَفْعُهُمَا تَوَجُّهٌ وَ وَضْعُهُمَا تَوَجُّهٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: “A man came out of a ship naked, or his clothes were taken from him, and he did not find anything to pray in.” Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray by signaling (with gestures), and if it is a woman, she should place her hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he should place his hand over his private part. Then they both should sit and perform prayer by gesturing, without bowing and without prostrating, so that what is behind them does not become exposed. Their prayer should be by gesturing with their heads." Imam (a.s) said: "And if they are in water or in a deep sea, they should not prostrate upon it, and the requirement of facing the Qiblah is lifted from them in that situation. They should gesture therein, raising their heads counts as turning (toward Qiblah), and lowering them counts as turning (toward Qiblah)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 392

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I asked Imam (a.s) of a group of people who prayed congregation while they were naked. Imam (a.s) said: "The imam should go ahead of them on his knees and lead them in prayer sitting, while he is also sitting."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ صَلَّوْا جَمَاعَةً وَ هُمْ عُرَاةٌ قَالَ« يَتَقَدَّمُهُمُ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ جُلُوساً وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) of a group of people who prayed congregation while they were naked. Imam (a.s) said: "The imam should go ahead of them on his knees and lead them in prayer sitting, while he is also sitting."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 392

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A group of people were ambushed on the road, and their clothes were taken from them, so they remained naked, and the time of prayer arrived, what should they do?” Imam (a.s) said: "Their imam (of prayer) should go ahead of them and sit, and they should sit behind him. He should gesture with signs for bowing and prostration, and they should perform bowing and prostration behind him by placing their faces on the ground."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَوْمٌ قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلطَّرِيقُ فَأُخِذَتْ ثِيَابُهُمْ فَبَقُوا عُرَاةً وَحَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُونَ فَقَالَ« يَتَقَدَّمُهُمْ إِمَامُهُمْ فَيَجْلِسُ وَ يَجْلِسُونَ خَلْفَهُ فَيُومِئُ إِيمَاءً بِالرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ هُمْ يَرْكَعُونَ وَ يَسْجُدُونَ خَلْفَهُ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A group of people were ambushed on the road, and their clothes were taken from them, so they remained naked, and the time of prayer arrived, what should they do?” Imam (a.s) said: "Their imam (of prayer) should go ahead of them and sit, and they should sit behind him. He should gesture with signs for bowing and prostration, and they should perform bowing and prostration behind him by placing their faces on the ground."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 392

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Amraki Al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man whose belongings were either taken from him or drowned, so he remained naked, and the time of prayer arrived, how should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: "If he finds grass with which he can cover his private parts, then he should complete his prayer with bowing and prostration; but if he does not find anything to cover his private parts, then he should gesture while standing."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ اَلْبُوفَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ غَرِقَ مَتَاعُهُ فَبَقِيَ عُرْيَاناً وَ حَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« إِنْ أَصَابَ حَشِيشاً يَسْتُرُ بِهِ عَوْرَتَهُ أَتَمَّ صَلاَتَهُ بِالرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْ شَيْئاً يَسْتُرُ بِهِ عَوْرَتَهُ أَوْمَأَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Amraki Al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man whose belongings were either taken from him or drowned, so he remained naked, and the time of prayer arrived, how should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: "If he finds grass with which he can cover his private parts, then he should complete his prayer with bowing and prostration; but if he does not find anything to cover his private parts, then he should gesture while standing."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 392

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskan, from some of his companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who goes out naked and the time of prayer comes upon him. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray naked while standing if no one sees him; but if someone sees him, then he should pray sitting."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ عُرْيَاناً فَتُدْرِكُهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي عُرْيَاناً قَائِماً إِنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ فَإِنْ رَآهُ أَحَدٌ صَلَّى جَالِساً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskan, from some of his companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who goes out naked and the time of prayer comes upon him. Imam (a.s) said: "He should pray naked while standing if no one sees him; but if someone sees him, then he should pray sitting."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 393

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from some of his companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The naked person who does not have a garment, if he finds a pit, he should enter it and perform prostration and bowing within it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْعَارِي اَلَّذِي لَيْسَ لَهُ ثَوْبٌ إِذَا وَجَدَ حُفْرَةً دَخَلَهَا وَ يَسْجُدُ فِيهَا وَ يَرْكَعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from some of his companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The naked person who does not have a garment, if he finds a pit, he should enter it and perform prostration and bowing within it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 393

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, said:
Murazim asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was present with Imam (a.s), about a man who is present (not traveling) and prays wearing only an izar (lower garment), wrapping it around his waist. Imam (a.s) said: "He can place cloth or turban over his neck and drape it over himself."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ مُرَازِمٌ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا مَعَهُ حَاضِرٌ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ اَلْحَاضِرِ يُصَلِّي فِي إِزَارِهِ مُؤْتَزِراً بِهِ قَالَ« يَجْعَلُ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ مِنْدِيلاً أَوْ عِمَامَةً يَتَرَدَّى بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Murazim asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was present with Imam (a.s), about a man who is present (not traveling) and prays wearing only an izar (lower garment), wrapping it around his waist. Imam (a.s) said: "He can place cloth or turban over his neck and drape it over himself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 393

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who has nothing with him except trousers. Imam (a.s) said: "He should untie its waistband and place it over his shoulder and pray." And Imam (a.s) said: "And if he has a sword with him and no garment, then he should hang the sword around his neck and pray standing."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ سَرَاوِيلُ قَالَ« يَحُلُّ اَلتِّكَّةَ مِنْهُ فَيَطْرَحُهَا عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ وَيُصَلِّي» وَ قَالَ« وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ سَيْفٌ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ ثَوْبٌ فَلْيَتَقَلَّدِ اَلسَّيْفَ وَ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who has nothing with him except trousers. Imam (a.s) said: "He should untie its waistband and place it over his shoulder and pray." And Imam (a.s) said: "And if he has a sword with him and no garment, then he should hang the sword around his neck and pray standing."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 393

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, by Al-‘Amraki, by Ali ibn Ja‘far, by his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s):
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, does it suffice for him to lead the prayer wearing trousers and a cap? Imam (a.s) said: "It does not suffice." And I asked Imam (a.s) about trousers, if they be used in place of izar (lower garment)? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَؤُمَّ فِي سَرَاوِيلَ وَ قَلَنْسُوَةٍ قَالَ« لاَ يَصْلُحُ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسَّرَاوِيلِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ مَكَانَ اَلْإِزَارِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, by Al-‘Amraki, by Ali ibn Ja‘far, by his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, does it suffice for him to lead the prayer wearing trousers and a cap? Imam (a.s) said: "It does not suffice." And I asked Imam (a.s) about trousers, if they be used in place of izar (lower garment)? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 393

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer wearing a shirt without a cloak over it. Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate unless he has a cloak or a turban with which he drapes himself."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فِي قَمِيصٍ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ رِدَاءٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَنْبَغِي إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ رِدَاءٌ أَوْ عِمَامَةٌ يَرْتَدِي بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer wearing a shirt without a cloak over it. Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate unless he has a cloak or a turban with which he drapes himself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 394

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a wet mouse that fell into water and then walked over clothes, may one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Wash whatever trace of it you see, and what you do not see, sprinkle it with water."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفَأْرَةِ اَلرَّطْبَةِ قَدْ وَقَعَتْ فِي اَلْمَاءِ فَتَمْشِي عَلَى اَلثِّيَابِ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا قَالَ« اِغْسِلْ مَا رَأَيْتَ مِنْ أَثَرِهَا وَ مَا لَمْ تَرَهُ اِنْضِحْهُ بِالْمَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a wet mouse that fell into water and then walked over clothes, may one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Wash whatever trace of it you see, and what you do not see, sprinkle it with water."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 394

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-‘Alawi, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about worms (maggots, parasitic worms, or decomposition worms) that fall from the toilet onto the garment, may one pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem unless you see a trace (of impurity), then you must wash it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلدُّودِ يَقَعُ مِنَ اَلْكَنِيفِ عَلَى اَلثَّوْبِ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَرَى أَثَراً فَتَغْسِلَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-‘Alawi, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about worms (maggots, parasitic worms, or decomposition worms) that fall from the toilet onto the garment, may one pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem unless you see a trace (of impurity), then you must wash it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 394

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, said:
I heard (Imam) Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, forbid the wearing of silk for both men and women, except for silk mixed with ‘khazz’ (a kind of fabric), the weft or the warp of which is ‘khazz’ or linen or cotton. Pure silk alone is disliked for both men and women.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَنْهَى عَنْ لِبَاسِ اَلْحَرِيرِ لِلرِّجَالِ وَاَلنِّسَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا كَانَ مِنْ حَرِيرٍ مَخْلُوطٍ بِخَزٍّ لَحْمَتُهُ أَوْ سَدَاهُ خَزٌّ أَوْ كَتَّانٌ أَوْ قُطْنٌ وَ إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ اَلْحَرِيرُ اَلْمَحْضُ لِلرِّجَالِ وَ اَلنِّسَاءِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard (Imam) Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, forbid the wearing of silk for both men and women, except for silk mixed with ‘khazz’ (a kind of fabric), the weft or the warp of which is ‘khazz’ or linen or cotton. Pure silk alone is disliked for both men and women.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 394

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-‘Abbas, from Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Muhammad ibn Husayn ibn Kathir, from his father, who said:
I saw on Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, a woolen cloak between two coarse garments, so I asked Imam (a.s) about that. Imam (a.s) said: "I saw my father wearing it. Indeed, when we intend to pray, we wear the roughest of our clothes."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ كَثِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُبَّةَ صُوفٍ بَيْنَ ثَوْبَيْنِ غَلِيظَيْنِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« رَأَيْتُ أَبِي يَلْبَسُهَا إِنَّا إِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُصَلِّيَ لَبِسْنَا أَخْشَنَ ثِيَابِنَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-‘Abbas, from Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Muhammad ibn Husayn ibn Kathir, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw on Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, a woolen cloak between two coarse garments, so I asked Imam (a.s) about that. Imam (a.s) said: "I saw my father wearing it. Indeed, when we intend to pray, we wear the roughest of our clothes."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Rayyan, who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), asking: “Is it permissible to pray in a garment that has in it human hair or fingernails, without shaking them off or removing them from it?” So Imam (a.s) wrote in response, peace be upon him: "It is permissible."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلرَّيَّانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي ثَوْبٍ يَكُونُ فِيهِ شَعْرٌ مِنْ شَعْرِ اَلْإِنْسَانِ وَ أَظْفَارُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَنْفُضَهُ وَ يُلْقِيَهُ عَنْهُ فَوَقَّعَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَجُوزُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Al-Rayyan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), asking: “Is it permissible to pray in a garment that has in it human hair or fingernails, without shaking them off or removing them from it?” So Imam (a.s) wrote in response, peace be upon him: "It is permissible."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 395

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Al-Hasan ibn Shihab, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about fox skins, if they have been purified (lawfully slaughtered), may one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ جُلُودِ اَلثَّعَالِبِ إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Al-Hasan ibn Shihab, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about fox skins, if they have been purified (lawfully slaughtered), may one pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 395

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, said:
I asked Him (a.s) about footwear made from foxes or garments from them, may one pray in them or not? Imam (a.s) said: "If it has been purified (lawfully slaughtered), then there is no problem with it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدٌ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْخِفَافِ مِنَ اَلثَّعَالِبِ أَوِ اَلْجِرْزِ مِنْهُ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا أَمْ لاَ قَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ ذَكِيّاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about footwear made from foxes or garments from them, may one pray in them or not? Imam (a.s) said: "If it has been purified (lawfully slaughtered), then there is no problem with it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 395

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who goes to the market and buys a fur cloak but does not know whether it is from a lawfully slaughtered animal or not, may he pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. You are not required to ask. Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, used to say: 'Indeed, the Khawarij imposed restrictions upon themselves out of their ignorance. Surely, the religion is broader than that.'"
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي اَلسُّوقَ فَيَشْتَرِي جُبَّةَ فِرَاءٍ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ ذَكِيَّةٌ هِيَ أَمْ غَيْرُ ذَكِيَّةٍ أَ يُصَلِّي فِيهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمُ اَلْمَسْأَلَةُ إِنَّ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ «إِنَّ اَلْخَوَارِجَ ضَيَّقُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ بِجَهَالَتِهِمْ إِنَّ اَلدِّينَ أَوْسَعُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ»»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who goes to the market and buys a fur cloak but does not know whether it is from a lawfully slaughtered animal or not, may he pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. You are not required to ask. Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, used to say: 'Indeed, the Khawarij imposed restrictions upon themselves out of their ignorance. Surely, the religion is broader than that.'"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 396

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem in praying in what is made from the wool of a carcass, for wool does not have a soul in it." Abdullah (ibn Muskan) said: “And Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to me that a man asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was with Imam (a.s), about a man who wears a sword around his neck and prays with it.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." So the man said: “There is ‘kaymukht’ in it.” Imam (a.s) said: "And what is ‘kaymukht’?" The man said: “Skins of animals, some of it is from a lawfully slaughtered animal, and some of it is from a carcass.” So Imam (a.s) said: "What you know to be from a carcass, do not pray in it."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيمَا كَانَ مِنْ صُوفِ اَلْمَيْتَةِ إِنَّ اَلصُّوفَ لَيْسَ فِيهِ رُوحٌ» قَالَ عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ وَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ أَنَّ رَجُلاً سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَقَلَّدُ اَلسَّيْفَ وَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِنَّ فِيهِ اَلْكَيْمُخْتَ فَقَالَ« وَمَا اَلْكَيْمُخْتُ» فَقَالَ جُلُودُ دَوَابَّ مِنْهُ مَا يَكُونُ ذَكِيّاً وَمِنْهُ مَا يَكُونُ مَيْتَةً فَقَالَ« مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ مَيْتَةٌ فَلاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem in praying in what is made from the wool of a carcass, for wool does not have a soul in it." Abdullah (ibn Muskan) said: “And Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to me that a man asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was with Imam (a.s), about a man who wears a sword around his neck and prays with it.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes." So the man said: “There is ‘kaymukht’ in it.” Imam (a.s) said: "And what is ‘kaymukht’?" The man said: “Skins of animals, some of it is from a lawfully slaughtered animal, and some of it is from a carcass.” So Imam (a.s) said: "What you know to be from a carcass, do not pray in it."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 396

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A cloth that is used for wiping, may a man place it on his shoulder or wrap it around his waist and pray in it?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مِنْدِيلٌ يُتَمَنْدَلُ بِهِ أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَضَعَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ عَلَى مَنْكِبِهِ أَوْ يَتَّزِرَ بِهِ وَ يُصَلِّيَ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A cloth that is used for wiping, may a man place it on his shoulder or wrap it around his waist and pray in it?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 396

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem in praying in Yemeni silk and in what is made in the lands of Islam." I said to Imam (a.s): “What if there are non-Muslims in it?” Imam (a.s) said: "If Muslims are predominant in it, then there is no problem."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبْدِ اَلصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْقَزِّ اَلْيَمَانِيِّ وَ فِيمَا صُنِعَ فِي أَرْضِ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ» قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا غَيْرُ أَهْلِ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ قَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْغَالِبَ عَلَيْهَا اَلْمُسْلِمُونَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih (a.s)), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem in praying in Yemeni silk and in what is made in the lands of Islam." I said to Imam (a.s): “What if there are non-Muslims in it?” Imam (a.s) said: "If Muslims are predominant in it, then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 396

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Al-Rayyan ibn Al-Salt, said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about wearing furs of samur (sable), sinjab (squirrel), ‘hawasil’ (small animals with gathered pelts), and what resembles them, and about belts, cloaks (al-kaymukht), clothing padded with silk, and footwear made from various types of leather. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with all of this, except for (what is made from) foxes (al-tha’alib)."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اَلرَّيَّانِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ لُبْسِ فِرَاءِ اَلسَّمُّورِ وَ اَلسِّنْجَابِ وَ اَلْحَوَاصِلِ وَ مَا أَشْبَهَهَا وَ اَلْمَنَاطِقِ وَ اَلْكَيْمُخْتِ وَ اَلْمَحْشُوِّ بِالْقَزِّ وَ اَلْخِفَافِ مِنْ أَصْنَافِ اَلْجُلُودِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهَذَا كُلِّهِ إِلاَّ بِالثَّعَالِبِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Al-Rayyan ibn Al-Salt, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about wearing furs of samur (sable), sinjab (squirrel), ‘hawasil’ (small animals with gathered pelts), and what resembles them, and about belts, cloaks (al-kaymukht), clothing padded with silk, and footwear made from various types of leather. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with all of this, except for (what is made from) foxes (al-tha’alib)."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 397

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about wearing ‘khazz’ (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it. Indeed, (Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, used to wear a ‘khazz’ cloak in the winter, and when summer came, He (a.s) would sell it and give its price in charity. And He (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)) used to say: 'I feel ashamed before my Lord (azj) to eat from the price of a garment in which I worshipped Allah (swt).'"
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ لُبْسِ اَلْخَزِّ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَلْبَسُ اَلْكِسَاءَ اَلْخَزِّ فِي اَلشِّتَاءِ فَإِذَا جَاءَ اَلصَّيْفُ بَاعَهُ وَتَصَدَّقَ بِثَمَنِهِ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ« إِنِّي لَأَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ رَبِّي أَنْ آكُلَ ثَمَنَ ثَوْبٍ قَدْ عَبَدْتُ اَللَّهَ فِيهِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about wearing ‘khazz’ (a type of fine fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem with it. Indeed, (Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, used to wear a ‘khazz’ cloak in the winter, and when summer came, He (a.s) would sell it and give its price in charity. And He (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)) used to say: 'I feel ashamed before my Lord (azj) to eat from the price of a garment in which I worshipped Allah (swt).'"

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ibrahim Al-Ahmari, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while his buttons are undone. Imam (a.s) said: "That is not appropriate."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْأَحْمَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يُصَلِّي وَ أَزْرَارُهُ مُحَلَّلَةٌ قَالَ« لاَ يَنْبَغِي ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ibrahim Al-Ahmari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prays while his buttons are undone. Imam (a.s) said: "That is not appropriate."

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘shadhakunah’ (a type of thick woolen or felt garment) that is affected by a wet dream, may one pray upon it? Imam (a.s) said: "No."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلشَّاذَكُونَةِ يُصِيبُهَا اَلاِحْتِلاَمُ أَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ« لاَ»

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the ‘shadhakunah’ (a type of felt or coarse cloth) upon which there is janabah (major ritual impurity) on it, is it permissible to pray on it in the litter (mahmil) (a type of carriage or travel seat)? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلشَّاذَكُونَةِ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهَا اَلْجَنَابَةُ أَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the ‘shadhakunah’ (a type of felt or coarse cloth) upon which there is janabah (major ritual impurity) on it, is it permissible to pray on it in the litter (mahmil) (a type of carriage or travel seat)? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
