chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Safwan, from Salih Al-Nili, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I pray upon the ‘shadhakunah’ (a thick or coarse cloth) while it has been affected by janabah (major ritual impurity)?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ صَالِحٍ اَلنِّيلِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي عَلَى اَلشَّاذَكُونَةِ وَ قَدْ أَصَابَتْهَا اَلْجَنَابَةُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Safwan, from Salih Al-Nili, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I pray upon the ‘shadhakunah’ (a thick or coarse cloth) while it has been affected by janabah (major ritual impurity)?” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a ‘bariyyah’ (a mat) whose reeds were moistened with impure water, does it suffice to pray on it? Imam (a.s) said: "If it has dried, then there is no problem in praying on it."
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْبَارِيَّةِ يُبَلُّ قَصَبُهَا بِمَاءٍ قَذِرٍ هَلْ يَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ« إِذَا جَفَّتْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ عَلَيْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a ‘bariyyah’ (a mat) whose reeds were moistened with impure water, does it suffice to pray on it? Imam (a.s) said: "If it has dried, then there is no problem in praying on it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa‘d ibn Isma‘il, from his father, said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about a prayer mat or carpet that has figures on it, may one stand on it and pray or not? Imam (a.s) said: "By Allah (swt), I dislike that." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who entered upon another man who had a carpet with a figure on it. Imam (a.s) said: "Do you find an image here?" Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do not sit on it and do not pray on it."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمُصَلَّى وَ اَلْبِسَاطِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ تَمَاثِيلُ أَ يَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ فَيُصَلِّي أَمْ لاَ فَقَالَ« وَ اَللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ» وَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ وَ عِنْدَهُ بِسَاطٌ عَلَيْهِ تِمْثَالٌ فَقَالَ« أَ تَجِدُ هَاهُنَا مِثَالاً» فَقَالَ« لاَ تَجْلِسُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لاَ تُصَلِّي عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa‘d ibn Isma‘il, from his father, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about a prayer mat or carpet that has figures on it, may one stand on it and pray or not? Imam (a.s) said: "By Allah (swt), I dislike that." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who entered upon another man who had a carpet with a figure on it. Imam (a.s) said: "Do you find an image here?" Then Imam (a.s) said: "Do not sit on it and do not pray on it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: “I pray while the figures are in front of me and I am looking at them?” Imam (a.s) said: "No. Cast a cloth over them. There is no problem if they are to your right, or to your left, or behind you, or beneath your feet, or above your head. But if they are in the direction of the Qiblah, then cover them with a cloth and pray."
arabicText: محمد بن احمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن الحسين عن الحسن ابن محبوب عن العلا عن محمد بن مسلم قال قلت لابي جعفر عليه السلام أصلي والتماثيل قدامي وانا انظر إليها؟ قال لا إطرح عليها ثوبا ولا بأس بها إذا كانت عن يمينك أو شمالك أو خلفك أو تحت رجلك أو فوق رأسك وإن كانت في القبلة فالق عليها ثوبا وصل
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him: “I pray while the figures are in front of me and I am looking at them?” Imam (a.s) said: "No. Cast a cloth over them. There is no problem if they are to your right, or to your left, or behind you, or beneath your feet, or above your head. But if they are in the direction of the Qiblah, then cover them with a cloth and pray."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah, who said: Ziyad ibn Al-Mundhir informed me, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, who said:
A man asked Imam (a.s) while I was present about a man who comes out of the bathhouse or performs ghusl, then drapes a cloth over himself and wears his shirt over the ‘izar’ (lower garment), and prays in that state. Imam (a.s) said: "This is the practice of the people of Lot." I asked: “What if he drapes the cloth over the shirt?” Imam (a.s) said: "This is from arrogance." I asked: “The shirt is thin, so he wraps himself with it.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes (that is acceptable)." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, unbuttoning one's shirt in prayer, flicking pebbles, chewing frankincense in gatherings, and sitting on the roadsides, all of this is from the actions of the people of Lot."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي زِيَادُ بْنُ اَلْمُنْذِرِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ وَأَنَا حَاضِرٌ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ مِنَ اَلْحَمَّامِ أَوْ يَغْتَسِلُ فَيَتَوَشَّحُ وَيَلْبَسُ قَمِيصَهُ فَوْقَ اَلْإِزَارِ فَيُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ« هَذَا عَمَلُ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ يَتَوَشَّحُ فَوْقَ اَلْقَمِيصِ فَقَالَ« هَذَا مِنَ اَلتَّجَبُّرِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنَّ اَلْقَمِيصَ رَقِيقٌ يَلْتَحِفُ بِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« إِنَّ حَلَّ اَلْأَزْرَارِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ اَلْخَذْفَ بِالْحَصَى وَمَضْغَ اَلْكُنْدُرِ فِي اَلْمَجَالِسِ وَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ اَلطَّرِيقِ مِنْ عَمَلِ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah, who said: Ziyad ibn Al-Mundhir informed me, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked Imam (a.s) while I was present about a man who comes out of the bathhouse or performs ghusl, then drapes a cloth over himself and wears his shirt over the ‘izar’ (lower garment), and prays in that state. Imam (a.s) said: "This is the practice of the people of Lot." I asked: “What if he drapes the cloth over the shirt?” Imam (a.s) said: "This is from arrogance." I asked: “The shirt is thin, so he wraps himself with it.” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes (that is acceptable)." Then Imam (a.s) said: "Indeed, unbuttoning one's shirt in prayer, flicking pebbles, chewing frankincense in gatherings, and sitting on the roadsides, all of this is from the actions of the people of Lot."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from his father:
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "A woman should not pray uncovered."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُصَلِّي اَلْمَرْأَةُ عُطُلاً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "A woman should not pray uncovered."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 399

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Sa‘d ibn Isma‘il, from his father Isma‘il ibn ‘Isa, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), about the fur skins which a man buys in the market from the markets of the mountain region, should he ask about their slaughtering (dhakah) if the seller is a Muslim but not one of the ‘Arif’ (not a ‘shia’)? He said "It is upon you to ask about it if you see that the sellers are polytheists. But if you see that (people) are praying in it, then do not ask about it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ جُلُودِ اَلْفِرَاءِ يَشْتَرِيهَا اَلرَّجُلُ فِي سُوقٍ مِنْ أَسْوَاقِ اَلْجَبَلِ أَ يَسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَكَاتِهِ إِذَا كَانَ اَلْبَائِعُ مُسْلِماً غَيْرَ عَارِفٍ قَالَ« عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْتُمْ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ إِذَا رَأَيْتُمُ اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ يَبِيعُونَ ذَلِكَ وَ إِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ يُصَلُّونَ فِيهِ فَلاَ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Sa‘d ibn Isma‘il, from his father Isma‘il ibn ‘Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (a.s), about the fur skins which a man buys in the market from the markets of the mountain region, should he ask about their slaughtering (dhakah) if the seller is a Muslim but not one of the ‘Arif’ (not a ‘shia’)? He said "It is upon you to ask about it if you see that the sellers are polytheists. But if you see that (people) are praying in it, then do not ask about it."

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about leather socks, if a man goes to the market and buys leather socks without knowing whether the leather is from a lawfully slaughtered animal or not, what do you say about praying in them while he does not know? Should he pray in them? Imam (a.s) said: "Yes. I buy leather socks from the market, and they are made for me, and I pray in them. And it is not obligatory upon you to ask."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْخَفَّافِ يَأْتِي اَلسُّوقَ فَيَشْتَرِي اَلْخُفَّ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ ذَكِيٌّ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَدْرِي أَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ أَنَا أَشْتَرِي اَلْخُفَّ مِنَ اَلسُّوقِ وَ يُصْنَعُ لِي وَ أُصَلِّي فِيهِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمُ اَلْمَسْأَلَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about leather socks, if a man goes to the market and buys leather socks without knowing whether the leather is from a lawfully slaughtered animal or not, what do you say about praying in them while he does not know? chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, by Ahmad, by his father, by Wahb ibn Wahb, from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s):
(Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The sword is like a cloak, you may pray with it as long as you do not see blood on it. And the bow is like a cloak."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلسَّيْفُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلرِّدَاءِ تُصَلِّي فِيهِ مَا لَمْ تَرَ فِيهِ دَماً وَ اَلْقَوْسُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلرِّدَاءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, by Ahmad, by his father, by Wahb ibn Wahb, from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The sword is like a cloak, you may pray with it as long as you do not see blood on it. And the bow is like a cloak."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d, from Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about the skins of ‘khazz’ (a type of fine cloth or fabric). Imam (a.s) said: "Here we are, we wear it." I asked: “That is fur, may I be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said: "When its fur is permissible, its skin is also permissible."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, by Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, by ‘Ammar ibn Musa:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prays while wearing an iron ring. Imam (a.s) said: "No, and a man should not wear it, for it is from the dress of the people of the Fire." And Imam (a.s) said: "A man should not wear gold nor pray in it, for it is from the dress of the people of Paradise." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a garment that has a border of brocade. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray in it." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a garment whose border has the image of a bird or something else, may one pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "No." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a filthy spot that is in the house or elsewhere and is not struck by sunlight but has dried. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray on it, and mark its place until he washes it." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about the sun, does it purify the ground? Imam (a.s) said: "If the place is filthy from urine or something else, and the sun strikes it, and then the place dries, then prayer on that spot is permissible. But if the sun strikes it and the filthy place has not dried and remains wet, then it is not permissible to pray on it until it dries. And if your foot is wet, or your forehead is wet, or any other part of you touches that filthy place, then do not pray on that spot until it dries, for it is not permissible." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who performs wudhu and walks barefoot while his foot is wet. Imam (a.s) said: "If your ground is paved, then it is sufficient for you to walk on it." And Imam (a.s) said: "As for us, it is permissible for us, because our ground is paved", meaning, covered with gravel. And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who wears a ring that has the engraved image of a bird or something else. Imam (a.s) said: "It is not permissible to pray with it."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَعَلَيْهِ خَاتَمُ حَدِيدٍ قَالَ« لاَ وَلاَ يَتَخَتَّمُ بِهِ اَلرَّجُلُ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ لِبَاسِ أَهْلِ اَلنَّارِ» وَقَالَ« لاَ يَلْبَسُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلذَّهَبَ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ لِأَنَّهُ مِنْ لِبَاسِ أَهْلِ اَلْجَنَّةِ» وَ عَنِ اَلثَّوْبِ يَكُونُ عَلَمُهُ دِيبَاجاً قَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ» وَ عَنِ اَلثَّوْبِ يَكُونُ فِي عَلَمِهِ مِثَالُ طَيْرٍ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ أَ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَالَ« لاَ» وَ عَنِ اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلْقَذِرِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ فَلاَ تُصِيبُهُ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ قَدْ يَبِسَ اَلْمَوْضِعُ اَلْقَذِرُ قَالَ« لاَ يُصَلِّي عَلَيْهِ وَ أَعْلَمَ مَوْضِعَهُ حَتَّى يَغْسِلَهُ» وَ عَنِ اَلشَّمْسِ هَلْ تُطَهِّرُ اَلْأَرْضَ قَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْمَوْضِعُ قَذِراً مِنْ بَوْلٍ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَأَصَابَتْهُ اَلشَّمْسُ ثُمَّ يَبِسَ اَلْمَوْضِعُ فَالصَّلاَةُ عَلَى اَلْمَوْضِعِ جَائِزَةٌ وَ إِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ لَمْ يَيْبَسِ اَلْمَوْضِعُ اَلْقَذِرُ وَ كَانَ رَطْباً فَلاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَيْبَسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ رِجْلُكَ رَطْبَةً أَوْ جَبْهَتُكَ رَطْبَةً أَوْ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكَ مَا يُصِيبُ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَوْضِعَ اَلْقَذِرَ فَلاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ اَلْمَوْضِعِ حَتَّى يَيْبَسَ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَتَوَضَّأُ وَ يَمْشِي حَافِياً وَ رِجْلُهُ رَطْبَةٌ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَتْ أَرْضُكُمْ مُبَلَّطَةً أَجْزَأَكُمُ اَلْمَشْيُ عَلَيْهَا» وَ قَالَ« أَمَّا نَحْنُ فَيَجُوزُ لَنَا ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ أَرْضَنَا مُبَلَّطَةٌ يَعْنِي مَفْرُوشَةً بِالْحَصَى» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَلْبَسُ اَلْخَاتَمَ فِيهِ نَقْشُ مِثَالِ اَلطَّيْرِ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ قَالَ« لاَ تَجُوزُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, by Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, by ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, by Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, by ‘Ammar ibn Musa:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prays while wearing an iron ring. Imam (a.s) said: "No, and a man should not wear it, for it is from the dress of the people of the Fire." And Imam (a.s) said: "A man should not wear gold nor pray in it, for it is from the dress of the people of Paradise." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a garment that has a border of brocade. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray in it." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a garment whose border has the image of a bird or something else, may one pray in it? Imam (a.s) said: "No." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a filthy spot that is in the house or elsewhere and is not struck by sunlight but has dried. Imam (a.s) said: "He should not pray on it, and mark its place until he washes it." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about the sun, does it purify the ground? Imam (a.s) said: "If the place is filthy from urine or something else, and the sun strikes it, and then the place dries, then prayer on that spot is permissible. But if the sun strikes it and the filthy place has not dried and remains wet, then it is not permissible to pray on it until it dries. And if your foot is wet, or your forehead is wet, or any other part of you touches that filthy place, then do not pray on that spot until it dries, for it is not permissible." And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who performs wudhu and walks barefoot while his foot is wet. Imam (a.s) said: "If your ground is paved, then it is sufficient for you to walk on it." And Imam (a.s) said: "As for us, it is permissible for us, because our ground is paved", meaning, covered with gravel. And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about a man who wears a ring that has the engraved image of a bird or something else. Imam (a.s) said: "It is not permissible to pray with it."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer is disliked in a heavily dyed, deeply colored, blood-red garment."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «تُكْرَهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلثَّوْبِ اَلْمَصْبُوغِ اَلْمُشْبَعِ اَلْمُفْدَمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer is disliked in a heavily dyed, deeply colored, blood-red garment."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from someone who narrated to him, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) disliked prayer in a garment saturated with safflower and dyed with saffron.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ خَلِيفَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ كَرِهَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي اَلْمُشْبَعِ بِالْعُصْفُرِ اَلْمُضَرَّجِ بِالزَّعْفَرَانِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, from someone who narrated to him, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) disliked prayer in a garment saturated with safflower and dyed with saffron.

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him (a.s) about a man, does it suffice for him to gather the two ends of his cloak over his left shoulder? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate to gather them over the left shoulder; rather, gather them over your right shoulder, or leave them." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about reed mats (al-bawari’) that have been soiled with urine, does prayer on them suffice if they have dried without being washed?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, there is no problem." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about praying on the reed mats of Christians and Jews, upon which they sit in their homes, does it suffice?” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray on them." And I asked Imam (a.s) about the sword, does it take the place of the cloak, such that one may lead the people in prayer wearing only the sword? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate to lead people in prayer while wearing only the sword, except in battle."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَجْمَعَ طَرَفَيْ رِدَائِهِ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ قَالَ« لاَ يَصْلُحُ جَمْعُهُمَا عَلَى اَلْيَسَارِ وَ لَكِنِ اِجْمَعْهُمَا عَلَى يَمِينِكَ أَوْ دَعْهُمَا» قَالَ وَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْبَوَارِي يُصِيبُهَا اَلْبَوْلُ هَلْ تَصْلُحُ اَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَيْهَا إِذَا جَفَّتْ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ تُغْسَلَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ عَلَى بَوَارِي اَلنَّصَارَى وَ اَلْيَهُودِ اَلَّذِينَ يَقْعُدُونَ عَلَيْهَا فِي بُيُوتِهِمْ أَ يَصْلُحُ قَالَ« لاَ تُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسَّيْفِ هَلْ يَجْرِي مَجْرَى اَلرِّدَاءِ يُؤَمُّ اَلْقَوْمُ فِي اَلسَّيْفِ قَالَ« لاَ يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يُؤَمَّ اَلْقَوْمُ فِي اَلسَّيْفِ إِلاَّ فِي حَرْبٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Him (a.s) about a man, does it suffice for him to gather the two ends of his cloak over his left shoulder? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate to gather them over the left shoulder; rather, gather them over your right shoulder, or leave them." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about reed mats (al-bawari’) that have been soiled with urine, does prayer on them suffice if they have dried without being washed?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, there is no problem." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about praying on the reed mats of Christians and Jews, upon which they sit in their homes, does it suffice?” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray on them." And I asked Imam (a.s) about the sword, does it take the place of the cloak, such that one may lead the people in prayer wearing only the sword? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not appropriate to lead people in prayer while wearing only the sword, except in battle."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Yazid Al-Qasmi, and Qasm is a tribe from Yemen residing in Basrah, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him:
He (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about the skins of ‘al-Darish’ (a type of animal) from which leather socks are made. Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in them, for they are tanned using dog feces."

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Yazid Al-Qasmi, and Qasm is a tribe from Yemen residing in Basrah, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him:

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah together, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, may he pray on a platform (raf) suspended between two palm trees? Imam (a.s) said: "If it is level, and he is able to perform the prayer on it, then there is no harm." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about beds or rugs made of silk or its like from dibaj (brocade), and a prayer mat of silk or brocade, is it permissible for a man to sleep on it, recline on it, and pray on it?” Imam (a.s) said: "He may lay it out and stand on it, but he should not prostrate on it." And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prays in a mosque whose walls are all covered with embroidery (kiwa), the qiblah wall and both side walls, and his wife prays in front of him, so that he sees her but she does not see him. Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem." And I asked Imam (a.s) about mats whose reeds were wetted with impure water, may one pray on them? Imam (a.s) said: "If they have dried, then there is no problem." And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed while having with him a saddle or other item made from donkey skin, and he was wearing sandals made from donkey skin, does his prayer suffice him or must he repeat it? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not proper for him to pray while it is with him unless he fears that it might be lost, then there is no problem in praying while it is with him."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ وَ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ عَلَى اَلرَّفِّ اَلْمُعَلَّقِ بَيْنَ نَخْلَتَيْنِ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ مُسْتَوِياً يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ عَلَيْهِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ فِرَاشِ حَرِيرٍ وَ مِثْلِهِ مِنَ اَلدِّيبَاجِ وَ مُصَلَّى حَرِيرٍ وَ مِثْلِهِ مِنَ اَلدِّيبَاجِ يَصْلُحُ لِلرَّجُلِ اَلنَّوْمُ عَلَيْهِ وَاَلتُّكَأَةُ وَاَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« يَفْرُشُهُ وَ يَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ وَلاَ يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي مَسْجِدٍ حِيطَانُهُ كِوَاءٌ كُلُّهُ قِبْلَتُهُ وَجَانِبَاهُ وَاِمْرَأَتُهُ تُصَلِّي حِيَالَهُ يَرَاهَا وَلاَ تَرَاهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» وَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْبَوَارِي يُبَلُّ قَصَبُهَا بِمَاءٍ قَذِرٍ أَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا قَالَ« إِذَا يَبِسَتْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ صَلَّى وَ مَعَهُ دَبَّةٌ مِنْ جِلْدِ حِمَارٍ وَعَلَيْهِ نَعْلٌ مِنْ جِلْدِ حِمَارٍ هَلْ تُجْزِيهِ صَلاَتُهُ أَوْ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةٌ قَالَ« لاَ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَهِيَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَتَخَوَّفَ عَلَيْهَا ذَهَابَهَا فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَ هِيَ مَعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah together, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man, may he pray on a platform (raf) suspended between two palm trees? Imam (a.s) said: "If it is level, and he is able to perform the prayer on it, then there is no harm." He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about beds or rugs made of silk or its like from dibaj (brocade), and a prayer mat of silk or brocade, is it permissible for a man to sleep on it, recline on it, and pray on it?” Imam (a.s) said: "He may lay it out and stand on it, but he should not prostrate on it." Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem." And I asked Imam (a.s) about mats whose reeds were wetted with impure water, may one pray on them? Imam (a.s) said: "If they have dried, then there is no problem." And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed while having with him a saddle or other item made from donkey skin, and he was wearing sandals made from donkey skin, does his prayer suffice him or must he repeat it? Imam (a.s) said: "It is not proper for him to pray while it is with him unless he fears that it might be lost, then there is no problem in praying while it is with him."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in the bathhouse. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is a clean place, then there is no problem."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي بَيْتِ اَلْحَمَّامِ قَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ مَوْضِعاً نَظِيفاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in the bathhouse. Imam (a.s) said: "If it is a clean place, then there is no problem."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa Al-‘Ubaydi, from Al-Husayn ibn Yaqtin, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madi, peace be upon him, about praying between graves, does it suffice? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ بَيْنَ اَلْقُبُورِ هَلْ تَصْلُحُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa Al-‘Ubaydi, from Al-Husayn ibn Yaqtin, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madi, peace be upon him, about praying between graves, does it suffice? Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from ‘Amir ibn Nu‘aym Al-Qummi, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The places where people lodge, there are the urines of animals and manure, and Jews and Christians enter them, what should be done about praying in them?” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray upon your garment."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَامِرِ بْنِ نُعَيْمٍ اَلْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْمَنَازِلُ اَلَّتِي يَنْزِلُهَا اَلنَّاسُ فِيهَا أَبْوَالُ اَلدَّوَابِّ وَاَلسِّرْجِينُ وَيَدْخُلُهَا اَلْيَهُودُ وَاَلنَّصَارَى كَيْفَ يُصْنَعُ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا قَالَ« صَلِّ عَلَى ثَوْبِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from ‘Amir ibn Nu‘aym Al-Qummi, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The places where people lodge, there are the urines of animals and manure, and Jews and Christians enter them, what should be done about praying in them?” Imam (a.s) said: "Pray upon your garment."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who wades into water and the time of prayer comes upon him. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is in battle, then gesturing suffices him; But if he is a merchant, then let him stop and not enter (the water) until he has prayed."
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخُوضُ اَلْمَاءَ فَتُدْرِكُهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ فِي حَرْبٍ فَإِنَّهُ يُجْزِيهِ اَلْإِيمَاءُ وَإِنْ كَانَ تَاجِراً فَلْيُقِمْ وَلاَ يَدْخُلُهُ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who wades into water and the time of prayer comes upon him. Imam (a.s) said: "If he is in battle, then gesturing suffices him; But if he is a merchant, then let him stop and not enter (the water) until he has prayed."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s): “We were in Al-Bayda’ at the end of the night, so I performed wudu and used a tooth-stick (siwak), and I was about to pray, then something entered my heart (caused doubt), is it permissible to pray in Al-Bayda’ while in the litter (on the camel)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in Al-Bayda’." I asked: “Where is the boundary of Al-Bayda’?” Imam (a.s) said: "Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, when He (a.s) reached Dhat Al-Jaysh, He (a.s) would quicken his pace and would not pray until He (a.s) reached the resting place of the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family." I said to Imam (a.s): “And where is Dhat Al-Jaysh?” Imam (a.s) said: "Three miles before Al-Hafirah."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّا كُنَّا فِي اَلْبَيْدَاءِ فِي آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ فَتَوَضَّأْتُ وَ اِسْتَكْتُ وَ أَنَا أَهُمُّ بِالصَّلاَةِ ثُمَّ كَأَنَّهُ دَخَلَ قَلْبِي شَيْءٌ فَهَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي اَلْبَيْدَاءِ فِي اَلْمَحْمِلِ فَقَالَ «لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي اَلْبَيْدَاءِ» قُلْتُ وَ أَيْنَ حَدُّ اَلْبَيْدَاءِ فَقَالَ« كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا بَلَغَ ذَاتَ اَلْجَيْشِ جَدَّ فِي اَلْمَسِيرِ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّي حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ مُعَرَّسَ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ» قُلْتُ لَهُ وَ أَيْنَ ذَاتُ اَلْجَيْشِ فَقَالَ« دُونَ اَلْحَفِيرَةِ بِثَلاَثَةِ أَمْيَالٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (a.s): “We were in Al-Bayda’ at the end of the night, so I performed wudu and used a tooth-stick (siwak), and I was about to pray, then something entered my heart (caused doubt), is it permissible to pray in Al-Bayda’ while in the litter (on the camel)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Do not pray in Al-Bayda’." I asked: “Where is the boundary of Al-Bayda’?” Imam (a.s) said: "Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, when He (a.s) reached Dhat Al-Jaysh, He (a.s) would quicken his pace and would not pray until He (a.s) reached the resting place of the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family." I said to Imam (a.s): “And where is Dhat Al-Jaysh?” Imam (a.s) said: "Three miles before Al-Hafirah."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Akhir, peace be upon him, said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “The time of prayer comes while a man is at Al-Bayda”. Imam (a.s) said: "Let him move away from the main paths to the right or the left, and then pray."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَخِيرِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ تَحْضُرُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ بِالْبَيْدَاءِ قَالَ« يَتَنَحَّى عَنِ اَلْجَوَادِّ يَمْنَةً وَ يَسْرَةً وَ يُصَلِّي»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Akhir, peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “The time of prayer comes while a man is at Al-Bayda”. Imam (a.s) said: "Let him move away from the main paths to the right or the left, and then pray."

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer is disliked in three places along the road: Al-Bayda’, which is Dhat Al-Jaysh, and Dhat Al-Salasil, and Dajnan." And Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem in praying between the side roads (zawahir), meaning the side paths of the roads, but it is discouraged to pray on the main thoroughfares (al-jawad)"
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ تُكْرَهُ فِي ثَلاَثَةِ مَوَاطِنَ مِنَ اَلطَّرِيقِ اَلْبَيْدَاءِ وَ هِيَ ذَاتُ اَلْجَيْشِ وَ ذَاتِ اَلصَّلاَصِلِ وَ ضَجْنَانَ» وَ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُصَلَّى بَيْنَ اَلظَّوَاهِرِ وَ هِيَ اَلْجَوَادُّ جَوَادُّ اَلطُّرُقِ وَ يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يُصَلَّى فِي اَلْجَوَادِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Prayer is disliked in three places along the road: Al-Bayda’, which is Dhat Al-Jaysh, and Dhat Al-Salasil, and Dajnan." And Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem in praying between the side roads (zawahir), meaning the side paths of the roads, but it is discouraged to pray on the main thoroughfares (al-jawad)"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in the Valley of Al-Shuqrah."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي وَادِي اَلشُّقْرَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in the Valley of Al-Shuqrah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s): “What is the extent of wet mud upon which prostration is not valid?” Imam (a.s) said: "When the forehead sinks into it and does not remain firmly upon the ground."
arabicText: محمد بن أحمد عن أحمد بن الحسن عن عمرو بن سعيد عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار الساباطي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن حد الطين الذي لا يسجد عليه ما هو؟ قال إذا غرق الجبهة ولم تثبت على الارض
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s): “What is the extent of wet mud upon which prostration is not valid?” Imam (a.s) said: "When the forehead sinks into it and does not remain firmly upon the ground."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri’ab, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I stand in prayer and I see in front of me, in the direction of the Qiblah, excrement.” Imam (a.s) said: "Move away from it as much as you can, and do not pray on the roads."
arabicText: سهل بن زياد عن ابن محبوب عن ابن رئاب عن جميل ابن صالح عن الفضيل بن يسار قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام أقوم في الصلاة فأرى قدامي في القبلة العذرة قال تنح عنها ما استطعت ولاتصل على الجواد
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri’ab, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I stand in prayer and I see in front of me, in the direction of the Qiblah, excrement.” Imam (a.s) said: "Move away from it as much as you can, and do not pray on the roads."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) said: "Do not perform the obligatory prayer inside the Ka‘bah."
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ فِي اَلْكَعْبَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: "Do not perform the obligatory prayer inside the Ka‘bah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Khalid ibn Abi Isma‘il, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man prays on top of Abu Qubays (mountain), facing the Qiblah” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي عَلَى أَبِي قُبَيْسٍ مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Khalid ibn Abi Isma‘il, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man prays on top of Abu Qubays (mountain), facing the Qiblah” Imam (a.s) said: "There is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Abd Al-Salam:
(Imam) Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding one who is overtaken by the time of prayer while he is above the Ka‘bah. Imam (a.s) said: "If he stands, he will have no Qiblah; rather, he should lie on his back and raise his eyes toward the sky and direct his heart toward the Qiblah that is in the heavens, the ‘Bayt al-Ma‘mur’, and recite. When he intends to bow, he should close his eyes, and when he wants to raise his head from bowing, he should open his eyes. And the prostration is to be done in the same manner."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلسَّلاَمِ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي اَلَّذِي تُدْرِكُهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ هُوَ فَوْقَ اَلْكَعْبَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ قَامَ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ قِبْلَةٌ وَلَكِنْ يَسْتَلْقِي عَلَى قَفَاهُ وَ يَفْتَحُ عَيْنَيْهِ إِلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ وَيَعْقِدُ بِقَلْبِهِ اَلْقِبْلَةَ اَلَّتِي فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ اَلْبَيْتَ اَلْمَعْمُورَ وَ يَقْرَأُ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَ اَلسُّجُودُ عَلَى نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Abd Al-Salam:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding one who is overtaken by the time of prayer while he is above the Ka‘bah. Imam (a.s) said: "If he stands, he will have no Qiblah; rather, he should lie on his back and raise his eyes toward the sky and direct his heart toward the Qiblah that is in the heavens, the ‘Bayt al-Ma‘mur’, and recite. When he intends to bow, he should close his eyes, and when he wants to raise his head from bowing, he should open his eyes. And the prostration is to be done in the same manner."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Hadid ibn Hakim Al-Azdi, who said:
We said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The rooftop upon which urine has fallen and people urinate on it, may one pray in that place?” Imam (a.s) said: "If the sun and wind reach it and it is dry, then there is no problem with it, unless it is a place that is habitually used as a urinal."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ حَدِيدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ اَلْأَزْدِيِّ قَالاَ: قُلْنَا لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلسَّطْحُ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْبَوْلُ وَ يُبَالُ عَلَيْهِ أَ يُصَلَّى فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْمَوْضِعِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ تُصِيبُهُ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ اَلرِّيحُ وَ كَانَ جَافّاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ يُتَّخَذُ مَبَالاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Hadid ibn Hakim Al-Azdi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The rooftop upon which urine has fallen and people urinate on it, may one pray in that place?” Imam (a.s) said: "If the sun and wind reach it and it is dry, then there is no problem with it, unless it is a place that is habitually used as a urinal."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in a house that contains wine or an intoxicant."
arabicText: محمد بن يحيى عن أحمد بن الحسن عن عمرو بن سعيد عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار الساباطي عن أبى عبد الله عليه السلام قال لا تصل في بيت فيه خمر أو مسكر
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in a house that contains wine or an intoxicant."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washsha’, from Aban, from ‘Amr ibn Khalid:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "Jibra’il, peace be upon him, said: ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), we do not enter a house in which there is an image of a human being (image-making of animate beings), nor a house in which there is urination (filth left exposed), nor a house in which there is a dog (ritually impure, najis al-ʿayn).’"
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «قَالَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّا لاَ نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ صُورَةُ إِنْسَانٍ وَلاَ بَيْتاً يُبَالُ فِيهِ وَلاَ بَيْتاً فِيهِ كَلْبٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washsha’, from Aban, from ‘Amr ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "Jibra’il, peace be upon him, said: ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), we do not enter a house in which there is an image of a human being (image-making of animate beings), nor a house in which there is urination (filth left exposed), nor a house in which there is a dog (ritually impure, najis al-ʿayn).’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu Ali Al-Ash‘ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, Jibra’il, peace be upon him, came to Me (saws) and said: ‘We, the company of angels, do not enter a house in which there is a dog (ritually impure, najis al-ʿayn), or a statue with a body (image-making of animate beings), or a vessel in which there is urination (filth left exposed).’"
arabicText: أَبُو عَلِيٍّ اَلْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَتَانِي فَقَالَ إِنَّا مَعَاشِرَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ لاَ نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ كَلْبٌ وَ لاَ تِمْثَالُ جَسَدٍ وَ لاَ إِنَاءٌ يُبَالُ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Abu Ali Al-Ash‘ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, Jibra’il, peace be upon him, came to Me (saws) and said: ‘We, the company of angels, do not enter a house in which there is a dog (ritually impure, najis al-ʿayn), or a statue with a body (image-making of animate beings), or a vessel in which there is urination (filth left exposed).’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in a house in which there is a Magian, and there is no problem in praying in a house in which there is a Jew or a Christian."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي بَيْتٍ فِيهِ مَجُوسِيٌّ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ فِي بَيْتٍ فِيهِ يَهُودِيٌّ أَوْ نَصْرَانِيٌّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "Do not pray in a house in which there is a Magian, and there is no problem in praying in a house in which there is a Jew or a Christian."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd Al-Malik Al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said to me: "O Abu Bakr (Al Hadrami), everything upon which the sun shines is pure."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ : «يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ كُلُّمَا أَشْرَقَتْ عَلَيْهِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَهُوَ طَاهِرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd Al-Malik Al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said to me: "O Abu Bakr (Al Hadrami), everything upon which the sun shines is pure."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Mu‘adhi, from Al-Tayalisi, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Ishaq, from Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, who said:
He (ibn Abdullah) said to (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray in Al-Masjid Al-Haram and I sit on my left leg because of the dampness (al-nada).” Imam (a.s) said: "Sit on your buttocks (al-yatayn), even if you are in the mud."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْمُعَاذِيِّ عَنِ اَلطَّيَالِسِيِّ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِجَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أُصَلِّي فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ فَأَقْعُدُ عَلَى رِجْلِيَ اَلْيُسْرَى مِنْ أَجْلِ اَلنَّدَى فَقَالَ« اُقْعُدْ عَلَى أَلْيَتَيْكَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي اَلطِّينِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Mu‘adhi, from Al-Tayalisi, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Ishaq, from Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (ibn Abdullah) said to (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray in Al-Masjid Al-Haram and I sit on my left leg because of the dampness (al-nada).” Imam (a.s) said: "Sit on your buttocks (al-yatayn), even if you are in the mud."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Amr, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il:
(Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is praying. Imam (a.s) said: "There should be in front of him a small mound of soil, or he should draw a line in front of himself."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عَمْرٍو عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« يَكُونُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ كُومَةٌ مِنْ تُرَابٍ أَوْ يَخُطُّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ بِخَطٍّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Amr, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is praying. Imam (a.s) said: "There should be in front of him a small mound of soil, or he should draw a line in front of himself."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, from Maslamah ibn ‘Ata’, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "What thing cuts (invalidates) the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "A man’s fiddling with his beard."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَسِّنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَسْلَمَةَ بْنِ عَطَاءٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ يَقْطَعُ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« عَبَثُ اَلرَّجُلِ بِلِحْيَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, from Maslamah ibn ‘Ata’, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): "What thing cuts (invalidates) the prayer?" Imam (a.s) said: "A man’s fiddling with his beard."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who has a wart or a wound, may he remove the wart during his prayer or pluck some flesh from that wound and throw it away? Imam (a.s) said: "If he does not fear that blood will flow, then there is no problem. But if he fears that blood will flow, then he should not do it." And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who, while in prayer, was struck by someone who caused a gash and blood flowed, so he left the prayer, washed it, and did not speak until he returned to the mosque, does he count what he already prayed or must he start over? Imam (a.s) said: "He must start the prayer from the beginning and not count anything of what he already prayed."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ بِهِ اَلثُّؤْلُولُ أَوِ اَلْجُرْحُ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْطَعَ اَلثُّؤْلُولَ وَهُوَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ أَوْ يَنْتِفَ بَعْضَ لَحْمِهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلْجُرْحِ وَيَطْرَحَهُ قَالَ« إِنْ لَمْ يَتَخَوَّفْ أَنْ يَسِيلَ اَلدَّمُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ تَخَوَّفَ أَنْ يَسِيلَ اَلدَّمُ فَلاَ يَفْعَلْهُ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَرَمَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَشَجَّهُ فَسَالَ اَلدَّمُ فَانْصَرَفَ فَغَسَلَهُ وَ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ حَتَّى رَجَعَ إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ هَلْ يَعْتَدُّ بِمَا صَلَّى أَوْ يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ لاَ يَعْتَدُّ بِشَيْءٍ مِمَّا صَلَّى»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who has a wart or a wound, may he remove the wart during his prayer or pluck some flesh from that wound and throw it away? Imam (a.s) said: "If he does not fear that blood will flow, then there is no problem. But if he fears that blood will flow, then he should not do it." And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who, while in prayer, was struck by someone who caused a gash and blood flowed, so he left the prayer, washed it, and did not speak until he returned to the mosque, does he count what he already prayed or must he start over? Imam (a.s) said: "He must start the prayer from the beginning and not count anything of what he already prayed."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "If one of you prays in an open desert, let him place in front of him something like the rear of a saddle. If he does not find that, then a stone; if he does not find that, then an arrow; and if he does not find that, then let him draw a line in the ground in front of him."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« إِذَا صَلَّى أَحَدُكُمْ بِأَرْضِ فَلاَةٍ فَلْيَجْعَلْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِثْلَ مُؤْخِرَةِ اَلرَّحْلِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَحَجَراً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَسَهْماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَلْيَخُطَّ فِي اَلْأَرْضِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from (Imam) Ja‘far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: "If one of you prays in an open desert, let him place in front of him something like the rear of a saddle. If he does not find that, then a stone; if he does not find that, then an arrow; and if he does not find that, then let him draw a line in the ground in front of him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ghiyath:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated that the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, placed a cap (‘qalansuwah’) and prayed facing it.
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن سنان عن غياث عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام ان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وضع قلنسوة وصلى إليها
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ghiyath:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated that the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, placed a cap (‘qalansuwah’) and prayed facing it.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Al-Fudayl:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "A woman may pray behind her husband, both the obligatory and the recommended prayers, and she may follow him in the prayer."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« اَلْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي خَلْفَ زَوْجِهَا اَلْفَرِيضَةَ وَ اَلتَّطَوُّعَ وَ تَأْتَمُّ بِهِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Al-Fudayl:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: "A woman may pray behind her husband, both the obligatory and the recommended prayers, and she may follow him in the prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad, from Al-Hajjal, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a woman who prays near a man. Imam (a.s) said: "If there is a barrier between them, then there is no problem."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي عِنْدَ اَلرَّجُلِ قَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا حَاجِزٌ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad, from Al-Hajjal, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a woman who prays near a man. Imam (a.s) said: "If there is a barrier between them, then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from someone who informed him, from Jamil:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is praying and a woman is beside him or next to him. Imam (a.s) said: "If her prostration occurs at the time of his bowing, then there is no problem."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ بِحِذَاهُ أَوْ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ سُجُودُهَا مَعَ رُكُوعِهِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from someone who informed him, from Jamil:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who is praying and a woman is beside him or next to him. Imam (a.s) said: "If her prostration occurs at the time of his bowing, then there is no problem."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a woman praying near a man. Imam (a.s) said: "A woman should not pray directly in line with a man, unless he is in front of her, even if only by the length of his chest."
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي عِنْدَ اَلرَّجُلِ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّي اَلْمَرْأَةُ بِحِيَالِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ قُدَّامَهَا وَ لَوْ بِصَدْرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a woman praying near a man. Imam (a.s) said: "A woman should not pray directly in line with a man, unless he is in front of her, even if only by the length of his chest."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on What is Permissible and Impermissible to Pray in - of Clothing and Place
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who was leading the Dhuhr prayer, and a woman stood beside him praying, thinking it was the ‘Asr prayer, does that invalidate the prayer of the group? And what is the ruling for the woman in her prayer with them, given that she had already prayed Dhuhr? Imam (a.s) said: "It does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer."
arabicText: محمد بن مسعود العياشي عن جعفر بن محمد قال حدثني العمركي عن علي بن جعفر عن أخيه موسى قال سألته عن إمام كان في الظهر فقامت امرأة بحياله تصلي وهي تحسب انها العصر هل يفسد ذلك على القوم؟ وما حال المرأة في صلاتها معهم وقد كانت صلت الظهر؟ قال لا يفسد ذلك على القوم وتعيد المرأة
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Mas‘ud Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother (Imam) Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who was leading the Dhuhr prayer, and a woman stood beside him praying, thinking it was the ‘Asr prayer, does that invalidate the prayer of the group? And what is the ruling for the woman in her prayer with them, given that she had already prayed Dhuhr? Imam (a.s) said: "It does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 2, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on the Ages That Children Are Commanded to Pray
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "We command our children to pray when they are five years old, so command your children to pray when they are seven years old. And we command our children to fast when they are seven years old, according to what they can handle of the day's fast, whether it be until midday, or more than that, or less. Then, if thirst and hunger overpower them, they may break their fast, so that they may get used to fasting and become able to bear it. So command your children, when they are nine years old, to fast as much of the day as they can. Then, if thirst overcomes them, they may break their fast."
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّا نَأْمُرُ صِبْيَانَنَا بِالصَّلاَةِ إِذَا كَانُوا بَنِي خَمْسِ سِنِينَ فَمُرُوا صِبْيَانَكُمْ بِالصَّلاَةِ إِذَا كَانُوا بَنِي سَبْعِ سِنِينَ وَ نَحْنُ نَأْمُرُ صِبْيَانَنَا بِالصَّوْمِ إِذَا كَانُوا بَنِي سَبْعِ سِنِينَ بِمَا أَطَاقُوا مِنْ صِيَامِ اَلْيَوْمِ إِنْ كَانَ إِلَى نِصْفِ اَلنَّهَارِ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَقَلَّ فَإِذَا غَلَبَهُمُ اَلْعَطَشُ وَ اَلْغَرَثُ أَفْطَرُوا حَتَّى يَتَعَوَّدُوا اَلصَّوْمَ فَيُطِيقُوهُ فَمُرُوا صِبْيَانَكُمْ إِذَا كَانُوا بَنِي تِسْعِ سِنِينَ بِالصَّوْمِ مَا اِسْتَطَاعُوا مِنْ صِيَامِ اَلْيَوْمِ فَإِذَا غَلَبَهُمُ اَلْعَطَشُ أَفْطَرُوا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, narrated from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "We command our children to pray when they are five years old, so command your children to pray when they are seven years old. And we command our children to fast when they are seven years old, according to what they can handle of the day's fast, whether it be until midday, or more than that, or less. Then, if thirst and hunger overpower them, they may break their fast, so that they may get used to fasting and become able to bear it. So command your children, when they are nine years old, to fast as much of the day as they can. Then, if thirst overcomes them, they may break their fast."

chapter: Chapter on the Ages That Children Are Commanded to Pray
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Rib‘i, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, said:
(Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, used to instruct the children to combine between Maghrib and ‘Isha (the later night prayer). Imam (a.s) would say: "It is better than that they sleep through it."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ يَأْمُرُ اَلصِّبْيَانَ يَجْمَعُونَ بَيْنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ يَقُولُ« هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَنْ يَنَامُوا عَنْهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Rib‘i, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, used to instruct the children to combine between Maghrib and ‘Isha (the later night prayer). Imam (a.s) would say: "It is better than that they sleep through it."
